Heading: Film review - Indian Express
Content:
A 21-year-old student of AISSMS College of Engineering committed suicide by jumping from his seventh-floor apartment on Friday evening.

The student, Ankush Ashok Gupta, is believed to have taken the extreme step after failing to clear his exams. He failed in six papers in his first year. Gupta had put in three of his papers for re-evaluation and had taken a provisional admission to the second year course in production engineering.

The re-evaluation results came out yesterday evening in which he cleared two of the three papers. He had four backlogs due to which he lost a year.

At around 8.30 pm he walked to the balcony of his seventh floor apartment on BT Kawade Road and jumped. Gupta's roommates were studying in another room at the time. The music in his room was playing loudly due to which they did not hear any sound. The watchman reported it to P Jangira, the secretary of the building, who informed police. One of his friends, Vipul Kumar, said, "Ankush learnt in the afternoon that his re-evaluation results had come. He went to the college and learnt he had lost a year. He came home and went to his room. Sometime later, he jumped down."

Ankush hails from Balia in UP. He had been studying in the city for the last one-and-a-half year. His friends said he was an average student. His uncle who stays in the city arrived after hearing the news. Ankush was living in Silver Dale Society with four other friends.

His family will be arriving in the city on Sunday.

Heading: NABARD releases 2nd installment for debt waiver scheme - Indian Express
Content:
Not interested
Movie name: EMI
Cast: Sanjay Dutt, Arjun Rampal, Malaika Arora Khan
Directed by: Saurabh Kabra
Showing at: City Pride Kothrud, E-Square, INOX, City Pride Satara Road, Fame Akurdi
There are two films in E.M.I. — one in which Malaika Arora Khan comes on every 10 minutes shaking her booty in clothes getting skimpier by the minute, and another in which four old men have a genuine conversation about their children in which the latter are allowed to have ambitions and to travel abroad without breaking their parents' hearts.
The sad part is that while director Saurabh Kabra could nicely shake and mix up the two, he makes no effort to. The two films run parallel in E.M.I., the good parts coming interspersed with the truly appalling.
And Kabra is working with a nice idea here and a fairly good script involving four different families who have all taken loans and are now defaulting on their EMIs for varied reasons. One a newly married and quickly separated couple; another a DJ who spends more than he earns; a third a father who has borrowed to send son abroad; and fourth a woman paying off the mob to get her husband's suicide turned into a murder to claim the Rs 2-crore insurance.
There are some very funny moments, like the smooth-talking personal bankers who won't be fazed by lecherous customers or cautious ones; the innovative gangsters who help you with getting bank loans so you can pay up their money, in installments; Sanjay Dutt, who can now do these roles of a kind-hearted gangster in his sleep and who here, in the placement of his expensive dark glasses a little too unevenly down his nose, conveys both his ambitions and limitations; and his gang of small, Munnabhai-esque lumpens.
And there are some very unfunny ones: Arjun Rampal, confusing himself once again as a serious musician (in a tweed hat, for God's sake); Ashish Choudhary's twitching moustache that has more motion than the rest of his face combined; Urmila Matondkar's grieving widow act dressed in expensive saris, including a transparent red piece, designer suits and twirling wine; and Malaika's ever-shortening wardrobe.
Please, for our sake and yours, get a makeover.

A sorry spy
Movie name: Quantum of Solace
Directed by: Marc Forster
Cast: Daniel Craig, Judi Dench, Giancarlo
Showing at: City Pride Kothrud, E-Square, INOX
THIS 007 had everything going for it: Daniel Craig, who wowed audiences and critics alike in his first outing as James Bond, not a mean feat considering how long the hunt was for the new MI6 agent; Judi Dench in a meatier role as M; Paul Haggis (Crash, In the Valley of Elah) as writer; and Marc Foster (Monster's Ball, Finding Neverland) as director.
However, Quantum of Solace ain't no Casino Royale. That film gave us a Bond we had never seen before: A bruised and confused 007, as capable of getting hurt as hurting. He found and lost love in the film, going through a betrayal in the middle.
Though Quantum of Solace picks up from there with a Bond determined to revenge that love, against unknown forces who killed her, it eventually turns out to be just an excuse to hang two hours of uninterrupted — interchangeable with convoluted — action and some great actors on (including the two Bond women, with not a decent cocktail dress between them).
The plot, moving from Rome to London to Haiti to Austria to Bolivia, back to Italy, then to Russia, is so complicated you better give up pretending you care. Greedy dictators, compromised governments and oil politics are thrown about.
It doesn't help that the villain apparently running circles around half the world's governments is an effete pretender (Mathieu Amalric) who probably won't be able to convince a classroom of kids of his eco-friendly intentions. To dress him up in Hawaiian shirts and a langourous gait is an insult to our intelligence.
Daniel Craig looks great and, once in a while, still uses those piercing blue eyes to good effect. But he has none of the spark, wit or wisdom to transcend him above the other JB - Jason Bourne.
As boats crash into ships, planes collide into mountains and entire hotels go apart in blasts, we are left looking for precisely the same thing as Bond apparently is: some quantum of solace. None of us is getting it, at least in this film.

Heading: Children from Jammu&Kashmir visit NDA - Indian Express
Content:
The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)'s Maharashtra regional office has released the second installment under the Government of India - agriculture debt waiver and debt relief scheme — aggregating Rs 339.54 crore — to cooperative and regional rural banks in the state.

With this, the Pune regional office has so far released Rs 3,169.12 crore to the state. According to chief general manager of NABARD Sukhbir Singh, an amount aggregating to Rs 865.58 crore, in addition to its regular refinance scheme for financing crop loans to the farmers, were released as additional liquidity. It has been released under the liquidity support assistance scheme 2008." He said that that the amount released by NABARD will improve the liquidity position of the banks and facilitate enhanced credit flow to the farmers.

Finance Minister P Chidambaram had announced the debt waiver scheme which was taken up by banks and financial institutions including State Bank of India, Indian Bank and NABARD which started the scheme with Rs 72,000 crore before June 30. This is the second installment.

NABARD had worked on a two pronged approach on the disbursement of the loan waiver to the eligible farmers through state cooperative banks and rural banks under the scheme.

Heading: Mitcon is turnkey consultant for Mahagenco - Indian Express
Content:
A group of 35 children from Jammu&Kashmir, accompanied by four teachers and five army personnel, visited the National Defence Academy (NDA) at Khadakwasla here.

The children were briefed about the various training activities at the NDA. They were taken to several training areas, such as the Equestrian lines, Peacock Bay and Tri-shakti Museum. The group also visited the cadets' mess.

The children called on Col Ajay Chauhan, on behalf of NDA Commandant Air Marshal T S Randhawa and had a discussion on a career in the armed forces, after which some of them showed keen interest to join the same.

The education and motivational tour is an initiative under 'Operation Sadbhavana,' aimed at providing an opportunity for exposure and integration to 'The future of India with the main land.' It will also present an opportunity to the children to familiarise and interact with people across the country and build friendships and understanding between them.

The trip is completely sponsored by the Indian Army, including transportation, lodging, boarding and allied expenses.

Heading: Nanao returns, gives credit to ASI for success - Indian Express
Content:
Pune's Mitcon Consultancy services, a consultancy organisation in renewable energy sector, has been appointed as a turnkey consultant for Mahagenco, a major power generation company which has recently forayed into a solar power project. They were selected through competitive bidding process.

The project is expected to be completed by 2009 and is also expected to enjoy carbon credit benefits.

India's total power generation capacity as on August 31 was 1,46,145.11 MW, out of which 12,932.74 MW (nearly 9 percent) was from renewable energy sources. Solar power project contributes a meager 2.74 MW. In order to tap the huge potential of solar energy and accelerate solar power development, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy has declared innovative generation-based incentive scheme in the eleventh five year plan.

The government had declared conductive policies for development of such potential as renewable energy projects are techno-commercially viable and presents strong business case. According to Pradeep Bavadekar, managing director, MITCON Consultancy services, project promoters should adopt such projects for business integration and environment protection.

Heading: Isha Lakhani only Indian in main draw of ITF tourney - Indian Express
Content:
Aiba Youth World boxing championship gold medalist, Thokchom Nanao Singh arrived in the city on Saturday evening.

He was received at the Pune Station by Lt Col S Jayakumar, training officer (boxing) at ASI, Colonel Satpal Ahlawat, commandant of the ASI, Subhedar BB Mohanty, boxing coach of the ASI and all the boxing trainees of the institute. The army band made sure it was a grand welcome for the young pugilist.

This was followed by a celebration in his honour.

A tea party was organised on his behalf at the boxing hall of the ASI. Athletes from various disciplines training at the ASI were present to congratulate the boxer.

He is to be awarded with a special blazer by the commandant of the ASI, Col Ahlawat for his boxing achievements in a ceremony that will take place on Monday.

2008 has been a great year for Nanao Singh as he has won two successive gold medals at the Commonwealth Youth Games which took place in Pune, and the AIBA Youth World boxing championships, held at Guadalajara, Mexico.

"I am absolutely delighted to have won another gold medal. Back to back gold medals is a great achievement for me. I would like to thank the entire boxing staff at the ASI. Their tireless work has helped me achieve this feat. The ASI is truly a great institution. If it were not for this institute, I would not be where I am today. I will get ready to train for the 2010 games as soon as possible as my aim is to win a gold medal there as well." said the lightweight.

Heading: Bisht, Raina score easy wins in Walchand cup finals - Indian Express
Content: Isha Lakhani is the sole Indian representative to have made it to the main draw of the 25000$ NECC-ITF women's tennis championships which are scheduled to commence on Monday at the Deccan Gymkhana tennis courts. Lakhani, who is ranked at 333 rd in the world, is one of 17 players to make it to the main draw of the tennis championships. This 23-year-old Mumbai girl came into the lime light in 1999 when she figured in the semifinals of the under 14 and under 16 national championship. She represented India in the NEC World Youth Cup in Jakarta in May 2000. In the junior circuit in July 2002, she won the PIC Junior ITF grade-2 tennis tournament held at Pretoria, South Africa. She beat third seeded South African, Kelly Anderson 7-6 (7-3), 7-5 in the final to become the first Indian girl to win a grade-2 title. In the same tournament, she went on to win the doubles title as well, with partner Sania Mirza. In December of 2003, she won the title of the Asian Junior Tennis Championships after defeating top seeded Yung-Jan Chan of Japan in straight sets at the DLTA complex, Delhi. In 2005 she represented the country at the Asian Tennis Championships at Tashkent, Uzbekistan. In May of this year she emerged champion of the BSNL-Kerala Open after she defeated sixth seed Miki Miyamura of Japan in three sets. Her career high singles ranking was 291 in May of this year. Her 2008 win-loss record is 18-14 and all hopes are resting on her to win the title and do the country proud.

Heading: Women’s Cricket: Bengal beat Maharashtra - Indian Express
Content:
Ankita Raina of Gujarat and Ronit Bisht of Delhi won double crowns winning the Boys and the girls singles title at the Walchand Cup under-16 National Series Tennis Tournament organised by Deccan Gymkhana and played on their tennis courts here.

In the finals played today second seeded Ronit Bisht of Delhi easily put out top seeded Maharashtra player Shahbaaz Khan 6-1, 6-2 for the title while in the girls event top seeded Ankita Raina of Gujarat had no problems in disposing off West Bengal player Amruta Mukherjee 6-2, 6-3. Both players had won the doubles titles yesterday. Ronit a student of the Amity International school played confident tennis to dispose of the tall and lanky Khan in a match lasting around an hourto win the titke and 75 AITA points.

Ankita Raina based in Pune and a student of the Symbiosis school justified her top billing scoring an easy win over a bespectacled Mukherjee in about an hour and 20 mins. The prizes were given away at the hands of J .L Deshmukh, managing director, Walchandnagar Industries.

Heading: At PU, scholarships worth lakhs lie unutilised - Indian Express
Content:
Bengal beat Maharashtra by 65 runs in the one dayer of the All Indiawomen's super league held at Anantpur Sports Village on Friday. Bengal were put in to bat and they reached a healthy total of 218 for the loss of 6 wickets in their stipulated 50 overs. Madhumati Bhattacharjee (59 runs) and Mandira Mahapatra (48 runs) played well for their team while Maharashtra bowler Shweta Mane picked up two wickets and tried to restrict the opposition to a low score. In reply the Maharashtian women could only manage to score 153 runs in their 50 overs thanks to some good bowling by Neha Maji and Ruma Mondal.

Kanchan Fajage top scored with 47 runs but did not do enough to affect the result. Bengal won the match by 65 runs.

Heading: Gangrape: Family to move HC seeking cancellation of bail given to accused - Indian Express
Content:
At Panjab University, if records are anything to go by, more than 60 students from different states have missed the opportunity and failed to claim scholarships announced by their respective governments.

While students say they were never told about the scholarships, authorities at the university blame it on the lack of awareness among the students. This communication gap leaves behind lakhs of unused amount which is sent back by the PU authorities to the states.

According to a data received by the PU Registrar's office under a Right to Information application, 25 students for the academic session 2006-07 from states such as Punjab and Haryana have not claimed the scholarships announced by their states. The figure is around 25 for the next two sessions, 2007-08 and 2008-09, as well. Scholarships up to Rs 10,000 announced by various states are lying unutilised.

Talking to Newsline, PU Registrar S S Bari said: "Most of the unused scholarships are either those where the student's department is not mentioned or where the departments, whom we forward the details to, do not get back to us. It is the duty of the students to approach us to claim scholarships, otherwise the unused amount is sent back to the respective state."

Bari added that whenever a state allots a scholarship, it also informs the student respectively — a step enough for a student to come forward and claim the amount. Meanwhile, the 60 students who have not availed the scholarships in the last three years are not the students of the university and must have taken admission elsewhere, the Registrar claimed.

Interestingly, not many outstation students are aware of the scholarships. Geetika, an MA student from Jullandhar said: "I don't even know that states give scholarships. After graduation, I moved to Chandigarh along with my family and have no contact with my native town. The PU authorities should take some concrete steps to inform the students of any such scholarships."

Simranjot, a student from Gurdaspur, said: "I am sure maximum students from other states have no idea about the scholarships. The administrative block is so chaotic that most of the students do not take the pain to get their scholarships enchased."

Meanwhile, a students' body at the university has decided to take up the cudgel and ensure that the recipients claim the opportunity they have been given. Talking to Newsline, NSUI member Nitin Goyal said: "We will help all the students who have not been awarded their said scholarship. The PU officials also need to be more sensitive about student-related works."

Heading: Proposed, on paper for years, PGI facilities yet to take off - Indian Express
Content:
After moving High Court demanding a CBI inquiry into the gangrape of a 17-year-old schoolgirl, the victim's family is now contemplating to file another petition against the bail given to one of the accused Aman Ahuja recently.

The family has alleged that Ahuja, a resident of Sector 10, was a main accused in the case and was involved in getting the pornographic CD of the victim made.

But the police deliberately went ahead omitting his name from the FIR, a family member said.

On the other hand, the police said that all efforts are being made to trace the accused. SHO of Sector-14 police station, Inspector Surjit Kumar said: "After sketches of the accused were made, we have visited different schools loking for some clue regarding the accused. We are investigating the case in details."

One of the victim's relative said: "Aman Ahuja was not only involved in the rape, but also blackmailed and tortured the victim. Despite the victim telling the police about his involvement, they have deliberately omitted his name from the FIR. It is shocking to see Ahuja roaming about in the court complex while our daughter is running from pillar to post seeking justice. No one is helping us.

Timeline

Sept 16: Vicitm gangraped and tortured throughout the night by five persons, including a girl called Chhavi

Sept 17: The victim left at Sector 4 by the accused at 5 am. She goes to her school, Chaman Lal DAV School, Sector 11 but is not allowed to participate in an event. Also receives threat calls from one of the accused, Jitesh

Sept 18: Family of the victim lodges an FIR under Sections 363, 366A, 376, 377, 342, 323, 34, 506 of the IPC

Sept 22: Aman Ahuja, a resident of Sector 10, arrested, taken on one-day remand and sent in judicial custody

Sept 26: Jitesh, resident of Sector 4, arrested, taken into five-day police remand. Police fail to crack the case and the accused sent to judicial custody

Oct 5: Chaman Lal of DAV School, Sector 11, refuses to take the victim and asks her to not come

Oct 6: The school takes a U-turn

Oct 7: Family claims that they are receiving threat calls and ask for police protection. No security provided.

Nov 1: Aman Ahuja gets bail

Nov 3: Rape victim visits DGP office but fails to meet him

Nov 4: The victim is made to wait outside the DSP (Headquater) office for more than two hours.

The DSP leaves without meeting the victim and her mother.

Another accused in the case — Tanu — who was called for questioning, is set free with the police taking a U-turn

Nov 5: Bail application of Jitesh dismissed

Nov 6: Kushal Kushul, the Swift owner involved in the case, applies for anticipatory bail, which will be heard on November 10

Heading: Sector 20 plagued with overgrown weeds, construction waste - Indian Express
Content:
Despite the slow pace of progress on its ongoing works, the premier health institute of the region, the PGI, is on way to introduce several new centres to ease patient load. As the flagship project of PGI director Prof K K Talwar, the Advanced Cardiac Care Centre, readies for a partial opening on November 17, Newsline takes a look at the development and plans of the leading projects of the institute.

Advanced Cardiac Centre: Opposite the School of Public Health, the Rs 46-crore project has been under construction for the last four years. The 200-bed centre would assist patients of the cardiology and cardiovascular surgery departments. Moving at a snail's pace, with completion deadlines extending every month, the PGI authorities now say the centre will be ready for OPD services from November 17. Equipment worth over Rs 8 crore was purchased for the centre, which is lying unused at present.

"We are planning to shift all OPD services of both the departments and the non-invasive investigations to the new centre from the next week. By January, all services, including the catheterisation laboratory or cath labs and the OTs would be functional," said a senior faculty.

The Advanced Cardiac Centre has four operation theatres and three cath labs. The two-storeyed centre is spread over 2.80 lakh sq ft.

"We receive around 200 OPD cardiology patients everyday at the PGI. Once the centre is functional, the load of patients at the OPD block and the Nehru Hospital would ease," added a senior faculty. Meanwhile, even as the structure of the centre nears completion, the faculty in-charge is yet to be decided.

Advanced Trauma Centre: On papers as a proposal for over a decade, formally sanctioned by the government way back in the Ninth Five-Year Plan, the Advanced Trauma Centre is under construction for more than two years. Coming up adjacent to the existing Emergency, this ambitious project, which once had on its plans a helipad for faster transportation of patients, is to come up on an area of 1.12 lakh sq ft. The sanctioned amount for the project is Rs 17.50 crore.

"The PGI Emergency is already under heavy pressure with 200 per cent occupancy at any given time. The trauma centre would strengthen the emergency care at the institute with the help of state-of-art-facilities," said PGI spokesperson Manju Wadwalkar.

The centre is designed to have 6 OTs with around 200 beds in the General, ICU, Observation and Private wards. Cases of four main departments -neurosurgery, orthopaedics, plastic and general surgery would be handled by the centre.

Pet scan: PET scan for the exact diagnosis of cancer cells in the body is hanging fire for the past few months due to the ongoing construction of the PET Centre. Construction to house the Rs 8-crore machinery is still underway near the PGI emergency. With the previous deadline of August already lapsed and the revised deadline of October also over, officials say due to the delay in construction, the project is taking time.

New facilities, centres at PGI in recent years:

* Advanced Eye centre

* Drug de-addiction centre

* Multi-storey parking outside the new OPD block

* Burns Unit and Hepatology ICUs

* Advanced Urology Centre

* Bone Marrow Transplant Centre

Heading: Students to assess teachers at govt schools, but with a twist - Indian Express
Content:
While the residents of Sector 20 acknowledge the provision of basic facilities in the area, they have their share of complaints, the prime among them being construction waste and overgrown weeds.

The area behind the mosque in the sector has overgrown weeds in abundance.

Saroj, a resident of the area, says. "Overgrown grass can be found in the entire lane. Garbage is dumped by people almost everywhere. The park needs to be cleaned as it is surrounded by filth."

Suman, another resident of the area, rues the ill-planned dumping of construction waste in the area.

"There is an enormous amount of construction waste lying all around. No one knows where it comes from. Strict rules need to be followed and the guilty should be fined," says Suman.

The police colony in the sector is plagued by the problems of leaking roofs and bad roads.

A resident of the area says that the situation during rains is miserable with water seeping and accumulating in almost all corners. For the market, the problem of inadequate parking tops the list. The high number of vehicles in the area coupled with the problem of haphazard parking further intensifies the parking woes.

Area councillor Rajesh Kumar Gupta says: "Many development works are going on in the sector. Paver blocks will be laid around the community centre and dispensary. We have applied for setting up a Sehaj Safai Kendra so that the sector becomes bin-free. Widening of the V-5 roads is going on, sodium vapour lamps are being put up for which the poles have been installed."

He adds: "The police colony comes under the jurisdiction of the Administration. I have approcahed the authorities with the problems being faced by the people. With joint efforts with the Administration the area would be developed and beautified."

Heading: 17 mediation centres inaugurated for alternate dispute redressal mechanism - Indian Express
Content:
Now, the principals will ask students to evaluate teachers' performance

While teachers in government schools continue to be under the assessment scanner of students despite a change of guard in the Education Department, this time round, the parameters are slightly different.

Unlike the earlier plan, whereby students filled a performance assessment form and submitted it to the appointed counsellor, the new idea proposes the heads of institutions to play a significant role.

Samwartak Singh, DPI (Schools) said the principals of schools will talk to children about the various aspects defining teaching. "The principals will ask students to judge the teachers' performance on different aspects like regularity and teaching methodology, among others. While in the previous plan, the heads were completely kept away from this exercise, this time we have decided to involve them."

The department is also working on the idea of having a questionnaire to review the teachers' performance. "The questionnaire will examine teachers on conduct in the class, taking regular class tests, unbiased relationship with students and the rapport shared with parents."

He added, "We will form a committee comprising the District Education Officer (DEO) and Deputy DEO who will analyse the data submitted to them by the schools on a monthly basis."

While the earlier plan had invited a lot of flak from the teaching fraternity due to the "odd" questions asked, teachers are happy with the latest proposal.

"The former feedback form, in a way, infringed upon the private lives of teachers with questions like for how long did a teacher talk over the mobile phone," said a teacher with the Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 35.

The teacher added, "Moreover, the reviewing criteria were very vague. With the department working afresh on it, we hope the objectivity is maintained."

Heading: Mental health fest ends at GCG-11 - Indian Express
Content:
"People are taking the services of goons to settle matters instead of coming to the judiciary. It is unfortunate and there is a need to stop the erosion of faith of the people in the judiciary," said Justice S B Sinha from the Supreme Court of India while inaugurating the mediation and conciliation centres in 17 districts through video conferencing at the Punjab and Haryana High Court, on Saturday.

Laying emphasis on cyber mediation centres, Justice Sinha said, "By 2025, we must have online mediation for which we have to prepare from now. Mediation and Conciliation is a means for achieving the Alternate Dispute Redressal Mechanism Vision 2025."

Justice Sinha inaugurated three permanent Lok Adalats in the premises of the High Court in the morning.

Speaking on the occasion, Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court Justice T S Thakur said that in 1955 when the court was shifted from Shimla, the strength of the judges was eight and pendency of the cases were 6,356 but, today, pendency has increased by nearly 30 times while the number of judges have increased by barely six times to 48.

Justice Thakur said Mediation is a voluntary non-binding process in which impartial and neutral mediators assist the parties in reaching an agreement.

He added, "The biggest challenge the Indian judiciary is facing today is the large number of cases with nearly three crore cases pending in the courts."

Justice Sinha said increasing the numbers of judges is not the solution to reduce the number of pending cases.

"There is much more needed to achieve good results and to reduce the pendency of the cases. These mediation and conciliation centres will help save time, money, loss of health and peace of mind," he added.

Heading: Day 2: PEC Fest rocks on - Indian Express
Content:
The two-day Mental Health fest organised at the GCG concluded on Saturday. On the second day, three talks by personalities from different walks of life were held. In the morning session, Swami Brahmeshnanda, secretary of Ramakrishna Mission, Chandigarh, spoke on 'Spiritual Techniques for Stress Management'. Swami started his lecture by a Sanskrit Shloka — "Sanve bavati sukhine, sarve santu niramaya".

He stressed that if one is mentally prepared, physical troubles do not seem big and they can be easily dealt with.

In the second session, Professor Rajesh Gill, Department of Sociology, Panjab University, discussed about "Adolescent Problems in Females".

Professor Gill said that the youngster needs are enormous and have changed with time. The pace of the things is much faster. The gap between parents and children is increased.

"Due to clash in parents-children opinions, adolescents are stuck in dilemma. They are unable to cope with the stress arising from these conditions. The peer pressure is increasing due to need for acceptance, privacy and secrecy being the villains of the time. The pressure of looking good, making boyfriends and other crises of life are increasing the problems and worries of life."

The third session was on Yoga Relaxation techniques. Yoga practitioner Meenakshi highlighted the successful applications of yoga as a therapeutic tool.

She emphasised on the role of body flexibility as the best relaxation strategy. She also demonstrated practically different yoga asanas and spoke about it uses.

Heading: ‘It was an overwhelming experience to visit India’ - Indian Express
Content:
After having spread the cheer on Day 1, students of Punjab Engineering College had more to offer on the second day of the PEC Fest on Saturday. The day began on a musical note with Bazm-e-Shayari.

Melodious tunes gave way to some serious literary competition with

Face Off, a group discussion. The afternoon session of the annual extravaganza witnessed a panel discussion by the Youth Parliament.

'Wordict' gave people a chance to unravel several word puzzles.

The quiz competition, Eureka, also witnessed great participation from the students.

Gautam Bose was the quizmaster of the day. Several other events had also been organised such as the couple football, tattoo making and face painting. People from all over crowded the PEC campus in the evening hours to witness the TNT Rock Nyt.

As many as 50 visually-impaired children from the Institute of Blind, Sector 26, were given access to the MI-26 Helicopter, AN-32 aircraft and IL-76 transport aircraft at 12-Wing, Air Force, Chandigarh, on Saturday. Under the aegis of the Air Force Wives' Welfare Association (L), the programme intended to give these children the exposure to 'feel' the flying machines in close proximity. Before boarding the aircraft, the students touched various miniature models to get a feel of the structure of various aircraft. The children were also shown Radio communication and navigational systems at the Air Traffic Control Tower. Air Commodore S R K Nair said: "We will present different aircraft models to the blind school so that the children can be enlightened about the aircraft used by the Indian Air Force." Kulwinder (10) said: "I never thought that I would be so close to a real aircraft. It is the experience of a lifetime."

Heading: Four separate accidents leave 5 dead, 10 injured - Indian Express
Content:
The government College in Sector 11 saw a special visitor on Saturday in the form of Professor J K Ashraf, a retired Urdu teacher from the Government College, Lahore University in Pakistan. He interacted with the faculty members and students of the college and spoke at length about the social life in Pakistan.

Ashraf said he had visited his native village on Friday and says the visit left him emotional.

Born in a village near Garhshankar, Punjab (India), Prof Ashraf had migrated to Pakistan at the time of partition. "It was an overwhelming experience. The natives were very warm and affectionate."

Speaking at the college auditorium, Prof Ashraf described his trip to the city as a "stimulating and memorable experience which is going to last a lifetime".

He also stressed on the fact that despite political divisions between the two nations, culturally and linguistically, "they are one and the same." Earlier, college principal Dr A L Gauba extended a warm welcome to him. Dean Dr Nindru Bal, vice-principal Manjit Kaur and Dean Students' Welfare Prof Sidhu found the interaction with the guest "very interesting and stimulating".

Students of the college had also organised a cultural show which included a folk dance performance.

Heading: Cop, trader sent to judicial remand in graft case - Indian Express
Content:
Five people died and ten were injured in four separate accidents in the region in the last 24 hours.

In Zirakpur, a Rajpura-bound three-wheeler rammed into an Army vehicle parked outside Apsara marriage palace on the Zirakpur-Patiala highway.

All eight passengers, including the driver, were rushed to GMCH-32, Chandigarh, where the three Rajpura residents — Raman Kumar, Kulwant Singh and Davinder Singh — died while the others were stated to be in critical condition.

Interestingly, the police have booked the three-wheeler driver for causing deaths and injuries due to negligence as preliminary investigations revealed that the Army vehicle was parked properly on the roadside.

In the second case, a vegetable vendor from Teera village, near Kharar, was killed while his associate from the same village was seriously injured when a speeding motorcycle crashed into the horse-cart they were riding.

While Bant Singh was declared brought dead, his associate Darbara Singh was admitted to the PGI, Chandigarh, in a critical condition, said the police while adding that the motorcycle driver was booked for causing death and injuries due to negligence.

In the third case, a youth died while another was injured after a recklessly driven private bus collided head-on with the scooter they were travelling on near the Kharar-Ropar stretch of the National Highway-21 in the morning hours, said Additional Sub-Inspector Malkiat Singh, the investigation officer (IO) in the case, said.

The youths, identified as Gurinder Singh of Balsanda village and Ramandeep Singh from Salempur village were rushed to the Kharar Civil Hospital, where Gurinder was declared dead on arrival while Ramandeep was referred to the PGI, Chandigarh, said the IO. The bus driver has been booked under Sections 279, 337, 427 and 304-A of the IPC.

In the fourth accident reported during the day, three persons from Dera

Bassi, including a couple, sustained serious injuries, after two of their motorcycles crashed into an autorickshaw, detained by the highway patrol police party on the Ambala-Chandigarh highway. While the injured were rushed to the

Dera Bassi Civil Hospital, the police have initiated investigations.

Heading: Eye on polls: Leaders mix morning walk with political talk - Indian Express
Content:
Sub-Inspector Sanjeev Kumar and Subhash Kataria, president of Sector 17 Traders' Association, were sent to judicial remand for 14 days on Saturday. The duo was produced by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) around 3 pm in the court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate.

In the court, the CBI produced a compact disc containing visuals of Kataria and the complainant. "The CD also contains the voice recording between the complainant and Sanjeev in which the later is asking him to deliver the money to Subhash," sources in the CBI said.

Sanjeev, the in-charge of the Neelam police post in Sector 17 and Subhash, owner of Delhi Jewellers, were arrested by the CBI sleuths on Friday for demanding and accepting bribe of Rs 50,000. The investigating agency had laid a trap and nabbed Kataria red-handed while accepting the money from local shopkeeper and complainant Arvind Pandey, owner of Pandey Book shop in Anand Theatre Complex, Sector 17.

Pandey had approached the CBI alleging that the sub-inspector had asked for money to get the shop vacated. Pandey had sublet one of his shops in under-bridge market in Sector 17 for Rs 26 lakh. His tenant Dina Nath, however, refused to vacate the shop and Pandey wanted to it vacated to handover the possession to the new buyer.

Before appearing in the court, Sanjeev told the media that he never asked for any bribe from Pandey or promised to get the shop vacated. He further said the matter was in court and sub-judice. "How could I get the shop vacated when the matter was in court? I have been implicated in the case," he said.

The Newsline also has the documents in which the court had ordered status quo on November 4. Also, Pandey had informed SHO of Sector 17 police station and Neelam police post incharge on November 3 that he and Dina Nath would either resolve the matter amicably or wait for the decision of the court. Till then, the keys of the shop were to remain in the custody of Kataria.

Sources in police said: "With these documents, it seems that the complainant had malafide intentions and the SI has been framed. When the matter was in court, how can anyone get the shop vacated? The matter should be probed thoroughly," they added.

House burgled in broad daylight

Mohali : A resident of Kansal village in Mohali district reported to the local police that his house was burgled in broad daylight on Saturday. Banwari Lal stated that he found his house ransacked after returning from the market along with his wife. Nearly 70 gram gold, Rs 8,000 cash and some other valuables were allegedly stolen. A case has been registered with the Mohali police.

Unidentified body found

Mohali : An unclaimed body of a man was found near Shivalik Vihar in Zirakpur on Saturday morning. According to the police, the deceased appears to be a migrant, aged around 50 years. The body has been sent for postmortem after initiating inquest proceedings Section 174 of the CrPC.

Heading: Global meltdown: ‘effective, unadulterated democratic system’ imperative - Indian Express
Content:
The city residents out for a morning walk have a bright chance of bumping into leaders of various political parties. With the elections to the Lok Sabha round the corner, the leaders have found novel ways to interact with residents.

Since the formal announcement of names of the candidates is awaited, the campaigning essentially comprises interaction at a personal level with the residents.

President of the Chandigarh unit of BJP Kamla Sharma says that the workers are interacting with voters in different sectors. "We are personally interacting with the residents. This is the time for reaching out to the residents. Once the elections are announced the focus shifts to addressing larger gatherings. At present, we are also holding meetings with groups of residents getting to know their problems."

The formal beginning of the campaign for the party will be with the Vijay Sankalp rally to be addressed by BJP prime ministerial candidate and Leader of Opposition L K Advani on November 16. The leaders are also interacting with the residents in the villages.

In the Congress camp too, interaction with the residents is the prime focus now.

A senior leader of the party says that regular interactions are being held with people in different sectors. Green belts also provide a perfect place to the leaders to meet the residents. It gives a chance to meet a large number of residents at one place.

Bahujan Samaj Party is engaged in constituting committees and distributing charges to different people. The visibility of the leaders at various events has also increased. This was evident at the Chhath Pooja held recently where leaders of all parties were present in full force. The parties are also busy taking up more issues affecting people.

The issues are diverse from inflation, rising prices of commodities, creation of jobs in the city, facilities for the poor as well as inadequate compensation to farmers to name a few.

BJP leaders meet Additional director of Food and Supplies department

A delegation of BJP leaders met Additional Director of Food and Supplies department Prerna Puri to discuss various demands including restarting scheme for issuing BPL cards. The delegation was led by state vice-president Kewal Krishan Addiwal, who was accompanied by councillors Ram Lal, Anil Dubey and Surinder Jagota.

The delegation apprised Puri about the difficulties being faced by the people living in different colonies. The members stated that the BPL cards should be issued after conducting fresh survey. They added that the supply of kerosene oil which was earlier being supplied to the residents of colonies has been stopped.

Where there are no government depots, the mobile vans should be used for supplying rations.

The delegation demanded that whenever the food inspectors are deputed to conduct surveys, the concerned area councillor should be informed. The time limit of the BPL card should be enhanced as has been done in case of APL card.

Heading: National-level seminar on global meltdown held at ABS - Indian Express
Content:
A one-day UGC sponsored seminar on "Global Economic Crisis," was held at the GGDSD College, Sector 32-C, on Saturday. The seminar was a collaborative effort of the Faculty Development Forum, CPE Scheme, and the Punjab Education Forum.

Speaking on the occasion, Professor S S Gill, economist from Punjabi University, Patiala, enunciated the basic reasons behind the rise and spread of the economic crisis. He tracked the history of the meltdown and described the American housing sector as the immediate cause behind the same.

Gill suggested "regulated capitalism" as a significant requirement for India. He added that the "governance in India has to be one that embodies a strong welfare system in it."

Professor H S Shergill, director, Punjab Development Studies, Chandigarh, elaborated the reasons behind the financial crisis.

He recommended "rule regulation and discretionary regulation" as the key forces that our economy needs to incorporate immediately.

Professor Manu Sood, from the IT department of HP University, spoke on the impact of the economic crisis on the IT sector in India. He said the IT boom is largely dependent on the American economy and is expected to be adversely affected by the financial meltdown.

He recommended the IT sector to focus on and tap the domestic market that offers a huge potential in the Indian economy.

Dr Manmohan Singh, former education secretary, Punjab, listed the various social and political causes behind the crisis while recommending an "effective, unadulterated democratic system" as a necessity to wade past the crisis.

Dr A C Vaid, principal of the college, said that it is fortunate that India does not have to depend on foreign flows significantly for its economic growth. He asserted that the impact can be minimised by means of the "right level of effort and intelligence" if we want to ensure a sustainable economic growth.

Heading: PGI chemist shops to give minimum 15% discount on medicines soon - Indian Express
Content:
"The Indian banking system is very strong and the Reserve Bank of India is one of the best central banks in the world. Global meltdown is a cyclical phenomenon but Indians should not lose faith in the economy," said Pawan Kumar Bansal, Minister of state for Finance and Parliamentary Affairs, at a national-level seminar — "Global Meltdown and India: Causes and Effects" — organised by the Aryans Business School(ABS) at the PHD Chamber on Saturday.

Bansal added: "We should not become bullish when the market is bullish and we should not become bearish when market is bearish."

Prof B S Ghuman, Dean, Faculty of Arts, PU, said the banks have to strike a balance between the monetary and fiscal policy which would help in equity considerations.

Prof B B Tandon, senior advisor, IBS, Chandigarh, related the cause of financial crisis to the transformation of the USA.

The seminar was presided over by Anshu Kataria, chairman, Aryans Group of Institutes (AGOI) while Rajiv Goyal, MD, Surya Pharmaceuticals Ltd, was the guest of honour.

Heading: Ousted IAS society members to lodge complaint - Indian Express
Content:
The medicines at the chemists shops within the PGIMER have now become cheaper as the institute has decided to increase the percentage of minimum discount on the sale of medicines and surgical items from the existing 5 per cent discount.

The increased rate of discount will also be available on other chemist shops in the due course, said PGI officials.

As per the earlier terms and conditions of allotment of chemist shops in the PGIMER premises, a minimum 5 per cent discount was admissible on the MRP of all the medical and surgical items. The institute has now increased the discount stating that a minimum 15 per cent discount would be available on MRP of branded medicines, minimum 30 per cent discount on MRP of generic and branded generic medicines and a minimum 30 per cent discount on MRP of consumable/surgical items.

Accordingly the institute has also invited fresh tenders for the allotment of chemist shops with the revised condition of increased discount. "The increased discount is applicable with immediate effect," said PGI authorities.

The new rates are available at the Consumer Medical Hall, Chemist Shop No 1, Under Ramp "B", Nehru Hospital, Sai Medicos, Chemist Shop No 9, Old Shopping Centre, (behind Oral Health Science Block), Child Care Chemist, Chemist Shop No 1, APC and Delhi Drugs Store, Chemist Shop No 5 and New Shopping Complex.

Heading: Kharar rape: Four suspects get two-day police custody - Indian Express
Content:
The ousted members of an IAS housing society in Mansa Devi Complex (MDC) in Panchkula are contemplating to file a criminal complaint against its former president IAS Neelam Pradeep Kasni for "illegally dropping their names" from the society's membership despite the stay orders. The membership of several members of the New Haryana Officers' Cooperative Society was illegally cancelled to allegedly accommodate some senior Haryana cadre IAS officers.

"The membership of around 35 members who were inducted in the society in 2003 were illegally cancelled in 2006 by Neelam Pradeep Kasni. The main reason behind this was that they wanted to accommodate other senior officers in lieu of the increase in the prices of the land due to the real estate boom," said Ram Kishan, one of the founder members of the society.

Another member of the society said: "The prices of land in Mansa Devi Complex near the Rajiv Gandhi Chandigarh IT Park has increased manifolds from Rs 2 crore to almost Rs 50 crore following a boom in the real estate industry."

"The worst was the fact that despite the stay orders on the cancellation of the membership by the registrar of Haryana Cooperative Society, their names were excluded from the final list by Kasni," he said.

Sources said that in 1998 when some senior IAS and IPS officers of the state joined to form a housing society with the name of New Haryana Officers' Cooperative Society with 80 members.

"The newly-formed society was also registered with the Haryana Cooperative societies after which they were allotted plot number two by HUDA in MDC near IT park," said the member.

In 2004, the Punjab and Haryana High Court had stayed the construction of any kind in the area.

"While it was a big loss as many of the members of the society left the membership after that, some new members were inducted to meet the economic liabilities. And today, the same members who came to their rescue then were made the scapegoat to include their own men," said a member.

While Neelam Kasni was not available for comments, a senior official of the Haryana Cooperative society said: "There is a lot of illegal bungling going on in the society. Not only the members were illegally removed, the entire election of their elective body was illegal. It was for this that the stay orders on the cancellation of the membership was given."

Heading: Punjab govt to start 3 new modern rural dairy training institutes - Indian Express
Content:
Four suspects-who were arrested in the gang rape case of a minor girl in Kharar village on Friday-were remanded to two-day police custody by a local court on Saturday, Kharar Station House Officer (SHO) Sub-Inspector Dalbeer Singh told Newsline. Singh, who is investigation officer in the case, said Mandeep Singh alias Rosy, Kulbeer Singh alias Nana, Mohan Singh and Sukhwinder Singh alias Ladi of Bhagomajra village near Kharar were produced before the Illaqa Magistrate, who directed to produce them again on Monday.

Already, two main suspects in the case-Kamaljeet Singh alias Kamal and Fateh Singh alais Titu of same village are in police custody till Monday. They were arrested on Thursday.

A 15-year-old girl was picked up from courtyard of her rented house and allegedly raped by six arrested youths, in turns after assaulting and gagging her while holding her elder sisters and aunt hostage in another room on Diwali night when the villagers were busy bursting crackers.

Kharar police had cracked the case within 48 hours of the registration of the FIR on Wednesday with the arrest of all of the six alleged rapists, claimed the SHO.

Heading: Three get life term for murder - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government will start three modern rural dairy training institutes to train new entrepreneurs to usher in a new era in the second white revolution, said Animal Husbandry, Fisheries and Dairy Development minister Gulzar Singh Ranike while addressing the farmers after laying the foundation stone of a hostel at the modern dairy training centre at Chatamali village.

He said these modern dairy training institutes were being set up at Abul Khurana village in Muktsar, Gill village in Moga and Verka village in Amritsar and would provide dairy training to more than 800 trainees in a year to adopt the financially viable venture.

He said that dairying has established its potentiality in the alternative commercial ventures in India and the modern dairy technology would usher in a new era in the second white revolution in the state as the demand of pure dairy products from Markfed had increased in India as well as other countries.

He added that agriculture as a profession was not a profitable venture these days due to high rates of inputs and costs of production but dairying has prominently evolved as an alternative profitable business for the unemployed, progressive farmers and new entrepreneurs to start with low costs as cottage industry.

Stressing on the need to set up commercial dairy units, Ranike said that the state government has enhanced budgetary provisions for dairy development to Rs 13,600 lakh in the 11th Five-year Plan as compared to the Rs 565.56 lakh for the 10th Five Year plan. The dairy department will stress on providing modern and professional training, registration of milching animals, better quality of milk, feed and fodder, hybrid artificial insemination, timely marketing information to the milk producers and to help entrepreneurs to obtain bank loans, he assured.

Ranike said that the dairy training centre at Chatamali village has launched a unique one-year dairy technology diploma course in collaboration with IGNOU besides other six monthly and short-term dairy training courses.

More than 800 youth and farmers had been trained by this centre last year.

The trainees from neighbouring states like Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Bihar had also contacted this centre for taking admissions in training courses, he added.

The minister disclosed that the Punjab government had already allotted Rs 40 lakh to construct a hostel for the trainees to reside in.

He also promised to provide more facilities at the centre and asked the department to develop it as a modern complex for providing ultra-modern training facilities.

He asked the unemployed youth not to run after government jobs but to adopt the profitable alternative profession.

Heading: In Panchkula, CCTVs on, connection ‘gone’ - Indian Express
Content:
After three years of trial, three accused of murder were awarded life imprisonment in the case. Additional District and Sessions judge, R S Attri on Saturday pronounced the quantum of sentence to Mewa Ram, Sucha Ram and Darshan Singh.

The court had convicted them four days ago under Section 302 and 201 of the Indian Penal Code, whereas Raj Kumar and Maheshi were acquitted in the case.

According to the prosecution, the police had recovered a mutilated body from a jungle near the Sector-39 grain market on the complaint of one Tinku.

The complainant turned hostile during the trial. The body had injury marks caused by a sharp-edged weapon. The word "Raju" was tattooed on the victim's hand but nobody turned up to claim the body.

During the trial, witness Jagtar Singh, who claimed to be a local BJP leader, stated that Mewa Ram and Sucha Ram had made judicial confession before him that they had committed the crime.

The police had arrested five members of the sansi tribe in the case citing illicit relations with a woman of their tribe as a motive behind the murder.

The police had arrested four brothers -- Sucha Singh, Raj Kumar, Darshan Singh and Maheshi -- living in a nearby orchard immediately after the crime. Mewa Ram was arrested later.

Another prosecution witness, Yusuf Khan confessed before the police that he had seen the victim with the accused a night before he was found murdered.

Though he had claimed to the police he knew all the accused, he failed to identify any of them. But going by the witnesses and circumstantial evidences, the court had found the three of them guilty.

The police, however, could not prove the role of the other two in the crime, therefore, they were acquitted.

Heading: Third-party intervention in Kashmir not acceptable: Pranab - Indian Express
Content:
On December 22 last year, Panchkula became the second city in the region after Delhi to install Close Circuit Television (CCTVs) cameras at some of the busiest traffic lights and roundabouts to check violations.

A year later, Newsline found that the CCTVs are connected nowhere. With no monitors attached, the cameras turned out to be mere showpieces.

"There are eight traffic lightpoints in Panchkula of which CCTVs were installed at the five busiest points. These are: Majri Chowk in Old Panchkula, Amartex traffic lightpoint, Sector 17/18 point, Mansa Devi Complex T-point and Sector 11/15. The installation of each unit of the CCTV includes four cameras and a digital video recorder at the cost of around Rs 1.5 lakh," said a traffic police officer on condition of anonymity.

"The cameras were installed with the help of a private company. Initially, the monitors of each unit of the CCTVs were temporarily kept at the corners meant for the PCR vans. After some time, all the monitors were shifted. Where were they later installed is a mystery for all," added the official.

The drive was conducted under the supervision of former DSP (Headquarters) Abhey Rao and no one from the traffic branch was told where the monitors were taken, the traffic police officer said.

An official at the traffic branch of the police department said the monitors for various CCTVs are at the District Inspectors (DI) office in Sector 1. Balwant Rai, the DI, said: "Neither do I have any monitors of the various CCTVs of the city in my office nor was I informed about it by my predecessor when were they installed. They might be at the police control room."

At the Panchkula police control room, officials were ignorant and another said requesting anonymity: "Why would the police control room have monitors for the traffic police' CCTVs. They will be with the traffic branch. No supervision for the same is either done from the SP's room or the police control room. We were, in fact, told that the monitors for the same are at the Sector-5 police station."

Sector-5 Station House Officer Ajit Singh denied that the police station was monitoring the cameras of the traffic branch.

While Sandeep Khirwar, Panchkula Superintendent of Police, is on a 15-day vacation, DSP (Headquarters) Rajesh Kalia, who is handling the charge in Khirwar's absence, was also unaware about the monitoring of the CCTVs.

Talking to Newsline, DSP Kalia said: "To my knowledge, the monitoring of the CCTVs was first done from the Sector-5 police station and has now been shifted to the District Inspector's office."

Heading: CFL collects samples from Salboni blast site - Indian Express
Content:
External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee on Saturday said that India will not accept any third-party intervention in Kashmir. Without specifically naming anyone, Mukherjee stressed that India considers the Kashmir issue as strictly bilateral, which can be resolved through dialogue between New Delhi and Islamabad.

He was speaking on the sidelines of a curtain-raiser for the forthcoming summit of Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technological and Economic Cooperation in Kolkata.

"We consider Kashmir to be a bilateral issue. Both countries are taking steps to resolve it," said Mukherjee.

He was reacting to a question on US President-elect Barak Obama's comment that he wants former President Bill Clinton as an emissary to resolve the Kashmir issue. Mukherjee said India considers the Shimla Agreement and the subsequent Lahore Agreement as the basis for resolving the Kashmir problem.

"The two agreements will pave the way for solving the issue," he said. On Obama's comments about reducing the outsourcing numbers during his election campaign, Mukherjee said, India will decide what to do, as and when the situation demands.

"Let the US first reduce its outsourcing numbers and then we will see how it impacts India and the world. We will decide what to do after that," he added.

Heading: Alumni defend BESU - Indian Express
Content: Central Forensic Laboratory officials collected 15 samples from the blast site in Salboni in West Midnapore for testing on Saturday. The samples included splinters and wire parts among other things. The team gave the samples to the CID, which will hand it over to the CFL. Meanwhile, the school students who were detained for questioning on Friday were released by the police. However three persons Sunil Hansda, Bhagabat Hansda and Sunil Mandi were not released. Senior police officers, including IG West Bengal Kuldeep Singh, interrogated them. Meanwhile, the Jharkhand Party (Naren) has alleged that the police are harassing its members on the issue. Party leaders said that Bhagabat, a party member, has been falsely implicated in the case.

Heading: BESU students held by police are IC followers - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when Bengal Engineering and Science University (BESU) is facing tough times, university alumni came to its defence at a meeting with the members of the National Board of Accreditation (NBA).

After instances of violence on the campus, the authorities had asked the undergraduate students to vacate the hostel on November 6. A 14-member team of the NBA had an interaction with some alumni and recruiters on Saturday on the state of affairs.

Although not more than a dozen recruiters and alumni were present, the NBA team asked the alumni their views on the matter.

"The unrest on the campus is just a reflection of what is happening outside," said a senior alumnus, adding that the institute attracts the best students and faculty.

"It was an important interaction with the members of the committee," said Achyut Ghosh, a 1961 batch student.

Representatives of companies like Tata Consultancy Services, M N Dastur and Company, and McNally Bharat Engineering attended the meeting.

Heading: Fate of PTTI students hangs in balance - Indian Express
Content:
Eight students of Bengal Engineering and Science University (BESU), who have been remanded in judicial custody till November 11, are supporters of the Independent Consolidation (IC).

The IC student faction is crying hoarse over the fact that members of the Students' Federation of India (SFI) were also held by the police for creating violence on the campus but they were let off.

"The students were booked under Section 353 of the IPC for preventing a public servant from doing his duty along with several other charges," said Gautam Bhang, counsel of the students. Sporadic instances of clashes between the two groups have been occurring on the campus since November 4.

DSP (Town) Anjan Chakraborty was injured in a clash with the students in front of the main administrative building at 11 am on November 6.

The police said since the students had attacked an officer, they have been booked under such charges. The university authorities asked the students to leave campus on November 6.

"Students are facing charges," said IC representative Rajorshri Dutta.

Heading: GJM begins stir for Tamang’s exit - Indian Express
Content:
Notwithstanding assurances by Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee in October that the stalemate over the Primary Teachers Training Institutes (PTTIs) would be resolved in 10 days, no solution seems to be in sight. The situation has only worsened after the alleged attack on the car of state School Education Minister Partha De by protesting students at Bishnupur in Bankura on Friday.

Meanwhile, the 11 students who were detained in connection with the incident were produced in a court, which sent them to judicial custody till November 17.

The state government had tried to put the ball in the Centre's court with the Chief Minister writing to Union Minister Pranab Mukherjee, asking him to mediate so that there is an early solution to the crisis. De had also made rounds of the National Council of Teachers Education (NCTE) and the Ministry of Human Resource Development last month without much success.

According to sources, the primary education department is facing a shortage of 40,000 teachers. Earlier, the Calcutta HC had declared the certificates issued by 122 PTTIs in the state invalid, and had asked the government to return the fees of those not completing their courses.

A student leader had sought written assurance from the government that the PTTI students will be absorbed.

Heading: Nandigram becomes focal point in state politics again - Indian Express
Content:
The Darjeeling hills are on the boil again as the Gorkha Janamukti Morcha (GJM) has started its agitation against All India Gorkha League (AIGL) leader Madan Tamang. Over 10,000 student supporters of the GJM on Saturday gheraoed Tamang's house for hours and demanded he should quit state politics.

Darjeeling Superintendent of Police Rahul Srivastava said: "Students gheraoed Tamang's house in Darjeeling. Later, they held a rally at the Chowk Bazar. We have made extensive security arrangements at Tamang's residence and AIGL party office. The situation is tense but under control." According to the police, over 50 personnel, including senior officers, were posted near Tamang's house to prevent any untoward incident.

Tamang had alleged that GJM chief Bimal Gurung had 'sold out' the non-cooperation movement launched by the Morcha. Subsequently, the GJM had set November 7 as the deadline for Tamang to prove his allegations.

Heading: Buddha foresees bleak future for countries that fail to board globalisation bus - Indian Express
Content:
Nandigram has once again become the focal point in Bengal politics. While the CPM is determined to keep Nandigram constituency under the Left Front's control in the Assembly by-elections to be held in December, the Trinamool Congress is also eyeing the seat.

For Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee, grabbing Nandigram is a prestige issue, as her party had wrested several seats from the Front in the recent panchayat elections.

CPM central committee member Mohammad Salim and State Transport Minister Subhas Chakraborty will attend an election rally at Nandigram on Sunday, a day before Banerjee's visit to the area.

A few weeks ago, Banerjee had announced that she would visit Nandigram. Soon, the CPM decided to send its leaders to the area. The December by-election is crucial for the CPM, as a victory here can wipe out the bad memories of defeat during panchayat polls.

Though the CPI, a Front constituent, won the Nandigram constituency in the 2006 Assembly polls, the ruling CPM may find it tough to retain the seat this time.

Sheikh Illias Mohammad, who won the seat twice in 2006 and 2001 Assembly polls, has recently resigned following his alleged involvement in a bribery case. Assembly Speaker Hasim Abdul Halim had ordered an inquiry into Illias' involvement in the bribery case, which was telecast by a private television channel. The investigation is still on.

CPI State Secretary Manju Kumar Majumdar said that his party will contest the seat this time too. But the CPM is worried about the outcome of the by-election as the government's move to set up the state's first SEZ at Nandigram faced stiff resistance.

In fact, Nandigram has proved to be a major blow to Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's plan to industrialise the state.

The Indonesia-based Salim Group was to set up a SEZ there, but due to stiff opposition from the Trinamool on the issue of land acquisition for the proposed SEZ, the government had to shelve its plan.

Not only Nandigram, the CPM and its allies also lost the East Midnapore zilla parishad seat to the Trinamool in the May panchayat elections.

According to sources in both the parties, Banerjee will try to convince the Nandigram electorate about her party's success in preventing the state government from acquiring land for the proposed SEZ.

The CPM, meanwhile, will try to highlight Banerjee's agitation at Singur, which compelled Ratan Tata to shift the Nano factory to Gujarat.

Heading: Encephalitis claims two more lives, but health minister sees no reason to panic - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee came out strongly in support of globalisation and went to the extent of saying that countries that fail to include themselves in the process are bound to be doomed.

"Globalisation is a must. Any country that chooses not to be part of globalisation is bound to be doomed," he said.

He was speaking at a curtain-raiser ceremony for the forthcoming summit of Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technological and Economic Cooperation in Kolkata.

Bhattacharjee, who has always been known to be the liberal face of the CPM, had earlier supported globalisation in stark contrast to the party line. In fact, a number of CPM leaders had blamed globalisation for the prevailing financial crisis in the country.

Bhattacharjee said that one has to bear the fallouts of a global crisis and India cannot be left out. Developing nations should come together to tide over the situation, he said.

Earlier, External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee said at the summit that India was looking forward to some favourable steps from the developed nations to tide over the global financial crisis.

"We are looking forward to the deliberations to be held by the G-20 member countries later this month," Mukherjee said.

He expressed the need to impress upon the developed nations that the present global meltdown is not only related to financial institutions and bankers, but is directly linked to the development of the country.

The matter is also likely to come up at a conference of foreign ministers of BIMSTEC member nations from November 11. India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, Myanmar, Thailand and Bangladesh are members of BIMSTEC.

A summit of leaders of the countries will begin in New Delhi from November 13.

Mukherjee stressed on the close cooperation among the BIMSTEC nations, adding that India wants to focus on the issue.

"We have already adopted the 'Look East' policy through which we want to develop trade ties with countries in East Asia," he said, adding that BIMSTEC, which was formed on June 6, 1997, could prove vital in the development of member countries.

Heading: And miles to go before I sleep... - Indian Express
Content:
Japanese Encephalitis and viral encephalitis have claimed two more lives in the state.

Mithu Pal, a resident of Sonarpur in South 24-Parganas, succumbed to Japanese Encephalitis in the National Medical College on Friday night. This is the second life that the disease has claimed in the state.

The first to fall victim to this dreaded disease was one Pralay Choudhury, a resident of Behala, at the School of Tropical Medicine. Even though Japanese Encephalitis has a high fatality rate, the state Health Department did not give special attention to the affected areas.

Abdul Khaleq, a resident of Bishnupur in South 24-Parganas, died of viral encephalitis at the National Medical College on Saturday.

"I have received reports of two deaths from the National Medical College. I am yet to receive the medical reports," said Sachhidananda Sarkar, Chief Medical Officer, Health, South 24-Parganas.

A hospital official confirmed that two persons from the district have died of the diseases. At a time when there has been an increase in vector-borne disease related deaths, the state Health Department has warned people not to be complacent. It also believes the situation is not as serious as previous years. The state health minister is blaming global warming for the spurt in vector-borne diseases.

"The World Health Organisation has said that global warming has resulted in a change in the profile of various diseases and that this change will lead to an increase in diseases in tropical countries. After all, mosquitoes do not adhere to borders," said Health Minister Surjya Kanta Mishra.

According to Mishra, while malaria had killed 76 people in the state last year, 146 had succumbed to it in 2006. This year, the toll has been 81.

"The previous year's data on the number of deaths indicate that the situation this year is not that grave. One should not press the panic button yet," said Mishra. The minister stressed on early detection and prompt treatment besides underlining the need to generate awareness among people and government officials.

According to him, the department is carrying out regular "audits" on deaths due to vector-borne diseases as and when reported.

Malaria claims one life in New Alipore: One Rajesh Mallick (30) of ward no. 81 in New Alipore died of malaria on Saturday. He had been admitted to MR Bangur Hospital on Thursday where doctors confirmed malignant malaria. He was referred to the National Medical College and Hospital on Saturday morning, where he breathed his last.

Heading: Paperweight - Indian Express
Content:
Gopal Mahapatra has been helping the needy in East Midnapore district. Mohana Dam finds out more

He was barely nine years old when he left his home. A long journey of experiencing life through the eyes of a chaa boy, a shoe polish man, a muri wala, and a wholesale rice seller, Gopal Mahapatra has learnt how to live life to the full: by doing a little service for those who need it the most.

Over the years Gopal became an established businessman. He donates almost Rs 40 lakh every year on causes which might otherwise seem to be unnecessary to many. The amount is a fair share of what he earns to support his livelihood and family. Yet he claims that the satisfaction he derives by donating the money is much more than what he gets by earning it.

Born in a small hamlet of Bishnupur in East Midnapore district of West Bengal, Gopal fled from his home after he was forbidden to watch jatras in his village. Life has made him a mature person, though. From an impulsive kid he has grown into a responsible youth with a family. But what has not changed in him is his desire to extend a helping hand to the needy.

The memory that still remains vivid in his mind is the picture of his ailing grandfather who from the time Gopal knew him had visual problems. Seeing the pain his grandfather bore and the manner in which grandpa used to touch his grandson's face to feel his presence, perhaps led Gopal to take up the initiative of providing eye care to the people in his hometown. For the past five years Gopal, with a team of well-wishers, has been holding eye camps for cataract operation and free distribution of spectacles in Tamluk, Egra, Digha and Contai.

After taking permission and help from the state health department, Gopal has gone a long way to finance 370 operations in the first year, 600 operations in the second, 800 operations in the third and fourth year respectively. Last year he distributed 8,000 spectacles among those having eye problems. He has vowed to carry on with his efforts for eye treatment every year.

Whenever Gopal steps in his village from his city home in Tollygunge, he is mobbed by many from his district who come with their financial problems seeking redressal. From tumour operation to other health issues, Gopal has borne the financial burden of all those who are stricken by poverty.

Among the long list of Gopal's selfless interests is his efforts to distribute books to schools which send a request to him highlighting the urgency and need for books. Everytime there is a requirement in some of the schools of East Midnapore, there is this person ready to donate.

Apart from health and academic services, Gopal has also built a house next to the Tarapith temple. Gopal recalls how everytime he visits the temple he finds beggars eating bhog from the floor.

Gopal spent Rs 10 lakh for the building next to the Tarapith temple in his mother's memory where at present hundreds of beggars eat their bhog and the place is given to the poor for the purpose of marriage, funeral and yagna. During the recent floods in Midnapore, he spent days with the families of those who were affected and chipped in with Rs 2,000 for each of the families who received Rs 6,000 from the state government to reconstruct their flattened homes.

Endless are his services for the poor which started from his very childhood when he used to take away rice from home and give it to the poor in his village. The samaritan believes that there are still many promises that he needs to keep and many a mile he needs to go before he calls it a day.

Heading: Cops beat up man in Jhansi - Indian Express
Content:
For the members of the railway colony in Sodepur, Sundays are a little different. Every Sunday morning, a few residents of the locality gather together, take along a cycle van and collect old newspapers from different doors. Accompanying the adults is a group of children. The adults in the colony have come together to form a small organisation called Our Eyes that collects old newspapers from the residents, sells them and buys school textbooks, which are then distributed to the poor children in the locality.

The idea, says Ambarish Nath Biswas, one of the members, is to make a difference in the lives of underprivileged children who want to study.

"We realised that most of the parents had little clue on the need for school textbooks. Many would buy just a single book for one academic year and would thrash their children when they asked for more. So we decided that we would collect money to buy these books so that the children can continue studying," says Biswas. Most of the children are from the neighbourhood and their parents are daily wage earners.

The adults of the neighbourhood are accompanied by their children on these weekly rounds, so that they understand the significance of money and the importance of not wasting the pages of their textbooks.

"Our children are privileged since they know that whenever they run out of stationery or books we will always buy them more. Yet there are children in their neighbourhood who cannot afford these and have to sell newspapers to study," says Biswas. At least in this colony, there is almost a utopian coexistence of the privileged and the underprivileged children, where they play and study together.

Apart from textbooks, the money is also spent on buying stationery. Yet, the idea is not merely to give the underprivileged children a proper education; it is to give them a normal childhood. That is why a tutor who conducts handwriting improvement classes has agreed to allow five underprivileged children into his class free of cost. When the children of the colony are sent to a dance instructor she is roped in to teach a few poor children too — free of cost.

The enterprise may be merely a year old but the signs of improvement in a few lives can already be seen. Adults claim that many of the children have already shown a remarkable improvement in their studies. Moreover, encouraged by the small group, many others, like the principal of a local school, have pledged their support to them by giving them their old test papers instead of selling them to scrap dealers. Many others have started giving free tuitions to these children, and there are plans to open classes to encourage them to take up extra-curricular activities like singing and dancing.

With 400 kg of newspapers collected from over 130 homes, the lives of nearly 140 children have changed.

"What we do may seem like a small gesture. But there is a bigger perspective behind it. It is not merely to help in the education of a few children, but also to change the mindsets and lives," says Ujjal Gangopadhyay, another member.

Encouraged by them, many of their friends have already set up similar ventures in places like Madhyamgram and North Bengal, and they have all been equally successful. Gangopadhyay makes it clear that they do not want money — all they want is old newspapers. For the smaller children like Sabarni Nath Biswas, Subhodeep Basak, Kinsuk Mukherjee and Ranjabati Rai, however, it is a chance to make a small difference in the lives of those they call their friends.

Heading: NGO to educate girls from minority communities - Indian Express
Content: An Agra-based trader was allegedly beaten up by a group of unidentified policemen in plain clothes at the Jhansi railway station on Friday. The victim had lodged a case of loot against some personnel of the Railway Protection Force (RPF) four years ago and had come to attend the hearing in the matter at the Jhansi court on Friday. Circle Officer (CO) GRP Jhansi Janardan Chaubey said: "The victim, Rajesh Kumar, has alleged that the assailants wanted to threaten him. He was about to leave the station after reaching Jhansi when some persons assaulted him. He is a dealer of leather goods in Agra."
