Chaubey said the injury marks on victim's body were evident and it appeared that some GRP personnel were involved in the attack. It was, however, yet to be verified if the attack was sequel to the old dispute with the RPF men, the CO said.

Heading: Now, I-cards for kids of labourers - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 600 girls belonging to Scheduled Castes and

minority communities will be provided education by Mahila Samakya, an NGO supported by the Union Ministry of Human Resource Development. The NGO will run six Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) in six districts of the state from November 14. These residential schools will not just educate the girls, but will also give them vocational training. The KGBVs were inaugurated in the state capital on Saturday. The new KGBVs will run in Balrampur (city block, Sadar block), Saharanpur (Deoband city block), Bulandshahr (Jehangirabad city block), Shrawasti (Ikauna block) and Sitapur (Parsendi block). State project director of Mahila Samakya, Dr Rashmi Sinha, said the NGO runs 27 KGBVs in 17 districts of the state.

Heading: To counter competition, LDA gets tech-savvy - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh government will provide Migratory Cards to children whose parents and who themselves are working in the unorganised sector as migratory labourers.

The cards will be given under the Education For All (EFA) scheme with the help of the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (UNICEF).

To provide education to migratory children in the state capital, a database will be prepared. It will contain essential details like educational profile of a students and details of his or her family.

Migratory children, who work at various construction and brick kiln sites, are unable to continue their study as they are forced to migrate to different locations. The Migratory Cards will help in keeping track of these students and enable them to continue their studies across the state.

If a student migrates to some other district and wishes to continue with his studies after a certain gap, the district officer will keep a track of that as well.

"Officials of the district, from which the child has migrated, will inform the officials of the other district where the child has moved to. This will help in keeping the track of their movement and their studies will not suffer," said the official.

"These Migratory Cards are being planned for the children studying between Class I and VIII. Under 'Education For All' scheme, all the children are entitled to get education.

However, there are many migratory students who have to leave their studies midway as they have to earn a living.

"Migration Cards will provide the relevant information about the children. Such children will be identified from various construction and brick kiln sites," said a senior EFA official.

"The task of making Migratory Cards has been assigned to the UNICEF. While the cards were made for around 150 migrant children last year, we are planning to cover the migrant children in all the districts this year," said Ruchi Mishra, District Coordinator, Lucknow.

Heading: Cops identify robber gunned down last week - Indian Express
Content:
To compete with private constructors, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) has decided to upgrade its technology in its future housing schemes.

According to LDA officials, the body has decided to develop earthquake, fire-resistant and water-proof houses. It will equip its upcoming multi-storeyed buildings with advanced construction technologies.

The LDA has constituted a six-member technical committee, headed by LDA chief engineer (civil), to list all such technologies and work out modalities for their implementation.

Other than the chief engineer (civil), the committee comprises chief engineer (electronics), joint director (land acquisition and development), head of department of civil engineering and head of department of earthquake engineering -- both from Indian Institute of Technology-Roorkee.

LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram has directed the committee members to start work on the assignment and submit recommendations within a month. The recommendations will be tabled at the next meeting of the LDA Board for approval.

In its October 13 meeting, the LDA Board had decided to develop only houses and multi-storeyed apartments and no plots in the future.

The decision was taken citing findings of a survey, which reported that thousands of plots were lying vacant and undeveloped even after 15 years of allotment. Property dealers had purchased these only for investment purposes, while those who really needed accommodation were suffering, Meshram said.

In his latest order, Meshram said that due to the poor construction work in housing schemes, people have become suspicious about their quality. Nehru Enclave, Awadh Apartment, EWS Houses of Vinamra Khand and Vastu Khand are few LDA housing schemes, which were unsuccessful due to poor construction work.

Meshram added that the technologies LDA is using at present are obsolete and hence, it will not be able to meet the expectations of consumers. So, it has become necessary for the body to use advanced construction technologies to compete with private real estate developers.

Heading: Meerut blast: Probe on - Indian Express
Content:
The Lucknow police on Saturday claimed to have identified the man, who was gunned down within an hour of a robbery on Wednesday at the residence of a jeweller in Thakurganj.

The deceased, Bablu alias Prem Nath Kauri, was a resident of Musahibganj, near Thakurganj.

Bablu's mother Uma Devi, however, denied the involvement of his son in the robbery. "The police killed him in a fake encounter. He could not have committed such a crime." The police said the deceased was disowned by his parents one and a half years ago due to his dubious relationship with a woman. "His mother told us that they had disowned him after he started living with a married woman in Bhattamau in Kakori ," Circle Officer (CO) Chowk, Vinay Chandra said.

Incidentally, Bablu did not have a criminal background. "So far, we have not been able to find any criminal case against him. However, his involvement in the case cannot be ruled out," said Chandra.

Heading: Mortar shell blast kills 5 in Meerut - Indian Express
Content:
SSP to find out whether Army had auctioned the mortar shells or the ragpickers had picked them up from the firing range

The DGP Headquarters of Uttar Pradesh has issued

directives to the Meerut police to find out the source from where the ragpickers had got the Army mortar shells that caused the blast in Meerut on Saturday.

On behalf of the headquarters, Inspector General (IG), Law & Order of Uttar Pradesh, BP Singh, said, "The SSP Meerut has been asked to find out if the Army had auctioned the shells or whether the ragpickers had picked them up from the firing-range in the Cantonment."

"If the investigation reveals the shells were amongst those that were auctioned, legal action would be initiated against the concerned contractor. Three of the injured victims, who are battling for life, too, are not in a state to speak about the incident," the IG said.

The ragpickers were hitting the shells with a blunt object without knowing that they were live, when one exploded, killing five and injuring three of them, Singh said.

Deputy Inspector General (DIG) UP Anti-Terror Squad, Rajiv Krishna, said, "The Meerut wing of the squad has gone to the spot to get a first-hand account of the incident. Primary investigation reveals that the shells were a part of the scrap ordnance of the army."

The DIG said that usually a few of the shells fired at the firing range in the Cantonment go missing and the ragpickers take them away.

"They take out the brass covers of the shells and sell them to the scrap dealers. Five such shells were recovered from the spot," said Krishna.

Heading: Come one, come all - Indian Express
Content:
Five persons, including four children, were killed when a mortar shell exploded in Ashiana colony's slum area under Lisari Gate Police circle in Meerut, on Saturday afternoon. The incident occurred when some ragpickers struck the shell to extract metal (brass) from it.

An accidental case has been lodged by the father of one of the deceased at the Lisari gate police station.

Seven injured have been admitted at the PL Sharma District Hospital and Medical College. The police said doctors had informed them that condition of two of the injured persons was critical.

Superintendent of Police, Meerut, Raghubeer Lal, said, "It is suspected that ragpickers had brought mortar shells from the Army shooting range in the cantonment area. They were stricking the shell with a hammer to extract metal (brass) when it exploded."

According to the police, on Saturday afternoon around 3.50 pm, residents of the slum area heard a loud deafening sound coming from one of the makeshift houses. When they reached the spot, they found bodies scattered on the ground. The police, who rushed to the site, took the injured to the hospital. Six live mortar shells were recovered from the site.

"All injured and deceased are natives of Assam and had been living in that area for a long time," added Lal. Sources said the population strength of the area where the incident occurred is around 5,000.

Inspector General (Meerut zone) Gurudarshan Singh said, "It was an accident and had no links with any terror activities". He added that they are planning to create awareness in the area and would request residents to avoid breaking any solid material without taking prior permission. "We would also talk to Army officials in this regard," he added.

The deceased have been identified as Sober Ali (16), Saedul Ali (10), Ejaz Ali (16), Izabul (12) and Mushrraf (20).

The injured are Habizul Rehman (11), Okia (3), Amir Ali (10), Sukhman (15), Kamela Bano (24), Mamta Bano (23) and Shaznal Jamal (7).

Meanwhile, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati has announced financial aid for the Meerut blast victims. The Chief Minister announced Rs 1 lakh for the relatives of each of the adult deceased and Rs 50,000 for the minor ones. A compensation of Rs 30,000 has been declared for each of the injured. She also directed the district administration to provide proper medical attention to the injured persons.

Heading: Heady mix - Indian Express
Content:
James Bond doesn't charm women alone; even the men can't hold back their admiration for the world's favourite spy. The Quantum of Solace premier at PVR Juhu saw a turnout that can make a Yash Raj Film premier look dull. Comprising the creamiest were Imran Khan and girlfriend Avantika Malik, Suzanne Khan, Shefali and Vipul Shah, Mandira Bedi, Atul Agnihotri, Rohit Roy, Maria Goretti, Azharuddin and Sangeeta Bijlani, Satish Kaushik, Shauna Chauhan and Bikram Saluja, Niharika Bhasin and Ayub Khan, Mugdha Godse and Nethra Raghuraman.

Bummer The always-charming-but-a-tad-boring Imran looked stunning until one glanced at his legs — he wore shiny black pants.

Heading: Be well - Indian Express
Content:
Roberto Bava talks of wine's grand love affair with music

Italian wine-maker Roberto Bava resembles a doctor scribbling a prescription as he jots down combinations of wine and music on a slip of paper— "Adagio for Stradivari, Ennio for Barolo, Gavi di Gavi for contemporary composers". But he's not rigid.

He's just a passionate about his wine, and his music.

Bava and his brothers were born into a family of wine-makers. Pioneers in the Barbera variety of local grape, the Bavas are known for such revolutionary wines like the Rosetta, the Stradivario and the Barolo — a sought after brand in the international wine market. The distinctive labels of the Stradivario or the 'Piedmont Super-Barolo' are testaments to the new way of winemarketing pioneered by the latest generation of Bavas. Borrowing the name from the legendary Stradivarius violins known for their fine wood that give them the unique sound, the Bavas take similar care to make their wine barrels. "If you see a double bass on the label, you know that it's a richer, heavier vintage," says Bava, interpreting their very successful marketing technique. "It's our way of combining culture with wine. We don't like to boast about the quantity of our produce. Then it becomes just an object, and wine for us is more than that."

Inspired by Keith Jarret's 1979 performance at the Montreal Jazz festival, Bava returned to his native Asti, in the Piedmont region of Italy, with a grand idea. "At that time my father was restoring one of our older cellars. My brother and I asked him to let us host classical music concerts in the cellar," he recalls.

Musicians performed for entire days at their cellars and kept trying different wines. As the day progressed, the musicians identified certain compositions or instruments with certain wines. "If you propose this to a mathematician, he will rubbish it. So it's obviously not mathematical. And how many people in the world understand mathematics?" he shrugs. But the wine connoisseur takes pride in his grape-pickers who can "tell you the exact temperature and rainfall that contributed to a particular vintage from any year," he beams.

Bava's wine estate boasts of a steady stream of musicians performing classical and jazz music at their vineyard, which now has two dedicated jazz halls.

In India through Finewinesmore, a wine promoter, to judge the India Wine Challenge in Delhi next week, and to promote his wine, Bava regrets the elitism attached to wine consumption in India. "My own wine is too expensive for me to afford here. I hope that changes in future."

Heading: Green Ludhiana still 3 months away - Indian Express
Content:
Nisha Javeri explains why her spa has everyone gushing

The entrance to the Myrah Spa in Juhu sets you in the right frame of mind for a relaxing spa treatment — a miniature fountain, a small Thai Buddha statuette and the scent of jasmines and roses. Inside, waiting is the charming hostess Nisha Javeri, who has just launched her spa's latest menu — the Royal Aura Signature Menu. Javeri is busy looking after her guests which include some famous faces like Rita Dhody, Lata Patel, Maria Goretti, Madhoo, Sandhya Mridul and Mini Mathur. Still she takes time out to talk about her spa and her personal wellness philosophy.

"It's a very luxurious set of treatments that we have introduced here," says Javeri, "We've used the most extravagant ingredients like chocolate, caviar, gold and diamonds to give people the best possible treatments." But do such obviously expensive packages work? She smiles and says, "That's what makes these treatments the ultimate in spa experiences. They're very, very effective and we have the research to back it up."

And what about ancient treatises that tell us about the benefits of certain herbs and fruits or even myths like Cleopatra's famous goat's milk baths? "We definitely don't offer Ayurvedic treatments here, if that's what you mean," Javeri says. Then she adds, "All our products and treatments are completely natural. We've tied up with Ainhoa, a European professional cosmetics company which specialises is spa products . They have come out with a whole range of products which are natural, result-oriented and they make you look, feel and smell divine."The guests who have tried out her latest treatments can't stop raving about them. "I just tried the vinotherapy massage and it's so luxurious. You can see it in my face. I have never felt so rejuvenated and relaxed in my life," says model Shonali Nagrani. "Next, I'm coming here to try the Choco Almond massage."

Myrah's motto is one of 'Divine wellness' and Javeri says she's made that motto a part of her life as well. "I think my whole lifestyle speaks for my commitment to wellness. I don't abuse my body by smoking or drinking, I practice yoga and I regularly detox. And I don't just believe in physically healing the body. Mental and spiritual wellness are just as important," she says, before rushing off to play hostess again. And as she ushers in more guests and graciously poses for photographs, you can't help but see the satisfaction she radiates. That is wellness, indeed.

Heading: For speedy disposal of cases, mediation centre opens up in city - Indian Express
Content:
Plantation drive postponed till February 2009 as MC fails to take timely decision on purchase of tree guards

In an effort to make the city clean and green, the plantation drive of the Ludhiana Municipal Corporation has been delayed by a year. Reason: the Finance and Contract Committee (F&CC) of the corporation took almost a year to take a unanimous decision on purchasing tree guards.

In the recently held meeting, the committee members approved the demand for tree guards but the Horticulture branch has specified that they will be planting saplings next February as this is not the right time to start the plantation drive.

The municipal corporation plans to spend Rs 60 lakh on the purchase of tree guards.

According to the plans of the Municipal Corporation, the drive was to be carried out in February this year but due to increase in the prices of steel, the MC could not take a final decision on purchasing tree guards.

"With the steel prices spiralling southwards in the recent times, MC has decided to purchase tree guards. We are hopeful of carrying out this drive in February next year on the main approach road, inner lanes so as to keep Ludhiana clean and green," said a horticulture expert.

However, the MC claims to have planted 30,000 saplings in parks and main roads without tree guards.

However, the condition of a majority of trees is in a bad shape as some of them are drooping while others have been uprooted.

Many plants have dried up on the Pakhowal Road and Barewal Road due to lack of proper watering.

"Mere plantation is not necessary, its upkeep is also important. On the main roads, the MC is responsible for their maintenance while in the inner colonies, the area residents should also take care of the plantation. However, it seems that most of the plants are nobody's baby and hence can be seen in a bad condition," said a city resident.

J S Bilga, executive engineer in the Horticulture department said that saplings are in a good condition. "The rest of the plantation will be done after using tree guards which will protect plants," he said.

Heading: From coach to speech therapist, this woman from Pakistan has done it all - Indian Express
Content:
To reduce the burden of pending cases on courts and to relieve litigants, as many as 19 mediation and conciliation centres have been set up in the courts of Punjab and Haryana. One such centre was inaugurated at the District Courts here today.

Justice S B Sinha of the Supreme Court today inaugurated these centres through video conferencing along with Justice T S Thakur, Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court at Chandigarh.

The new centres will function at Jalandhar, Ludhiana, Sangrur, Amritsar, Hoshiarpur, Ferozepur, Patiala, Faridkot at Moga districts courts in Punjab and Faridabad, Gurgaon, Rohtak, Sonepat, Jind, Karnal, Kurukshetra, Rewari and Hisar districts courts in Haryana.

In Ludhiana, this centre has been set up in room number 15-A in the judicial court complex building on the third floor.

Giving details, the District and Sessions Judge and Chairman District Legal Services Authority G K Rai said Additional District and Session Judge Kishore Kumar and Civil Judge Randhir Verma will act as mediators in the centre.

Rai further said that 173 cases have been referred by various courts, out of them 128 were taken up on the first day. The judge said that this centre will try to resolve these cases with the mutual consent of the concerned parties within 90 days.

He said that in this centre, the cases relating to civil suits, matrimonial disputes, Motor Accident and Claims Tribunal (MACT) cases and cheque bounce cases will be settled with mutual consent of the parties involved. He said people should bring their cases in the Mediation and Conciliation Centre for speedy disposal of their cases. Rai further said the centre will not only provide speedy justice to litigants, but also help in reducing the pendency of cases.

Other judicial officers and the members of the District Bar Association (DBA) were also present on the occasion.

Heading: Advani to open IMC conference today - Indian Express
Content:
For the past two decades, she has been serving special children in her city. After her postgraduation in Botany and in special education, she started working as special educator at the National Special Education Centre in Islamabad.

From an athletics coach to a speech therapist, she has done it all.

Meet Rukhenaz, a Pakistani coach, who is accompanying a group of 37 special children from different schools across Pakistan to participate in the 11th Punjab State Special Olympics being held at Guru Nanak Public School in the city.

"Special children need special attention. You love them and they will reciprocate the feelings. I share a wonderful bond with these children. My three college going sons also volunteer their services for them. My sons help these students in learning different games and has helped prepare them for these Olympics."

Rukhenaz, who has been to many countries to attend specialised training programmes, said, "Children are alike all across the world. They are innocence personified. In Pakistan, we have specialised courses for these kids along with practical works. But the teaching method resembles India."

"Visiting Ludhiana is like home coming for me. As my father belongs to Amritsar and mother belonged to Batala. I will see if I can visit my ancestral village," she concludes.

Heading: Residents irked as shops operate from LIT flats - Indian Express
Content:
Leader of the Opposition Lal Krishn Advani will inaugurate a two-day national conference of the Indian Media Centre (IMC) at Pal Auditorium in Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) on Sunday.

According to IMC Director Shyam Khosla and IMC Punjab Chapter general secretary Dr Harjinder Singh Lall, Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal will be the chief guest on the occasion.

They said that about 125 delegates from across the nation will participate in the conference. Several journalists and editors from across the state are also likely to be a part of the meet. Delegates from different states will be presenting their progress reports during the business session on Sunday, they said.

A seminar on 'Covering Terrorism: Where to draw the line' will be organised on Monday. The key note address would be delivered by Chandan Mitra, Editor of Pioneer and IMC Chairman. A seminar on Citizen Journalism would also be held on the second day. On November 11, the delegates would be taken to Amritsar for a visit to the Golden Temple, Wagha Border and Durgiana Mandir.

Heading: College students protest against fee hike, Gosain assures to resolve the matter - Indian Express
Content:
In a clear violation of a Ludhiana Improvement Trust (LIT) scheme, commercial activity seems to be going on unabated in the high income group (HIG) flats located at Sant Ishar Singh Nagar on the Pakhowal Road.

A resident of the area, Vikas Rekhi, has lodged a complaint with LIT authorities stating that apart from showrooms, a bakery is also operationg from one of the flats. Cream and Crunch is preparing a range of bakery products from the flat, he alleged. Rekhi in his complaint said, "The bakery starts operating in the wee hours of the morning. I am really upset with the noise pollution that is created and moreover, it is a violation of law to run a bakery unit from a residential flat." Interestingly, Rekhi had lodged a complained about a month back and following his complaint, a team had raided the flat on September 24 and found machines running in the flat. In a signed letter, Executive Officer (EO) Avtar Singh Azad had also ordered to disconnect the power connection of the bakery but nothing has been done till date.

PSEB authorities, however, visited the flat on September 25 and the owner was given a week's notice but no action was taken thereafter.

In a recent development, the owner of the flat, Mangal Singh Sandhu has filed a complaint with the NRI cell of the police department stating that Vikas Rekhi is a threat to his and his son Charan Kamal Sandhu's life. In the complaint, however, Sandhu admitted to running a bakery shop in the LIT flats which are meant for residential purposes. He, however, denied setting up a bakery workshop within the same area. Meanwhile, the complainant Vikas Rekhi has asked LIT authorities to take immediate action against the violator for causing nuisance.

Heading: Builder dumps mud on roadside in Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar - Indian Express
Content:
The protests by commerce students of city colleges, against a fee hike, entered its fourth day on Saturday as they sought help from the deputy speaker of the Punjab Legislative Assembly, Satpal Gosain, to sort out the issue.

The protests took a new turn as the deputy speaker assured the students that he will convey their resentment to Prof R C Sobti, Vice-Chancellor of Panjab University, Chandigarh, in order to resolve the issue.

Students of the commerce departments of three colleges including Guru Nanak Khalsa College for Women, Gujarkhan Campus, Model Town, and Gujrawala Guru Nanak Khalsa College, Civil Lines and DD Jain Memorial College for Women, Kidwai Nagar, have registered their resentment in a series of protests in the past few days.

While the students of other colleges relented to comment on the issue after talks with the college management which claimed the hike to have been made at the university level, a group of students of DD Jain College said they were not ready to accept the 'huge fee hike', whether made at the college or university level.

Gosain, meanwhile, said the agitation should end as soon as possible and that he would take up the matter with the PU V-C.

"A group of students came to me today and discussed the problem pertaining to the fee hike (in the second instalment of fees). We are going to take up the matter with university officials as we do not want students to feel overburdened or overcharged," he said.

He further added,

"I accompanied the students and met the college management.

After discussions and seeing the university circular, it was observed that the fee has been raised by the university and not the colleges."

Heading: ‘Govt will revamp education system’ - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar are allegedly upset over the construction of multi-storeyed high income group (HIG) flats by a private builder in the area.

They complained that workers were digging up at the site and the earth being taken out is being kept on roadside in big heaps. Residents also claimed that the rest of the mud is being stored on another 100-feet wide road which may prove to be a threat for commuters.

"The number of cases of dust allergies in the area has increased. Also, the builder is causing nuisance in a residential area," rued Arvind Sharma, a resident.

Meanwhile, it needs to be mentioned that as per rules, the builder is supposed to shift the mud to some other place in closed vehicles without causing any hassle to the area residents. According to sources, the builder is constructing flats for the Ludhiana Improvement Trust (LIT). The trust authorities, however, have not yet directed the builder to shift the heaps of mud from the roadside.

Heading: No respite from dengue, 35 fresh cases reported - Indian Express
Content: The Punjab government has envisaged an ambitious programme to revamp the entire education system to develop state-of-the-art education facilities including three new international-level universities and a number of professional institutes. This was stated by Bikram Singh Majathia Minister for Information and Public Relations, Water and Sanitation, Science and Technology Punjab, while presiding over an annual day function 'Virasat 2008' of Guru Gobind Singh Public School at Guru Nanak Dev Bhawan on Saturday. Majithia said that a new university will set up in Amritsar at a cost of Rs 4000 crore and a central university was coming up at Bathinda.

Heading: Special Olympics  kickstart in city, 350 children to showcase their talent - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 35 fresh cases were added to the official tally of confirmed dengue cases in the district which put the present count at 2,115. There seems to be no end to fresh cases of dengue pouring in at various hospitals across the city.

The number has been steadily swelling with an average of 40 cases being added every day.

On the other hand, the overall number of cases has touched the 3,500 mark with over 400 cases put in the suspected cases category and over 1,000 patients being treated at the hospitals in the city hailing from other parts of the state.

The number of unofficial deaths is also reported to have surpassed the 50 mark. The Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMCH) has reported 32 deaths due to dengue while the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) has also reportedly registered 20 deaths since the disease spread in the district.

Other districts in the state which are also affected are Jalandhar and Patiala. However, more than 70 per cent of the dengue cases have been reported from the district alone, which is the primary reason why a team from the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme visited the city recently to acquire data regarding the spread of the disease.

Heading: Metro rail project: ROW demand struck down - Indian Express
Content:
Child development specialist Tasneema Ghazi has been rewriting texts incorporating science, social studies and history for decades now

She has added 'critical thinking' to the teachings of the Quran and turned the book of Salah (or the daily prayer guide), into an enjoyable learning experience for children.

Meet Dr Tasneema Ghazi, who, after introducing a refreshingly new approach to the teaching style and curricula to Islamic studies in Singapore and the US, has returned home to promote her works here. Tasneema, a masters from the Harvard University, is a specialist in child development at the Chicago-based IQRA' International Education Foundation.

She and her husband Dr Abidullah Ghazi, also a Harvard scholar, are now in Mumbai to establish a scientific, global and comprehensive approach to Islamic studies. "We have already published 25 easy-to-read English books here. These books relate to issues like what is Muslim life and what our holy text preaches. We have integrated it liberally with national history, an Indian perceptive and social and global issues."

The idea came way back in 1967, while the couple was in Harvard. "We realised the texts used in Indian madarsas were not written for children. That's when the idea to write and publish our own books took shape. After 40 years, we are convinced this kind of work takes a lifetime to accomplish," she says.

Tasneema recalls that had it not been for her children, she would never have identified this need. "Back then, there were very few Muslims in the US. We had two children, a girl aged three and a year-old boy and wanted them to have some understanding of the religion. That's when my Christian and Jewish friends told me about Sunday schools and I decided to follow a similar model," she says.

Today, in Singapore, more than 60 imaginative and hands-on titles have already rolled out for students of Grade one to Grade 10. However, for Tasneema, her work has not ended. "It was a progressive process," she says, adding, "I keep reworking texts incorporating a bit of science, social studies and history. Basically, I want students to understand that one cannot separate religion from scientific, social and global issues."

The new Indian books cost Rs 50 and more, which Abidullah feels the average Muslim family here cannot afford. "We are in talks with the ulemas of various madarsas to make the books part of their curriculum. Till then, we plan to introduce them as complementary education," he says.

Farooq Mulla, secretary of mosque/community affairs of the Muslim Council of Britain said: "As of now, these books can't be introduced as mainstream studies in madarsas, but they can be part of complementary studies."

Women pray with men at Haj house
A sense of emancipation was in the air at the Haj House, CST on Saturday afternoon as over 40 men and women assembled in the prayer hall to offer collective namaz. In India, where women are usually barred from praying in public alongside men, this was a movement of sorts that took off due to the efforts of spirited scholars and intellectuals calling for emancipation of women. Talks were also delivered on the second day of the four-day convention to launch Iqra International Women's Alliance (IIWA) in India. "India and Pakistan are the only countries that do not allow women to pray in public. In UK and the US and even the UAE they are allowed to enter mosques. It is indeed a great moment for us to be praying with the men," said Uzma Naheed, president, IIWA. After the 15-minutes prayer, a young girl said, "It gives me a great sense of equality to stand should-to-shoulder with men and offer namaz."

Heading: Slum-dwellers’ dream house? - Indian Express
Content:
Pre-bid meet: Nodal agency refuses 90% right-of-way before start of Charkop-Bandra-Mankhurd corridor work

The consortium constructing the city's first metro rail stretch is yet to get the entire right-of-way (ROW) it requires and now, the nodal agency for the Mumbai Metro Rail Project has struck down the demand of seven business consortia bidding for the Charkop-Bandra-Mankhurd corridor for 90 per cent ROW at the outset of the construction work.

Row is the access given to the contractor to carry out the construction work.

At a pre-bid meeting at Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) headquarters earlier this week, the representatives of the seven in the fray for the contract demanded 90 per cent ROW at the start of the construction of the 32-km corridor to minimise hindrances.

Ratnakar Gaikwad, Metropolitan Commissioner, declined it stating that rehabilitation of Project Affected Persons (PAPs) would be done while the work is in progress, as being done in the case of the Versova-Andheri-Ghatkopar corridor.

"They demanded 90 per cent ROW on the lines of the model concession agreement (MCA), which is yet to be approved. Giving 90 per cent ROW would be impossible and therefore encroachments along the route and at the car depot at Charkop would be settled as the work progresses," Gaikwad told Newsline.

Bidders believe this could lead to several hurdles in construction once work orders are given, causing delays. It was the issue of the ROW handover by the MMRDA to the Reliance Infrastructure Ltd-led consortium that delayed the start of the construction of the 11.2-km Corridor One. Ten months after the Mumbai Metro One Pvt Ltd began the civil construction, the MMRDA is still to resettle PAPs at J P Road, Andheri and hand over the 200 metre stretch near Andheri station on both east and west sides.

MMRDA is still to demolish a hillock at Asalpha and construct a road before handing over a 600 metre stretch to the contractor. Another stretch from Saki Naka to Sarvodaya junction in Ghatkopar was still to be handed over to MMOPL. Contractors are still to start work on a 2.5-km stretch.

When asked whether the ROW issue would cause delays in the second corridor, Gaikwad said even for other large scale projects in the city, encroachments are cleared when the work is in progress.

Though, the MMRDA is still to survey PAPs on the route, the state government has given its clearance to rehabilitate nearly 14,000 displaced families on the 50-hectare car depot land in Charkop.

"We're still to carry out a survey to determine the exact number of PAPs on the stretch," said Dilip Kawathkar, joint project director (public relations).

Gaikwad said, "Most of the corridor would go through the Link Road, so there is no major problem. We expect PAPs in areas like Kurla, Mankhurd, etc." According to a rough estimate, the MMRDA is expecting around 1,500 PAPs, excluding the displaced families at Charkop.

During the pre-bid meeting, MMRDA agreed to the demand of bidders to extend the last date for submission of fiscal bids by 45 days. Gaikwad said the extension of time will not delay the project significantly. The MMRDA had earlier planned to start work on the line two by January end, which will now start in March end. "After the bids are in, selection would take around a month, following which the creation of the special purpose vehicle (SPV) and awarding of civil contract, etc would be done by April. So the actual construction is expected to start by June," Gaikwad added.

So the actual construction is expected to start by June," Gaikwad added.

Heading: Efficient transport system still eludes metro - Indian Express
Content:
Project under BSUP may bring hope for Mandala residents

Ever since she left Guwahati and reached Mumbai ten years ago, Anawari Shaikh has been making houses for others. She is a construction worker who stays in slums frequently uprooted during demolition drives. And now she may own a house herself.

Shaikh is one of the 3,500 families from Mandala slums in Mankhurd living on the fringes for the last four years after their shanties repeatedly came under the bulldozer as part of the state government's slum demolition drive.

Their shanties, built post-1995, had no legal protection to claim right to housing. But in what could be a unique project if approved, these slum-dwellers have submitted a housing project to the central government under the Basic Services for the Urban Poor (BSUP).

BSUP is one of the components of the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM ).

"I have built homes for so many people, I am capable of building a home for my family too," said Anawari who would be among the many slum-dwellers who will work as labourers on the project in case it is approved. Many others would chip in with services as plumbers, carpenters, electricians and the like in a project which will not involve any developer in any way.

The activist group Ghar Banao Ghar Bachao, which has mobilised slum dwellers for the project, has submitted a proposal to the state housing department as well as the Central Urban Poverty Alleviation Ministry, which handles BSUP.

On the direction of the central ministry, the Housing And Urban Development Corporation Ltd has given its report on the feasibility of the project at Mandala.

If approved, half the money for the Rs 156-crore proposal would be given by the centre, 25% by the state and the remaining in equal shares by the urban local body and the community, the slum dwellers in this case. The project aims at 58 four-storeyed buildings as well as balwadis, schools, dispensaries, markets and other civic amenities.

While housing secretary Sitaram Kunte was away and unavailable for comment, D Hadadare, chief engineer for MHADA (the nodal agency for BSUP in Mumbai) said, "Unlike the Slum Rehabilitation Scheme, BSUP doesn't specify any cut-off date as eligibility criteria. However, no other group of slum dwellers from Mumbai has come forward with any community participation proposal under BSUP so far. If it is implemented it would be the first-of-its-kind project."

The land, on which the project is proposed, was reserved for rehabilitating slum dwellers prior to 2000 whose homes were mowed down. "Only about 50 such families have been rehabilitated on that land so far. Of the total 55 acre land, we have asked for 14 acres for the project. The people here are ready to pay whatever price the government demands," said Simpreet Singh from Ghar Banao Ghar Bacho Andolan.

"We are not asking for free houses. Even now, we pay a rent of Rs 1,000 per month for our shanties and another good sum for illegal electricity connection and water supply. We are willing to put in the money and labour if we are allowed to go ahead with the project," said local resident Amravati Chaudhari.

Heading: Now, Anbumani Ramadoss trains gun on junk food, alcohol, drugs - Indian Express
Content:
Ailing undertakings, insufficient bus fleets, infighting among corporations are bottlenecks

Sample the following scenario:

* Thane Municipal Transport (TMT) has 288 buses, of which only 188 run on the road. Of the total, 196 are over 10 years old and must be scrapped. TMT needs 500 more buses for 60 routes.

* Navi Mumbai Municipal Transport (NMMT) has 280 buses, of which 235 run on 33 routes. There is a demand to run more buses on 77 more routes.

Such is the plight of almost all the municipal transport undertakings in the Mumbai Metropolitan region (MMR) which is managed by different corporations. Unlike the Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST), which plans to take its fleet to 4,000 buses by March 2009, other transport units are either ailing or do not have enough money and expertise to run the service. Moreover, despite shortage of buses, many undertakings have many old buses, on the verge of getting scrapped.

The MMR region requires 3,000 more buses. Last week, BEST sent a proposal to the state transport department seeking permission to venture into Thane territory. "We want to operate on all TMT routes," says Uttam Khobragade, General Manager of BEST. To which secretary of the transport department, Ramanath Jha, replies, "The BEST proposal can be worked out."

Currently, apart from the BMC, four municipal corporations — Thane, Navi Mumbai, Kalyan-Dombivli, Mira Bhayander — have their own transport units. However, smaller corporations and councils which still do not have their transport units have to rely on autorickshaws and Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) buses, but that is not enough. The existing services are running at losses, costing the corporations dearly.

So all these transport units have been aiming to provide better services than thinking making profit. Agrees former deputy CM Chhagan Bhujbal, who has been Mumbai mayor, "BEST's transport wing is a loss making unit, but that loss is absorbed by its electricity supply unit."

But not all corporations have such luxury. "Inefficiency, mismanagement and corruption are major reasons which paralyse the transport units," says Khobragade, who has also been managing director of MSRTC. "Plus, indiscipline at large effects in terms of the service and maintenance of the buses," he adds.

"Managing these municipal transports needs expertise, and all corporations lack it," admits deputy speaker of legislative council and former Thane mayor, Vasant Davkhare. Except the BEST and TMT no other corporation or council has a dedicated officer (either an IAS or from state administrative service officer) to manage the affairs. Sadly, despite inadequate fleets, most transports undertaking are opposed to allowing others to venture into their territory.

Heading: Wall collapse at construction site claims 2 lives - Indian Express
Content:
Union Health Minister reiterates stand on homosexuality, says will fight laws that make it illegal

After the smoking ban, Union Health Minister has now shifted his attention to junk food, alcohol and drugs. In the city to lay the foundation stone of the Grant Medical College at JJ hospital, Dr Anbumani Ramadoss also said he would continue his fight to make homosexuality legal.

Speaking at the function, he said, "Apart from tobacco consumption, junk food, alcohol and drugs are also adversely affecting the health of nation. They need to be regulated on priority basis."

"There is a serious impact on the health of young India due to these four elements. Even parents are unaware about the seriousness of the adverse impact on their children. We need to create awareness. The government is working on it," he added.

Ramadoss laid the foundation stone for a new 11-storey college building. The building is part of the 120-crore makeover of the JJ hospital under the first phase of the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY). To make the yet-to-be-inaugurated metro blood bank at JJ hospital the best in the world after Germany, Dr Ramadoss announced an additional Rs 50 crore. "It will be the best in the world like the one in Germany. We have earmarked additional funds for that," said Dr Ramadoss.

The Centre has also awarded Rs 125 crore to the Nagpur Medical College as grant under the second phase of PMSSY to upgrade it to AIIMS standards.

Ramadoss said, "Government hospitals need hospital management and information services. There are pilot project happening across the country, we now need to scale it up to all hospitals."

Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Murli Deora who was present at the function announced Rs 16 crore for a CT scan and MRI machine at St George hospital. "All the patients from all the hospitals in the JJ Group (St George, Cama hospital, GT hospital) refer patients to JJ Hospital's radiology department. That's why there is a wait of 25 days for the patients. The new machine will ease patient load on JJ Hospital and all patients from the other three hospital will be referred to St George," said Dr Pravin Shingare, deputy director, Directorate Medical Education and Research.

GAIL India has also donated Rs 10 crore for cancer treatment at Cama Hospital. "The funds will be used to procure linear accelerator machine for radiotherapy for women and children ailing from cancer," said Deora.

Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh urged the Ramadoss to relax Medical Council of India (MCI) guidelines to start a medical college at St George hospital. According to MCI guidelines, hospital campus should have at least 25 acres to start a medical college but Deshmukh has asked the minister to relax the rule. "If need be we can increase floor space index to two or even three. We'll add additional floors also," he said.

Later in the day, Ramadoss inaugurated A E Kalsekar hospital of Unani Medicine of Anjuman -I- Islam (Charitable Trust) at Andheri. On making homosexuality legal, Dr Ramadoss said he was not giving up his activism on section 377, the section of Indian law, which says homosexuality is illegal.

He said he would approach the Prime Minister for help. Ramadoss has already taken on many of his cabinet colleagues especially Home Minister Shivraj Patil on the issue and has also gone against the government's point of view in the Delhi High Court.

Heading: Question paper goof-up: MU suspends five employees - Indian Express
Content:
Case of causing death by negligence has been registered against the contractors, say cops

A part of the wall of a building at the Matunga railway colony collapsed on Saturday morning, killing two employees of a construction company. The Shahu Nagar Police rushed to the spot after receiving a call and registered a case against the contractors. According to the police, the incident happened at around 10.45 am. "We rushed to the spot after receiving a call from the control room. Even the fire brigade was also informed about the incident," said an official attached to the Shahu Nagar police station.

The injured workers, identified as Dakhva(30) and Ishwar Arjun Behram (28) were rushed to the Sion Hospital where they were declared brought dead. "These wokers were employed by labour contractors named Chirag Contractors who were in turn hired by the Perfect Engineering to carry out construction works for the BMC," said Senior Police Inspector Shyam Gundewadi of the Shahu Nagar police station.

The two workers were digging and working on a mortar pipeline at outer side of the wall at TH Kataria Road near the Matunga railway colony. During this time, a part of the wall collapsed on them ad crushed them to death, said the police.

"The workers had been contracted to carry out mortar work at the road beside the wall at the Matunga railway colony. The work has been going on for the past 15 days and there were a total of 20-25 workers at the spot," said Narendra Pajare, a sub-engineer of the BMC who was on the spot when part of the wall collapsed. Pajare also said the part of the wall might have collapsed as it was very old and in a dilapidated condition.

A case of causing death by negligence has been registered against the contractors by the police. "Even though the digging work was going near the base of the wall, there was no support given to the wall to prevent the wall from falling over the workers. Moreover, the workers were not provided with helmets or safety devices. Keeping this in mind, we have registered the case," Gundewadi said.

Asked for the names of the accused, Gundewadi said, "So far, we are conducting enquiries to find out which personnel from the contractor's office was directly responsible for the work happening in such circumstances. As this is the weekend, we have not been able to communicate with the relevant BMC officials. As soon as the weekend gets over, we shall be communicating with the BMC to help us with enquiry."

Heading: Fence to be raised to prevent train robberies - Indian Express
Content:
Five employees of the examination department of the University of Mumbai were suspended on Friday for the goof-up that occurred last Monday when the university failed to print question papers of two subjects. The examination was to be conducted for students belonging to first year Masters programme of history who were repeating their papers. As a result, the exams had to be postponed to Saturday affecting around 90 students across the state.  

Those suspended from the examination department include the assistant registrar, a head clerk, two senior clerks and a superintendent. Following the incident on Monday, the university formed a fact-finding committee comprising of Dr Arun Kshirsagar, Director of Garware Institute of Career Education and Development, Sriram Patil of the Faculty of science and an official of the printing department. Members of the committee met on Saturday for an enquiry meeting during which Vilas Shinde, controller of examinations and the five employees were interrogated.

K Venkatramani, registrar of the university said that the university had informed the department of education (higher and technical education department) about the fiasco and the subsequent initiation of the enquiry. "The enquiry will take time. Till that time these five employees will remain suspended and staff from other departments will carry on the examination department work."   

Madhu Paranjape, joint-secretary of the Bombay University College Teachers Union (BUCTU) said, "A situation like question papers not getting printed in time for the examination is unprecedented. Initiation of stringent action is necessary but action cannot be taken only against the lower level employees." Paranjpe also said that the controller of examinations should have taken moral responsibility for the fiasco and resigned.

A member of the Mumbai University Employees Association concurred, "Those suspended are not at fault. We will wait for the enquiry report and accordingly plan our next move." He also threatened to strike work if employees were not taken back.

Heading: Purdue University to ink pact with Indian varsities - Indian Express
Content:
The snatching of a mobile phone from a woman commuter a couple of days ago has once again brought into focus the frequent robberies and chain-snatching incidents on local trains between Churni Road and Churchagte. The modus operandi is to snatch valuables from commuters, mostly women, when a train is waiting for the green signal. The low-height fencing in the area facilitates their easy escape.

The answer to the problem was found by the Government Railway Police around five months back, when it suggested the Western Railway to increase the height of the fencing. But so far, it has not materialised and despite heavy patrolling and checking, the incidents continue. The latest was on November 4. According to sources, 32-year-old Anupama Anubhav Mishra had boarded a Churchgate-bound train from Mahalaxmi station at around 7.30 pm. She was talking on her mobile phone when the train slowed down near a signal. A goon snatched away the phone, jumped down from the train and ran away after scaling the low fence.

M D Raskar, Senior Police inspector said, "A case of theft has been registered against the unidentified person." The Western Railway authorities now say that a proposal to increase the height of the barricades had been submitted to headquarters.

With the phone-snatching incident, the number of cases, including a couple of murders, has gone up to 11 in a three-and-a-half-year span in the Churchgate-Churni Road stretch. Eight incidents took place in the ladies' compartment of the local trains. All the incidents happened when the trains were standing for the green signal.

On June 9, after a woman commuter, Pritanka Chowdhary, was robbed in the ladies' first class compartment, security was beefed up in the ladies compartments of fast locals by the GRP. The incident took place three days after Raskar had taken charge of the area. After investigating the case, he had made a report and found that people easily crossed the iron fencing and entered the ladies' compartment when Churchgate-bound trains stopped at the red signal. On June 12, he sent the report to AK Sharma, commissioner GRP and he in turn forwarded it to the Divisional Railway Manager WR. In his report, Raskar wrote, "From Churchgate to Charni Road (east) there should be 8 to 10-ft-high fencing along the tracks."

CP Sharma, DRM, Mumbai Division was out of station, so Shyam Sunder Gupta, Chief Public Relations Officer, Western Railway informed, "A proposal has been sent to the headquarters. After getting the proposal sanctioned, work to increase the height of the fencing will be started within a year. WR has decided to make 5-ft-high concrete wall in the area. There will be a fencing of around 5 ft height on the concrete wall."

11cases in three years
In 2006, three crimes were reported on trains between Churchgate and Churni Road and one was a case of murder. In two cases of theft, goons snatched a gold chain and a mobilephone after entering the ladies' compartment. In 2007, there were three cases and again one was a murder case. In the theft cases, a person had entered the ladies compartment and snatched a gold chain and on February 4, 2007, goons boarded the ladies compartment at Marine Line and after assaulting her, ran away with her bag. In 2008, five cases of armed robbery and theft were reported. The last was on November 4, in which a mobilephone was snatched from a woman. There were three chain-snatching incidents in the ladies' compartment. On May 10, a bag was snatched from a commuter in the women's compartment.

Heading: Mumbai’s traffic situation catches Russia’s attention - Indian Express
Content:
America's Purdue University is planning to strengthen old ties and build new ones with universities in India, as a result of which some of the city's premier institutions will initiate various exchange programmes and alliances with Purdue.

In Mumbai, representatives of the Purdue University, including its president France Cordova met officials from the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IITB), the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), University Institute of Chemical Technology (UICT) and the S P Jain Institute.

"We began a partnership with the TIFR in 2005 where two students from the institute came to Purdue and later, two students from Purdue visited TIFR as well. As a result, we had a joint research symposium on Malaria as an infectious disease," said Pankaj Sharma, associate director in-charge of operations and international affairs at Purdue. "We're looking for funding from the Indo-US Science and Technology Forum (IUSSTF) to facilitate more exchange programmes," he said.

Engineering students from the IITB too have had an exchange programme with the Purdue University earlier, where some students have attended one semester at the Purdue. "Three years ago, a faculty member from the IITB came to Purdue and published a paper on biomass as an alternate means of energy," said Sharma. "We're planning to initiate a research project on nanotechnology in December," he said. Sharma also said Purdue had already established a tie-up with the school of chemical engineering at the UICT some years ago.

In the other cities too, Purdue has sealed some deals with leading educational institutions. In Pune, the university has tied up with Cummins India and the Cummins College of Engineering for Women. In Bangalore, the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research and Purdue University will come together for a joint research programme on Nanomaterials. In Hyderabad, the university has teamed up with the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) to do work on bio-nanotechnology.

Heading: Crimson tide: Rise in sea level changing Gujarat’s contours - Indian Express
Content:
A Russian delegation is in the city to mark 66 years of the sister-city programme

Mumbai's bumpy roads and traffic snarls did not fail to catch the eye of the visiting Russian delegation in the city. "It is very chaotic situation," said Russian deputy governor Alexander Vakhmistrov who is in the city to celebrate the 66th sister-city programme.

When asked about the condition of the city's roads, Vakhmistrov said, "It is a difficult question to answer. There are too many vehicles on the road making the situation very chaotic. But despite the obvious chaos, we saw no road accidents. This proves that Indian drivers are good at handling the traffic."

Stating that transport and traffic are the main issues for both St. Petersburg and Mumbai (celebrating the sister-city programme), he stressed on modernising transport systems. He also drew a comparison between Mumbai's and St Petersburg's traffic condition. "The situation was bad, however, we improved it by widening the roads and building dedicated routes for public transport where private vehicles are not allowed," he said adding that underground train system also helped a lot.

Meanwhile, St Petersburg is looking forward to helping Mumbai in infrastructure and educational development. Among other things, the delegation said that they can help Mumbai with the water purification project. Vakhmistrov also spoke of greater interaction among students of the two cities through exchange programmes. "We will be meeting with the vice-chancellor of Mumbai university and suggest more student-exchange programmes between the two cities," he said.

A sister-city programme is a unique facilitation for a cultural exchange, to give countries a sneak peek into different cultures. In February this year, Mumbai celebrated 40 years of association with Stuttgart. Earlier this week, BMC marked the 66 years of cultural exchanges with St. Petersburg. "We want to strengthen the relationship between the two countries by facilitating more business and cultural exchanges and overcoming these problems," said Vakhmistrov.

In another collaborative association, the ICLEI-Local Governments for Sustainability has selected Mumbai as their 1000th member to promote local government sustainability. "The exchange of ideas on urban management between the cities of ICLEI and Mumbai will further improve city-to-city cooperation," said Municipal commissioner Jairaj Phatak.

Heading: Maharaj of Sabridham on ATS radar - Indian Express
Content:
'The government has constructed sea protection walls near some of the most vulnerable coastal villages, including Danti, Udwada and Kaladra. If required, more such walls will be erected to protect human habitat along the coastline'

In what appears to be a cause of concern, the coastline of south Gujarat is gradually changing shape, threatening several coastal villages. One of the reasons why the sea is eroding the coast could be a rise in the sea level due to Global Warming.

In fact, the fishing village of Dandi in Valsad district and Kaladra village located on the estuary of Narmada River in Bharuch district have already started bearing the brunt of this disturbing phenomenon. Several families have already vacated these villages due to the advancing seawater every year.

The fact that the sea has been eroding the south Gujarat coast at an alarming pace was brought out through an exhibition of satellite images put up at the venue of an annual conference of the Indian National Cartographic Association (INCA) held at Gandhinagar last Tuesday. ISRO Chairman G Madhavan Nair, Chief Minister Narendra Modi and many others keenly observed the satellite images at the exhibition and expressed concern over the coastline changing shape.

"Our preliminary observations reveal that seawater has shifted by 10-15 metres in the last one decade, and at places it has moved around 80 metres horizontally," said Dr Nikhil Desai, a Geology professor at M S University, Vadodara.

Dr Desai is part of a survey of the Gujarat coastline being carried out by the Space Applications Centre, ISRO. The Union Ministry of Environment and Forest has appointed ISRO as the nodal agency to conduct the survey.

Dr Desai told Newsline on Saturday: "The rise in sea level due to Global Warming could be just one of the reasons for the erosion along the south Gujarat coast. But local factors such as neo-tectonic activities —shifts in the seabed level — could also cause the sea level to rise. If there are disturbances in sediment budgeting along the coast (the amount of deposits from rivers), it could also affect the water level."

He added: "We are still conducting the survey and collecting all relevant data on this disturbing phenomenon. It will still take a couple of months for our survey team to complete the study and ascertain which of these reasons is driving the changes along the coast."

He added that rapid industrialisation and other human-induced activities along the Gujarat coastline could also be a contributing factor.

Sources in the Sachivalaya said that the government is concerned about the reports of south Gujarat coastline changing shape. "The government has constructed sea protection walls near some of the most vulnerable coastal villages, including Danti, Udwada and Kaladra. If required, more such walls will be erected to protect human habitat along the coastline," they said.

However, a sea wall erected near the Kaladra village about 20 years ago is now a relic of the past, and a road constructed two years ago (at a cost of Rs 30 lakh) has been cut by the lashing waves. The Rathod fishing colony here had been washed away about 20 years ago, forcing the authorities to resettle the residents in New Kaladra, just a little higher up the estuary.

Heading: Consumer organisation to file complaint against LPG cylinder dealers - Indian Express
Content:
swami ashimanaNd has gone underground since Sadhvi Pragya's arrest

Swami Ashimanand Maharaj of Sabridham in Dangs district is under the scanner of the Mumbai Anti-Terror Squad (ATS), after his close associate Sunil Dhawde was arrested in connection with the Malegaon blast, from Vapi in Valsad district, a couple of days ago.

According to P P Swami, one of Maharaj's close friends, the latter originally belongs to West Bengal, and was much associated with the Hindu Jagran Samiti, following which he joined Hindu outfits and started working for the development of the tribals. He had completed his MSc from West Bengal and had later joined a private firm for a job.

It was while working for the tribals that he learnt about the riots between the Hindu and the Christian groups in Dangs in 1998. Several churches were burnt in the incident. Following this, he came to Dangs, and with the help of the VHP and other Hindu organisations, started the work of bringing back the converted tribals into the Hindu fold. He visited different villages in Dangs for this work. Apparently, Maharaj was very close to the national leaders of the VHP and the RSS.

Maharaj also acquired land at Subir village in Dangs from one of the local villagers identified as Lasu Gavit, a resident of Mokhamad village in Ahwa taluka. Sources in Mokhamad village said the entire amount of the land was not given to the land owner.

Maharaj had originally shown that the purpose of acquiring the land was to start a hospital for the tribals, but later he built a small temple of Sabrimata to attract the triabls, and also four rooms for the accommodation of pilgrims. Incidentally, several people had provided funds for the temple and the Ashram.

Maharaj also started the Vanwasi Kalyan Ashram School in Vaghai, which he has been running for the last seven years to provide free education to the tribal children. Different branches of Vanwasi Kalyan Ashram School were opened in different villages in Ahwa taluka. All these schools were run with the support of Hindu organisations.

With the help of the Vanvasi Kalyan Parishad and the Van Vikas Parishad, a three-day Sabri Kumbh Mela (Fair) was also organised on February 11, 2006. Several leaders of Hindu organisations and Maharajs from Gujarat and Maharashtra and elsewhere visited the fair.

Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur, one of the accused in the Malegaon blast, came in contact with Maharaj and the two developed a close rapport. Reportedly, Maharaj also provided a car to Sadhvi Pragya for her visit to different villages in Dangs district during her few weeks stay here at the fair.

Sunil Dhawde, one of Maharaj's close associates, who chauffeured Sadhvi Pragya to different villages in Dangs during her stay here, was picked up after the Mumbai ATS found his number in

Pragya's mobile phone. The police now suspect Maharaj's involvement in the Malegaon blasts, as he has gone underground following the arrest of Sadhvi Pragya.

Heading: Woman abandoned by husband, in-laws for delivering girl - Indian Express
Content:
With LPG dealers across the state having resolved to go on an indefinite strike from November 10, the city's Consumer Protection Organisation on Saturday threatened to file a complaint against them under the Essential Commodity Act (ECA).

The dealers are agitating against the introduction of the licensing system by the Gujarat government.

P B Murjani, Managing Director of Consumer Protection Organisation, said: "Any essential commodity including gas and petrol cannot be disconnected without the prior permission of the government. We will ask for monetary compensation for any inconvenience caused to the consumers."

While collector Vijay Nehra announced on Friday that even with 41 gas agencies on strike, the supply will not be disrupted, Murjani said: "It will be impossible to meet the requirements of the entire city with most of the agencies going on strike. We will help the consumers get compensation."

Heading: Foresters ‘chip in’ to check man-animal conflict - Indian Express
Content:
While the much-hyped Beti Bachao Andolan is in full swing in the state, an incident from Dhoraji has indicated that the girl child is still gasping for breath in Gujarat.

A young woman was shown the door by her husband and in-laws after she delivered a baby girl.

When Meena got married to

Mahesh two years ago, she had no idea that her first child would become the reason for her separation from her husband. According to the Dhoraji taluka police, Meena was mentally and physically harassed by Mahesh and her in-laws, residents of Kalana village.

After being abandoned by her husband, Meena went to her parents' house in Manavadar taluka of Junagadh district and has been living with them ever since, the police said.

Meena filed a complaint with the Patanvav police station in Dhoraji taluka on November 7. Her father-in-law Karsan, mother-in-law Kanchan and sister-in-law Vijaya have been booked for inflicting mental and physical torture.

In her complaint, Meena said that while all the family members were very happy when she was expecting, their attitude changed soon after she delivered a baby girl six months ago.

The police said they have "started the investigation in the case."

Preliminary investigation has revealed that Meena's husband has not asked her to come back as he and his family are not willing to accept the girl child. Mahesh reportedly works as a labourer.

Heading: ‘Shukravari Bazaar is temporary, poses no threat to VMC’ - Indian Express
Content:
Microchips to be implanted on leopards to track their movement

Forest officials in south Gujarat have voiced concern over the increased likelihood of man-animal conflict with the start of the sugarcane harvesting season. Now, the Forest Department has decided to initiate the micro-chipping of leopards in those places where the maximum number of attacks on humans by these big cats have taken place.

The project is still in the planning stage and officials have said that the first phase will begin with the training of the foresters.

"We will not like to hasten the process. We have gathered the technical know-how. First, we will train our staff for using the tranquiliser gun. By December, we plan to start the training so that after implementing the project, it continues without any problem," said Surat Conservator of Forests R J Asari.

He said the leopards will first be tranquilised and a passive microchip will be inserted into its body through a minor surgery. "Once the process is done, the leopards will be safely released at a proper place," he said. He added that the project is expected to work as a major step in resolving man-animal conflict. Once implemented, it will not only help the foresters identify the problem areas, but also help in accurate census of the leopards, which has not taken place for a long time in the state, particularly in this region.

"As part of the process, we will also gather information about the problem areas where leopards are sighted in close vicinity of human habitats in the rural areas," he said.

He added: "There are hundreds of sugarcane fields across south Gujarat, and the harvesting season is expected to begin in December. We have already witnessed a number of incidents where the leopard cubs were either charred to death or they were left behind by their mothers. Moreover, once the sugarcane fields are torched as part of the harvesting process, there are chances that the animal could come out, resulting in increased chances of man-animal conflict."

He said they are also taking the help of other organisations which are already working in the field of leopard-human conflicts in the region as their knowledge is important for implementing the project.

Heading: Vendors at the receiving end - Indian Express
Content:
While city police officials passed the buck to the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) regarding the ongoing issue of the removal of Shukravari Bazaar from the Fatehpura area, senior Corporation officials maintained they have not made any formal communication with the police administration in this regard.

VMC officials said they have received a letter from the police department in which they have mentioned various reasons related to the market and the law and order situation in the area. Some senior VMC officials were surprised when they were informed that the police is passing the buck on the corporation.

"The VMC has nothing to do with the Shukravari Bazaar, which is going on since the time of the princely Baroda state. We have received a formal communication in this regard, seeking our opinion, but we have no role in this. Primarily, we do not consider the Shukravari Bazaar as an encroachment because it is a temporary market. As far as other aspects including traffic congestion, and issues pertaining to law and order situation are concerned, it will be up to the police to take the required action," said VMC Deputy Municipal Commissioner C M Makwana.

"We are unnecessarily being dragged into this controversy,"said another official on condition of anonymity.

The official added: "If at all the VMC had any problems with that market, it would have been discussed in the general board meeting or any other coordination meeting. But it was never part of the agenda since it is not a problem for us. It is just a day-long affair and it does not result into any sort of permanent problem for the VMC. Let the police handle the issue the way they want to."

Heading: Information on your fingertips at Gujarat bus stations - Indian Express
Content:
The move has not only damaged the small retail business, but spelt doom for nearly 4,000 vendors from the Waghri and Muslim communities. They ran their business from makeshift laaris from Adaninapol to Gujarat Tekra, and from Panjrigar Mohalla to Fatehpura

Shukarvaari Bazaar, the city's Friday flea market that was the scene of hustle and bustle from morning till evening for many decades, may now draw a complete silence with the administration imposing a ban on it.

The move has not only damaged the small retail business, but spelt doom for nearly 4,000 vendors from the Waghri and Muslim communities, who ran their business on makeshift laaris from Adaninapol to Gujarat Tekra, and from Panjrigar Mohalla to Fatehpura.

Modha Khoda (60), a vendor selling electronic and cane items, said: "I stay at Hanuman Tekri in the Warasia area. Ours has been an old business, which was started by my father. But now, we are not allowed tospread our wares, as the police say that we 'spread' terror. But here, it is a daily struggle just for bread and butter."

The market attracts around 150 vendors from as far as Dharavi and Manisha markets in Mumbai, Dahod and Panchmahals district. It has also created a separate market for tiffinwallahs: selling puri-bhaji and mouth watering biriyanis in the localities of Fathehpura. Now, with the ban, these tiffinwallahs have lost half of their business.

In the Ranavaas locality of Fathepura, Shabbir Shaikh (60) has been selling biriyani for the last 15 years. He has suffered losses ever since the ban has been imposed. "I am suffering major losses every month after the closure," he said.

Near Shaikh's laari sits a group of vendors from Dharavi. Shahid Pathan is one such vendor. He said: "We come here every week because we see good market in this city with people coming from all strata. We used to earn Rs 1,000 every week mostly by selling clothes and items brought from Mumbai. We are suffering losses after the eviction."

Gita Patanwadi, a woman vendor, said, "I am forced to sell second-hand goods, as my husband has tuberculosis and is weak to earn for our four kids. Can the police make amends for us?"

Heading: Teen claims mother’s death was no accident, but murder - Indian Express
Content:
The Internet kiosks will provide users with state and city-centric information. A special portal created for the purpose gives access to the Gujarat government website, education and employment related details, as well as schedule information on bus, railway, airport and other city-centric infrastructure

The Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation (GSRTC) is all set to install Internet kiosks at every bus station across the state. After the installation of such kiosks in Ahmedabad a few months ago, the Corporation aims to install similar facilities for the public at the bus stands.

"We were approached by a few private companies to set up such kiosks at bus stands in Ahmedabad, but we decided not to restrict it to Ahmedabad, but instead spread it across the state," said GSRTC Secretary P D Patel.

GSRTC now aims to complete the installation across all the 245 bus stations in the state by March 2009.

"It comes completely free to us as the company will generate revenue from advertisements. We have just asked them to have a trained person at every kiosk to guide the people, and we hope to have this facility at all stations before the state celebrates Swarnim Gujarat," said Patel.

The Internet kiosks will provide users with state and city-centric information. A special portal created for the purpose gives access to the Gujarat government website, education and employment related details, as well as schedule information on bus, railway, airport and other city-centric infrastructure.

"We are at par with the technology available anywhere in the world. We simply need to utilise the technology in a way that would help the society. The portal that we have made, has been created keeping in mind the kind of information the public needs on a daily basis," said Parag Joshi from Namste Indya Communications Pvt Ltd (NICPL).

He said: "We have kept in mind every age group and every category. With the Tatas coming up with 5,000 new employments in the state, we also intend to advertise one eligible person on our portal every day."

To cut the language barrier, the portal is available in both English and Gujarati. The company has estimated a budget of Rs 80 crore for the project.

Heading: VMC axe to fall on defaulting cellphone, other private cos - Indian Express
Content:
Says an autorickshaw driver set her ablaze after she refused to give in to his 'illicit' demands
'On Saturday, we registered a case of murder against Rathod. We have launched a search for him,' said a police officer. He added that Mumtaz, in her dying declaration, called the incident an accident as Rathod had threatened to kill her children

The Statement of a 13-year-old girl has given a new turn to what the police so far considered a case of accidental death. Three days after a 32-year-old woman, Mumtaz, succumbed to her burn injuries, her daughter Afsana alleged that an autorickshaw driver had set her ablaze.

Mumtaz was admitted to the Rajkot Civil Hospital on October 31 with severe burn injuries. She breathed her last on November 5.

Afsana told the Rajkot city police that Rama Rathod was forcing her mother into an illicit relationship.

"On Saturday, we registered a case of murder against Rathod. We have launched a search for him," said a police officer. He added that Mumtaz, in her dying declaration, called the incident an accident as Rathod had threatened her to kill her children.

The police said the accused had also threatened the two kids against disclosing the truth. Afsana, however, gathered the courage to speak out the truth after meeting her grandparents, who visited them to attend the last rites on Thursday.

She told the police that Rathod was a regular visitor to their home, 25 Variya Niwas at Ghanteshwar on the Jamnagar Road. He would often come in a drunken state and ask Mumtaz for money.

On October 31, when Rathod came to their house at night, Afsana and her 10-year-old brother Sultan were also at home. Afsana said that Rathod, who was drunk, poured kerosene on her mother after she refused to give in to his commands. He kept the kids hostage for the entire night and took Mumtaz to the hospital the next morning.

Heading: Surat BJP gives a cold shoulder to local MP at poll meeting - Indian Express
Content:
The Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) will hold a special meeting of the standing committee on Tuesday to discuss the issue of recovery of incremental charges from private companies that have laid underground cables. Their target also includes cellphone operators who have placed hoardings without making payment for the same.

According to VMC officials, nearly Rs 63 crore was recovered as property tax from citizens and private parties during a recent drive. Now, the focus is on the recovery of the incremental charges and pending cases of octroi.
