The changes that we observed in Vadodara forests might be occurring in other forest areas of the country as well," said Prof Daniel, who will release a book 'Taxonomy: Evolution at Work' in a few months.

There are two schools of thought in this regard. While one group believes it is the external factors like radiations and chemicals in the atmosphere which stimulate the variation in genetic materials, the other thinks that the variations are an act of survival, which takes place when the plants are faced with adverse conditions.

"Plants are as smart as human beings. They change because they want to survive. The changes in their pattern show how they fight for survival. Our second phase of the research will envisage all these details," he said.

He added: "Once we list these changes, we will try to find out if the variations are genetic. Then we will be looking at other characteristics like chemical, embryological and cytological characters. And if there are enough characteristics, these plants may be considered as new evolved species."

Heading: Sarpanchs of 19 villages form action committee to oppose railway project - Indian Express
Content:
The proposed 'full-fledged' police station at the Polan Bazar area in Godhra has courted controversy, with the local Muslim leaders claiming that the land allotted for the purpose is meant for a burial ground for the community.

Godhra is all set to get two new police divisions in the town and an additional police outpost near Kalol at the Vejalpur highway. Godhra Town police Inspector R S Babhor said the two new divisions would make their work easier to administer the town.

"A police station at Polan Bazar will help us keep the anti-social elements at bay," Babhor said, adding that the new station would be housed in an abandoned land of the Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation (GSRTC).

Muslim leaders, including Muslim Ghachee Samaj president Firdous Kothi, however, have opposed the move, saying the land belongs to the Samaj.

"In 1962, we gave some part of the burial ground to the state transport corporation for a bus stand at the request of the state government. After acquiring the land, they assured us that whenever we need the land for the burial purpose, we could take it back. No money was taken for the land transfer," said Kothi.

Though a building was constructed by the GSRTC, it was never used as bus stand, he added.

He further said that a case over the land ownership is pending in the court of law for the last 10 years. "The Muslim Ghachee Panchayat had filed a case against the government in 1998 demanding the land back for burial purposes as per the deal. How can they give it to the police department?" said Kothi.

The police, on the other hand, said they have got a clearance from the GSRTC to set up the new police station in the area. "We plan to step in the new police station by early next year or even earlier. The repairs would start immediately," Babhor added.

Heading: City researcher wins first prize at 28th INCA Congress - Indian Express
Content:
After voicing their protest against the Indian Railways' Dedicated Freight Corridor project, 19 village sarpanchs from Vadodara district have formed an action committee to oppose the acquisition of land for the project.

At a meeting held in Bil Village near Padra in Vadodara, the village sarpanchs, represented by Baroda District Kheva Samaj chairman Hasmukh Bhatt, prepared a seven-point opposition letter addressed to the railway authorities.

The letter cites that most of the affected people do not have any other option other than their lands. It also brings out the fact that since almost all the lands have been acquired by the Vadodara Urban Development Authority (VUDA) for a mega-city project, the farmers would be left with nothing.

According to Bhatt, VUDA has already marked a 640-metre road in one of the villages within Vadodara district for its Vadodara Mega City project.

The letter also cites that railway officials are offering government prices for the lands, which tripled over the years, thanks to VUDA's ambitious project.

Meanwhile, railway officials have mooted the argument by the action committee, saying the whole movement has been instigated by the builder lobby in the city.

However, Bhatt has said the farmers do not have any other profession apart from agriculture and therefore, the question of a builder lobby does not arise.

Heading: Karjan shopkeeper murder case: All six accused arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty students from across the world presented papers on collaborative mapping

city-based Naishadh Dave (27) has won the first prize in the Young Researcher category at the recently held 28th INCA International Congress hosted by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) at Gandhinagar. Twenty students from across the world participated in the event.

Naishadh is pursuing his doctoral degree from RMIT University of Melbourne. He is a student of the Department of Mathematical and Geospatial Sciences. Naishadh completed his graduation from M S University.

Naishadh's paper titled "Understanding the risk associated with tourism in Port Campbell National Park–a cluster analysis to map out the behavioural risk" focused on the rise in the tourism sector. It also covered the risks involved in the process, both to the environment and the visitors.

"Although I have taken up Port Campbell as my model study, with the rise in nature tourism, the potential risk to the environment and the visitors are ubiquitous," said Naishadh.

He has used Global Positioning System (GPS) to monitor visitors' behavioural pattern and their movement when they are in a national park.

"Laxity in visitors' attitude not just damages the environment, it also leads to unwanted casualties," said Naishadh who presented his research under Collaborative Mapping and Space Technology theme.

Naishadh has identified 18 different characteristics of the visitors, which lead to instances of damage to the environment or casualty of the visitors themselves. Such characteristics include plucking flowers, polluting environment, falling down from a cliff or accidents during adventurous activities undertaken by visitors.

"If the tourism departments across the globe take interest in incorporating the GPS system to identify area specific flaws and map the visitors' characteristics, it will help them in taking up proactive planning to avoid the risks as well," said Naishadh.

Rushikesh Dave, Naishadh's father, said, "He was never interested in academics, but things changed when he came in contact with a prominent science writer at NASA."

Heading: Eight arrested for using pirated educational software - Indian Express
Content:
The Karjan police have arrested all six accused of the Anwar Shiekh murder case. The police said the six had taken shelter at one of the accused's house in the Navapura area.

The police are yet to ascertain the real motive behind the murder. On Saturday, they had said that the murder took place over business rivalry.

Shiekh, a shopkeeper from a municipal market in Karjan, was stabbed to death on Friday afternoon in the market. When Shiekh was passing by one of the accused's shop, Yasin Ghulam Shiekh stopped him, which resulted in an argument between the two. Soon, four people reached the spot and beat up Shiekh with an iron rod.

Assistant Sub-Inspector Kanu Patel, who was present at the spot, tried to intervene, but he also sustained severe injuries on the head and one Ajit Usman Shiekh repeatedly slapped him.

Thereafter, Yasin and others stabbed Shiekh with swords, the police said.

While Anwar Ismail Shiekh, Anku alias Kadiyo Shiekh and Usman Sheikh aided Yasin, he brutally stabbed Anwar.

Sources in Karjan said that the victim was associated closely with the local municipal corporation and because of a business rivalry, he wanted the accused to be out of the market.

Heading: DCB takes convict in custody for smuggling cellphone into Sabarmati jail - Indian Express
Content:
The Ahmedabad City Police on Saturday conducted raids at 10 computer education centres for allegedly using pirated versions of educational software without the permission of the concerned company.

Following the raids, eight people were arrested under the provisions of the Copyright Act. The raids were conducted with the help of a private investigation agency working to implement the intellectual property laws in association with the city police in Maninagar, Bapunagar, Vastrapur, Ashram Road, Navrangpura and Gujarat University areas.

The arrested have been identified as Bhavesh Patel, Nikunj Shah and Himanshu Jaiswal of Sai Technology; Dharmendra Trivedi and Ajay Prasad of Hubglobal Technology; Vijay Chhabra of ERP Consulting; Yogesh Patel of New Horizons Computer Learning Center and Rambihari Tripathi of Hugemony.

Gujarat University police inspector B M Rajapara said the accused were using the pirated version of an educational programme of a private firm without their prior consent.

Heading: RBI cancels licence of Nutan Sahakari Bank - Indian Express
Content:
The Ahmedabad city Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) on Saturday took a murder convict, lodged at the Sabarmati Central Jail, in its custody for his alleged involvement in a case of smuggling prohibited items into the jail.

The DCB said on Sunday that more arrests of jail staff and other prisoners in connection with the case are likely soon.

The arrested inmate was identified as Niyaz Hussain Saiyed. A metropolitan court remanded Saiyed in police custody for 11 days on Sunday.

He is accused of acquiring a mobile phone inside the high-security jail premises through his brother-in-law Mehmoodkhan Pathan alias Kajiyo from Shahpur. The cellphone was sneaked inside the jail with the help of a clerk-cum-typist of the jail, Ashok Japadia.

According to a press release issued by the DCB, Saiyed was taken into custody after interrogating Pathan and Japadia.

During interrogation, the DCB said, Saiyed told the police that some other jail officials and prisoners were also involved in a similar racket of getting prohibited things inside the jail.

Both Pathan and Japadia were caught by the DCB on October 16 when the former met Japadia near the Subhash Bridge Circle to give him a mobile phone to be smuggled into the jail.

Heading: IIM-A event explores potential of social entrepreneurship - Indian Express
Content:
Process of paying back the depositors of the cooperative bank will be set in motion

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has cancelled banking licence of Vadodara-based Nutan Sahakari Bank Limited after all efforts to revive it failed and uncertainty about its operations continued to harass the depositors.

The RBI order cancelling the cooperative bank's licence was delivered on November 5 after closure of banking hours, an RBI release said.

The apex bank has also asked the Registrar of Co-operatives to issue an order for winding up the bank and appoint a liquidator. On liquidation, every depositor is entitled to repayment up to a monetary ceiling of Rs 1 lakh from the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) under usual terms and conditions.

Nutan Sahakari Bank was granted banking licence on December 16, 1986. The statutory inspection of the bank with respect to its position as on December 31, 2002 had indicated that its financial position was impaired. Based on the finding as on March 31, 2005, the bank was prohibited from accepting fresh deposits, allowing premature withdrawals and granting fresh advances through a letter dated August 18, 2005.

Subsequently, as the bank's financial position deteriorated further, it was issued directions under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 vide a directive dated August 8, 2007, restricting its operations, including placing a ceiling on withdrawal of deposits at Rs 1,000.

The statutory inspection of the bank as on March 31, 2007 revealed that its financial position was precarious. The RBI issued a show-cause notice on September 5, 2007 asking as to why the bank's banking licence should not be cancelled. The bank did not have a viable plan of action for its revival and/ or merger with another bank, the RBI release said.

With the cancellation of the bank's licence and commencement of liquidation proceedings, the process of paying back the depositors of the bank will be set in motion subject to the terms and conditions of the Deposit Insurance Scheme, the release said.

Heading: Two drown in Narmada canal - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad, held its second social entrepreneurship fair Pratyarpan on Sunday.

It included a speakers round, a social B-plan round (Rachana), incubation plan (Pratyancha) and an innovative idea event for laymen (Ek Samadhan).

Speakers at the event Bhushan Punani from the Blind People's Association and Parth Vasavada from YUVA recognised the potential of social entrepreneurship and the fact that the ideation and innovation in the field seems to be sufficient for fuelling a sustainable impact.

However, they also identified synergising as a major challenge to innovators. Srijan Pal Singh, general secretary of the Student Affairs Council and the Chief Coordinator of the event said, "While there are a number of innovative ideas, we realise that there is a need to create synergy between innovations and ideas. In the next Pratyarpan, we will concentrate more on this aspect."

Participants in the event showcased innovative solutions to everyday problems and presented business plans for its cost-effective implementation.

Participants in the Pratyancha also presented business plans for innovations such as low cost sanitary pad machine by the team from Xaviers Institute of Management Bhubaneshwar (XIMB) and SP Jain Institute of Management and Research; natural water coolers by a team from K J Somaiya Institute of Management; and low cost and low maintenance motorcycle-run ambulance by a team from National Institute of Industrial Engineering (NIIE) Mumbai.

Ek Samadhan had ideas such as recognising societies for making fertilisers out of waste food and constructing a garden around railway gardens and better utilisation of non-renewable energy sources.

Participating groups made presentations of business plans with details of the projects.

The motorcycle-ambulance was targeted to reduce the Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) in rural areas being a cost-effective mode, while students developed business plans of the sanitary napkin machine and the natural water cooler.

The winners of Rachana and Pratyancha will be given cash prize of Rs 30,000 by the Centre for Innovation and Incubation (CII) at the institute.

Heading: AICTE makes room for 10,000 more seats in engineering colleges - Indian Express
Content:
A truck driver and a cleaner drowned in the Narmada canal near Malvan village of Surendranagar district while taking bath on Saturday afternoon.

The deceased were identified as Shambhu Ahir (25) and Mahadev Ahir (24), both residents of Saterada village in Anjar taluka of Kutch district.

According to the Patdi police, the incident occurred when drivers and cleaners of two trucks, carrying lignite, stopped at the canal to take bath.

Sub-Inspector M M Ganguly said: "Instead of taking bath at the stairs of the canal, the four jumped into the deep water and two of them drowned."

He said there was a possibility that their legs got entangled in some plants inside the canal.

Their attempts to come out could also have been foiled because of the strong current, said Ganguly.

The villagers tried to help them come out, but their efforts went in vain.

The officials of the Ahmedabad Fire and Emergency Services rushed to the spot, but were too late to save them. They fished out the bodies on Sunday.

Heading: Poetic Ponderings - Indian Express
Content:
The council has given its green signal to colleges to operate in two shifts; the colleges will have to apply for it now

Even as most of the government engineering colleges in the state are faced with shortage of teachers, the All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE) has made room for 10,000 more seats in self-financed and government colleges from the next academic year.

To accommodate the extra students, the AICTE has given its green signal to the colleges to operate in two shifts. The colleges seeking to have double shifts will need to apply for the same to the Council.

"With the additional 10,000 seats, we will for sure face the problem of faculties. At present, only four government colleges have principals. Rest of them are taken care by in-charge and senior professors," said M N Patel, principal, L D College of Engineering, Ahmedabad.

Patel added: "In government colleges, nearly 40 per cent positions for permanent faculties are empty. The ratio of faculty and student should be 1:15, but it is around 1: 30 at present."

He welcomed AICTE's move to allow colleges to run overtime, but added that a very few institutes in the state have sufficient infrastructure and staff.

"In the last few years, the junior teachers and freshers, who have just completed their bachelor, have been appointed on temporary basis. But this is not the solution," he said.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, principal of a government engineering college said, "It's not a wise decision. We are already facing shortage of teachers, especially experienced faculties. I doubt if we will be able to meet the requirements."

As of now, there are 54 engineering colleges in the state with an intake capacity of 18,774 students. Out of this, 37 are self-financed having a strength of 13,000 students. The rest 17 are government colleges with a room for 5,374 students.

Heading: Movie Masala - Indian Express
Content:
Poetry is mother art for Muzaffar Ali

All I have done has sprung from poetry and I am fortunate to be driven by poetry and equally fortunate not to be a poet, for I can fly with poetry,'' film-maker, fashion designer, painter, revivalist, social-worker has poetry on his mind and in his heart. Here on the invitation of the Chandigarh Lalit Kala Akademi to talk on Art Binds Us All, the chock-a-block hall at the Government Museum also had the privilege to view his short film, Breathe Into Me, on the Persian poet Rumi. Tracing his journey as an artist, smiles Ali is tough, for art is connected through the soul and life, and all that he has done has sprung from poetry, for poetry becomes films, music, clothes, architecture for him. "Poetry is mother art and poets are blessed for their inspiration is human and sadly, we in India, especially the last three generations have been deprived of poetry and the sensitive awareness of life, relationships, and I feel that we as artists need to take poetry to people,'' feels Muzaffar. The painter feels that artists in this global world have a fresh challenge of putting art into social, intellectual and human perspective and not be passive observers, and poetry and films can be powerful, sacred mediums to purify hearts and make people one. "Our viraasat is incomparable and we have to have a larger vision, respect other cultures and make a difference to people's life. Art should touch the heart of someone and address the feelings,'' Ali is these days working on script of Rumi, to explore his soul, vision, poetry and life.

Ali's album Paigham-e-Mohabbat , has lyrics by distinguished poets like Ali Sardar Jaffery, Ahmad Faraz, Rahi Masoom Raza, Faiz Ahmad Faiz, Qazi Nazrul Islam and he believes artists have the power to restore peace in the region. "I am not separate from my work. I'm sensitive to what is around me and it's a constant journey of self-discovery and quest to find solutions to pain and anguish and my films are a reflection of my life, thoughts,'' Ali refers to Awadh, Gaman and Umrao Jaan.

Having set up the Rumi Foundation and also a magazine on poetry, the next issue is on the poets of Punjab, Ali says he is always learning, "I don't get bound by regulations, formalities or follow a school of thought. I always need to break open and see it from a human point of view,'' the painter talks about the human touch..

Heading: 2 IRB companies from state deputed for C’garh polls - Indian Express
Content:
While Hollywood's already minting millions from it, Bollywood is warming up to the cash flow. That's right, movie merchandise is where the moolah is

Nine billion dollars. That's the amount George Lucas made just off his Star Wars merchandise. With it, he gave the industry what we now call the entertainment licensing. One move and Star Wars was a merchandising powerhouse, a model cloned in no time. Walt Disney jumped on to the wagon. Harry Potter's already loading close to 12 billion dollars. Mr & Mrs Smith flashed their Tissots while James Bond's cashed in billions with his fancy suits, snazzy cars and super gadgets. That's Hollywood - they invent the formula, we copy it. Cut to home ground, and Bollywood's getting a grip of this whole new money minting machine - movie merchandise. The Roshans made their bit off Krrish. Despite the flop, Harry Baweja raked in enough through spy gadgets, hovercrafts, interactive robots and the boo doll. Farah Khan got her returns from clothing line - apparently these sell the most. Even Ram Gopal Varma sold his Bhoot dolls. Roadside Romeo has an interactive website, and news is that a game around Ghajini too is being planned. It may be directly proportional to the box office fate of the film, but c'mon, wouldn't you just love to have that tee Shah Rukh was wearing or a sexy pair of jeans Hrithik had slipped in, John's underwear, or for that matter, Madhuri's gorgeous ninety nine yards of gold saree, Bips and Bebo's funky fashion line-up? Boutique owners went mad when women crashed in to get that exact copy of Madhuri's purple saree in Hum Aapke Hain Kaun. After the release of Maine Pyaar Kiya and Dil Hai Ki Maanta Nahin, everyone was seen tipping a Friend and Captain cap. Once Kuch Kuch Hota Hai was out, the cool chain became a rage. So did those snappy friendship bands.

Dolls, masks, key chains, school bags and T-shirts, the new media with its ring tones, smses, games - the Hindi film industry is looking to duplicate the Hollywood effect where manufacturers and retailers collectively earn $16 bn annually from their movie merchandise. Although Bollywood trade analysts like Komal Nahta define this as a nascent stage, director-producer Harry Baweja, despite the BO blooper, was more than happy with his earnings. "Earlier, we had all these romantic films with little or zero scope for merchandise...it was limited to apparel. But now films have superheroes, new technology, stars are treated as brand ambassadors and there's a young audience ready to lap it up. It is a niche market at the moment, but I see huge revenues from it," Baweja. While Baweja feels it's dependent on the longetivity of the character - a hit superhero sells, Nahta says it's related to BO results. "If the film flops, the merchandise to an extent fails. Hollywood makes millions, we've just crossed a crore!" Nahta is waiting for Rab Ne Bana Jodi and Big Pictures big plans with it. Meanwhile, Sesha Saye, Director Walt Disney Company, Corporate Communications term their division as the Disney Difference. "For us, it's constant story-telling that goes beyond the film. It's about the company creating creative property which we are able to transcend across different businesses," he says. So it's comic books, shows, websites, ringtones, games, collectibles, downloads, music, toys..."technology is the key focus are for us and the new media makes immense space for entertainment opportunities," Sesha's quite positive. Speaking of which, Walt Disney's out with Roadside Romeo's jazzy website www.roadsideromeo.com complete with RR products, characters, interactive widget, games, music et al.

A word with the big players in movie merchandise, Zapak, Arun Mehra, Chief Marketing Officer, Zapak Digital Entertainment Ltd says the life of the merchandise is more than the life of the movie. "Therefore, the merchandise not only creates a lot of promotion and buzz around the movie before it releases but it also keeps it alive even after the movie is off the theatres." Zapak forayed in the business of movie merchandising as a leader with Bhoothnath and restarted this trend which was taken over by pirates. Where there is an estimated business of Rs 300 crore, films were getting hardly 10 per cent! "Earlier people didn't enter this space with the right products for the audience with the right price points. We thus launched merchandise at very nominal price points for the perspective is not sales but the benefit that both the industries," Arun feels that films and gaming have added a new chapter in book of movie marketing. "Right now film-makers are looking at extending the life span of their movies beyond the four to five week stint in cinema halls. The life of a game or toy (in most cases) is more than the life of the movie," Zapak's created merchandise for Drona which includes toys and games. There's a series of comics too called "The Adventures of Drona". The company also brought out Love Story 2050's space carrier, space listener, Priyanka's cuddly robot pet Boo, then there's 'Hari Puttar: A Comedy of Terrors' for with its magic tricks for kids, brain twisters and teasers. Recently, Percept with Bollywood Retail are expected to invest Rs 500 million to sell Bollywood merchandise. Like they say: Show me the money!

Heading: HJC slams Cong for ‘killing’ youth - Indian Express
Content: Ten companies from the First and Second India Reserve Battalions in Haryana have been dispatched for security duties during the forthcoming assembly elections in Chattisgarh, following directions of the Election Commission. A spokesman of the Haryana Police said that the the 1198-strong force comprises two assistant commandants, nine deputy superintendents of police, 13 inspectors, 50 non gazetted officers, 222 head constables, 835 constables, one doctor, nine pharmacists and 57 class IV employees. It would be headed by a commandant. An advance team has already reached Chattisgarh to liaison with the local authorities and make arrangements for the stay of the force, he said.

Heading: Power shortage will be history, says Hooda - Indian Express
Content:
Accusing the state's Congress government of killing of innocent youths in fake encounters, the women's wing of the Haryana Janhit Congress Party (B) today alleged that the government had lost its control over the police. Expressing her condolence over the recent death of a youth, Kuldip, in an alleged fake encounter, state president of the wing, Kushum Sharma, said people feel insecure under the present rule.

Demanding immediate dismissal of the government, Sharma said President's rule should be imposed in the state. Vice-president Veena Sharma accused the Congress government of creating lawlessness.

Heading: Protect Marathis: Deshmukh to Haryana - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana government has signed an agreement for the purchase of 3,100 MW power for the next 25 years apart from the expected production of 5,000 MW by 2010.

Claiming that the state would face no shortage of power after the plans are implemented, Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda said, "The problem of electricity bills has already been resolved and the government is determined to eliminate the problem of shortage of power."

Addressing a public rally at Ghoghrian village after laying the foundation stone of a 132-KV substation, he said, "For next three consecutive years, one power generation plant would be commissioned every year."

He said, "Construction work of the 1200-MW Rajiv Gandhi Thermal Power Plant, Khedar, is in full swing and 48 per cent of the work has already been completed. First unit of the project will be commissioned before December 2009 and second unit before March 2010."

He later inaugurated a 33-KV substation at village Kakrod, constructed by the Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam at cost of Rs two crore.

Heading: Land allotted to Japanese major in Bahadurgarh - Indian Express
Content:
Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on Sunday said he was in touch with his Haryana counterpart to ensure adequate protection for Marathi families in that state.

Reacting to reports that a Marathi family in Haryana had to leave that state after being allegedly harassed in the wake of MNS leader Raj Thackeray's anti-North Indian stir, Deshmukh told reporters here that the incident should be treated as an isolated one and not be generalised.

"We have already brought the incident to the notice of the Haryana authorities and we are sure proper measures will be taken to curb recurrence of such happenings", he added. Depty Chief Minister R R Patil said the state government will write to the Haryana CM urging him to provide adequate security to the Maharashtrian family in Karnal.

Heading: Wife, 2 children of HCS officer found dead - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana State Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation (HSIIDC) has handed over possession of 25 acre land in Industrial Estate, Bahadurgarh, to Japanese company Yokohama for the construction of a Rs 1000- crore plant there.

Rajiv Arora, Managing Director, HSIIDC, said Japanese investment in Haryana had so far been limited to Gurgaon, Manesar and Faridabad, but now it was spreading to other parts of the state as well. "Yokohama Tyres is the first major Japanese investment in the Rohtak-Jhajjar belt," he said.

Arora said this major Japanese investment would create a number of employment opportunities.

"When completed, the tyre project is expected to provide employment to about 900 people directly and to an equal number indirectly. It will also promote ancillaries in the surrounding areas of Bahadurgarh," said Arora.

Yokohama, the seventh largest car tyre manufacturer in the world, will be setting up an automotive car tyre manufacturing unit at Bahadurgarh in the National Capital Region (NCR), further adding to Haryana's reputation as the automotive manufacturing capital of the country.

The 100 per cent foreign direct investment (FDI) project is proposed to be financed entirely through the capital and internal finances of the company.

Heading: Conservation Bill being drafted - Indian Express
Content:
Forensic evidence suggests she shot the kids before killing herself

In a shocking incident, Anju Sherawat, wife of GM, Haryana Roadways, Karnal, Varinder Singh Sherawat, reportedly committed suicide at their residence in Samalkha, Panipat, along with her two minor children, Meghna and Paras.

"The three were found lying dead on the bed when the bedroom door was broken open by the police. A bullet each was fired in the heads of the three from close quarters," said Samalkha SHO Tularam.

A .32-bore revolver was found in her bedroom, which was locked from inside, according to sources in the police.

Varinder Sherawat, an HCS officer, was transferred to Hansi from Karnal two days ago and was reportedly not at home when the incident took place.

While the daughter, Meghna, was 11 years old, son Paras was aged seven.

A suicide note written by Anju has also been found at the residence, sources said.

Tularam, who is the investigating officer in the case, said forensic experts had immediately been called after the incident came to light today morning, but the Panipat police refused to divulge any information.Forensic experts said gun powder was found on the hands of Anju, which implies that it was she who had fired the gun. The hands of Varinder Singh Sherawat were also examined by the forensic experts, but no gun powder was found on his hands.

"The post-mortem report has confirmed that the deaths of the three occurred due to bullet injuries," said Tularam.

Sources said Anju was distressed by the charge of molestation levelled against her husband by a woman of Gannaur. Sherawat was earlier posted as SDM, Gannaur, Sonepat.

"The enquiry in that molestation and rape case is being conducted by the Gannaur DSP," said Tularam.

Panipat SP Mahender Sheoran said the police was investigating the matter and there was a chance that it could be a case of suicide.

He said Sherawat was in a state of shock and was not in a position to give a statement, which could prove vital to the case.

Heading: The saving grace: Harike - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Ministry of Environment and Forest has proposed a Bill for the conservation and regulation of wetlands in India. Tentatively called the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2008, the draft, which is still in the suggestion-incorporation stage, says, "Many wetlands are seriously threatened by reclamation through drainage and landfill, pollution, hydrological alterations and over-exploitation of their natural resources…" The draft suggests categorisation of wetlands on various basis, including location and size.

It also has provision for the setting up of District Wetland Conservation Committees at the lowest level to monitor the implementation of its directives and the identification of means to make the wetland economically viable, if situated on private land. While the draft is silent as to who would retain or get the ownership of such wetlands, it has mooted a provision for public consultation after a management action plan is prepared, with all the stakeholders and those affected having a say in the finalisation.

Scientists at the PSCST suggest the inclusion of village ponds too and taking suggestion of the village panchayats regarding the identification of ponds as wetlands. "The specifications may or may not be fulfilled by the village ponds, which, in any case, have a large role to play in the ecological health of a village. We will suggest inclusion of these ponds in the wetland category irrespective of size," sources at the council say.

A senior IFS officer in Punjab's Forest Department, however, says, "We have enough laws already, but the need of the hour is to implement them and "not lay our ecology mortgage to vested political and business interests".

Presently open to suggestions, the copy of the draft is available on the ministry's website.

Heading: Fate of Fazilka’s Badha Lake - Indian Express
Content:
In 2000, it took a military operation to halt the march of water hyacinth in Harike, one of the internationally protected wetlands in India, famous for a large number of birds, both local and migratory. The invasive hyacinth problem was squeezing the life out of its 41-square-metre area for some time. The Army took up the battle and formed a Harike Task Force to preserve the lake and till October 2000, when the project was suspended, it had cleared about 1,00,250 tonnes of water hyacinth from an eight-square-kilometre area, much more than the initial target. But the hyacinth resurfaces with a vengeance time and again and the Army certainly has more duties to perform than clean it up.

From what was a sprawling 41-square kilometre home to thousand of species, the Harike wetland has been reduced to a 28-square-kilometre virtual dumpsite for industrial waste of the Ludhiana industry.

Basantha Rajkumar, Divisional Forest Officer, Ferozepur, says the biggest threat to the wetland is pollution. according to a study by the PSCST, about 700 million litres of polluted water reaches Harike everyday. The action taken by the state government against the 26 polluting units listed by the PPCB, if any, seems to have stayed on paper alone.

But talking of it being a bright spot, it cannot be overlooked that the sanctuary, formed on the confluence of rivers Beas and Satluj, is connected with three districts, which include 12 villages of Ferozepur, eight of Tarn Taran and seven of Kapurthala, and boasts of 23 islands, covered with wild grass, which provide safe nestling places for birds.

It is the venue for winter sojourn of birds that arrive here after blankets of ice and snow cover Siberia. The winged guests spend three to four months and breed here. The rare birds spotted here include the cotton pygmy goose, tufted duck, brown and black headed gull, yellow-legged gull, Indian skimmer, white tern, hen harrier, Eurasian sparrow hawk, black-necked grebe, shrike and warbler besides Siberian cranes, white storks and painted storks.

The species of birds found here are around 360, besides eight species of turtles and 38 taxa of plants and numerous species of snakes and fish. The wetland is also home to the rare Indus Dolphin. It is an example of how community participation and international conventions, for instance the Ramsar Convention which has listed Harike as a wetland of international significance, can facilitate conservation.

In May last, a team of British environmental experts landed here. Led by J Blackney, the team comprising four members, conducted a survey of the bird sanctuary.

The team's focus was to find out opportunities for international-level tourism here and a report has been submitted to the state government. Asian Development Bank also conducted a survey here recently and funding might be provided by them as well.

Heading: Maharaja’s haunt long lost - Indian Express
Content:
The town of Fazilka owes its very existence to the location of Badha Lake at the place where the town stands now. In 1844, Vans Pat Agnew, the first British officer stationed in the area, selected the place for installation of a surveillance station of East India Company and built himself a bungalow on the banks of the horse-shoe lake of Badha.

The bungalow still exists and houses the office of the Sub-Divisional Officer (Civil), Fazilka. But the irony is that the once 150-acre lake is nowhere to be found. It dried out, or rather, was made to dry out by people. The lake, which was, till the 60s, a flourishing water body that attracted several species of migratory birds, now exists only on paper. "A horseshoe lake develops when a river enters the plains and seeks its path of least resistance. Badha Lake received water as recharge from Satluj, but the ill-conceived Indus Water Treaty, 1960, sealed its fate. The Satluj has been truncated at Suleimanki Head Works by the Water Commission of the Central government, leaving it with no source of water," says Dr Bhupinder Singh, an IIT professor, who has written a booklet on the issue. "The stretch of stream from Ferozepur to Fazilka hardly gets any water from Satluj; all the 105-kilometre stretch carries is waste from the leather industry of Kasur in Pakistan. This has affected the ecology badly and has left many such smaller horse-shoe lakes on its banks dry," he adds.

"It was home to a huge population of peacocks, running into hundreds, but now not even one peacock is alive and if this is the fate of the national bird, one can well imagine the callous attitude of the officials concerned," says Navdeep Asija, a researcher based in Chandigarh.

The attitude of the authorities can very well be gauged from the fact that despite the wetland being a place famous for the peacock population that once thronged it, District Forest Officer (Wildlife) Balbir Singh is unaware of its existence. However, when told about its history and importance, he said he would personally visit the area and inspect.

The lake was a source of quality drinking water for 100 years (1844-1946). In the 50s, people of this region used hand pumps to extract water from a depth of four metres. But following the treaty and the subsequent diversion of Satluj, ground water depleted to such an extent that people now have to install submersible pumps to lift water from the a depth of 30 metres.

The lake-bed is now listed as panchayat land in the local revenue department's documents and has been leased out for cultivation. "Repeated attempts have been made to construct colonies and to mine sand from its dry bed, but vigil by some local people has helped stop the area from becoming a concrete jungle," says Asija.

"In 2000, the Punjab State Council for Science and Technology (PSCST) warned in its report to the state Environment Department that the conservation of this wetland is essential. Even the then DC of Ferozepur, Kulbir Singh Sidhu, had assured of all efforts to retrieve the sites as the natural habitats of migratory birds. Till today, no long-term conservation measure on saving wetlands has been taken by the government," he adds. Ferozepur DC Megh Raj, however, does not remember any such assurance given by one of his predecessors and, perhaps not so surprisingly, is not even aware of the two major wetlands we mentioned in the conversation with him-Ganj Baksh and Badha. Both of these are situated in his own district, Ferozepur. He says, "I have been caught up in election duties and procurement, the issue of environment has not got my due attention I admit."

Scientists at the PSCST say that disappearance is a serious matter, but express helplessness as the lake-bed is panchayat land. "It can still be recharged through a channel routed from the Bhakra main canal to the existing network of channels in south Punjab, but past experience stands testimony that the lake's obituary is well overdue. All we can do is hope," rues Dr Bhupinder.

Heading: Wetlands: High and dry - Indian Express
Content:
The Bhupinder Sagar Lake is still alive on paper, but a visit reveals that fields are ploughed where the Maharaja of Patiala's hunting ground once was.

Named after the erstwhile Maharaja of Patiala, the Bhupinder Sagar Lake in Sangrur district, which was once popular for its stature as the favourite hunting spot of the late Maharaja Bhupinder Singh, has altogether vanished. The lake was once spread over an area of about 1,280 hectare and the forest near it was spread on almost 15 acre around it.

Maharaja Bhupinder Singh used to visit it often and hunting was a common practice in the region, something the Maharaja loved. An exotic and wide array of migratory birds also visited the place. "He had once taken the Viceroy of India there for hunting and he had loved the place," said a close friend of Malvinder Singh, the great grandson of Bhupinder Singh.

According to records available with the Forest Department, the wetland was notified on February 28, 1952, by the Punjab government. "It was bought from the local people in 1954 for a lump sum amount of Rs 2,000," reads a torn piece of document available with the Forest Department.

Records suggest that numerous fish were found in the pond at Bhupinder Sagar and the annual contract for fishing was always given at high rates.

The land is located in Patran, surrounded by Dogaal, Hariau Jattan, Dhoorh, Jhingna, Khangnewala and Sehelwala villages.

According to Divisional Forest Officer K S Jattana, migratory birds including ducks, geese of various kinds, including the famous bar-headed goose, cobbed duck, flying cock and cranes were regularly sighted at the wetland. "Great crested grebe, white-necked stork, adjutant stork, glossy ibis, pintail, gadwall, eastern purple heron, coot, tailor bird, peafowl and ruddy sheduck were also found in abundance", he said.

Septuagenarian Patiala resident Raghubir Singh, who earlier served at the wetland when he was in the Government Consolidation Department, said the villagers used to pay a rent of 25 paise to cross the wetland. "Now it is totally lost and the entire area is taken over by farmers and villagers and sadly there is no sight of the wetland," he rued.

Heading: Tube talk - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab's ecology has suffered enormously due to the gross misuse of water resources. Area under wetlands has gone down from 1.32 per cent to .46 per cent, and the dangers have encompassed the whole ecological system of the state

Owing to gross negligence and insensitive attitude of the government and, more significantly, the common man, the number of wetlands in the state has been declining fast over the last half a century. The state has a mere 0.46 per cent of its area under wetlands, as per the records of the Central government, a fall of more than 70 per cent from the 1.32 per cent in the early 50s. Disappearance of more than 30 wetlands that existed once has gone unnoticed except for the occasional flutter in the files of the state government and the Ministry of Environment and Forests.

The Centre puts the figure of surviving wetlands at 14, including 12 natural and two man-made. According to the latest survey by the Punjab State Council for Science and Technology, the nodal agency on wetland preservation and conservation in the state, the total wetland area in Punjab is 3,711 hectare, out of which about 918 hectare is outside water in the form of small islands in the middle of wetlands.

"Some wetlands, including the Bhupinder Sagar in Patiala and Rahon de Chhamb in Jalandhar, were as large as 1,280 hectares and 350 hectares, respectively, but the locals have filled them up and started cultivation on its bed," says Dr S S Ladhar, PSCST joint director (environment) who has conducted a survey of the wetlands in Punjab three years ago. His study, 'Wetland conservation in Punjab', done in 2005 under the purview of the PSCST, blames the swelling needs of the ever-swelling population, human insensitivity and lack of information.

The council had identified eight wetlands of economic potential five years ago and authorities say, "We are doing our best to suggest ways and means to save the wetlands we have. Harike and Kanjli wetlands, for example, have been sustaining themselves well."

The council pegs the number of surviving wetlands at 32, a number that counts the now-extinct ones, including Badha and Gang Baksh in Ferozepur district and Lobana and Bhupinder Sagar in Patiala district. But a list of important wetlands of the state, as per the PSCST, includes 13 wetlands, including the man-made Harike and Nangal.

As per a study done by M Singh and K Brar, Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, "Since 1960s, wetlands in the state were drained and reclaimed for either cultivation or urbanisation. As a result, only 11 per cent of the natural wetlands remain."

Some of the reasons for the extinction of wetlands are reclamation of land for cultivation, leasing out of panchayati land for revenue, diversion of the water to fields and draining out the low-lying areas to use it for other purposes.

"Another big reason for the extinction of some natural wetlands is the taming of rivers by the authorities to serve short-term needs," says Dr Bhupinder Singh, a professor at IIT, Roorki. "A case in point is the diversion of Satluj, which has resulted in extinction of several wetlands, including the Badha Lake at Fazilka in Ferozepur district," he adds.

The authorities say they are helpless as the reclamation of wetlands on private or panchayat land is something that cannot be legally stopped.

Few of the now-dry wetlands are Chhangli Chhamb (1,000 hectares), Chhangli Tabo (140 hectares), Chhamb Gurditwala in Ferozpur (100 hectares); Sangeri in Mansa (41 hectares); Sharmkot in Gurdaspur (12 hectares); Gaunspur Chhamb (100 hectares) and Jandwal Chhamb in Hoshiarpur (100 hectares).

Surinder Singh, director, Kheti Virasat, an NGO that has done a survey on wetlands of Punjab, emphasises the historical and cultural significance of the wetlands. "The town of Nabha had a pond on all four corners, which are nowhere to be found now," he cites. With the destruction of wetlands, not only does the water drain out, but the species of animals, mainly birds, are rendered homeless, resulting in extinction and ecological imbalance.

The lowering of water table, a huge problem in a state where more than one million tubewells suck the earth dry every season, has a lot to do with these wetlands, as the replenishment of ground water is done after the collection of water in the low-lying areas.

Extinction of vital species of birds, such as the vulture and the common house sparrow, is also indirectly linked to the destruction of wetlands. Several migratory birds have borne the brunt of the change in ecology. M P Rai, Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife), Punjab, says they have their task cut out only in the wetlands declared as sanctuaries, including Harike, as most of the wetlands are on private or panchayati land.

Ironically, man-made wetlands have survived and are doing comparatively well. The Harike wetland attracts hundreds of species of birds annually and rare sightings of Indus Dolphin have been reported here. But according to scientist at the PSCST, even the man-made wetlands are facing challenges of silting and the Harike wetland, which covered 41 square kilometres of area at the time of its inception in 1952, has been reduced to just 28 square kilometres.

"The problem is worldwide. Almost 50,000 hectare area goes dry or the water on it is polluted beyond repair every year in Asia alone," says Dr Ladhar. Scientists and experts say that apart from legislations and the usual anti-encroachment drives, it is the awareness among the common man that needs to be stressed upon.

Basantha Rajkumar, Divisional Forest Officer, Ferozepur, says, "Urbanisation is one big reason behind this, especially in Punjab, where forest-based life does not exist. For example, in Orissa, wetlands would have survived as people value nature and its gifts."

Neelima Jerath, Additional Director, Environment, PSCST, says the draft bill being prepared by the Centre for wetland conservation (see box, bottom left ) can help in saving the vital ecosystems through the concept of community participation, a concept which, Basnatha Rajkumar opines, is the only way out.

Heading: Foot loose - Indian Express
Content:
Designer Aki Narula on dressing up the hunks in Tarun Mansukhani's Dostana

Life is supposedly one long party when you're based in Miami. Aki Narula, however, discovered that life on pristine beaches can also mean a lot of hard work. The designer, who has dressed up actors John Abraham, Abhishek Bachchan, Bobby Deol and a handful of others (only Priyanka Chopra's costumes have been done by Manish Malhotra) for Tarun Mansukhani's film Dostana that releases this Friday, got his brief for the film approved in half an hour, when he met the director and producer Karan Johar in Mumbai last November. But when he landed in Miami for a recce in early January, he knew he was in for a mad ride. "There's a very Cuban, Mexican feel to Miami, particularly with its cosmopolitan crowd, its white sands and clear blue skies. Since the characters in the film are based there, imbibing the local culture was important. Translating that mood to clothes was quite a task," he says.

In the movie, Abraham plays a fashion photographer and Bachchan a male nurse, while Bobby Deol is an urban sophisticate. So while Deol goes around in more formal clothing— slim Louis Vuitton suits and Dolce Gabbana jackets, the other two have a more casual style. "Choosing clothes for John was easy. He's in shorts for most of the movie and all you ladies are in for a treat with his toned body on display," smiles Aki. "I gave him a lot of tees with social messages on them. I made Abhishek wear all sorts of bright colours, from oranges to greens to reds and pinks with low-waisted jeans and cargo pants," says Narula, who has been styling for Bachchan junior since his Bunty Aur Babli days. In fact, Narula experimented a fair bit with Bachchan's outfit, apart from making him wear colour. "Even though this movie is aimed for an urban crowd, I always believe that a trend should be able to cut across masses, like the shirt kurtis in Bunty Aur Babli that became such a rage after the movie.

Most of the shirts that Abhishek wears in Dostana have collars that are 30 inches long, and reach his knees. A friend of mine was telling me he has already seen replicas on Carter Road!" says Narula. Shooting was a whole lot of fun too. "John would be ready in a jiffy while the other two took their time getting dressed for the shot. So John would laugh his head off all the while and irritate them," he grins. Post Dostana, Narula's appointment diary is choc-a-bloc with assignments. Up next is Aditya Chopra's Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi, and Renzil D' silva's debut film with Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor and Viveik Oberoi. He is also doing the costumes for Kareena Kapoor for her next project, Kambaqt Ishq. For now though, look out for the dandies.

Heading: A View Within - Indian Express
Content:
Fancy a face

The three-week long Ebony Kids Carnival kicked off on Saturday. The first weekend witnessed a fancy dress competition especially for the children between the age group of two to six years and five to six years. There were kids all over the store, dressed up in bright and colourful dresses. The winners were given Ebony gift vouchers.

In full flow

The grand performance night organized by Club Salsa India and Varun Dance Studio at Hotel Shivalikview saw as many as 60 couples participate in the event. There were four couples that competed in the final round of the Open Salsa Championship. Those who salsa-ed their way to a win are Mayank and Prachi who have won themselves a three-month Platinum membership at Ozone while Ankur and Amita were awarded a complete makeover from Strands. The winning list also incuded Ahmar and Kanupriya who have won three months of free Salsa class at Varun Dance Studio. The guest judge for the evening DJ Will from Hong Kong also performed a demo for Bachata - a romantic dance from Dominican Republic. Getting the crowd moving, DJ Will spun heady salsa tracks for everyone. There were group performances choreographed by Varun and Barsha as well.

Heading: Desert Dreams - Indian Express
Content:
'Panjabi Beat' promises to present the state's "neglected" heritage on its pages

When something goes wrong within the state, the world believes that Punjab will deal with it in the right spirit. After all, Punjab is known for its hearty fortitude. "But are we merely that? The world knows us only due to our political history...the Partition, the turbulences, emergency etc. What about the rich religious heritage?" questions Reema Anand, Chief Editor of 'Panjabi Beat', an English bi-monthly. "My association with Reema is decades old. She has taken a great task to generate awareness amongst Punjabis the world over," mentioned HK Dua, Editor-in-Chief, The Tribune, who launched the magazine in the city on Sunday.

"Ignorance may be bliss, but is it actually the case? Do Punjabis all over the globe really want to stay in this stupor? In fact, Punjab's history has been reduced to mere politics and its religious heritage condemned to oblivion. Panjabiat exists only as a nine-letter word," feels Anand, who has also made documentaries on various Punjab-related issues. "My goal is to preserve the art, history, architecture, music et al of Punjab for which no agency or Punjabis here or abroad are doing anything. So Panjabi Beat is a step in that direction. I often ask myself, are we drugged and comatose like the youth out there? This is not a blame game, but it also does not mean we become silent partners in this huge loss. Panjabi Beat aims to generate enough energy for everybody to not just sit back and accept things as they are handed, but to question them," Anand signs off..

Heading: Gleaming in green - Indian Express
Content:
Five students from the College of Art bring back from Rajasthan memories, experiences & sights in print

It was meant to be a project, but it turned out to be an enriching experience. A trip to Rajasthan is any college student's dream vacation... the safaris, the palaces, the dances. But sometimes, you come across those who want to take the road less travelled, like this talented bunch of students from Government College of Art, Chandigarh. As you quiz them about the fun times, it all ends up around their love for art and photography. It's been a month since Charanjot, Rajveer, Nitin, Aditya and Aspaan came back from the desert, but the experiences are afresh and vivid.

"The idea was to capture the Rajasthan that tourists seldom see. We did not want typical images of the state," shares Charanjot. That's not the only thing that's unique about the project. All five students are from different trades, and they also claim this is a first-of-its kind initiative in the history of the college. Partially funded by Chandigarh Tourism, the group hired a jeep and ventured into areas like Khilchipur, Sherpur, Dhani, Ranthambore and Balaas. "We wanted to focus on the villages in the interiors. It was like a trip back in time. Many people demanded money for being clicked and some even reacted back in anger. The villagers did not know Hindi, they had never seen a camera and were shocked at our attires. There were no facilities available to them, yet they were so happy, their attitude made us all introspect," reflects Nitin, while for Aspaan it was an opportunity to study their lifestyle. She shares, "Colour sense, style and a sense of composition is inborn in them." The result was eight days of total experimentation of colours, compositions, techniques et al. They came back with about 2,000 captures, 40 of which will be on display at Government Art Gallery and Museum from November 10 to 14. "It has made us realize that to get a complete grasp over something, it is important to work beyond one's comfort zone and keep an open mind," Aspaan sums it up aptly.

Heading: Yes, you can! - Indian Express
Content:
Young and robust, Tsavorite is a relatively young gemstone

Heard of Tiffany's Tsavorite? Tsavorite, a young gemstone was first discovered in Tanzania in 1967 by the Scottish geologist Campbell R Bridges. Way back in 1974 Tiffany & Company began an extensive campaign to acquaint the American market with this exceptional and exquisitely brilliant gem. In honour of the Tsavo National Park owing to its profusion of game and the Tsavo River that flows through it Henry Platt, the former president of Tiffany & Company christened this young one of Garnet family as Tsavorite. Numerous companies globally soon followed to let stone lovers romance Tsavorite.

Tsavorite is a green grossularite and belongs to the multihued garnet family. East Africa may pride itself in offering the world its singular deposits of Tsavorite. It is found only in Kenya and Tanzania. Vanadium from the host rock and at times traces of chromium lends Tsavorite its brilliant green. Tsavorite is a radiant green with the array including a spring-like light green to a resolute blue green and a deep-forest green. The beaming blue-green is the most admired and prized in its league. This robust marvel of nature displays superior brilliance and amazing transparency, thanks to its high index of refraction. The beauty of the gem is further enhanced due to the fewer number of inclusions in it. Designers enjoy a liberal hand at styling stunning jewellery pieces of various sensibilities since the gemstone shapes include round, ovals, squares, cushions, trillions as well as emerald cuts. Another score for the gem comes from its hardness which being high allows the 'invisible' setting style unlike emeralds that crack being brittle. Tsavorites are mostly available less than three carats. Even the smaller sizes of Tsavorites are unusually brilliant and inclusions fail to deter the sparkle. Tsavorites above 20 carats in fine quality are collector's pieces. The largest fine quality Tsavorite is nearly flawless at 16.67 carats, is an emerald cut and is a part of Richard Webster's Collection. Just after 36 years of its discovery, Tsavorite is a much successful gem in delighting jewellery aficionados.

Tsavorite garnet has never been synthesized. It isn't heated, optic on treated or oiled. It's one of the few 100 percent natural gemstones in the market today. Please do request for a GIA certification accompanying your gemstone as one can't rule out imitations like green glass or YAG. Clean it with tepid, soapy water and avoid heat and acids. Tsavorite looks best in daylight hence very flauntable for all winter brunches, picnics and outdoor fairs. With winters almost there, let's raise our glasses to Tsavorite this time!

(The writer is a city-based researcher specialising in jewellery art and can be contacted at sameeraahaan02@gmail.com)

Heading: Here, B in BDO stands for bungling - Indian Express
Content:
Mind, body, life or work, meet the guru who promises to help you manage it all

What happens when at office you don't do something? Somebody else does it, right? Similarly, if you don't tell your wife that you love her, somebody else will," PS Rathore states the simple funda of life. As we muse over the equation he furthers, "Leave alone partners or friends, people don't even understand themselves. They doubt what they believe, they believe what they doubt," states Rathore, CEO, Rathore Management Corporation. In town to conduct a day long workshop 'Discover the power within', Rathore tells people that the power to succeed lies within.

We walk into his workshop only to watch about 60 people dancing to 'Mauja hi mauja'! "It's to create a stimulus, and because it's fun!" he smiles. Rathore refuses to let his seminars be merely a 'sit and go affair". Trained in New Linguistic Programming from US, Rathore has been into corporate management for almost six years now. "I attended a management seminar in Singapore, it hit me then that this was the thing for me," after which he left his job and took about three years to master what he preaches now. "It's an amazing feeling to be able to change somebody's life. I teach them how to place themselves in the context, no one behaviour suits all situations," tells this Swami Ramdev fan. "He is transforming so many lives, I want to be as popular as him."

Rathore's approach is very practical and technical. "I believe in getting to the basics and sticking to them." But how sustainable is the attitude change? "Change happens in a fraction, of course you need practice." Is it that simple? "Well yes, if you tell yourself that it is. The body and mind work in a synthesis. Just decide that you will do something and the cosmos will take care of you." Haven't we heard that so many times before? "That's because it is true!" Muse on that.

Heading: 50% flats vacant around city as buyers go missing - Indian Express
Content:
BDO allegedly misappropriated Rs 1.5-cr development funds, forged signatures of sarpanches, opened fake bank accounts

Bungling of Rs 1.5-crore rural development funds issued under various schemes, including the National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGA), has come to light in Tarsikka Block of Majitha sub-division.

The Vigilance Bureau, after getting written complaints, has started search for Tarsikka BDO Dhanwant Singh. Vigilance SSP Dilbagh Singh said they were carrying out raids to nab the BDO, who has been missing for the past few days. He said though an accountant in the BDO office has been rounded up, they were yet to register a case.

Tarsem Singh Sialka, chairman of Tarsikka Block Samiti who had lodged a complaint with the Vigilance, said, "Rs 1.5-crore funds have been siphoned off and there is a prima facie case against the BDO, as he had forged the signatures of various sarpanches to misappropriate funds issued under NREGA and other Central and Punjab government schemes. I have sought the registration of a case and arrest of Dhanwant Singh," said Sialka.

The BDO has been charged with preparing fake bills of labour engaged for carrying out development works and opening more than one fake account to deposit the money embezzled from the government treasury. "Dozens of sarpanches have approached me with affidavits, saying that their signatures to clear the bills were forged and money was shown to have been withdrawn by them," said Sialka.

The complainant also alleged the money was meant for laying of streets, repair of schools and panchayat building. Apart from this bungling, a major scam in the auction of land on lease has also been reported.

"There are 90 villages in the block and almost every panchayat has land in its name which is auctioned for a specific period for agricultural purposes. The revenue thus earned is spent on villages' development. But here, land was auctioned to a chosen few and various panchayats lost thousands of rupees' in revenue," he alleged.

Dilbagh Singh, meanwhile, said they would not spare anyone. "We are on the job and in a day or two, a full-fledged inquiry will be initiated," he said.

Heading: CHB has nothing to cheer either - Indian Express
Content:
FLAt world: Exorbitant prices, stricter home loans coupled with global recession, have taken a hit on the realty sector

In the absence of demand, coupled with inflation and banks getting stricter on home loans, more than 50 per cent of the apartments at the periphery of the city are waiting for buyers. The problem is expected to worsen once these flats are put up for sale.

A vast array of flats that came up in the Zirakpur and Dera Bassi region during the realty boom due to its locational advantage, today either stand vacant or have had their construction shelved in the absence of liquidity. Financiers who earlier used to buy land and put their money in the construction, too, have abandoned the real estate projects, thereby leaving developers and builders in the lurch. Developers, thus, have shifted their focus from investors to buyers.

"One of the driving forces for the flat boom in the periphery of Chandigarh was the high returns developers had foreseen. They had gone overboard by churning out flats rather than carving out plots. Around 25,000 flats will come up in Zirakpur, Dera Bassi, Mohali, Kharar and nearby areas in the near future. Of these, more than 50 per cent are lying vacant. The figure includes both constructed and completed flats as well as those that have been stalled due to lack of financial resources," said Dee Ess Estates developer in Zirakpur, R P Malhotra.

Apparently, Delhi builders have not taken time to realise that the apartment culture in the region will still take time to take off and have failed to achieve their target figures. Their modus operandi in the initial months of the realty boom that led to speculation of properties was a huge hit as a majority of the flats was booked by property dealers by making the down payment. They intended to sell it by charging high premium from buyers. They were successful to a very small extent but could not maintain the same spirit for long. 

"The experience I have gained from my relatives and friends who have waged their money into flats is very discouraging. I would prefer an independent floor of a smaller area in the city even if I have to pay more, rather than investing in a flat with hardly any infrastructure available. People are neither able to move into these apartments, nor they are able to sell it even at marginal profits as there are no takers," said Vikas Sharma, a resident of Chandigarh.

Even different alluring schemes, such as freebies offered by the developers, have failed to attract the prospective buyers. These freebies range anywhere from cash discounts, consumer goods, air tickets to automobiles.

Heading: Now, transfer deeds find favour with city folks - Indian Express
Content:
The over-ambitious mega housing project of the Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB), in collaboration with the Parsvnath Developers in the Rajiv Gandhi Information Technology Park has received a poor response.

Of the 1,314 units of Prideasia, only 160 units could be sold, with two and three-bedroom apartments being the hot favourites.

The trouble for the mega project, however, does not end here.

This figure, which hardly constitutes 12 per cent of the total units, has a poor ratio of villas. Only six out of 34 villas has managed to find buyers.

Commenting on the exorbitant prices kept for villas and apartments, a senior CHB official said that once the project comes under the purview of the board, there would be no problem in finding buyers for the apartments.

"The flats would be sold in no time as the board will not sell them at high rates," said the official.

The developer was supposed to pay the bid money of Rs 821.21 crore to the CHB in six quarterly installments in three years. According to the terms of agreement, the payment was to be done through an Escrow agent.

But out of the total bid money, the CHB claims to have received only Rs 517 crore.

Failing to pay the bid money within the stipulated time, CHB officials will either charge penal interest or can forfeit the amount paid so far.

"If the bid amount is not paid, but there are genuine reasons for the delay we will charge penal interest with some extension.

In rare cases, however, the board can even forfeit the amount paid so far on the lapse of the period," said a senior CHB official.

When asked about the amount received by the CHB from the developer as 30 per cent of the sale proceeds from each unit, apart from the bid money, one of the senior CHB officials said, "The total sale proceeds is with the board. As per the guidelines, the total amount first comes to the board, which further transfers the developer's share of 70 per cent."

Whopping price tags?
The project, which was much talked about even before its launch in 2007, not only for its exorbitant prices (one-room studio apartment for over Rs 52 lakh, two to five bedroom apartments from Rs 1 to 3.5 crore and villas for over Rs 6 crore) had to go through a difficult patch because of the land acquisition issues.

Now the issue of the rail link from Chandigarh to Baddi is spelling trouble for the project.

Heading: Chandigarh-Baddi rail link not on track - Indian Express
Content:
city residents prefer to register residential properties under their names through transfer deeds as compared to the once more readily accepted sale deeds. This is evident from the records of the Chandigarh Sub-Registrar, where the number of residential properties registered as transfer deeds had significantly increased from 1,266 in 2007 to1,805 in 2008.

Out of the total number of documents registered with the Sub-Registrar's office from April 1, 2007 to March 31, 2008, which was 6,019, 1,805 are transfer deeds. The rest include sale deeds, gift deeds, mortgages, DOC and Trust.

With the exemption of stamp duty from transfer deeds from June 14, 2007, the records reflect the dominance of transfer deeds. The stamp duty of 6.3 per cent on Rs 24,960 per square yard (which is the per square yard property value calculated by the estate office as per guidelines) continues to be charged from the sale deeds. Now, only registration charges of a minimum 1 per cent and maximum Rs 10,000 are applicable for a transfer deed. 

As no stamp duty is involved, it has become quite popular with families where property is passed on from parents to children.

"City residents no longer wait for a will to transfer property in their name. They are getting the properties transferred through transfer deeds now.This not only serves the purpose of avoiding extended litigations and effort, but also saves the amount of tax paid as the stamp duty," said an official at the Sub-Registrar office.

Legal property advisors agree that there has been an increase in the trend to transfer property through transfer deeds."In a day, I deal with about three to four property transfer cases, with most of them being transfer deeds. The concept of sale of floors in Chandigarh, though the ownership rights are distributed as 50, 30 and 20 per cent for ground, first and second floor respectively, is another reason for parents opting for property transfer to their children's name," said a legal advisor in Sector 17.

Heading: Second blow for Maharaja City MD, police slap another case of fraud - Indian Express
Content:
The fate of the proposed Chandigarh-Baddi rail link seems to be in doldrums as the project of the Northern Railways is caught in the land acquisition tangle. The construction work on the project, which was scheduled to commence by early next year, has been under the scanner right from day one.

Parsvnath Prideasia, the housing project in collaboration with the Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) is the disputable part of the land through which the rail link will pass.

Minister of State for Railways Dr R Velu said, "There have been problems in the process of land acquisition in the past as well. Efforts are on to resolve the issue with the authorities in order to initiate the project."

The final location survey for the project has already been conducted by the railway authorities to check the feasibility of the new line. Agreeing to the fact that the rail line is facing roadblocks due to acquisition of land, a senior railway official at the Chandigarh construction office said, "The housing project is spelling trouble for the rail line."

The Chandigarh-Baddi New Broad Gauge Rail Link project with an estimated cost of Rs 750.81 crore will have a length of 33.75 kilometre. Six railway stations namely Chandigarh, Saketri, Khuda Ali Sher, Kasauli Punjab, Khokara Nawanhnagar and Baddi will fall enroute. The project alignment will consist of eleven major bridges, 27 minor bridges, two road over bridges (ROB), eight road under bridges (RUB) and nine tunnels.

A similar roadblock has been faced by the Chandigarh-Ludhiana rail link which was proposed a decade ago. At present, of the 112 kms of the rail line, about 260 acres of land has been acquired for the second phase. The entire land is still expected to be acquired by the next year. The work at three stations namely Khamano, Samrala and Madpur between Morinda and Sahnewal (Phase II) will commence after the land acquisition.

Heading: Three-day PEC fest concludes - Indian Express
Content:
Four days after a criminal case was lodged against the Managing Director of Maharaja City Rajbir Singh, the Punjab Police have slapped another criminal case against him on charges of cheating investors and violating the provisions of the Punjab Urban Development Authority Act.

Vinay Kumar, a Kurali resident, has alleged that Rajbir took an earnest money of nearly Rs 5.96 lakh from him for the transfer of Plot no 177 in Maharaja City in his name. Despite accepting the earnest money; Rajbir did not get the registered deed executed and even refused to return the earnest money, alleged Vinay in his complainant.

The police investigations also reveal that while Rajbir had got the approval-licence from the Punjab Urban Development Authority (PUDA) for Maharaja City on August 17, 2006, he had already entered into sale-agreements two to three months prior to the approval.

Station House Officer, Ropar, Sub-Inspector Sital Singh, said, "The Economic Offences Wing, investigating the matter, recommended the registration of a case, based on their inquiry on a particular complaint. We have, so far, registered two criminal cases against Rajbir, but more complaints are being investigated into by the Economic Offences wing".

The first case was registered against Rajbir on the complaint of one Ajit Singh who alleged that Rajbir had not transferred a plot in Maharaja City in his name after having taken Rs 10.35 lakh for the same.

According to the Ropar police, they received a series of complaints against Rajbir alleging that he accepted money to the tune of lakhs of rupees from them in lieu of giving them plots in Maharaja City — an 18-acre plot on the Ropar-Morinda road.

Rajbir complains of chest pain, hospitalised

Ever since Rajbir Singh was arrested on November 5 and granted two days' police custody by the Ropar court, his interrogations have been pending. The reason: Rajbir complained of severe chest pain late in the night and was taken to the Ropar Civil Hospital, where he was admitted for check up.

"He is complaining of persistent chest pain and is admitted in the hospital. After a lapse of two days, when we produced him again, he was remanded in judicial custody. He was, however, not taken to jail, as he again complained of chest pain and was sent back to the hospital, " said SHO SI Sital Singh while adding that they will seek his production warrant in the second case on Monday. The complainants, meanwhile, allege that Rajbir has been in good health and is feigning illness to avoid police interrogation.

Heading: Key witness in Harpreet murder case dies in accident - Indian Express
Content:
After three days of fun and frolic, the PEC Fest held at Punjab Engineering College concluded on Sunday.

The final day saw the final rounds of Cross-Words, Crotchet and a musical event. Events like Couture with Rags, Couple Football, Fiesta, On the Move, Nukkad Naatak (a street play competition) and JAM—Just A Minute (a literary competition) were also held.

While business wizards showed their acumen at Biz Baron, technocrats displayed their talent in Digital Graffiti.

The artistic side of students was in the limelight at Waste Marvels and Click — a photography competition.

Couples danced to romantic Spanish music in a Salsa workshop.

The finale was a star-studded event with famous singers, Hard Kaur and Lambher Hussainpuriyab setting the crowd on fire.

Heading: Student held for rape, making obscene MMS - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Balwinder Singh Sohal, a senior government doctor who is a key witness in the case of murder of Harpreet Kaur, daughter of former SGPC chief Bibi Jagir Kaur, died in a road accident near Jandiala Guru late last night.

Dr Sohal was coming to Amritsar when his Maruti Zen car was hit by a truck coming from the opposite direction on the GT Road. He was rushed to the local Guru Ram Das Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. Dr Sohal, who was posted at Ran Singh village's primary health centre in the neighbouring Tarn Taran district, had deposed as a key witness in the Harpreet murder case registered in 2000, in which Bibi Jagir Kaur is the main accused apart from seven others.

"It looks like an accident. We have registered a case, and the truck driver has been arrested," said Jandiala Guru DSP Hardev Singh.

Heading: Technical institutes give thumbs up to AICTE decisions - Indian Express
Content:
A student of Plus One in Bhuchho has been arrested for allegedly filming obscene video of his girlfriend, a student of Class X, after "administering" her an intoxicant.

DSP (Rural) Joginder Singh said Preet Kanwal Singh, who is the son of a Junior Engineer in Lehra Mohabbat Thermal Plant, allegedly placed the obscene MMS online and circulated its CDs. The girl's father, who runs a shop in Lehra Mohabbat, claimed that the family came to know of the MMS after the girl jumped off the roof of the house in mid-September and had to be hospitalised.

He said his daughter and the accused were friends and used to travel in the same bus to school. While Preet Kanwal or any of his family members could not be contacted, the DSP said a case was registered after a complaint was lodged, accusing the boy of "repeatedly raping" the "victim" and making her obscene video.

Heading: ‘Obama’s win comes as a blessing for the coloured races’ - Indian Express
Content:
The technical institutes in the state have lauded the efforts of the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) for the different decisions it has taken to ensure the optimum utilisation of resources and reduction in the running-cost of institutions.

Punjab Unaided Technical Institutions Association (PUTIA) President Dr J S Dhaliwal said the permission for conduction evening engineering and polytechnic colleges would lead to the best use of infrastructure.
