Dr Zora Singh, senior vice-president, PUTIA, added that the concept of having an integrated campus with multiple disciplines would allow the common use of facilities like library and computer lab in the big campuses for the morning and evening sessions in the college.

Anshu Kataria, media secretary, PUTIA, said that the 20 per cent land relaxation comes as a major relief for the existing and new institutions.

He welcomed the move for permitting BBA and BCA classes in the existing colleges for MBA and MCA.

PUTIA members also appreciated the AICTE for the ground work done in calculating a national average ratio of the number of seats to the existing population.

Heading: Congress is a pro-poor party, says Bansal - Indian Express
Content:
WINNY KAUSHALMSc, Food & Nutrition Government Home Science College Sector 10

The entire world appears to have been enveloped in the Barack "Obamania" after his victory in the US Presidential elections. It is a move that has been welcomed by everyone, irrespective of caste, colour or creed.

With Obama becoming the President of the USA, the American democracy has come of age. He was born at a time when even the effort of voting put in by a "coloured" person invited death sentence. And now, America has one such president.

Obama, however, should realise that holding the most important office in the world has its share of responsibilities. He has to address several issues, including the Iraq problem and the ever-increasing tentacles of Taliban.

His predecessor has left a "bed of thorns" and the new president-elect is expected to have several sleepless nights before he savours the bitter-sweet fruit of his triumph.

Obama's victory comes as a blessing for the coloured races and the immigrants residing in America. The US has always been infamous for its racial discrimination.

The hate crimes that were unleashed after 9/11 are proof enough that Americans have a dominant streak of racism in them. The pride of being a "white" has made them overlook humanity and their collective responsibility as a civilised society.

For once, the coloured can hope to breathe easy. There is a flicker of hope that racial discrimination will now be dealt

with by someone who has experienced it first hand.

Obama's win may also prove beneficial for the Indo-Pak ties. While George Bush was always accused of having a biased stand when it came to Pakistan, the change of guard may help the relationship between the two neighbours.

Obama must not forget that the entire world is watching him with great expectations. He needs to work hard to justify

his victory.

Heading: Ambala traders get threat calls for ransom - Indian Express
Content:
"Need-based changes made by residents must be regularised," said Union Minister of State for Finance Pawan Kumar Bansal while speaking at a public meeting organised by the Chandigarh Territorial Youth Congress (CTYC) and the Resident Welfare Association in Sector 30-B, on Sunday. The minister addressed public meetings in other parts of the city as well. Speaking at a meeting in Vikas Nagar, Mauli Jagaran, Bansal said the Congress is a "pro-poor party" and that it is committed to uplifting the poor and downtrodden sections of the society. CTYC President H S Lucky also attacked the Bharatiya Janata Party for its "double standards" and stated that during the BJP regime, onions were sold at Rs 100 per kg.

BJP says budgetory cuts for state a cruel joke
The Central Government's move to impose a cut of nearly Rs 139 crore in the state budgetary allocations for the year has drawn flak from former BJP parliamentarian Satya Pal Jain. Jain said the decision of the Congress-led UPA government is "a cruel joke" for the residents while he was addressing public meetings in Sector 45-D, Sector 47-D, Colony Number 5, Dhanas, Palsora and other places on Sunday to mobilise support for the 'Vijay Sankalp Rally' scheduled for November 16. Jain said the city residents pay nearly Rs 1000 crore annually as taxes to the Central Government and despite this, their budgetary allocations are being reduced instead of being increased.

Heading: Tread the path shown by martyrs: minister - Indian Express
Content:
Panic gripped Ambala Cantonment after two businessmen received threat calls seeking Rs 50 lakh as ransom, failing which they would be gunned down.

The calls were received by a trader at Pul Chameli bazaar. Some unidentified persons fired a gunshot near the residence of the trader. The incident was followed by a call, presumed to have been made from Hapur (Uttar Pradesh). The caller warned him to pay money or he would be shot dead.

A property dealer in the city also received a similar threatening call.

In the recent days, businessmen receiving threat calls has been a regular occurance in the city. Earlier, a software manufacturer and Haryana Janhit Congress leader Tilk Raj Taneja received several ransom calls. Besides Taneja, an LPG dealer Capt Baldev Singh and a practicing doctor Ashok Goel had also received threatening calls for ransom.

Heading: Rising prices of chicken, fish leave a bitter taste in the mouth - Indian Express
Content:
Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Consumer Affairs Dr Akhilesh Prasad Singh called upon the people of country to tread the path shown by the great martyrs who made supreme sacrifice for the protection of their religion and the country's honour.

He was speaking at a function organised by Bhai Mati Dass Commemoration Society to mark the 333rd year of martyrdom of Bhai Mati Dass at Rampur Sarseri village in Ambala Cantonment on Sunday.

He said that their sacrifice had relevance when the country was threatened by subversive forces to divide the country on the basis of religion, region and language. He asked the countrymen to work for the unity and integrity of the country.

Former Punjab Governor Lt Gen (Retd) B K N Chhiber also paid tributes to the martyrs.

Ambala Division commissioner Mohinder Kumar, ex-MLA Anil Vij and others were present on the occasion.

Heading: It Rocks! - Indian Express
Content:
For the non-vegetarian consumers, eating is all set to become dearer with the prices of chicken, fish and eggs, all experiencing a rise in prices.

While the prices of chicken have risen by almost Rs 60 per kg to be currently valued at Rs 140 per kg, eggs, at Rs 30 per dozen, have also become dearer by Rs 2 per dozen over the last week.

Even fish-lovers are shelling out more this year with the Sea Sole variety currently priced at Rs 180 per kg, almost 25 per cent more compared to the last year.

The Singhada variety has also experienced a marginal increase of Rs 10 compared to last year's price of Rs 140 per kg.

"The prices of chicken and fish appear to have gone beyond the reach of the common man now. For chicken lovers, the rise in prices is definitely a let down," said Prabhsher Singh, a resident of Sector 21.

Heading: Resident of Janta Colony stabbed - Indian Express
Content:
Studio, school, website, band practice, mixing music...Nirdosh's days are literally jampacked!

"There never is a schedule," a long yawn and wide stretch later, Nirdosh gets ready for the next leg of the session.

It's Sunday and he's been locked in his studio since 11 am. "My days are full of targets, one after the other, which basically translates into no breaks, no recess — just one long gruelling session of recording, practice and meetings," smiles the 22-year-old musician, part of an award-winning rock band called De Innovatives.

Nirdosh also runs a music school aptly titled School of Rock, where he teaches the guitar and drums.

"Apart from this, it's non-stop work on our first album, upgrading our website and practice sessions for our next concert."

Breakfast down; Nirdosh's day begins with recording in his studio. Money is of

the essence, therefore, multi-tasking is

the norm.

"I can't afford to hire assistants or helpers at this struggling stage," he winks, shaking off the cobwebs of sleep.

"Slept at 5:30 in the morning, was judging a music contest at Punjab Engineering College," he explains.

In the evening, Nirdosh is ready to program the drumming. "The drummer is absent, so I've got to do this," he's right when he says nothing is planned.

In another hour or so, the band members will walk in and the jammin' session will kickstart. "Anything for the spirit of rock!"

"There's another thing actually. We've entered A R Rahman's Big Band reality show and need to compose tracks for it — one Bollywood interpretation and one which Rahman's given. I like his tune because it's classical and I've trained in it."

He has his fingers crossed for if they get the three-year contract, his life will be on a roll!

Well, while this is one of the major concerns, there are couple of others lurking on the periphery — "a concert on the 14th at CEC Landran, a website by end of this month, find sponsors for the album, fix a photo shoot for tomorrow, band practice" — yes, we get it! "See, I never know when will I get to sleep!"

Anything for music.

—Jaskiran Kapoor

Heading: Panchkula gangrape: youth to be quizzed missing after summons - Indian Express
Content:
A 34-year-old resident of Janta Colony, Sector 25, was reportedly stabbed by eight assailants while returning home from the Sector-24 police post late on Saturday night. The victim sustained injuries on the head, chest and arms and was rushed to the PGI. Dharamveer works in a cycle puncture repair shop.

According to the police, the attack was a result of a scuffle that broke out between the victim's brothers and a rival group, led by one Jai Bhagwan, two hours before the incident. The police had rounded up several youth for preventive action at the Sector-24 police post and Dharamveer had gone there to meet his brothers. As he set out for his house, he was allegedly attacked by members of the rival group.

Six people have been booked while a one minor was arrested under Section 324 IPC (voluntarily causing hurt), Section 506 IPC (criminal intimidation) and Sections 147 and 148 (rioting) under of the IPC. "Investigations are on to nab the remaining accused," said a police officer.

Heading: ‘A tunnel network in Kashmir is an option worth considering’ - Indian Express
Content:
While the 10-day summon period for Chanky Sharma alias Sunny, whose role is being probed in the Panchkula rape case, ends on Monday, the police and his family are still clueless on his whereabouts.

"It was after the call details of the victim's cellphone were taken, that the summons to the family of Chanky Sharma were issued nearly 10 days ago. The same youth was called for investigations earlier as well," said Inspector Surjit Kumar, Station House Officer, Sector 14, who is the Investigating officer (IO) in the case.

Sharma's family, meanwhile, claims to have applied for an anticipatory bail in the Punjab and Haryana High Court and add that the court had directed the police to give a 10 days' minimum prior notice to the youth before summoning him for investigation.

The family maintains that they are not aware of the whereabouts of their son who has been missing since the day the summon period began.

Sharma's mother said, "My son has no involvement in the case and is being harassed by the police.

The whereabouts of Sunny are not known to anyone from the day he was called by the police for investigation and was manhandled by them."

The rape victim, meanwhile, denied the role of Sunny in the crime, claiming that he was "only her friend".

"I know him from quite sometime and we used to talk on the phone. As far as his involvement in the case is concerned, he has no role to play in it," said the victim.

Eventful Monday

* 10-day summon notice period of Chanky Sharma ends.

* Hearing of anticipatory bail application of Kushal Kaushal, whose car was allegedly used in the crime, to be heard in the additional session's court.

* Family of victim to move High Court for cancellation of the bail of Aman Ahuja who was earlier arrested in the case.

Heading: ‘Maharashtra violence indicates extreme behavioural practice’ - Indian Express
Content:
Gone are the days when countries relied only on conventional methods for fighting war. The time has now come to stun the enemy with localised nuclear and biological attack. It is evident with the efforts that China and India are making to score over each other, if a war breaks out.

The Army is contemplating the idea of building deep tunnels in Kashmir, along its borders with China and Pakistan, to protect its troops from nuclear, chemical and biological attacks, if any, at the hands of the two countries.

There have been threats coming from Pakistan of a possible use of nuclear weapons against India. While the retaliatory action by India could virtually wipe out Pakistan from the international map, it is, nonetheless, preferable to equip ourselves against any lethal attacks.

Our intelligence agencies confirm the reports that China has undertaken the construction of a large-scale tunnel project on the border between India and China's Tibetan region. It is, therefore, the need of the hour for India to start building its tunnel network to thwart any attack from China in the event of a war.

Border disputes have plagued relations between India and China for decades, and had also led to war in 1962. While India has claims that Beijing is "illegally holding" a part of Kashmir, China lays stakes on large tracts of Arunachal Pradesh. On the other hand, both India and Pakistan, since Independence, have been fighting for Kashmir, which has already been divided into two parts, each controlled by India and Pakistan.

China has been increasing its defence budget every year by 15 to 18 per cent. The kind of investments that China is making in research and development can pose a threat to India in the future. While they have already constructed roads and other defence-oriented structures on the border, the tunnels, now, are a major cause for concern.

We have already lost men and land to our neighbouring countries. To avert such situations, the strategy should be to prevent enemies from gauging our strength. A tunnel network in Kashmir is an option worth considering.

Heading: Forum tells institute to refund Rs 15,000 to student - Indian Express
Content:
"We have established ourselves in the international arena and the signing of the nuclear deal is a huge success for the country," said former Union Minister of State for External Affairs, Salman Khurshid, while interacting with the media in the city on Sunday.

Khurshid added that the victory of the Democrats in the US presidential elections is not just a cause for passing excitement to India and that in the wake of the global meltdown, outsourcing of industries and businesses stand as important political issues for America.

"The issue of terrorism can be dealt with by streamlining land issues, particularly in tribal areas, providing job opportunities, avoiding any kind of ideological mistakes and lopsided development," added the former minister.

Speaking of the challenges in the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections, Khurshid listed out social justice, empowerment of weaker sections and free education as priorities.

The minister added that nearly 90 districts have been identified as "Special Institution Districts", which will be provided with special funding in education and other progressive programmes for minorities.

Khurshid announced that Mohammed Abid Khan will contest polls from Uttar Pradesh as an independent candidate, backed by the Congress and the Samajwadi Party.

Asked about his comments on the recent outburst of Margaret Alva over the sale of tickets for Rajya Sabha seats, Khurshid said, "The disciplinary committee will decide on the issue." While speaking on Raj Thackeray's way of politics, Khurshid termed the happenings in Maharashtra as an "extreme behavioural practice".

He, however, chose to reserve his comments when asked if the Left could be expected to be part of the UPA after the Lok Sabha elections.

'Landscape architecture will undo damage to ecology'
Chandigarh: Landscape architecture will act as a rejuvenating tool for undoing the widespread damage to ecology and the natural environment, said Salman Khurshid, former Minister of State for External Affairs and a senior Congress leader. He was delivering a talk on 'Emerging Trends in Landscape Architecture' at a conference organised by the Saakaar Foundation at Government Museum and Art Gallery, Sector 10, on Sunday.

Khurshid stated that with the dismal scenario of the world's environment, the nature and scope of the application of landscape architecture has been further enhanced.

The first lecture on 'European Landscape Architecture' was delivered by Professor Günther Vogt, a landscape architect and author from Switzerland. He spoke about the emerging trends in landscape architecture at a global level.

This was followed by a presentation by Dr Mustafa Var, Director of the Forestry, Research and Application Centre at Karadeniz Technical University, Turkey. He deliberated on urban transformation of the slum areas by proposing a green texture and rehabilitating the settlers to a modern and healthy residential area.

Summing up the session, architect-planner Jit K Gupta said that urban transformation is a valuable instrument to make cities more livable, productive, sustainable and supportive of an assured quality of life.

Andy Schönholzer, a landscape architect from Zurich, gave a presentation on 'Urban Transformation Processes' wherein he elaborated on a project in Switzerland which was refurbished on the pattern of Chandigarh in terms of planning.

Olivier Lasserre, a landscape architect, biologist and photographer from Switzerland, made an audio visual presentation. He commented that the landscape pattern may be different in Chandigarh and Switzerland on a cultural or botanical level, but it is essentially the same in its relations with the territory.

Professor Samir Mathur spoke on 'Cities, Open Spaces and Modernity'. He said: "Modernity is an ever-changing virtue and is independent of mere form and mortal beauty. Since open spaces in cities are an inseparable part of the daily lives of its citizens, it becomes essential to realise the direct and indirect impact of modernity on these spaces. These spaces define the character of the city and its inhabitants."

Landscape architect Aarti Grover presented her study titled 'Open Space Structure of Chandigarh' and gave certain suggestions to improve the city's environment.

S K Sharma, president of the Environment Society of Chandigarh, underlined the value of preserving heritage trees and ponds.

Recommendations

* Need for a common controlling authority for the city and its periphery

* Need for a comprehensive landscape development plan for the city

* Rehabilitation solutions for slum-dwellers

* Strengthening of buffer between industrial and residential zones

* To frame a department dedicated to landscape architecture

Heading: CN & Heard - Indian Express
Content:
Upholding an order of the Panchkula district consumer forum, the UT State Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed a private management institute to refund Rs 15,000 to a student and pay Rs 5,000 as compensation. The institute will also have to pay Rs 2,000 as litigation costs. The order was passed by the Panchkula district forum in 2001.

The complainant, Preetinder Singh Brar, had received admission in the MCA course at the Indian Institute of Management and Computers, Industrial Area, Phase II, Panchkula. The institute's director had told him that the centre was affiliated to the Madurai Kamraj University. After he deposited Rs 15,000 as fee, he was assured that if he was unable to clear the entrance test, the amount would be refunded.

But Brar averred that he was neither informed of the date of the entrance examination, nor was he admitted to the regular course. Later, he discovered that the institute was not an authorised centre of Madurai Kamraj University either.

In reply, the counsel for the institute said that their advertisement did not state that their centre was affiliated to any university. Also, the brochure had merely stated that the curriculum was based on the one at the Madurai Kamraj University and IGNOU. The fee charged was for coaching and not for a regular course. They also stated that the respondent attended classes for over a year commencing on July 1998, and as such they were not liable to refund the amount.

The commission found that the prospectus does not state that the institute is a coaching centre at all. Also, there is no documentary evidence that the student had attended coaching classes for the MCA course, thus amounting to unfair trade practice.

Heading: Hans Raj to sing Akali tune this poll opera - Indian Express
Content:
Fabulous Three
At a time when the cricketing scribes are paying glowing tributes to the fabulous three of Indian batting viz Tendulkar, Ganguly and Dravid, people in Chandigarh are drawing parallels to a troika in UT politics. Messers Harmohan Dhawan, Satpal Jain and Pawan Bansal have been contesting elections from time immemorial. In fact, most people's living memories fail to think of any other name on city's political firmament. These three are crossing swords for the fifth time. But whereas the three batsmen have played a remarkable role in the success of Indian cricket and are now in the autumn of their careers, with one of them already having announced his retirement, the city would have to bear with the politico trinity for many more years to come.

Robin Hood
It is not often that the Chief Minister of Punjab loses his temper. But in the press conference last week, Parkash Singh Badal got visibly irritated when a scribe put a question as to from where would he collect money for the various welfare schemes and subsidies that he keeps on announcing. To strengthen his argument, the journalist quoted some not so impressive figures about the state's finances. This got the goat of the Chief Minister who snapped, "Well, if need arises we would commit dacoity to collect funds for public welfare." Did we hear you say - Robin Hood?

Good economics
Badal might not be averse to 'adapt' drastic measures to provide money for state's welfare schemes. But leader of Opposition Rajinder Kaur Bhattal has suddenly adapted a very 'rational' and 'dispassionate' view on state's finances. In a latest press note issued by her office in her name, she lambasted not only the Akalis but also the previous Congress governments, blaming them for state's miserable finances. Her new avatar of preaching economic discipline has left everyone stunned and her censure of her own party has perplexed several of her colleagues.

Unisexual
Sample this highly interesting conversation overheard in a highly exclusive party featuring two prominent personalities of the city. One of them, a man of taste and flamboyance, was showing off a latest perfume which he claimed to have purchased from Paris. The person he was seeking to impress did like its fragrance and may be the thought of gifting it to a loved one crossed his mind. He asked, "Is it bi-sexual?". Realising that he had committed a faux pas and could be an object of ridicule, a well-wisher standing nearby asked, "He wants to know if the perfume is unisexual." But apparently our man was so impressed by the new perfume that he seemed curiously incapable of realising his verbal mistake or of suffering any embarrassment. He continued with his enquiry, "Yeah that is what I asked. Is it bisexual? Can it be used both by women and men?" Ahem!

Silence is golden
If you think the concept of back-benchers is associated only with classrooms, here's an eye opener. A number of Councillors of Municipal Corporation are known to occupy these benches during every House Meet. Just like the blissfully ignorant students, they, too, do not have much idea about the proceedings of the House or the issues raised. In fact some are yet to strain their vocal chords. With councillors elected by the people to be their voice, it leaves many wondering at the selection.

Heading: Advani raps media’s role during Emergency - Indian Express
Content:
Sufi singer to contest from Jalandhar LS seat

Within minutes of state singer and Sain of Lal Badshah Darbar Hans Raj Hans' joining the SAD (B) today, he was declared the party candidate from Jalandhar for the coming Lok Sabha elections.

However, many Akalis were not happy over this announcement, as they felt that Hans had made no contribution to the party. Notably, Jalandhar had become a reserved seat after delimitation.

Former BSP leader Pawan Kumar Tinu, who had joined the SAD along with his supporters after leaving the Bhujan Kranti Dal, was also looking dejected, as he was also in the race for a party ticket. He was assured a suitable place and former SAD candidate from Jalandhar Naresh Gujral had openly urged Sukhbir Badal to give him a ticket.

However, Tinu was given the post of SAD Joint Secretary and promised an Assembly ticket in the next elections.

Till date, the SAD has announced four candidates for the LS elections, including Dr Rattan Singh Ajnala from Khadoor Sahib, SS Dhindsa from Sangrur, Deputy LS Speaker Charnajit Singh Atwal from Fatehgarh Sahib and Hans Raj Hans.

In the last polls, Naresh Gujral had fought from Jalandhar.

Heading: Suit Yourself - Indian Express
Content:
At a function organised by a media organisation, the leader of Opposition and BJP's Prime Ministerial candidate Lal Krishan Advani here today criticised the role played by the media during Emergency.

Addressing the second national convention of the Indian Media Centre (IMC), organised in collaboration with the Centre for Communication and International Linkage, Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Advani said, "When I became the Information and Broadcasting Minister in 1977, once I told the scribes that during Emergency, the Indira government wanted the journalists to just bend, but many of them started crawling."

He said it were the lawyers and judges who did a commendable job during Emergency. "Even the lawyer who pursued our cases was arrested and jailed when Atal Behari Vajpayee, other Opposition leaders and I were lodged in the Rohtak jail," he said. Advani said, "Even the British had not arrested any lawyer for defending freedom fighters."

Advani said during Emergency, the Indira government had repealed the Parliamentary Proceedings (Protection of Publication) Bill, 1977, popularly known as the Feroze Gandhi Act. "When I became the I&B Minister, I got the ordinance re-enacted," he added.

Asserting that the media should adopt self-regulation, Advani said, "We should use media to promote good governance and value-based politics. The trivialisation and sensationalising of news should be discouraged."

CM Parkash Singh Badal exhorted mediapersons to discharge their duties with dedication and sincerity because they owe the responsibility of strengthening the democratic system of the country. Badal appreciated the efforts of IMC for playing an instrumental role in projecting the developmental policies and programmes of the state. Capt Kanwaljit Singh, Cooperative Minister; Hira Singh Gabria, Jails Minister; Master Mohan Lal, Transport Minister; MP Chandan Mitra, who is also the Chairman of IMC; Irwin Khanna, Chairman of IMC's Punjab chapter, and Shyam Khosla, Director, IMC, also spoke on the occasion .

On LS polls

LK Advani said the NDA would contest the next Lok Sabha elections on the common minimum programme of good governance. About Punjab, he said their party would continue with the earlier seat-sharing arrangement. On Raj Thackeray's acts, Advani said the NDA had already condemned them.

Heading: Fiery Gordimer slams Naipaul, praises Tagore and Rushdie - Indian Express
Content:
'Performing a play in Chandigarh is such a significant moment for me,' Neelam Man Singh Chowdhry on her brand-new production, The Suit

It was long-awaited — the staging of Neelam Man Singh Chowdhry's latest play, The Suit, which opened at the Rangshankara Festival in October 2007. And almost a year later, the director is set to stage it for the Chandigarh audiences. Presented by People For Animals (PFA), the play has been sponsored totally, "and 100 per cent burden is off my head," Neelam agrees that the organizational aspect is a logistic nightmare for her and she was very relieved not to wear too many hats. According to Payal Sodhi of PFA, by supporting art, culture, they are looking for support from the city, to help them branch out, "and I'm so happy with the response from our sponsors. People here have really opened up to our work and concern.''

"The inspiration for my work comes from this city, this environment has nurtured me, so performing here is so significant and exciting, for my actors of The Company and me,'' the play has been inspired by a three-page story by South African writer Can Themba and deals with a cruel moral dilemma faced by a young married couple. The husband discovers his wife in bed with her lover. The lover flees, leaving his suit behind. The husband then forces the woman to treat the abandoned suit as an honoured guest, accompanying them even on walks and at the dinner table. Though intended as a constant and tormenting reminder of infidelity, the suit becomes a witness as much to the husband's own misery as to the slow mental disintegration of the wife.

Neelam recalls seeing the play in '95 at the Tricycle Theatre in London during the London International Festival of Theatre (LIFT). "Performed in a realistic manner, I was moved by it and kept using it as a reference and sub-consciously, I wanted to move into another genre," Neelam says that the play is deeply rooted in the politics of South Africa and the presence of the suit in the play is a metaphor for apartheid. Neelam says the political metaphors did not work for her at all, as she cannot work on a decontextualized frame. Dramatized by Surjit Patar, Neelam says a lot of improvisation, team-work and character building went into the production. "The play is apolitical with no agenda. While reading the story I felt anger of the characters, their sense of being betrayed by their own natures. It may appear a simple tale of a husband and wife and loyalty, but ultimately, theatre becomes a courtroom in which we judge ourselves and our mysteries. Is the husband guilty of brutalizing his wife? Is his wife guilty of adultery? Was he angry, and she lonely? it is for theatre to mediate."

The Suit will be staged at the Rock Garden from November 12 to 16 at 7 pm.

Heading: Lucky numbers behind Obama’s rise: surgeon - Indian Express
Content:
She's a small woman and seemingly fragile but, even at 84, Nadine Gordimer remains outspoken as ever.

The South African Nobel Laureate and social activist, who was in Mumbai on Sunday, spoke strongly of her likes and dislikes among Indian authors. She rattled of a list of those she admires: "Rabindranath Tagore, Nayantara Sahgal, R K Narayanan, Shashi Tharoor, and of course, the great Salman Rushdie," she said.

"I also read Arvind Adiga's White Tiger. It is brilliantly written, but he's stressed the more shocking aspects of society too much. He tends to rub it in a bit," she smiled.

She heaped praise on Sahgal's Mistaken Identity. In today's world, on account of terrorism's threat, "we all have become suspects...like prisoners we go through security checks," she said.

But Gordimer was not too charitable about Indian-born Nobel winner writer V S Naipaul. Naipaul, she said, was a great writer, but "his novel on Africa is too racist".

The outspoken author also expressed her strong political views. She criticised the present political situation in her country. "The African National Congress has split and I'm torn," said Gordimer, who had joined the ANC when it was still banned. "On the one hand I feel loyal to my old party. But I find the man who has caused the rift, Jacob Zuma, to be morally dubious. He's populist and promises everything and he's not afraid of advocating violence."

She was speaking at a special book-reading session and interaction at the Durbar Hall of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai. She had been invited by the Sahitya Akademi of India and the Asiatic Society of Mumbai; the interaction was arranged by the Ministry of External Affairs.

Even the choice of story to read from reflected her strong feelings. She had picked the right story to read in these times of turmoil, she told her audience.

"I was going to read something from my last book, Beethoven Was One-Sixteenth Black and Other Stories," she said, "but I decided that with the terrible happenings in the world - children starving in an endless cycle of violence and immigration - it would be more appropriate to read The Ultimate Safari, a story about a little girl and her family fleeing to South Africa from civil war in Mozambique."

Telling the story from the point of view of a little girl came easily to her. "The BBC was shooting a documentary in the refugee camps and I'd accompanied them. When I saw the children, I had the urge to put myself in their shoes. I realised that what I'd just heard about — the trek these people make through the Kruger National Park — is the ultimate safari and that's how the story came to be written."

She was critical of the modern habit of relying more on images and relegating reading to a secondary position. "The written word is becoming less and less relied upon for its ability to impart information," she said.

Gordimer has won international acclaim for The Lying Days, July's People and The Conservationist. Her impressive body of work, peppered with political activism, won her the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1991.

She was active in the fight against apartheid in her home country. Her outspokenness on race issues led to two of her books, Burger's Daughter and The Late Bourgeois World, being banned by the apartheid government.

Recently, she's campaigned against the South African government's stance on HIV/AIDS; in 2004, she organised 20 major writers to contribute short fiction for Telling Tales, a fundraising book for South Africa's Treatment Action Campaign, which lobbies for government funding for HIV/AIDS prevention and cure.

(With PTI inputs)

Heading: Grilled twice by cops, Raj wants to skip court - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty-one sailors have died in an accident on board a Russian nuclear submarine that was to have been leased to the Indian Navy next year. Another 21 sailors were injured after deadly Freon gas leaked from the submarine's fire extinguishing system during sea trials off Vladivostok Saturday night.

The Akula II class 'Nerpa' nuclear attack submarine was to have joined the Navy as the INS Chakra on August 15, 2009 on a 10-year lease. A first batch of 40 Indian naval personnel was scheduled to leave New Delhi next week to train on the submarine later this month.

The Navy refused to comment on the incident that took place "on a Russian boat with a Russian crew on board". But the accident may delay the induction, as New Delhi now insists on more tests before accepting the submarine.

Initial reports received by the Navy, however, indicate that the submarine has not suffered any major structural or reactor damage, and the gas leak could have been the result of a human error. All the dead and injured have been identified as Russian naval personnel and shipyard technicians.

"The extent of damage does not seem to be much as it is just a gas leak and no structural damage has been reported. More checks may be required to ensure that everything onboard is functional but we don't anticipate it to delay things too much," a senior officer said.

The Akula II class nuclear attack submarine is the most modern in Russia's fleet, and also its quietest and deadliest. It was launched in 1991 at the Komsomolsk-on-Amur shipyard, but was put into cold storage before completion due to financial constraints. The project was revived after India showed interest in leasing a nuclear attack submarine to train its sailors for a future class of indigenous nuclear submarines, and work on the refitting was completed this June. Last month, the shipyard announced that the submarine had been moved after factory trials to a temporary facility near Vladivostok on the Pacific Ocean, where it would undergo a series of sea trials.

India and Russia have never officially acknowledged that the 'Nerpa' is to be inducted into the Indian Navy, though Indian naval officers and men have been training at Russian facilities to operate the submarine. In a candid admission with this newspaper in December last year, Navy Chief Admiral Sureesh Mehta had admitted that the Navy was looking for a nuclear submarine to train its men on the future class of indigenous Advance Technology Vessel (ATV) nuclear submarines.

"We have not been operating on a nuclear platform and had taken the 'Chakra' on lease from Russia earlier. Now we want one more Akula sub to train our boys on how to operate a nuclear platform," Admiral Mehta had told The Indian Express.

The Akula II class vessel will be the second nuclear submarine to be leased by Russia to India after the 'Chakra' Charlie I class nuclear attack sub that was leased for four years from 1988. Unofficial estimates put the cost of the submarine at close to $1 billion.

Heading: Attack on Burney’s office condemned - Indian Express
Content:
For the second day in a row, Maharashtra Navnnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray presented before the Government Railway Police (GRP) at Kalyan in connection with attacks by MNS activists against aspirants who had turned up to take a railway recruitment board exam at Kalyan and Dombivili last month.

Thackeray, along with trusted aides, turned up at the Kalyan police station where he was questioned by Assistant Commissioner of Police S S Sarvade and Senior Police Inspector Ashok Jadhav regarding attacks on examinees at Kalyan and Manpada on October 19.

According to advocate Sambhaji Patil, a party member who was present during the police inquiry, Thackeray had turned up at the Kalyan GRP police station at 11 am on Saturday, and at the same time on Sunday. "The inquiry did not last for more than 30-40 minutes. The inquiry may well be in its concluding stages and we hope that Rajsaheb will not have to come again," Patil said.

The hearing in the MNS attack case at the Kalyan GRP will come before the Kalyan railway court on Monday. Advocate Patil said Thackeray would seek exemption from appearing for the court hearings, a decision on which lies at the discretion of the court.

Thackeray is being questioned in the two cases for his role in inciting party members to attack the examinees for the railway recruitment board exams at Kalyan and Manpada at Dombivli on October 19, 2008. The Kalyan GRP have booked 18 MNS activists for rioting, assault and other charges in the FIR lodged with them, while 27 have been booked for the attack that happened under the jurisdiction of Dombivli's Manpada police station.

The accused MNS activists have since been released on bail.

Heading: Speeding bus kills 60-yr-old - Indian Express
Content:
The firing at the office of human rights activist Dr Ansar Burney in Karachi was condemned by several activists including director Mahesh Bhatt.

Ansar Burney's residence was attacked by unidentified gunmen on Friday, November 7.

The gunmen, reportedly, came in cars and fired many rounds at the ground floor of the office of the Ansar Burney Trust at Arambagh road in Pakistan's port city of Karachi.

Burney was present in the office at the time of firing. However he escaped unhurt.

The incident occurred less than a fortnight after the government withdrew his police security. Five guards posted at his home in Karachi and two armed bodyguards assigned to him were withdrawn on the eve of his visit to India to accept the third Mother Teresa Memorial International Award for human rights and social justice. The award was presented to Burney on October 26.

State minorities commission vice-chairperson Dr Abraham Mathai said that Burney has received many death threats for his work, including his campaign to save Indian prisoner Sarabjit Singh.

Heading: Thirteen arrested for assault on Dalit family - Indian Express
Content:
A Sixty-year-old man was killed on Sunday when a speeding private bus hit him. The bus belongs to Shreeji travels. It was speeding along the highway near Ramabai Ambedkar Nagar in Ghatkopar and collided with an electric pole and hit the man killing him.

Three children between ages three and seven and a laborer in his twenties also sustained minor injuries. According to the Police sub-inspector Mohan Sable of Pantnagar who is the investigating officer in the case, the driver Shantkumar "Sabanna (24) was heading towards Kandivali from Sindhudurg when he crashed into the electric pole. Sabanna lost control over the wheel and the bus climbed the pavement. Gopal Bhima Patil was taking a morning walk when the bus went over his foot. He also sustained a head injury leading to his death. Road construction activity was also underway at the site and three small children of labourers and a worker Gopal Rathod (45) was injured," said Sable.

However he added that the children and Rathod have suffered only superficial injuries and will be discharged from hospital soon.

The police have arrested Sabanna for rash and negligent driving.

Heading: Approver in Pradeep Jain murder case turns hostile - Indian Express
Content:
The family is unhappy as the man who allegedly led the attack is still at large

Thirteen persons have been arrested in connection with the assault on nine members of a Dalit family in Deravali village that took place on Tuesday night. While the New Panvel police, which made the arrest, claim to have beefed up security at the village, the Gaikwad family is unable to overcome their fears as the prime accused is still at large.

Deputy Commissioner of Police Ashok Dudhe said, "Two teams sent out to nab the accused made the arrests on Friday. Meanwhile the medical reports of one

of the victims revealed that his injury was serious in nature. In addition to booking the accused under the Rioting Act, Atrocities Act, Arms Act and Bombay Police Act, we have also booked them for attempt to murder."Dudhe added that though the situation at the village is peaceful, the security has been increased with four constables positioned in the area. However Harishchandra and Narendra Gaikwad who are recuperating in the hospital along with seven other family members of their family, are wary of the course that the investigation is taking.

"They have arrested all the other accused except Vishnu Namdeo Bhoir who led the attack against us. Though we gave names of 14 persons whom we could clearly identify, they were a part of a larger group of around 40 -45 persons. With Bhoir still at large, the possibility of him instigating another attack can't be ruled out," said Gaikwad.

"With nine of us male members in the hospital, our house back in the village has women members now and we worry about their safety," said Harishchandra.

Heading: Rs 5,000-crore project makes corporators tread cautiously - Indian Express
Content:
One of the two approvers in the 1995 Pradeep Jain murder case against extradited gangster Abu Salem, has turned hostile. The prosecution is now contemplating making him an accused in the case again. 

Riyaz Siddiqui who is in jail for his alleged role in the 1993 serial bomb blast case and is also a cellmate of Salem at the Arthur Road Jail was arrested in the Jain murder case by the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) of Mumbai police soon after Salem was extradited to India in November 2005. Siddiqui was believed to be part of the conspiracy where Salem is alleged to have ordered the killing of Jain after he had a tiff with him, over a piece of land owned by Jain's family in Andheri.

According to the police, Siddiqui had in 2007, moved an application requesting pardon as he had turned an approver. The Special Terrorist and Disruptive Activities Act (TADA) court had made him and another accused Naeem Khan, approvers in the case. The court granted them pardon under section 306 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC) under which an accused can be granted pardon, 'on condition of his making a full and true disclosure of the circumstances within his knowledge relative to the offence and to every other person concerned'. Once a person becomes an approver, a confessional statement of the approvers is recorded before a magistrate and the accused is then treated as a prosecution witness and at after the judgment is pronounced acquitted.

As per Siddiqui's statement he was present at the conspiracy meetings called by Salem and Anees Ibrahim, brother of underworld don Dawood Ibrahim in Dubai. He also narrated the entire Jain murder plot.

However, recently when Siddiqui stepped into the dock he did not support the prosecution and denied Salem's as well as his role in the Jain murder case, a TADA court source said. The prosecution declared him hostile and he was also cross-examined by the prosecution. Special Public prosecutor in the case Ujjwal Nikam refused to comment on the development.

The TADA court is trying Salem and two other accused, builder Virendra Jhamb and Mehndi Hassan, for their alleged role in the Jain murder case. According to the police, on March 7, 1995, Jain a city-based builder was shot dead by assailants outside his Juhu bungalow after he refused to part with his huge property to Salem. The case is almost at the completion. Around three or four witnesses are to be examined.

Heading: Economics to be fun at Arth-Manthan - Indian Express
Content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's biggest project to date—the Rs 5,000 crore-project to partially shut Deonar dumping ground and set up waste processing plant and sanitary landfill which would also help them earn carbon credits — is making the corporators jittery.

Tabled in the standing committee, the proposal is scheduled to come up for discussion on Monday. The project has raised many questions . "The project needs to be thoroughly discussed as it is the biggest till date and has a budget of Rs 5,000 crore," said committee chairman and ruling party Shiv Sena leader Ravindra Waikar.

"We need to verify whether the project can be implemented at a lesser cost and other aspects have to be explored too." A consortium of United Phosphorus Limited, Kerala based POABS and German based MDSE, has been proposed to carry out the contract. According to the proposal, the contractor will also be responsible for operation and maintenance of the site for the next 25 years.

Congress leader and committee member Vinod Shekhar said that the civic administration has asked for the approval of the project within 30 days or else it will be deemed as approved. "It seems that the civic administration is in a hurry to get the approval. United Phosphorus Limited is the only company which responded to the tender," he said.

The proposal, if approved, will pave way for the BMC's largest and biggest project which envisages the closure of the dumping ground. The project, divided in two phases, will see 65 hectares of land to be closed while the remaining 55 will have a processing plant and sanitary landfill. It will also earn carbon credits in future and generate electricity by capturing methane gas.

Heading: Image Consultants - Indian Express
Content:
Economics will come in a more fun-filled, exciting avatar on December 16 and 17, when N G Acharya and D K Marathe College hosts its annual economics-based festival Arth-Manthan. This is the city's only festival that has a theme, events and seminars that revolve solely on one of the most seemingly inscrutable subjects there is.

With thirteen events spread over two days, organisers believe if economics is put across to students interestingly, as is the case with their events, the subject will not be considered as dry as it is made out to be. "Economics is perceived as a very boring subject, with tough jargons and a more theoretical than practical approach. We try and make it more interesting by having events where the themes in the subject are brought out through song and drama competitions," said Rajesh Mahanty, a second year Commerce student at NGADKM, and a member of the organising committee.

This year, the festival will revolve around four main themes: the agrarian crisis, global warming, the financial crisis and what the organisers call a leadership crisis. "We decided it was important to examine why we don't have a transparent, dedicated, uncorrupt leader," said Shashi Panikar, an economics professor and a guiding force for the festival, along with professor Amit Joshi from Swami Vivekananda College, Dombivli and D K Mule, principal of the host college.

Among the events to be held at Arth-Manthan this year are the Maha Debate, where contestants will debate on whether or not India can produce a Barack Obama and what India seeks in a leader; a Global Leaders Meet, where participants from various colleges will come representing various countries and their environmental issues and Business Plan. In this event, the team with the best entrepreneurship plan will win.

"This is one of the most innovative festivals I have seen. Imagine explaining economic terms in a song, which is part of an event held each year," said Saylee Katkar, a participant from Ruia college who participated in Arth-Manthan last year. The festival had also attracted international attention when in 2007, it was presented at the International Developments in Economics Education (DEE) Conference organised by the Higher Education Academy (UK) in Cambridge. Among the economists and academicians who have spoken at the festival in the past are G N Bajpai, Ex-Chairman SEBI, Shri Minoo Shroff, president, Forum of Free Enterprise and Sharad Joshi, founder, Shetkari Sanghatna.

While it started out with 12 participating colleges in 2001, Arth-Manthan now has over 60 colleges participating in various events and records a footfall of 5000 each year. The festival also has a book exhibition as part of the events during the two days, in order to help students and teachers update themselves with the best of books available around the world.

Heading: De-Stress Call for Dogs - Indian Express
Content:
A group of students took on the task of giving Ghatkopar police station a makeover, and the results are dramatic

They came, they cleaned, they repaired and they painted. And after 10 days of tireless effort, 69 students of the Shrimati P N Doshi Women's College of Arts in Ghatkopar successfully transformed the Ghatkopar police station from 'dreary and dirty' to 'clean and green'.

Where earlier a cluttered perch with clay flower pots stood neglected at the centre of the station's courtyard, the zealous students cleared the clutter to find that the dusty perch was in fact a fountain, complete with fish and a turtle. Over 150 new saplings now dot the campus and a simple border of bricks surrounds every plant. Peeling paint on the walls was replaced by a fresh coat and the cracks on the cement platforms that serve as seats were filled in neatly.

"The girls who are a part of the National Service Scheme (which aims at roping in youth for community service) took on the task of the police station's makeover as a project. However what started out as a project work gradually became fun and will always remain etched in their memories as an achievement," said Ashok Salve, a professor from the college.

The idea of beautifying the station had taken root when some professors of the college had met Ghatkopar's Police Inspector for community issues, Fulsingh Pawar, in August requesting permission to organize a students rally. "Encouraged by his forthcoming attitude, we broached the idea of undertaking a beautification campaign at the police station, and he immediately agreed," said Manisha Parelkar, another professor. The group of students and 12 teachers armed with brooms and spades then descended upon the police station on November 2.

Pawar himself added that the tansformation has been incredible. "The dedication of the students is amazing. They also overcame their fear of the police station in the process," he said.

In addition to improving the physical surroundings, the students also organized small events aimed at the welfare of the policemen and their families, staying at official quarters located within the station's campus. "We organized recipe competitions for the women and a drawing contest for the children. We held a module on stress management for the policemen and had invited a BPCL representative to conduct a 'Safety in the Kitchen' demonstration. Our 'adopt a tree' campaign also involves the children of policemen whereby two of our students and two children from the campus would be responsible for maintaining a sapling," said Parelkar.

The students who had earlier cringed at the prospect of clearing garbage can hardly believe that they carried it out successfully. "The hardest thing was to clean up the garbage that had been dumped in the campus. There was stale food, plastic as well as construction debris and the first thought that crossed our mind was that we haven't even done this at home," said Ankita Rawal, a first year B.Com student.

Besides tackling garbage, tackling the skepticism of the families was another challenge that the girls overcame.

"During the initial days, the families staying here would look at is suspiciously and ask whether we were being paid to do this. Earlier we had doors shut on our face when we went to invite the women to participate in the contests and the children would refuse with sarcastic replies. However gradually they realized that our aim was genuine and have become very co-operative," said Gautami Rao, a junior college student.

However, for the professors, the success of the police station's makeover is a sweeter reward especially after facing rejection for the first time. "We had initially conceptualized the makeover of the Ghatkopar railway station but after six months of discussion with the Central Railway authorities, they refused to give permission for it. However the railway station's loss is the police station's gain." said Salve.

Heading: Untapped Energies - Indian Express
Content:
This young woman will soon be India's first qualified canine physiotherapist

A few years ago, Sonia Khanvilkar (now 24) administered hydrotherapy on an injured deer at the Pune zoo and helped it walk. Now after attending a certified veterinary programme in 'canine physiotherapy' in the US, she is back in Mumbai to treat dogs.

Working at the K-9 Veterinary Consultant and Dermatology Centre, a veterinary clinic in Chembur, Khanvilkar explains, "I am still studying and will have to return in December 2009, briefly, to submit my thesis. Meanwhile, I have started working with a vet and treating ailing dogs. I hope to soon be the first qualified canine physiotherapist in the city."

Khanvilkar offers an array of services like hydrotherapy (immersing the affected part in water and helping mobilization), exercise therapy (administering special motor exercises to mobilize the animal) and hot and cold therapy to her patients. "Currently, I am treating a one year old Golden Retriever with hip dislocation, an arthritic dog and two more dogs with injuries. The physiotherapy process is long-drawn and takes about 15 to 19 visits for the dog to completely recuperate, however, the pet feels immense comfort with the massage and exercise technique," she says, adding that often the patients drift off to sleep on the therapy bed when a session is in progress.

Khanvilkar charges Rs 500-Rs 600 per pet for an initial evaluation visit and between Rs 300-400 for each following visit. "Usually, at least two visits per week is recommended but for severe cases we suggest 3-4 visits per week," she says. While the charges may be a bit steep, Khanvilkar believes the specialization will interest animal lovers, who seek utmost comfort for their pets. "These days, many people keep breeds like pugs and daschunds for pets. These breeds, because of the construction of their body, often suffer from knee and back displacement. In such conditions, medicines can't cure, only systematic exercise can get the animal on its feet again," she adds.

However, Khanvilkar points out that physiotherapy is not easy on animals. Several tests need to be conducted before starting treatment. An initial evaluation is done, where the records by the referring veterinarian are studied, a complete history of the animal is acquired, and an assessment its current status is made. This includes several types of measurements, neurological evaluation, pain evaluation, and movement evaluation, she elucidates.

Strangely enough, Khanvilkar confesses to be a qualified human physiotherapist who "would rather put her skills in helping animals".

"Ever since I was a kid I wanted to be a vet," she laughs, "But I wasn't able to get admission in Mumbai's or Pune's veterinary colleges, and so enrolled myself at the Pune's Hardikar Hospital for a degree in physiotherapy instead. However, I always knew, I wanted to use my expertise on animals." She is confident that physiotherapy will soon become a sought after treatment in India for dogs as well as other animals with arthritis, hip and elbow dysplasia, pre and post operative care, and even in extreme cases like cancer. She also looks forward to practising massage therapy to relieved stressed canines.

"In fact, once I complete my studies, I plan to contact the Mumbai dog squad and suggest to de-stress their dogs," she says, "the police dogs in our city work very hard and are obviously stressed out. I know with my therapy I could help them relax."

Heading: Fake visas: Scanner on agents in Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
This annual festival brings those suffering from mental illnesses into the mainstream

A benign man smiles at you from behind a small stall selling intricately crafted diyas, paper bags, purses and cards at the Manav Foundation's annual event 'Flow- the Stream of Energies'. All around the crowded room, men and women stand chattering away to one another.

"I wonder if you can recognize any of the patients by looking around the room and tell them apart," says Meena Abhaymutha, a trustee at the Manav Foundation, a challenge in her question. That some among the crowd suffer from different forms of mental illness is not immediately apparent, and not one of them can be told apart from the volunteers or staff of Manav. "This is one of our biggest aims — to bring those who suffer from emotional distress or mental illness into mainstream society," she says.

The Manav Foundation was started four years ago, to help give individuals with various mental illnesses a chance to be treated and brought back into society while also fighting against the stigma associated with mental illnesses. "Our day care centre is open six days a week, from Monday to Saturday and we provide a holistic approach to psycho-social therapy," says Abhaymutha.

"In the process of starting the Manav Rehabilitation Centre, we realized that there was a lot of artistic and creative talent that was not recognized. That's when we planned Flow - the Stream of Energies. Legwork for this event starts months in advance," says Binaifer Jesia, director, Manav Foundation.

While the foundation has four trustees and five permanent volunteers, on days when there are events, the number goes up to 25, of which there is a mix of students, collegians, social workers and housewives. "I go in twice a week and teach cooking and artwork. When I joined I wondered if they would really accept me, since I don't have a professional background. But this way, I learn a lot too, along with them," says Maghu Dugar, a housewife who feels that working with the Manav Foundation has helped give her a chance to give back to society.

At the annual event, the adults who go in for treatment at the Manav Foundation all come together on one platform to perform. They take part in a drama competition, a fresh flower rangoli competition and a sound creation competition. Like the director says, the programme is always a big success, even when it comes to educating people about the issues surrounding mental illness. "We want to actually take it out there and create awareness, instead of just preaching to the converted," says Jesia.

Heading: GIS-based mapping ready to start soon - Indian Express
Content:
The two main travel agents who allegedly procured fake visas and work permits found in the possession of 14 persons arrested at Sahar Airport on Thursday night are believed to be based in Anand and Vadodara districts of Gujarat.

The Sahar police will be shortly sending a team to Gujarat to nab them.

The information on the whereabouts of the two agents behind the racket were reportedly given by seven sub-agents arrested along with the 14 passengers during interrogation.

"In the next couple of days, we will be sending a team to arrest the two running the racket. The sub-agents were merely here to guide the passengers through airport formalities. The two main culprits at the helm of the scam are in Gujarat and we have full knowledge of their whereabouts. We will be collaborating with the Gujarat police and arresting them," said senior police inspector, Sahar police station, Dilip Joshi.

Based on a tip-off, Sahar police had arrested the 14 passengers who were about to board a flight for London. The cops had also nabbed the seven sub-agents accompanying the passengers to the airport. "All the passengers come from a poor background and were headed to work as hotel waiters or housekeeping staff. They had paid Rs 3.5 lakh each for procuring the documents," said Joshi.

The Sahar police had registered around 300 such cases in the year 2007.

Heading: Ahead of court verdict, Reliance Energy union leader murdered in public - Indian Express
Content:
After a delay of almost a year, the financial capital is finally set to have Geographical Information System (GIS) enabled maps that will not only record the city's 3 lakh properties but will also mark every road, tree, dustbin and manhole in a locality alongside the vital installations. This will allow Mumbaiites to view these details on a map at the click of a mouse even as the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation is able to keep an eye on property tax defaulters, water leakages and miscreants who regularly encroach on or rupture the city's pipelines.

However, it will be another two years before the facility is finally ready.

Starting with the one of the smallest wards, mostly B Ward in South Mumbai, the pilot project for the GIS map and property mapping is expected to begin in the next four months.

The GIS maps will be prepared using Quick Bird Satellite images with the highest possible resolution for the land that will allow recording of the smallest features. The final maps are expected to be complete within two years.

While tenders were invited in May this year, the civic administration made several revisions to the plan. "The project has been delayed but we wanted the implementation to be up to date. Many cities have followed the system but in a haphazard manner, we did not want to do the same," said joint municipal commissioner (improvements) V Radha.

As per the new provisions, along with the entire 468-sq km area of Mumbai city and its vital installations—dams, water lakes, pumping stations, purification centers—will be digitally mapped. Along with property mapping, four major departments will also have their data recorded: water supply, sewage, roads / traffic (including transportation facilities like bus stands, taxi stands and petrol pumps) and storm water drains. Mapping of underground water utilities, sewer lines, drainage lines, storm water drains will begin independently.

In the property mapping, each property in the city with the name of the property owner, its type (flat, bungalow, chawl), its usage and carpet area will be mapped digitally and physically. Once completed, the mapping will allow the property tax department to identify the defaulter — tax payment will be automatically linked with a software and the map will highlight defaulting properties automatically.

Similarly, the civic administration hopes new properties will also be brought into the property tax net through the mapping.

The National Informatics Center (NIC) which has already delayed the submission is now expected to hand over the base maps by next year. The base maps will provide 3D images with low flying photographs for comparison with the satellite images and the ground mapping. Details of other departments will then be superimposed on these maps. Once complete, the digital maps will also be uploaded on the civic portal.

"Barring confidential information which includes data on properties and vital installations, the basic data of roads and directions will be uploaded for citizens' convenience," Radha said.

Heading: Recession Chic - Indian Express

Wedding belle

Heading: Back on track - Indian Express
Content:
How to look trendy when the economy is not looking good? Here is the designers' guide

Anupamaa Dayal
Recession hardly means dressing down. What it does imply, instead, is to cut out whimsical shopping. Buy one item of clothing, but make sure it is of the best quality. Trans-seasonal dressing is going to be big. Buy a dress which you can also wear in summer, but team it up with a polo neck sweater, leggings or skinny jeans, and accessories like a dressy shawl or stole. This way you'll have a compact wardrobe, but you'll still be dressed for the season.

Zubair Kirmani
Mix and match items of clothing to get the perfect look. The ideal thing to do is to buy one designer item, like a pair of trousers or a skirt, and then team it up with everyday items from the wardrobe. Colours go a long way in defining your dressing sensibility. Invest in safer colours like charcoal, ivory and maroon which can hold its own beyond a single season. Focus more on visually rich looking accessories, like mufflers, caps, bangles, all of which can make you look classy, yet simple.

Varun Bahl
Even though recession might not affect trousseau expenses, you can exercise moderation in your everyday wardrobe. Go for basic clothing, which you can team up with a lot of other accents. Bring back black. Invest in a lot of blacks, since it is one colour that can be worn in a lot of different ways, for both casual and formal occasions. You can go in for bright accessories — bright belts, colourful bags and shoes. It will lend warmth to the entire look.

David Abraham of Abraham and Thakore
The meltdown can actually lead to a better time. The optimistic thing to do now would be to go in for cheerful dressing, as if nothing has happened. Bring out the classy items and dress it up. For our Autumn-Winter collection, we have worked with baroque influences on a muted-colour palette. We have used colours like black, dull-gold, coffee and toffee with dull metallic glints to make the whole look rich and luxurious.

Heading: Whisky nights - Indian Express
Content:
After three years off screen, Chitrangada Singh explains how the break helped her

Chitrangada Singh created a stir in just her first film, Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi in 2003, as a South Indian girl from abroad. But after a dud, Kal: Yesterday and Tomorrow, in 2005, she vanished from the scene. The demands of stardom and the sudden lime light became too much for the newbie to handle. Not as the as per rumours that the pressures from a nagging husband forced her to take this decision. But after a few charcoal painting sessions, yoga and dabbling in interior design, Singh is sure she wants to return.

Her latest movie Sorry Bhai directed by Onir, starring Shabana Azmi and Boman Irani is releasing this month. And you can already sense the anxiety in her voice. "I'm slightly nervous; it has been some time since I acted," says the actor showing off a tan from her sky-diving camp in Hissar.

Singh doesn't call this a comeback but a "new beginning". The break did her good as she can strategise, plan and organise her life they way she wants. She also realises that that she has hardly made a pinprick into Bollywood, being just two films old. "When I joined, I had no godfather. Now I have learnt to cope with the attention myself. But there is no pressure on me to perform," she adds. The timing of her film could not have been any better as she was eager to make a comeback. "I had changed my number and was hesitant to call up directors and ask for work. Someone leaked my number to Onir and I immediately agreed to do his film," she laughs.

The film sees Singh playing the role of a fun loving girl not sure of who she loves. So she is caught between the affection of two brothers, played by Sanjay Suri and Sharman Joshi. "I liked the script; there is a twist to the love angle. It was dealt with innocently and happily rather than clichéd love triangles," she explains. Incidentally Sorry Bhai sees Singh cast opposite her childhood idol, actor Shabana Azmi. "Even after so many years she handles and guides the scene effortlessly. On sets, I was a sucker for her and would sit for hours and watch her. She even advised me against studying acting," Singh smiles.

Singh makes no bones about who her favourite director is either. Her first film with Sudhir Mishra was a runaway hit and her next project with him, Aur Devdas, where she plays Chandramukhi, the courtesan, commences shooting in December. "He appreciates my acting and I like his kind of cinema which is off the beaten track."

Singh also stars in Mishra's Nawab and John Company which release in July 2009.

Heading: Shades of Triumph - Indian Express
Content:
When it comes to making a mark, Ballantine's Finest knows how to do it in style. The best selling whiskey, which is the latest addition to the Pernod Ricard India stable, was launched in India with the Leave an Impression tour, which saw musicians, new-age tabla artiste Bickram Ghosh and percussionist Pete Lockett perform with guitarist Guiliano Modarelli and DJ Vicky, across India.

Ballantine has a long and illustrious history in the world of fine scotch. It earns second spot on the list of the world's best whiskies and is the tenth most widely sold spirit in the world. But wouldn't the reputation of the drink be its own advertisement? Why recruit musicians to do so? Bikram Basu, the vice-president of marketing, Pernod Ricard India, says, "The choice and decision to take on these musicians was immediate. They leave an indelible impression with their individuality and musical style; and that is what our brand stands for - Leave an Impression."

The musicians performed in Mumbai on November 7 at Dragonfly, Nariman Point, after having already performed in Delhi's F Bar and Bangalore's Windsor Manor. Next on the itinerary is Kolkata's Soho. Ghosh believes that his brand of fusion music goes well with the aura of a nightclub. "Usually, the music at nightclubs is very DJ-driven and regular patrons of this scene are looking for a change. The new-age synthesis of a traditional and classical instrument like the tabla with the more modern sound of drums and guitars makes for an exciting new experience," he explains, "And when you combine that with the act of drinking fine scotch, it becomes a magical experience."

For Lockett, who's a regular on the Indian musical circuit, there won't be anything new about performing yet again in this country. But he's excited all the same. "Very few people actually think of this kind of fusion music would be appropriate for drinking to. But you'd be surprised at how well it goes with a nightclub atmosphere."

If leaving an impression is the intention, then it looks like Ballantine's Finest has got off to a good start with its unusual launch.
