Heading: Everlasting Bond - Indian Express
Content:
Threading together art and craft, an exhibition titled Parables of the Thread brings together 16 artists. They venture into the territory of what is usually considered 'craft', bringing a contemporary edge to the practice of using cloth, thread, dyes and traditional methods of designing to make fresh statements. The show premiers at The Loft in Lower Parel, on

November 14, and promises to be an interesting exercise of revisiting the genre of traditional painting.

"This exhibition is conceived as a colloquium to bring forth a dialogue between craftsmen, designers and artists. They all use cloth and environment-friendly materials but conceptualise their images in distinctive ways," as Jayaram Poduval puts it.

In another part of the city, an exhibition showcasing video art and photography and the contemporary visual culture of new media art, brings about another kind of dialogue. The exhibition titled Synonymous premiered in the city at the Guild last Friday.

Curator Shubhalakshmi Shukla puts together a collection of well-known names from this genre while focusing on "representations of the self, extending questions of identity. It could mean a direct political presence in a life-scale cut-out image, a larger-than-life image in a film, or an endorsement".

While these two shows are remarkably diverse, the common areas which are covered by both are of a shared desire to represent mediums other than painting.

Artist like Rakhi Peswani, Lavanya Mani, Ranjith Raman and Hemali Bhuta, who feature in the Parables exhibition have been engaged in exploring mediums like soft sculpture, natural dye on cotton and graphic works. The idea behind these practices is to introduce new dialogues on what was traditionally considered craft—like, domestic occupations of housewives that were not fit to enter the realm of high art.

Peswani's sculptures and embroidery work directly take on this issue, reversing the beauty and functionality usually attributed to 'decorative' objects like table mats, bolsters and wall hangings.

Mani revisits the era of British colonialism and the spice trade of the Dutch, Portuguese and the British through her natural dye prints on cloth. She also learnt Kalamkari from C Subramanyam from Kalahasti, Andhra Pardesh, during the course of her research on the medium. "It is my way of

revisiting craft and keeping it alive through contemporary issues. In my own way I hope to add to this history by reviving the medium," says Mani.

In the other exhibition, we get an opportunity to encounter the medium of photography and stills from video works. The curator acknowledges that photography's transition from its roots in documenting and journalism to art is something that played out in the West. However, the context in which artists like, Kiran Subbaiah, Navjot Altaf, Tejal Shah, Binu Bhaskar and Vidya Kamat, place themselves in re-looks at the entire history of image making. Subbaia, who currently lives in Amsterdam, constantly examines his identity as diaspora and questions his place as an Asian in Neo-Colonial times

of globalisation.

Shah and Kamat revisit the Victorian era where women, dressed in full-sleeved and high collared dresses, were constantly looked on as liabilities. While Shah digs deep into hysteria and its 'treatment' Kamat approaches her own mortality with a frilled collar made of deaths heads. Navjot visits the site of body tattooing while Sen's kitschy diptych comments on decorative jewellery and sexuality.

All the works are politically loaded and both shows are well worth visiting.

Heading: Who is a Pieter Bruegel? - Indian Express
Content:
In his newest book, Ruskin Bond once again recaptures his idyllic boyhood days in Dehra Dun

If you take Ruskin Bond's birth certificate into account, he is 74. But when you turn the pages of The Parrot Who Wouldn't Talk and Other Stories, then he is slightly older than 10. After sharing his charming boyhood many a times with his ardent readers, the author now recalls the eccentricities of his relatives living in Dehra Dun.

"I think everyone has at least one eccentric aunt or uncle in the family. I had more than one. My boyhood days were enlivened by them," says the iconic writer on the jacket of the book. The stories, 14 of them, reveal his grandfather's mastery in disguise, Aunt Ruby's misadventures with a pet parrot, great-grandfather's regimental mynah, stationmaster Mr Ghosh's family of white mice and bachelor scoutmaster Mr Oliver's grief over his pup's death. But it's Uncle Ken who shines through them-with his goofiness and ability to court trouble and limitless bicycle rides with his young nephew. He puts Ruskin on a wrong train and misses the ship on their way to London at Port Said.

Apart from Uncle Ken, it's the author's favourite Dehra that brightens up the tales. Most of the actions of this collection take place in this hill town. In the course of the book, the author mentions a number of times the loss of Dehra's greenery and beauty. The last two stories of the book have Bond reminiscing his early years there in the lap of greenery and in the company of his grandparents.

The book published by Puffin is meant for young readers. But it won't be at all surprising if older Bond fans, not restricted to any age group, pick up The Parrot Who Wouldn't Talk to get a fresh dose of his delightful tales. After all, who doesn't like a heartwarming tale of childhood. That apart, Bond's lucid and interactive writing style as always manages to tug at his readers' heartstrings.

What adds to the book's appeal are Kavita Arvind's beautiful illustrations. They are simple, cute and funny—just like the stories.

A prolific writer, Bond has till date written 30 books for children. It's amazing how so many more stories are left within him. One can credit it to his wonderful childhood in the hills. Or one, can simply salute the genius of this master storyteller.

Heading: Culture vulture - Indian Express
Content:
Browsing through a bookstore, a colleague asked if buying an art book on the artist Pieter Bruegel the Elder was 'worth it'. It certainly is, since the artist is one of the most prominent of the Flemish-Dutch Renaissance and has many followers among artists and viewers. The artist is especially celebrated for his ability to turn,

sayings, parables and phrases like, Blind Leading the Blind and Netherlandish Proverbs into delightfully humorous paintings.

To trace back to his beginnings, Breugel (1525-69) began as an apprentice in a guild that was run by his father-in-law-to-be, Pieter Coeke van Aelst. After learning the basics and marrying his tutor's daughter Mayken, Bruegel travelled to France, Italy (where he was exposed to the Italian Renaissance) and Antwerp. It was in Antwerp, that he established himself as a master painter in 1551. The artist chose not to paint the elaborate and divine paintings that characterised Italy but was interested in capturing peasant life. He was even nicknamed, 'Peasant Bruegel' because of his habit of dressing like a peasant and mingling with them to learn their customs, study their costumes and jot down studies on his note pad, that fueled his large works of art.

Injecting his panoramic vistas with a dash of humour, the artist set a precedent for his sons. Pieter Bruegel the Younger and Jan Bruegel the Elder both inherited their father's legacy though it is said that neither of them were old enough to have studied directly under his tutelage.

It is speculated that perhaps the boys studied under their grandmother Mayken Verhulst, who was also a painter and alive at the time.

Besides his immediate family, Bruegel has inspired artists like Milburn Cherian, who is currently having a solo at Art Musings gallery. If one cannot afford the ticket to Brussels, Belgium or London, to view the great Flemish masters works, mosey over to the gallery to get a taste of what his was like.

Demystify art ,e-mail georgina.maddox@expressindia.com

Heading: Customs hold Central Rly - Indian Express
Content:
Festive season
It's that time of the year again, when Prithvi Theatre wears a festive air and spreads the theatre-mania across the city. The 30th edition of Prithvi Theatre Festival has found two more venues this year, Karnataka Sangha and Horminan Circle Garden, apart from its Juhu address. Those wanting to enjoy and experience the festivities can catch Sakubai, Antigone, Shakkar Ke Paanch Daane, Cotton 56, Polyster 84, Giribala, All About Women, Karodo Mein Ek and C for Clown. Those looking for an additional dose of theatre can catch platform performances at Prithvi Theatre at 8.15 every evening till the festival concludes on November 16.
Log on to prithvitheatre.org for show details

Cityscape
SWARUP, a recent immigrant to Kolkata, reveals a distant observer's gaze on the events and happenings in the city of Mumbai. As an outsider who observes events on the ground from a distance; his work often takes a bird's eye-view. The bustling crowd do not ever appear human, but as marionettes. They are perpetually on move, on foot and on old fashioned public transport like the hand-pulled rickshaws. They appear to be moving on fixed tracks, like the tram-tracks. His gaze on scurrying people is not critical, but more so it is filled with amazement. Swarup's pictures fall just short of celebrating the daily rhythm of urban life of Kolkatta, as he feels apprehensive of touching that life.
At Art Desh, Film Centre Building, Tardeo, till November 10

Fashionable
INSPIRED by the Lakme Fashion Week and then the success of Madhur Bhandarkar's Fashion, artists Sameer Mondal, Arzaan Khambatta and Naina Kanodia, Babu Xavier and Jayasri Burman are hosting a show by the same title. Already predisposed to reacting to popular culture, these artists have responded to the fusing of the two disciplines. Both creations are visual and tactile, artists and designers respond to colour, texture and form. Often there is a meeting of minds as globally, designers shown at art museums like at NGMA in Mumbai, V&A in London and MOMA in San Francisco.
At Jamaat Art Gallery, Apolo Bunder, till December 4

Buddha within
PRADEEP Verma is inspired by Buddha, the enlightened one who lived a life of austerity, renouncing all worldly possessions. The irony is that this made his presence stronger and people felt a sense of pride, prosperity and tranquility towards the Buddha. The artist having discovered Buddha has been led towards the path of meditation which is the inspiration behind this exhibition and most of Verma's works. Before painting the Buddha, he finds a very special serene place inside himself and then paints his inner feelings with a sense of total timelessness.
At Zenzi, Waterfield Road, Bandra, till November 20

Heading: English crash-course for Vikrant, Sushant - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai Customs held Central Railway to a 3-3 draw in the MHA-Super League played at the MHA stadium, Churchgate on Sunday.

Leading 2-1 at the break, the railmen looked comfortable at 3-1 with their talented upcoming striker Haridas scoring a hat-trick.

He started with a penalty conversion in the 25th minute, and followed that with a fine angular pass unleashed from the axis by Amit Singh, to bang it into the net and double the lead.

The third goal came in the latter half from fine efforts from Ajaz Qureshi who after dodging past a couple of Customs defenders accurately released the ball to a well-positioned Haridas, in the 52nd minute.

Customs had gone into the lead early after Suresh Maibam convered an indirect penalty corner in the 21st minute. Thereafter the railmen ran up a 3-1 lead, before Customs equalised.

While the railmen could convert only 1 of their 12 corners, Customs managed three off their 10.

Heading: Auxiliary wins Reddy Memorial Cup - Indian Express
Content:
Off-spinner Vikrant Yelligetti and batsman Sushant Marathe, two youngsters of Mumbai XI, had their wish fulfilled after spending five minutes with England skipper Kevin Pietersen.

It was a perfect platform for the young Mumbai XI side led by Nilesh Kulkarni, to showcase their performance against a solid side. And when the stage was set, there was nothing to lose, much to gain for the young Mumbai line-up. As the match ended on a losing note for Mumbai at Cricket Club of India on Sunday, Sushant and Vikrant made sure not to miss a chance to have a chat with Pietersen.

"We just requested him and he was ready to speak at that very moment," says Vikrant. The five minutes-talk was all about batting and technique of playing in different conditions. "We just wanted to know how he (Pietersen) prepared himself before every match," says Sushant.

Being a member of Mumbai Indians, Vikrant earlier had a chance to talk to several big players including Sachin Tendulkar during Indian Premier League (IPL).

"Just be focussed and don't take your nets lightly," Pietersen told both youngsters. The England captain was impressed with the youngsters and he even complimented Vikrant on his bowling effort.

In a match which saw Owais Shah and Andrew Flintoff score runs heavily, Vikrant finished with a 10 over-spell giving away just 41 runs and taking the wicket of opener Ian Bell. Whereas, southpaw opener Sushant scored a decent 36 off 58 balls against a solid English bowling line-up.

Vikrant recalls how during his spell Flintoff was finding it tough to tackle his spin.

"When Nilesh and I were bowling they were finding it a little difficult to play spin. But later Flintoff came to me and told me that it's my turn to hear the music," says the off-spinner.

Heading: Raghav in Round 2 - Indian Express
Content:
Vasant Mayur of Maharashtra and S Settu of Tamil Nadu bagged doubles in the 2nd GVK AISTA Senior National Ranking Tennis Championship, which concluded at the Practennis courts, Andheri on Sunday. While Mayur Vasant won the singles and doubles title in the over-45 category, S Settu claimed a double in over-55 category. D S Rama Rao claimed the doubles in the over-55 category, while he finished runner-up in the singles.

In the singles final of over-45, eighth seed Vasant Mayur blanked third seed V Srinivasa Reddy (AP) 6-0, 6-0. Mayur then partnered Chetan Desai and toppled the top seed pairing of R.V.Rama Raju & G.Krishnam Raju (AP) 6-1, 6-0.

In the over-55 category, third seed S. Settu (TN) had to sweat it out to overcome a stiff challenge from the unseeded D S Rama Rao to clinch the title 6-4, 4-6, 6-4. S Settu was rattled and nervous after the second set, which was won by Rama Rao.

He matched his game with S.Settu by playing drop shots, serve and volley, and also hitting winners on both the sides. Finally the fit and energetic S Settu was lucky to win the match due to the unforced errors committed by Rama Rao.

In the over-65 category top seed S Parekh (Mah) bt third seed V.R.Kulkarni (Kar) 6-3, 6-4.

Heading: Dikshit files nomination papers - Indian Express
Content:
Nine students were on Monday injured when a school bus overturned in Omega sector in Greater Noida, police sources said.

The incident occurred when a KDS Public School bus, carrying 80 children, overturned in Omega sector injuring nine students, SP(Greater Noida) S K Verma said.

The bus driver, in an effort to avoid a head-on collision with a car, lost control over the vehicle and it overturned, he said.

Nine injured students were taken to a nearby hospital, he said, adding six of them have been discharged while three were still admitted to the ICU.

Drivers of both bus and car are absconding, he added.

Heading: Another Lovely in the fray from Cong camp? - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit on Monday filed her nomination papers from New Delhi assembly constituency and expressed confidence that Congress will come back to power for a third term.

Dikshit, accompanied by DPCC chief Jaiprakash Aggarwal, her son Sandeep Dikshit MP and daughter Latika, submitted her nomination papers before the Additional District Magistrate Bansh Raj at Jamnagar House in New Delhi.

Union Minister Ajay Maken, a known Dikshit detractor and the Lok Sabha member from New Delhi, was not present when the Chief Minister filed her documents for fighting the Delhi elections for a third time.

A large number of workers gathered at the ADM office in Shahjahan Road and shouted slogans in favour of Dikshit and Congress.

"I am confident of victory. My campaign has picked up," she told reporters after filing the nominations.

Her main opponent BJP's Vijay Jolly will file his nomination papers on Tuesday.

Finance Minister A K Walia and Delhi BJP president Harsh Vardhan also filed their nomination papers for Laxmi Nagar and Krishna Nagar constituencies on Monday.

A total of 193 candidates had filed their nominations till Saturday after the filing of nominations started on November 4.

Tuesday is the last date for filing of nominations.

Both Walia and Harsh Vardhan filed their nomination papers at Deputy Commissioner (East).

Walia, who was accompanied by a large number of party workers, said "all the good works done by Congress in last 10 years and the development measures implemented by him during three-time tenure as MLA will help him to win."

Former cricketer and BJP MP Navjot S Sidhu accompanied the BJP state president during filing of nomination.

There was a stampede-like situation when Sidhu and Harsh Vardhan reached the office to submit the papers. Police had a tough time handling the situation.

Heading: Gurgaon hit by global recession, many export houses shut, others on way out - Indian Express
Content:
Assembly polls : Buta Singh's son Ravinder Singh Lovely may contest from Deoli seat

As party stalwarts continue to lock horns over selection of candidates for the remaining 22 seats, the Central Election Committee of the Congress, headed by party chief Sonia Gandhi, is considering another 'Lovely' for the Delhi Assembly elections.

After retaining Education Minister Arvinder Singh 'Lovely' for the Gandhi Nagar Assembly seat in East Delhi, the party chief, according to sources, is contemplating fielding former Bihar governor Buta Singh's elder son Ravinder Singh 'Lovely' for the Deoli seat in South Delhi.

This is one of the reasons, party insiders say, for the delay in the finalisation of candidates for the 22 seats. "The party is expecting opposition from MP Sajjan Kumar who may not accept an 'outsider' being given a ticket in his area. The party is not taking any chances and may declare the names only a day before the last day of nominations," said a Congress member. The last date for filing of nominations is November 11 and the list is expected to be declared only on Monday. The election committee is scheduled to meet late on Sunday night to discuss the matter.

Deoli is a reserved seat for the Scheduled Caste category and the party was earlier considering Rajesh Rajora, sitting municipal councillor from Vasant Kunj, and Rajesh Chauhan, who had contested the 2003 elections as an independent from Ambedkar Nagar against Chaudhary Prem Singh, for the seat. Rajora was primarily being backed by Delhi Congress chief J P Aggarwal.

Sources claim that the decision to select Lovely as a candidate, backed by AICC general secretaries Ashok Gehlot and Ahmad Patel, is a result of intense lobbying done by Buta Singh, who was disappointed after not being able to secure a ticket for the Rajasthan Assembly elections.

Singh belongs to the Scheduled Caste category. According to the sources, he may get the ticket because Deoli has an electorate of about 1.5 lakh that comprises a mix of the Khatik caste from Rajasthan (other backward classes), Jatavs and Valmikis (both belong to SC category).

With the BJP fielding Bhim Singh, a Jatav from the area, and the Bahujan Samaj Party, too, giving ticket to an SC candidate, Lal Pradan, the Congress insiders feel the party will face a tough fight despite Delhi Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhary Prem Singh's presence.

Prior to delimitation, Deoli was part of Ambedkar Nagar and BJP MLA Vijay Jolly's Sainik Farm constituency.

Picture clearer on 18 seats
The Congress has zeroed in on a list of probables for 18 seats. They include New Delhi Municipal Council member Mukesh Bhatt for Kasturba Nagar, Health Minister Yoganand Shastri for Mehrauli, Tarvinder S Marwah for Jangpura, former MLA P C Kaushik for Mundka and former IPS officer Amod Kant for Sangam Vihar. The party is yet to arrive at a decision on candidates for BJP strongholds like Greater Kailash (opposite V K Malhotra), Jayshree Panwar being one of the contenders, Tilak Nagar (O P Babbar) and Rajinder Nagar (MLA Puran Chand Yogi) and Gurjjar/Jatav-dominated Karawal Nagar in East Delhi. Ramesh Lamba is being fielded from Hari Nagar and Deepak Tyagi from Burari.

Sheila to file papers today
Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit will file her nomination papers for the New Delhi constituency before Additional District Magistrate Bansh Raj at Jam Nagar house on Shahjahan Road on Monday. While about 193 candidates have already filed their papers, election officials are expecting a heavy rush on Monday and Tuesday. Other candidates expected to file their papers tomorrow are Chaudhary Prem Singh (Ambedkar Nagar), Arvinder Singh Lovely (Gandhi Nagar), A K Walia (Laxmi Nagar) and Haroon Yusuf (Ballimaran). From the BJP, Harsh Vardhan (Krishna Nagar), Praveen Khandelwal (Chandi Chowk), Ram Bhaj (Malviya Nagar) and M L Sodhi (Ballimaran) will file their papers on Monday.

Slain inspector's widow says no to BJP ticket
Maya Sharma, the wife of slain Delhi Police Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma, turned down the BJP's offer to contest the Delhi Assembly elections when the party approached her in the last week of October. "I'm bogged down by too many responsibilities. I have to look after my children and aged in-laws," said Maya.

Heading: Look who’s making money this poll season: chartered accountants - Indian Express
Content:
The global economic downturn has started hitting Indian exporters. With their overseas markets, such as the US, facing a big meltdown, garment industry owners and export houses in Gurgaon are shutting shops. Several have already left, hoping to find better alternatives elsewhere in the country.

Says Ashwini Chachra, co-owner of Supreme Craft Export that also owns Satyam Cinemas in Delhi: "I had an annual turnover of Rs 90 crore from my four readymade garments and fabric units that employed around 2,000 people. With practically no orders in hand and due to costly labour and electricity charges, there was no alternative but to shut the units after paying the compensation for the notice period." The four properties are up for rent or sale, whichever is earlier.

A recent study by Dun & Bradstreet revealed that the financial crisis had started feeding into the real economy in the US and that the situation would improve only in 18 to 24 months. "Almost 6,700 companies filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcies in the US in 2008, compared to 3,600 in 2006," it noted.

US is the single largest destination for Indian exporters, accounting for almost 13 per cent of exports last year. Though it is difficult to put any number to job losses here because of the global slowdown, industry insiders said many employees on contract had to face retrenchment. "The job losses could be as high as 10 to 12 per cent, and more could follow in the coming months," said an exporter, who did not wish to be named.

According to Krishan Kapoor, chairman and general secretary of the Haryana Industrial Association (HIA), if the situation does not improve by the end of this year, Gurgaon may see "35-40 per cent companies shut down completely". In fact, India's exports grew at the slowest pace in 18 months in September.

"The recession has affected practically all sectors here — be it garment exporters, automobile spare part exporters or the information technology (IT) and the IT-enabled services sector. Companies are either closing down or are terminating the services of their employees as a cost-cutting measure, or not giving increments," explained Kapoor.

Most of these export houses and garment manufacturers were severely affected when the dollar took a plunge in 2007. "Since the payments are made in US dollars and not Indian rupees, exporters had to bear the losses. If companies fail to fulfil the commitments made by them, they are blacklisted," said Kapoor, adding that since countries such as China and Pakistan did not face such problems, they increased their share in the global trade.

Over 100 companies had then packed up their units in Gurgaon and shifted to other states like HP and Uttaranchal where electricity and land rates are cheaper. Also, industries in these states are exempted from excise duty for 10 years.

According to Kapoor, the orders have decreased by almost 35 per cent since the slowdown. "Be it spare parts exporters or electronic parts producers or those in garment export, the slowdown has taken its toll on everyone. Though companies abroad are bound by the contract, they can reject the consignment on the slightest of pretext, like poor quality or delay by even a day or two," he said, adding that it was the responsibility of both the Haryana government and the Centre to help the industry at a time like this.

Heading: Low visibility delays 75 flights at IGI - Indian Express
Content:
Election fever has gripped Delhi and opened avenues of earning some quick bucks for many. Among those who are raking in the moolah are chartered accountants who specialise in filing bonds and preparing affidavits.

As soon as major political parties kicked off the poll process by announcing their lists of candidates, advertisements and pamphlets from these accountants started making appearances at the party offices. Most of the names, however, go around through word of mouth.

Both the major parties — the Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) — have their legal cells in place that help the candidates fill nomination papers and prepare accounts. "We have told our candidates to be very careful while submitting nomination papers. There is a specialised legal cell to help them with all necessary formalities," says Delhi BJP president Dr Harsh Vardhan.

It is, usually, the independent candidates who are left without any support system. In the last Assembly elections, a majority of the 759 candidates who had filed nominations were independents.

Every candidate who is filing nominations has to submit nearly 11 documents — their electoral certificate, electoral certificate of their proposers, income tax returns and education certificate of the candidate and spouse, certificate of property tax, wealth tax, sales tax or VAT, pending criminal or court case, balance sheet and detailed value assessment of property among others.

Chartered accountant Gulshan Dhingra (47) has been "helping" candidates file their nominations for the last 15 years. "I started out in 1993 with late BJP MP K L Sharma. Later, I worked for other BJP leaders like Nand Kishore Gard and Sahib Singh Verma," he says. Though Dhingra claims to be a devout BJP worker, he agrees that he does help independents if they approached him. "I do the work free of cost for BJP candidates. But when independent candidates panic at the last moment, I do dispatch my accountants to them," he says.

"One needs to be extremely careful with filing of the nomination papers and preparing the accounts like property value assessments. If any of the opponents file a counter affidavit, there is a possibility of the nomination being cancelled. It usually comes as a package and we charge according to the candidate's financial capabilities," says Pawan Kumar, a chartered accountant. This year, more than 100 independent candidates have already filed their nominations.

The entire process can be nerve wrecking, the candidates feel. "I had hired a lawyer to help me file the nomination papers, but at the last moment I had to seek help from an accountant too. I spoke to several political friends who referred me to the accountant who specialises in filing nominations," says Brij Mohan Upreti, an independent candidate contesting from the New Delhi constituency against Sheila Dikshit.

Heading: Slain cop MC Sharma’s wife turns down BJP offer of ticket - Indian Express
Content:
Flights continue to be delayed at the Indira Gandhi International Airport, despite the new, Instrument Landing System (ILS)-enabled run-way, 29-11.

Delhi witnesses a lot of fog and smog at this time of the year, causing low visibility. Flight delays have already touched the 100 mark in two days. As many as 75 flights were delayed on Sunday, with the duration ranging from 30 minutes to three hours. Peak-hour flights that were delayed because of morning smog resulted in a huge backlog till the evening. "The visibility had been as low as 500 metres since 5.30 am, which got a little better around 8.30 am. It improved to 800 metres around 10 am," a Met department official said.

An Air India flight scheduled for departure at 11.25 am took off at 1.30 pm. A Jet flight from Jodhpur arrived an hour late. "The backlog resulted in air congestion," said an Air Traffic Control official. On Saturday, runway 29-11 remained non-operational for more than an hour due to a technical snag in the ILS. Airport officials have said the new runway can take care of flights even when the visibility is low. "Flights can land in low visibility conditions on the new runway. But we are facing problems due to some technical faults on the runway," an official said.

Heading: Scolded by father for poor result, Class IX boy hangs self - Indian Express
Content:
family says it might reconsider its decision before lok sabha polls if 'govt apathy' continues

The wife of Delhi Police Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma, Maya Sharma, turned down the BJP offer to contest the Delhi Assembly elections when the party approached her in the last week of October.

After Sharma was killed in the Batla House encounter, the BJP included the issue in its Delhi Assembly campaign and plans to do the same for its parliamentary election campaign.

"I'm bogged down by too many responsibilities. I have to look after my children and aged in-laws. How could I have then agreed to contest an election? The BJP had approached my father-in-law in the last week of October," said Maya Sharma.

BJP chief ministerial candidate V K Malhotra confirms the party had approached her "through emissaries". A former Youth Congress leader, known for his anti-terror campaigns, also figured in initial talks with the family.

The inspector's father Narotam Sharma says: "BJP workers and the media have been concerned about our well-being. But elections are a no-no."

However, he says the family might reconsider its decision and contest Lok Sabha elections if the "government agencies remain apathetic to the family hero's martyrdom."

After the BJP's slogan capturing the Batla House encounter, which it thought would strike a chord with the masses, "sacrifice versus sedition", the party is now working on a slogan for the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections "Jeetega Bhajpa, jeetega Bharat, haarega aatank".

Maya Sharma could, thus, have acted as a rallying point for the party's anti-terror campaign feels a dominant section of the BJP.

On the party's decision to approach her, BJP general secretary and contender for Delhi Chief Ministership initially, Vijay Goel says, "Every party has a right to approach a candidate, and similarly, a candidate has every right to turn it down."

The wife of the slain Delhi Police Inspector is, however, more concerned about the future of her children.

"I recently met families of personnel who attained martyrdom in the Parliament House attack. I was distressed to hear stories of red-tapism after the government had assured to look after their interests. The Government has not considered three of our demands sympathetically after my husband was martyred."

The family had demanded that Inspector Sharma be posthumously awarded the Ashok Chakra, promoted to ACP rank with retrospective effect; and the family be awarded a CNG-LPG cylinder gas agency.

"I wrote letters to the Prime Minister, the Home Minister and the Delhi Police Commissioner, but didn't even get an acknowledgment," rues Narotam.

The Sharmas are, however, happy that Chief Minister Sheila Dikhsit promptly forwarded their CNG/PLG agency request to Union Petroleum Minister Murli Deora.

Heading: Follow DoE schedule or face action, schools told - Indian Express
Content:
A class IX student committed suicide after his father scolded him for getting less marks in his exams in Dwarka area of Southwest district on Saturday. According to the police, the incident occurred in the Kakrora More colony of Dwarka area.

"The deceased, Rahul Singh, 14, hanged himself in his room. He was a student of Spring Public School in the same area," a senior police officer said.

The police added that yesterday he got his school exam results. As he had not done well, he was quite upset. When he showed his report card to his father, he scolded him.

The police said after his father's scolding he went up to his room on the second floor and bolted the door from inside.

He then used his sister's shawl to hang himself. His cousin, who stays with them, saw him go into the room.

Later, she became suspicious when he did not answer the door.

His cousin told his parents that he is not opening the door of his room on which Singh's parents broke it open and discovered his dead body.

They then called the police. They were not able to recover any suicide note. The body was taken to Deen Dayal Upadhayay Hospital for post mortem.

The police said Rahul's father Maharaj Singh owns a small shop in the same area and they are residents of B-Block Kakrora More.

The deceased's brother Deepak owns a chemist shop in another sector of Dwarka.

Senior police officers said prima facie it seems like the deceased was upset at his father's scolding and committed suicide.

However, the postmortem report is awaited and further investigations are on.

Heading: VOTERS SPEAK: Dr D K Sharma - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi government has warned all private, unaided and recognised schools in the Capital against non-compliance with the admission schedule outlined by the Directorate of Education (DoE). Aiming to regularise nursery admissions, a government letter dated November 3 said if the schools failed to follow the schedule, the matter "would be viewed seriously".

The letter adds that it has come to DoE's notice that some schools have been distributing forms without seeking prior approval from the government as mentioned in the guidelines issued on October 27. In that notice, the DoE had asked schools to continue to accept forms until January 7.

In an interview with Newsline last week, Education Secretary Rina Ray had said schools must seek DoE's approval and parents and guardians must notify any discrepency in the admission process to the government. Jain said schools that have come out with the forms will notify the DoE before December 14.

However, according to Ray, a notification does not mean anything. An approval is required, she said last week.

Newsline reported last week that schools that had started their admission procedure might be asked to re-issue registration forms between December 15 and 31, according to Rina Ray. A circular dated October 27 had said schools that had their own admission schedules must notify the DoE by December 14, failing which they would have to follow the one announced by the department.

While the admission process has started in many schools, Sanskriti School in Chanakyapuri is learnt to have postponed its dates for issuing forms to December 15. Previously, it was scheduled for November 10. The website of Amrita Vidyalayam, a school in Pushp Vihar, too, says the distribution of forms will start on December 15.

The new letter specifically states that schools, which have announced their admission dates that are at variance with the DoE schedule, "must continue" with the registration for pre-school/pre-primary classes during the period mentioned in the DoE order.

Schools, however, claim that such an order violates the spirit of the Supreme Court's interim order giving autonomy to schools with regard to their schedule and admission criteria. The DoE guidelines asking schools to notify the government of their schedule came after some schools had begun their registration process according to the Supreme Court's ruling, say the schools.

It has now led to confusion among the schools. Should schools that have already begun the process cancel admissions and start all over again, or they should just notify the government before December 14?

Newsline had earlier reported that DPS-Mathura Road and DPS International-RK Puram had already come out with their nursery admission forms.

According to the website, while the last date for online submission of forms is already over, the date of submission of attested documents is November 11. All branches of Bal Bharati, too, have started the admission process, besides a number of smaller schools in Rohini, Dwarka and Paschim Vihar.

S L Jain, chairman of the National Progressive Schools Conference, said these schools would notify the DoE as required in the circular, which also outlines other guidelines that the schools must follow.

Nearly 110 schools under the NPSC will start the admission process from December 1. The association said it would protest the DoE's new guidelines. DoE officials could not be reached for comments.

Shilpa Gupta, a parent, who is seeking admission for her son, said such an initiative was welcome relief but only if the government was successful in implementing it.

"Nursery admissions are in a mess and need more supervision. I don't know how sincere these efforts are," she said.

Satish Mohindra, who runs a playschool in Nehru Enclave, says lines are blurred between what is legal and what is illegal.

Heading: Reaching out to special people - Indian Express
Content:
Medical Superintendent, AIIMS
Constituency: R K Puram
Age: 46 years

On safety
As a doctor I see how lives are lost in accidents and blasts and I think in the current scenario people in Delhi need safety more than anything else. No one should have to think twice before going to a crowded market on a Saturday.

On why voting is important
Dr D K Sharma cast his vote the first time in 1983, when he was an undergraduate student pursuing MBBS. "Voting day fell right in the middle of my MBBS final exams. I was excited about being eligible to vote, so I went despite my exams. "
Asked whether he votes every time he said, "If I do not vote I will lose my right to point out the wrongs in the way the government functions. My vote counts and every one must vote if they want power in responsible hands."

On improvement of civic amenities
Apart from safety, Dr Sharma thinks a lot of work needs to be done to make civic amenities better. "So much money is pumped into construction of roads and due to corruption we have no results to show for the money spent. Water supply - shortage and the lack of it in many areas is also a concern. Electricity supply during summers is also a big concern for me as a citizen."

Heading: Consumer bodies push for power reforms - Indian Express
Content:
Several cases on making life comfortable for the physically challenged are pending in the High Court. Ramps at historical monuments, specially-trained teachers, and disabled-friendly public transport are some changes that need to be brought about.

The Economic Survey of Delhi 2007-08 takes a look at what the Capital offers to its special residents.

The estimated number of physically-challenged persons in Delhi was 1,02,427 as on October 1, 2002, which constitutes about 0.71per cent of projected population on the same day. Out of this 4,966 were in rural areas and 97,461 in urban areas.

Sex-wise breakup: Out of the total, 65,351 (63.80 per cent) were male and 37,076 (36.20 per cent) were female.

Out of the total, 12,970 (12.66 per cent) were mentally disabled, 7,308 (7.13 per cent) visually disabled, 5,326 (5.20 per cent) had communication problems, 70,026 (68.37 per cent) suffered from locomotor dysfunction and 6,797 (6.64 per cent) had multiple disabilities.

Education: Out of the total number of physically-challenged persons in Delhi (five years and above) 63.08 per cent were literate and 36.92 per cent were illiterate.

Education till the 10+2 level or above had been completed by 9.84 per cent, 7.63 per cent were educated up to the secondary level, 13.21 per cent had cleared middle level and 32.40 per cent had attained the primary level of education.

Extent of disability: 58.62 per cent of the physically-challenged persons could take care of themselves without any aid or appliance, 18.05 per cent could do so with aid or appliance and 19.08 per cent cannot take care of themselves on their own.

In the workforce: 71.40 per cent of the special population was not a part of the labour force in Delhi.

The above findings are taken into consideration by respective departments while drawing up special schemes for the

physically-challenged groups.

Education and training: The Department of Social Welfare runs four schools for the auditorily challenged with 976 students, three training-cum-production centres and two sheltered workshops for the physically-challenged, one hostel for college-going visually-challenged male students and a school for the visually-challenged with 113 students. There is also one school for mentally-challenged children with 682 students.

Apart from providing free education to the physically-challenged, the Delhi Government also provides stipends and scholarships ranging from Rs 125 to Rs 500 per month to all categories of the disabled, depending upon the level of the course.

Under the Unemployment Allowance for disabled persons scheme, a monthly allowance of Rs 600 per month is being provided to persons with more than 40 per cent disability, who are between the age group of 18-50 years and are registered in the employment exchange for last two years. During 2006-07, about 2,074 physically-challenged students benefited from this programme.

Heading: RWA forum leader  joins BJP - Indian Express
Content:
Six years after privatisation of the power sector in the Capital, consumer awareness seems to be on the rise. Consumer bodies are lobbying hard with the DERC to introduce proposals aimed at empowering the consumer.

First on the list is the suggestion by the Electricity Consumer Advocates Committee (ECAC) to ensure that meters become the responsibility of discoms.

"This ought to take care of allegations of tampering and enhance the safety of consumers. Steps in this direction are already being taken and the committee has requested a report be tabled regarding the same before its next meeting," a member of the ECAC said.

"Most consumers are not aware that they can seek compensation from discoms if they are not able to meet standards of performance. Consumers are often unaware of the standards of performance (SoP) and hence do not approach discoms to claim compensation that is rightly theirs. In such a case, many members felt, discoms should voluntarily release compensation," a stakeholder who attended SAC's last meeting told Newsline.

To this end suggestions have been forwarded to the DERC to set up a computerised system that ensures that discoms voluntarily disburse such compensation.

Other measures include a recommendation for all discoms to set up a toll-free hotline.

Heading: Delhi underground - Indian Express
Content:
The chairperson of United Residents Joint Action (URJA), a federation of residents organisations of Delhi and the president of People's Action, a voluntary organisation, Sanjay Kaul, joined the BJP in the presence of Delhi Pradesh BJP President Harsh Vardhan.

With this, around 900 residents' organisations are now connected to the BJP.

"There is a conspiracy to break the country and the danger to our security and regionalism is also increasing. The Congress government has completely failed in dealing with these things.

BJP is the only party which can take the country forward with nationalistic thinking and keeping it united," Kaul said.

Kaul has earlier fought on behalf of residents against 'arbitrary' behaviour of power companies and against alleged conspiracy of the Congress to privatise the Delhi Jal Board.

"The Sheila Dikshit government has broken all the records when it comes to oppression of residents of the Capital in the last 10 years. People are suffering due to spiralling prices, terrorism, poor law and order, but the government is paying no heed," Harsh Vardhan said today.

Heading: Get Floured - Indian Express
Content:
Here is the designers' guide to look trendy even when the economy is not looking good

Zubair Kirmani:
Go, mix and match items of clothing to get the perfect look. The ideal thing to do is buy one designer item, like a pair of trousers or a skirt, and then team it with everyday items from the wardrobe. Colours go a long way in defining your dressing sensibility. Invest in safe colours like charcoal-grey, ivory and maroon that can hold its own beyond a single season. Focus on visually rich looking accessories, like mufflers, caps, bangles, which can make you look simple, yet classy.

Anupamaa Dayal:
Recession hardly means dressing down. What it does imply, instead, is to cut out whimsical shopping. Buy one item of clothing, but make sure it is of the best quality. Trans-seasonal dressing is going to be big in a way, since the ideal way to deal with the situation is to buy clothing which is not seasonal. Buy a dress which you can also wear in summer, but team it up with a polo neck sweater, leggings or skinny jeans, and accessories like a dressy shawl or stole. This way you'll have a compact wardrobe, but you'll still be dressed for the season. I am not particularly fond of classic styles of dressing, unless it's pepped up with imaginative accents. For my autumn-winter collection, I have been careful to keep the silhouettes slim because you cannot go in for a layered look if any one item is bulky.

Varun Bahl:
Even though recession might not affect trousseau expenses, you can exercise moderation in your everyday wardrobe. Go for basic clothing, which you can team up with a lot of other accents. Bring back black. Invest in a lot of blacks, since it is one colour that can be worn in many different ways, for both casual and formal occasions. You can go in for bright accessories — bright belts, colourful bags and shoes. These will lend warmth to the entire look.

Heading: Drawing the Soul Out - Indian Express
Content:
Arshi Dhupia's cakes are whimsical sculptures made of flour and sugar

Arshi Dhupia had been sculpting clay for a long time but didn't make much money out of her hobby. Then she switched medium, from clay to flour, and suddenly there were takers for her art. In her mixing bowl are the usual ingredients — flour, sugar and eggs with yellow eyes ready to be folded. But Dhupia, 32, is not satisfied making the everyday plum cake and walnut cake though she does bake them as well. She adds some ounces of whimsy and fun, and crafts cakes that look like vodka bottles and sneakers, Hanuman and Disney characters and even a bearded Sikh doctor surrounded by capsules and stethoscope. And then there are risqué, sexplicit baked fantasies.

"I've always enjoyed working with clay, but then I decided to take my sculpting skills to a different level and began baking cakes with a twist," says Dhupia, who has had no formal training in baking. And when she's not donning her apron and getting her hands messy, she studies law at Delhi University.

She has been baking at her Golf Links home for seven years now, but the business picked up recently when she started churning out theme-baked cakes. "They have really caught on," says Dhupia, who takes a day to deliver the order. She gets at least half-dozen orders a day, though a particularly busy one has seen her bake 250 cakes. In the past month, Dhupia has designed and baked a zoo, a pirate ship and a Volkswagen Beetle. Dhupia laughs when I ask her about the special "adult" cakes. "There are hen parties and women do use their imagination. I get a few orders that are rather daring and it is fun to bake those cakes," she says, followed by more laughter. Cakes have seldom been this fun.

Prices begin at Rs 350 per kilo. Contact 9811296858

Content:

Heading: Daddy Dearest - Indian Express
Content:
Unlike the film industry, new soaps introduce 'fresh' faces for lead roles instead of cashing in on the established ones

With every new soap, half-a-dozen new faces are launched. If we go by the average — five new soaps a month — 2008 alone has seen over 250 new actors on television. The astounding statistics compel one to ask how does the industry absorb so many actors?

Part of the answer lies in the launch of new channels. But the main reason is the dynamics of the industry where a fresh face is preferred over an established name. The known actors then rarely return in lead roles, acceding to play supporting cast in a soap or participating in reality shows.

Often, 'big' faces go obscure once the soap's off the air or the script changes track. They age off, die, get kidnapped or undergo plastic surgery. Sumeet Sachdev, Gautam in Kyunkii Saas Bhi Bahu Thi, was once the lead but generation leaps ate into his role. He's not been part of another show. Now, with Kyunkii's doubtful future, he too may become invisible unless he reinvents himself. Instant recollection yields other such names — Preeti Amin of Jhoom Barabar Jhoom, Poorva Gokhale of Kkoi Dil Mein Hai, Vikas Manaktala and Priyanka Bassi of Left Right Left.

The word in the industry is that the new-face phenomenon is the offshoot of the tantrums the actors throw after tasting success. The producers however, deny this. "The characters on the small screen are more memorable than the actors who play them. So it's difficult to launch, say, a Rajshri Thakur as the lead in another show as people still remember her as Saloni of Saat Phere. Moreover, even though I wish to hire her, I can't, unless I have a script where her character will override Saloni's popularity," explains Sunjoy Wadhwa of Sphere Origin Productions. One can recall how Sakshi Tanwar's role as Ganga in

Kahaani Hamaarey Mahabharat Ki didn't go down well with the audience because they couldn't think of her as anyone but Parvati of Kahaani Ghar Ghar Kii.

Rajan Shahi of Director's Kut feels that time commitments also contribute to the strain. "To play the lead is as much a drawback as an advantage. If an actor is shooting for me 10 hours a day, they don't have time to do much else," he remarks. "Besides, soaps are driven by scripts — new faces bring freshness to new characters." Citing an example, he points out that there are hardly any faces in the industry that could have done

justice to the four young characters in the new show Miley Jab Hum Tum.

It leads to fierce competition, but these days, with the advent of reality shows and experimentation with scripts, a la Balika Vadhu, the actors have more options. Karan Panthaky, the lead in Jhoom Barabar Jhoom, points out, "Reality shows like Nach Baliye require many senior actors, which paves the way for new ones on other shows." Panthaky has not been seen after his show went off air two months ago. "I'm open to doing non-lead roles; after all, these days, villains are more important."

But Sanjeeda Sheikh disagrees that the career scope of an actor is limited after having played the lead. "My role as a vamp in Kayamath became more popular than my lead character in Kya Hoga Nimmo Ka."

Sheikh will soon be seen in a film but says she's happier doing TV. "There's so much to do. I have no complains."

Heading: Talking point with  RJ Maliska - Indian Express
Content:
My Daddy the Crocodile Hunter
Animal Planet
Sunday, Nov 9, 8 pm
Rating***

What's it about? On September 4, 2006, crocodile hunter Steve Irwin died an untimely death in the oceans while filming for his show, when he was speared through the heart by a sting ray. The world lamented the loss of a naturalist who had brought glamour to khaki shorts and had made reptiles and creepy-crawlies seem lovable. This show is a dedication to that man and features his daughter, nine-year-old Bindi Irwin. The special one-hour long programme will take viewers behind the scenes and will show them what it was like to grow up with her famous father.

Who's in it? The show is very ably hosted by a young and charismatic Bindi Sue Irwin. Bindi, who was named by Steve after his favourite crocodile, has spent practically all her life in front of the camera — right from the moment she was born. She's very much at ease and for those worried whether she'll overplay the sentimental card; there's nothing to fear as Bindi manages to keep the mood upbeat; although, fans of Steve, will occasionally feel choked up at the sight of the old Crocodile Hunter footage. Steve's widow, Terry Irwin, gets her few minutes before the camera too, as she talks about her daughter, but essentially the show belongs to little Bindi

What's hot? Steve, Steve and more Steve. The Crocodile Hunter may have died, but his charisma and mystique live on in the behind-the-scenes and home-video footage that his daughter shows. Bindi herself is well on her way to becoming a star in her own right and it shows in the panache and confidence with which she hosts the show. Also, watch it to know why Bindi's tribute to her dad at his funeral received a standing ovation and went on to be declared the TV moment of 2006. The girl speaks from her heart and thankfully, avoids th saccharin sweetness that afflicts so many TV tributes Also, like her father, even bestows goodbye kisses on the little creepy-crawlies that she handles at Australia Zoo. Cute.

What's not? This is not a show for initiates into the world of wildlife conservation, but for confirmed Steve Irwin fans who miss the naturalist and his famously zany ways with animals. Some might also find Bindi a little precocious, as she talks nineteen-to-the-dozen about her dad and sings about how "To you he's the Crocodile Hunter, but to me he was always Dad."

Should you be watching it? Definitely. This is a tribute to one of the TV legends of our times, touchingly told by his daughter. And even of you were never a Steve Irwin fan, do tune into the show to see why he appealed to so many all over the world.

Heading: Chatter box - Indian Express
Content:
Orderly (peon), Tis Hazari Court
Residence: Zakir Hussain Marg
Constituency: New Delhi

On Security
The recent blasts have left a scar in our minds. I think the issue of security in Delhi is something that needs immediate attention. One should be able to walk around the city freely without any fear. Why should people die in terror attacks for no fault of theirs?

The government must make an effort to guard against terror attacks.

On price rise
If salaried employees like me have to face the heat due to rising prices, how will the underprivileged cope? Prices of even basic amenities have gone through the roof making it difficult for the common man to make ends meet. I shudder when I think how difficult it must be for those without a fixed income to cope.

On casting the vote
We live in a democratic country and must exercise our voting rights. Citizens, being agents of change, should always vote. By casting my vote, I can exercise my right as a citizen and also give a chance to the worthy contestants who could bring about a positive change in society. Voting should be compulsory.

Heading: Bail granted to couple held for ‘brutality’ against help - Indian Express
Content:
Oye lucky
Chinky, the little girl from Zee TV's Chota Packet Bada Dhamaka, has brought such extraordinary luck to her parents, that they now believe she is an avatar of Vaishnodevi herself. After several years of marriage, Chinky's parents had lost all hope of conceiving. Chinky's dad visited the Vaishnodevi shrine in Kashmir and, soon after his return, the couple conceived. Chinky's birth reconciled all the issues that Chinky's mom had with her in-laws and they started living like a happy family.

Ghost riders
KEEPING in mind the Halloween night, Chak De had a Ghost special episode where the contestants were dressed as their favourite ghost characters. The hosts of the show, Manoj Tiwary and Roshni Chopra were dressed as vampires. One of the contestants, Anirudh, performed to the tune of Apni toh Pathshala in the character of Ghost Rider. Shaberi sure looked like a dead woman haunting the audience. She performed on the song Bhoot hoon mein to match best with her character.

Double Deal
The most loved host of Indian Idol 4 Chang, is winning hearts with his gentle ways with the contestants. But do not forget he is also a trained dentist. Most contestants are seen running towards Dr Chang at the mere sign of a toothache. And very often one finds the doc peering into the mouth of the contestants on the sets. It is quite another thing that Chang also happens to be the heart-throb of all the female contestants and they would leave no opportunity to spend time with the good looking Chang.

Warning: Spoiler ahead
Nach Baliye 4 is doing everything possible to match up to the TRP ratings its predecessors had effortlessly managed. This time around, not one but two jodis will be eliminated from the show. The theme this week is 'time machine' wherein the teams are asked to perform on the blockbuster dance format of yesteryears or jump ahead into future. To decide which team will perform first, judge Karisma Kapoor suggests that the representatives form the respective teams will play the game of staring into each other's eyes. Whoever blinks first loses the toss. It all sounds fun but here's a spoiler: the jodis that finally get eliminated are KarnVir Bora and Teejay Sidhu and Vineet and Tanushree.

Heading: The Magic Continues - Indian Express
Content:
The couple arrested in Gurgaon on Saturday on charges of brutally beating up their 13-year-old domestic help were released on bail on Sunday.

Debokjyoti Das, senior manager in Genpact, and his wife Paromita, assistant director in a Delhi-based private firm, were arrested from their Kendriya Vihar house in Sector 56 early on Saturday morning after the National Commission for Women (NCW) and Shakti Vahini, an NGO, had rescued Lakhi, their domestic help. Lakhi's eyes were swollen and red, two fingers broken and had blisters on her hands. A team was sent to Das' house following a complaint to the NCW from a neighbour.

A medical test on Lakhi confirmed a broken upper jaw and teeth and bruises below the right eye, advising opinions of a dental surgeon and an eye specialist. The report found a deformed little finger on her right hand and healed wounds and scars all over her body, besides pain in the back and other external injuries. The report also confirmed that all the injuries were inflicted by a blunt object within 72 hours before her rescue.

Debokjyoti and Paromita were charged under Sections 323 (voluntarily causing injuries), 342 (wrongful confinement) and 374 (unlawful compulsory labour) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 15 of the Child Labour Regulatory Act. While Debokjyoti got bail on Sunday, his wife had got bail late on Saturday night.

DCP (East) Jagdish Nagar said the sections related to "beating". When asked why charges under the Juvenile Protection Act were not brought against the couple, he said it was applicable to cruelty against children up to the age of 13 years. "I do not have a medical report as of now but I was told she is 14 years old," Nagar said, adding that he was yet to personally look into all the matters related to the case.

Investigating officer Hawa Singh said the sections were decided after long discussions. "I had only heard of such cases. This is the first time in my 32-year-old career that I have seen such a case. Getting bail does not mean they have been acquitted. If her eye report says she may lose vision, we will include Section 326, which is non-bailable."

When asked why Paromita was released on Saturday, Singh said according to directions from the Supreme Court, a child or a woman could not be detained overnight unless they were arrested for a heinous crime.

Heading: Small talk - Indian Express
Content:
The 2500th show of the popular Marathi play Gadhvacha Lagna also proves to be a tribute to eminent stage artiste Prakash Inamdar as it continues to create the same magic even after 25 years

Taking over the stage once again, this time for its 2500th show, 'Gadhvacha Lagna', the renowned piece of Marathi folk theatre, entertained the city based theatre lovers making them indulge in a laugh riot. Coincidentally this year the play celebrates its silver jubilee as well.

Gadhvacha Lagna with its local flavour was first showcased by Kalasangam on November 9, 1983. Woven around the characters of Sawla Kumbhar, his wife Gangi and Gandharva (the prince who turns into a donkey), the play is a vagnatya (comedy that makes a comment on socio-political issues).

"The play has drawn hordes of crowd whenever it has been staged because of its common touch," says Jaymala Inamdar, wife of late Prakash Inamdar and a celebrated stage personality, who has played the character of Gangi opposite Sawla Kumbhar a character portrayed by her husband ever since the play was first staged.

Although the main plot of the play was penned by Haribhau Vadgaonkar, while the elements of Gan, Gauran and Rang Baji that add on to its folk background and precede the main plot were written by late Prakash Inamdar.

Talking about the 2500th enactment of the play, Jaymala informs "This basically fulfills the dream of my husband who had always wanted that the 2500th showcasing will be held in Shaniwar wada. Also in honour of late Prakash Inamdar we at Kalasangam decided to present a donkey to a needy kumbhar family on the day of the play."

With the recent demise of Prakash Inamdar, the 2500th show of the comic play, organised by Kala Sangam and Samvad saw Pradeep Patwardhan taking over the role of Sawla Kumbhar, the character that had been immortalised by the former. Reminiscing the days when her husband was alive, an emotional Jaymala says, "Prakash ji was not only my husband but also my guru. He always said that the couple of Amitabh and Rekha can split up but our companionship on stage and off stage will never terminate. However this time he was not there and his absence was terribly felt," adds she.

Having brought Gangi to life on stage for the past 25 years, an ecstatic Inamdar says "I consider myself as more of Gangi than Jaymala. And it is Gangi's innocence that makes me fall in love with the character again and again"

Cutting across language barriers, the play has won huge accolades in cities like Hyderabad and Bangalore apart from Maharashtra. Expressing the family's emotional attachment with the play, Dhanalaxmi Inamdar, daughter of the Inamdar couple, who's also a part of the play, says, "Our emotional involvement with the play goes to the extent that for us donkey has become a luck charm."

Having befriended the stage for 40 years now, for Jaymala Inamdar, stage is the place, which gives her the maximum pleasure. "For me being on stage is the ultimate tonic of all my problems and I would like to perform till the last days of my life, " concludes she.

Content:

Content:

Heading: Tuning Right - Indian Express
Content:
Artiste Rohan Pore unveils Pu La's endearing personality at Pulotsav through his sketches

The interesting irony in artiste Rohan Pore's life is that one of the saddest moments of his life made him think about one of the most humourous authors in the history of Marathi literature. Seven years ago, when Pore lost his guru and uncle Chandrakant Pore, he decided to explore his sketching and painting abilities by creating a collection of paintings of Pu La Deshpande. It is this collection, which is on display at Pulotsav that started on Saturday.

"I have always been a painter but after my uncle's death, I was shattered. He was my teacher, mentor and a great source of motivation. At that point, it was Pu La's books that helped me get over the grief. I read almost all the books by Pu La and while reading, found his character interesting. That is when I thought of coming up with a collection of Pu La's paintings. Initially I did this collection on my own but when I got to know about Pulotsav, I approached the organisers and redid the entire work on a bigger scale," says Pore, a final year fine arts student of Bharti Vidyapeeth College of Fine arts, Nasik. He further adds, "This man who brought smiles on the faces of countless Maharashtrians had a comic face as well. He was a true actor and exactly knew how to convey the expressions to the audience. But from drawing point of view, there are two typical features that easily depict his personality - his nose and his spectacles."

The exhibition of over 18 sketches depicts Pu La's journey from his childhood till his death. It unveils various facets of Pu La's personality through portraits that display his expressions while reading, writing, relaxing with his wife, acting in plays like Batatyachi chawl and so on. "These are black and white sketches and I have done them by using pencil, pen and charcoal as the mediums. The organisers, after finalising the exhibition, gave me 23 days and I sat for almost 12 hours every day to complete the task," says Pore.

Pore, who has won a number of prizes that include Camlin award, ETV award and state level awards says, "We normally do paintings on white paper and darken the black portion. In one of the pictures however, I have used white marker on black paper. Thus it was a challenging task as I had to leave open the black portion and highlight the rest. It was difficult but at the end of the day, this painting is my most memorable one."

And why wouldn't it be? After all, isn't this painting synonymous with Pore's life?

Heading: Readers’ Paradise - Indian Express
Content:
After putting together the first-of- its kind violin orchestra in India, the Suzuki School of Violin accomplished an enriching music weekend for its students and at Khandala

A child learns music at our school in much the same way the mother tongue is learnt, what we do is develop and enhance this ability of a child through a nurturing environment," said Rama Chobe, who is the first teacher and founder of Suzuki School in India. A gold medalist in Indian classical music, Chobe is also a faculty at Lalit Kala Academy (UOP). Leading the school, which is part of Suzuki Association, worldwide, Rama is trained in the Suzuki method of teaching music to small children from academy at Florida and has done a teachers training course at Suzuki Association in Japan.

Dr Shinichi Suzuki, the legendary Japanese teacher, founded the Suzuki method of education. He called the process as the Mother Tongue method and the whole system of teaching as Talent Education. Today, the movement has over four lakh children in 38 countries.

At Pune School, 60 budding violinists between ages two and15 are trained in the Suzuki method. The students have now formed India's first of its kind violin orchestra that regularly performs at concerts in Pune.

"In the west we learn only one language and never get perfect in learning any other language. It's amazing in India every Indian knows more than two languages, its this ability that makes Indians master anything very easily," said Helen Brunner, the founder of the London Suzuki group who regularly visits Pune school to take group classes. Western classical exponents and students from France, Germany and UK also come regularly to share their experiences.

Over the weekend on November 8 and 9, a two-day conference was organised by school at Khandala, designed towards inspiring children to develop listening skills and the art of appreciating Indian and western classical music. The music conference aimed towards children and parents who together experienced a weekend of music and melodies. It was attended by luminaries like Suzuki music teacher Helen Brunner from UK. Special invitee sessions conducted by Dr Kedar, professor, FTII, Pune, Arnaud Devic, western classical music patron, France and Ashok Ranade, Hindustani classical vocalist, the students also performed in a concert to end the conference where they rendered the Suzuki repertoire as well as folk songs and classical music from India.

Heading: Innocence with a flaw - Indian Express
Content:
Book exhibition- Mymarathi by Akshardhara offers a wide range of Marathi novels, short stories, biographies and reference books

There was a time when Marathi books did not need marketing and copies used to be booked much before the release. Today, however, the scenario is different. Sharing a small section in mega bookstores, Marathi is no more the only language of books but just a name given to a corner.

To promote Marathi books, Akshardhara has organised a month long Marathi book fair named Mymarathi at Atre Sabhagriha, Bajirao road. The exhibition in its 14th year is the 300th book fair in the state. "Not many people these days read Marathi books. There are authors and publishers. But it is of no use if there are no readers. We have been doing this exhibition with only one motive of promoting quality Marathi books," says Laxman Rathiwadekar, chief manager, Akshardhara.

The exhibition consists of a collection of nearly 1,00,000 books by well-known Marathi authors. To name a few, it includes books by renowned writers such as P K Atre, P L Deshpande, Maruti Chitampalli, Mangesh Padgaonkar and so on. Some of the most favourite biographical books are Idli Arcade ani me by Viththal Kamat of Kamat hotels, Chakwa Chandan by Maruti Chitampalli, Me kasa Jhalo by P K Atre, Wise and Otherwise by Sudha Murthy and so on. "We are running this exhibition on a no profit no loss basis. In fact for the first time in the history of Marathii books we have also introduced buy one get one free scheme," says Rathiwadekar.

"We are developing a database wherein the readers can come up with their own ideas about how Marathi literature can be promoted. We have introduced a form in which they can write about what kind of topics can be handled by Marathi authors, what should be the ideal prices of Marathi books ," says Rathiwadekar. For all the book lovers this is a must visit.

Heading: Failure to register alliance cost BJP, Sena PMC opposition leader post - Indian Express
Content:
The anti child begging campaign by the city's youth and NGOs aims to bring to notice the ill effects of offering alms to a child beggar

Next time you roll down the glass of your window panes when your car screeches to halt at a signal to oblige a six–year old beggar, think again. As the city youngsters gear up to make people aware what giving alms to child beggars lead to , the act of hunting pockets t for change everytime you encounter a child beggar, mostly to earn the benefits of a karmic bonus will face severe criminal charges.

By this, most of us would be encouraging these kids to beg throughout their lives. "In due course of time these kids get used to getting easy money. Even if they can take out time to study and the ones in their late teens, who can find time to work prefer begging because that is easy money and we by encouraging this are surely committing a crime," says Nupur Nanal, SYB, Fergusson College who is volunteering for the Anti Child Begging Campaign jointly organised by the NGOs Dream India 2020 and Samidha.

The campaingn is scheduled to be on November 15 and 16.

The campaign that aims at driving home the message that giving alms to child beggars is dragging the kids towards the world of gambling, pick pocketting and other petty thefts will have counters put up at various pockets in the city where the volunteeres will interact with people. "We are putting up couters at MG Road, Sauras Bagh, Sambhaji Park, Inox and E- Square. We are having this campaign on a weekend when MG Road will have 'Walking Plaza, which will give us a better opportunity to interact with people. We are also having a street play staged by college sudents in those two days," says 24 - year - old Amit Subhash Gawade, software engineer who too is volunteering for the event.

With an attempt to pull off the mask that misleads one's vision into committing this crime the campaign will also have fliers stating the reasons why one should not give alms to child beggars. "Unknowingly, common people like us promote child begging by giving alms to children at traffic-signals, road sides and in public places. Child beggars involved in criminal activities pose a serious threat to social security, not to mention the very moral fabric of society. The easy money lure them into tobacco chewing, gambling and other such activities," shares Saurabh Pethekar, IT professional and a volunteer for the campaign.

Through the campaign they make an appeal to the Puneites to stop giving alms to child beggars. "We humbly request the people to contact and support government agencies, welfare committees, NGOs and institutions working for such children i this regard if found any child begger. When you give them alms these organisations' efforts to rehabilitate child beggars is getting affected," says Nanal.

The campaign also aims to support NGOs in giving these children a chance to get off the streets, to get a decent education, and to live a life with dignity and self-respect.

Heading: Proposal: Let consumer pay more for zero loadshedding - Indian Express
Content:
Cannot be counted as allies as they never registered an alliance, rule judges

The Shiv Sena and BJP may call themselves allies at the national and state levels but they cannot use the same tag in the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), the Bombay High Court has ruled. This was because they had not registered an alliance before or after the polls.

As such, BJP councillor Vikas Mathkari cannot be Leader of the Opposition, the court ruled, pointing out that his claim had been based on the combined BJP-Sena strength. It revoked the decision of Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale appointing Mathkari and passed a judgment in favour of the Congress for the post of Leader of the Opposition.

The court observed that the BJP and the Sena were not a single entity and the alliance did not exist in PMC technically. "In our view, the combined strength of BJP-Shiv Sena cannot be considered an alliance in this case," a bench of S B Mhase and A A Kumbhakoni said.

The court pointed out that there was no pre-poll alliance or post-poll alliance registered by the BJP-Shiv Sena or the councillors elected on the support of these two parties, as laid down in the Maharashtra Local Authority Members' Disqualification Act, 1986.

City BJP chief Girish Bapat refused to comment on the order, but said, "Not completing a technical process caused the loss of the post." The decision has left the BJP neither in the ruling alliance nor in the lead in the Opposition.

"We cannot be blamed for the situation of the BJP in the PMC. The BJP never formally tabled any proposal for registering the alliance. Had they done so, we would have responded then itself," Shyam Deshpande, Shiv Sena leader in the PMC, said.

The court said the Gazette Notification issued as per the election rules demonstrated that candidates were separately sponsored by the BJP and the Sena and the BJP-Sena alliance as such did not sponsor even a single candidate in the civic elections on February 14, 2007.

A mere claim that the BJP and Sena were working as an alliance for a considerable length of time in the state cannot mean that councillors sponsored by either becomes a candidate of the alliance, it said. The court added that their combined strength cannot be considered for deciding which party had the greatest numerical strength in the Opposition or for Mathkari to stake a claim as Leader of the Opposition.

Considering the case in perspective, the court said the party strength in the PMC was likewise; NCP (41), Congress (36), BJP (25), Shiv Sena (20). Thus, it can be concluded that the leader of INC will be entitled to be recognised as the "leader of the party in the Opposition", as it is the largest party in the Opposition.

Heading: Enough of civic garbage: villagers want dump moved - Indian Express
Content:
With Tata Power Company reportedly expressing its inability to provide additional power at the prescribed rate for continuing the Pune model of zero loadshedding, consumers may now have to pay more. A proposal has been made to the power regulatory council to pass on part of the cost on to the consumer.

"There is an increase in power prices due to growing demand throughout the country. Tata Power Company is unable to procure and supply additional power at the prescribed rate to fill the power gap in the zero loadshedding model run jointly by the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Ltd (MSEDCL) and the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII)," said Ajay Bhushan Pandey, managing director of MSEDCL.

The Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC) had allowed MSEDCL to purchase power from Tata Power Company at a maximum Rs 8.54 per unit to fill the gap in Pune Model, he said. But the company had expressed its inability to do so, due to an increase in power prices, he added.

"We plan to continue the Pune model. In a recent review meeting with CII and NGO Prayas, it has been decided to approach MERC to seek an increase in prices for power procurement from Tata Power Company to overcome the deficit. This will be done through a proposal to increase the reliability charge from consumers," Pandey said.

There is no other way for MSEDCL to keep the Pune model operational, he said, adding that the deficit in November last year was 180 MW, which increased to 308 MW for the same month this year, due to a rise in demand.

The Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court will hear a petition against MSEDCL for allegedly favouring some cities for uninterrupted power, Pandey said.

Heading: Cash war over Games cables threatens progress pace - Indian Express
Content:
For years, people on the outskirts of Pune have been seeing their villages being turned into a dumping ground for the city's garbage. Villagers of Uruli Devachi and Phursungi had wanted state pollution control authorities to rein in the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), alleging they were facing health hazards.

But to their dismay, the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) has failed to take any action other than issuing notices to the civic body for "unscientifically" dumping the garbage.

Now, the MPCB is said to be getting ready to send the "final" notice to PMC. The civic body, on the other hand, is ready with a garbage processing unit, but the angry villagers would have none of that. Tired of mere warnings against the PMC every now and then, the villagers, particularly from Uruli Devachi and Phursungi, are seeking concrete action from MPCB and want the garbage dump shifted.

The gram panchayats of Uruli Devachi and Phursungi had, from time to time, been complaining against contamination of groundwater including water in the village wells, the stench from the dump and frequent fires at the site spewing out smoke. In a notice in September 2008 issued to PMC chief medical officer (solid waste management), the MPCB had rapped the civic body for unscientific disposal of municipal solid waste.
