"You (PMC) have failed to provide proper transportation arrangement for carrying Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) to the site, due to which, spillover of garbage was noticed at many places creating a foul smell," the notice says.

In November 2001 and again in September 2004, the MPCB issued notices pointing out many deficiencies in the garbage disposal system of PMC.

"MPCB has merely forwarded notices to PMC and failed to take any concrete action, even though we have been having a harrowing time since years because of this open dumping of garbage and suffering from many health issues," said a villager.

Regional officer, MPCB, P K Mirashe said, "Sending notices is part of our action." He admitted though that despite regular reminders, the PMC has largely failed to take concrete action. "Finally our head office in Mumbai has now sent a comprehensive and final notice to the civic body covering all the issues. Now, we will give them some time to execute these or else we will start legal action immediately."

Responding to this, municipal commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi said, "We are ready with a garbage processing unit, but the villagers do not want it. They want the dump shifted out, which is why we could not operate the unit. We are also launching a project to seal the garbage and procure methane from it. But it will take some time."

Heading: Kids who lived on streets cycle for those who still do - Indian Express
Content:
A tussle over who will bear the cost incurred for laying underground power cables below roads readied before the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) is threatening to slow down infrastructure development work that had peaked last month under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM).

The Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Ltd (MSEDCL) has locked horns with the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) as well as the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) on the matter.

Under the assumption that MSEDCL would incur the expenditure, the PMC and PCMC had carried out road development work in record time for the Games. They shifted electricity poles and and laid down underground cables on their own to avoid any delay. But the MSEDCL is refusing to foot the bill.

The issue cropped up on Sunday at a meeting of the Pune District Electricity Coordination Committee, where State Energy Minister Dilip Walse-Patil ruled out MSEDCL paying up.

Seconding his view at the council hall, Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar said, "MSEDCL cannot incur the cost of laying electric cables for work undertaken by the civic body. It is not possible for MSEDCL to pay PMC and PCMC because other local bodies will follow suit and the electricity company cannot afford such bills."

The issue was raised by BJP legislator Girish Bapat who commended the work of laying underground cables in place of overhead wires keeping safety in view.

PMC Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi said no funds were allotted for underground electricity cables in projects under JNNURM and the expenses were too high to be borne by the civic body. "The laying of cables is MSEDCL's responsibility. They should at least share the expense with the civic body," he said.

PCMC Commissioner Ashish Sharma said PCMC had to pay Rs 75 crore just for laying underground cables on a road construction project for which Rs 200 crore had been allotted under JNNURM. He added that it was not viable for the civic body to spend such a big amount on cables when there was no provision of funds from the Union government.

The state energy minister said is MSEDCL bears the expenses, other civic bodies would seek the same. "MSEDCL is now a company and cannot afford to pay local civic bodies for such work," he said and added, "The MSEDCL had considered the demand as a special case and offered to share 50 per cent of the expenses. But it did not receive any response from both the civic bodies."

Pawar has directed the officials of MSEDCL, PMC and PCMC to hold a meeting soon to resolve the issue.

Heading: Look for alternative sites, govt tells civic body - Indian Express
Content:
Not long ago, these visitors to the city from Bangalore lived on the streets and did odd jobs to survive. Chance brought them to an art school in Bangalore, to a life less harsh. Now, they are on their way to Pakistan and are travelling to Lahore, on bicycles. The aim is to spread a message that will bring a better life for more children like themselves.

The bicycle campaigners are now camping in Pune city. Their message: "war economy" is fuelling "child labour economy" and both India and Pakistan are doing the same, by spending more on defence and wars.

"All these children who once lived on the streets are now carrying a message to children of Pakistan about non-violence and rejection of war. In any war, children are affected the most," said John Devaraj, a Bangalore-based artist, who runs an art school for street children and is now taking them to Lahore.

"We'll be travelling to Dandi in a few days and will make salt like the Mahatma did, again to embrace non-violence," he said.

All these children have a tragic past, a life of abuse and being subjected to violence being common to all their stories. Juanita, who took the name after an artist, was a domestic help in Gujarat. She was abused by her employers who tried to force her into marriage. "I escaped, begged, lived in some hostels, then found my way to John's school. Now I learn ballet, art, dance and theatre," Juanita (19) said.

Frieda, also 19, once worked in a silk factory in Salem. Gaja,10, from Bihar, was sold by his family; Jairam, 20, worked in a restaurant and was once jailed for stealing bullets for scrap value; Satish, 12, was a "child soldier" in Chhattisgarh.

On Sunday evening, they staged a street show to spread their message. On Monday morning, they will interact with children of Bhojwani School and present another play. The group is expected to reach Lahore on November 27. Only some of them will be able to enter Pakistan, through the Wagah border though, because of visa problems .

Heading: Withdraw semester system: UoP senate members - Indian Express
Content:
Principal Secretary, Environment, Valsa Nair, has issued orders to PMC to ready a plan for alternate garbage dumping sites as well as develop methods of biodegradable waste treatment facility at garbage treatment plants. "Around 600 metric tonne garbage is generated at this site daily and there is a need for scientific treatment of the waste. The municipal corporation should take this on priority as it is affecting the villagers in the area," said Nair.

She said once the new sites are ready, the old site needs to be capped and treated scientifically. The coming week will see Nair and Additional Chief Secretary, Health, Chandra Iyengar, inspecting the site. "A time frame will be given to ensure speedy execution,"she added.

Meanwhile, the PMC has apparently zeroed in on two sites, but Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi did not want to reveal the names of the sites as yet for fear of any agitation from the residents.

"We will be putting up the proposal shortly," he said, adding that he had discussed the new sites with the corporators.

Heading: Hard times for firms big and small - Indian Express
Content:
Hardly five months after introducing semester system for postgraduate courses, the University of Pune's (UoP) senate members have forwarded their resolution to withdraw the system.

Three senate members Suresh Todkar, advocate Chintamani Ghate and Hari Solanki have sought withdrawal of the semester pattern. The main reason cited is that students were facing difficulties in adjusting to the change which required them to appear for exams three times a year at the end of each semester. The members have also complained that professors do not get enough time to complete the entire syllabus within one semester resulting in students' loss. "Most of their time goes in preparing for the exams and paper setting," stated Suresh Todkar in his resolution.

Solanki, on the other hand has reasoned that rural students have to bear the burden of paying examination fees thrice a year. He has stated in his resolution that "it delays the declaration of results". Ghate's resolution also stated that "the semester pattern introduced in some faculties be replaced with annual pattern to ensure academic continuity and reduction of financial burden on students".

It was on May 9 this year, that UoP vice chancellor Dr Narendra Jadhav announced the introduction of the semester pattern at postgraduate-level studies in all its affiliated colleges and recognised institutions from 2008-09.

Greater flexibility and reforms like credit-based evaluation, dual degrees and credit sharing with universities abroad, were cited as the reasons for switching over to the semester system. Also, UoP was the first in the country to introduce the semester pattern of studies at its on-campus post-graduate (PG) science departments in 1971. However, the pattern never went beyond the PG science subjects to include other streams.

There are more than 250 UoP affiliated colleges offering PG courses.

Heading: Two IT engineers killed in accident on Mumbai-Bangalore highway - Indian Express
Content:
As recession continues, companies mull labour cut, extend credit period for payment

If the recession continues for more than six months, the jobs of over 1,50,000 unskilled labourers who are employed in the 7,000 small scale units and several medium scale ones in Pimpri, Bhosari, Chikali and Chakan could be the hardest hit. Small-scale companies, many of whom do not have deep pockets, will resort to terminating the contracts of a chunk of these employees, said Suresh Mehtre, chairman of Pimpri Chinchwad Small Industries Association.

Vendors of large companies usually offload their work to sub vendors. These sub vendors are already hit as orders from vendors are down to a trickle.

Many are already leading a hand-to-mouth existence. Due to low demand, inventories at many small-scale industries are building up.

"We are not planning any labour cuts at the moment. But 10 of our vendors have disengaged a total of 50 staff. If this situation continues for more than three months, a lot of small workshops may go for labour cuts of up to 50 per cent. Exports have taken a hit, as many European companies have cancelled orders foreseeing low demand and extended their credit periods" said Deepak Bhoite, CEO of Vijay Engeineering works.

"For the deliveries made, many companies are extending the credit period for payment. For example, earlier, Tata Motors used to make payments to vendors in 30 days. Now, they do it in 60 days. Many organisations are making half payments and wants longer credit periods.

On the other hand, banks are not lending money easily to these industries. This, coupled with high interest rates, is making the whole situation grim. This year, many small-scale units also gave their staff extended Diwali holidays due low demand,'' said Mehtre.

A leading labour supplier from the city, employing 6,000 people, who refused to be named said, "We have cut 20 per cent of work force as our clients don't need them owing to low production."

Heading: 21 employees of firm suffers food infection - Indian Express
Content:
Two computer engineers were killed when the tyre of the car they were travelling in burst and rammed into another car. The accident occurred at 12.30 pm near Tanaji Patil Nagar near Ranwara hotel on the Mumbai-Bangalore highway on Saturday.

According to PSI S Patil, who is investigating the case, "Babasaheb Bhosale (26) was driving his Mitsubishi Lancer towards Katraj when its tyre burst. It rammed into a Mercedes, which was stationery, and skidded off to the other side of the road where it collided with a truck laden with gas cylinders."

Babasaheb was traveling along with his friend Manjusha Patekar (26). Both of them died on the spot.

Bhosale, a resident of Balajinagar in Dhankawadi, was working with Cognizant Technologies while Manjusha, a Kothrud resident, was working with a software firm in Hadapsar, Patil said.

"People in the other car, belonging to a manager from Venky's, escaped unharmed and the truck driver sustained minor injuries," Patil said

Heading: Police aspirant dies at recruitment ground - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 21employees of Premier Energy Transmission Limited were admitted at various hospitals in Pimpri-Chinchwad after they suffered food infection. The Nigdi police are conducting preliminary investigations to if the employees were infected from the breakfast and lunch they had from the company canteen on Friday.

While fifteen patients have been admitted to Lokmanya Hospital, six were admitted to Kanitkar hospital, Chinchwad. Those admitted to Kantikar hospital were discharged by afternoon after medical treatment.

Speaking on the issue, PCMC medical chief Nagkumar Kunachgi said, "It is difficult to term the condition as food poisoning. The employees had symptoms of food infection like headache and stomachache. But it cannot be said that the incident happened after the employees had food at the company as they had food at home also after that."

Inspector Sudam Darekar of Nigdi police station said, " We have not registered any case yet. We will conduct preliminary investigations first."

"We have recorded the statements of those employees admitted to Lokmanya Hospital. None of them are in serious conditions. At least, three out of the fourteen admitted patients refused to give their statements," he said.

Darekar said that the patients said that they had 'poha' in the company on Friday morning and after that they had food at home also.

"About 300 employees had food in the company canteen and only some were infected. Food inspectors who visited the hospitals said that food poisoning is detected within eight hours but these patients were admitted two days after they had food at the company," said Darekar.

Shrikrishna Barshikar, Personal Manager of the company, said, " We don't know what is the reason of infection. It might also be possible that they might have got their own tiffins and shared food. We might be able to tell you the reason after the investigations are over."

Heading: Rs 38-cr fraud: Court order against bank’s ex-chairman and director - Indian Express
Content:
A 27-year-old youth died at the State Reserve Police Force (SRPF) ground in Hadapsar soon after completing his running test for the physical examination of police recruitment on Saturday. Heart failure is suspected to be the cause of the death.

The deceased was identified as Anil Hanumant Raskar, resident of Kodre Mala, Yavat. Police said that Raskar was working in a private company and had married eight months back.

A family member said that Raskar had wanted to join police force since childhood. He tried three times before but was unable to clear the recruitment examination. This time he had prepared hard. "He studied hard and exercised everyday for the last few months," he added.

Raskar came to Pune on Friday, as he was short listed for the physical test. He was staying with a relative and reached the SRPF ground at 7 am on Saturday. After completing the 800 meters running test, in which he stood first, he felt chest pain.

He, however, did not take it seriously and laid down under a tree for rest. Around 12 pm, when other candidates went to call him for the remaining tests, he did not wake up.

They informed the police and Raskar was rushed to the Command Hospital at Wanavdi, where he was pronounced dead. The Hadapsar police have registered an accidental death case. Raskar's body was sent for postmortem. Police have informed his family members in Yevat and Solapur.

Heading: In Bhilai, Maya begins election campaign - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune District and sessions court has issued an order against the absconding director and ex-chairman of Ajit Co-operative Bank to be present in the court before December 5 for having misappropriated funds to the tune of Rs 38 crores by providing faulty documents and taking multiple loans.

The court order has been issued against Vilas Sarnobat, the former chairman of the bank and Rajendra Konde, director of the bank. ACP Netaji Shinde, who is investigating the case said, "The complaint had been registered against the two in August, and the first warrant had been issued on September 10. The two, however, did not appear and that's why an order has been issued against them."

There are five irregular loan counts against Konde. Sarnobat too had been instrumental in providing false documents and passing fake loans, the police said. A total of 23 members of the bank were found guilty and five of them have also been arrested earlier. They were, however, let off on bail.

They have been booked under sections 403, 409, 467, 468, 471, and 34 of the IPC. According to the police, the two had mortgaged their property to pay off the amount but had still fallen short of 25 crores. They added that in case they fail to appear before the court by the stipulated time, the court would seize all their properties.

The bank has three branches in the city at Dhankawadi, Hadapsar and Shirur. The police said that they had used fake photographs and minors as guarantors to get the loans approved.

The police have appealed to the citizens to contact them at 26208377 if they have any information on these two men.

Heading: Adib Khan is Cong-SP candidate for RS - Indian Express
Content:
The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) national president Mayawati kicked off her poll campaign on Sunday with an election rally in Bhilai, Chhatisgarh.

The party has started working in full swing for the assembly elections in five states. Jobs have been allotted to each minister, parliamentarian and legislator and each Bhaichara Committee coordinator — with clear instructions and a special warning not to violate the Election Commission guidelines.

The programme of Mayawati, too, is being given a final shape.

"She will be addressing five public meetings in each state," said a party leader. Her next visits to Madhya Pradesh have been slated for November 17 and 24. For Rajasthan, the proposed dates are November 26 and December 4. Her trusted lieutenant Satish Chandra Mishra is expected to accompany her to most meetings.

Known for its organised campaigning style, the BSP had deployed state in-charges in Delhi, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh.

Cabinet ministers Badshah Singh and Rangnath Mishra — the in-charges of Madhya Pradesh — have been camping in the state since the party came to power in UP.

Similarly, Cabinet minister Nakul Dubey and party leader Sewa Ram are spending most of their time in Chhattisgarh as state in-charges. Aligarh legislator Mahendra Singh and Ganga Charan Dinkar, who lost the assembly polls in Bundelkhand, have been made permanent in-charges of Delhi.

Given the magnitude of their tasks, these in-charges did not even participate in the gala event of filing of Rajya Sabha nominations on Friday. Party sources confirm that Mayawati herself has been spending her weekends in Delhi for over a year and she has been visiting other states too. "Since she will be travelling more frequently to other states for public meetings now, most of her meetings in Delhi will be held in the evenings," said a senior party leader.

Working on the formula of social engineering, the BSP chief has allotted specific duties to senior party leaders. Naseemuddin Siddiqui has been working to motivate the Muslim voter and is sorting out all election-related preparation in each state. Brajesh Pathak is working to bring in Brahmin voters into the party fold. Cabinet minister Anant Kumar Mishra was roped in for Rajasthan earlier, but recently he has been redeployed in Delhi. Paras Nath Maurya — chairman Pichhara Varg Ayog and cabinet minister and party's state president Swami Prasad Maurya — are regularly touring the states to woo backward communities.

Mayawati has instructed her legislators to gather in Delhi on November 14, when they will be allotted election-related duties.

Over a dozen Bhaichara Committees, meanwhile, have been set up in each state. These communities are working to win into the party fold different castes and communities. "Each and every minister, legislator, parliamentarian or Bhaichara Committee coordinator has been entrusted with some specific task in all the states that are going for elections," said a Bhaichara Committee coordinator.

Heading: Lecturer yet to provide papers of cars seized from her homes - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress and the Samajwadi Party have finally decided to support Independent candidate Mohd Adib from Aligarh for the Rajya Sabha elections.

The decision came a day after lengthy discussions between senior SP and Congress leaders at 10 Janpath on Saturday. Adib will file his nomination on Monday, the last day for filing nominations.

Adib is known to work for educational and social upliftment of minorities for decades. He was the coordinator of the minorities' cell of the All India Congress Committee. But when the party reportedly denied him a seat for Lok Sabha elections, he left the party. Adib is an alumnus of the Aligarh Muslim University and has been the student wing president in AMU during late 60s. He moved to Delhi in the early 90s and has been involved with various social activities for the welfare of the minorities since.

"When both parties decided that they had to unite on secular issues, they knew that I was the man," Adib told The Indian Express from Delhi. "It is my secular ideologies against the BJP and my fight against the alienation of Muslims which led to my selection."

Expressing his views against the BJP and its leader LK Advani, Adib said: "Muslims have started feeling alienated and they feel that justice is not meted out to them. When a Muslim boy is arrested, Advani says book him under POTA, but when a non-Muslim is arrested, they book him under some simple criminal act." "I do not belong to any party," Adib said. "My aim is to work for the ideologies I believe in. It is because of this fact both the parties agreed on my name."

Sources in the Congress say parliamentarian Ahmad Patel exerted his influence in finalising Adib's name.

"He has been with Congress for a long time and has been consolidating the party's relation with the minorities," said Rita Bahuguna Joshi, President of the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee. "When both parties were finding it hard to agree on a name, Adib's name was suggested by the Samajwadi Party and Soniaji agreed on it," Joshi added.

Adib's name was a surprise for many as the chief contenders for the seat included Joshi herself, AICC general secretary Salman Khurshid and Congress Legislative Party leader Pramod Tiwari.

Earlier, the Samajwadi Party was keen on fielding Abu Asim Azmi.

As per the strength of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly, 37 votes are required to get a candidate elected to the Rajya Sabha.

The SP, which has 94 legislators, has already fielded Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav. For the third candidate, they needed the support of the Congress, which has 21 legislators.

Maya will make the going tough
Though the SP and Congress have decided to field Md Adib Khan as their joint candidate for the Rajya Sabha seat from Uttar Pradesh, BSP leader Mayawati's aggressive poaching in their camp is likely to haunt them in the Rajya Sabha elections, too. With a candidate requiring 37 first preference votes to get through the Rajya Sabha polls, the ruling BSP in the state seems set to win 5 seats on its own with over two dozen votes to spare.
After Mayawati announced six candidates for the RS polls from her party, poaching would be rampant as the sixth BSP candidate would require more than half a dozen votes to sail through.
And given that Akhilesh Das, a Congress rebel, is BSP's sixth candidate, other political parties in UP are gearing themselves to avoid any kind of eventuality even though Das may muster the desired numbers from independents.
No party is willing to take chances - be it BJP's Kusum Rai and SP's Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav or SP-Congress candidate Adib Khan - during the RS elections.

The situation may become more challenging if more than 10 candidates file for the RS seats, with Monday being the last day of filing the nominations. In demand then would be Ajit Singh's RLD which has 10 MLAs but no candidate of its own.

Heading: LDA to survey flats and shops rented 48 years ago - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly a month after the police had recovered 12 vehicles (four cars and nine motorcycles) from the two houses of a lecturer at the Sampurnanad Jail Training Institute in Lucknow — she is yet to produce any documents for the vehicles.

While nine vehicles were recovered from Shobha Sharma's husband's house in Alambagh, three were found at her residence at the institute campus.

Sharma (36), a lecturer of the criminology department at the institute, has been allotted flat at the institute campus.

According to the police, on October 15, they received information that a betting racket was being run at the house of Sharma's husband Kaushal Kishore Kaushik in Alambagh's Pawanpuri Colony.

During a raid, the police had recovered several four-wheelers, two-wheelers and playing cards from the house.

Several notebooks, which allegedly contained the names of those involved in the betting racket, were also recovered. The notebooks had details dating back to 1992. Around 151 signed cheques and several stamp papers were also found.

During the raid, Kaushik and one Kamal Srivastava managed to escape. Two others, Lalitesh Mishra and Virendra Pal, were arrested. Both were from Barabanki. Later, the police had raided Sharma's house at the institute campus.

The investigating officer of the case, D R Khanna said: "Shobha Sharma claims the three vehicles found at her residence belongs to her husband. She said that while one vehicle was purchased from Rajasthan, the others were bought at Ghaziabad."

He added, "When asked about registration and other documents, she said the papers were with her husband who was not at home."

The hunt is on to trace both Kaushik and Srivastava, who along with Lalitesh Mishra was a tenant at the Alambagh house.

According to the findings of a preliminary investigation, the vehicles were forcibly taken away from those who had lost during betting, said Khanna.

Acting In-charge of the Alambagh police station, A K Singh, also said that no one had visited the police station with the relevant documents for the seized vehicles.

"All vehicles are stationed at the Alambagh police station campus," he added.

Acting Deputy Director of Sampurnanad Jail Training Institute, Captain S K Pandey, said: "I don't know much about the case.

We have information that the vehicles were recovered from Shobha's house. She has been working here for the last 15 years." He added the vehicles had been parked outside Sharma's residence for a long time. "We have sent a detailed report, including all the documents related to the incident to the prison headquarter," he added.

Inspector General (Prison) Sulkhan Singh said: "We are waiting for the district police to complete the investigation. Then only we will decide our next course of action."

Heading: Allahabad to witness all-India marathon on November 19 - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 2,171 residential flats and 1,659 commercial shops of the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA), given out on rent 48 years ago, are reportedly under possession of unauthorised tenants. But the LDA has failed to get them vacated.

Sources said that people occupying these flats and shops were sublet the places. They are paying hefty rent to the original tenant. On the other hand, the LDA receives a very nominal share as rent ranging between Rs 15 to 25 per month, which was set five decades ago.  

Gearing up to dispose of these properties, the LDA has now decided to start a survey of these properties and sell them to the current willing occupants.

The LDA Vice-Chairman, Mukesh Kumar Meshram, has set up 23 teams of 73 members including 23 control officers to start the survey of these properties from Monday and submit their report positively by Friday.

The officials will meet on Saturday to review the status of the rented properties and chalk out the strategy to sell them.

The Lucknow Municipal Corporation (LMC) had given out over 4,000 residential properties on rent 48 years ago, said a LDA official.

"The management of the flats and shops were transferred to LDA when it came into existence in 1974. But the LDA never got any flat or shop vacated from the occupants," added the official.

According to the official, in 1996, the LDA had asked the tenants to purchase the shops or flats they were occupying for a long period. But the High Court had put a stay on the exercise asking the authorities not to force the tenants to purchase the flats. They, however, had succeeded in selling almost half these properties by then. Complaints have been registered against the original tenants who had rented out the remaining 2,171 flats and 1,700 shops

without obtaining LDA's permission.

"Whenever the LDA conducted a physical verification, occupants of the flats and shops claimed to be family members of the original tenants. So, we could not force them to vacate the property," said the official.

In the latest order, Meshram said that documents related to some of these properties were missing as well and emphasised the necessity of disposing of these properties.

Heading: Ramesh opens two-day leather fair in Agra - Indian Express
Content:
The Sangam City is all set to witness the 24th all-India Indira Marathon on November 19. Around 200 participants are scheduled to participate in the marathon.

They have to cover a 42-km stretch — from Anand Bhavan and end at Chandra Shekhar Azad Park.

District Magistrate Rajeev Agrawal reviewed the preparations for the event on Sunday. The winners from the men and the women's categories will get Rs 1.1 lakh each.

While Rs 50,000 each will be given to the second position holders, the third position holders from the two groups will get Rs 20,000 each.

A consolation prize of Rs 5,000 each will be given to 11 participants from both categories.

As a special feature this year, the administration has decided to earmark a separate route for elder participants. The district magistrate has also ordered that roads be repaired at certain areas for the marathon.

Along with the Indira Marathon, a cross-country race for youths below 20 years will also be organised. In this, the participants will have to cover a distance of 4 km.

The first, second and third position holders will receive cash prize of Rs 1,500, 1,000 and Rs 500. The race will begin from Anand Bhavan and end at Chandra Shekhar Azad Park.

Heading: Now, Lucknow University to hold workshops for boys in hostels as well - Indian Express
Content:
The two-day leather, footwear components and technology fair kicked off on Sunday at the Kalakriti auditorium in Agra.

Inaugurating the second edition of "Meet at Agra", Union Minister of State for Commerce Jairam Ramesh, said: "The Agra leather industry has the potential to improve its performance. The Centre has various schemes to modernise the industry by establishing a leather park and develop the human resources."

He also responded to most of the demands of the Agra Footwear Manufacturers and Exporters Chamber and promised to give all the required funds to help the industry prosper.

As for the demand to declare Agra as a leather and footwear cluster, Ramesh, said: "Agra is a natural cluster of footwear manufacturers and all it needs is to organise its resources well."

"The industry should take inspiration from the southern states, where to help people work in several manufacturing units, industries have promoted Self Help Group and cluster development programme. The same needs to be implemented here," he added.

Expressing serious concern over non-utilisation of funds and schemes, Ramesh, said: "Unfortunately 80 per cent of the funds released by the ministry are not utilised by the state governments. Exporters and manufacturers of the city should mount continuous pressure on the government so that the industry could maximise its benefits."

On the issue of developing an exhibition centre in Agra, the minister was clear that the government was not in a position to "give lands". But he assured that the government would provide with the funds required to build the centre.

Hailing the industry for achieving its growth target of 13.67 per cent at $3.47 billion during 2007-08, Ramesh said a four-year record growth has prompted the industry to set an ambitious target of $4 billion for the current fiscal and hoped that the leather export will touch $6-7 billion till 2010.

In order to boost the export, he also asked the manufacturers to target the volume market along with the value markets like China, Canada and America.

Chariman of Council for Leather Exports M Rafeeque Ahmed said the Agra industry is enjoying a stable position as a foreign exchange earner and a mass employment provider.

Heading: Lucknownama - Indian Express
Content:
Taking a lesson from its girls' hostels, the Lucknow University (LU) has decided to organise creative workshops and lectures in the boys' hostels as well.

While it is considered an important step in the image makeover of the university, according to sources, the step comes after a comment made by the President Pratibha Patil on her recent visit to the campus.

She had highlighted the performance of the girl students and called upon the boys to work harder and not lag behind. The LU administration strongly believes that these workshops will not only encourage the boys towards some constructive work but will also act as a personality grooming exercise.

"As the atmosphere in the boys' hostels has changed and everything is under the control of the university, we have decided to organise creative workshops for the students. The workshops will be held on extra-curricular activities like writing, drama, painting, debates, health awareness camps, quiz competitions and sports sessions," said Prof Nishi Pandey, Dean of Students' Welfare.

Pandey added that intellectuals and university professors will also deliver lectures to motivate the students. "Though the university will provide the necessary infrastructure for conducting the workshops, it is the responsibility of the students to organise them," she added.

A meeting of all the hostel provosts will be convened this week to chalk out a strategy to organise the workshops.

The university has 17 hostels, including 11 for boys and five for girls in both new campus and old campus. It organises debates, painting, plays and dance competitions during "Udaan", a festival held every year in the girls' hostels.

"Such activities have received an overwhelming response from girl students. As the image of the boys' hostel has changed in the last two years, now cultural workshops could be organised in the boys' hostels peacefully," said Dr Rakesh Chandra, Head of Sanskritiki, the cultural committee of LU.

Heading: Prize Pooch - Indian Express
Content:
Mace of Hanuman for battle on terror
Obama might have won the world's top job, but to help him execute it, a city-based institute is invoking the blessings of Lord Hanuman. The students of Sardar Bhagat Singh College of Technology are sending the "gada" of Lord Hanuman to the US President-elect all the way to Chicago. One of the functions of the weapon would ostensibly be to fight terror — their congratulatory letter makes a special mention of the fact that they depend on Obama to win the battle against terror that was begun by Bush. The college authorities have completed all the groundwork to ensure that Obama receives the gift. College Vice-Chairman Pankaj Singh Bhadauriya said: "Obama is currently residing in Chicago. I have got his Chicago address where the gift is being sent through courier service."

Seat sharing? The matter of pact
Trust Mayawati and her style of politics. Now, how does one justify the nomination of Akhilesh Das for the Rajya Sabha polls, who has spent a crore in his Lok Sabha election campaign for the Lucknow seat? Questions are bound to be asked — is there any secret understanding between Mayawati and the BJP over seat, which is currently held by Atal Bihari Vajpayee? If the grapevine is to be believed, then Mayawati has reached a tacit understanding with the BJP and Vajpayee is most likely to contest from this seat once again in the forthcoming elections. For the BJP, it was an uphill task to find an alternative to Vajpayee and losing this seat to a greenhorn like Das would have sent a negative message for the party desperately waiting to grab power at the Centre. As for Mayawati, the onus is on her to prevent the Congress-led UPA, backed by the Samajwadi Party, from coming to power. So it's not a bad bargain for her to back the NDA bandwagon.

Polio resurgence? Centre's fault
Why work when you can blame it on others?
The state government seems to be in no mood to pay heed to the resurgence of polio P1 virus — the most virulent type — in the Badaun district.
Health organisations from across the world have proven that negligence in conducting the polio immunisation drive during the first quarter has led to the present resurgence.
Interestingly, following the pressure from Centre as well as media to take action, the government sent transfer orders to the district Chief Medical Official for negligence in conducting the polio drive.
But rather than ensuring quick identification of the cases and increased routine immunisation activities in the area, the state government is busy blaming the Centre for not taking action or formalising any separate strategy for the state.
Asked about polio eradication in the state, a senior officer of the state Health Department associated with the polio eradication says: "We did our best. Changes in the strategies have to be made by the Centre and they are not reacting fast."

Blood brothers in jail
Now, imagine this: camaraderie between jail authorities and its inmates — that, too through blood donation.
The latest missive to jail authorities by the prison department asking them to donate blood has left the officials amused. For each unit of blood they would donate, some inmate facing medical emergency would be treated.
Those who have to donate blood see no rationale behind this decision. But on the other hand, the bosses hope that the noble deed will help promote brotherhood among the inmates and the jail officials.

Heading: Take one - Indian Express
Content:
It was a show of beauty and brains as whining pets of city's caninophiles strutted their stuff over the weekend at the Police Lines. Awadh Kennel Club organised the Obedience Dog Show to bring to the fore the amazing virtues of man's best friend.

Breeds of the participants comprised Labrador, Pug, German Shepard, Doberman, Golden Retriever and Great Dan, giving a hard to task of decision to Justice CR Patnaik.

Chief guest Jaya Srivastava, wife of SSP Akhil Kumar, took time off her birthday celebrations to give away prizes to those adjudged the best of the 26 entries.

Lyka was declared the Challenger Winner, while Begum of Sunny Land was the C4 winner.

Companion winner title too went to Lyka, informedE Chandel, show convenor.

Heading: The Comeback Girl - Indian Express
Content:
Private sector utility Calcutta Electric Supply Corporation Limited (CESC) has entered into an agreement with SP Global Solutions — a subsidiary of Singapore Power — for strengthening the distribution system in the CESC-licensed areas of the city.

"It is essentially a technology transfer, aimed at improving the standard of the distribution system of the CESC," said CESC's vice-chairman Sanjiv Goenka.

Under the agreement, the CESC will shell out Rs 6 crore as the consultancy fees to SP Global Solutions.

When it comes to distribution systems, Singapore is one of top countries in the System Average Interruption Duration Index — which is an index for average power disruption per costumer per year.

"As per Indian standards, we have been giving better services to our costumers, but the agreement is an attempt to raise the standards for ourselves," said Goenka.

The CESC will spend nearly 20 crore in the next three to five years for strengthening the distribution network. The funds will go into network augmentation and setting up of more control systems. According to the CESC officials, with a robust distribution system in place, the reduction in powercuts can generate more revenue for the company in the long run.

"As per the pollution control norms, power plants will have to be set up outside Kolkata metropolitan area. In the next five years, we will have to distribute an additional 600-800 MW from our power plant in Haldia," Goenka said.

Heading: Fever’s latest victim: Trinamool leader - Indian Express
Content:
Then, the adulation flustered Chitrangada Singh; now, she is eager for more

They loved her for her looks; they loved her for her histrionics. Five years ago, most of those who walked out of the cinemas, having watched the end credits roll on Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi, got starry-eyed about Chitrangada Singh. Since talented dusky heroines have to be called the new Smita Patil, that moniker also stuck. It was anybody's dream debut, except that she wasn't ready for it. "The adulation was too unsettling for me and I did not know how to react. I had to think about what I really wanted to do," says Singh, at her home in Gurgaon, having returned from a sky-diving camp in Hissar.

So she disappeared from the scene, except for an appearance in the 2005 dud Kal: Yesterday and Tomorrow, while rumours went about in B-town that her husband, the golfer Jyoti Randhawa, had stopped her from acting. Now, after a child, a few charcoal painting sessions and yoga, she is back — in Onir's Sorry Bhai, that also stars Shabana Azmi and Boman Irani. Singh calls this "a new beginning" rather than a "comeback", and you can already sense the anxiety in her voice. "I am slightly nervous. It has been some time since I acted," she says.

The break evidently did her good; for one, she realised that two films are not even a blip in Bollywood. "When I joined, I had no godfather. Now I have learnt to cope with the attention and I don't discount the fame that my first movie has brought; it has got me where I am today. But there is no pressure to perform," she says. And Onir called her just when she was eager to return before the camera. "I had changed my phone number and was out of touch with everyone in the industry. I was also hesitant to call up directors and ask for work. Somehow, someone gave my number to Onir, he asked me and I immediately agreed to do the film," she says, laughing at the serendipity of it all.

The film sees Singh playing a girl caught between the affection of two brothers played by Sanjay Suri and Sharman Joshi. "There is a twist to the love angle. It is dealt with innocently and happily, not like a clichéd love triangle," she says. Sorry Bhai also sees Singh cast alongside her childhood idol, Shabana Azmi. "I just admire her career graph. She handles and guides the scene effortlessly, which is an art in itself. On the sets, I was a sucker for her and sat for hours watching her. She even advised me against studying acting," says Singh, as she rates Arth and Masoom among Azmi's greatest films.

The comeback girl, who calls herself "a director's actor who can't act if she doesn't understand the role", is not choosy. "Any challenging role appeals to me. Commercial, art house, period — I am open to anything," she says. After her dream debut with Sudhir Mishra, she will be back on his sets in December for Aur Devdas where she plays Chandramukhi. "He appreciates my acting and I like his kind of cinema," she says. The Mishra-Singh tango doesn't end there. She also stars in his Nawab and John Company that releases in July next year.

Heading: Med officer’s wings clipped for fudging data - Indian Express
Content:
The Trinamool Congress wants a probe into the death of a Trinamool Youth Congress leader early Sunday morning.

He was suffering from fever. There are allegations that the malarial clinic in Kasba where the patient was undergoing treatment lost his blood samples that delayed treatment for a day.

Ratan Sarkar, 52, the block president of Trinamool Youth Congress in Kasba, complained of high fever on Friday. He went to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation's malaria detection clinic at Talbagan in Kasba where doctors took his blood samples and asked him to come back after two hours to collect the report. He was also given the customary preventive dose for malaria.

According to reports, on his return Sarkar was told that the sample was lost and it had to be collected again. This delayed the report as the doctors had finished their work and left for the day.

Sarkar was told that he would get the report the next day. His condition deteriorated by Saturday and he was taken to the Sambhunath Pandit hospital, from where he was later referred to the SSKM Hospital.

His condition deteriorated further on Saturday night and he died at 1.30 am. The Trinamool Congress has alleged that had the malarial clinic diagnosed the disease in time, Sarkar could have been saved.

"We will raise the issue in the corporation. We want a probe in the matter. The erring health employees should be identified and punished," said Javed Khan, leader of the opposition at the KMC.

Heading: Traffic snarl at Maniktala after residents, auto drivers clash - Indian Express
Content:
The government has taken over the job of making public the data on Bengal's vector-borne diseases. But inside the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, which is to provide the raw figures to the government, some reshuffling has been done as well.

Chief Municipal Health Officer (CMHO) Deb Dwaipayan Chattopadhyay had his wings clipped for fudging figures and was told that no data will now be given to him. Everything will be routed through the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) department of KMC, headed by Basudeb Chattopadhyay.

After being accused by the government of deliberately suppressing data, Chattopadhaya was forced to issue an inter-departmental circular, asking all reports from 83 malaria clinics of the civic body and several private clinics to be sent to the IDSP department, where the figures of the KMC malaria clinics will be compiled with the data received from several state-run hospitals and private nursing homes.

The compiled data will be sent to the state health department for scrutiny by the state health officials.

Earlier, the KMC was asked to reveal the actual data by Sanchita Bakshi, director, state health services, who said that no figure on the vector-borne diseases coming from the KMC was authentic.

Chattopadhaya has been forced to reveal the actual data after several KMC health officials complained to Municipal Commissioner Alapan Bandyopadhaya. They had reportedly said that Chattopadhaya deliberately suppressed to cover up the failure of the KMC health department in preventing and combating the outbreak.

Significantly, the report till 29th September, sent to the state health department, reveals that 25,109 people have been afflicted with vector-borne diseases with 1,476 positive cases of falciparum malaria. But after the actual data is released, figures of afflicted cases went up to 41,223, with 4,781 cases of falciparum.

The contradiction clearly points out how the facts have been fudged.

Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya, however, is not yet ready to accept that any fact has been suppressed by the KMC health department.

"Facts related to vector-borne diseases have not been suppressed deliberately. Earlier, we did not receive some data from the private clinics and private nursing homes. As of now, we have received reports from some private clinics and nursing homes. So, the data took a jump," he said.

"Compared to the previous years, the situation in the state is not that grave. But the danger is there and there is no need to be complacent. We are carrying regular audits as cases are being reported to us," said state health minister Surjya Kanta Mishra. "There was a lot of backlog, which has been cleared and KMC's data report has got the updated figure," he added.

Heading: Two robbed, beaten up in broad daylight - Indian Express
Content:
Tension prevailed on the Maniktala main road in north Kolkata on Sunday, following a clash between auto-rickshaw drivers and a group of local residents, demanding better management of the traffic movement on the road. The police had to use force to control the situation.

According to the police, Kaushik Patra, a Class X student, was admitted to the Calcutta Medical College and Hospital in a critical condition after he was hit by an unknown vehicle on the Maniktala main road in Bagmari on Saturday.

Following the accident, a group of locals, led by local Congress Councillor Sunanda Guha, set up a road blockade on the Maniktala main road around 10:30 am on Sunday. "This is an accident-prone zone. But the police have not taken any steps to control the traffic movement here," said Guha. The situation, however, took an ugly turn when the protesters damaged a few auto-rickshaws plying on the road and attacked their drivers. Subsequently, the auto-rickshaw drivers set up another road blockade a few hundred metres away to protest against the attack. This was followed by a clash between the auto drivers and the residents, in which a few protesters from both the sides were injured. The police force was sent to the spot, as the road blockades and subsequent violence led to a traffic jam on the busy Maniktala main road. Even after repeated requests, when the protesters refused to lift the road blockades, the police had to use force to disperse them.

Later, the protesters alleged the police resorted to lathicharge in which many people were injured. Assistant Commissioner of Police A Sailesh, however, said the allegations were baseless.

Heading: Maternity benefit scheme for positives - Indian Express
Content:
In broad daylight, a group of miscreants stopped a mini-bus and robbed two passengers on Sunday. The incident occurred in the Watgunj area, with fellow passengers acting as mute spectator. Two of the accused persons have been arrested.

The police said two youths Rabi Mondol (26) and Shib Prasad Dahanuk were travelling in the bus on the Metiabruz-Howrah route.

Around 9 am, when the bus reached the CGR Road and Brooke Lane crossing, a group of youth stopped the bus. They got into the bus and began beating up Dahanuk and Mondol. The duo were then dragged out of the bus and taken to a desolate place, where they were severely beaten up.

The co-passengers did not dare to intervene in the matter. "The youth were carrying firearms and were openly brandishing them," said a police officer of West Port police station.

The miscreants also took away the money that the duo were carrying. They left the spot soon after the incident. The victims, however, managed to reach the local police station and lodged a complaint.

The goons have been identified as Akhtar Hossain (33), Sohel Khan (32), Robin Das (27), Golam Khan (24), Md. Munna (35) and Anand Gupta, said a police officer.

A small part of the money and a mobile phone was recovered from the two miscreants, who were arrested. —ENS

Heading: Seth Left Front’s choice for Nandigram - Indian Express
Content:
To encourage institutional delivery among HIV positive women, the West Bengal State AIDS Prevention and Control Society (WBSAPCS) will launch a maternity benefit scheme from December 1 to prevent the transmission of the virus from the parent to the child .

"We will introduce a new scheme — Jagrity, under which we will conduct the delivery of HIV positive mothers in such a way that the children do not get affected by the virus," said state Health Minister Surjya Kanta Mishra.

The state Health Department under WBSAPCS already runs a Prevention of Parent to Child Transmission (PPTCT) programme at government institutions and sub-divisional hospitals, under which financial help of Rs 500 is provided to HIV positive mothers. This programme, however, covers only antenatal checkups and screening for HIV antibody reactivity of HIV positive mothers.

Under the Jagrity scheme, the Health Department will place HIV positive mothers under antiretroviral (ARV) chemoprophylaxis to prevent the transmission of the virus to their newborns.

The WBSAPCS will provide a one-time payment of Rs 1,000 to HIV positive pregnant women for delivering in any state-run hospital. The scheme will extend to all HIV positive mothers irrespective of their economic status.

Under the scheme, PPTCT counsellors will issue a Jagrity card to an HIV positive pregnant woman that will contain details like checkup dates, due date of the delivery along with the name of hospital where the delivery will take place.

The scheme will facilitate HIV positive women to avail free medical tests like CT Scan, MRI and Ultrasonography in government-run hospitals.

The HIV positive mothers admitted to government hospitals will also be provided with free medicines.

"From December 1, the Central government under National AIDS Control Organisation will implement a new scheme to provide a second line of drug treatment to HIV positive women," said Mishra.

"We will also open an antiretroviral treatment facility at the RG Kar Hospital and the Malda Medical College soon," the minister added.

To strengthen the Buladi AIDS awareness campaign, the government will now cover all the blocks of 10 districts of West Bengal.

"Five buses will be provided to Health Department teams and other government officials to conduct the campaign in 10 districts of the state," said the health minister.

While the state Health Department pegs the number of HIV positive mothers in West Bengal to be 496, the ARV-registered figure of HIV-positive mothers is 9,627 in the state.

Heading: Tamang gets ultimatum to prove allegations - Indian Express
Content:
Even after the Nandigram faux pas and the party's drubbing in the recent panchayat polls in the district, the CPM does not seem to have lost faith in Lakshman Seth, the parliamentarian from Tamluk.

On Sunday, on the sidelines of a rally in Nandigram, transport minister Subhas Chakraborty announced that Seth would again be the party's choice for the Tamluk Lok Sabha seat. "We will have to win back the section of people we have lost," he added.

Chakraborty's visit amid extraordinary security arrangement was the party's attempt to provide a much-needed boost to cadres on the eve of the Nandigram by-elections in December.

The move is also meant to initiate the party's campaign for the Lok Sabha polls scheduled for the next year.

On Monday, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee is to address a rally there.

Seth came in for much criticism after he, without consulting the party top brass, had issued a notice for land acquisition for a chemical hub in Nandigram, which had triggered widespread violence, culminating in the police firing on March 14 that claimed 14 lives. He is also under the CBI scanner for the same.

On Sunday, at the Democratic Youth Federation of India rally, Chakraborty informed his party cadres that a majority of the state's people are with them. These people, he said, know how the residents of Nandigram are being victimised by reactionary forces for their vested interests.

"Don't worry about these reactionary forces. They are instigating the people across the state against the Left Front in hope of snatching power from us," he said. "In Nandigram, Mamata Banerjee has no land, even Sisir Adhikary has no land here. But, they are pushing farmers in Nandigram to fight each other."

Highlighting the sacrifices of his party cadres in past days, Chakraborty said, "I assure you that I will bring intellectuals and social workers in Nandigram before the election. I am trying to offer my best effort so that Argentine football star Diego Maradona can hover in the sky over Nandigram on 6 December by helicopter."

Heading: After talks fail in Lalgarh, govt appeals to priests - Indian Express
Content:
After barricading All India Gorkha League president Madan Tamang in his Darjeeling home on Saturday, the Gorkha Janmukti Vidyarthi Morcha (GJVM) said on Sunday that he has time till November 12 to prove his allegations against Bimal Gurung.

The Gorkha Janamukti Morcha (GJM) and its student wing had initially set November 7 as the deadline for Tamang to prove his allegations or quit politics. "We will have another public meeting on November 12, where decision on our future course of action against Tamang will be taken," said GJVM leader Kismat Chettri. "For now, we have filed a general diary with the police against his supporters who threatened us with pistols during our gherao."

Tamang is being targeted for his comments alleging that GJM chief Bimal Gurung had held a "secret" meeting with state home secretary Ashok Mohan Chakrabarti, where the decision to suspend the non-cooperation movement was taken.

On Saturday, thousands of GJVM supporters had gathered outside Tamang's home and organised a public meeting. To avoid any untoward incident, the administration had deployed over 100 police personnel.

Tamang said the gherao amounted to a total "breakdown of law and order in Darjeeling" and demanded that Article 355 be imposed. "The Chief Minister has the Constitutional responsibility to ensure law and order," he told The Indian Express. "I'm used to this kind of action against me for over 20 years. Earlier it was by the GNLF, now it's the GJM. But they have their limitations. My boys are ready for them." He added that the police had requested him to control his supporters, and had assured him that his house will be protected.

"Even now, there are some policemen posted outside my home, but how long can this go on?" he asked. "This is sheer goonda behaviour — burning houses of political leaders, using strong-arm tactics to prevent public meetings of other political parties. Who are these people to issue deadlines to anyone?"

The Superintendent of Police, Darjeeling, Rahul Srivastav, said the police team will stay in place. "We're not expecting any violence, but still we are alert. There was no problem today nor any protests against Tamang," he said.

Heading: Banned giant wheels at work during Jagadhatri Puja, police clueless - Indian Express
Content:
The West Midnapore district administration is seeking the help of 'jan gurus' or tribal priests to reach out to the tribal community seething with the anger in Lalgarh after the arrest of three teenage tribal students. The students — Gautam Patra, Buddhadeb Patra and Eban Murumu —are all aged between 16 and 17. The class X students from the area were arrested in connection with last Sunday's Salboni blast targeting chief minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee.

An all-party meeting aimed at restoring peace failed after an Opposition walkout on Sunday. The meeting at Lalgarh police station on Sunday was called by district magistrate Nayan Swarup Nigam. Offended Opposition members stormed out of the meeting after some CPM leaders allegedly remarked that the Opposition morphed into Maoist cadres by night. Representatives of the Trinamool Congress, the Congress, Jharkhand Party (Naren) and Jharkhand Party (Aditya) were present at the meeting.

After the talks failed, the district administration drafted in priests to soothe frayed tempers of 30 tribal villages. "The tribals generally hold their jan gurus in high esteem. We have asked them to convince people that the police are not the enemy," said a district police officer.

Following the blast on November 2, several persons were picked up from Lalgarh. The police allegedly harassed villagers and beat up women while combing the area. A few days ago, tribals laid siege on Lalgarh police station for the entire day.

The district administration has decided to reconsider the case of students. "The police have not filed any chargesheet against them. Their role will be examined and necessary changes will be made if they are found to be innocent," said the district magistrate.

The CID, entrusted with the investigation of the case, have been cautioned against making arbitrary arrests, said a police source.

Heading: Post Salboni, special security cover in place for film festival - Indian Express
Content:
Despite imposing a ban on electric giant wheels during Durga Puja this year. But a month on, during Jagadhatri Puja, the Kolkata police seem clueless about the ban "Giant wheels are run by fair organisers after obtaining permission from the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC). We had banned them during Durga Puja to prevent accidents, but we don't know whether or not the civic body has given permission to the organisers to run them during Jagadhatri Puja," said Vineet Goyal, Deputy Commissioner (Headquarters).

The accidental death of a man who fell from an electric giant wheel during pujas had prompted the Kolkata police to ban them from all fairs this year. The police had also asked the KMC to keep a close watch on any giant wheels running in its area.

According to the Fire Service Department officials, there are around 572 Jagadhatri Puja pandals in West Bengal, of which 157 are in Kolkata. "Our numbers reflect only those pujas which are being conducted by our permission. But many organisers conduct it without informing us," a fire department official said.

The MMi-C of the Parks and Square Department, Faiyaz Ahmad Khan, said: "What happened during Durga Puja was an accident. Accidents happen on roads too but that does not mean we ban vehicles. We give permission only after ensuring that fair organisers have taken care of the basic safety measures."

Khan, however, admitted that in the absence of adequate staff, the KMC was unable to send its staff to each and every fair ground to conduct inspections. "As long as fair organisers are ready to ensure that they have followed all the safety measures, we give them the permission to set up giant wheels," said Khan.

Heading: Kolkata confidential - Indian Express
Content:
Elaborate security arrangements have been made for the 14th Kolkata Film Festival.

Keeping in mind the recent blast in Salboni, special security arrangements are already in force for Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, who frequents the festival every year.

"Both plain-clothed and uniformed policemen will be deployed at the venue," said Vineet Goyel, Deputy Commissioner (Headquarters).

Last year, there were several snap demonstrations following the Nandigram incident that put the Kolkata police in a tight spot. This time, too, the police as well as the special branch officers are keeping a strict watch on such demonstrators.

The week-long festival will begin from November 10. This year, the festival will pay centenary tribute to renowned French director Jacques Tati and screen four of his masterpieces — The Big Day, Mosiure Hulots Holiday, My Uncle and Play Time.

A special segment of Satyajit Ray's favourite Hollywood films as well as his restored ones will also be screened.

About 250 films, including short films and documentaries, will be screened at various theatres across the city.

Heading: Ties that Bind - Indian Express
Content:
Reading tea leaves
As the Principal Secretary, Home, Asoke Mohan Chakrabarti, is all set to become the chief secretary of the state following the retirement of present incumbent Amit Kiran Deb in December, the question doing the rounds at the corridors of Writers is: who is going to be next Home Secretary? Two names have surfaced: Ardhendu Sen, the Resident Commissioner of West Bengal in Delhi and Sabyasachi Sen, the principal Secretary, Commerce and Industries. Grapevine has it that the chances of Ardhendu Sen, who was not very keen to come back to West Bengal because his family stays in Delhi, are brighter as far as the prized post is concerned.

Nuts and bolts
After the transfer of P K Agarwal from the post of Land Reforms Commissioner (LRC) the importance of Sanat Mukherjee, Joint Secretary, Land Reforms Department, has risen manifold. This is owing to the fact that subsequent LRCs — SC Tewary and the present incumbent Balbir Ram — are not regarded as fully conversant with the nitty-gritty of the department. And whenever the Commerce and Industries Department is in a soup, Mukherjee is called in. Last Friday, a meeting was called at the residence of Advocate General Balai Roy to find out a way to get out of the ongoing cases at the Supreme Court. While the Commerce and Industries Department was represented by principal secretary Sabyasachi Sen and WBIDC managing director Subrata Gupta, the land reforms department was represented by Mukherjee. No wonder the state government had to give an extension to Mukherjee, who was to retire earlier this year.

'Cushion' talk
Following the Salboni blast, security around Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee has been tightened to a great extent. And the new commandos do not think twice before destroying things that appear remotely dangerous. On Saturday, around 5 pm, Bhattacharjee was to attend a function at a five-star hotel on the E M Bypass. Securitymen had gathered at the hotel since morning. During a check of the dais, the metal detector beeped near a cushion. The hotel employees, who were asked to remove it, insisted that nothing was amiss. But during the second round of checks, the metal detector beeped again. This time however, the securitymen simply tore open the cushion. Finding nothing incriminating inside, they just asked the hotel employees to clean up the area.

Who cares?
After the attack on Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's convoy in Salboni, the Left Front ministers appear shaken and stirred. Many of them were heard cribbing in personal circles about the lack of security in their convoys. One was heard saying, "He is the chief minister and has so many policemen with sophisticated equipment guarding him round-the-clock. I just have a police escort. What will I do if they target me? I visited that area so many times." Some of the ministers also raised the point that only chief minister's security is ever discussed at the Left Front meeting. "What about us?" one demanded, "it seems that our lives do not matter."

Heading: Shaken and Stirred - Indian Express
Content:
Film: Edge of Heaven

Director: Fatih Akin

Cast: Baki Davrak, Nursel Kose, Hanna Schygulla, Tuncel Kurtiz, Nurgul Yesilcay

Rating: *****

Running at: Fame (South City)

Ours is a cynical age. Simple human emotions and bonds take a backseat as greater goals are pursued. Mothers abandon daughters to pursue a better future. Random cruelties of life numb us to atrocities and idealism is all but scoffed at. Yet, as German director Fatih Akin's protagonist in his brilliantly structured Edge of Heaven proves, redemption is only a gesture away. Indeed, Akin forges a statement for the world from the intimacies of his characters, and in doing so gives their experience a universal stature.

The film travels between Turkey and Germany to narrate the story of six people who are in a way, victims of the troubled relationship between these countries. Ali (Tuncil Kurtiz) a retired Turkish immigrant in Germany, brings home a prostitute, Yeter (Nursel Korse) as a companion. Their shared history (she also happens to be Turkish immigrant) proves to be another incentive. Ali's son Nejat (Baki Davrat) initially doesn't seem to be very happy with the arrangement, but warms up to Yeter as he gets to know her better. The relationship between the father and the son get strained as Ali suspects that his son is having an affair with his mistress. In an encounter, he accidentally kills Yeter. In an effort to undo his father's crime, Nejat travels to Turkey to seek out Yeter's daughter and sponsor her studies. Unbeknownst to him, Yeter's daughter Ayten (Nurgul Yesilcay) is actually in Germany to flee persecution in her own country for being a political activist. As a penniless, illegal immigrant in Germany she is hiding from the police and seeking refuge in abandoned ATM counters, until Lotte ( Patriciya Ziolkowska) befriends her and takes gives her shelter, to the disapproval of her mother (Hanna Schygulla).

These two tracks converge in the historic city of Istanbul, which for centuries has been the meeting point of the East and the West. Akin paints a thriving, vibrant city of contradictions where one can peacefully sip chai (tea) at one corner and be gunned down by street urchins at another. This is why Edge of Heaven can also be seen as an examination of modern Turkey, where Akin illuminates the confrontation between the secular and the extremist Islamic worlds with Pamuk-like precision.

Also illuminating is Akin's generosity of giving his characters the emotional room and the screen-time to grow on you. Never does he let any of them end up as prototypes as they so frequently do in such political films. Take the character of Nejat for instance, as a somewhat uncharismatic professor of Turkish in a German university, he could have been a symbol of declination. Instead Akin empowers him with a redemptive mission. Similarly compassionate is the portrayal of Lotte's mother, a disapproving figure who can't deal with her daughter's obsession with the troublesome Ayten. As she is confronted with a tragedy, she embraces her fate with resilience and character.

But the best thing about Edge of Heaven is the way in which it reveals itself to be a very private testimony. Evidently, Arkin talks about his country/countries from personal experiences and not bookish cockiness.

Heading: Take One - Indian Express
Content:
Victim's kin says justice delivered after years of struggle, accused should not be pardoned

After spending 18 years in jail, a 70-year-old man on death row is awaiting decision on his mercy plea pending in the President's office for the last over five years.

Piara Singh, alias Nihang, his two young sons and a relative are waiting for the final word from the head of the state. Piara is the main accused in a mass murder case that took place at Basarke Bhaini village in which the entire family of farmer Jagir Singh was eliminated in 1991. Seventeen persons were killed when he, along with others, opened fire when the victim family was preparing for a marriage party.

He was sentenced to be hanged till death in 1996 by a local court and the verdict was upheld by the High Court in the same year and finally by the Supreme Court in 2003. "It was then that we filed the mercy plea. Apart from Piara, his two young sons, Satnam Singh and Gurdev Singh, and relative Sarbjit Singh have also been sentenced to death," says Baljinder Singh, brother of Piara Singh.

He said they had sent various reminders to former President Dr APJ Abdul Kalam and incumbent Pratibha Patil. During the years when Piara and his sons were in jail, the family was uprooted from the village.

Piara allegedly had links with the militants and was locked in a land dispute with Jagir Singh's family. "My family members have done no wrong. My husband had surrendered before the police, as his name was being dragged in the case. They were wrongly convicted. They have already spent 18 years in jail; they should be released and their sentence be changed to life imprisonment," said Piar Kaur, wife of Piara.

Central Jail Superintendent SP Singh said these four convicts have been waiting for the final decision from the President. He said there were some more cases in which the verdict from the President's office was awaited. "Various factors

have to be considered before taking a decision in such cases," he said.

Angrej Singh, 37, who was a teenager when most of his family members were killed 18 years ago, said Piara and his kin deserve no mercy.

"We fought for many years and finally the verdict was delivered in our favour. There were enough evidence and eyewitnesses to fix Piara Singh and others who ruined our lives. If mercy is provided, we will challenge the decision and again fight for justice. There should be no delay in hanging them," he said.

"I had saved my life by hiding behind piles of wood. I lost my father, two brothers, two uncles, two cousins and even neighbours. One of my aunts was eight-month pregnant and cousins were in their teens," he said.

"How can anyone pardon them?" he asked.

Heading: Comedy Centre - Indian Express
Content:
Model-turned-actor Mugdha Godse on life after Fashion

When director Madhur Bhandarkar came to Mugdha Godse with the script of Fashion, the model was unsure about how her character would make an impact, considering the stronger roles for co-actors Priyanka Chopra and Kangana Ranaut. "But that was before I read the script. Once I was through, I knew Janet's character had as much scope to perform. If I did it with honesty, it could get me a little appreciation," says Godse. In the movie, she plays the second-rung model, Janet, married to a gay designer.

It has been a week since the movie released, but the "little appreciation" that Godse had hoped for, has snowballed into generous accolades. "There's been a steady stream of congratulatory messages and phonecalls. Priyanka texted 'Babe, you blew my mind!' at three in the morning, and I was totally floored. The one person who is vindicated is Madhur sir. Everytime he told me I had it in me to make it as an actor, I would tell him not to speculate. Now, with each review that I have received, he has been telling me 'I told you so'," she giggles.

For Godse, the most touching praise has come from her family. "My family is quite critical of me, so I was apprehensive of their reaction. They went for first-day-first-show, when I was still promoting the film in Dubai. My sister later told me they were left speechless by my performance," she says.

There have been quite a few offers since the movie released, but the model-turned-actor says she will only announce them once she signs on the dotted line. "As of now, I have signed with Percept Picture Company for three of their films," she says. Modelling, she says, will definitely be on the backburner for the time being. "Fashion's given me opportunities which I would be stupid to ignore. It's not as if I am giving up modelling completely, but I'll do only select shows," she says.

Heading: Bagan walk a tightrope to beat Churchill - Indian Express
Content:
In an interview with Dipti Nagpaul-D'Souza,Sanjeev Bhaskar talks about his new show Mumbai Calling that blends call centre, race relations and serious comedy. Excerpts:

How did Mumbai Calling happen?
Producer Allan McKeown was interested in setting a comedy in a call centre in India. I had started writing a movie about a call centre some years ago, which I abandoned to pursue other projects. I dusted those ideas and developed a situation comedy. Actor Nitin Ganatra and writer Simon Blackwell are friends. I brought them on board and they added to the series.

What's your character Kenny Gupta like?
Kenny Gupta is a British-born Indian who comes to Mumbai to manage a call centre.

Although he looks like everybody else, he's a fish out of water and is constantly looking forward to the day he can return to his cold, rainy, depressing bit of London.

Is this yet another attempt at speaking about race relations?
From Goodness Gracious Me through The Kumars at No. 42 to a documentary series on India, my work has always been about playing with people's perceptions and stereotypes. I hope to do the same with Mumbai Calling.

How is the race scene in the UK now?
Better than it was when my parents came here. After President Obama, who knows, we might have an Indian prime minister of the UK.

Do you fear that given the current economic scenario and the western take on outsourcing, the show might face criticism in the UK?
Mumbai Calling is entertainment and thus employs dramatic licence. It isn't a documentary, so any criticism other than from an entertainment point of view is pointless.

Your wife Meera Syal has not been a part of Mumbai Calling. What is she up to?
Meera has been writing movie scripts and acting in a comedy on British TV, called Beautiful People, so she is busy.

What makes a good joke — a situation or a punch line?
Both make a good joke. A combination of the two makes a great one.

Who are your favourite comedians?
The Marx brothers, Woody Allen, Monty Python, Peter Sellers, Robin Williams... the list goes on. At the moment my three-year-old son Shaan makes me laugh more than anyone else.

The show is on at HBO from November 8

Heading: Debut bash for Bengal in Ranji opener - Indian Express
Content:
I-LEAGUE: Churchill Brothers miffed with 'poor' refereeing

For full 90 minutes they virtually walked the line. Lady luck, however, smiled on Mohun Bagan as they managed to cling on to their one-goal lead and defeated Churchill Brothers in the I-League seventh round encounter at Yuba Bharati Krirangan (YBK) tonight. PC Lalawmpuia capitalised on a Gourmangi Singh error to score the all-important goal in the 14th minute. Marcos Pereira sent a long ball from the right, Gourmangi misjudged the flight and presented the opportunity to Lalawmpuia. The latter created the angle with an excellent first touch and placed the ball past an advancing Churchill custodian Arindam Bhattacharya. Lalawmpuia figured in the starting line-up for the first time in this tournament as Jose Barreto was out suspended. He made the most out of this opportunity.

In fact, the Bagan strikers, Baichung Bhutia and Lalawmpuia had very little scope of making their presence felt as they lacked support upfront. After taking the lead, coach Karim Bencherifa strangely opted to defend deep which created a huge gap between the attacking-third and the middle-third.

Churchill accepted the favour gleefully and took their opponent by the scruff of the neck. That they couldn't score was because of two factors. The finishing was poor and the Bagan defenders didn't allow Odafe Okolie any space to manoeuvre with the ball.

The visitors came very close to scoring on a number of occasions. In the 19th minute, a misunderstanding between Bagan defender Peter Odafe and goalkeeper Sangram Mukherjee saw Reishngmi Vasmum get a golden opportunity to equalise. But he delayed his shot and allowed NS Manju to save the situation. In the 47th minute, another Odafe error gave Felix Chimhokwu a clear sight of the goal. He too couldn't convert. In the 68th minute, Okolie set it up nicely for substitute Nicholas Rodrigues. The latter took an overhead kick from eight yards that sailed over the crossbar.

To their credit, Bagan defended manfully. Especially, Dipak Mondal was outstanding, though the Man of the Match award went to his Brazilian team-mate Marcos Pereira. The hosts also had a few chances against the run of play in the second half. Lalawmpuia had a one-on-one with Bhattacharya in the 69th but hit straight at the goalkeeper. In the 80th minute, James Singh wasted another one from close range. By that time Bhutia had decided to drop back in the midfield to take a creative role. It somewhat helped ease off the pressure. Against his old team, it was a prestige fight for the Bagan coach. Bencherifa can heave a sigh of relief as his team won and moved to nine points, while Churchill stay on 12.
