The book looks at what lies beneath the surface of slavery with an the ambivalent, disturbing story of a mother who casts off her daughter in order to save her. The opening line of A Mercy is: "Don't be afraid.''

MUSIC

A good year for black musicians, with R&B ruling the charts. Beyonce Knowles releases her third album, titled, I am...Sasha Fierce, later this month. She also stars as famed blues singer Etta James in upcoming film Cadillac Records. In February, Leona Lewis broke American charts with Bleeding Love which peaked at number one for four non-consecutive weeks. Bleeding Love also became the first track by a UK female to hit number one since Kim Wilde in 1987. Not to forget Ashanti, who has sold 7 million albums in the US alone. The track The Way That I Love You has sold over 8 million ring tones in the US. And then there was Will.I.am who wrote the song Yes We Can inspired by Obama's speech that had more than a million hits in its first five days on YouTube. R&B singer Rihanna's single Take A Bow, from the re-release of her album Good Girl Gone Bad, reached No 1 on iTunes.

— Aabha Rathee, Paromita Chakrabarti, Anushree Majumdar

Heading: To break deadlock, Southern African leaders start summit on Zimbabwe - Indian Express
Content:
Faced with one of the most important transfers of presidential power in American history — amid wars on two fronts, the looming threat of terrorism at home, and a full-blown economic crisis — the outgoing Bush administration and the incoming Obama team have responded with nearly unprecedented cooperation on those issues, aides and outside experts say.

Serious decisions, and potentially divisive ones, still remain for the politically and ideologically divided camps, such as access to classified information and, in particular, battles over the regulations and executive orders that will define the policy of the two administrations.

But the days since Tuesday's election have shown a striking level of comity following the rancor of the campaign, enhanced by President Bush's months-long efforts to pave the way for a smooth transition and Barack Obama's pre-election determination to move quickly.

"Ensuring that this transition is seamless is a top priority for the rest of my time in office," Bush said in his weekly radio address on Saturday. "My administration will work hard to ensure that the next president and his team can hit the ground running."

Bush has created a transition coordinating council, populated by experts from inside and outside the administration, and has streamlined the process for obtaining security clearances for key transition officials. National Intelligence Director Mike McConnell flew to Chicago on Thursday to deliver Obama's first daily intelligence briefing.

The Obama team has begun submitting names to the FBI for expedited security clearances, which is allowed under an intelligence reform law passed in 2004. Officials said that more than 100 positions, down to the level of undersecretary, are eligible under the statute.

Bush's chief of staff, Joshua B Bolten, said the White House is even preparing a "tabletop" exercise to simulate how Obama's national security officials should respond in the event of a terrorist attack.

"If a crisis hits on January 21, they're the ones that are going to have to deal with it," Bolten said in an interview taped for broadcast Sunday on C-SPAN. "We need to make sure they're as well-prepared as possible."

Likewise, the administration is laying the groundwork for an unusual level of access to the Treasury Department and other agencies involved in attempts to stabilize the foundering economy. White House spokesman Tony Fratto said Friday that Treasury is preparing office space that will allow Obama aides to sit alongside current administration officials.

Fratto said such efforts are intended to send a signal that Treasury's approach will not change too abruptly when Obama takes office. "They don't want to surprise markets; they want to try to make sure that they have predictable information for markets," he said.

Bush and Obama are scheduled to meet at the White House on Monday, after a long and tough campaign in which Obama's chief charge was that a vote for Republican rival John McCain would be a vote for a third Bush term.

Heading: Haiti school collapse toll 88 - Indian Express
Content:
Southern African leaders opened a regional summit on Zimbabwe in South Africa on Sunday, hoping to break a deadlock over the allocation of cabinet posts which has prevented formation of a power-sharing government.

The 15-nation Southern African Development Community (SADC) meeting is trying to end the impasse between President Robert Mugabe and opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai and put into effect a power-sharing deal reached in September.

South African President Kgalema Motlanthe said in opening remarks that the agreement signed by Zimbabwe's political rivals was the only hope for the country to revive its collapsed economy.

The historical agreement signed on the 15th of September is the only vehicle to help Zimbabweans (with) their economic challenges, Motlanthe told the summit.

Mugabe and Tsvangirai were both attending the summit.

Motlanthe said there was some disappointment that the Zimbabwean parties had not agreed how to allocate cabinet posts. "We hope the parties will show political maturity by putting the interest of the people of Zimbabwe first," he said.

Past meetings of regional heads of state have failed to produce a breakthrough and there were new signs that the parties may face another round of difficult negotiations.

Tsvangirai's MDC said last week that Mugabe's ZANU-PF party had put a full stop to negotiations on forming a government by carrying out what it said was widespread violence.

Zimbabwean state media reported on Sunday that Mugabe's government would not change its stance on key positions in a power-sharing cabinet and the opposition should accept joint control of the interior ministry.

Justice Minister Patrick Chinamasa told the state-run Sunday Mail the deadlock would end only if Tsvangirai agreed to joint control of the ministry, which oversees the police.

"The proposals are on the table and the ball is in Tsvangirai's court," Chinamasa said.

"We want to make it clear that this proposal, which ZANU-PF accepted as a compromise, was originated by Tsvangirai himself."

Tsvangirai, who would become prime minister under the power-sharing deal, has accused ZANU-PF of trying to seize the lion's share of important ministries and relegating the MDC to the role of junior partner.

South Africa's government has said it will take a tough stand at the summit — a sharp change from the style of former President Thabo Mbeki, the official mediator whose policy of quiet diplomacy was criticised as ineffective.

It is not clear what practical steps the SADC could take to force an agreement on the two rivals.

Zimbabwe's economic crisis has forced millions of its citizens to flee the country, an estimated three million of them moving to neighbouring South Africa alone.

Ties between Zimbabwe and neighbouring Botswana have also become strained after Botswanan President Seretse Khama Ian Khama said a new election was the only solution to the crisis.

Heading: ‘Al-Qaeda planning UK terror attacks’ - Indian Express
Content:
International rescue teams joined the search for survivors in the rubble of a Haitian school that collapsed on classrooms filled with students and teachers, killing at least 88 people.

Thousands of hopeful Haitians crowded around the school in the Port-au-Prince suburb, cheering and shouting directions as searchers dug through the remnants of College La Promesse, occasionally finding survivors a day after it collapsed. Trucks carrying oxygen and other medical supplies rumbled up the mountainside.

Roughly 500 children and teenagers typically crowded into Petionville's three-story school building.

Local authorities used bare hands to pull bleeding students from the wreckage before heavy equipment and international teams began arriving on Saturday.

Nearly 40 search-and-rescue officials from Fairfax County, Virginia arrived to help rescuers.

"I see a dramatic turn-about in the situation once they're here because these guys are the real experts," said Alexandre Deprez, acting director of the US Agency for International Development in Haiti. "We've done everything we've possibly can practically from the first hour."

France also sent a team of 15 firefighters and doctors with two rescue dogs. A French civil protection official, Commandant Patrick Vailli, said the workers spotted five people believed to be alive in the school's two basements and recovered two bodies.

It is unclear whether the five people were rescued alive.

Some parents clutched pictures of their children as they watched rescue workers sidestep the limbs of dead people sticking out under the rubble. Riot police chased away several Haitians who had found their way around the yellow tape and began excavating themselves.

President Rene Preval said poor construction, including a lack of steel reinforcement, was to blame for Friday's collapse of the concrete College La Promesse in Petionville.

Preval told The Associated Press that structures throughout Haiti are at similar risk because of poor construction and a lack of government oversight. "It's not just schools, it's where people live, it's churches," he said at the site of the collapse as crews picked through the wreckage in search of more victims.

Doctors Without Borders was treating more than 80 people, many with serious injuries, said Francois Servranckx, a spokesman for the aid group.

Heading: Airstrikes kill 13 militants in northwest Pak - Indian Express
Content:
Al-Qaeda-Linked extremists are planning attacks intended to cause mass casualties in the UK, a top British intelligence report has warned.

The report, which has been prepared by the intelligence branch of the British Ministry of Defence, MI5 and Special Branch, warned that secret cells of al-Qaeda extremists based in London, Birmingham and Luton are planning attacks in the UK.

The so-called Government Security Zone (GSZ), an area which covers the Houses of Parliament, Whitehall, Buckingham and St James' Palaces, is a possible target of the al-Qaeda cells, with threat level in the GSZ described as "severe", the Daily Telegraph reported.

"For the foreseeable future the UK will continue to be a high-priority target for international terrorists aligned with al-Qaeda. It will face a threat from British nationals, including Muslim converts, and UK-based foreign terrorists, as well as terrorists planning attacks from abroad," the top intelligence report said.

Heading: The start of the Holocaust: writer unearths history in German village - Indian Express
Content:
Airstrikes pounded suspected insurgent hide-outs in a northwestern Pakistan tribal region bordering Afghanistan on Sunday, killing 13 alleged militants in the latest round of a bloody army offensive, officials said.

Meanwhile, a remote-controlled bomb planted on a motorcycle killed a passer-by and wounded five others in a market in the southwest Baluchistan province. An ethnic Baluch nationalist group claimed responsibility.

The Pakistani army, using helicopter gunships, fighter jets and ground troops, has pursued an offensive against militants in Bajur, a tribal region considered a militant stronghold, since early August. The army says it has killed 1,500 insurgents in Bajur.

The US has praised the offensive, saying it has helped reduce violence on the Afghan side of the border.

Government official Jamil Khan said the strikes Sunday targeted six militant hide-outs and killed at least 13 insurgents. The claims are nearly impossible to verify independently because of restrictions on travel in the remote, dangerous region.

The remote-controlled bomb blast occurred in Baluchistan's Sui town, police officer Abdul Majid Dasti said. He confirmed the casualties.

In a phone call to reporters, Baluchistan Republican Army spokesman Sarbaz Baluch said the group was behind the attack. He claimed the explosion killed an opponent of the movement, but police would not confirm that.

The Baluchistan Republican Army is part of a low-level insurgency that has long rattled the province. The insurgents are seeking greater provincial autonomy and more control over the area's natural resources.

Elsewhere in Pakistan's northwest, security forces fatally shot a local journalist late on Saturday, officials said. The killing occurred in the Swat Valley area, where the military also is engaged in an offensive against insurgents.

The journalist, Mohammad Shoaib, worked for the Azadi newspaper and apparently did not stop his vehicle when signaled to do so, said Anwar Saadat, a police officer.

Mazhar Abbas, a top official with the Pakistan Federal Union of Journalists, confirmed the shooting, as did Akhtar Ali, a colleague of Shoaib's at the Azadi paper. Abbas said local journalists already had staged protests in Mingora and that more were planned.

Heading: Bali bombers executed - Indian Express
Content:
Transition advisers to President-elect Barack Obama have compiled a list of about 200 Bush administration actions and executive orders that could be swiftly undone to reverse White House policies on climate change, stem cell research, reproductive rights and other issues, according to congressional Democrats, campaign aides and experts working with the transition team.

A team of four dozen advisers, working for months in virtual solitude, set out to identify regulatory and policy changes Obama could implement soon after his inauguration. The team is now consulting with liberal advocacy groups, Capitol Hill staffers and potential agency chiefs to prioritise those they regard as the most onerous or ideologically offensive, said a top transition official who was not permitted to speak on the record about the inner workings of the transition.

In some instances, Obama would be quickly delivering on promises he made during his two-year campaign, while in others, he would be embracing Clinton-era policies upended by President Bush during his eight years in office.

"The kind of regulations they are looking at" are those imposed by Bush for "overtly political" reasons, in pursuit of what Democrats say was a partisan Republican agenda, said Dan Mendelson, a former associate administrator for health in the Clinton administration's Office of Management and Budget. The list of executive orders targeted by Obama's team could well get longer in the coming days, as Bush's appointees are rushing to enact a number of last-minute policies in an effort to extend his legacy.

A spokeswoman said on Saturday that no plans for regulatory changes had been finalised. Still, the pre-election transition team, comprising mainly lawyers, has positioned the incoming president to move fast on high-priority items without waiting for Congress.

Obama himself has signaled, for example, that he intends to reverse Bush's controversial limit on federal funding of embryonic stem cell research, a decision that scientists say has restrained research into some of the most promising avenues for defeating a wide array of diseases such as Parkinson's. Bush's August 2001 decision pleased religious conservatives who have moral objections to the use of cells from days-old human embryos, which are destroyed in the process.

The new president is also expected to lift a so-called global gag rule barring international family planning groups that receive US aid from counseling women about the availability of abortion, even in countries where the procedure is legal, said Cecile Richards, the president of Planned Parenthood Federation of America. When Bill Clinton took office in 1993, he rescinded the Reagan-era regulation, known as the Mexico City Policy, but Bush reimposed it.

The president-elect has said that he intends to quickly reverse the Bush administration's decision last December to deny California the authority to regulate carbon dioxide emissions from automobiles. "Effectively tackling global warming demands bold and innovative solutions, and given the failure of this administration to act, California should be allowed to pioneer," Obama said last January.

Before the election, Obama told others that he favors declaring that carbon dioxide emissions are endangering human welfare, following an Enironment Protection Agency task force recommendation last December that Bush and his aides shunned in order to protect the utility and auto industries. Other early Obama initiatives may address the need for improved food and drug regulation and chart a new course for immigration enforcement, some Obama advisers say.

Heading: After Assam blasts, congratulations from Bangladesh to ‘planner’ in Agartala - Indian Express
Content:
Three Indonesian militants executed on Sunday for the 2002 Bali bombings were buried by their families at ceremonies attended by thousands of sobbing supporters shouting Allahu akbar (God is great).

The three men from the militant group Jemaah Islamiah — Imam Samudra, 38, Mukhlas, 48, and Amrozi, 46 — were executed by firing squad on Nusakambangan island in central Java shortly after midnight, the attorney-general's office said.

The two explosions on Bali's Kuta strip on October 12, 2002 killed 202 people including 88 Australians and 38 Indonesians.

The bombers' bodies were flown from the prison by helicopter to their home towns — brothers Mukhlas and Amrozi to Tenggulun in Lamongan, East Java, and Samudra to Serang in West Java.

Some friends and supporters chanted "live nobly" or "die as martyrs" until the bodies of brothers Mukhlas and Amrozi were lowered into the ground. After the burial, supporters stood in the rain and prayed for the bombers. Imam Samudra was buried in a private ceremony attended by just his family and friends.

The attorney general's spokesman, Jasman Pandjaitan, said the bombers, who asked not to be blindfolded during the execution, were cooperative.

"Only one bullet hit the victims, right on the left chest hitting the heart," Pandjaitan told a news conference. "There was no resistance and they were very cooperative."

Earlier, thousands of Indonesians poured onto the streets for the funerals of the three militants causing some clashes between police and emotional supporters.

"Looking at this, I feel sad, but then I am also proud that he is a Mujahid (Muslim fighter)," said Nuranda, a woman who came to offer her condolences to Samudra's family.

Tensions ran high as about 3,000 people from west Java cities gathered when Samudra's body, covered in a black shroud with Islamic inscriptions, was carried to a mosque for prayers. Some jostled to touch the body or help carry the bier.

In Tenggulun, thousands of militant Islamists from groups such as the Islamic Defenders' Front had gathered, shadowed by armed police and many reporters.

People chanted "Goodbye Syuhada" (heroes) and "Allahu Akbar" as the bodies of Mukhlas and Amrozi were taken from the mosque to an Islamic boarding school where controversial cleric Abu Bakar Bashir prayed for the brothers.

Some clashed with police as authorities tried to prevent them from getting too close to the bodies.

Among those in the streets were followers of Bashir, who was accused of co-founding regional militant group Jemaah Islamiah and jailed for conspiracy over the Bali bombings, but later cleared of wrongdoing.

Indonesia tightened security amid fears of revenge attacks as tensions ran high, but one analyst said the executions were unlikely to spark active terrorism.

"People need to be vigilant and there's a possibility of someone responding to the appeal of the three dead men but I don't think people should believe that there will automatically be some active terrorism," Sidney Jones, a security expert from the Brussels-based International Crisis Group, told Reuters.

Although there have been no major bomb attacks since 2005, Indonesia is considered still at risk.

Jemaah Islamiah said the Bali attacks were intended to deter foreigners as part of a drive to make Indonesia, the world's most populous Muslim country, part of a larger Islamic caliphate.

Australia immediately issued a travel warning for citizens going to Indonesia and Foreign Minister Stephen Smith warned of possible reprisals. "We continue to have credible information that terrorists may be planning attacks in Indonesia," Smith said on Australian TV.

Prime Minister Kevin Rudd said his thoughts were with the families of the victims. "Their lives remain shattered. They have been changed fundamentally by that murder," he told reporters.

Although new attacks targeting bars and tourist hangouts were possible, Jemaah Islamiah's network was fractured and sympathy for the bombers was low, said a leading Australian analyst.

"There will be some people in Indonesian society who regard them as martyrs, but they will be a very small proportion," said Damien Kingsbury, an associate professor at Deakin University.

"Jemaah Islamiyah's willingness and capacity to carry out bomb attacks is much reduced," he said.

About a hundred Balinese, including some survivors, prayed at a memorial near the blast site in Kuta.

The Balinese widow of a security officer killed in the blasts said she hoped the executions would mark some closure.

"So, let the past be behind us and I hope there will not be any revenge from their families and supporters," said Wayan Rasmi. The body of her husband was never found after the blasts.

Heading: Man accused in TDP MLA’s murder is bludgeoned to death in prison cell - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty-one sailors have died in an accident on board a Russian nuclear submarine that was to have been leased to the Indian Navy next year. Another 21 sailors were injured after deadly Freon gas leaked from the submarine's fire extinguishing system during sea trials off Vladivostok Saturday night.

The Akula II class 'Nerpa' nuclear attack submarine was to have joined the Navy as the INS Chakra on August 15, 2009 on a 10-year lease. A first batch of 40 Indian naval personnel was scheduled to leave New Delhi next week to train on the submarine later this month.

The Navy refused to comment on the incident that took place "on a Russian boat with a Russian crew on board". But the accident may delay the induction, as New Delhi now insists on more tests before accepting the submarine.

Initial reports received by the Navy, however, indicate that the submarine has not suffered any major structural or reactor damage, and the gas leak could have been the result of a human error. All the dead and injured have been identified as Russian naval personnel and shipyard technicians.

"The extent of damage does not seem to be much as it is just a gas leak and no structural damage has been reported. More checks may be required to ensure that everything onboard is functional but we don't anticipate it to delay things too much," a senior officer said.

The Akula II class nuclear attack submarine is the most modern in Russia's fleet, and also its quietest and deadliest. It was launched in 1991 at the Komsomolsk-on-Amur shipyard, but was put into cold storage before completion due to financial constraints. The project was revived after India showed interest in leasing a nuclear attack submarine to train its sailors for a future class of indigenous nuclear submarines, and work on the refitting was completed this June. Last month, the shipyard announced that the submarine had been moved after factory trials to a temporary facility near Vladivostok on the Pacific Ocean, where it would undergo a series of sea trials.

India and Russia have never officially acknowledged that the 'Nerpa' is to be inducted into the Indian Navy, though Indian naval officers and men have been training at Russian facilities to operate the submarine. In a candid admission with this newspaper in December last year, Navy Chief Admiral Sureesh Mehta had admitted that the Navy was looking for a nuclear submarine to train its men on the future class of indigenous Advance Technology Vessel (ATV) nuclear submarines.

"We have not been operating on a nuclear platform and had taken the 'Chakra' on lease from Russia earlier. Now we want one more Akula sub to train our boys on how to operate a nuclear platform," Admiral Mehta had told The Indian Express.

The Akula II class vessel will be the second nuclear submarine to be leased by Russia to India after the 'Chakra' Charlie I class nuclear attack sub that was leased for four years from 1988. Unofficial estimates put the cost of the submarine at close to $1 billion.

Heading: No VHP links, we condemn riots in Gujarat: Sonal Shah’s brother - Indian Express
Content:
The three-year-old murder of Rayalseema MLA Paritala Ravindra — who fashioned himself as a modern-day Robin Hood, accused of eliminating rivals without mercy while giving huge donations to the poor and needy — has come back to haunt the Congress Government of Y S Rajasekhara Reddy. Last night, in the high-security Anantapur Jail, one of the main accused in the murder, Moddu Seenu, was bludgeoned to death by a cell mate with dumbbells, incidentally after he had decided to turn approver in the case.

Paritala's wife Suneetha and TDP leaders have alleged a conspiracy, saying the same people who eliminated the TDP MLA were behind the attack on Seenu. Suneetha has hinted at the involvement of Chief Minister Rajasekhara Reddy. A CBI inquiry into the case is still on.

Jail officials have denied this, saying Seenu's death was the result of a clash over "keeping the lights on" and had nothing to do with Paritala's murder.

Anantapur Superintendent of Police M K Singh told The Indian Express that Om Prakash, an inter-state dacoit, had confessed to beating up Moddu Seenu (whose real name was J Srinivas Reddy) as he had been "harassing him for the past 10 days by not allowing him to write his daily 'Ram Kothi'. Seenu apparently was also not letting him keep the light on at night. Om Prakash admitted that he hit Seenu on the head with improvised dumbbells."

Saying too much was being read into the incident, the SP added: "Paritala Ravi's former gang member is also lodged in the same barracks but he and Seenu never fought."

However, Seenu's killing is likely to be seen as another chapter in Anantapur's 200-year-old chronicle of bloodshed, and the three-decade-old feud between the landlord family of Paritala on one side and two other landlord families on the other.

Seenu had been captured after a long hunt of 10 months, during which time he gave an interview to a TV channel claiming to have shot Paritala several times between the eyes, and the arrest itself had been dramatic. On November 17, 2005, a bomb he was assembling in a hotel room in Chandannagar in Hyderabad had exploded, leaving him seriously injured. It was only after he was admitted to a hospital did the police realise he was the "most wanted" Moddu Seenu.

Among those impressed with the story was Bollywood producer-director Ram Gopal Verma, who once interviewed Seenu behind bars for a film on the faction feuds of Rayalseema.

In jail, Seenu often complained that his life was under threat. In spite of this, point out Paritala supporters, undertrial Om Prakash, a hardened criminal, was lodged with him in jail.

Talking to The Indian Express over the phone, Suneetha, who was elected as MLA from Penukonda after Paritala's death, said: "Moddu Seenu had decided to turn approver after his accomplice Ram Mohan Reddy did the same. He was about to spill the beans on those who planned and financed the murder of Paritala Ravi. I think the state Government headed by Dr Y S Rajasekhara Reddy is involved in getting him killed because such things don't happen in a high-security jail."

A four-time MLA from Penukonda and the minister of labour in NTR's Government, Paritala, 47, was shot dead by Seenu and three accomplices on January 24, 2005, when he was coming out of the TDP office in Anantapur.

Hugely popular in Anantapur district, Paritala was known to give huge amounts of money to the needy, sometimes arranging mass weddings for them. As known was his 30-year-old criminal record, including murder and intimidation. He was accused of having ruthlessly and systematically gone about eliminating those involved in the murders of his father Sriramulu and brother Srihari.

By the time the factional feud took his own life, Paritala was blamed for the murders of all the male members of one rival family and the head of another. At least four persons allegedly involved a car-bomb attack on him were also tracked and murdered.

Heading: Gogoi says Assam short of 8,500 police personnel - Indian Express
Content:
A top executive of a city-based popular chain of hotels has been arrested for alleged involvement in human trafficking to the United States.

P R Shivakumar, Managing Director and son of Saravana Bhavan Group of Hotels proprietor Rajagopal, was arrested by the Crime Branch CID police on Saturday night on a complaint from the US consulate general office, police said on Sunday.

Shivakumar had allegedly prepared fake documents for four of his employees with an ulterior motive of getting US visas under the pretext of visiting an expo and getting them employed in America, they said. One of the four employees, Ramu Murugaiyan, was arrested this morning.

During the course of their visa interview at the consulate, the officials found out that all the four employees had produced fake documents. All the documents were recovered from the corporate office of the Saravana Bhavan Group of Hotels.

Cases have been registered against the accused for various offences, including cheating and forgery, under various sections of the IPC. Rajagopal, who runs the chain of hotels, was convicted in connection with the murder of an employee a few years ago.

Heading: No question of ceding any part of Arunachal: Pranab - Indian Express
Content:
Assam, which was recently hit by ethnic riots in Udalguri and Darrang districts, followed by the serial blasts across the state, is currently facing a shortage of over 8,500 policemen, according to Chief Minister Tarun Gogoi.

"The Assam Police currently has a sanctioned strength of 65,630 persons. But even as we have been able to appoint 5,719 personnel during this year, the Assam Police is still short of 8,511 personnel," the Chief Minister said.

Gogoi said the financial crisis when he took over as Chief Minister in 2001 had delayed recruitments. "But later, as we began the recruitment process, some people went to the High Court and some even to the Supreme Court, which has delayed the whole process," he said, adding that he had raised the issue at a conference of chief justices in New Delhi recently. "I asked how we can tackle insurgency if the recruitment process was delayed."

"Insurgency has gone up. The number of insurgent groups has gone up. Yet, there is a shortage of manpower in the Assam Police," he said.

Despite problems, including court cases, the state Government has been able to select 4,500 people, but now the problem is that of training them. "We want to strengthen the police force. But we have limited training facilities. Our existing infrastructure can churn out only 2,000 policemen a year. So we are asking the Border Security Force to help us," Gogoi said.

The Gogoi Cabinet had only last week decided to upgrade Guwahati City Police to a police commissionerate. But the city police, which is responsible for the security of over two million, is currently running with several crucial posts lying vacant. The crucial posts of SP (Operations) and Additional SP (Operations), for instance, have been lying vacant for more than two months now. The Dispur police station, which covers the state capital complex apart from a huge area that includes VIP residences and other Government offices, is running short of not only police personnel, but also vehicles.

"Guwahati City Police also has the additional burden of providing escort and security cover to a large number of VIPs who pass through the city en route to other states," an official said.

The capital city, however, is not the only district that is suffering from shortage of staff. Udalguri, a district where about 40,000 people are still lodged in relief camps following ethnic riots six weeks ago, also has several top posts vacant.

Heading: Selling India’s growth story, PM pitches for investment from Gulf - Indian Express
Content:
Rebuffing China's claim on Arunachal Pradesh, India on Sunday asserted that the northeastern state was its integral part and ruled out ceding any part of it. "China is often making claims on Arunachal Pradesh, but Arunachal Pradesh has a special place in our heart," External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee, who visited a 400-year-old Buddhist monastery here in this border town, the second in importance to the one at Lhasa in Tibet, said.

"People of Arunachal Pradesh regularly elect two representatives to the Lok Sabha and there is an elected state Assembly carrying out the responsibility of administration like any of the other 27 states. The question of parting company of Arunachal or any of its part does not arise," he said amidst deafening cheers.

Mukherjee's rejection of the Chinese claim on Arunachal Pradesh follows the recent declaration of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh during a visit to the state that Arunachal Pradesh was "our land of rising sun".

Addressing as chief guest at the 8th Buddha Mahotsava, Mukherjee said "both India and China are seeking a peaceful solution to the border dispute. The special representatives of the Prime Ministers of both India and China have completed 12 rounds of talks. There are problems in identification of land between the two countries.

Amidst loud applause from thousands of people gathered on the occasion, Mukherjee said one of the parameters that India was insisting on in sorting out the boundary issue was that no settled population could be exchanged.

During a public meeting in Arunachal capital Itanagar on January 31 last, the PM had also announced a Rs 20,000-crore financial package for rapid development of the mountainous tribal state. Mukherjee said he was pleased to get an opportunity to come to Tawang, the birth place of the 6th Dalai Lama.

"There are some places which are not just geographical entities. Because of cultural heritage and history associated with them, they occupy special places in our hearts and Tawang is such a place where righteous people create an atmosphere free from violence and hatred," he said.

Heading: AGP, BJP inch closer, seat-sharing talks today - Indian Express
Content:
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Sunday invited the captains of Oman's industry and finance to invest surplus liquidity in key infrastructure sectors in India which he said would require $500 billion to be pumped in over the next five years. Coming against the backdrop of the global economic meltdown, Singh's first visit as Prime Minister to the Gulf region assumes significance as he is clearly targeting the almost five million strong Indian expat community to invest majorly in the Indian economy, even as he prepares for the first visit by an Indian PM to Qatar later in the day.

The Prime Minister, while appreciating the Indian community in Oman that is already making annual remittances to the tune of $780 million, called upon them to "continue to display the same confidence in the future and invest in the future of our children and grand children." Referring to the bilateral trade between the two countries, he said the total non-oil trade which was less than $200 million in 2000 had gone up seven-fold to around $1.4 billion this year. "I am told this figure could soon cross $2 billion," he said.

Singh expressed his faith in the strong fundamentals of the Indian economy in the face of the economic crisis. "Due to the current international economic and financial situation, our growth rate may come down somewhat next year. However, we still hope to achieve a growth rate of 7 to 7.5 per cent next year. The fundamentals of our economy are strong. Our banking system and financial institutions are well capitalised and secure. I have constituted a high-level committee to monitor the situation and suggest short-term and long-term measure to use this opportunity to further accelerate our growth," he said.

Singh said India was undergoing a major transformation with a rapidly expanding economy. "Our domestic savings rate is 35 per cent of our GDP and our investment rate is 37 per cent of our GDP. Our young demographic profile will lead to a further increase in these rates of savings and investment over the coming years," he said.

Referring to the MoU signed on Saturday to establish the India-Oman Joint Investment Fund, the PM said, the fund was the first, but a long overdue step. "This is only the beginning. I hope that this fund will open the door for far greater investment and economic cooperation between our two countries," he said.

"I would call upon captains of Oman's industry and financial companies to invest surplus liquidity into key infrastructure sectors in India. We are determined to create a hospitable climate for investment, particularly foreign investment from friendly countries like Oman. The Gulf region is an area of great importance to India. It is part of our extended neighbourhood, and home to five million Indians. It is the largest source of our energy supplies. We have active trade and investment interests. Piracy, criminal activities and terrorism on our seas and land threaten the Gulf countries and India as well," Singh said while listing reasons for the two countries to work closely together.

Among those business leaders present were the CEOs and chairmen of Oman Oil Co, MB Holding Co, WJ Towell Group, Oman Arab Bank, Bank Muscat and those with Indian footprints like, Gulfaar, Shobha Developers and Lulu hypermarkets.

Heading: Another chapter in Anantapur’s bloody tale of political vendetta - Indian Express
Content:
With the Lok Sabha elections drawing closer, the Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) and BJP are inching closer in order to work out a seat-sharing arrangement in Assam. A delegation of the regional party, headed by its president Chandra Mohan Patowari, is leaving for New Delhi on Monday to hold discussions with top BJP leaders on the issue.

"We are meeting senior BJP leaders in New Delhi tomorrow to finalise our strategy for the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections," Patowari said on Sunday. He, however, said though the regional party was entering into an understanding with the BJP, it was not joining the NDA at the moment.

The AGP leaders would also meet leaders of other national parties and discuss the recent serial blasts in Guwahati and three other towns of the state. "We are also planning to meet the President and place before her the demand for dismissal of the Congress-led Government headed by Tarun Gogoi," Patowari said.

"The Congress-led Government has failed utterly to protect the lives of the people. But what is more alarming is that it is also scared of the jehadi elements, including the HuJI, which are responsible for the deadly serial blasts of October 30," the AGP president said.

The AGP and BJP had won two seats each out of a total of 14 Lok Sabha seats in Assam in 2004. The Congress party had won nine while one had gone to an independent who is currently an ally of the Congress and UPA.

Heading: On CIA site, Left Front still backs UPA - Indian Express
Content:
The murder in prison of Moddu Seenu — one of the main accused in the murder of TDP MLA Paritala Ravi — on Sunday adds one more chapter to a bloody feud that raged in Anantapur district of Andhra Pradesh for over three decades.

Paritala Ravi's introduction into violent factionalism began at the age of 17 with the murder of his Communist father Paritala Sriramulu in 1975. He had donated most of his land to the poor and landless and fought for their rights when two other landlords — Gangula Narayana Reddy and S Chenna Reddy — started occupying lands in Venkatapuram village, Anantapur district.

Sriramulu joined the former CPI(ML) party in 1971 and rose to become a top leader of the Naxalite movement. The land struggle soon turned into a vendetta and caste war when he was killed on May 29, 1975 by his own follower who was allegedly hired by Gangula Reddy and Chenna Reddy. Srihari, Paritala Ravi's younger brother, also joined the Naxalites in 1979 but was shot dead by the police in November 1982.

Although Paritala Ravi escaped from his home village, it didn't take long for him to be drawn into the Naxalite fold and to unleash a string of revenge murders in the region, beginning with masterminding the killing of Gangula Narayana Reddy who was hacked to death in a lodge in 1983. Two henchmen of Gangula were also killed similarly.

"At that time, S Chenna Reddy and his two sons Ramana Reddy and Obul Reddy were a terror in the area too. They were joined by Surya Narayana Reddy, son of Gangula Narayana Reddy. The two Reddy gangs killed several followers and friends of Paritala Ravi's family. In 1991, S Channa Reddy was killed by Naxalites, who raided his house wearing police uniforms," says a police officer who served as SP Anantapur.

After the PWG expelled its founder Kondapalli Sitaramaiah, several splinter groups were formed, one of which was the Re-organising Committee (ROC) to which Paritala Ravi attached himself. The ROC then went about abducting and killing henchmen, friends and relatives of Obul Reddy and Surya Narayana Reddy.

In 1993, Paritala Ravi allegedly recruited a television repairman to plant a bomb in Surya Narayana Reddy's TV set, which was brought to his shop for repair. The bomb exploded when it was switched on in the house of Surya Narayana Reddy, killing his mother and three siblings.

That year, Paritala Ravi won the Penukonda seat on a TDP ticket against Ramana Reddy and went on to become labour minister in NTR's government. He remained in NTR's group when N Chandrababu Naidu staged a coup but joined him after NTR's death and again won from Penukonda in 1996.

All this while, the revenge killings did not stop. In 1996, Paritala Ravi's ROC members slit the throat of Obul Reddy in a hotel at Hyderabad. The killings inspired Surya Narayana Reddy, alias Soori, to take revenge on Paritala Ravi. He allegedly triggered a remote-controlled car bomb kept outside D Rama Naidu Studio just when Paritala Ravi and actor Mohan Babu—who was supposed to start in Sriramuliah, a film based on Paritala Ravi's father — were passing by in a car. It was a providential escape for Ravi, as a car carrying a TV channel crew had just overtaken them and took the full impact of the blast.

Soori was arrested and at least four others involved in the car-bomb attack were hunted down and killed, allegedly by members of the ROC. Finally, Ramana Reddy, former MLA and brother of Obul Reddy, was killed in 1999 in a house in Banjara Hills.

In 2004, Paritala Ravi again contested on a TDP ticket and won with 24,000 votes though his party lost power. Suneetha, Paritala's widow, alleges that a few days after the Congress came to power, killings of TDP activists began in Anantapur district. At least six followers of Paritala Ravi were allegedly killed by Soori's gang.

On January 24, 2005, Moddu Seenu and two others shot dead Paritala Ravi outside the TDP office in Anantapur.

Heading: Problem leopard to be shot down - Indian Express
Content:
The United States' Central Intelligence Agency, perceived to have the best spy network, appears clueless about a significant development in Indian politics in the past few months — the Left parties' withdrawal of support to the UPA government.

"Privatisation of government-owned industries remains stalled and continues to generate political debate; populist pressure from within the UPA government and from its Left Front allies continues to restrain needed initiatives," says the World Factbook section of the CIA website about the state of the Indian economy.

What is interesting is that the India page was last updated on November 6, 2008, while the Left Front withdrew its support to the Government in July this year. The withdrawal of support had led to a trust vote, along with accusations of horse trading in Parliament — all played out on TV channels across the country.

The CIA maintains a World Factbook on its website, which is regularly updated and has information ranging from politics to economy on almost all countries.

Heading: Angry at train’s delay, mob sets on fire railway office in Bihar - Indian Express
Content:
In what appears to be a repeat of last November's Talodhi incident, when a tiger had to be shot dead after it killed four persons, orders to shoot a leopard were issued by Principal Chief Conservator of Forest (Wildlife) B Majumdar on Sunday.

The leopard has killed two persons and injured three others right inside the precincts of this remote village. After a man was killed in full public view on November 6, a riot-like situation arose in Vejgaon, with villagers attacking vehicles belonging to top forest officials. Over 100 commandos had to rush in to control the situation.

"I received shoot orders, but our priority will be to first trap or tranquilise the animal," said Divisional Forest Officer Rama Rao.

The man-animal conflict in Chandrapur district, first reported by The Indian Express, started assuming serious proportions in 2006. Tiger attacks have claimed 38 lives since January 2006, but leopard attacks are a relatively recent phenomenon, with four casualties and eight injuries reported over the past 45 days.

Vidya Athreya, a leopard expert from Pune, also visited Vejgaon on the request of the PCCF. "You can't take any more risks in this situation. But this is aberrant behaviour. Maybe some of this is due to human beings. This had happened in Junnar near Pune where 50 people had died in leopard attacks in 2001 and 2002 following large-scale trapping of leopards," she said.

Incidentally, these attacks are now being connected with an incident in which three animals were caged in Junona village, where a leopard family killed two persons and injured five others. One leopard was released in Kothari forest about 25 km from Vejgaon. "It is still a mystery how the leopard made a sudden appearance in Vejgaon. I can't say if the one released in Kothari could have come this side," said Rama Rao.

Heading: Z-category security for Puri seer who criticised missionaries - Indian Express
Content:
Over two dozens passengers torched the office of assistant station master (ASM) at Saharsa railway station on Sunday morning when their train did not arrive even after 18 hours past its scheduled time. Nobody, however, was injured in the incident.

The Government Railway Police (GRP), Saharsa, said the passengers lost patience after 5279 UP Saharsa-New Delhi Purbiya Express scheduled to arrive at the station at 10.35 am on Saturday did not turn up till 4.40 am on Sunday.

The passengers got angry when no announcement about the train arrival was made. The train comes to Saharasa from Barauni and leaves for New Delhi.

Saharsa GRP station in-charge M P Singh said: "Over 20 passengers entered ASM M K Jha's office and torched furniture and some documents. The police promptly rushed to the spot to avoid further damage." Jha, however, was not present in the office at the time of the incident. Jha had asked for police help, sensing passengers' ire.

The police have arrested five passengers. The train finally arrived at 9.35 am.

Heading: Banks clogging judicial system: court report - Indian Express
Content:
The Ministry of Home Affairs has asked the Orissa Government to immediately provide Z-Category security for Sankaracharya of Puri Gobardhan Peetha Jagadaguru Swami Nischalananda Saraswati in view of the threat to his life. Nischalananda has been criticising Christian missionaries over religious conversion since the murder of Laxmanananda Saraswati.

With VHP and RSS top shots making a beeline to his ashram in Puri over the past two months, the state does not want to take any chance with the high-profile seer's security. Last November, the seer had received a postcard, allegedly from the al-Qaeda, warning him of dire consequences if he did not embrace Islam.

In Bargarh district, the police have arrested two Bajrang Dal activists over their alleged role in the burning of a 22-year-old Hindu tribal girl during the Kandhamal riots. The girl, Rajni Majhi, worked in an orphanage run by Christian missionaries in Padampur sub-division.

DIG Y B Khurania said Bajrang Dal western Orissa convenor Prashant Majhi and activist Karticka Nag have been booked for their role in the incident as well as arson during the riots. Prashanta allegedly led the mob which damaged missionary-run institutions at Madhupur, Chichinda, Tungibandhli and Padampur besides Khuntpali where Rajani Nag was set afire.

Meanwhile, a group of writers owing allgience to the Sangh Parivar alleged that the Kandhamal riot was an international conspiracy to defame Orissa and sully its image in the world.

Around 72 writers and columnists who came together under an association called the Writers' Forum on Sunday alleged that the Christian missionaries under the instruction of the international churches were engaged in converting Dalits and motivating them to fight against the tribals.

Heading: Indian groups celebrate new Maldives President - Indian Express
Content:
Statistics in a Delhi High Court report seem to confirm what the Chief Justice of India (CJI), K G Balakrishnan, lamented just a few days ago during a hearing — bounced cheque cases are clogging the judicial system, especially at the lower levels, leading to extended delays in other criminal trials.

The CJI had even remarked that banks and other financial institutions appear to be using the judiciary as their "collection agents" by filing bounced cheque cases instituted under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments (NI) Act.

His fears are not unfounded. The Indian Express has access to an internal report prepared by the Delhi High Court, which highlights how the subordinate judiciary is collapsing under the weight of such cases. As of June 1, 2008, out of a total backlog of 7,66,974 criminal cases pending in all four district courts (excluding the newly opened court in Saket) in the Capital, 5,14,533 are cases of bounced cheques instituted under Section 138 of the NI Act -- nearly two-thirds of the total pendency of magistrate courts in the national Capital.

There are 110 courts of metropolitan magistrates spread across four district courts here dealing with several of these cases. Even more unfortunate is the number of judicial officers burdened with disposing of these cases. The report points out, "Thirty-two courts are exclusively dealing with Section 138 NI Act cases, with five at Patiala House, eight in Rohini courts, three and six each at Tis Hazari and Karkardooma courts respectively". Fifty per cent of the 32 courts that exclusively handle cheque bouncing cases are burdened with complaints where the amount is not more than Rs 50,000.

In tune with CJI Balakrishnan's remarks, the majority of these cases are filed by banking and financial institutions. As on February 29, 2008, the total pendency of such cases was 3,66,197. The number, as of date, has now risen to 4,28,498.

Incidentally, one of the most prolific litigants burdening these courts is ICICI Bank, which has 83,523 cases pending in four district courts, reveals the Delhi High Court report.

Even government-owned banking and financial institutions are not far behind in adding to these courts' burden. For instance, the State Bank of India has close to 20,000 cases pending in three district courts.

With Section 138 NI Act cases forming the majority chunk of arrears in district courts, the HC has for the first time, suggested transfer of all these cases to Dwarka district court, which is to come up soon.

It has been proposed that a "separate category of cases involving financial institutions and banking companies" be allocated to special courts to be made functional at Dwarka Court complex."

Taking into account the anomaly that bounced cheque complaints, unlike other criminal or civil cases in Delhi are not filed according to districts or police stations, it has been recommended that all complaints under Section 138 NI Act be filed and allocated district wise.

Heading: Congress likely to abstain during Uttarakhand RS poll - Indian Express
Content:
As India sends Vice-President M Hamid Ansari in its first high-level engagement with new Maldivian President Mohamed Nasheed regime on Monday, the Indian supporters of the new Maldivian president — who defeated President Abdul Gayoom on October 28 to end his 30-year rule — are also celebrating his victory, with some even going to attend the swearing-in ceremony on November 11.

Among Nasheed's allies in India are civil society groups and think tanks like the prestigious Observer Research Foundation (ORF), the South Asia Analysis Group (SAAG), and former diplomats.

Nasheed, 41, who has been a crusading campaigner for democratic reforms in Maldives for the last 19 years, was in Delhi and Chennai this July.The diplomatic establishment, which for years did not encourage long-time friend Gayoom's detractors, finally granted an audience to the delegation, with Foreign Secretary Shiv Shankar Menon meeting with Nasheed.

Also to attend the swearing-in ceremony on Tuesday is ORF's Chennai chapter's director, N Sathiyamoorthy. "Nasheed's win ends the 30-year-old one-man democracy under President Gayoom. He came across as a very warm human being. He is not bitter about Gayoom's treatment towards him, and has publicly declared that he will not harass the former president. That forgiving nature is a remarkable quality in him despite having spent several years in jail and exile," said Sathiyamoorthy.

Dr S Chandrasekharan, who heads NCR-based think-tank South Asia Analysis Group (SAAG), has known Nasheed for several years. "When Nasheed's children were born, he was either in exile or in prison. But, when the Maldivian Police Commissioner and the defence chiefs called on him after his win, he told them that it was time to move on," he said.

The UK-educated Nasheed, who has close relations with the British Conservative party, has been sent to jail several times for showing open dissent against the Gayoom regime.

Chandrasekharan recalls asking Nasheed why he did not reach out to Indian political parties for support. "He told me that he did reach out to them, but they didn't respond. Now is the opportunity for India to cultivate him," he said.

Former foreign secretary Lalit Mansingh explains New Delhi's approach, "India was being sensitive to the Gayoom government and didn't want to be seen as encouraging destabilising the incumbent President".

Kuldip Sahdev, who was head of Maldives division in the MEA between 1985 and 1990, and has maintained close ties ever since, says, "I have known Nasheed for the last 15 years, as a young man who has been jailed 13 times and for a total period of six years, and yet doesn't show any signs of vindictiveness against Gayoom."

Sahdev, who spoke to Nasheed over the phone after his win, says, "He is very clear about the Maldives' economic and democratic development, and looks towards India for support."

Sahdev, a retired 1963-batch Indian Foreign Service officer , says, "He will be visiting India shortly, and his relations with India —I know — are right on top of his foreign policy agenda."

Heading: Palm chopping case: Orissa doctors put off strike - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttarakhand Congress is likely to abstain in the election to the Rajya Sabha seat that falls vacant later this month. Falling short in numbers to give a fight to the BJP candidate Bhagat Singh Koshiari, the Congress is unlikely to put up a candidate. Party sources say that there is no option but to abstain from voting. The nomination for the seat falling vacant after the term of the Congress leader Harish Rawat comes to an end later this month is to be filed on Monday.

The Uttarakhand Assembly has 36 members from the BJP while the Congress has 20. There are eight legislators of the BSP and three of the Uttarakhand Kranti Dal. There are three independents and one nominated member.

There are three Rajya Sabha members from Uttarakhand and at present all the three seats are held by the Congress. Besides Rawat, the other two members of the upper house of the Parliament from the state are Captain Satish Sharma and Satyavrat Chaturvedi.

Heading: Wife, kids of senior Haryana officer found dead - Indian Express
Content:
Orissa heaved a sigh of relief after 2,400-odd Government doctors on Saturday night agreed to put off their scheduled strike by at least three months following an assurance from Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik.

Last week, the doctors had resigned en masse and threatened to stop working from Sunday to protest against the dismissal of three doctors, who lost their jobs for allegedly cutting off the palms of five tribals while performing autopsies on their bodies in January 2006.

The five tribals were among the 12 who were kiled in the Kalinga Nagar police firing. The agitating doctors also demanded a government notification raising the salaries of entry-level doctors.

The resignation had led to large-scale panic as hundreds of patients left the government hospitals fearing long absence of doctors.

Though the Government imposed Essential Services Maintenance Act to force the doctors to carry on their work, officials soon pointed out that the already decrepit healthcare in rural areas would be badly affected. With elections a few months away, the Government did not want to risk a strike.

Orissa Medical Service Association president Madhusudan Mishra said the CM had assured a sympathetic hearing to their demands. Cadre restructuring of doctors will be completed within three months and a legislation for security to doctors on duty will be brought in the next Assembly session.

During talks the Chief Minister also indicated that the dismissal of the three doctors would be kept in abeyance.

"But we will not wait for more than three months. We hope the Government fulfils its assurance before the deadline," Mishra said.

Heading: Soon, Jamaat caravans to travel across country - Indian Express
Content:
Anju Sherawat, wife of GM, Haryana Roadways, Karnal, Varinder Singh Sherawat, reportedly committed suicide at their residence in Samalkha, Panipat, along with her two minor children, Meghna and Parth.

A .32-bore revolver was found in her bedroom, which was locked from inside, according to sources in the police. Varinder Sherawat, an HCS officer, was transferred to Hansi from Karnal two days ago and was reportedly not at home in Panipat when the incident took place.

"The three were found lying dead on the bed when the bedroom door was broken open by the police. A bullet each was fired in the heads of the three from close quarters," said Samalkha SHO Tularam.

While the daughter, Meghna, was 11-year-old, son Parth was seven. A suicide note, supposedly written by Anju, has also been found at the residence, sources said.

Tularam, who is the investigating officer in the case, said forensic experts had immediately been called after the incident came to light on Sunday morning, but the Panipat police refused to divulge any information.

Forensic experts said gun powder was found on the hands of Anju, which implies that it was she who had fired the gun. The hands of Varinder Singh Sherawat were also examined by the forensic experts, but no gun powder was found on his hands.

"The post-mortem examination report has confirmed that the deaths of the three occurred due to bullet injuries," said Tularam.

Sources said Anju was distressed by the charge of molestation and rape levied against her husband by a woman of Gannaur. Sherawat was earlier posted as SDM, Gannaur, Sonepat.

"The inquiry in that molestation and rape case is being conducted by the Gannaur DSP," said Tularam.

Panipat SP Mahender Sheoran said the police was investigating the matter and there was a chance that it could be a suicide case.

He said Sherawat was in a state of shock and was not in a position to give a statement, which could prove vital to the case.

Heading: German rape victim’s mother to withdraw charge: lawyer - Indian Express
Content:
Mainstream Muslim outfits in India have gone into an overdrive to de-link terror from Islam and to break the negative perception about the religion. The latest to join the bandwagon is the Jamaat-e-Islami Hind which is taking out caravans seeking justice in a bid to exploit the sentiment among the community members.

While the Jamaat is going to raise its voice against labelling of the community, it is also demanding that the ban should be lifted from SIMI, which is under the scanner for several bomb attacks. The two caravans will set off from Delhi on Monday and will travel across the country in the next fortnight.

Jamaat leaders said the Muslim community was being victimised and its youth harassed in the name of fighting terror. Having decided to launch a Muslim political outfit, the caravans are seen as an attempt to fire up its cadre and drum up support by tapping the popular feeling among Muslims that they were being victimised.

Though coming close on the heels of around 5,000 clerics denouncing terror at a Jamiat-Ulema-i-Hind meet in Hyderabad, the Jamaat caravans will be raising several other issues, including demands for police and jail reforms, effective legal mechanism to check police atrocities, illegal detentions, fake encounters, and custodial deaths.

Other demands are setting up of an independent high-powered commission to probe all riots and "disruptive acts" that took place in the last decade, recruitment of people from minority communities in state police forces to ensure that at least 25 per cent of the posts at all levels belong to minorities and putting an end to harassment of relatives of the detainees.

In the wake of the Jamia Nagar incident, it also demands that a locality should not be targeted or victimised for just one incident.

It also wants that confidential reports and confessions "extracted under duress" should not be leaked to the media and seeks scrapping of all legislations which make confessions in police custody admissible in courts or which allow police to keep persons arrested without filing chargesheets.

While the caravans will be led by Jamaat president Maulana Syed Jalaluddin Umari and secretary general Nusrat Ali, the organisation claimed that prominent social activists like Swami Agnivesh, John Dayal, Sandeep Pande, Khairnar, Medha Patkar, Amresh Mishra and Ajit Sahi will be part of the caravans.

Heading: Polls a week away, but election season yet to register in Valley autumn - Indian Express
Content:
Fadela Fuchs, the German researcher who accused Goa Education Minister Antanasio Monseratte's son Rohit of raping her minor daughter, on Sunday said she wanted to withdraw her complaint, expressing "frustration" over the manner the probe is moving, her lawyer said. "She has written to Calangute police station expressing frustration over the way the investigation is proceeding. She has said that she intends to withdraw her complaint," her lawyer Aires Rodrigues said.

The complaint against 21-year-old Rohit was filed on October 2 and subsequently the First Information Report (FIR) was lodged on October 14. Police booked Rohit on the charge of raping, outraging the modesty of, abetting crime and sending lewd messages to the 14- year-old girl. Sunday's development attains significance as Rohit is in police custody and his bail petition would be heard by Goa Children's Court on Monday.

Rohit, who went into hiding after the FIR was lodged, appeared before the police on November 1 to depose. His statement was recorded hours before the girl deposed before the Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC).

Sources said the girl, during her deposition, had accused Rohit of raping her and a medical examination the next day confirmed the rape. Rohit was arrested on November 4 and remanded to police custody.

Rodrigues alleged the girl's mother was being "victimised" by the police and was under constant pressure. "She finally decided to give way as she was frustrated," he said. Police officers were not available for comment.

The girl's mother had also accused Public Works Department minister Churchill Alemao's nephew Warren of sexually exploiting her daughter. But during the entire investigation, except for the statement taken by Calangute police, there was no investigation into Warren's role.

Heading: Congress Ganderbal candidate threatens to withdraw nomination - Indian Express
Content:
The first phase of polling is just nine days away, and Kashmir is yet to witness the stirrings of an election campaign. The mainstream political parties are reluctant to hold public rallies and the candidates are instead holding closed-door meetings to seek votes.

While unlike the 2002 and 1996 Assembly polls, the anti-election violence by the militants is negligible, the recent separatist upsurge has left political parties nervous.

The Government itself is taking no chances. A planned separatist march to Srinagar's grand mosque on Friday was countered with an undeclared curfew, and most of the separatist leadership — except Mirwaiz Umar Farooq — is under arrest. Seventy other activists have been booked under the Public Safety Act to thwart the announced poll boycott.

As the separatists call for similar marches on polling days, asking people to organise protest rallies and boycott elections, the Government is determined to react as strongly. Says Inspector General of J-K Police, Kashmir range, B Srinivas: "We will do everything to keep them (separatists) at bay during polling days."

Sources in the Government say the plan is clear. "Apart from the border constituencies of Uri, Tangdhar and Gurez, there is no doubt that we will have a very low turnout in Valley constituencies," a senior officer told The Indian Express. "This is why the polls are being held in seven phases. We are mixing the low-turnout constituencies of Kashmir with Jammu and Ladakh so that the consolidated turnout is decent in each phase. The worst will be Srinagar city, which is scheduled for the last phase."

Kashmir's two main political parties — the National Conference and Peoples Democratic Party — have correctly gauged this public mood, and are holding workers' meetings instead of public rallies.

"We are content with holding workers' convention because they form the party's cadre," senior PDP leader and former minister Tariq Hameed Karra told The Indian Express. "We don't have plans to hold big rallies."

There is another reason the party — which is fighting on a soft separatist political agenda, seeking shared sovereignty between India and Pakistan — is shy of holding public rallies. The separatists consider the party's manifesto an attempt to dilute their larger agenda while straddling the moderate middle ground.

On November 2, the PDP candidate from Dooru constituency in south Kashmir, Farooq Andrabi, and his workers were attacked by a crowd at Dialgam while they were on their way to attend a workers' rally in Anantnag. The police and CRPF had to fire teargas shells to rescue Andrabi and his workers from the separatist supporters.

The National Conference too has chosen holding workers' conventions under police and CRPF protection instead of open public rallies. On October 25, soon after party president Omar Abdullah had left a workers' meeting in Sonawari constituency, partymen had been attacked by pro-separatist crowds.

On November 3, when Omar went to file nomination papers from Ganderbal, the police and CRPF had to literally seal off the entire town. As soon as the cordon was relaxed, protestors clashed with the police and pelted stones.

Two days later, supporters of Independent candidate Usman Majeed were attacked at Bandipore ahead of his public rally there. Finally Majeed had to leave the place without addressing the rally.

As the police crack down against the poll boycott, the separatists are banking on public resentment. Mirwaiz calls the barricades erected across Srinagar city and his detention under house arrest ahead of the Friday congregation at Srinagar's grand mosque as itself a victory of the people. The Government, he says, "is scared of the people".

Heading: Cong wakes up to J&K election, Azad to head campaign committee - Indian Express
Content:
Ishfaq Ahmad Sheikh, the Congress candidate in Ganderbal, has threatened to withdraw his nomination blaming the police for arresting and threatening his party workers. Sheikh is taking on NC patron Omar Abdullah and Peoples Democratic Party nominee and former forest minister Qazi Afzal in the all-important seat. "My workers are being arrested and harassed by the police," Sheikh said. "Two of my prominent workers, Ajaz Ahmad and Bashir Ahmad from Behama, are in custody. The police has framed them in a false case, claiming that they were running an election boycott campaign in Ganderbal," he said.

"I will opt out of the race if the police continue to arrest and harass my workers," he said, adding that the decision has already been conveyed to the party high command.

Heading: Pilot training centre to take off from Soren’s turf - Indian Express
Content:
With just a week to go for the first phase of elections in Jammu and Kashmir, the Congress finally woke from its slumber and announced on Sunday that former chief minister, Ghulam Nabi Azad would head the campaign committee of the Congress in the state. The party is yet to start its election campaign in Kashmir and has neither released its poll manifesto nor announced its chief ministerial candidate.

JKPCC president Saifuddin Soz who made the announcement said , "Under Azad's leadership, the party will vigorously campaign in all the three regions of the state." Other members of the campaign committee include CWC member Makhan Lal Fotedar, MPs Karan Singh, Lal Singh and Madan Lal, former JK Deputy CM Mangat Ram Sharma, former PCC president Peerzada Sayeed, former ministers, B R Kundal, Taj Mohiuddin and Rigzin Jora. Party sources said that while the campaign committee members would be the Congress's star campaigners, it would also rope in Central leaders for the purpose. The Congress is looking to improve its 2002 election tally of 20 seats in spite of the anti-incumbency factor and the Amarnath land row.

However, the Congress seems to be far behind in its poll preparation, with the PDP already having floated its proposal for self-rule and backing former CM Mufti Mohammed Sayeed as its chief ministerial candidate and the NC nominating Farooq Abdullah its choice for CM.

Heading: LIVING IN THE SHADOWS - Indian Express
Content:
Jharkhand Chief Minister Shibu Soren is all set to launch the state's first commercial pilot training centre in the name of his late father in his constituency Dumka. The Sobran Soren Rashtriya Udan Academy is to be inaugurated by the CM on Monday. "The work related with starting the centre will start from tomorrow," he told the media on Sunday afternoon.

The 500-crore project, conceived by the Arjun Munda-led NDA Government in 2006 and approved by the state cabinet last month, envisages a two-year commercial pilot training course for 160 students, 30 of whom will be from the Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes. They will be given free training.

But there are worries about the additional burden the project is likely to put on the state exchequer. "Anticipating that the Academy would become another white elephant, I had opposed the project. But the state government did not care to listen to me," said a senior IAS officer.

But Secretary (Home) J B Tubid, the brain behind the project, defended the project saying the Academy would have met its objective if it can train 30 pilots from the underprivileged sections of the society every year . "Moreover, by earning from trainee pilots of the privileged sections, the project will become financially viable,"Tubid added.

Heading: Cong, SP agree on Muslim RS candidate - Indian Express
Content:
Abhinav Bharat, the name that once shook the British Government during India's struggle for independence, is now in the news as a radical Hindu outfit, members of which allegedly planned the Malegaon blasts, killing five persons and injuring many on September 29.

The group's working president, trustee, publicist and now a serving Army officer, who "advised" the group's members, are charged, among other things, with hatching a conspiracy, planning terror attacks and also under various sections of the Indian Explosive Act. According to officials at the Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS), the group was started by a historian

with a good "social purpose" but later "hijacked by officials with an Army background".

The website of Abhinav Bharat which was pulled off on October 26 soon after Major (retd) Ramesh Upadhyay was picked up for questioning. The details of the website state that the group was formed in June 2006 at Raigadh fort with the aim of combating terrorism and rebuilding the nation around Bharatiya and Hindu culture.

On the Monday morning when the group had assembled at 7 am at the historic landmark where Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's coronation was held, in the crowd was a Pune-based historian along with Himani Savarkar, the daughter of Gopal Godse, brother of Nathuram Godse who had assassinated Mahatma Gandhi. Her husband was late Ashok Savarkar, the nephew of Veer Savarkar. "The idea then was to revive the organisation which was once floated by freedom fighter and staunch Hindu, Vinayak Damodar Savarkar also known as Veer Savarkar," says Himani.

She is referring to the "secret movement" of 1904, when Abhinav Bharat was a secret society for starting an armed struggle against the British. The act of Abhinav Bharat member Madan Lal Dhingara assassinating a British official Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie in August 1909 inspired revolutionary movements in India. Savarkar dissolved Abhinav Bharat in 1952, saying there was no need for armed struggle in independent India and appealed to the youth to join the Armed Forces for serving the country.

"The idea of the new Abhinav Bharat in the year 2006 when we came together was to generate a sense of patriotism among the youths through non-violent ways like lectures, discussions and exhibitions," adds Himani. Except, since its inception, the group has allegedly charted a new path, a new constitution and new articles, something which Himani feigns ignorance about. After Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, the other states were to follow with the group members creating "awareness by non-violent ways on various social problems and injustice done to Hindus," she adds. "I am not even aware of the group's new website," she says.

The website, which The Indian Express has access to, says the outfit aims to "promote, train, encourage and induct traditional Bharatiyata. Indoctrinate Bharatiya Rashtriyatva in young generation". This new website with the constitution and the group's organisational structure was registered on May 19, 2007. The group's new working president in the website is Major (retd) Ramesh Upadhyay and the group's official address is the same as the residence of the group's trustee, Ajay Eknath Rahirkar.

In the remand application filed in the Nashik chief judicial magistrate court, the ATS has detailed that main accused Sadhvi Pragya Thakur came in touch with Upadhyay and later Sameer Kulkarni, both of them in their capacity as office-bearers of the group. The application further explains the nature of functioning of the group, attributing words like "secret meeting" to some important group meetings in Bhopal and Jabalpur that took place in the early part of the year, where the presence of Purohit was also recorded.

Officials who have questioned Upadhyay allege it was Purohit who had "hijacked" the group, with the prosecution's argument in the open court also being that "it was Purohit who contacted Upadhyay and asked him to meet him".

Purohit has taken the ATS team to Madhya Pradesh, Khandala and to Pune where Rahirkar stays. According to Upadhyay's interrogation, it is Purohit who "advised" the group while the remand application terms Purohit an expert who guided, among other things, a few members of Abhinav Bharat at training camps, including one at the Army's favourite hillock, Sinhagad in Pune. It was Purohit who led the investigation to Rahirkar whose house was the organisation's headquarter.

The officials at ATS who are probing the group's role point out that the story of the September 29 blasts lies in this

"hijacking" of the group's founding principles by the Army officers.

The constitution of the group has details like "Bharatiya armed forces should be reconstructed with Bharatiya traditions and value system and replace words like the defence services with words like armed forces and Ministry of Defence with Ministry of War".

Though Himani adds that in the early days the group was more in the nature of a "social outfit" which never supported violence, a quick look at its membership forms reveals that members were made to sign and abide by "duties handed over by the higher authorities and be under oath to serve Bharat Mata from now onwards, whenever and wherever required". The group's objectives, according to the website, are Swarajya (self-rule), Surajya (welfare state), Suraksha (safety) and Sushanti (peace). The organisation believes in creating shastra (armed) India as a means to achieve its objectives. The organisation describes a Central Hindu Government as its national committee and lists strong views and has separate committees, including one specifically looking at training.

A saffron flag having a golden border, with torch of four flames in golden colour depicting four Vedas, and Vande Mataram as the organisational song and "Jay Bharat" as the organisational greeting became the characteristics of the group.

The induction of retired and serving Army officers was based on the networking of the historian. Later, as the organisation grew, the idea that found root was that the Government has completely failed to tackle Islamic terrorism, and that time had come to encourage Hindu youths to take up arms for combating the problem, states an official who has interrogated Upadhyay.

The website constitution also begins with words: "The situation is deteriorating day by day as far as social, economical and, most importantly, security aspects are concerned...". It adds that "changing demographic patterns to include the marriages of convenience amongst the self-centred political parties have further concretised the already deteriorating situation. This and many other issues pertaining to culture of the country have compelled a group of patriots to join hands and form and generate this movement". The ATS will now have to prove the nature of this movement whose members, they say, held secret meetings, training camps in Pune, Nanded and Sholapur, sourced explosives, funded via the hawala route with Purohit's accounts showing a huge money transfer to the group's treasurer, who in turn gave it to the other accused to source explosives and live cartridges and, worst of all, allegedly also sourced RDX, traces of which were found in 19 forensic proofs from the blast site of Malegaon.
