They feel he will do something for them," Sahani said.

Meanwhile, the MNVS said it supports modernisation processes like installation of electronic meters in taxis and using CNG. Issues like toll taxes, number of licences given, payment for eight years taken at one go and no check later will be raised by MNVS.

"We will follow whatever Raj says. Even if there are protests on the streets, no one will dare touch those vehicles. With the 24-hour centre here and computerised connectivity, we will reach out to all our members at all times," said Haji Mastan Sheikh, chief of MNVS. "We are planning to give insurance to all our members for accidents and damages. Details are still being worked out," he added.

Heading: Channels bank on reruns to avoid pay hike - Indian Express
Content:
The route would have 18 stations from Jacob Circle to Chembur

The Mumbai Metropolitan Regional Development Authority (MMRDA) has formally handed over the Letter of Agreement (LOA) to the consortium led by Larsen & Toubro with Scomi Engineering, a Malaysia-based company, to build the country's first monorail.

The consortium had bagged the contract for the monorail project, from Jacob Circle to Chembur via Wadala, on October 10 but had not received the LOA.

With the LOA being handed over, the work on the monorail is expected to start by January. The monorail project is to being built on a Design-Build-Operate-Transfer (DBOT) basis and is expected to cost around Rs 2,460 crore.

As per the design prepared by the consortium, 18 stations are expected on the 20 km route. The 'straddle' type monorail will not connect the island city to suburbs, but would provide interconnectivity to the existing suburban railway (Mahalaxmi and Lower Parel stations of Western Railway, Curry Road, Dadar and Wadala stations of Central Railway) and forthcoming Metro Rail as part of multimodal transport system.

The 18 proposed stations are Gadge Maharaj Chowk (Jacob Circle), Chinchpokli, Lower Parel (Curry Road), Mint Colony (Lalbaug), Ambedkar Nagar (KEM hospital), Naigaon (Bombay spinning mills), Dadar east (Wadala BEST bus depot), Acharya Atre Nagar (Barkat Ali), Antop Hill, Guru Teg Bahadur Nagar (Sion Koliwada), Wadala depot, Bhakti Park, Mysore colony, Bharat Petroleum, Fertiliser Township, VNP and RC Marg Junction, Chembur railway station.

As per the agreement, the project has to be competed within 30 months. Of this, the first phase (from Jacob Circle to Wadala) would be fully operational in 24 months while the second phase (from Wadala to Chembur via Mahul) would be operational in next 6 months.

Earlier, apart from Larsen & Toubro and Scomi, a consortium led by Reliance Infrastructure with Hitachi (Japan) and Canada-based Bombardier had been short-listed for the project. But Bombardier backed out of the bidding and Reliance-Hitachi consortium was disqualified in the 'technical-bids' process.

Heading: Plan to ease chaos on SV Road - Indian Express
Content:
Broadcasters announce cost-cutting, re-runs of all TV shows save Bigg Boss

In what is turning out to be the worst ever phase for the Indian television industry, starting yesterday, all channels have stopped airing original programming.

This implies that no fresh episodes produced locally will be aired, with the exception of Bigg Boss and only reruns will be telecast. The decision was announced at a press conference attended by the various channel heads on Monday evening.

The decision closely follows the warning letter, dated October 30, issued jointly by the broadcasters — INX Media, Star India, Sahara One Media and Entertainment, Viacom18 Media and NDTV Imagine — to various producers' associations.

The letter stated the channels' refusal to increase production budgets and appealed to cine workers and producers to resume normalcy in work by November 9. Any failure in doing so, the letter said, would result in reruns of all shows thereon. Bigg Boss, however, is an exception for two reasons: the format of the show does not accommodate any such modifications and there are only ten more days for the show to end, said the statement issued by the broadcasters at the meet.

The problem between producers and cine workers has been on for over a month now. On October 1, cine workers went on a four-day strike, which ended after a resolution to reconsider wages was reached. However, the arrangement didn't last long and all of last week had producers shooting only two hours of primetime content while other shows went on reruns.

It is being said that the channels' refusal to meet budget demands is the direct offshoot of the ongoing economic tight-fisting. However, the various heads of producers' associations claim channels are not yet undergoing losses. "The channels are playing a dirty game because they know production houses currently have no choice but to work out a solution with the cine workers' associations. How can they be undergoing a loss if so many producers' payments are still pending?" says T P Agarwal, president, IMPAA.

The cine workers' associations, on the other hand, are unwilling to give up; the previous strike was ended only after they had had the producers sign an agreement to comply with their demands.

The worst affected are the producers. While most are willing to patiently wait it out and abide by whatever the producers' associations decide, some are anxious about the future. Sudhir Sharma, head of Sunshine Media, producers of Miley Jab Hum Tum on Star Plus, says that the new shows have taken a bad hit. "Broadcasters do not begin paying up till 60-90 days after the show premiers. My show is merely 26 episodes-old and currently, with no cash buffer, all expenses and infrastructure of my show are on hold."

According to Agarwal, if their demands are not met with, producers will indulge in free trade and hire outside of the cine workers' associations, defying their treaty.

Heading: Mumbai ‘laid back’ in kicking the butt - Indian Express
Content:
After tunnel idea, 1.5-km road to be now widened

Commuters fuming during traffic snarls from S V Road at Ville-Parle to Milan subway can look forward to smoother rides soon.

With the earlier plan for a tunnel beneath Juhu Aerodrome runway being shelved, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation is now going to widen the road. The civic road department has proposed widening of the 1.5-km stretch from V M Road and S V Road junction at Ville Parle to Milan Subway till the Link Road. The existing width is 90 feet and BMC proposes to make it 120 feet.

It now takes more than 45 mintues during peak hours to cover the stretch. "We are proposing widening of S V Road," said chief engineer (roads) D L Shinde. "After the tunnel project, this is the most viable option." The civic administration studied the feasibility of the road widening project after frequent complaints from MLAs and commuters about the traffic chaos. "The widening is feasible. We will have to acquire some land from private owners and maybe the civil aviation depatrment," Shinde said. The V M Road-S V Road junction stretch will be extended over Rasraj nullah passing through civil aviation property till Santacruz bus depot. "The road will be constructed above the nullah without obstructing it," an official said.

And from Milan subway to the Link Road, land will be acquired for the project. The proposal will soon be put up with municipal commissioner Jairaj Phatak so that meetings with civil aviation officials can begin soon and work taken up by next year.

Earlier, MMRDA, under the Mumbai Urban Infrastructure Project (MUIP) had proposed a Link Road from Santa Cruz to JVPD with a 3-km tunnel under Juhu Airport. The Airports Authority of India denied permission citing security reasons.

Officials said as per the original plan Juhu Tara road was to be partially closed and traffic from Link Road diverted through the tunnel. MMRDA officials said the AAI opposed it and therefore the project was shelved. "To ease traffic, BMC will have to come up with new plans," said chief engineer (roads), MMRDA, S R Nandargikar.

Heading: Separate employment centre, modernised mills for mill workers, kin - Indian Express
Content:
Over a month after the much hyped smoking ban was introduced in the country, the figures point out that Mumbai has lagged behind in imposing the ban. The officials could collect only a meagre amount of Rs 25,000 from 290 persons in the city.

Saying that not just Mumbai but the whole state is 'laid back' in implementing the ban, officials from the Union Health Ministry said that states like Jharkhand, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and even Gujarat have shown far more enthusiasm than Maharashtra to enforce the ban.

According to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), none of the newly appointed inspectors, even in the government sector, have contributed to the fine collection.

In charge of the 'no-smoking' programme and director, public health, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Dr Vinayak Prasad, said, "Maharashtra is faring badly since there is a lack of interest and initiative among people, administrators and even doctors."

However, according to the FDA officials, the figures have shown improvement in comparison with last two years' collection. "In just two months, we managed to collect the double of whatever we could have in last two years," said Dhanraj Kamatkar, commissioner, Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Maharashtra. From August to October, FDA food inspectors collected Rs 4.5 lakh as compared to Rs 2.5 lakh in 2004- 2007 in the state.

According to the recent amendment, police officials, municipal corporation officials, railway stationmasters, postal officers, medical superintendents at private and public hospitals, heads of institutions, HR managers of private firms, college and school principals, airport managers, directors of public health and library officials along with excise inspectors, gazetted officers of state and central governments are all empowered to restrict smoking in their areas and collect fine from violators.

Unaware of who's the nodal officer for the programme, BMC says it's collecting the fine. "Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's public health department has collected Rs 5,000 from the violators in the city. We have put it in BMC treasury since we don't know the nodal officer for the programme. But more than smoking habits, it's the habit chewing tobacco that needs to be tackled," said Dr Jairaj Thanekar, executive health officer, BMC's health department.

Though Newsline tried to contact Joint Police Commissioner K L Prasad for his comment on the issue, he was not available.

"The law was already in place since 2004 and the new officials authorised to fine the offenders have been identified in the recent amendment to the law," said Mohan Patankar, joint commissioner, food department, FDA.

"The second amendment— pictorial warning on cigarette packets— will be implemented by end of November," he said.

Lack of awareness in both urban and rural areas, especially among those who are authorised to collect fine, acts as a barrier in enforcing the ban.

"It's very difficult to fine offenders as they question our authority to do so. Even police do not come to our help," said Patankar.

There're only 10 food inspectors in FDA to carry out inspection in Mumbai. "There are 260 food inspectors in Maharashtra and only last year 100 posts were filled," he said.

"After a meeting in the month of August, we intensified the drive. The nation-wide drive has created awareness in a big way," said Patankar.

Heading: MHCC gives nod to renovation of members’ enclosure at RWITC - Indian Express
Content:
The Maharashtra government has decided to closely monitor the modernisation of mills and form a separate employment exchange centre to provide jobs to millworkers and their family members in industries or offices set up on the mill land.

"We have received about 39,000 applications for jobs from millworkers and their children," principal secretary, urban development department, T C Benjamin said. "The list of eligible persons would be finalised after the concerned millowner checks each and every case and certifies the eligibility. The final list would be displayed by December 5," he added.

Benjamin further said a separate employment exchange centre would be created by the government exclusively for millworkers and their family members in the diversified industries coming up on the mill land.

At the meeting held at Mantralaya on Monday, chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh asked officials to examine modernisation proposals and monitor whether millowners were following the norms. Accordingly, officials are to visit four mills against which complaints have been received. The officials are expected to submit their report in two weeks.

Deshmukh instructed officials against giving permission for modernisation to any millowner until all dues of workers are paid.

The government has evolved a scheme whereby millowners are expected to train millworkers rendered jobless and provide placements in new offices or businesses coming up on the mill-land. The state has imposed a condition that preference should be given to millworkers and their children in jobs in new ventures on mill sites.

The four mills which are under scanner of the government are Prakash Mills, Ruby Mills and two units of Bombay Dyeing. According to official records, the four mills have not handed over 39,000 square metres of land out of 50,000 square metres that was to be given to Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) as per norms.

Jobs for displaced millworkers are likely to be streamlined by February 2009, according to Benjamin.

Heading: 24-year-old dies in accident at Lokhandwala - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Heritage Conservation Committee (MHCC) has given an 'in-principle' approval to the Royal Western India Turf Club's (RWITC) plan of restoring the members' enclosure, while asking the club to stick to the original design and style and make no alterations that contradict the 'heritage feel'.

The committee has said utmost care should be taken for fire safety. The stands at the RWITC were gutted twice in three months time. The MHCC, which met on Monday, gave an 'in-principle' approval to the RWITC's revamp plan. Chairman of the committee, Dinesh Afzalpurkar, said the RWITC has been given the permission, subject to certain conditions.

"They had suggested a number of minor changes which were different from the original heritage structure and failed to portray the old charm. We have told them to stick to the original style and grandeur of the structure and ruled out any new changes," he said.

The top two levels of the RWITC members' enclosure were gutted in fires that broke out on July 3 and September 18, respectively. The stand has a seating capacity of 300 people and has been built over an area of 826.49 sq m.

Afzalpurkar said while the original structure has not remained fireproof after the two fires, it was important to ensure that the structure is made fireproof again. "The façade should be fireproof and all the fire safety rules should be followed," he added. The racing season, which was to start on November 16, has been now postponed to mid-January due to illness of horses.

Vivek Jain, chairman of the marketing and media committee, RWITC, said the club will follow the committee's recommendations. "Work will begin as soon as the civic Building Proposal department gives the approval for the restoration," he said.

Heading: State may waive VAT for housing projects - Indian Express
Content:
A youth was killed in an accident near Lokhandwala Circle on Sunday after a car collided with his motorcycle while taking a turn. The incident took place when Sahil Desai (24) was returning to his residence in Shastri Nagar with his brand new Comet motorcycle, and Mona Gowda(31), who was coming from the opposite direction, took a turn to enter her residence in Royal Empire.

Her Skoda Octavia collided with Desai's bike right outside her building's gate, following which he fell and hit his head on the road. Since he was not wearing a helmet, he received serious head injuries and also fractured his leg.

Gowda immediately rushed him to Cooper Hospital Irla where he succumbed to his injuries while being treated. The Versova police have registered a case of rash and negligent driving against Gowda and she was produced in court for custody on Monday.

"The lady has been charged with rash and negligent driving," said Senior Police Inspector Suresh Nalavade of Versova Police station. "Had she ignored her civic duty and not rushed him to the hospital she would have been in more trouble. But I must mention that the boy's chances of survival would have been much better had he worn a helmet," added Nalavade.

Desai was returning with his friend Yash Shah (20) after picking up his new bike. Shah, who was riding behind him on another bike, was not injured though he has witnessed the accident and was the complainant in the case against Gowda. Desai's father Rasik Desai owns an ice factory in Saki Naka. None of the family members, however, was willing to comment.

Mona Gowda lives in an 11th-floor flat in Royal Empire with her husband for the last 6-7 months and her husband works in a mining company in Goa. The couple could not be contacted for comment as both of them were in court on Monday.

Heading: City sees hot days, cool nights due to easterly winds - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on Monday said that the state government is planning to scrap Value Added Tax(VAT) for the housing projects. Addressing the 'Advantage Maharashtra Convention on Housing for All' organised by the Maharashtra Chamber of Housing Industries (MCHI) at NCPA in south Mumbai, he said that the decision was taken following requests from real estate developers.

Since new house is just like any other manufactured product, the sales tax department had proposed a 5 per cent VAT on new flats in 2006, a move that was opposed by builders. "VAT should not be applicable for housing projects as such a tax will never bring affordable houses to consumers," said Deshmukh and added that his government would soon work on removing VAT on property purchase.

Pointing out that there was a deficit of 27 billion houses in India at the end of the 10th five year plan, Deshmukh said that the year 2009 would be the housing year in Maharashtra. "Over the next two years, we will be constructing 10 lakh houses," he said. According to the state housing department, these projects would include houses generated through schemes under Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority, National Urban Renewal Mission, Indira Awas Yogna, Nivara Yojana and the Slum Rehabilitation Authority.

Asked about introducing the much-delayed housing regulatory commission draft bill in the assembly, Deshmukh said it may be a while before the state government imposed regulatory mechanism on the real estate industry. "There are a few issues that need to be sorted out," he said without elaborating on the issues.

Housing Secretary Sitaram Kunte explained that following requests that the draft bill be opened up for public discussion, it has been sent to the speaker of the assembly for his approval.

Urging developers to come up with cost-effective ways to facilitate affordable housing, Deshmukh asked them to build houses for the common man drawing a parallel with the Nano car manufactured by the Tatas.

Deshmukh also agreed to extend policy decisions such as the recent hike in Floor Space Index (FSI) from 1 to 1.33 in Mumbai to the entire state. Another Mumbai-specific policy that will be made applicable to the entire state is the September 2008 government decision to allow IT parks — which enjoy higher FSI— to utilise 80 per cent of the total constructed area for financial services and banks.

Heading: Rainwater harvesting only option after water cut by BMC - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai, over the last few days, has been experiencing unusual weather: while temperatures soar during the daytime, nights are pleasantly cool, with gentle breeze blowing occasionally.

While only January and February are considered to be winter months in Mumbai, according to the Indian Metrological Department (IMD), these kinds of weather features are typical in November, K Sathidevi, director of IMD Mumbai said. She pointed out, "Scorching day temperatures and cool night temperatures are common during this season due to the influx of easterly and north-easterly winds."

She explained, "Being a coastal city, Mumbai sees a lot of sea breeze. While this breeze ¿ which is moist and cool in nature — is responsible for high humidity, it also keeps the temperature low." She further added, "Easterly winds, which are dry landward winds, take over in November. When easterlies blow into the city, the coastal breeze is pushed back, delaying its setting-in. This is a reason why the day temperatures soar."

On the other hand, a considerable drop in the night temperatures is also an outcome of this weather feature, she said. "These easterly winds are dry and naturally cool and faster than moist winds. That is exactly why, as night falls, the temperatures drop" Sathidevi said.

On Monday, the maximum temperatures were a few degrees above normal while the minimum a degree below normal. Colaba recorded a maximum temperature of 34.2 degrees and Santacruz 35.2 degrees. The minimum temperatures recorded at Colaba and Santacruz were 22.2 degrees and 19.2 degrees Celsius respectively.

The relative humidity too was pleasantly low at 84 per cent and 51 per cent in Colaba and Santacruz respectively.

Sathidevi pointed out that the normal temperatures for this month is 33 degrees during daytime and 20 degrees at night. The IMD has, meanwhile, predicted that the temperatures will remain stable between 35 degrees and 19 degrees Celsius till Wednesday.

Heading: BMC proposes medical college at Cooper Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Move may force builders to go green; but there are glitches, admits civic body

The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's (BMC) latest move of cutting down water supply to new buildings might have left several Mumbaiites into a tizzy, but rainwater harvesting can be the answer to the impending water crisis for builders and residents. In fact, many in realty business admit the move may force builders to adopt the green route.

In rainwater harvesting, the rainwater that falls on rooftops is collected and stored in tanks, trenches, borewells, etc. In 2002, the BMC had made it mandatory for the new buildings having a plot area of 1,000 square meters to have rainwater harvesting facility. By 2007, the same provision became mandatory to buildings having a plot area of 300 square meters and above.

By that notion, the civic officials state, all the new constructions should invariably have this facility. However, the BMC statistics reveal a very low figure. According to the records available at the civic body's rainwater harvesting cell, till 2007 only 171 new buildings have adopted the facility.

The BMC maintains that both awareness campaigns and stricter rules have proved futile. "Since 2002 we have adopted a stricter rule in this regards. Any building proposal is cleared only when they have made facilities for this (rainwater harvesting) technique. Otherwise, the occupational certificate (OC) is not given to the builder," said assistant engineer of BMC's rainwater harvesting cell, Suprabha Marathe.

But the real problem, Marathe says, is that many builders have the facility only symbolically. "Sometimes builders have the plan on paper but they never implement it. There are three different entities when it comes to any building —builder, architects and residents. Though the onus lies on the builder to implement the facility, unfortunately occupants are of the law and never question the builder," Marathe said.

The main problem the BMC faces is in implementing and monitoring the law properly, she says. "In other cities, rainwater harvesting has succeeded immensely as the residents hold the builders answerable. This makes even their municipal bodies to take active participation. Unless, we have an active monitoring body, the rule will never be successful in the city," Marathe said.

Keeping in mind the mushrooming constructions in the suburbs, the BMC has decided to cut down the supply of water from the present 90 litres to 45 litres per person per day. This is also for only those buildings whose demand is less than 2 lakh litres per day.

However, many builders believe BMC's new decision will compel builders to take the green route. Suresh Gadekar, project manager of the Supreme Builders which is coming up with a seven-floor building in Charkop, says: "We have installed an open terrace rainwater-harvesting system. We have also installed storm water drains and percolation tanks on the ground. These facilities will help the residents here deal with water shortage." Gadekar adds that "the BMC's decision will force many builders to adopt "green" construction. Praful Kanajoia, manager, Kalapataru Properties, which has residential and retail projects coming up in Kandivili, Andheri and Thane, says they installed the facility in all their buildings even before the civic body came up with the rule. "We have installed borewells and underground rainwater tanks in all our buildings. Considering the looming water crisis, this is the only way to properly utilise and save BMC-supplied water," Kanajoia said.

Meanwhile, BMC also plans to go ahead with retrofitting projects in existing buildings. "We are asking old and existing societies to adopt rainwater harvesting. Though many people are yet to warm up to the idea, the cost factor is also a major deterrent. They don't realise money is only spent in the initial stage. Despite our best efforts to spread awareness, people still have reservations," said Marathe.

Environmentalists also opine that rainwater harvesting is a feasible option. "With rainwater harvesting underground water can be easily pumped. Also since our city gets good monsoon, this is a good way to utilise the rainwater. Moreover, it also helps in reducing flooding remarkably," said Vishal Bhanushali, an engineer with Eureka Forbes Institute of environment.

Heading: Civic body plans Rs 100 for anti-rabies vaccine, health dept says it’s ‘mistake’ - Indian Express
Content:
To help ease burden on crumbling civic hospital infrastructure

The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation has proposed a new medical college at the Dr RN Cooper Hospital. This is in addition to the existing three medical colleges in the city. While 100 medical students will receive admission, the college will also help ease the burden on the present crumbling civic hospital infrastructure.

The civic standing committee on Monday approved the proposal for setting up the medical college and post-graduation courses for training at the Cooper Hospital in Vile Parle (west).

The Rs 10 core project will now be tabled before the state government and then will be placed before the Medical Council of India (MCI)for final approval.

As many as 100 students will get admission annually once the college starts and around 100 lecturers, professors and associate professors will be also be appointed to teach the students. Cooper Hospital has a capacity of 520 beds and fulfills the terms and conditions of the Indian Medical Council to start a medical college with a potential to admit 100 students for MBBS.

From the current set-up, both Shatabdi Hospital at Kandivli and Cooper Hospital were meeting the requirements to setup the medical college and accordingly the civic administration has proposed the name of the latter. An FSI of four will be provided for the construction of the new college on an area of 5,000 sq metres.

Mumbai is the only city to have its own set-up of tertiary civic hospitals and medical colleges. KEM, Nair and Sion are the premier hospitals with established medical colleges in the city area, however in the suburban zone there is not a single medical college, the civic administration has observed.

Considering the shortage of medical infrastructure in the city- government, public and private- BMC feels rightfully there is a need of a medical college keeping in mind the increase in population twenty-years later.

Heading: Revolvers stolen from businessmen’s homes - Indian Express
Content:
A 'mistake' by civic officials may cost you Rs 100 to get the vital anti-rabies vaccine in case of a dog bite. While the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's (BMC) standing committee approved a proposal that makes the patients pay for the vaccine, its health department said that there was some 'goof-up' and it had no intention to do so. The vaccine is provided for free to the patients for last two years.

Executive Health Officer Dr Jairaj Thanekar said that the health department had planned to withdraw the proposal from the standing committee. "We're investigating how the proposal got tabled in the committee. It's definitely an administrative mistake and the matter will be sorted after a meeting with senior officials in a fortnight," he said.

Earlier, an amount of Rs 30 was collected from the patients for the vaccine, but it had been made free at all civic hospitals for last two years. The civic administration felt that some amount should be collected from patients as the cost of the vaccine had shot to Rs 286. "Every patient has to take at least five vaccines. Thus, around Rs 1500 is spent for every patient, so it was proposed that instead of providing it for free, an amount of Rs 100 per vaccine should be collected," said Dr Thanekar. The BMC in its budget allocates Rs 4 crore for the ARV to treat around 50,000 dog bites annually. In 2006, the civic administration had tabled a proposal at the public health committee meeting, however, uproar from members and corporators led to its withdrawal. Meanwhile, municipal commissioner had also given his recommendations that the vaccine should be provided free of cost.

On Monday, a contradictory proposal, comprising a request to charge Rs 100 from patients and commissioner's report that vaccines should be given free was tabled in the standing committee and was even approved by the members.

Committee chairman and Shiv Sena leader Ravindra Waikar said the committee had approved the commissioner's report. Committee members said the proposal would be reopened once again for discussion and the civic administration would be told to withdraw it. Sena member Rahul Shewale said the stray dog menace was created by people, so why the sufferers should be charged for the vaccine. In next meeting, the proposal will be reopened again, he added.

Heading: Caution: Dempo ahead - Indian Express
Content:
Two .32-bore revolvers — one with five live cartridges and another with 3 live cartridges — have been stolen from the houses of an Oshiwara-based businessman and an Agripada-based businessman respectively. Cases of theft have been registered in Oshiwara and Agripada police stations.

The Oshiwara-based businessman, Prakash Chawla (40), alleged that his revolver was stolen around the end of September, while the Agripada-based businessman, Altaf Patel (45) alleged that his revolver was stolen from his house on Sunday. Both revolvers were licensed and were allegedly stolen by men who were working on reparation and renovation of the houses.

Chawla had last seen his revolver on September 26, when he was putting it in his cupboard. Unable to open his cupboard, he kept it in his bathroom and left in a hurry. He believed his wife had put it in his cupboard and didn't give it another thought since he had to go abroad during the period between the theft and his complaint. On returning from abroad, he found his revolver missing and registered a complaint.

"We are interrogating the people who were doing work in his house," said Police Inspector (crime) Dattatray Sankhe of Oshiwara police station. "It is definitely one of them as there was no case of a housebreaking in his flat," he added.

In the Agripada case, DCP Zone 3 Ashok Deshbradar said, "We have arrested one man who was working in the house of Patel and will be producing him in the court for custody and will take the case forward."

Heading: Chembur Kreeda, Shri Sai in final - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai FC coach David Booth not taking out-of-form defending champions lightly

Coach David Booth counsels some old-fashioned caution when Mumbai FC run into a stuttering Dempo at the Cooperage on Tuesday. The English coach of the city side doesn't put it beyond the defending champions - languishing ninth on the table currently - to strike good form when playing their Round 7 encounter against the hosts, presently plateauing 4th on the table. "They'll come good for sure. I'm just hoping it's not against us tomorrow," Booth quipped ahead of what will be a scrappy affair on the dodgy Cooperage patch.

Ahmed Felix Aboagy suffered a thigh strain heading into the breather against Vasco over the weekend. And it was evident from the way Mumbai FC lost the plot thereafter and had to be content with 1-1 scoreline against the bottom-placed side, that the forward's absence is acutely felt. "He's trained a little today, but we'll see him in the morning and decide. It was apparent that we struggled after he went out," Booth said.

Still, approaching the quarterway-stage of the league, it is perhaps the best time to run into holders Dempo for the hosts. "It's probably a good time to pin them down and for our players to pull up their socks otherwise we'll be swamped," Booth adds. But after a fine start to their I-League campaign, Mumbai FC have stumbled in their path - twice conceding goals from set-pieces, and another two times from passes from inside their own half. "I'm a little disappointed about our last two games, where mistakes have cost us points. And it's a case of not being at our best, giving away poor goals," the coach says.

Dempo, too come into the game - a tad fatigued from their cluttered schedule. "My players are not machines and the lack of rest is showing," says coach Armando Colaco. After their poor start, last year's champions have struggled to string together two wins on a trot, and are looking to get their fluent form going. "We are playing three matches within the span of eight days, it is tough on us. There is lot of traveling which doesn't allow the players to recuperate," Colaco adds.

But Colaco is not unduly hassled by the Goan team's recent losses against Sporting Club de Goa (0-1) and Mohun Bagan (0-1). "I know my boys. We just need one win and they will be back on top of the table. Even when we made our debut in 2001, we finished fifth but that motivated us to do well and make a good comeback to top of the table," he says hopefully.

Colaco marks out striker Abhishek Yadav and goalkeeper Kalyan Choubey as the key men, even as his own ranks are depleted with defender Mahesh Gawli and Clifford Miranda being doubtful starters for the tie - Miranda having to consult Dr Anant Joshi after a feared ligament tear.

Heading: Venkatraman sole leader after sixth round - Indian Express
Content:
Favourites Air-India continued their winning streak in the ongoing MHA league at BHA stadium with a thumping 7-1 win over ONGC, after leading 2-1 at half-time. The oilmen suffered their first loss in six matches, albeit a comprehensive one against the fancied airmen on Monday.

Amit Bharadwaj deflected a cross from close range to put ONGC ahead. But the airmen, led by Dhanraj Pillay struck within six minutes, qith Sumeet Singh finding the equaliser through an indirect penalty corner conversion. In another six minutes, the airmen went into the lead, with Pillay relaying a through ball pass to youngster Yuvraj Walmiki on the right of the semicircle as Walmiki complimented the move by clinically sneaking in a goal from an acute angle.

On resumption, ONGC looked totally off-colour and allowed their rivals to pump in five more goals. Sumeet Singh hogged the limelight for the airmen as he tallied four goals in the 21st, 38th, 60th and 69th minutes, while Dhanraj Pillay struck another in the 42nd - Sameer dad completing the score in the 52nd.

Heading: Chatterati - Indian Express
Content:
Subodh Gupta brings together 30 artists to contribute towards relief work in Bihar and Orissa through an auction
RELIEF WORK: (Above) Gupta; Anju Dodiya's work

The art mart may be going through a low phase with the economic recession affecting the prices of canvases but Subodh Gupta is convinced that when it comes to contributing to a good cause, the money will come in.

"The market conditions may not be the best but the needy can't wait," says the Delhi-based artist as he readies for the Saffronart Artists Flood Relief Auction, organised to collect funds for flood victims in Orissa and Bihar. While the initiative came from Gupta and wife Bharti Kher, chipping in for the online auction that will take place today and tomorrow are a total of 31 artists, each of whom has donated a canvas.

"No one has charged anything and there are no artist cuts. Every penny will be directed towards relief," states Gupta, who has decided to direct the proceeds to two NGOs, Samajik Shaikshanik Vikas Kendra and Goonj.

"I would have liked to visit the affected areas myself, but don't think that will be as beneficial. I would rather contribute through art," says Gupta.

He has been working towards the auction for a month and has managed to get together an impressive range of art which includes Atul Dodiya's watercolour on paper titled Proust from the 'Pale Ancestors' series, Riyas Komu's 2008 oil on canvas titled Uttara II and TV Santhosh's untitled watercolour on paper.

While Ranbir Singh Kaleka's oil on wood titled Man with Torch has an estimate price of Rs 30- 40 lakh, Bharti Kher's bindis on board titled This Way and Never Another Way is estimated to fetch 45-65 lakh. The highest bid, however, is expected for Gupta's untitled oil on canvas, which has an estimate price of Rs 90 lakh to 1.2 crore.

While the artist is uncertain about the total proceeds that he will manage through the auction, Dinesh Vazirani, founder of Saffronart, is hopeful of collecting between Rs 3 to 4 crore for the NGOs. "The cause should act as a driving factor. We are looking forward to bids from the world over," he smiles. And the collectors get great art in return.

Heading: Qayamuddin’s family refuses to comment on his arrest - Indian Express
Content:
It's business as usual at the art auctions,even if bidding is half the price

Art will not depreciate the way other assets have." These words from auctioneer Vikram Bachhawat, of Emami Chisel, reflect the sentiments of many auction houses that are braving the economic recession and going ahead with plans to auction art.

"The new breed of collectors who were in it just for the money will not be buying art just for the profits," he adds. The auction showcasing artists like Amrita Sher-Gil, M F Husain (Rs 4.4 crore) and Bikash Bhattacharya (Rs 45-50 lakh) have an international market and online bidding enables them to reach out beyond geographical boundaries. "Artists will never depreciate the way shares and stocks have," insists the auctioneer.

Recently, Saffronart had artist Subodh Gupta, whose canvases have been fetching nothing less than Rs 4-5 crore, down for the preview of the charity auction they are planning.

"Since the financial crisis, there haven't been dedicated

Indian auctions. However the charity auction is for a cause and going to flood-relief victims so one cannot really say how our December auctions will go," says Dinesh Vazirani of Saffronart.

With the Christie's Hong Kong auction lined up for the end of November, Sotheby's has an upcoming auction of Indian maps and books, and Emami Chisel closed its auction this month, one can assume that business will go on, even if at half the price.

Both Christie's and Sotheby's held autumn print auctions in London last week and the results were illuminating. Christie's sold about 55 per cent of its lots, and Sotheby's was over 60 per cent.

"With these two big auction houses selling at lower prices than estimated, it's bound to affect the Indian market. While galleries are holding their price, global art market and the interest in Indian art has not declined, we can assume that prices are going to be slashed no matter what," adds Vazirani.

The Serpentine Gallery at London's Hyde Park is having a show of Contemporary Indian artists and Gupta still wields clout at the auctions. We can all look out for the market slowdown but it is now about "Collectors and not investors".

Heading: HC defers hearing on Gujcoc bill till Dec 10 - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of Bagh-e-chishtiya in the Wadi area of the city — where the alleged Ahmedabad and Delhi serial mastermind, Qayamuddin Kapadia, lived before he went missing — have refused to comment on his arrest.

Vadodara Detection of Crime Branch Inspector K M Polra said his brother, Rafiuddin, was arrested one-and-a-half months ago for stabbing a person and there are cases of fake stamps pending against him.

"Rafiuddin is now in the Vadodara Central Jail as he was arrested in September for knifing one person and causing him grievous injury. During interrogation, we found that that he was also making fake rubber stamps," said Polra.

He, however, refused to comment whether Rafiuddin arrest and subsequent interrogation led to Qayamuddin's arrest. Interestingly, police officers also added that before the Madhya Pradesh Police came looking for Qayamuddin, when he had fled from the city, he was working in his brother's rubber stamp business at a shop in Nagarwada.

Rafiuddin, the police said, also ran a tyre business in Nagarwada.

While, Qayamuddin's family was not available for comment on the arrest of Qayamuddin on Monday, one of the neighbours, on condition of anonymity said, that before Qayamuddin escaped, he had estranged relations with his family. After Safdar Nagori's arrest in March, Qayamuddin's family was reportedly questioned by the Ahmedabad Crime Branch.

Heading: Naroda Gam riot case accused seek narco test - Indian Express
Content:
Additional Solicitor General informed the court that the Union Cabinet is considering the matter

A division bench of the Gujarat High Court comprising Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Aqil Qureshi on Monday deferred the hearing on a petition imploring that Gujarat Control of Organised Crime Bill, 2003, passed by the State Assembly be forwarded by the Central Government to the President of India.

The hearing was postponed till December 10 after Additional Solicitor General Harin Raval informed the court that the Union Cabinet was considering the matter.

The matter was filed in the court in 2006 on behalf of NGO Justice on Trial represented by Justice (Retd) S M Soni.

Earlier, pleading before the court, advocate Tushar Mehta representing the NGO had stated that the state needed a strong anti-terror law following the recent serial bomb blasts. He contended that if states such as neighbouring Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka could have anti-terror laws why the Centre was not recommending Gujcoc to the President of India.

He had pleaded that it was for the President to approve or disapprove the Bill and the Centre could not hold it.

The Gujcoc bill passed by the State Assembly has been pending with the central Government since 2003. While the ruling BJP in the state has been insisting for approval of the Bill by the President and recently it also staged a sit-in agitation after the July serial bomb blasts, Congress, several human rights groups and NGOs in the state have been vehemently opposing it pleading that the BJP wanted to use it to harass and intimidate minorities, particularly Muslims.

Those who oppose Gujcoc, cite the examples of misuse of Prevention of Terrorism Act and Terrorist And Disruptive Activities (Prevention) acts by the BJP government against Muslims in the past. According to them, all the persons booked under POTA in the state have been Muslims and none of those involved in mass massacre of Muslims were booked under this law.

Heading: Two fall to death in freak accidents - Indian Express
Content:
They allege of having been implicated, and that the witnesses bore false testimony

Apprehensive about being 'implicated' on the basis of 'false' statements of the victims of the Naroda Gam rioting of 2002, four accused in the case have sought permission for narco-analysis tests to be conducted on them and the witnesses in order to 'bring out the truth'.

Residents of Naroda Gam, Vasudev Patel, Bhupendra Thakur, Ashok Panchal and Pramukh Patel had made this rare request in an application filed with the Special Investigation Team (SIT) office in Gandhinagar on Friday.

They had alleged that the witnesses had given false statements against them due to ulterior motives. They were, however, arrested on Sunday night and later produced before a local court on Monday.

The Supreme Court-appointed SIT, which has been investigating the Naroda Gam rioting case, arrested the four on charges of murder, conspiracy, rioting and arson.

"The arrests were made after their names opened up during our investigation in the case," said P L Mal, the Deputy Superintendent of Police, SIT.

About the four seeking narco tests on them and the witnesses, Mal said: "They were arrested on the basis of evidence we had against them and there is no need to conduct the narco test right now."

The Sunday arrest was the fourth set of arrests by the SIT during the re-investigation of the Naroda Gam rioting under Supreme Court instructions. Bajrang Dal leader Babu Bajrangi had allegedly led the mob that had butchered 11 people on February 28, 2002, when the Vishwa Hindu Parishad had called for a statewide bandh protesting against the death of 59 kar sevaks in the ill-fated Sabarmati Express a day earlier.

Heading: Ratatouille: SSNNL Dam metal detectors fall prey to rat bite - Indian Express
Content:
In a freak accident, an 11-year-old boy from Vapi fell to his death from the seventh floor of a prominent hotel in Usmanpura on Ashram Road. The mishap took place around 7 pm, when the victim, Ahad Saiyed, was playing in the hotel corridor.

According to Naranpura police, Ahad happened to topple out of an opening on one side of the long corridor while he was playing. "The boy fell over a porch before hitting the ground," police said.

A profusely bleeding Ahad was rushed to V S Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment.

Naranpura police have registered a complaint of accidental death. Police said that Ahad was staying on the seventh floor of the hotel with his family. The Vapi-based business family had checked into the hotel four days ago and were on vacation.

In an unrelated case, a 40-year-old labourer, Krishna Gop, fell to his death from the eighth floor of an under-construction building near Prahlad Nagar in Satellite. The incident took place on Monday morning when a Jharkhand-based Gop was working there. Satellite police have registered a complaint of accidental death and are investigating the case.

Heading: In the name of honour: Family kills daughter for eloping with lover - Indian Express
Content:
Radio mechanics at the dam discovered that rats had entered the wooden frame of the detectors and chomped on the wires

In A major security breach, metal detectors installed at the Sardar Sarovar Dam at Kevadia Colony have stopped functioning after rats nibbled the wires damaging the circuit of the equipment.

According to sources, rats have damaged the circuits of the Door Frame Metal Detector (DFM) near SSNNL Dyke number-1.

Police personnel posted at the Sardar Sarovar Dam have said that at present, two of the DFMs installed at SSNNL, are not functioning. One of them is near SSNNL Dyke number-1 and the other is at SSNNL River Bed Power House (RBPH), where the DFM has stopped functioning for the last two months.

Police men said that the damage occurred after rats entered the metal frame. "The radio-mechanics employed by SSNNL found out that there were problems in the wiring system. Now, the entire wooden circuit had to be installed again. We are trying to coordinate with the Ankleshawar-based 'Encode' security agency over this," said a police officer.

Police personnel deployed at Kevadia Colony have also affirmed that they are using 11 hand-held metal detectors to check on the visitors at the tourist site.

This is not the first time though, that rats have damaged the security apparatus at the Sardar Sarovar dam and its canal network. Earlier, following the canal breach at Mehsana, the dam authorities had admitted to a Right to Information (RTI) query that rodents were affecting the canal network at places, leading to breaches and issues of maintenance along with other factors.

Incidentally, SSNNL Chief Engineer K J Trivedi has said that there are no loopholes in the security. "The security is alert and all the DFM's are functioning," he has said.

Meanwhile, an SSNNL official said on condition of anonymity: "Though we have hand-held metal detectors, at times it becomes difficult to manage huge crowds at the dam."

Citing the recent Diwali festival, police officers also said: "It became difficult for us to manage a huge chunk of visitors during the Diwali festival when all the guest houses at SSNNL were packed with visitors from the neighbouring districts. Besides, the door frame metal detectors are expensive and the only way to make it functional is to replace the entire circuit."

Narmada Superintendent of Police Khurshid Ahmed said: "We have hand-held metal detectors on a temporary basis. While, permission has been given to install CCTVs, SSNNL is yet to make the purchases."

The executive committee comprising the sub-divisional magistrate, Narmada superintendent of police and SSNNL chief engineer was formed around three months ago, and various plans about installing Closed Circuit Televisions (CCTV) were floated.

Heading: 3 killed, two injured in hit-and-run case - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty-year-old Smita Patel had no inkling about the tragic end that was awaiting her when she accepted the invitation of her parents to visit them with her husband and in-laws.

Two months ago, she had eloped with Manish Patel of Umarala village, much to the chagrin of her family. On Sunday, Smita's family took their revenge by killing her in cold blood to keep their honour intact.

The incident took place at Machiyala village, some 10 kilometres from Junagadh. The police have arrested Smita's parents and elder sister while her two brothers are absconding.

According to the Junagadh taluka police, on November 9 Smita's father, Keshu Patel, had invited her, Manish and his parents to their home to settle the issue happily and end the rivalry between the two families.

On Sunday morning, Smita went to her parental home with her husband and in-laws. Around 10.30 am, Keshu called Smita to a separate room where he, his sons Praful and Vithal, wife Rama and elder daughter Manisha pounced on her with knives and other weapons en masse.

Smita's husband Manish tried to intervene, but could not save her. Manish somehow managed to escape and went straight to the police station. After recording his statement, the police immediately rushed to the village where they found that the victim's body had been taken to the village crematorium to perform the last rites.

Without wasting time, the police rushed to the crematorium, where they found that the pyre had already been lit.

The fire brigade was immediately called in to extinguish the fire. The police recovered Smita's half-burnt body and dispatched it to Jamnagar for post mortem after conducting the preliminary inquest.

Upon Manish's complaint, the police registered a case under Sections 320, 129(B), 114, 342, 397, and 201 of the IPC. Besides, the victim's kin and the accused in this incident, Keshu Patel, Rama and Manisha, have been arrested.

On Monday, the accused were produced before a Junagadh court. The police have sought their remand, but the court's order is awaited.

Meanwhile, Sub-Inspector B V Gohil said that the hunt is on to nab the absconding brothers of the victim.

Heading: Senior Dalit Congress leader to quit party - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 20 boys and girls, all probably drunk, were accompanying in an Alto and four bikes and fled the place

In A major hit and run case, three people were killed and two were injured when a speeding Maruti Swift car ran over them in Shilaj village on the outskirts of Ahmedabad on Sunday night.

The five were sitting on a bench near a tea-stall at Kalhar Patiya before going to guard their farms nearby, when the car mowed them down.

The Sarkhej police have registered a case of death caused by negligence against the unidentified car driver. Two empty bottles of alcohol were recovered from the newly purchased car that did not even have a registration number.

Sub-Inspector R V Desai said: "The car was purchased recently. That's why it does not have a registration number. We have identified its owner with the help of the car dealer. The car is registered in the name of one Mohanlal Thakkar, a resident of Swami Narayan Society in Paldi area. We checked his address but the house was closed. We are trying to trace him."

According to Kamlesh Thakor, an eye-witness, "There was a group of 15-20 boys and girls. An Alto and around four motorbikes were accompanying the Maruti Swift. All the boys and girls looked drunk. Immediately after the accident, they abandoned the car and escaped in the Alto and the bikes."

The deceased have been identified as Sardarji Thakor and Ranchhodji Thakor of Shilaj village and Ramaji Juhaji Thakor of Palodia village near Shilaj. Jamaji Thakor and Ramaji Maganji Thakor who were injured, were admitted to the Sola Civil Hospital by passers-by.

Jamaji Thakor, an injured and also a complainant in the case, told Newsline: "We were sitting on the benches when suddenly a car came from behind us. Before we could understand anything, it hit us and we were thrown in different directions. Sardarji Thakor and Ranchhodji Thakor died on the spot. We were brought to the hospital by passers-by."

While Jamaji has been discharged from the hospital, Ramaji Maganji Thakor is being treated at the Ahmedabad Civil Hospital where his condition is stated to be stable.

Heading: Nasik Merchants Bank may take over Nutan Sahakari Bank - Indian Express
Content:
Senior Dalit leader from Gujarat Yogendra Makwana is all set to walk out of the Congress fold. The 70-year-old leader, who has been associated with the party since 1969, will announce his break-up with the party at a press meet in New Delhi on November 15.

Makwana, who was a central minister during Indira Gandhi's premiership, has already formed a pan-India political outfit, the National Bahujan Congress (NBC). He is fielding candidates for the December Assembly elections in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and New Delhi.

The NBC is fielding as many as 150 candidates in Rajasthan, and will fight on eight seats in New Delhi and five seats in Madhya Pradesh.

Makwana is also trying to mobilise the Dalits, backwards, Scheduled Tribes and minorities in support of his party. His party also plans to field candidates at the 2009 Parliamentary elections..

Besides, he will also release a booklet in English on the failure of the Congress party to uplift the conditions of the Scheduled Castes in the country. The Hindi translation of the booklet has been completed and printed, and will be distributed in the states going for the Assembly polls.

Over 200 Dalit and Scheduled Tribe leaders from all over the state are also likely to resign from the Congress after November 15.

Makwana told Newsline over the phone from New Delhi, that he will hold a meeting in Ahmedabad in the third week of November where a number of party leaders fed with the "dictatorial" functioning of the senior leaders, will announce their resignation. Among those resigning, will be members from the group that once formed the "Amarsinh Chaudhary faction," he said.

As for reasons for leaving the Congress with which he had such a long association, he said that the party was now neglecting the interests of the Scheduled Castes. Citing examples, he said that the party did not allot poll tickets to the Scheduled Caste department heads in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and New Delhi, though it expected the Dalits to support the party.

Makwana heads the Congress party's SC department at the national level and has reportedly been invited to join other parties, but has decided to float his own outfit.

One of his closest friends and former Congress Minister Ishwarsinh Chavda is also likely to resign from the party. Though Chavda could not be contacted, Makwana said that Chavda had made up his mind and will announce quitting the party soon.

Heading: Financial woes lead woman to commit suicide, say cops - Indian Express
Content:
The Vadodara-based Nutan Sahakari Bank Ltd, which has gone into liquidation, is likely to be taken over by the Nasik Merchants Co-operative Bank Ltd, a multi-state co-operative bank.

Bhaskar Shinde, the general manager and in-charge managing director of Nasik Merchants Co-operative Bank confirmed the move, saying that efforts were on for over last three months in this direction.

"We had sent our proposal around three months ago to the Reserve Bank of India. At present, we are in the process of resolving the RBI's queries about our proposal," said Shinde.

Incidentally, Vasantrao Gite took charge as the new chairman of the Nasik Merchants bank on Monday.

Outgoing chairman Kantilal Jain was not available for comments on the takeover proposal.

Shinde said that Nasik Merchants Bank was established in 1959 and has 45 branches at present, including one in Surat.

According to Shinde, the Nasik Merchants Bank has a deposit base of Rs 550 crore and its advances come to Rs 245 crore.

He said this suggests the bank has a careful lending policy despite enjoying a good investor confidence.

Officials at the Nutan Bank in Vadodara said the move was there to revive the bank and the takeover proposal was a part of it.

Joint Registrar of Co-operatives R V Baria, who has been appointed official liquidator, said the bank was facing liquidity.

The bank's loss accumulated to Rs 7 crore which eroded half of its deposit base of Rs 14 crore. To top it, the default in credit stood at Rs 7.60 crore in the form of advances, he said.

The Nutan Sahakari Bank has 24,000 depositors who will be required to submit their claims for insurance money of Rs one lakh in the next three months.

Baria said once this is done, the bank will start the recovery drive.

Heading: Two yarn merchants, employees abducted from Sachin GIDC - Indian Express
Content:
A 30-year-old tribal woman of Vyara committed suicide as she was upset at the seizure of her husband's tempo by forest officials recently.

According to the Vyara police, Ila Gamit, a resident of Dhaturi village in Vyara taluka of Tapi district, set herself ablaze by dousing kerosene on her body on November 1.

The woman's husband, Narsingh Gamit, who was sleeping inside the house, tried to save her by wrapping her with a shawl but he also sustained burns on his hands.

The couple was rushed to the Sardar Smarak Hospital at Bardoli for treatment. Ila was later shifted to the New Civil Hospital in Surat, where she succumbed to her injuries on Wednesday.

According to police investigation, the couple was disturbed after forest officials had seized Narsingh's tempo, which was the only source of income for the family.

Moreover, the pending loan installments added to the family's financial woes.

This led the woman to take the extreme step.

On the other hand, forest officials of Vyara contend that Narsingh was involved in illegal trade of teak wood from the forest. Vyara Range Forest Officer Mahendrasinh Solanki said that onOctober 15 they had kept a watch on his movements at Palawadi village but had failed to catch him.

He said later they found his tempo being driven by one

Anil Gamit, a resident of Dhaturi village.

As Anil failed to give satisfactory answers to their queries, the tempo was taken into possession, Solanki said they will take Narsingh's statement and continue their investigation.

Heading: 2 BJP councillors charged with supplying weapon to criminal, one arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Six youths abducted two yarn merchants and two of their employees from their factory in Sachin GIDC on Saturday.

The police suspect a monetary dispute to be the reason behind the incident.

The police said Ashok and Bablu Sharma, residents of Parvat patia in Surat, run a yarn business at Hojiwala estate in Sachin GIDC.

On Saturday, six unidentified persons entered the premises and inquired about Guddu, a supervisor working in the same firm.

When Ashok and Bablu did not give a proper response, the youths overpowered them, and punched and kicked them.

Meanwhile, two of the employees of the firm, who entered their bosses' cabin suspecting something wrong, were also beaten up by the unidentified people.

In the melee, Ashok somehow called his friend Dharmesh Singh Rajput and informed him about the incident in the factory.

Meanwhile, the accused abducted Ashok, Bablu, and the two employees and escaped in their Tavera MUV. Dharmesh rushed to the spot to help his friends and through some of the neighbours learnt that they had been abducted. Dharmesh then lodged a complaint of abduction with the Sachin police.

The police immediately swung into action and started a search operation at the suspected places.

The police raided some premises at Sachin and Pandesara and detained some youths.

They are now carrying out investigations to find out the whereabouts of the yarn merchants and their employees.

Sachin Inspector K R Bhuwa said: "We have detained some youths who were earlier working in Sharma's factory and are interrogating them to find out some links."

Heading: Rs 26 lakh theft  case solved, claim Rajkot police - Indian Express
Content:
The Special Operation Group (SOG) of Jamnagar police on Sunday arrested three people, including BJP Rajkot councillor Ramesh Dhava, for supplying a .38 bore police revolver to a notorious criminal.

Dhava, who was arrested along with Manharsinh Rana of Rajkot and Jitubha Jadeja of Jamnagar, revealed the name of another BJP Rajkot councillor, Raju Boricha, for supplying him with the weapon. Boricha, however, managed to escape.

The revolver that was recently recovered along with five cartridges from notorious criminal Salim Ismail from near the Dharagadh railway crossing is used only by police officers.

This has fuelled suspicion that there might be some link between the revolver and the murder of Rajkot Sub-Inspector R J Gajia. The Sub-Inspector was murdered on January 4, 2004. During investigation, his service revolver was found missing. Even after four years, the case lies unsolved.

Investigating officer R B Nimavat of the SOG said: "During the two-day remand, Salim Ismail gave the names of three persons for supplying him the prohibited arm. After the three were arrested, Dhava gave the name of another Rajkot BJP councillor for supplying the revolver to him. We tried to arrest Boricha, but he managed to escape."

When contacted, Jamnagar DSP R V Jotangia told Newsline, "We have not found any link between the Gajia murder case and the .38 bore revolver recovered from a notorious criminal. But we will match the body number of the revolver with missing revolvers so that we can reach a conclusion."

Rajkot Police Commissioner Sudhir Sinha firmly denied any link between the two cases.

"Body number of the recovered revolver is different from that of Gajia's service revolver. There is no connection between the two," Sinha said.

Heading: Court asks GU to prove validity of giving affiliation to 152 institutes - Indian Express
Content:
The Rajkot Crime Branch on Monday claimed to solve one of the major theft cases in the city, and arrested one person with Rs 1.75 lakh cash in this regard.

The police had suspected Dipendra, a Nepalese guard at the bungalow of Radhe Group owner Dr Shailesh Mankadia in the Vrindawan Society, for the theft of Rs 26 lakh from the residence, as he was found missing after the crime.

Crime Branch Sub-Inspector M V Kikani said they interrogated a few other Nepalese guards at Mankadia's factory and picked up one Padamsingh Kalusinh Thakur when he was planning to flee to Nepal.

Kikani said: "Padamsinh has revealed the entire plan to us. The main accused is Dipendra, a guard at Dr Mankadia's residence. Dipendra had plotted the theft some 3-4 months ago and involved four other Nepalese guards including Biren, Bum, Bharat and Padamsingh from Dr Mankadia's factory, in the crime. On Diwali, when the entire family was on holiday, Dipendra and four of his friends committed the crime between 1 and 4 am."

He said after the theft, Dipendra gave Rs 2 lakh each to Padamsingh and the three other accused and kept all the jewellery and the remaining cash with him and fled away in luxury bus towards Nepal. The next day, while three of the accused succeeded in escaping towards Nepal, Padamsingh was caught by the police. "We have recovered Rs.1.75 lakh from Padamsingh as he has spent Rs 25, 000 from his share," said Kikani.

He said Crime Branch personnel are now camping at the Nepal border and the other absconders will be caught soon.

Padamsingh was produced before the court on Monday, which sent him to the Malavyanagar police station.

Heading: Cops arrest three for betting on Ranji match - Indian Express
Content:
It is the job of the university's academic and executive councils and not the V-Cs to look into colleges' affiliations, says petitioner

A two-judge bench comprising Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Justice Aqil Qureshi on Monday issued a notice to Gujarat University asking it to furnish before it the validity of the Vice Chancellor's action pertaining to the affiliation given to 152 self-financed colleges recently.

The notice is returnable on December 2.

The notice was issued on a petition filed by Arts Faculty Dean Pradeep Prajapati seeking directions to quash and set aside the decision of the Vice Chancellor in according affiliation to self-financed colleges and direct the university to follow the provisions of the Gujarat University Act, 1989.

Submitting before the court, Prajatpati contended that it was the job of the university's academic council and executive council to look into the affiliation of colleges.

Quoting university rules, he pointed out that the academic council recommended the cases to the executive council and the latter took the decision on these recommendations.

Prajapati, however, argued that Vice Chancellor Parimal Trivedi had violated the rules and had taken the decision on his own in the syndicate meeting. He submitted that the V-C only communicated his decision to the executive council.

Further, he pointed out, that there was no provision in the GU Act to grant affiliation to self-financed colleges.

He reminded the court that in 2001 the High Court had quashed the affiliation to some self-financed colleges on a petition filed by Narhari Amin, the former Deputy Chief Minister and a former member of the university's executive council.

Advocate Suresh Shelat, representing the university, submitted that as the affiliations had been granted to as many as 152 colleges, their cancellations would have serious repercussions.

He pleaded that the petitioner should instead represent before the state government.

The court, however, did not accept his arguments and issued a notice to the university to file an affidavit, proving validity of the affiliations, on December 2.

Heading: All-women police station opens in city - Indian Express
Content:
Betting in Ranji trophy matches is a rare phenomenon, as it mostly take place at the international level.

Nevertheless, the Vadodara Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) arrested three people red-handed at an apartment in Hari Nagar on Monday for placing bets on Ranji Trophy matches between Baroda and Uttar Pradesh on the first day of the game.

Sleuths from the DCB said that the gang operated through code words and could be associated with bigger betting syndicates in the country.

"We were intercepting the phone calls of the accused on suspicion, and it took some time to figure out what they were exactly dealing with," said Inspector K M Polra.

On Monday afternoon, the police recovered seven mobile phones worth Rs 3,000, one laptop worth Rs 20,000 and a colour television set worth Rs 13,000 from the apartment.

The accused were betting on the Ranji Trophy match. The police, however, did not recover any cash from the three accused.

While one of the accused, Alpesh Kapasi is from Ahmedabad, the other two, namely Satish Jaiswal and Piyush Shah, are from Vadodara. The police said the accused were known to have links with betting rackets across the country.

Polra refused to comment on the nature of the betting and the people involved in the racket.

Documented evidence with the Central Bureau of Investigation shows that the last Ranji Trophy, where bets were possibly placed, took place in 1991 in a match involving the Delhi Cricket Association and Bombay, which the former deliberately lost.

Heading: Rural voters more alert about voter ID cards, says admn - Indian Express
Content:
The city got its first all-women police station near SSG Hospital on Monday. With the opening of the new police station, the total number of police stations in the city has gone up to 14.

Police officers said that the idea behind the move is to tackle the increasing number of crimes against women in the state. The new police station will act as a one-stop counter for all such crimes in the city, they added.

The police station will be sharing its quarters with the police station of the Vadodara Detection of Crime Branch (DCB). According to the police, a total of 36 women police staff will be deployed at the new police station.

Inspector M D Parmar, who has been in police service for the last 36 years, said: "I joined Vadodara police as a constable with Nari Suraksha Bal, but never imagined that I will be heading a full-fledged police station one day. This is a great move by the government and the police commissioner."

She added: "A women's police station will encourage a lot of women to join the police force. However, heading it will be a challenging task. But, we have the best sub-inspectors and assistant sub-inspectors in this police station, besides 24 women constables, who have equally taken part in ensuring security and safety in the city."

Heading: Shukarvaari Bazaar a hallmark of communal harmony - Indian Express
Content:
In an interesting find, Vadodara district administration officials have said that it is the rural voters who are more alert when it comes to getting their Elector's Photo Identity Card (EPIC) as compared to the urban voters.

Vadodara District Collector Vijay Nehra, while disclosing information about the improvements and changes in the electoral list, said that despite giving several chances and means to inform the district administration about the changes in the voter's information, there has been a lukewarm response from the citizens.

"There has been no problem in the rural belt. The reason is the size of the population in the villages and faster internal communication between the villagers. Whenever there are some changes to be made in the voters list, the message is spread quickly in the villages. They even know the government officials and panchayat members. That results in a flawless procedure," Nehra said.

On the other hand, there has been a lack of interest among the urban voters. "This time also, we have dedicated 2420000 number as helpline. We have kept six lines just to furnish all the required details related to EPIC. But surprisingly, the special helpline numbers that were set up during the last electoral list reforms were hardly used. Even we are surprised that although all confusions pertaining to EPIC could be removed through a phone call, it has not been used by the citizens."

Meanwhile, those completing 18 years on January 1, 2009 along with those who have migrated to different places will be able to register their names for the forthcoming elections. "We will have special arrangements to make the changes between November 10 and 24. Those who want to make changes can even approach the designated locations. Even on the two Sundays of November 16 and 23, special arrangements have been made just to ensure that people can approach us and take the advantage of the process to avoid last minute problems during the polling," Nehra said.

Heading: SSG Hospital patients to shift to super-speciality ward - Indian Express
Content:
The Shukarvaari Bazaar in the city is not an ordinary market for, it is home to a unique camaraderie between Hindus and Muslims.

Out of a total 4,000 vendors in the market, 60 per cent belong to the Waghri community. The rest are Muslims who sell birds, cutlery and clothes, according to Mansuri Abbas, who has been a vendor for 25 years.

"The Friday flea market is 70 years old. We all had a symbiotic relationship. Some vendors who wanted to place their laaris in the main part of the market, that is, Adaniapul, had to pay extra to the retail shop owners so that their place is booked and not taken over by others," said Rajesh Sadaja of the Waghri community.

Septuagenarian H D Shah from Raopura still comes in his bicycle and shows a bagful of articles, chatting with his friend Shah Nawaz who stays at Fatehpura. "Nothing has changed except police creating chaos in the market. I still remember my family coming here and doing purchases right from 5 am. We are afraid if the existence of the market would stop," Shah said.

Hanif Hasan is a bird-seller from Panjrigar Mohalla near Fatehpura. He said: "There has never been any communal tension in Fatehpura because of the market. In fact, it is where both Hindus and Muslims meet each other. Authorities have few reasons to close the market. But once it is closed, it will be too difficult to help the starving families of both the communities."

Heading: Cong outs all names: Amod Kant in Sangam Vihar, Kochar takes on VK - Indian Express
Content:
The patients undergoing treatment at the four wards of Sir Sayajirao General (SSG) Hospital's Department of Medicine will soon heave a sigh of relief as the hospital authorities plan to shift the patients soon to the newly constructed super-speciality ward.

The wards, including ward numbers one to four, are located in the old building of the hospital and come under the Department of Medicine.

The two-storeyed building, which is nearly a century-old, was constructed during the reign of the Gaekwad royal family of the erstwhile Baroda State. The hospital has been neglected and lacks in adequate facilities for the admitted patients.

"The facilities in the building are still inadequate. It does not even have the proper facility to carry patients on a stretcher. The construction of our newly constructed super-speciality ward is almost over and we plan to shift some of the patients there," said M H Gadhavi, executive officer at SSG hospital.

Since the super-speciality ward, which can accommodate around 200 beds, is still under construction, the patients on the first floor of the building will be shifted initially. "We can accommodate some 100 patients there and we will start shifting the patients within this week," said Gadhavi.

The hospital authorities also intend to seek government intervention for renovating and reconstructing the old building with an estimated cost of Rs 10 crore.

"We are still working on the cost of the complete restoration of the old building. Since it is a heritage building, we will have to take extra care," said Gadhavi.

Heading: VOTERS SPEAK: Sunny Dhingra - Indian Express
Content:
Kant will aim at wooing the migrant population from Bihar and eastern uttar pradesh, while kochar is expected to give a tough fight to bjp's V K malhotra

Putting an end to the nail- biting suspense of who would be in the election battlefield this time, the Delhi Congress on Monday declared the final list of candidates contesting in the Assembly elections scheduled for November 29.

While the party had declared 48 names last week, candidates for 22 seats were withheld for further discussion and approval from AICC President Sonia Gandhi. These seats included BJP strongholds like Greater Kailash I, Narela, Mundka, Rohini, Hari Nagar, Rajinder Nagar and Tilak Nagar.

As per the list of the final 22 put up by the Central Election Committee on Monday evening, the party would be fielding former IPS officer Amod Kant from Sangam Vihar constituency. Kant was reportedly backed by Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit and is expected to woo the migrant population from Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh in the unauthorised colony up for regularisation.

Hoping to give a tough fight to BJP chief ministerial candidate V K Malhotra, is former municipal councillor Jitender Kochar.

Backed by Delhi Congress chief J P Aggarwal, Kochar's name was withheld last week, with the party looking at alternatives in former mayor Jaishree Pawar, backed by Ajay Maken, and sitting MLA Subhash Chopra from Kalkaji, only to get back in the list.

Former Bihar governor Buta Singh's son Ravinder Singh Lovely would be fighting the Delhi Assembly elections from Deoli in South Delhi. Lovely was earlier hoping to contest the Rajasthan assembly elections but was denied a ticket.

Minto Road sitting MLA and NDMC vice-president lost out to delimitation and has not been given a ticket this time. With Tajdar Babar's Minto Road constituency being removed from the election map, she was hoping to grab a seat in Jangpura. The seat has been allotted to sitting MLA Tarwinder Singh Marwah.

Health Minister Yoganand Shastri who had lost his Malviya Nagar constituency to Hauz Khas sitting MLA Kiran Walia will be constesting from Mehrauli. Sitting MLA Rajesh Jain has retained his Sadar Paharganj seat.

Former NSUI president Neeraj Basoya will be contesting from Kasturba Nagar and sitting municipal councillor Anita Babar will be contesting from Tilak Nagar. Ramesh Lamba, who had lost out Rajouri Garden to Dayanand Chandilla will be fighting from Hari Nagar opposite BJP's Harcharan Singh Balli. The Congress is fielding former MLA P C Kaushik from Mundka and Deepak Tyagi from Burari.

All candidates will be filing their nomination papers tomorrow which also happens to be the last date for filing nominations.

Heading: Jamia Nagar Coordination Committee to field independent candidate - Indian Express
Content:
1st year student, International Hotel Management, PUSA University
Area: Vasant KunjAge: 22 years

Though a first time voter, Sunny Dhingra is not too excited about the election. He feels that neither the Congress nor the BJP can do any good for the city. "Since it is my right to vote, I will not miss it," he says. "Both parties have been playing vote bank politics and have not focussed on important issues. But as a sincere citizen I feel that we just cannot let the city go into just anyone's hands," he says.

On construction of flyovers: Sunny feels teh construction of flyovers takes a long time in Delhi. "In developed countries, a flyover is constructed in a month's time.
