But here the project goes on for years. I think the government needs to learn this technology from other countries," says Sunny. "I am sure this will help us overcome unnecessary traffic jams and road accidents," he says.

On corruption of the police: Sunny feels for an ordinary man, getting a complaint registered is an impossible task to do. If the police feel the complaint is not too serious, they simply refuse to lodge an FIR.

"I cannot get an FIR registered if I do not know any politician or a bureaucrat. Only if my uncle is a politician or I have enough money in my pocket, can I get a complaint registered with the police, or else they can make a person run around for days," says Sunny. "The time has come when the government needs to rid us of the corruption in the police force," he says.

Heading: BJP ‘chargesheets’ Congress, outlining areas of failure - Indian Express
Content:
Despite the presence of three big political parties vying for the Jamia Nagar vote and a sitting MLA in power for the last 15 years, a section of Jamia Nagar has decided to field an independent candidate from the colony in the upcoming Assembly elections.

The Jamia Nagar Coordination Committee — formed last year to protest the 'excesses of the local police' — has decided to field committee convenor Irfanullah Khan as an independent against Congress MLA Pervez Hashmi.

"This colony has been neglected all along. We will fight the elections to improve civic amenities," said Khan who would be filing his nomination from Okhla constituency tomorrow.

"The Congress MLA has not spent a rupee in Jamia Nagar and we have RTI records to that effect," he said.

Since its formation last year, the body has played an important role in maintaining peace after the encounter and has consistently opposed the proposal to set up another police station in the area after a police post was burnt down last September.

While five odd independents and parties like the Samajwadi Party, Bahujan Samaj Party and the BJP have already declared their candidates, Khan said, "We'll welcome an alliance with any party," he said.

The ghost of the Batla House incident continues to haunt the coordination committee as well.

"The Prime Minister has refused to initiate a judicial probe in the encounter. We will take it up as part of our election agenda," Khan added.

While the BSP' s state unit head Brahm Singh will be contesting from this constituency, the BJP is fielding Surender Bidhuri from Okhla for the seat and is primarily eyeing areas in the Gurjjar belt.

Heading: No turn in this twist - Indian Express
Content:
On the lines of their Vision 2003 — issued during the last Assembly elections, the Delhi BJP on Monday released a 'chargesheet' cataloguing their charges against the Congress government and outlining the issues they would be campaigning on.

"Our main charge against the Congress is that neither is the life of common man safe nor his pocket," said Arun Jaitley, spearheading his party's election campaign. The chargesheet has listed 14 topics on which the BJP is attacking Congress. This chargesheet would be distributed to each candidate who have been told to distribute it in their constituencies.

Starting with price rise, the BJP claims rates of essential commodities have risen from 25 per cent to 200 per cent. The BJP has also raised the question of drinking water scarcity. Delhi needs 900 million gallons per day (MGD ) of water while only 600 MGD is available. "In 1998 Sheila Dikshit had announced that there will not be any scarcity of water in two years time, but nothing has been done as yet," chargesheet states.

The BJP has also hit out at Congress on privatisation of power, increase in tariff and power cuts. The BJP is also claiming that 24 lakh BPL cardholders are not getting foodgrains from fair price shops.

"The Congress had promised four lakh flats for the poor, but three months ahead of elections the government says only ten thousands flats are ready," the chargesheet says.

The Yamuna Action Plan and closure of industries in Delhi has also been taken up. "Not a single unauthorised colony has been regularised in ten years. Instead a provisional certificate has been given just two months ahead of elections," the chargesheet claims.

The chargesheet also touched upon health services, transport system, unemployment, education and corruption.

Heading: Bowlers get even at Palam - Indian Express
Content:
EC flexes muscle
The Election Commission is not happy with the BJP chief ministerial candidate flexing his muscle while filing his nomination and bringing with him an entire crowd; and has sent him a notice seeking explanation by 5 pm on Tuesday. BJP leader Arun Jaitley told reporters the party would file their reply soon.

Senior BJP and Akali Dal leaders were present in the office of returning officer Bans Raj Ram, and several cars carrying the BJP leaders had been parked inside the premises of the district commissioner's office in Jam Nagar. The EC has already transferred Bans Raj Ram, ACP Pushpender Kumar and Sub-Inspector K L Yadav of the Tilak Marg police station for failing to implement its instructions. The BJP leaders of course claimed they had not violated any rules.

Confusing names
Seems twin names can be mindboggling even for political parties. While Education Minister Arvinder Singh Lovely is already gearing up to retain his Gandhi Nagar constituency in East Delhi and giving BJP rivals sleepless nights, his name popped up again as the chosen candidate for the Deoli seat in South Delhi on Monday. While Lovely's was cleared only last week, a double check revealed that the AICC listmakers confused Arvinder Singh Lovely with Ravinder Singh Lovely, who is former Bihar governor Buta Singh's elder son. The latter Lovely has been allotted a ticket from Delhi after being denied one from Rajasthan.

Heading: Physio runs half marathon... 785 miles away - Indian Express
Content:
Vidarbha pacers pave their way back in after Services fold their batting for 151

After a spate of draws and batting-dominated results in the first round of the Ranji Trophy Plate league, the Palam ground track came as a pleasant surprise for seam-up bowlers. Being forced to fish in the 'wet' track, Vidarbha lost a bad toss in the first place, but at stumps there was every evidence of giving their hosts a taste of their own medicine as Services were still trailing by 108 runs.

Vidarbha pacers Mohammad Hashim, Sandeep Singh and Alind Naidu bore accountability for the opposition's top five returnnig to the hut, sharing the wickets of Tahir Khan, Madhusudan Reddy and Yashpal Singh.

However, like their first outing against Tripura, Services set the pace of the game early on, following the same trail to lose ground by sunset.

But for the first time, the pitch did most of the talking than anything else. Left-arm pacer Rakesh Kumar swung it out, nipped it back, let a few follow the same trajectory after pitching to pave his way to a fourth consecutive five-wicket haul (without an innings to go) since his debut versus Assam last year. "The wetness of the pitch helped, but for that too I had to pitch the ball in the right areas. The first five-seven overs weren't conducive to swing, but after that it started stopping on the batsman with a bit of movement," said Kumar.

Even Pankaj Kumar, coming as a replacement for Hari Prasad, had the wickets of Rahul Chikalkar and skipper Pritam Gandhe as a token of the bounce the track offered.

Among the pacers wreaking havoc, Shuvra Karmakar's left-arm spin had little help from the track, but was just enough to tame the tail, rattling Madhusudhan Acharya and Mohammad Hashim's timber — off an arm ball and error of judgement, respectively. Services' job with the red cherry was rounded off by a couple of sharp catches from Yashpal Singh at slips with 151 runs on board for the visitors. But almost inevitably, things began on an ominous note while facing it.

With the sun rising and setting without a glimpse, there was hardly any change in the content of the pitch and skipper Sunil Tomar's run out early on didn't serve his team's cause. Calling it the same old story would be a bit harsh on the Services' top order — especially the way Yashpal Singh opened up until the ball from Alind Naidu that did just enough to kiss his edge — but there were still a few ifs and buts that kept ringing in the air. With the forecast nothing extraordinary, Services still might have to do a lot of fishing on a slippery track on Tuesday. Their deeper batting wouldn't bring solace, but application might, as was evident from their skipper's words. "Every day can't be called a bad day. Our bowlers have done extremely well, but the batsmen haven't applied themselves to the task," said Tomar.

Brief scores: Vidarbha 151 (Shalabh Srivastava 42 no; Rakesh Kumar 5/45, Shuvra Karmakar 3/38) lead Services 43 for 5 (Mohammad Hashim 2/18) by 103 runs.

Heading: Anureet Singh: Delhi’s loss & Railways’ gain - Indian Express
Content:
The owner of jersey number 7273 was ready in time for the Delhi half marathon — so what if he competed some 785 miles away from the actual course of the race, and finished an hour after the eventual winners.

Badrinath Prathi longed to be part of the half-marathon but his professional commitments came in the way as an obstacle; without flinching, the Delhi team physio was up at 7 am on Sunday morning at the Rajiv Gandhi Stadium in Uppal - the same time when the half-marathon began in the capital — wearing the same dress as designated to run along simultaneously.

And after 54 laps of the ground and timing 2 hours and 17 seconds on the clock strapped around his waist, Badri, as he's fondly called, raised his hands up in celebration as members of the Delhi Ranji squad, who had just arrived for practice ahead of their Ranji game against Hyderabad, gave him a standing ovation to applaud his commitment of running 21 kilometres.

"It was my childhood desire to run a marathon and I have been preparing close to four weeks for this half-marathon."I always look forward to visiting Hyderabad, which is my native place. Ironically when I finally got here, I was wishing I was back in Delhi ," laughs the Hyderabadi. "That Ethiopian guy who won, what's his timing? He did it under an hour right? I was down with fever, otherwise I could have improved on my timing," he says.

Sunil Dev, DDCA sports secretary who flew down for the match, said, "Badri requested to stay back for the marathon and I told him 'you can, provided you resign first'. But on a serious note, I made him understand that he needs to be with the team and unfortunately that means he cannot be part of the marathon,' he says even as the Delhi team reserves pull in loud cheer for their 'champion'.

Heading: Bay Watch - Indian Express
Content:
Vijay Tendulkar's new compilation of plays for children shows he wasn't just inspired by politics

Forty years ago, Vijay Tendulkar used to attract a very young audience. As they applauded, six of his plays—written especially for children—enjoyed the spotlight. Since their stage run wasn't long enough, these plays soon faded into obscurity. Now, five of them are staging a comeback, albeit in print.

The book, simply called Five Plays for Children, is translated by Pune-based Ajay Joshi and published by Scholastic. In its introduction, Joshi says, "Much has been written about Tendulkar's plays and the playwright himself, but little is available on the six plays he wrote for children."

It isn't difficult to find the reason behind it. "These plays seem to have been tucked away from the arc lights, overpowered by the powerful presence of his path-breaking adult writings," the translator adds. Joshi, who started translating the plays into English early last year, had to work on retaining the original flavour, pun and nuances in English.

Another challenge was to unravel what Tendulkar wanted to communicate. Interestingly, the period when the legendary playwright wrote the plays coincides with the creation of some his greatest plays like Gidhade, Shantata! Court Chalu Aahe and Sakharam Binder. "Tendulkar wrote the children plays in the 1960s and the early 70s," says Joshi. So many find it incredulous that the dramatist who appeared to be such a harsh critic of the society, could come up with plays are so gentle. Tendulkar's sixth play for children couldn't be included in the collection as Joshi couldn't trace it in time.

It's Sulabha Deshpande who made Tendulkar write these plays. The actor, who was teaching at the Chabbildas School, Dadar, was part of the theatre movement to move away from the traditional musical theatre. Tendulkar too, was involved in this movement of presenting more relevant and realistic theatre. Deshpande urged the late dramatist to write plays for her school so that her students could take part in competitions. Deshpande says that coming from Tendulkar, the plays were amazingly "simple and straightforward".

Joshi, however, has a different take on it. "The plays have the Tendulkar touch—with multiple layers." For each play, Tendulkar adopted a distinct form and context. "He used the idioms of folk theatre for The King and Queen Want Sweat (Raja Ranila Gham Hava). This is said to be the precursor to Sakharam Binder," Joshi says.

The book has four more plays— The Wedding of the Village Headman's Daughter (Patlachya Poricha Lageen), Bobby's Story (Bobbychi Goshta), The Play of the Nosey Parker (Chambhar Chaukashiche Natak) and Missing: A Father (Baba Haravale Ahet).

Though these plays were not widely staged, Awishkar Theatre Group has produced them in the past. In fact, the memory-tickling black-and-white images of the plays in the book are sourced from the group. The collection's cover serves as another pointer to the plays; the illustrations on it are inspired by the characters of the plays.

Heading: Comic relief - Indian Express
Content:
Designer Aki Narula on dressing up the hunks in Tarun Mansukhani's Dostana

Life is supposedly one long party when you're based in Miami. Aki Narula, however, discovered that life on pristine beaches can also mean a lot of hard work. The designer, who has dressed up actors John Abraham, Abhishek Bachchan, Bobby Deol and a handful of others (only Priyanka Chopra's costumes have been done by Manish Malhotra) for Tarun Mansukhani's film Dostana that releases this Friday, got his brief for the film approved in half an hour, when he met the director and producer Karan Johar in Mumbai last November. But when he landed in Miami for a recce in early January, he knew he was in for a mad ride. "There's a very Cuban, Mexican feel to Miami, particularly with its cosmopolitan crowd, its white sands and clear blue skies. Since the characters in the film are based there, imbibing the local culture was important. Translating that mood to clothes was quite a task," he says.

In the movie, Abraham plays a fashion photographer and Bachchan a male nurse, while Bobby Deol is an urban sophisticate. So while Deol goes around in more formal clothing— slim Louis Vuitton suits and Dolce Gabbana jackets, the other two have a more casual style. "Choosing clothes for John was easy. He's in shorts for most of the movie and all you ladies are in for a treat with his toned body on display," smiles Aki. "I gave him a lot of tees with social messages on them. I made Abhishek wear all sorts of bright colours, from oranges to greens to reds and pinks with low-waisted jeans and cargo pants," says Narula, who has been styling for Bachchan junior since his Bunty Aur Babli days. In fact, Narula experimented a fair bit with Bachchan's outfit, apart from making him wear colour. "Even though this movie is aimed for an urban crowd, I always believe that a trend should be able to cut across masses, like the shirt kurtis in Bunty Aur Babli that became such a rage after the movie.

Most of the shirts that Abhishek wears in Dostana have collars that are 30 inches long, and reach his knees. A friend of mine was telling me he has already seen replicas on Carter Road!" says Narula. Shooting was a whole lot of fun too. "John would be ready in a jiffy while the other two took their time getting dressed for the shot. So John would laugh his head off all the while and irritate them," he grins. Post Dostana, Narula's appointment diary is choc-a-bloc with assignments. Up next is Aditya Chopra's Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi, and Renzil D' silva's debut film with Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor and Viveik Oberoi. He is also doing the costumes for Kareena Kapoor for her next project, Kambaqt Ishq. For now though, look out for the dandies.

Heading: The 20/20 Opera - Indian Express
Content:
At the French literary festival, new writers and illustrators surface, with vivid drawings and spunky text

On a chilly Saturday evening at the Alliance Française Delhi (AFD), 20 children walked with Detective John Chatterton, the zesty black detective cat (inset), trawling a shady part of a big city for clues leading to the missing young girl—slyly dressed up like Little Red Riding Hood. While storyteller Paro Anand, known for her theatrical storytelling style lead the children to the clues, French writer-illustrator Yvan Pommaux, clad in a red jacket, and the brains behind the suited black cat, stood in a corner. "My English is not that good," smiled Pommaux (in the picture below), in India, for the launch of his book John Chatterton translated into English and Hindi by Rajkamal Publishers. The launch is a part of a five day literary festival "Lire en Fête" which includes an exhibition of illustration workshops and book discussions, and the first French book fair in India.

Pommaux, 61, remarked, "I have been translated in Japanese, Spanish, Korean but never in English. The book, first published in France in 1993 has finally been translated in English, that too by an Indian publisher."

However, Pommaux, who blithely combines clipped dialogues with comic simplicity, has no training as an illustrator and worked his way up by designing pastry and working in hairdressers shops. He drew constantly from an early age. Later, he also juggled illustrating text books published by École des Loisirs. "I had to do odd jobs that permitted me to draw. École des Loisirs spotted me and gave me the job of illustrating text books to keep me afloat," shared Pommaux.

Meanwhile, Francophiles can get a copy of Voltaire or Rousseau for Rs 50 and French pocket dictionaries at 20 per cent discount. You can also find a French translation of Salman Rushdie's

Midnight' Children and Oscar Wilde's The Canterville Ghost and some interesting French comic books. Also, have a look at the exhibition of 12 authors and illustrators including former French minister Azouz Begag, Frédéric Clément and Michel Honaker at FIRC, at Aurangzeb Road.

The festival will go on till November 12 at Alliance Française. For details call 30410052

Heading: Home Front - Indian Express
Content:
Arbaaz Khan dons the garb of a producer

Not content with his recent visibility in films, Arbaaz Khan recently launched his own production house, Arbaaz Khan Productions.

"I am glad to have been seen in some good films of late, but I wanted to take my role in the industry further. I stumbled upon a good director and a great script, which is when I decided to take up the project," explains the actor.

There has been no formal launch but the actor plans an official announcement closer to the date when the project goes on floors in April. The first film under the banner, says Khan, is a commercial drama based on relationships and conflicts.

"It has a role for Salman and I may be acting too." Refusing to divulge further details, he adds that the film will be directed by debutant director Abhinav Kashyap. Talking about his future projects, Khan says that after the success of Fashion, he would like to focus on his forthcoming films —Madhureeta Anand's Mere Khwabon Mein Jo Aaye and Kissan under his brother's Sohail Khan Productions.

On suggestion that he could have worked under his brother's banner as a producer, the actor says that the production house already has an established name and is busy with projects like Mr and Mrs Khanna.

Afraid that people might misconstrue the equation between the two brothers, Khan is quick to clarify, "The names may be different but the machinery to run the two companies is common. We are and will always be one."

Heading: Fermented by East - Indian Express
Content:
Subodh Gupta brings together 30 artists to contribute towards relief work in Bihar and Orissa through an auction

The art mart may be going through a low phase with the economic recession affecting the prices of canvases but Subodh Gupta is convinced that when it comes to contributing to a good cause, the money will come in. "The market conditions may not be the best but the needy can't wait," says the Delhi-based artist as he readies for the Saffronart Artists Flood Relief Auction, organised to collect funds for flood victims in Orissa and Bihar.

While the initiative came from Gupta and wife Bharti Kher, chipping in for the online auction that will take place today and tomorrow are a total of 31 artists, each of whom has donated a canvas. "No one has charged anything and there are no artist cuts. Every penny will be directed towards relief," states Gupta, who has decided to direct the proceeds to two NGOs, Samajik Shaikshanik Vikas Kendra and Goonj. "I would have liked to visit the affected areas myself, but don't think that will be as beneficial. I would rather contribute through art," says Gupta. He has been working towards the auction for a month and has managed to get together an impressive range of art which includes Atul Dodiya's watercolour on paper titled Proust from the 'Pale Ancestors' series, Riyas Komu's 2008 oil on canvas titled Uttara II and TV Santhosh's untitled watercolour on paper.

While Ranbir Singh Kaleka's oil on wood titled Man with Torch has an estimate price of Rs 30- 40 lakh, Bharti Kher's bindis on board titled This Way and Never Another Way is estimated to fetch 45-65 lakh. The highest bid, however, is expected for Gupta's untitled oil on canvas, which has an estimate price of Rs 90 lakh to 1.2 crore. While the artist is uncertain about the total proceeds that he will manage through the auction, Dinesh Vazirani, founder of Saffronart, is hopeful of collecting between Rs 3 to 4 crore for the NGOs.. "The cause should act as a driving factor. We are looking forward to bids from the world over," he smiles. And the collectors get great art in return.

Heading: Armed men rob bank cashier, customers - Indian Express
Content: If it was not the molten amber of Scotch, it was a straight Bourbon or an easier-on-the-wallet, made-in-India brew. Japanese whisky might sound like an oxymoron to a non-connoisseur who associates just sake and shochu with the sushi-eaters. But single-malt lovers have long known that Yoichi and Yamazaki can give the Scots a run for their money, and Japan is the second-largest producer of single malts. Now, Wasabi has brought in some of these singular malts and you can indulge in the Yoichi, 10-year-old single malt with its remarkable oak and spicy notes or the ripe Nikka, or the famed Yoichi, 20-year-old single malt, which has been voted the Best Single Malt Whisky in the World at the World Whisky Awards 2008. They are available at Rs 325 -1550 for 30 ml.

Heading: On way to school, 12 students hurt as bus overturns; 3 children critical - Indian Express
Content:
Four armed assailants robbed the UCO Bank branch in Hauz Khas after forcing a woman customer into the branch at the point of a gun on Monday afternoon.

The assailants also looted Rs 25,000 that the victim, one Ritu Singh, had withdrawn minutes prior to the incident, and Rs 8,000 from another customer who had come to deposit the amount.

The incident was reported from UCO Bank in E-5, Hauz Khas, around 4.30 pm.

The bank's zonal manager, Raja Ram, said they are yet to estimate the amount robbed from the cashier but a bank employee (name withheld on request) put the amount at over Rs 5 lakh. Asked to confirm the amount, a senior officer said the police were told that the robbery was "in lakhs".

According to the police, the assailants surrounded Ritu Singh, a resident of DLF Phase-III in Gurgaon, the moment she stepped out of the bank after withdrawing Rs 25,000. One of them pointed a gun at her waist and the others forced her to enter the bank again and step up near the cashier on the pretext of making queries, a police officer said.

"The assailants then snatched money from the cashier," the officer said. "After the cashier raised alarm, another customer, Prakash Chand, went to check. At this point the robbers fired two shots on the ground and hit Chand on the head with the butt of the gun."

The four then took money from Ritu Singh (Rs 25,000) and Prakash Chand (Rs 8,000 he had come to deposit) and made their way out.

The police officer said the robbers had come on two motorbikes.

Chand was taken to AIIMS and discharged after first-aid. He told Newsline over the phone that he had gone to the cashier's desk to check what was going on after hearing "abuses being exchanged".

Chand works at an electronics store in the area.

Zonal manager Raja Ram said CCTVs are installed in the bank. "We have not put an estimate on the amount robbed from the cashier and are still counting," he said.

DCP (South) H G S Dhaliwal was not available for comment despite trips to his office and phone calls till late in the evening.

Heading: Discoms cheer as SC says cut power if dues head north - Indian Express
Content:
Twelve students of KDS Public School were reported injured after their school bus collided with a Santro car near Omega sector in Greater Noida on Monday morning.

Three students received multiple scalp injuries. Doctors at Kailash Hospital, where they are admitted, said the three are critical and in the Intensive Care Unit.

The police said the school bus driver, Ravinder Singh, and the conductor fled after the accident. A case of negligent driving has been lodged against Ravinder. The police said the driver already had a case registered against him under sections dealing with negligent driving causing death, at Kasna police station, earlier.

Today's accident took place at 8 am when the speeding school bus hit the car near a roundabout, the police said. "The bus overturned and left several students injured," Station House Officer (Kasna) Ajay Kumar Chowdhary said. "The driver and the conductor abandoned the bus after the accident and fled. The locals informed the police and helped carry the injured to the hospital."

According to doctors at the hospital, Manoj, a student of Class IV, Rocky, a Class II student, and Class I student Gautam are still in the ICU. "Of the 12 students who came to us, we have discharged seven and five are still admitted. Three children are under observation," Dr N Kapoor, a senior doctor at Kailash Hospital, said.

About the case registered against the errant driver earlier, a police officer said the incident, which took place about a year-and-a-half ago, left one person dead.

School principal M S Parmar said she had employed the driver after he submitted a character certificate and showed a valid driving licence. She said the police did not register her complaint since the owner of the Santro car had already filed an FIR against the school bus driver. "I told the policemen that they should at least register that I came to the police station with an application," Parmar said, "but they did not entertain that."

Based on the car owner Bhagwan Dass Sanwaria's complaint, a criminal case under IPC Sections 279 (rash driving), 338 (causing grievous hurt by act endangering life), and 427 (mishief causing damage) has been registered against the driver Ravinder Singh.

Heading: Illegal constructions thrive around heritage sites - Indian Express
Content:
A Supreme Court judgment on power distribution has put the smiles back on the face of officials in Delhi's power distribution companies, harried by complaints from dissatisfied customers.

The apex court on Friday ruled that power distribution companies (discoms) retain the right to disconnect supply if outstanding dues are not cleared. On Monday, an official of a discom said, "The Supreme Court ruling would certainly make our task easier. There have been instances of consumers filing cases with the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity regarding disconnection due to non-payment of dues. That will probably stop now."

The apex court bench of Justices R V Raveendran and L S Panta gave the decision while ruling on a suit filed by a consumer against Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam, of Uttar Pradesh. The consumer had moved court contending that the distributor's refusal to restore connection to buyers of a sub-divided plot was illegal. But ruling in favour of the distributor, the Bench observed, "We do not find anything unreasonable in a provision enabling the distributor/supplier to disconnect supply if dues are not paid."

Even in cases where the plot has been sold or sub-divided, the Bench held that the provision should be upheld.

A senior Power department official said the decision is expected to reduce cases in which people sell the property when faced with electricity disconnection after drawing up humongous dues. "The onus is now also on buyers to ensure that all dues are cleared before they purchase a property," the official said. Discoms operating in the Capital, however, are in no hurry to go on a disconnection drive. "The ruling upholds the prevalent law, so it will make it easier for us to enforce the law when the need arises," a discom official said.

What apex court says
* Power distributors can snap supply if dues cross a certain limit
* Applicable even to plot/premise that has been sold or sub-divided
* Buyer/occupants should ensure there are no dues pending

What discoms say
* Decision will stop unnecessary cases for disconnection due to non-payment
* Won't go on any disconnection overdrive ¿ enough time to settle dues

Heading: Now, evening courts to take on bounced cheque cases - Indian Express
Content:
The recent demolition of the Lal Mahal, 13th century monument at Nizamuddin has put the spotlight on vulnerable heritage structures in the Capital. While many of Delhi's monuments, including baolis and mosques, have served as public spaces within communities, the older communities settled around a monument have been replaced by illegal encroachments.

According to ASI rules, no construction is allowed at least 100 metres around a protected monument. Buildings constructed after 1992 around the monument encroaching this space, are eligible for removal. Near the World Heritage Site of Humayun's Tomb, the Nizamuddin basti houses several such monuments. The settlement sprang up around the shrine of the Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya, in his lifetime and has remained inhabited since.

While the crowded bylanes of the basti are most famous for Auliya's dargah, they also have around 10 protected monuments, and several other heritage structures, that have still not been notified as 'protected'. Lal Mahal, was one such structure.

Another such structure is the Kalan Masjid, built in 1370 by the prime minister of Feroze Shah Tughlaq. The mosque has been reinforced with concrete and white- washed. The baoli or step-well near the dargah, once reputed to have magical qualities, has sewage water in it.

The 'protected' tag does not guarantee prevention from encroachments. The Chaunsath Khamba, the 17th century marble tomb of Mirza Aziz Kokltash, the son of Ataga Khan, and Jiji Anga (Akbar's wet nurse) share a similar fate. The 64-pillared tomb is now surrounded by multi-storied buildings.

The Urs Mahal, an open courtyard in front of it, has a similar setting. Next to it, lies Mirza Ghalib's grave, which was given a boundary recently, but remains surrounded by high rise buildings.

In Kotla Mubarakpur, a village named named after the tomb and the mosque in the area built by Mubarak Shah Saiyyid in the 15th century, the Mubarakshah Mosque and a small tomb are also in danger.

The baoli in the area has big buildings all around. These are in contrast to the Bade Khan-Chhote Khan tombs which are in an enclosed garden. An FIR has been lodged but according to the Archaeological Survey of India, no action has been taken so far.

The MCD and Delhi Police have the authority to take action if an FIRs is lodged.

The area of Mohammadpur before the Bhikaji Cama Place, houses several monuments from the Lodi period, the most prominent being the Teen Burj tomb, a three-domed structure visible from the main road.

Heading: Fiscal soup: Slowdown raises empty tables at city restaurants - Indian Express
Content:
Six magisterial courts will be open for two extra hours in the evenings from Wednesday to scale down the tall stack of nearly 5 lakh pending cases on dishonoured cheques.

This new initiative — spearheaded by the Delhi High Court — is aimed at lessening the agony of litigants, among whom is one Sudesh Kumar Arora who has spent over Rs 20,000 in lawyer's fees for a case he filed in 2006. The trial on Arora's petition is yet to begin.

Borrowing a page from the evening-court tradition in Gujarat — the first state to introduce the system — six courts, three at the Patiala House complex and another three at Karkardooma, will hear cases between 5 pm and 7 pm on working days.

Metropolitan magistrates on rotation will be empowered to decide cases under the Negotiable Instruments Act for bounced cheques upto an amount of Rs 25,000. These cases will be transferred to them from all magisterial courts of that complex. It has been further proposed that not more than 500 cases should be pending in a given court, at any point of time. Cases will be referred to evening courts with the consent of the parties concerned, and if these courts fail to arrive at a solution for a particular matter, it will be sent back to the referral court for routine adjudication.

Judges and the evening court staff — to be drawn from the existing strength — will be paid an additional 25 per cent of their month's salary as pay for the work.

Over 5 lakh cases on bounced cheques have accumulated in court corridors, prompting two judges — Justices Madan B Lokur and Ravinder Bhat — to moot the idea and evolve its framework.

Realising the need for such a set-up, District and Sessions Judge Mamta Sehgal had also sent a proposal to the High Court in September to start evening courts that would take on the ever-mounting cases without putting a burden on the exchequer.

Consultations between the High Court and the government threw up 'evening courts' as the answer. Though 25 courts were proposed initially, the experiment will be launched in six at present.

Advocate Ashok Yadav said: "The biggest advantage of evening courts is that litigants need not take leave from work. In case of temporary employees, this meant loss in earnings."

Advocate Piyush Prabhakar pointed out, "The judiciary has a role to play in matters of commercial and mercantile activities. This cannot be overlooked. Unless we have a system to quickly dispose of cases related to dishonoured cheques, investment growth will certainly be affected."

Delhi follows Gujarat, TN
Gujarat started evening courts first — in November, 2006. The main objective was to bring down pending cases so that judges could spend more time hearing criminal and other important cases during day. Morevoer, the existing courts did not meet the needs of a growing population.

Tamil Nadu followed soon, setting up evening courts in Tuticorin last October. Since then, the concept of evening courts has been discussed at conferences of chief ministers and chief justices, with several state judiciaries excited at the need to do something.

Heading: Beaten and scarred, help says: Like it here at child home - Indian Express
Content:
On a nippy Sunday evening, dinner at a high-end restaurant in Saket turns out to be low key fare. There are no waiting lists getting steadily inked and just four tables are occupied.

While most restaurateurs will respond with a big 'No' when asked about declining footfalls, they agree that business is not as good as it was, even some time ago, as the economic slowdown gathers pace.

Smoke House Grill in GK-II is definitely not unaffected. "We have a strong expatriate clientele but their footfall has staggered over the last one month. Also, bookings for corporate luncheons and parties have not been encouraging this month," restaurant director Shiv Karan Singh says.

At Tabula Rasa in Saket, owner Sohrab Sitaram says: "About 40 per cent to 50 per cent of our revenue was generated through parties but this month the bookings have dipped by 20 per cent. Our corporate clients are cancelling bookings and even at the parties that we are currently organising, hosts are trimming their budgets."

Sitaram says one way to cut cost is going for cheaper alternatives for alcohol.

Though restaurateurs insist local customers are not alarmed by the slowdown, the picture is hardly rosy. Ritu Dalmia of Diva says, "Sales of imported wines have dipped big time at restaurants. There has been a considerable dip in the guest list too, but it is not so alarming."

At The Big Chill in Khan Market, where a plate of pasta or creamy cheese cake usually came after an hour long waiting over weekends, reservations are easier now. Owner Aseem Grover says, "Starting mid-September, the next two months are filled with festivities. People tend to go slow on dining out. We see a drop of 10 per cent to 15 per cent during this season every year but that hardly has anything to do with the economic slowdown."

Restaurants are now going heavy on strategies to attract guests. For instance, there are luncheons with free-flowing champagne and exotic brunch dos to pull back guests. Varun Tuli, of The Yum Yum Tree, says: "We are getting guests from the five-stars also; we conjure up a similar experience for lesser rates. Many standalone restaurants now offer a similar ambience with smart food and expatriate chefs that was once a forte of five-star hotels."

But not all is lost: a major dip in rentals due to the slowdown is a good sign, says food consultant Sudha Kukreja. "Rentals are going down and it is very encouraging for new restaurateurs in search of ideal locations," she says. "People eat out of habit, and restaurants, especially in the medium segment, hardly lose out on clients."

"We are still reaping the rewards of last year. Restaurants are barely hit since the rentals have gone down," says food consultant Manu Mohindra, currently handling 70-odd restaurant projects across Delhi and NCR.

Heading: Too young or too old for nursery admissions? - Indian Express
Content:
November 14, celebrated as Children's Day, is just another day in the calendar for Lokkhi, as the teenager waits for her father to come here and take her home.

Working as a domestic help in an executive couple's house in Gurgaon's upscale Kendriya Vihar in Sector 56, the 13-year-old says she has lost count of the number of days and months since she left home in Karimganj, a small village on the India-Bangladesh border in Assam.

Two days after she was rescued from her employers' home, Lokkhi is now recuperating at the Salam Balak Home here.

Beaten and bruised, both physically and emotionally, the teenager said, "I am happy here. I do not have to do any work — they do not even ask me to wash my plate and spoon."

Brought to Gurgaon by "Ajay-da", who she said was a neighbour back in her village, she was shown the usual dreams: of a comfortable life with little work. Her mother died many years ago, and for her family now means her elderly father and two elder brothers, who, she said, are working abroad.

Her father, she said, lost his vision partially after an accident.

Lokkhi — Bangla for Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth — was rescued by the National Commission for Women and the NGO Shakti Vahini on November 8, following complaints lodged against her employers Debokjyoti Das and Paromita. The couple works as senior executives in reputed firms.

So, what prompted her employers to beat her so cruelly? Lokkhi said Paromita did not like the "tone and the pitch in which I had said 'coming' when she called for me that morning."

A neighbour, who did not want to be named, said: "We did not know Lokkhi, we had never even seen her. But we were forced to take action (register complaint with NCW) following repeated complaints by our help — she said the girl had confided to her that her employers beat her regularly."

At the children's home, Lokkhi remembers the last Durga Puja and Saraswati Puja in her village — "I wore new clothes." But that's history. At the Das household, she alleged, her employers not only beat her, "regularly and often without any reason", but also encouraged their children, aged 4 and 5 years, to hit her.

"There were days when I went to bed hungry as I could not eat the mashed leftovers of the children — the only food given to me," she said. "I was forced to eat those leftovers only when I felt very weak. On the few occasions I accompanied them out, they threatened me and told me not to tell anyone the reason behind my bruises."

Lokkhi has clot in her right eye and she said her vision was hazy. Two of her upper incisors are partly broken and her face, neck, arms, waist and legs are scarred with injury marks — some fresh, some old.

Heading: MCD contractor shot dead - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi Public School, Mathura Road, recently published an advertisement specifying the upper age limit for children seeking admissions in nursery, in violation of a government order that says the child should be three plus by March 31 in the year admission is sought for the pre-school class.

Some parents, however, feel such specific advertisements at least create less confusion. The DoE guidelines set no upper age limit. Three-plus years on a particular date can mean anything, a parent said.

Education Secretary Rina Ray said on Monday that fixing an upper age limit would mean discrimination on the basis of age which violates the basic principles of the Right to Education Bill, recently cleared by the Cabinet. "We don't have to wait for the bill to come into effect," she said. "We can follow it in good spirit. You can't deny a child admission on the basis of age."

For parents, the DoE guidelines are ambiguous and they would rather have schools fix an upper age limit as part of their admission criteria rather than waste energy and resources on applying to schools where their child could be rejected on the basis of age.

In case of DPS Mathura Road, the child should be born between April 1, 2005 to March 31, 2006 to be eligible for admissions in nursery.

"Schools must define upper and lower age limits," Sanjay Singh, a parent based in Vasant Vihar, said. "We want them to make it very clear. Only then can parents channelise their efforts and apply to the schools for which their children are eligible. The Supreme Court has given the schools autonomy. Whether or not they follow the DoE guidelines is up to them."

However, the big question is: where do children born in January, February or in March in 2005 go? a parent, who did not wish to be named, asked. "There should be a uniform pattern that all schools should follow with regard to age," he said.

Two other schools, DPS International and Mount Carmel, set September 30, 2008, as their cut-off date for the child to be three plus years as opposed to March 31, 2009. But these are exceptions. One being a minority school and the other being an international one, do not come within the purview of the DoE.

Satish Mohindra, who runs a play school in Nehru Enclave, said such confusion is unwarranted and given the competition for nursery admission, parents might just change the birth date of the child on the birth certificates to ensure they are eligible for admissions.

"In case the child is four plus, parents will be forced to change dates or else apply to KG class," he said.

After the Delhi government decided to open admissions to three-year-old children last year to catch up with other states that have children between the age group of 5-6 years attending Class I, schools have had to deal with varied age groups in nursery classes, Amol Arora, managing director of Shemrock Schools, said. "Schools are having problems handling three-year-olds," he said. "But very few schools are taking in 4-year-olds too. There's no transparency in admissions. Schools ideally would not like to take a varied age group."

Some parents said they feared their children would get rejected if they were too young or too old, in which case the principal might want them to attend pre-primary class. But for a child to directly attend KG classes without attending formal school is not a good idea, they said.

Heading: Magistrate pulled up for overstepping authority - Indian Express
Content:
A 30-year-old Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) contractor was allegedly shot dead by unidentified assailants, just 100 metres away from the Najafgarh police station and 300 meters away from his home in Outer Delhi, on Monday.

Officers said the incident occurred around 12.15 am this morning, when the victim, identified as Hitender Dagar, alias Sonu, was going home to Najafgarh after attending a function. "Hitender was going home after attending a marriage in the Hastsal area of Uttam Nagar last night. He had gone along with two of his friends in his Swift car. He had dropped them off at their homes when he was murdered in Najafgarh," a senior police officer said.

The police said Hitender was in the driver's seat when he was killed and that the window on the driver's side was broken. "It seems that the assailants first broke the glass and then shot him dead. The engine of his car was also running," the senior officer said. Hitender was shot thrice.

The police rushed Hitender to the Narayani Hospital in the area, where he was declared dead on arrival. His body has been sent for a postmortem.

"While two shots hit him on the neck, he was also shot in the back," the police said.

The police are waiting for postmortem reports before further investigations can be pursued.

Hitender was a resident of Todar Mal Lane in the Najafgarh area and is survived by his wife and two children. His father, Dilbagh Dagar, is a retired PTI teacher and his mother, Kamla Dagar, stood for the recent corporation elections. Hitender also has two brothers.

Apart from being a MCD contractor, Hitender worked as a transporter too and owned three buses, the police said.

The police said that though the police station was nearby, they couldn't hear any thing because a marriage function was going on near the police station and loud music was being played there.

Officers are not yet certain about the reasons for the murder. "His family denied any personal enmity and the exact cause of the incident has not been ascertained yet," the police said.

Officers said they are probing the case from road rage and personal enmity angles. "Initial investigations suggest these two reasons might be behind the murder," the police said. A case of murder was lodged at the Najafgarh police station and further investigations are on. Deputy commissioner of police, Outer District, was unavailable for comments, despite repeated attempts.

Heading: MCD to set up own hot mix plant, fill up potholes - Indian Express
Content:
An act of judicial activism by a magistrate, who overstepped his authority, has earned him words of criticism from an additional sessions judge, who observed that every judicial officer was expected to exercise his or her jurisdiction only within the purview of powers available to them and not otherwise.

Additional Sessions Judge P K Saxena made these remarks while quashing an order by a lower court judge, wherein the latter had passed adverse remarks against the officers of the Karol Bagh police station and sent a copy of the order to the Delhi Police commissioner and Home Secretary, Government of India.

ASJ Saxena held the magistrate's order was not good in law, as it suffered from legal infirmity. "I could not find any justifiable reason on the part of the learned magistrate, as to why without taking any action as against the concerned erring subordinate police official, he was so keen to direct the Commissioner of Police and the Home Secretary, to take steps in compliance of his order and by further directing them to receive a copy of the order personally,?" the court said in a recent order.

The magistrate passed the order in May while hearing a criminal case. An action taken report filed by the police did not go down well with him and he said it smacked of the malafide intent of the police and their attempt to screen offenders. Urging the commissioner and the Home Secretary to receive the order "personally", the magistrate sought stringent actions against the policemen and some reforms in the policing system.

The police subsequently filed a revision petition against the magistrate's order, claiming his was exceeding the authority vested in his office. The prosecutor also said the averments against officials of the Karol Bagh police station were unwarranted and uncalled for, because they had duly complied with the directions of the magistrate during all the hearings.

The court remitted the matter back to the concerned court for trial as per legal provisions.

Heading: Sheila files papers, says she, party will win - Indian Express
Content:
Having received much criticism for the bad condition of roads in the Capital during the monsoon, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi is looking at a new solution for the old problem. Instead of depending on contractors to fill up potholes, the Corporation has given assurances it will take care of the potholes on its own.

The Corporation will set up its own hot mix plant in Faridabad. "Contractors are given contracts for a stretch of road and are unwilling to fill potholes unless they are given a contract for the entire stretch. With our own plant, we will be able to handle the problem of potholes in a better way," a Corporation official said.

The Delhi High Court had in 1998 ordered that hot mix plants be shifted out of Delhi. There are about a dozen plants along the borders with Uttar Pradesh and Haryana.

Most of them are owned by agencies that are into road construction, and the Corporation, which has 16,000 km of road with itself, has to depend on them for its roads.

After the 1998 High Court order was passed, the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) was to lay down guidelines for the setting up of hot mix plants in Delhi but no guidelines have been drawn up in the last ten years. "The Corporation will approach the High Court on this matter. We want the court to give a time-bound direction to the CPCB, so that we can take up this work. We face this problem every monsoon and till the time there is a direction from CPCB, we can't work towards this solution," MCD Standing Committee chairman Vijendar Gupta said.

The Corporation has also proposed that trucks, which carry the mixture from the hot mix plants to construction sites, should be covered. During the winter months, it is difficult to carry on with road construction. "By the time the hot mix is transported from the plant to the site, it cools down a bit. The cold tar doesn't stick and hold on to the road. Consequently, the road can't handle heavy traffic," an officer of the engineering department said.

The Corporation is now working on a new plan. In new specifications for road contractors, which will be out soon, the contractors will need to have closed trucks for transporting the mixture. "Though they cover the truck with a plastic sheet, the practice is not very effective," the engineer said.

"Work on the Faridabad plant will start soon. We hope that by next year there will be fewer potholes on Corporation roads," Gupta said.

Heading: RIL slows down work in Gurgaon SEZ - Indian Express
Content:
With just a day left for candidates to file their nomination papers, a confident Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit on Monday filed her nomination papers for the upcoming Assembly elections at Jamnagar House on Shahjahan Road.

Accompanied by son and Member of Parliament Sandeep Dikshit and daughter Latika at around 11.15 am on Monday, Dikshit filed her nomination from the New Delhi constituency. Dikshit, 71, was also accompanied by her seven-year old grand daugher Aafia who was cheering for her grandmother along with a crowd of party supporters standing outside Jamnagar House blocking the entire area.

Aafia is class II student of Sanskriti School and the daughter of Dikshit's daughter Latika. She was holding a huge Congress flag in support of her grandmother who was filing her nomination papers inside.

In her affidavit filed with returning officer Faizi Hashmi, Dikshit, gave a break-up of her assets. These include a house in south Delhi's Nizamuddin locality with a current market value of over Rs 63 lakh and about Rs 45 lakh invested in mutual funds.

However, unlike her BJP counterpart VK Malhotra who had BJP stalwarts like Arun Jaitley, Sushma Swaraj, Vijay Goel and even Mayor Arti Mehra welcoming him at Jamnagar House last Saturday, Diskhit was accompanied only by Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee (DPCC) chief JP Aggarwal in the morning.

Incidentally, both Aggarwal and Dikshit, members of the Central Election Committee of the Congress have reportedly been at loggerheads over finalising candidates for the state Assembly elections over the last one week.

Minister of state for Urban Development, Ajay Maken, also Member of Parliament from the New Delhi constituency was conspicuous by absence.

After filing her nomination, Diskhit said she is proud of the Congress and is confident that the party will come back to power.

"I will win from my constituency," she said after referring to her government's efforts to build flyovers and infrastructure in the Capital.

Other leaders who filed their nomination papers are Power Minister AK Walia from Laxmi Nagar and Dr Harsh Vardhan from Krishna Nagar.

Heading: Choudhary sets stage for state-level function on Nov 15 - Indian Express
Content:
Call it the global meltdown or the increased restrictions over the Special Economic Zones (SEZs), Mukesh Ambani-led the Reliance Industries Limited has slowed down its ambitious multi-product SEZ at Gurgaon.

Company sources, on condition of anonymity, said the company has been finding it difficult to acquire land after the restrictions and state's non-intervening attitude towards land acquisition.

The SEZ is likely to go in cold storage till the economic condition improves and congenial atmosphere is created for developing it in the state.

However, the company, according to the sources, would continue with its plans to develop certain facilities at the 1,500 acre piece of land provided by the Haryana Industries and Infrastructure Development Corporation (HSIIDC). Sources said company's land acquisition drive had almost halted after the revised land acquisition policy of the state. Certain farmers of the area, on their own or at the behest of opposition parties, had refused to sell their land to the RIL.

But after the revised policy even those who were ready to sell, started demanding exorbitant prices.

"We had never expected this and could have purchased nearly 8,000 acres of more land at Jhajjar.

We were expecting the state would come to our rescue for contiguity of the area but with the recent restrictions it has become a herculean task to purchase land," said a senior functionary of the RIL, who was closely associated with the SEZ.

It is better to wait than to hurry in such a venture where so much money is at stake, he added.

Ironically, the proposed SEZ, touted as the biggest in the country, has been suffering one jolt after the other ever since its conception, about three years ago.

The company had planned to develop its Rs 40,000 crore- SEZ over an area of 25,000 acres. It purchased land scattered in various areas of Jhajjar, depending on the government in acquiring it. The land was purchased at about Rs 22 lakh per acre, the opposition parties entered the arena and demanded a higher price for the farmers.

This led the Centre to interfere and a parliamentary committee, after visiting the site, put a number of restrictions on the size of the SEZ. With one stroke the biggest SEZ of the country was reduced to half its size at 12,500 acres. However, the RIL still found a leeway and decided to raise two SEZs of equal size in the area. But the state revised its land acquisition policy and decided not to interfere in the land acquisition by any company, making it difficult for the company to negotiate with the farmers.

RIL sources are tightlipped, but conceded that the work has slowed down because of other reasons as well. "We are trying to convince the company to continue its drive to acquire land. We would be ready to help them within the limits of our policy regarding the SEZs," said a senior officer.

Heading: Paddy arrives in state mandis - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Sports and Tourism Minister Kiran Choudhary is now camping in Bhiwani for organising a state-level function to mark the 62 birth anniversary of late Surinder Singh on November 15.

The function is politically significant as Surinder Singh's daughter, Shruti, is a strong contender for the Congress ticket.

Sources said Kiran Choudhary is trying to motivate all the villages of Bhiwani to come and remember their leader on the day. It will prove useful to seek votes during the Lok Sabha election.

Presently, she is holding a series of rallies at Tosham Assembly constituency to ensure the function is a great success. Union Minister Pranab Mukherjee and Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda besides other senior leaders will address the function.

A big statue of late Surinder Singh will be installed and announcement relating to development of Bhiwani are expected.Talking to The Indian Express, Kiran Choudhary said a big crowd is expected. Shruti would contest the election if she is given the party ticket by the party high command. We are members of the party and we are bound to obey the party's directives.

Heading: Migrants from state prefer Maharashtra for work, Rajasthan for marriage: Census - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 33.99 lakh tonnes of paddy arrived in the state mandis during the current Kharif season. A spokesman of the Food and Supplies Department said out of the total paddy arrival, about 17.59 lakh tonnes has been procured by the government agencies at the minimum support price and the remaining 16.40 lakh tonnes has been purchased by the private millers and traders, which includes 3.23 lakh tonnes leviable and 13.16 lakh tonnes non-leviable paddy.

Hafed has procured 7.45 lakh tonnes, Food and Supplies Department has procured 5.22 lakh tonnes, Haryana Agro Industries Corporation, 1.80 lakh tonnes, HWC 67,189 tonnes, FCI 8,454 tonnes and Confed has purchased 2.35 lakh tonnes of paddy.

Kurukshetra district lead with the arrival of 6.76 lakh tonnes, followed by Karnal 5.76 lakh tonnes, Fatehabad 4.33 lakh tonnes, Kaithal 3.80 lakh tonnes, Ambala 3.14 lakh, Yamunanagar 2.36 lakh tonnes, Jind 2.07 lakh tonnes, Sirsa 1.63 lakh tonnes, Panipat 1.42 lakh tonnes, Faridabad 91,186 tonnes, Sonepat 75,243 tonnes, Panchkula 43,890 tonnes, Hisar 36,756 tonnes, Rohtak 12,964 tonnes and Mewat 7,574 tonnes of paddy.

Similarly, 3.31 lakh metric tonnes of Bajra arrived in the mandis during the current Kharif season. Out of the total Bajra arrival, 3.11 lakh metric tonnes has been procured by the government agencies at the minimum support price and the remaining, about 20,126 metric tonnes, has been purchased by the private traders.

Heading: Haryana forest department proposes project to World Bank - Indian Express
Content:
When it comes to work and employment, Maharashtra is the most favoured destination of the Haryanvis. While the state popular among them, when it comes to marrying off their daughters, is Rajasthan.

These were some of the interesting facts, that came to light in the recent compilation of the census figures by the state, under separate heads, by the Haryana Census Department. The figures are based on the 2001 census and reveal Maharashtra attracted the highest number of migrants from Haryana for employment at 27.5 per cent, followed by Chandigarh at 27.21 per cent. Rajasthan attracted maximum number of brides from the state, followed by Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Delhi. Delhi also has the highest number of Haryanvis with 5.55 lakh migrants from the state. Punjab came in next with 3.6 lakh and Rajasthan with 3.51 lakh

migrants.

Chandigarh attracted more than 85,000 people. Maharashtra, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu Kashmir were way behind, according to the data available. Haryanvis coming for work to Delhi and other purposes was 35.25 per cent, followed by 22.91 per cent in Punjab and 22.30 per cent in Rajasthan. Despite Chandigarh's growing status as an attractive investment destination, it could attract just 5.41 per cent of the Haryanvis.

Talking to The Indian Express, Karan Singh, Additional Director Census Department, Haryana, said one important facet was the study of migration arising out of various social, cultural, economic or political reasons. For a large country like India, the complexity of movement of population in different parts of the country helps in understanding the dynamics of society, he said.

As far as inter-state migration is concerned, Faridabad has the largest number of migrants born in other states, while Jind district had the lowest number of migrants. Karnal district has the highest concentration of international migrants, while

Mahendragarh district has the lowest. Nepal contributes 9.22 per cent of the total international migrants in Haryana, the census data revealed.

Heading: Homoeopathic association alleges favouritism in recruitment - Indian Express
Content:
With the aim to bring 20 per cent of the total land under forests by 2020, the Haryana State Forest department has proposed a Resource Management and Livelihood Project to the World Bank for funding. The project has been approved by the Government of India and approval from the World Bank is expected soon.

The project cost is estimated to be Rs 230 crore and it will be implemented in 500 villages over 11 districts, including Ambala, Panchkula, Kurukshetra, Sirsa, Fatehabad, Bhiwani and Rewari.

S K Dhar, Principal Chief Conservator of Forests told The Indian Express, a three-member pre-approval mission of World Bank visited Haryana recently and was convinced to sanction the project to the state.

"The team has suggested a few changes in the proposal with new components to be added. They have asked us to include the water logged areas of Jhajjar, Rohtak, Sonepat in the plan. After that the financial agreement will be signed," said Dhar.

The objective of the project is to improve the environment through sustainable management of rural resources and reduction of green house gases. The project will undertake the necessary steps to generate Kyoto-compliant carbon credits under the roles established for afforestation and reforestation as well as energy efficient activities under Clean Development Mechanism. The carbon credits generated by the projects will represent an additional income for the local communities.

Dhar said, "Our focus will be to work with the local community and help women empowerment.

We will also encourage formation of self help groups to involve people in various activities. Special attention will be paid to the needs and perspectives of various disadvantaged groups. The model villages are ready and the strategy is to enhance the radius of our activities."

The project will stabilise the surface sand over 5,000 hectares, create barriers for moving sands and reduce evapo-transpiration at the erodible sites of Shivaliks.

The project will make 10,000 hectares of barren land productive by plantation of trees, grass and shrubs.

Besides, an ongoing project on integrated natural resource management and poverty reduction is being executed with the financial assistance of Rs 286 crore from the Japan Bank of International Cooperation. "Under the project, the department has set a target to bring 48,800 hectares under tree plantation by 2011. About 330 villages will be covered under this and a review mission is expected by next month," said Dhar.

Heading: Victim lying or cops shooting in the dark? - Indian Express
Content:
Dr P S Ranu, state convener of the Indian Homoeopathic Medical Association (IHMA), has alleged that the entrance test to recruit Homoeopathic Medical Officers on contractual basis, under the National Rural Health Mission Scheme (NRHM), was nothing more than a "backdoor entry to adjust candidates for some pecuniary interests".

Dr Ranu, also a member of the Central Council of Homoeopathy and former chairman of Homoeopathic Council, raised numerous questions in an official statement on Monday regarding the process of recruitment adopted by the state government.

"Nothing was mentioned about a written test in the first advertisement issued by the government. The age limit of 60 years was also unjustified as many retired medical officials apply on the basis of their experience. Candidates appearing in the test were totally unaware of the pattern of the examination, syllabus and distribution of marks. Even the general public did not know if a selection committee had been formed and what was the process adopted by the committee, who were the examiners and passed out from which university," the statement read.

"In October, the Chandigarh Administration had also recruited Homoeopathic and Ayurvedic Medical Officers under NRHM scheme without holding any test and entirely on the basis of merit," said Dr Ranu.

Flaying the recruitment entrance test for Homoeopathic Medical Officers, the IHMA-Punjab unit urged the state chief minister to check the ongoing recruitment process under NRHM for becoming a "one-man show" at the hands of a senior bureaucrat.

Heading: Mohali gets cyber police station, forensic lab - Indian Express
Content:
As the victim's statements differ from the call details gathered by the police in the Panchkula gangrape case, Newsline profiles the persons involved in the case.

"Though the FIR states the name of two accused — Jatin and Chhavi — along with three unidentified youths, the names of Jatin, Jitesh, Chhavi, Aman Ahuja and Tanu figure in the victim's statement recorded before the magistrate," said DSP (City) Ram Chander Rathi.

On the basis of cellphone call details, the role of another youth, Chanky Sharma alias Sunny, is also being probed.

Jitesh
Jitesh, a resident of Sector 4, Panchkula, is the main accused. According the victim's statement, Jitesh has been mistakenly referred to as Jatin in the FIR. She alleged that the youth was involved in making a pornographic MMS of her at the Indian Palace hotel a year ago and raped her several times before September 16 as well. While the victim claims that she was taken to Morni on September 5 by Jitesh, according to the police, the call details show both were in Sector 25, Panchkula. Jitesh's family claim the youth was at home on the day of the crime.

Chhavi
The girl's identity is still a mystery for the police. According to the victim, Chhavi was her senior at school and was involved in making the MMS . Chhavi also allegedly tortured the victim.

Chanky Sharma alias Sunny
The victim gave him a clean chit stating that Sunny is a good 'friend' but the police are not so sure. According to the police, call details show that both were together on the day of crime. Sunny, a resident of Sector 4, is the son of a businessman.
According to member of Chanky's family: "Sunny was alone with the girl on September 16 till late at night owing to which he got a beating from his father."

Kushal Kaushal
A national-level judo player, Kaushal's car was reportedly involved in transporting the victim from Sector 12-A , Panchkula, to Chandigarh on the day of the crime. The youth was also involved in a group clash on September 14. While the victim claims that the youth was involved, according to the police, Kaushal's call details do not substantiate the fact. His anticipatory bail application will be heard in the court on Tuesday.

Aman Ahuja
According to the victim, Ahuja was involved in making the MMS and blackmailed her last year. The girl says that while he threatened her on the day of the crime, he did not rape her. Ahuja, a resident of Sector 10, is the son of the Haryana Additional District Transport Officer and was released on bail earlier.

Jatin
According to the victim's statement, Jatin was one of the persons who raped her on September 16. Jatin's details are still not known to the police.

Heading: Admn officials inspect Leisure Valley ahead of Chandigarh Carnival - Indian Express
Content:
Rs 8-crore project to end Punjab Police's dependency on other labs across the country

Mohali police on Monday took a lead in getting the state's first cyber crime police station-cum-forensic science laboratory. The Rs 8-crore state-of-the-art project will end the Punjab Police's dependency on forensic science laboratories in other states for various tests.

So far, the Punjab Police were depending on forensic science laboratories in Chandigarh, Ahmedabad and Bangalore for various types of forensic tests.

N P S Aulakh, Punjab Director General of Police (DGP), kickstarted work on the four-storeyed building, which will come up in Phase IV, by laying its foundation stone.

The building — which will house a cyber crime police station and laboratories in Physics, Texilogy, lie-detection, Biology, Chemistry and Ballistic, as part of forensic science — will come up within two years. The Punjab Police Housing Corporation (PPHC) is the executing agency of the project.

In his inaugural speech, the Punjab DGP said the project is a step forward for the Punjab Police towards becoming cyber-savvy and a hi-tech police force with effective investigation of crimes through advanced modes.

Lauding the dedication and professionalism of PPHC, Aulakh said that the PPHC will soon sign an MoU with the Karnataka State Police Housing Corporation for a web-based project management system, which will help in close monitoring of the progress, including quality control and introduction of the e-tendering system within a period of six months.

Besides, another MoU will be signed with the Border Security Force (BSF) to undertake the construction of their future projects in the state.

He added that the construction work of the Punjab Police Training Institute for private security guards at Jahan Khelan is in full swing and will be completed by June 2009.

The institute, which is worth Rs 10 crore, will provide training to 4,000 security guards every year and with the implementation of the Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act, 2005, the training of private security guards to be hired by the private security agencies has become imperative to create employment opportunities for the unemployed of the state. On this occasion, the DGP gave away certificates to 18 officers of the PPHC for their excellent performance during 2008.

Heading: New SGPC chief will be elected on Nov 22 - Indian Express
Content:
Officials of the Chandigarh Administration today inspected the Leisure Valley in Sector 10, the site for the Chandigarh Carnival starting November 22.

A team of senior officials, headed by Home Secretary Ram Niwas, inspected the venue and instructed officials to expedite the preparation work to make the carnival a remarkable event.

While inspecting the site, Niwas asked the officials to earmark specific places for the Police Control Room, Senior Citizens' Corner, traffic station, food court and stalls. He directed the officials to expedite the process for the same and work in sync with other departments.

Ram Niwas also instructed the civic officials to set up a pyramid of flowers in front of the main entry point to the carnival to add more colour to the event.

Niwas also guided the officials of the Electrical Wing to properly light up the carnival and provide special colourful lights on the trees surrounding the area.

Police officers were also asked to take suitable security measures during the Chandigarh Carnival.

Heading: 18 yrs in jail, 70-yr-old convict awaits President’s decision on mercy plea - Indian Express
Content:
ON THE HOT SEAT Makkar may get yet another term; Bibi Jagir Kaur and Badungar also in race; Badal may keep LS polls in mind

The election to the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) chief's post for one-year term will be held on November 22 at Teja Singh Samundari Hall here.

Though incumbent Avtar Singh Makkar is emerging as a frontrunner, two more former heads of the body, Bibi Jagir Kaur and Kirpal Singh Badungar, are also pulling the strings.

The coming parliamentary elections would also weigh heavy on the minds of CM Parkash Singh Badal and SAD (B) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, as they would like to have one of their loyalists on the post.

Though Badal had chosen Makkar, the "urban face of Sikhs", three years ago, there is likelihood that junior Badal might assign some other responsibility to him in the party, keeping in mind the ensuing Lok Sabha polls.

"I have done fairly well. See the developmental works carried out during my last three successive terms, the dharam prachaar, celebration of various centenaries and taking up of Sikh issues on the international platform. Given a chance, I will continue to serve the panth with devotion," said Makkar, while talking to The Indian Express.

He also said that in the first term, one learns about the administration, in the second, plans are made and results are achieved in the third term. "In the fourth term, the experience thus gained will be used for the benefit of the religious body," he said.

Makkar, though non-controversial and a loyal soldier of the party, was often criticised for being a "weak president" by his detractors. He was also accused of being a "feeble administrator" during jathedars' tussles.

On the other hand, his followers feel that his placid approach weakens the controversies. There were also allegations of favouritism and corruption, but those were never proved.

On the other hand, Bibi Jagir Kaur is making earnest efforts to grab the seat once again. Though a tough administrator, Badal family loyalist and shrewd politician, Bibi may suffer due to the murder case of her daughter, Harpreet Kaur, which is pending in the court. The verdict would have far-reaching ramifications on the ruling party, but if Badal is ready to take risk to gain political mileage due to her mass following, he might choose Bibi.

Another Badal loyalist and educated urban Sikh leader Kirpal Singh Badungar might also come out of hibernation. He is a strategist with a long experience in managing party's affairs that could prove beneficial during the Lok Sabha elections, as Akalis' "gurdwara politics" would once again emerge as a key factor in the polls, which are also an acid test for the one-and-a-half-year-old Badal government in the state.

There is also a possibility that Badal, instead of choosing any of these bigwigs, might bring in a new face to avoid political hobnobbing in the poll season.

Dissidence during in the election year might prove detrimental for the party at a time when stakes are high. Badal family might look for a seasoned but non-controversial figure to head the body that has an annual budget of Rs 400 crore.

"Badal might get a political leader to head the cash-rich body this time," said a political scientist at Guru Nanak Dev University.

Heading: Final draw for Sec-63 housing scheme held - Indian Express
Content:
Model-turned-actor Mugdha Godse on life after Fashion

When director Madhur Bhandarkar came to Mugdha Godse with the script of Fashion, the model was unsure about how her character would make an impact, considering the stronger roles for co-actors Priyanka Chopra and Kangana Ranaut. "But that was before I read the script. Once I was through, I knew Janet's character had as much scope to perform. If I did it with honesty, it could get me a little appreciation," says Godse. In the movie, she plays the second-rung model, Janet, married to a gay designer.

It has been a week since the movie released, but the "little appreciation" that Godse had hoped for, has snowballed into generous accolades. "There's been a steady stream of congratulatory messages and phonecalls. Priyanka texted 'Babe, you blew my mind!' at three in the morning, and I was totally floored. The one person who is vindicated is Madhur sir. Everytime he told me I had it in me to make it as an actor, I would tell him not to speculate. Now, with each review that I have received, he has been telling me 'I told you so'," she giggles.

For Godse, the most touching praise has come from her family. "My family is quite critical of me, so I was apprehensive of their reaction. They went for first-day-first-show, when I was still promoting the film in Dubai. My sister later told me they were left speechless by my performance," she says.

There have been quite a few offers since the movie released, but the model-turned-actor says she will only announce them once she signs on the dotted line. "As of now, I have signed with Percept Picture Company for three of their films," she says. Modelling, she says, will definitely be on the backburner for the time being. "Fashion's given me opportunities which I would be stupid to ignore. It's not as if I am giving up modelling completely, but I'll do only select shows," she says.

Heading: Even in Canada, Punjabis don’t want daughters: Writer - Indian Express
Content:
The final draw for the Self-Financing Housing Scheme in Sector 63 of the Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) was held at the Government Medical College and Hospital auditorium in Sector 32 on Monday.

The draw of lots was conducted for a total of 276 units of the three-bedroom flats (186 general category, 36 in SC, 14 each in defence, OBC and retired personnel category (RP), while 9 in physically handicapped and three in Board employee category).

In the two-bedroom category, 754 units were put for draw, where 505 were placed under general category, 99 in SC, 40 each in defence, OBC and RP group, 24 in PH (physically handicapped) and six in Board employee categories.

In the one-bedroom category, out of a total of 482 units, 328 were put in for general category, 63 for SC, 25 each for DP, OBC and RP category, 15 for PH and 1 for Board category.

For the waiting list, 20 per cent of the total in each category was taken out in the draw. These applicants selected in the waiting list are active for one year and in case there is any default or cancellation by the final selected applicants, the waiting list will be considered for allotment.

During this one year, the applicants in the waiting list will not be allowed to refund the application money.

For allottees opting for installments, the Board will charge an interest of 12 per cent per annum. The allotment will be made on leasehold basis for a period of 99 years. During this period, the allottees will be required to pay a ground rent at the rate of 0.25 per cent per annum of the price of the dwelling unit.

Heading: Dengue outbreak: Bathinda health officials inspect jail - Indian Express
Content:
