The incidence of female foeticide is so high among Punjabis in Canada that the US doctors, who own scan centers, advertise in Canadian Punjabi newspapers. This was stated by well-known Punjabi writer Ajmer Rode at a function organised to release and discuss his play, 'Nirlaj', which is also based on the issue of foeticide.

Rode, who lives in Canada, said, "Some time back, a few organisations and writers began a protest campaign and we forced the newspaper owners not to publish the adverts of such doctors. Though we were successful in our campaign, the practice of killing unborn daughters is still prevalent in our community."

The author, who along with his brother Navtej Bharti is known for a classic in Punjabi poetry, 'Leela', said, "The first draft of this play was written in 1996, when an organisation opposing female foeticide wanted to stage it. It was a skit at that time, but then the menace assumed alarming proportions and I decided to turn it into a full-fledged play."

Taking the discussion further, Punjabi thinker and critic Amarjeet Singh Grewal said, "This practice of killing daughters is most common in Jat Sikhs, and the reason behind it is the feudal system."

Grewal said, "Sadly, the Jats, who consider themselves to be the true Sikhs, do not practise what is written in the Guru Granth Sahib or the rehat maryada. Guru Granth Sahib has a very clear stand against female foeticide, and rehat maryada orders

Sikhs not to keep any relation with people who kill their daughters."

Heading: Human trafficking case: ‘Daler need not  surrender passport’ - Indian Express
Content:
Fearing that dengue might grip Bathinda Central Jail, a team of district health officials, led by Civil Surgeon Dr Neelam Bajaj, today visited the prison and instructed the staff to adopt precautionary measures.

The Health Department has been on tenterhooks due to a large number of dengue cases reported in the city. "In Bathinda city alone, 10 confirmed cases have been reported and about 100 are suspected cases," said district epidemiologist Dr MS Gill, adding that the number of confirmed cases in the district stood at 205 till date.

Notably, the required machine for dengue treatment in Bathinda hospital had developed a snag and could be made operational only in mid-October, before which patients were forced to go to Ludhiana.

"Today's visit was aimed at spreading awareness in the jail, where dengue larvae were found a few days ago," said Dr Bajaj. She said, "There was a suspected case of dengue in the jail, which later tested negative. The inmate had a fatty liver."

Meanwhile, the Health Department carried out fogging inside the jail. "We do not want to take chances. Even if it is viral fever, I have instructed the jail's medical officer to conduct a test for dengue as well," said Bathinda Jail Superintendent Capt LS Jakhar.

Heading: P’kula gangrape: HC notices to Haryana DGP, SP - Indian Express
Content:
In a major relief to Punjabi pop singer Daler Mehndi, an accused in a human trafficking case, a local court here today allowed him to use of his passport. While hearing the case, Judicial Magistrate First Class PS Rai today dismissed the application moved by the complainant, Bakshish Singh, through his counsel Gurpreet Singh, seeking the surrender of Daler's passport before the trial court.

The complainant had pleaded that since all the other accused in the case had submitted their passports, Daler should also surrender it till the trial was on. Daler's counsel BS Sodhi said the singer had not misused his passport and had been present in the court on every hearing.

The defence also pleaded that since Daler was a singer, he required the passport for overseas performances. He said surrendering the passport was also not a pre-condition during the grant of his regular bail application.

Notably, Daler's passport was earlier seized by the police in 2003 when his name cropped up in the case.

Daler later sought the release of his passport in June 2004 and then submitted it after travelling abroad. He again sought the court's permission to get his passport, which was allowed in 2004.

Ever since, Daler has kept his passport.

Heading: Edict for BJP ministers who failed to keep date with public - Indian Express
Content:
Petitioner had moved court demanding that probe be transferred to an independent investigating agency

The Punjab and Haryana High Court has issued notices to the Haryana Director General of Police Ranjiv Dalal, Superintendent of Police Sandeep Khirwar and Station House Officer of the Sector-14 police station, Panchkula, on a petition filed by Geeta Nayyar. Nayyar is the mother of the 17-year-old girl who was allegedly gangraped by four persons in September.

The petitioner had moved High Court demanding that the investigation be transferred to an independent investigating agency like the Criminal Investigation Agency or the Central Bureau of Investigation.

On Monday, the petition came up for hearing before Justice Pritam Pal. But he questioned the request asking: "You mean the Haryana Police is not an independent agency? Are they not functioning properly? Have they not arrested the accused?"

In reply, advocate Gaurav Singh Hooda said the Haryana Police are not conducting a proper investigation and are shielding the actual accused. Taking note of the accusations, the High Court issued notices to the Haryana government and the police officers concerned.

Alleging shoddy investigation by the Haryana Police, the petition states that the police omitted certain facts disclosed by the victim.

"Despite several requests, the police did not collect the clothes worn by my daughter at the time of the incident. Even during the medico-legal examination of the victim, the police exerted pressure upon the medical staff to misrepresent facts in order to help the accused. The local DSP and the SHO visited our house on a few occasions, late in the night, and asked my daughter to accompany them on the pretext of questioning. We have also received several threats from the police to reach a compromise with the accused," reads the petition.

Heading: HP to get 3,800-cr ADB funding - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) isn't much impressed with the way its ministers have been treating party's much-flaunted public meeting sessions held everyday at the party office here.

BJP ministers in Punjab are supposed to sit in the office for at least two hours everyday, between 11 am and 1 pm, to redress public grievances. However, the ministers often missed their date with the people on one pretext or the other.

The state unit of the BJP has now stepped in to make amends. It has officially communicated to its ministers to intimate their absence at least a couple of days prior to their turn. They have also been asked to give reasons for it.

The directive by the state units said that ministers could swap their task with another minister in case of an urgent commitment.

The meeting aimed at holding a face-to-face dialogue between ministers and public. BJP sources said visitors, many whom reached the party office in Chandigarh from distant places, were invariable left waiting for the minister, who never turned up, and they were asked to come again.

Another recurring grouse was delayed arrivals. A two-hour session has been anything but possible. A team of The Indian Express visited the party office today and Industry Minister Manoranjan Kalia, who was scheduled to come today, reached 50 minutes late.

Cabinet minister Swarna Ram, who had been ill for quite some time, gets the benefit of doubt. President of the Punjab BJP Rajinder Bhandari said, "The letter was sent to ensure that ministers meet public regularly. Our effort is to redress people's problems."

Heading: State to work on traceability, safety of farm produce - Indian Express
Content:
Aid for four medium, mega hydel projects will boost power generation plans

Making a major breakthrough in the power sector, the Prem Kumar Dhumal government today entered into a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to avail $ 800 million (approximately Rs 3,800 crore) funding for hydel power generation.

For the hill state, whose annual budget for 2008-09 is just Rs 12,542 crore, the ADB assistance for four medium and mega hydel projects is expected to give a major boost to power generation plans.

The funding, which will be in the ratio of 90:10 as grant and loan, would be utilised under Himachal Pradesh Clean Energy Development Investment Programme.

The agreement was signed by Govind Mohan, Director (Infrastructure), Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, on behalf of the Government of India and Tadashi Kondo, Country Director of Indian Resident Mission of Asian Development Bank, in Delhi today.

The project agreement was signed by state's Principal Secretary (Power) Ajay Mittal, Himachal Power Corporation MD Tarun Kapoor and Jagdish Sharma, Member (Finance), in the State Electricity Board.

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal congratulated the authorities for succeeding in getting the highest-ever ADB loan sanctioned for the state, which is bound to boost hydel power generation in the state.

He said that the state government had been pursuing the case at different stages with the Government of India and ADB to get the amount sanctioned on priority so that execution of the proposed projects could be started on priority.

The projects identified for execution by the Himachal Power Corporation with ADB funding include

Sawra-Kuddu (111 MW); Kashang-I, II and III (195 MW), Sainj Project (100 MW) and the Shongtong-Karchham (402 MW). The state government, so far, has allotted six projects to the Corporation.

The total generation from these four projects will be in an order of 3,434 million units and the estimated cost would be about Rs 7,500 crore, of which the ADB has agreed to finance $ 800 million in the form of a multi-tranche financing facility.

"The loan will be covering around 53.3 per cent cost of the projects. For the remaining amount, funding will be arranged from equity and other financial institutions. The biggest advantage to Himachal will be that the funding will be on the pattern of 90:10, grant and loan, respectively, and will be repaid over a period of 25 years," said Dhumal here.

Himachal has a power potential of 21,000 MW, of which only 6,400 MW has been exploited so far.

However, some Central PSUs, including NHPC, NTPC, and joint ventures and the private sector have been allotted major projects to generate at least 10,000 MW of power by 2015.

Heading: Cong accuses govt of political vendetta - Indian Express
Content:
Having already carved a niche in the production of the finest fruit varieties — now also having a demand in foreign markets — and off-seasonal vegetables, Himachal Pradesh is looking ahead to promote sustainable farm practices of world recognition.

For the first time, the state has started working on the food traceability issue, one of the key ingredients already adopted in some foreign countries to ensure safe and efficient supply of farm produce. Together with this, the government proposes to address the issue of food safety and introduce clean farm practices — mainly the production of organic vegetables and fruits grown under controlled conditions.

Elaborating on some innovative plans, state's Principal Secretary (Agriculture) P.C. Kapoor said a beginning has already been made in organic farming in some areas of the state. "An Rs 154.92-crore project has been sanctioned to encourage farmers to set up polyhouses, use sprinklers/drip irrigation and follow strict organic farm practices. The produce will be properly branded and marketed at recognised sale outlets under the organic food chain," he revealed here.

One of the systems that has become popular in foreign countries such as Japan and China is food traceability. Explains Kapoor, "This means the consumers who buy the produce will get to know the origin of produce and also its producer on the farm. Himachal has already started working on this and is framing farm modules and practices."

In fact, the trend has already taken root in the floriculture sector and to some extent in horticulture in Kullu and Shimla districts. The vegetable-growing farmers are yet to learn about the issue and switch over to food safety matters. This ultimately will make Himachal farmers fetch a higher price for the produce and meet export marketing demands.

Over 10,000 farmers have already been registered as organic farmers. Once the state government rolls out new plans on crop diversification and polyhouse-based farming for off-season vegetables, they are expected to find it lucrative and innovative.

Kapoor, however, made it clear that the state's agriculture department will not directly enter into any farm or marketing activity. It will rather restrict itself in upgrading farmers' skills, providing technological inputs, clean farm practices, grading and standarisation and inform them about markets available for the sale of certificate farm produce. The government is seeking Japanese collaboration in crop diversification and marketing of quality produce.

One of the problems that the fruit growers and vegetable farmers have faced in marketing is caused due to lack of grading. "Grading is one aspect that requires a serious attention in marketing," he added.

In the agriculture sector, 69 per cent of the state's population is engaged in active farming. Ironically, 80 per cent area is rainfed.

Small and marginal farmers constitute 86.4 per cent of land holdings, while large holdings cover only 0.4 per cent. Thus most of the farmers in Himachal fall in category of small and marginal farmers. Vegetable production is 11.44 lack tonnes,

generating an income of Rs 800 crore.

Heading: Bakery owner in Shimla held after 16 customers take ill - Indian Express
Content:
Accusing the present Bharatiya Janata Party government of allegedly adopting a vengeful attitude to throttle the voice of political opponents, leader of opposition Vidya Stokes today said that the government was misleading the masses over the issue of opening of a medical college in Mandi district.

She said BJP leaders were also trying to take the credit for various developmental schemes initiated by the previous Congress government in different parts of the state. She said the medical college has been sanctioned by the UPA government and the present government had no role in getting it sanctioned.

Talking to mediapersons here today, Stokes said the termination of services of hundreds of teachers recruited by the Parent-Teachers' Association has resulted into a large number of posts lying vacant in hundreds of government schools across the state. This had adversely affected the academic atmosphere in schools, especially in rural parts. Besides, she said the party would also launch a massive door-to-door campaign against the alleged anti-people policies of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party government in view of Parliamentary elections.

She said the alleged anti-people policies of the government have virtually been bringing down its popularity graph. Large-scale transfers of employees out of political vendetta, hike in bus fare and the government's failure in not reducing the value added tax on petroleum products has made the life of the common man more miserable.

Stokes said that previous Congress government, instead of acting vengefully, chose to regularise the services of vidya upasaks appointed by the BJP during its previous regime.

Replying to a question, she said the party high command has decided to field all the sitting members of Parliament in the coming Lok Sabha elections.

Heading: Kangra attracts Delhi-based metal firm - Indian Express
Content:
The owner of a reputed bakery and confectionary shop on The Mall was today arrested by the police and later bailed out, as 16 customers who had consumed burgers and cheese rolls from his shop reported to hospitals with food poisoning. The incident has raised a question on the sanitary and hygienic conditions of the bakery kitchen and the quality of raw material used.

The kitchens are situated in a dilapidated old wooden building near the Lift and do not have a proper drainage system, water and sanitation condition for the people working there.

It is learnt that apart from an annual check, the health department of the Shimla Municipal Corporation conducts no surprise checks apart from the time when the licences are renewed. When asked, health officer of the Corporation, Sonam Negi, said, "When we check them at the time of licence renewal, everything is alright. Though the conditions in their kitchens are not ideal, they are almost satisfactory."

An FIR was registered in the latest case of food poisoning by one of the consumers with the Shimla Sadar Police Station under Section 270 of the IPC. While 13 people from different places across Shimla, all who had consumed burgers on Friday and Thursday last week, reported to Deen Dayal Upadhyaya (DDU) Hospital in Shimla, three persons of a family who had come to Shimla from Mandi are also seeking medical treatment in the hospital.

Dr Arun Chandel, who works with a private hospital in Sundernagar, said all his family members had eaten burgers from The City Point confectioners on November 7 evening and within a few hours, all suffered from stomach ache, dehydration, vomiting and high fever.

Prior to the arrest of shop owner Ravinder Singh, samples of burgers, paneer roll and ketchup were collected and sent for examination to Kandaghat laboratory. The reports are awaited.

Heading: Review departmental clean chit to Haryana officer: HC - Indian Express
Content:
Met Trade India Limited, a Delhi-based private company, is entering this hill state as it has decided to set up non-ferrous metal units at Motli in Indora tehsil of Kangra district. These non-ferrous metal units would be the first of its kind in the state and would also create opportunities to set up various small ancillary units.

The state government had cleared the project, which would be set up at a cost of Rs 500 crore, at the single window clearance meeting held recently.

The company is determined to start the project shortly and is purchasing private land. In fact, the company has already struck a deal with the owners of the land to purchase it and only then had it moved its case with the state government, said sources in the industries department. The company would purchase nearly 900 kanals. Sources said a case to seek permission to purchase land under Section 118 of the HP

Tenancy and Land Reforms Act has been moved to the government through the district administration. They said not only the permission to purchase land would be given without any loss of time, but the land transferred in the name of the company.

Sources said as soon as permission to buy the land is accorded, the company proposes to move a case for the environmental clearance to the Union Ministry of Forest and Environment. Sources said there would not be any hitch in getting environmental clearance as no trees exist on the proposed land.

Sources said these non-ferrous projects would generate direct employment opportunities for as many as 681 persons.

The company would make available employment opportunities to technical hands, skilled and semi-skilled and persons apart from officials. Besides, indirect employment opportunities would also be generated, said sources.

The company proposes three types of projects, namely aluminum, copper projects and lead projects. Under the aluminum project, rolled products, billet logs, alloy ingots and extrusion profiles would be manufactured. The copper products would be tubes and CCR rods.

Similarly, under lead project, lead ingots through electro-refining process, grey, red and litharge lead oxides and lead alloy ingots would be manufactured, said sources.

Confirming that Delhi-based Met Trade India Limited company has been given permission to set up its non-ferrous metal project, General Manager, Industries, Kangra district, Satish Chaudhary said the company would not only generate direct employment opportunities, but also help in flourishing of other subsidiary copper and aluminum metal-related small units set up in the area. More small units might come up once this major project starts functioning, he added.

"These small units will get cheap raw material at their doorstep once the production starts,'' Chaudhary said. The general manager said the company was moving fast and would complete the formalities very soon. He hoped that the company would start setting up its project within a few months.

Heading: 24-hr helpline to give tips on how to save broken teeth - Indian Express
Content:
2002 gangrape Accused Vigilance DSP was on the run for 133 days but 'regularly reported for work'

The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the Haryana Inspector General of Police (IGP) to review the finding given in the favour of Phool Kumar, Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP), Vigilance, Haryana.

According to the finding, Kumar, who allegedly remained absconding for 133 days after he figured as an accused in a gangrape case and was declared a proclaimed offender by the court thereafter, was exonerated. It was submitted in the finding that he reported regularly for duty.

Shocked at the finding, a Division Bench headed by Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur took the Haryana Police to task on Monday. The court made it clear that any observation by the Bench would not affect the officer who will review the finding.

It also asked that Kumar be issued showcause notices by the inquiry officer and given an opportunity to present his case.

On the last date of hearing, the court had asked the Haryana Director General of Police (DGP) to look into the matter and file an affidavit.

Dissatisfied with the finding, the DGP submitted on Monday that the report needs to be reviewed. He also recommended punitive action against Kumar. Since it falls in the ambit of the Haryana government, thus the same is being recommended to it, read the affidavit of the DGP.

Disapproving the DGP's report, the Chief Justice remarked: "Your director does not seems to have understood what we asked. He is passing the buck. If he is unable to understand, then we will make him understand by appearing here in person."

Making it clear that the court was not interested in the promotion given to Kumar, from an SHO to DSP, the court observed: "We are concerned with the correction of the inquiry and the finding submitted by the senior police officer. We are not concerned with the promotion given to Kumar. Are we reversing the promotion? We are not concerned with the charge of rape. We fail to understand as to how an officer, who has been declared a proclaimed offender, was present on duty. An innocent man has no business to abscond. What kind of finding is this? If this is the state of affairs in Haryana, then we are shocked. This finding should be reviewed, we are not satisfied with it."

The case relates to a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by Surinder Kunal Juneja, president, Yuva Shakti Manch, Ambala.

Juneja had challenged the promotion of Kumar to the post of Vigilance DSP, despite him being an accused in the gangrape case of a minor in 2002. The department had given a clean chit to Kumar who was then serving as an inspector.

Though, Kumar was acquitted from the case as the victim turned hostile in a court which had no jurisdiction to record her statements, the proceedings of proclaimed offender against Kumar continued for six years.

Heading: Pollution control board draws flak from High Court - Indian Express
Content:
With cases of dentofacial trauma (which affect a patient's teeth and facial structure) trebling in the last few years, the Department of Oral Health Sciences, PGI, has established a helpline which will provide tips on how to save broken teeth.

The 24-hour helpline — 9914208717 — will be managed by a team of doctors to provide necessary guidance on the management and transportation of teeth in trauma cases.

Professor A K Uttreja, chairman of the department, said: "Due to increased traffic on the highways as well as within cities, there has been a substantial increase in the number of accidents in recent years. A few years ago, we received only one or two such trauma cases in a week but now the figure has risen to five per week. Also, falls and fights during sports activities also cause complete or partial damage to teeth."

The professor added: "In these situations, the damaged teeth can be re-implanted successfully if they are carefully transported within a short time. For example, a simple tip to save a tooth is to keep it in milk while transportation."

Heading: Aishwarya coming to Manali - Indian Express
Content:
While the 'polluting' meat processing industries in Dera Bassi have come under the scanner of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, the Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB) is in the dock for allowing those units to continue which have no pollution control equipment.

A division bench comprising Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and Justice Jasbir Singh questioned the existence of such industries and the reasons behind giving no-objection certificates by the PPCB. "Who allowed these units to operate? It is quite bothering that what ought to be done is being done after the industries have been given consent to operate. The larger question is: should people be allowed to generate effluents or should they be first checked. What is the hurry in allowing these industries to operate if they have not installed everything properly?" the court asked.

The defence counsel for M K Overseas, one of the meat processing units under the scanner, maintained that adequate steps are being taken to make the effluent treatment plant functional.

The observations were made in the wake of a public interest litigation (PIL) filed against various meat processing industries in and around Dera Bassi, Mohali.

Taking the PPCB to take, the Chief Justice asked: "Nobody pointed out that the plant is not functional. You do not put the effluent treatment plant to test when you grant permission to operate. Why was this plant allowed to start without completing the devices? We want to address his problem. Shall we direct Vigilance to look into it?"

The High Court has summoned the record of the reports and the no-objection certificates issued by various PPCB officers, including the chairman. The High Court has also summoned the norms and conditions looked into by the Board before giving consent to operate the units.

Heading: Out of the box - Indian Express
Content:
Noted actor and former Miss World Aishwarya Rai is arriving in Kullu-Manali on November 14 in connecting with the shooting of film "Endhiran", in which she is playing the lead role opposite Tamil superstar Rajnikanth. Both will travel together for the shooting. The film was earlier shot in Goa for over a week and in Peru before that.

Reports say Aishwarya Rai will be in Manali for nearly a week. Her husband Abhishek Bachchan is currently shooting in Kochi for Mani Ratnam's Ravana.

The film production unit has kept Aishwarya Rai's travel plans quite secret and there are chances that she will travel by a chartered plane to reach Bhuntar in Kullu.

This will be the first time when Aishwarya will be shooting in Himachal Pradesh. Her father-in-law, superstar Amitabh Bachchan, was recently in Shimla for a long shooting schedule during summer.

The pre-winter shooting schedule of the film is planned before snowfall in the area. Currently, only the higher reaches, including Rohtang Pass (over 13,000 feet), have witnessed snow. The pass will be officially closed for vehicular traffic in November and will open in May next year.

Heading: Rock On ! - Indian Express
Content:
More and more couples are opting for television-free lives

Kishore Majgaonkar has vivid memories of the day his wife, Lalita, unplugged the television and put it away in the loft 12 years ago. "There was too much time being spent watching television even though the only channels being telecast back then were DD1 and DD2, and that annoyed her no end," laughs Kishore. The Majgaonkar household has not since bothered to reinstate "idiot box" and nor do they miss it. The Majgaonkars may have been "unusual" a decade ago but today, they won't find themselves alone as many young couples are following suit and ditching the idiot box for "a better lifestyle".

When Richa and Mohit Kathuria got married a year ago, one of the three TVs owned by the joint family was promptly moved to their room. Though busy with their careers, they would spend their free time flipping through the channels. But after a few months the TV went for repair and they never bothered to bring it back into their bedroom. "Today, it shocks me when over family get-togethers, which are anyway rare, people prefer to discuss TV shows than chat up—it's become a tool of judgement," remarks Mohit.

Like the Kathurias, Jinita and Himanshu Kode also happened to chance upon this phenomenon. After moving into a new apartment, the couple postponed the purchase of a TV set due to financial constraints but realised that they don't really miss it. "Not only have we invested that money but also our time," says Jinita, as she readies to leave for a weekend trip. "I think we would have wasted this weekend watching TV if we had one."

A few couples, on the other hand, took calculative measures to throw the "evil" out of their lives. Prapti Dangwal and Sandeep Suvarna are one. They have planned to get rid of their TV before they get married next year. Dangwal, an advertising professional, was a TV buff but decided that they had to do away with the "junk box" because, given their work schedules, they cannot afford to compromise their couple time. She does miss TV at times but makes up for it by watching films on her laptop.

Elsewhere, tired of his wife's "addiction" to the soppy saas-bahu shows, Dr Manmit Singh decided to pull the cable out. "That's when we started spending more time with each other," tells Singh who took his wife, Jagjot, a school principal to out of city trips and family get togethers. "I have found time to catch up on my reading," says a thankful Jagjot. Ditto for Dinesh Narayanan, a media professional, who decided to junk his set in 2000 as it was eating into his reading time. However, he wasn't sure how his fiancé would react to a television-free lifestyle. But Archana Choudhary played a sport and decided to test it out only to realise that it gives her enough time to cook and pursue singing —activities she thought she never had time for. Jinita too, claims that her culinary skills can be attributed to the missing TV set.

The couples accept that there are times.when they miss the tube, "especially when there's important news or an interesting match on" but Choudhary sums up the benefits when she remarks, "We are better off than others — at least our lives aren't ruled by commercial breaks".

Heading: Cat’s Whiskers! - Indian Express
Content:
A band of four teenagers who began preparing for the PEC Fest '08 only a week before, share their winning 'notes'

It was only a year-and-half back, when they were still at school, that these four friends started jamming together and Harmonic Friction was born. The PEC Fest knocked, but they did not even make it to the finals. Time travel to PEC Fest 2008 and Harmonic Friction has been crowned the king of rock. But that's not all, "there were speculations if the rock contest would happen at all. It was a week before the event that we received a confirmation and that's when we began rehearsing," Sharang Sharma, vocalist and rhythm guitarist is all smiles and elated about the win.

So was it luck or sheer talent that helped them score over their much-experienced 'seniors'? "Can't pinpoint one reason, but I guess this time there was no pressure on us. We were out there just to have fun...and we wanted to win!" shares Atul Gupta, the drummer. Antriksh Bansal on bass guitar and Saurabh Dhir, the lead guitarist, complete the band. The youngest Saurabh is still at school. The group's practice sessions would usually be held at Sharang's recording studio and they had only two hours a day to get their act together, for they had exams to prepare for too. In the 15 minutes given to them the band played an original — Disappear and Neil Young's Rocking In The Free World. As for their style of music..."it's different. Though the genre is restricting, we play alternative rock which is not really mainstream. It's not heavy, but soft and melodious. We are among the few in the region who play the acoustic guitar, though we agree our music is difficult to understand and the audience doesn't accept it quickly," Sharang reveals, and they believe they gained marks on originality.

So is the rock scene in the city in transformation mode? "It's actually like the stock market, unpredictable. College fests are a great platform, but need to be frequent," Atul hopes that Chandigarh catches up with Delhi's pub scene. And who do they head-bang to? "It's Junkyard Grooves from India, while abroad Porcupine Tree, Blackfield, Incubus and Opeth rock!,'' they chorus. Next on the cards is Campus Rock Idol, a lot of recording, mixing, jamming sessions ,"and hopefully some paid gigs as well!" Keep strumming!

Heading: Live it up - Indian Express
Content:
French author Yvan Pommaux narrates visual stories & three of the comics will now be translated into Hindi & English

There's a story-teller living in this artist and a creator wrapped in this narrator. Yvan Pommaux's drawings and stories emerge simultaneously, as opposed to 30 years back when this French author for children would rely on his drawings to tell a story. The creator of John Chatterton, The Detective Cat, Yvan is a follower of the clear line style and studied fine arts and began his career illustrating school and children's books. For the last many decades, he has been creating a range of characters and stories that appeal to children of all ages, "I prefer to call my illustrated books albums and not comics and am happy that three of them from John Chatterton, The Detective Cat series will be translated into English and Hindi.'' Here at the Alliance Francaise, the author and artist in many of his books, especially for children between five and eight uses animals to tell the story, which he feels is the traditional way, "but I don't restrict my imagination, so people, history, documentary, adventure, humour and even I are a part of my creations.'' The author clarifies that he doesn't mean to put across any message through his books, but agrees that most readers, children and teachers do read in-between the lines. Yvan candidly agrees he may not be a best-seller, but has his faithful admirers, with the books being both ambitious and with an attitude. "It's my livelihood, the passion began with drawing and the stories flowed in,'' Yvan shyly mentions that back in France, there are three villages named after him. "That's kind of flattering, for it's an honour that's usually conferred on the dead,'' Yvan shows you the hard-bound beautifully illustrated books, some of which we soon can devour.

Heading: Hello, brother - Indian Express
Content:
The condition of safai karamcharis in Gujarat is possibly the worst, Santosh Chowdhary, the Chairperson of the National Commission for Safai Karmacharis has said.

She was at a press meet in the state capital in response to a petition filed by the sweepers to President Pratibha Patil, seeking permission for self-immolation.

Ninety-four sweepers of the notified areas of Gandhinagar had gone on an indefinite strike for the last three months, of which 35 had signed the petition for mass self-immolation.

"For the last 20 years, we have been working as sweepers in the notified areas of Gandhinagar, earning merely Rs 30 per day. After repeated applications to the government, we went on a strike. But when even after three months nothing was done, we had to resort to mass self-immolation to get ourselves heard," said Bharat Patel, one of the sweepers.

Chowdhary held the state government responsible for the despondent condition of the safai karmacharis in Gujarat. She said: "The government should charge the concerned official with the Atrocities Act (1989) if any negligence is shown towards these people. The Centre has spent Rs 700 billion to stop manual scavenging in India, but the scenario in Gujarat hasn't changed much."

There are more than 12,000 manual scavengers and about 65,000 sweepers in Gujarat. The minimum wages entitled to the workers is Rs 120 per day whereas the sweepers get only Rs 20 or 30. Overlooking the improper wages, poor housing, no sanitation and the absence of other basic necessities, the safai karmacharis work for more than 10 to 12 hours a day. About 22 workers died inside potholes in 2006.

Despite the presence of the Valmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana (VAMBAY) and other schemes, more than 12,000 safai karmacharis are yet to be rehabilitated in Gujarat.

Chowdhary said the Centre is regularly funding the state government to build toilets. In the last three years, Rs 185.5 crore was spent on sanitation. She also promised that by 2012, toilets will be provided at all homes in the state.

Under the Right to Information Act filed by the safai karmachais, about 30 non-Dalit workers were found to be registering on the musters and taking the daily wages without doing any work. About 70 other workers were also found who were taking daily wages by working for fewer hours.

Chowdhary said the government should encourage more job posts for the sweepers.

She also expressed surprise that there are 50 vacant posts in Gandhinagar, while the government is extracting more work from the fewer workers. She further said the state government has a good amount of the unspent money, which it had taken from the Centre.

In an interactive session with the safai karmacharis after the press meet, Chowdhary requested the workers to call off the strike. She also opposed to the trend of giving part time jobs to safai karamcharis. She said the jobs of the workers should be fully regularised, and that the government should generate jobs in the rural areas, which will lead to a healthier Gujarat.

Incidentally, about 14 people, including one pregnant woman were fired from their jobs in the last few days without any notice in writing.

Pravin Vaghela, one of the sweepers who was fired, told Newsline: "I was tired at the end of the day, working for the past 10 hours in different areas of Gandhinagar. When I requested to do the work the next day, I was immediately fired."

Chowdhary said that when other states have incorporated a system for the safai karmacharis, then why Gujarat has not followed suit.

"In Maharashtra, 7,500 job posts were created for the safai karmacharis. The daily wagers were given regular jobs with a hike in their wages. I would appeal to the Prime Minister to regularise their jobs and give them the minimum wages entitled. I am positive that by March 2009, manual scavenging will stop," she said.

Heading: Contestant to be paid promised prize money - Indian Express
Content: Every actor worth a Khan surname is turning producer. The latest to clamber on to the Bollywood filmmaker bandwagon is Arbaaz Khan, who has launched his production house Arbaaz Khan Productions (no surprise there). "I am glad to have acted in some good films recently, but I wanted to take my role in the industry further. I stumbled upon a good director and a great script, which is when I decided to take up the project," says Khan. There has been no formal launch, but the actor plans an official announcement when the project goes on the floors in April. The film, he says, is based on relationships — and some of the roles stay in the family. "It has a role for Salman and I may be acting too," says Khan, adding that the film will be directed by debutant Abhinav Kashyap. Meanwhile, acting hasn't  been left behind. After the success of Fashion, he is focusing on his forthcoming films, Madhureeta Anand's Mere Khwabon Mein Jo Aaye and Kissan under his brother's Sohail Khan Productions.

Heading: Forest, farmland in city being encroached upon, says study - Indian Express
Content:
The Tata Tele Services received flak from the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum on Monday for intentionally evading the prize money of Rs 2 lakh won by a contestant.

Apart from the prize money, the forum has directed the service provider to pay Rs 50,000 as compensation to the contestant.

"The company has indulged in unfair trade practice. They tried to befool the public by introducing the contest and earned crores itself by introducing the scheme," the forum observed.

J P Nanda, a resident of Mohali, said he received an SMS by the telecom providers, asking him to participate in a contest — Horror Haveli — later changed to "PECHAN" at Rs 6 per minute. The winner was supposed to win an Indica car. The complainant participated in the contest through SMS and got 34160 points. The contest was, however, closed without announcing the results.

When the complainant pursued the matter, he came to know that he had got the highest points and was entitled for a prize of Rs 10,000. He, however, received Rs 7,000 after tax deductions.

The complainant again took up the matter and asked the company to disclose the name of the contestant who secured more points than him.

The company, however, failed to respond. The service provider claimed that Rs 2 lakh was the first prize and not the car. They said the contestant had won the first prize in the weekly category and was, therefore, given the prize of Rs 10,000.

They further claimed that there was another contestant who won the first prize as he had scored more points than Nanda.

The consumer forum, however, observed that the complainant had scored the highest points and the service provider had failed to provide any record of the winner they had claimed had scored more points than Nanda.

Heading: To rein in violence, Students’ Centre made no-vehicle zone - Indian Express
Content:
A study on 'Open Structure of Chandigarh' conducted by a Delhi-based landscape architect has revealed a number of issues in the city that need immediate attention.

The study was discussed recently during a conference on 'Emerging Trends in Landscape Architecture' organised by the Saakaar Foundation.

In the study, landscape architect Aarti Grover lists the problems as: haphazard growth in fringe areas, unplanned spatial growth, changes in land use and growth of unchecked encroachments among others.

The study finds that the forest and farmlands in the periphery of the city are also being encroached upon.

In the absence of a comprehensive masterplan or a development plan, the new constructions being planned at the cost of forests is a threat to the overall ecology and environment of the city, warns the study.

The study holds the slums around the city as a major environmental threat. The open green have become virtual "junkyards" with several green pockets inside the sectors and along the roads being rendered useless, highlights the study.

Grover states that the buffer zone between the industrial and residential areas too needs to be strengthened.

The study also offers recommendations for the development of open spaces. There is the need for a comprehensive landscape development plan for the city, including areas like Sukhna Chowk, the Capitol Complex as well as the newly-constructed southern sectors, suggests the study.

Grover says rain water harvesting can help tackle the depleting groundwater situation.

Heading: A show full of emergency skills and fire - Indian Express
Content:
Snazzy cars at the Students' Centre in Panjab University are a thing of the past now with the authorities declaring it a vehicle-free zone.

Stepping up security in the wake of the violent clashes at PU, even shop-owners are not allowed to park their vehicles here.

Also, the police can now issue a challan to anyone (read students) found violating traffic rules within the campus.

This is a significant departure from the earlier mode of functioning when the police was called in only after a mishap or for crowd-control.

It seems the recent clash outside his house has nudged Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti into action.

After all the previous incidents, the V-C merely formed a committee to look into the matter but this time he has taken things into his own hands.

Professor Sobti said: "We are working on several schemes to maintain peace in the campus."

Nitin Goyal, a member of the National Students' Union of India (NSUI), said: "The decisions are a welcome move and will definitely help curb violence on the campus. We are ready to join hands with the V-C to help the cause."

Steps taken by PU
* Only gate number 2 (from Sector 15) will remain open after 6 pm
* Students' Centre made vehicle-free zone
* Number of policemen increased on campus
* Police allowed to issue challans to students
* Departments asked to make students aware of traffic rules

Heading: Patiala SSP’s tryst with the wrong side of the law - Indian Express
Content:
The Fire and Emergency Services department of the Municipal Corporation conducted a fire drill-cum-exhibition of fire-fighting equipments at the Fire Station, Ramdarbar, Industrial Area Phase-II on Monday.

The drill began with paying homage to Amarjit Singh Mavi, the fireman who recently lost his life during a fire-fighting operation at Sector 22.

The firemen created situations of emergency and displayed the skills applied to tackle such cases. Proximity suits meant to protect firemen from high intensity fire were also displayed.

The other demonstrations included power-operated spread cutter, RCC cutter for building-collapse incidents, motorcycles equipped with water mist equipment and AFT machines among others. The Hydraulic Turn table ladder with a capacity to reach a height of 42 feet was also displayed during the drill.

While addressing the gathering, the Mayor said that the Fire and Emergency Services department of the Municipal Corporation is equipped with the latest fire-fighting equipments and high technology communication system.

Municipal Corporation commissioner Dr Roshan Sunkaria said that fire prevention is better than fighting. Fire incidents can be minimised if adequate precautions are taken, added Sunkaria.

Heading: Frozen in time - Indian Express
Content:
Be it the Bhadaur Gurdwara clash or allegedly assaulting a 70-year-old woman in a bid to transfer her property, it seems Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) of Patiala S K Asthana is always found on the wrong side of the law.

'Slapping and intimidating' an old lady
Asthana's conduct has come under scanner of the High Court for allegedly thrashing an old lady and threatening her to transfer her property in the name of her son. He earned the HC's wrath for getting an FIR registered against a woman, Raman Kanta, a resident of Patiala, for an episode which took place 17 years ago. The FIR was registered after the woman had moved the Punjab Human Rights Commission levelling allegations against the SSP accusing him of slapping, abusing and intimidating her.

Coming down heavily on Asthana and the Punjab Police for their high-handedness, Justice Ranjit Singh Randhawa took the SSP and the police force to task. On the last date of hearing, Justice Randhawa strongly disapproved of the affidavit filed by Asthana and granted anticipatory bail to Kanta.
"I am not satisfied with the SSP's conduct in the manner as it has been disclosed. After 17 years, the issue has been raked up, that too when a complaint against the police is submitted to the Human Rights Commission and this court. The FIR seems to be a reaction to this approach made by the petitioners. The interim anticipatory bail granted to Kanta is made absolute. This order will ensure till the filing of a challan and thereafter, petitioners will be at liberty to approach the trial court for regular bail," the order read.
Justice Randhawa has also sought the outcome of the investigation carried out by the ADGP (Crime). The High Court has asked the Human Rights Commission as to whether any requirement of issuing any directions for inquiry against SSP Patiala or other police is required.

Bhadaur Gurudwara clash
Though the High Court had dismissed a petition demanding a CBI inquiry in the Bhadaur Gurudwara clash, which took place in October 2006, the conduct of Asthana for his alleged involvement in the clash has come under the scanner of Justice H S Bhalla.
One Ruban Masih had died in the clash. Asthana was posted as SSP in Barnala at that time and was blamed for beating Masih to death. "Is there no IPS officer in entire Punjab or is he the only officer left to be given such a plum posting despite such serious allegations against him?" the Court had questioned.
Taking a dig at the Punjab government, Justice H S Bhalla had sought explanation from the Punjab government. "Are police officers like Asthana indispensable?" the Court had questioned the "special" treatment meted out to Asthana.
"Why should he continue as SSP despite such serious allegations against him? Why are you giving him such important cases? It is clear that you want to shield him. There are so many officers in the Punjab Police. I want to raise the curtain on this issue. Do you want to use him in a particular manner?" Justice Bhalla had said.

Virk case
Asthana is the investigating officer of the case registered against former Director General of Police (DGP) S S Virk and former CRPF officer Anurag Saxena. The High Court has asked the Punjab government to file a reply as to why Asthana is being allowed to continue as the investigating officer in the case.
The allegations against Saxena and Virk are that the former SSP used his official position to promote buying of security equipment worth crores from Saxena after taking a bribe.
The defence counsel for Saxena had submitted that Saxena had supplied security equipment to Punjab Police twice. Stoutly denying allegations of any purchase facilitated by Virk to the Punjab Police, Saxena had submitted that both the times the supply was made through a senior Punjab Police officer and Asthana.
Owing to this, the High Court had directed Asthana to file a reply explaining his own role in the case.

Heading: Trained teachers, separate section for special kids - Indian Express
Content:
People are being given candyfloss in the name of cinema, says Prof AF Mathew

If Prof AF Mathew is to be believed, the growth of Indian cinema came to a halt after the year '91. "Before that Indian movies contributed positively to society, look at the cinema now...films aren't benefiting anybody. A multiplex collection measures the success of the movies today," rues Prof Mathew, here for a day-long workshop at Chitkara School of Mass Communication. An Assistant Professor at MICA, Ahmedabad, Mathew spoke on 'Cinema Intrinsic to Indian Culture.'

"There was a time when Indian cinema was secular and democratic, today all terrorists have to be Muslims. We have become more conservative and regressive," remarks Mathew. But whatever happened to cinema being the mirror of society? "If that were true then does it mean that we don't need the judiciary? Are emotions, insecurities of the common man above the law," Mathew refers to A Wednesday. He stresses on the need to sensitize ourselves. A scribe brings in Rang de Basanti, but Mathew sees it as a distortion of Bhagat Singh's reality. "Read the visionary's writings and then compare it with history presented in the movie. There's a lot of difference." Here is where the role of teachers becomes prominent. "We need to talk the language of non-violence, justice and peace. For change to happen, education has to upgrade itself. As media professionals it is important that you ask the right questions," he states and we are tempted to ask what his definition of 'good cinema' is. A smile and the answer follows, "good cinema is Sholay, Jab Jab Phool Khiley... the kind that connects with people, speaks good politics and is least fundamentalist in its content. Today we have so many advantages in terms of accessibility and technology. I don't understand why we are not responding to it." Currently, Mathew is working on a project on sexuality in advertising. Ask him about his contribution in giving cinema the 'right' shape and he retorts, "My job is to teach and I'll stick to that." Need we say more?

Heading: NHRC to look into complaint in favour of  Malegaon blast - Indian Express
Content:
Government schools in the city score poorly when it comes to catering to the needs of special children — not a single school has an exclusive section or teachers devoted to such children.

But the Education Department has several plans up its sleeve to rectify the situation, including tying up with NGOs and appointing trained teachers who can guide mentally challenged children.

"The department was always keen to help special children but several limitations, such as paucity of funds and non-availability of trained staff, stood in the way," said Director Public Instructions (Schools) Samwartak Singh.

To overcome the problem of lack of teachers, the department plans to rope in counsellors and experts from the State Institute of Education to instruct recruits. "We have also decided to tie up with different NGOs which have been working with kids. The development of the children will be monitored by the department by conducting regular medical check-ups," said Singh.

"For visually challenged students, the department will print customised textbooks," he added.

The department also plans to start a separate section for special children. "We will make sure that children suffering from dyslexia and autism are taught life skills by experts and without burning a hole in the parents' pocket," said Singh.

Heading: ‘Prototype furniture cannot be deemed as heritage’ - Indian Express
Content:
Bridal Bonanza
Wedding Asia is back again with all its grandeur, pomp and show. The fourth edition of Wedding Asia 2008 will be on at Hotel Taj from November 14 to 16. The exhibition brings in everything related to weddings, be it dazzling designer and traditional jewellery, trousseau wear, trendy accessories complete with household decor, furnishings and wedding planners and honeymoon destinations. "Wedding Asia is a premium show where we endeavour to bring innovative, creative and quality brands together at a common platform for shopaholics. The wedding season is on and the show will fulfill requirements of sellers and buyers," mentioned Maninder Singh Sethi, the organizer. Among those coming in for the show include celebrity designers like Punita Trrikha who has designed for Bollywood beauties and for the Hollywood film Marigold and Nisha Merchant who recently showcased her rich Indian bridal wear at the Wills India Lifestyle Fashion Week 2008.

Flying High
THIS Monday saw the Air Hostess Academy (AHA) conduct an in-flight training programme for its students from Punjab on Kingfisher Airlines. As part of the training, students of AHA Air Hostess Academy were taken aboard a special Kingfisher Airlines flight, where they were introduced to intricacies of in-flight service and familiarized with the responsibilities of the cabin crew. The exposure took the students through the depths of operational aspects of the airline industry and made familiar with the responsibilities and criticalities of the air hostess and flight steward. Said Sapna Gupta, founder and chief consultant, AHA, "In-flight exposure is an important part of the curriculum wherein we charter a special Boeing."

House Wise
FOR those wanting to refurbish their home with contemporary furniture, Zen Spaces is putting up an exhibition of indoor and outdoor furniture and accessories from November 14 to 15 at Episode, Sector 9. Check out lamps, cushion covers, candle-holders and platters.

Party time for Rajputs
THE first Friday of November each year is a day to be remembered for serving and veteran officers of the Rajput Regiment in the City. This is the day when all of them get together and catch up with each other and of course, what's happening in the Regiment. This year's get-together was held at Hotel Shivalikview and saw a large number of Rajput officers in attendance with wives. Lt Gen ML Naidu, Colonel of the Rajput Regiment, came from Delhi with his wife and Col JS Kang, convenor of the Chandigarh Chapter of the Association, gave a run-down on the recent visit of Rajput veterans to Kolkata and Port Blair. Lt Gen RS Dyal, one of the senior retired officers of the Regiment, presented the Rajput Association wall plate to Lt Gen ML Naidu and Lt Gen VS Tonk, GOC 11 Corps, who had come from Jalandhar to attend this get-together.

The Aftermath
WHAT happens when a national tragedy creeps into the lives of common people? This question was explored by Theatre Arts, a city-based theatre group. Performed at Sector 17 Plaza the street play 'Dhamakey Ke Baad' traces the life of a young man who becomes a victim of terrorism. Protagonist Iqbal is an intelligent young man who ends up in the wrong company. His journey from fulfilling his parents' dreams to becoming a mass murderer is a complex one. The play opens in the court as a death sentence is pronounced upon Iqbal. But his mother chooses to be the one to kill him. Jagan Nath Bains explains, "the aim is to stress that parents should check who their children hang out with, where they go. The intention is not to interfere, but to protect...in individual, familial and national interest."

Heading: 42-yr-old burnt alive in Daruya village - Indian Express
Content:
In 2007, some pieces of furniture from Chandigarh were auctioned by the Christie's for whopping prices between $3,000 and $5,000 at the Rockefeller Plaza in New York. While Le Corbusier's famous leather chairs had been used in various Hollywood flicks earlier, it was for the first time that the furniture, based on the designs of Pierre Jeanneret, was auctioned abroad.

The news startled the Chandigarh Administration because it was sold as "junk" with their consent.

There was nothing illegal about the sale of the discarded furniture and their auction. Why the prototype furniture fetched high prices amuses me because Le Corbusier's famous leather chair can be purchased in India for $1,000.

It was in 1999 that Eric Toucheaume, from France, with the help of a teacher of the Chandigarh College of Architecture, discovered that such valuable furniture was lying junk in many offices. Toucheaume sensed the worth of the discarded furniture in the West and made efforts to buy them.

A committee was constituted by the Chandigarh Administration to ascertain the facts regarding the sale of the furniture, with the supposed heritage value. The findings of the committee were, however, not known, much as one expected.

The UT Administration, nevertheless, for the first time ventured to visit the city museum early this year and ordered to locate such furniture for repairs and display in the city museum.

This was, however, perceived as an over-reaction on their part as the prototype furniture cannot be deemed as 'heritage' irrespective of the prices they fetched at the Christie's Auction in New York.

It was during my recent visit to the city museum in Sector 10 that I saw, to my utter dismay, the horrid pieces of furniture on display being attributed to Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret. Besides denigrating the great names of our architectural history, this highlights the utter ignorance of the selectors. Interestingly, such ugly furniture has occupied the most valuable space in the city museum.

As many of the original pieces of furniture, designed by Pierre Jeanneret, are already on display, one hopes that the Chandigarh Administration will take immediate steps to remove the wrong furniture, to restore the dignity of the city museum.

Heading: Bansal rubbishes claims of Centre’s budgetary cuts - Indian Express
Content:
A 42-year-old man, identified as Harbans Lal, was burnt alive at his residence in Daruya village on Monday. The police are yet to ascertain if the incident was a suicide or an accident.

Police officers said they received a call from the victim's neighbour, informing them of the incident.

"When we reached the spot, the body was charred beyond identification," an officer said.

Eyewitnesses told police that they rushed to the victim's house after hearing his shouts for help. "People tried to douse the flames, neighbours brought blankets and pitched in to save him. But it was too late by the time the fire was controlled," the officer said, adding they found a gas stove near the body.

Lal was living alone as a tenant in the house for the past few years. Police have initiated inquest proceedings under Section 174 of the CrPC. The body has been sent to the Government Multi-Specialty Hospital in Sector 16.

Heading: Re-employment scheme gets into hot water - Indian Express
Content:
Union Minister of State for Finance Pawan Kumar Bansal has written a letter to the UT Administrator stating that the reports about the Centre imposing budgetary cuts are misleading.

He said the allegations that posts are not being sanctioned for recruitment in the Chandigarh police are baseless.

The letter states: "The reports say that the Centre had imposed a cut of 10 per cent on non-plan and 5 per cent on plan budget. This news is apparently based on an unofficial briefing by some responsible officer of the Chandigarh Administration as it goes on to give details of the demand intended to be made to the Centre."

Bansal has clarified that the date fixed for discussion on the Revised Estimates (RE) is November 14. But the impression being given is that the Centre had already imposed a "cut" on Chandigarh's budget.

Interestingly, imposition of this cut of Rs 140 crore is simultaneously critised by a senior BJP leader. This is not the first time that reports based on unofficial briefings by UT officers have surfaced.

He further writes that recently there were allegations that UT Administration's proposal for more posts in Chandigarh police had been turned down by the Centre because of politics. It makes one wonder whether the UT Administration considers Government of India as an adversary.

"Leaving aside the question of desirability and appropriateness of such a briefing by a responsible officer of the Administration against the Centre, I only wish to bring to your notice that at the time of preparation of the budget for 2008- 09, Chandigarh's case had gone by default as no officer was present at the meeting fixed for the purpose. Still the allocations were made more than the Budget Estimates (BE), both on plan and non-plan side. The final picture always emerges at the RE stage. Last year, when the UT officers asked me to intervene, we were able to get an additional Rs 50 crore," the letter states.

He adds: "I am sure our officers know the details of budget-making process and non-acceptance of some proposals does not mean that a 'cut in the budget' has been imposed. Also, the surplus revenue of a union territory is not the same thing as that of a state, though we must keep raising our demand for greater allocations."

Heading: Chugging dreams: A train journey of a different kind - Indian Express
Content:
PU professors say 'affidavit clause' in the scheme infringes upon their Fundamental Right

The re-employment scheme mooted by the Panjab University (PU) for the retired professors has received a cold response from the teaching fraternity.

The reason: the requirement of an affidavit, from anyone applying for the re-employment, stating that he/she would not move the Supreme Court.

Professor A C Julka has written to Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti demanding an immediate withdrawal of the attached condition.

Talking to Newsline, Professor Julka said, "It is absolutely wrong and no condition like furnishing an affidavit can be attached by the university. Moving the court is a Fundamental Right of all citizens. I have written to the vice-chancellor for an immediate removal of the condition."

The PU authorities, meanwhile, appear adamant on their stand.

Talking to Newsline, Professor R C Sobti said: "If anyone has any issues with the conditions attached to the scheme, they are free to move court against it. Let them get me a decision from the court that I cannot attach such a condition, and I will do away with the same immediately."

Professor Sobti added that he has received nearly 35 applications for the scheme and all have furnished the said affidavit.

With the Punjab and Haryana High Court turning down the appeal of the PU professors to enhance the retirement age from 60 to 65 years, the re-employment scheme was started by the university to address the issue of faculty crunch.

Heading: One-hour respite from power cuts - Indian Express
Content:
Train journeys are always fun for children and they become all the more special and memorable for those who board them for the first time. On Sunday, 45 girls and 15 boys of Bapu Dham Colony got a chance to travel by train to Kiratpur Sahib, a first for many of them.

Organised by volunteers of Yuvsatta, an NGO, as part of their activities with adolescent children of this slum area, the trip cost was sponsored by social activists Ranee Kochhar and Advocate Harinder Singh Sidhu.

Expressing her joy, Anjana, the captain of the junior cricket team of Bapu Dham said, "The trees and the electric poles seemed to be moving from the train. I will never forget this journey."

"The journey itself was more enjoyable than the final destination," remarked Ashok, a volunteer with Kitab Ghar-the Bapu Dham children's library.

"Their enthusiasm for little moments of happiness in life is touching," said Pooja Sharma, member of the Chandigarh Social Welfare Board, who accompanied the children on the trip. Other 11-year-olds Madhu and Preeti say they were always fascinated by trains. "There is something magical about seeing a train move against the backdrop of the countryside," they exclaimed.

Vikramjit Singh, another volunteer, was the guide for the trip who explained the historic importance and relevance of the city of Kiratpur Sahib to the children.

Heading: Symbiosis observes first national education day - Indian Express
Content:
The Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) will reduce load-shedding by an hour in the state. The revised schedule will be implemented on an experimental basis for 15 days.

In Pune, it will be reduced by an hour and 15 minutes in Group A and an hour in Group B and C areas, S P Nagtilak, Chief Engineer, Pune division of MSEDCL said on Monday.

Practically the whole of Pune saw no respite from power cuts which lasted for five to seven hours on Sunday and Monday.

On Monday, MSEDCL decided to reduce power cuts by an hour. Divisions like Kothrud, Padmavati and Shivajinagar and other Group A areas which face a power cut of five hours and 45 minutes will have one hour and 15 minutes less of power cuts. The power cuts in Group A areas will be from 6.30 am to 8.45 am and 12.30 pm to 2.45 pm. Other areas in the same group will see load shedding from 8.45 am to 11 am and 2.45 pm. to 5 pm.

The revised schedule for Parvati, Bundgarden, Rasta Peth and Bhosari divisions in Group B will mean a power cut of five-and-a-half-hour against six-and-a-half earlier. Here, the power cut will last from 6 am to 8.45 am and from 1.30 pm to 4.15 pm.

In certain areas and in other areas in the same group it will be from 8.45 am to 11.30 am and 4.15 pm to 7 pm.

As for Group C which includes Pimpri division and Nagar road, the power cut will last six hours 15 minutes against the earlier seven hours and 15 minutes, MSEDCL officials said. Here power cuts will be from 6 am to 9 am and 12.45 pm to 4 pm.

The revision of the loadshedding schedule is a policy decision, Nagtilak said. While officials at MSEDCL pointed out that they were trying to make various arrangements to cope with the crisis, the shortage of coal at the thermal power stations has compounded the problem. The power generated at thermal power stations is less than 5000 MW in the state.

While power available in the state is around 11,000 MW, the demand has shot up to 15,000 MW, a 4000 MW shortfall. Before the revision of the load-shedding schedule, there was a withdrawal of power cuts in areas that had less transmission and distribution losses. But to maintain a uniform load-shedding, all the areas will face a reduction in power cuts by an hour.

Meanwhile Sajag Grahak Manch has urged Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and Energy Minister Dilip Walse Patil to look into the matter as the state had faced unprecedented load-shedding in the last few days.

Vivek Velankar, President of the Sajag Grahak Manch pointed out that the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC) top post has been vacant for five months leading to a delay in decisions on issues like load shedding protocol. Velankar has urged that appointment of the MERC chief be done soon.

Heading: Two-day event to promote biotechnology - Indian Express
Content:
On country's first National Education Day — November 10, Symbiosis International University (SIU) had organised day-long functions for its students at Symbiosis Vishwabhavan.

The Ministry of Human Resource and Development and University Grants Commission (UGC) had sent a request in October this year to all the educational institutes to celebrate the day in their own way. "Accordingly, Symbiosis has planned lectures, discussions, seminars and cultural programmes today," said Dr S B Mujumdar, president and founder director of Symbiosis.

The aim was to introduce Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, first minister of education in independent India, and his works to about 45,000 Indian and foreign students.

Heading: Teachers getting poor marks from parents may quit - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has initiated a two-day event to create awareness about biotechnology among the general public, promote biotechnology among students and to provide a forum for academic talent and interactions.

The event titled 'Mahabio 2008' will take place in Pune on November 14 and 15 and will be inaugurated by Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh.

The event is organised by Department of Industries, along with Institute of Bioinformatics and Biotechnology, University of Pune and Wisitex Foundation.

Announcing this on Monday, UoP V-C Narendra Jadhav said, "Dr R A Mashelkar, chairman, Maharashtra Biotechnology Commission will address the inaugural ceremony — to be held at Chandrashekhar auditorium, IUCAA — followed by eminent biotechnology scientists and academicians Ashok Kolaskar, former vice-chancellor of UoP, A S Ninawe, vice-chancellor of Maharashtra Animal and Fisheries University, Nagpur and Dilip Deobagkar, vice-chancellor of Goa University among others.

An exhibition of biotechnology will be held at Jaykar library in UoP where, about 20 industries, related to biotechnology, shall put their stalls. "The exhibition will be open to all college and university students," Jadhav said.

Heading: Tryst with life - Indian Express
Content:
Civic body's move starts showing results

With parents of students giving marks to teachers, incompetent teachers in schools run by the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) may soon be weeded out.

The PMC move of grading teachers seems to be working, with teachers improving their teaching skills.

But there are also some teachers who are quitting, perhaps sensing the actual blow that may come soon from the scheme.

The PMC had taken the initiative to give performance-based salary to teachers. The judgement was to be made by the parents of students. Now, even before the actual action begins, a few of the teachers whom parents are believed to have given low scores, have offered to apply for the Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) fearing action.

"We have constituted a committee, mostly of parents, for each of the 270 civic schools. Assessment of teachers is yet to begin, but the initiative itself has improved quality of education with teachers becoming more alert," Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi said.

According to PMC Education Officer Sudhakar M Tambe, even before the committee starts its work, a few of the teachers likely to fall in the "incompetent" category have offered to apply for VRS. The committee is headed by local corporator and have a doctor and engineer along with parents on board. "It has been observed that the teachers have become alert and improved teaching skills," he said.

The PMC has also framed certain guidelines for teachers, Tambe said adding that no teacher would be given more than one casual leave per month. Those willing to take leave upto one month will have to inform the education board in advance, he said. A list of retired teachers of civic schools have been prepared and would be appointed for a month to replace teachers going on long leave, Tambe said.

The PMC School Board has also set up a parallel machinery for assessing performance of teachers and had carried out a detailed study on it.

For involving public participation in providing quality education, Tambe said the PMC would soon be signing an MoU with city-based NGO Teach for India, and Deepak Fertilisers Ltd next week.

In the two-year contract, Teach for India would provide 50 teaching volunteers to the PMC for imparting education initially in English medium schools run by the civic body while Deepak Fertilisers Ltd on pilot basis would adopt 44 balwadi's in Yerawada and Mundwa, Pardeshi said.

The merger of 32 of civic schools with other schools due to a decrease in strength of students had reduced number of schools from 302 to 270. The PMC has also converted 25 of its Marathi medium schools into semi-English medium schools. There are around one lakh students in the civic-body-run schools.

Heading: Suspended civic body employee attempts suicide - Indian Express
Content:
As SIMC students hone their communication skills with various NGOs, the work introduces them to another facet of life

Its six week of internship with life for the students of Symbiosis Institute of Media and Communication, that, in its endeavor to make their students more pro active in fields of media and communication management, had launched the Social Change Communication Internships for the students of batch 2008-2010.

Akshay Brijkrishnan, a first year advertising student, is working with PAWS, an organisation that works for animal in need. He says, "It has been a great experience which has helped me in broadening my understanding of problems which the society faces. I am in charge of designing brochures for the organization, spreading awareness through games for children and have also been working on a film showing the plight of stray dogs." He says that working with PAWS had helped him to apply all his theoretical knowledge to the practical aspect of life. He further adds that it gives him immense satisfaction in doing humanitarian work because at the end of the day getting a degree is not always about earning money.

Ajay Hatti, pursuing an MBA in Public Relations, is working with CYDA- Youth Empowerment. The organisation handles issues like suicide among youngsters. He says, "It is very important to address issues such as suicides which are on the rise, especially in the age bracket of 15-25."

Hatti was responsible for designing, publishing and advertising the brochures of the NGO. He said that the role of media was central in CYDA's strategy for creating awareness about the issue. "The sooner people recognise the issue the better it is for us," he adds. He further admits that working with CYDA had changed him as a person and is in all praise for the dedicated members of the organisation.

Another student, Nikhita Arora, pursuing a MBA in communication management, is working with YP foundation Delhi. "Ours is a social communication module which helps to connect to the cause of mental health among youths. I help in organizing events and workshops including those for the Hijara community," she explains. She further adds that in the coming days she would take part in visits to the local community and interact with the children. She says it feels nice in making a difference to the kids' life and helping them grow toward a brighter future. She has decided to take up the cause by pursuing the social communication sector after her internship.

The programme is being widely appreciated by students; many of who are opting for far flung regions of India to complete their training under various organisations. Robin Raju of the internship coordination committee says, "The College had provided a series of lectures addressing the various issues which saw many social workers and media personalities coming out in support of the issue. This brought within us a desire to work at the grass root levels itself so as to get a first hand experience of the problems plaguing our nation."

The effort also serves SIMC's approach to churn up professionals who fulfill the needs of the industry in terms of their holistic knowledge, their technological and inter-personal skills, and their professional code of conduct.

Heading: The K- factor - Indian Express
Content:
A suspended employee of the Pune Municipal Corporation attempted to commit suicide on Monday, by consuming sleeping pills in the civic headquarters, alleging harassment from the civic officials.

The suspended employee, Sudam Patole, was later shifted to Sassoon General Hospital and his condition was reported to be stable.

In a note recovered from him, Patole urged the Municipal Commissioner to conduct an inquiry into the allegation of harassment levelled by him against certain officers.

"I am ending my life and hope that the inquiry would be conducted after my death," Patole said adding that his request had been repeatedly turned down by the civic administration.

Joint Commissioner for Urban Community Development Ashok Kalamkar said that Patole, a Class IV employee with Sahakarnagar Ward office, was facing an inquiry for allegedly siphoning off insurance amount of a beneficiary.

Patole was called for an inquiry in the civic headquarters, but he consumed the sleeping pills before the hearing could start.

Authorities at the Sassoon General Hospital said that Patole is out of danger and undergoing treatment.

The Shivajinagar police have not yet registered any case in this regard.

Heading: Abolish nuclear weapons, says Tilman Ruff - Indian Express
Content:
The versatile Ruheen Sheoran combines her excellence in kathak with an expertise in karate to make for an impressive combination of grace and gumption

She merges elegance and vigour to develop a striking personality. Nevertheless it always comes as a surprise to most to learn that 19-year-old Ruheen Sheoran, in addition to her graduate degree in Kathak dance, also holds the Black Belt First Dan in Karate with a bronze and gold medal to her credit.

Currently pursuing her masters in psychology from Jai Hind College, Sheoran has been receiving training in dance for the last 12 years. "I have been into dancing as well as karate since the age of 8. However I have been more inclined towards dance. I took up karate as a kid since my brother would attend the Karate classes.
