And I managed to excel at both with my parents' support," adds Sheoran who has also done a course and performed Tap Dance under the danseuse Jane Goldsberg and has trained Shaimak Davar's Special Performance Batch.

Her list has creative and classical Kathak, Thumri, fusion compositions and folk dance forms of Gujarat and Rajasthan including Shiv Tandav, which is her most cherished performance. Starting her basic training in Jhansi from Guru Raj Kumarji Bhati from Delhi, Sheoran performed numerous dance ballets including her solo recital at Mehergarh Fort Jodhpur. Speaking on her career in Kathak, Sheoran says, "I am pursuing formal training in various dance form. I plan to learn more on this form of art and take it as a profession.

When asked what is her first love, pat comes the reply,"Kathak of course" She adds,"Kathak is my dream. Karate happened by chance though I consider it an art form only. However, I would love to pursue a career in Kathak. But I am still in college and can't comment on my future so soon."

Coming from a family with an army background, Sheoran has traveled extensively. "Travelling has helped me a lot in my dance. I learnt from every place I went and in future I would love to promote artistic tradition of classical dancing."

The proud father, Maj Gen Ashok Sheoran feels his child is gifted. "It came as a surprise to me when Ruheen took up both karate and Kathak and did equally well in both such diverse spheres. But I am happy with her progress and would encourage her in future," he says. More power to the girl who sure has managed a commendable balance between femininity and a fiesty spirit.

Heading: Machine to read mind on its way - Indian Express
Content:
Various treaties like the Nuclear Non Proliferation Treaty (NPT) have been nearly thrown into dustbin by those who swear by it. Nuclear arms race is threatening the very existence of flora and fauna on the earth. And now, the only way out is to abolish nuclear weapons, said Dr Tilman Alfred Ruff, former president, Medical Association for Prevention of War, Australia, an affiliate of International Physicians for the Prevention of Nuclear War (IPPNW).

He is in the country on the invitation of the Indian Doctors for Peace and Development (IDPD) to participate in the Peace Week, observed from November 7 - 14 to commemorate the contribution of Jawahar Lal Nehru in promoting peace and disarmament. He will address the staff and students of D Y Patil medical college, Pimpri on Wednesday.

There are 27,000 nuclear weapons possessed by the US, Russia and seven other countries, escalating terrorism and new pressure for expanded civilian nuclear power that would increase proliferation risks, Ruff said in a statement issued by D Y Patil medical college.

The NPT review conferences held last year have been a wasteful exercise with the US administration sabotaging it. Unfortunately countries like India and Pakistan too have fallen trap to this nuclear arms race, he averred.

The IPPNW has launched International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons (ICAN). The demands of the campaign are to hold a Nuclear Weapons Convention, which would prohibit immediate development, production, testing, deployment, stockpiling, transfer and use of nuclear weapons.

Countries must adopt the 'No first Use of Nuclear Weapons' policy, he said. A seminar on Peace Health and Development will be held at D Y Patil medical college.

Heading: Two die in separate road accidents - Indian Express
Content:
Computer reads facial expressions to identify potential security threats

Technology is being increasingly used as a tool by criminals and terrorists. But the same technology is set to make their life tougher.

Efforts are on to develop a computer that can identify terrorists and other potential security threats by virtually scanning their thoughts from facial expressions.

Dr Prabir Bhattacharya, a professor at Concordia University in Montreal and a graduate student Abu Sayeed Sohail are developing a computer image processing system that has the potential to identify a person's mindset on the basis of facial expressions.

One aspect of this work was put forth for the first time at the Third International Conference on Artificial Intelligence held in Pune last December where it was ranked as the best scientific paper from over 800 submitted and 150 presented. A year down the line, the research duo have fine-tuned their work to such an extent that international security agencies have started contacting them for the project. "But I would rather keep that confidential at present," said Bhattacharya, who has been working with digital images and object recognition with the help of computers for the last two decades.

According to Bhattacharya, one of the primary aims of this system is to take and analyse photographs of individuals, especially in high traffic area where security is a major concern, such as airports.

These photographs could then be speedily processed and studied by security personnel to locate any individual who may appear to be security threats due to certain expressions seen on their faces. Following that, a check could be kept on these suspects.

"This is a fascinating area and uses considerable mathematical and statistical tools that many people do not realise," said Bhattacharya, a graduate from New Delhi's St Stephen's College who also holds an endowed Canada Research Chair that comes with a 2 million dollar grant from the Canadian government.

The system involves running digital photographs through a computer using sophisticated image-processing techniques based on mathematics to analyse and categorise facial expressions.

Explaining the system, Bhattacharya said, "The image after digitisation consists of an array of 0s and 1s. The researchers develop computer programs (algorithms) to process such arrays to do various tasks as image-matching, finding connected components and so on."

The system reads actions of specific sets of muscles near the eyes, nose and mouth and scans and measures 15 key points of the face. It then compares the measurements with a stored database. Although there is a large variety of expressions across individuals and culture, the researchers have identified seven universal expressions. They concede, though, that the research still has a long way to go before it becomes a practical possibility.

But will it really be able to spot and segregate anti-social elements and even terrorists? "It will help by trying to detect abnormal behaviour by analysing facial expressions like anger and so on, but is of course not foolproof," said Bhattacharya, as he added that the research will also be applied to areas like computer-aided surgery, robotics, driver safety and satellite image analysis.

Heading: It’s not about money, honey - Indian Express
Content:
With the rising incidents of road rage and road accidents claiming numerous lives in the city in recent times, two separate road accidents on Sunday claimed the lives of two.

At a road accident on the Mumbai-Pune Highway near the Phugewadi bus stop, Yamunabai More, 78, was mowed down by an unidentified motorcyclist. She was standing at the bus stop when the bike came and rammed into her. Before the public could catch he had reportedly escaped from the spot.

The Bhosari police have booked him under sections 279, 338, 304 (A), and 119/177, 132 (1)(A) of the motor vehicle act.

In another incident, a 22-year-old youth was killed on the Mumbai Pune Expressway bypass near Pashan when the motorcycle that he was riding rammed into a divider. According to the police he was going from Chandni Chowk towards Sus Road when the incident occurred.

They said that he was riding carelessly and hit the divider. He fell down from the bike and had hurt his head seriously. He died on the spot. The case is being investigated by the Chaturshinghi police.

Heading: Finetuning the future - Indian Express
Content:
How to look trendy when the economy is not looking good? Here is the designers' guide

Anupamaa Dayal
Recession hardly means dressing down. What it does imply, instead, is to cut out whimsical shopping. Buy one item of clothing, but make sure it is of the best quality. Trans-seasonal dressing is going to be big. Buy a dress which you can also wear in summer, but team it up with a polo neck sweater, leggings or skinny jeans, and accessories like a dressy shawl or stole. This way you'll have a compact wardrobe, but you'll still be dressed for the season.

Zubair Kirmani
Mix and match items of clothing to get the perfect look. The ideal thing to do is to buy one designer item, like a pair of trousers or a skirt, and then team it up with everyday items from the wardrobe. Colours go a long way in defining your dressing sensibility. Invest in safer colours like charcoal, ivory and maroon which can hold its own beyond a single season. Focus more on visually rich looking accessories, like mufflers, caps, bangles, all of which can make you look classy, yet simple.

Varun Bahl
Even though recession might not affect trousseau expenses, you can exercise moderation in your everyday wardrobe. Go for basic clothing, which you can team up with a lot of other accents. Bring back black. Invest in a lot of blacks, since it is one colour that can be worn in a lot of different ways, for both casual and formal occasions. You can go in for bright accessories — bright belts, colourful bags and shoes. It will lend warmth to the entire look.

David Abraham of Abraham and Thakore
The meltdown can actually lead to a better time. The optimistic thing to do now would be to go in for cheerful dressing, as if nothing has happened. Bring out the classy items and dress it up. For our Autumn-Winter collection, we have worked with baroque influences on a muted-colour palette. We have used colours like black, dull-gold, coffee and toffee with dull metallic glints to make the whole look rich and luxurious.

Heading: Afghan teachers learn how to manage education institutes at Azam campus - Indian Express
Content:
Violin maestro, L Subramanium is optimistic on the changing scenario of music in India and feels more stage shows will help new musicians learn better

It helped Shah Rukh Khan instill strength in the students to declare their love without fear in Mohabbatein, and it helped Lucky Ali teach life to his student in the Hindi flick Sur. Considered to be the most romantic musical instrument, the violin has of late won many preachers. But it wasn't a night with the posers, but with a maestro, who has mastered the strings with years of dedication and long hours of riyaaz.

Violin maestro L Subramaniam, was in town to grace the ongoing musical fest Chintamani Jayanti samaroh to commemorate birth anniversary of Pandit C R Vyas (Gunijaan).

Despite suffering from a tennis elbow, the maestro kept the audience spellbound with his mesmerising performance. He played raga Abhogi.

Giving his views on Hindi cinema's contribution in popularising violin, Subramanium says, "I am happy that Hindi cinema has brought violin on screen. With movies based on music, I hope a lot could be done in this regard. I will be happier of same transformation cold be brought for classical music which needs more attention and care."

The legend expressed his satisfaction in the growing career options with violin and other musical instruments. "With many orchestras and concert being held many times in a year, this field could also boast of unlimited option now. This is good sign, especially for people, who could not pursue music due to financial instability. However, passion and hard work doesn't have a substitute and these two are the key factors in any art," observes he.

When asked about the changing scenario in music schools, the maestro says that teacher-pupil relationship has undergone a change, which was inevitable. However, stage performance should be stressed, as it helps in learning with confidence.

Sharing a memorable experience, he says, "According to my father, one learns more by meeting different people. So once he put me on the stage and asked me to meet people. That incident helped me a lot in every aspect."

Talking about Pune, he says that the city is a beautiful place for music, given its cultural history and popularity of art among denizens. "It is always great to play in front of Pune audience."

Accompanying him was playback singer and wife, Kavitha Krishnamurthy. "The event is not only a treat for music lovers but also a service to the society by bringing quality music to people and re-introducing them to the rich Indian culture."

The couple's son Ambi Subramanium also performed on the evening. It was his third performance in the city.

Heading: Police release sketches of brigadier’s kidnappers - Indian Express
Content:
Management of educational institutes, a newly introduced course at the Maharashtra Cosmopolitan Education (MCE) Society's PAI International Centre will bring a brigade of Afghanistan teachers to India. Here, they will learn how to manage educational institutions back home.

PAI International Centre for Management Excellence and Afghanistan Education Department have signed a memorandum of understanding in this regard on Monday.

The four-month training programme of 20-student-batch will include modules on management, English, accounts, bookkeeping, information technology and economics. 'This training will help us to build its education pattern and the teachers will be contributing in its development," said Salim Qayum, Deputy Education Minister, Afghanistan Government.

As part of its initiatives to have its own education management system, Afghanistan-based National Institute of Management and Administration (NIMA), had invited proposals for such a course and accordingly, MCE Society's proposal was selected, P A Inamdar, president of MCE Society said. The first batch of 20 teachers from NIMA has already enrolled for the course and will be in MCE Society's Azam campus for four months.

"The course is being run on a no-profit no-loss basis and our management staff from the PAI International Centre for Management Excellence will teach the students," Inamdar said. He added that the society plans to teach at least 800 Afghan teachers in the next five years.

Explaining the importance of such a programme, Inamdar said, "Unlike India, Afghanistan does not have proper school management system. And those having a proper system are run by non-Afghans and funded by foreign countries."

Heading: IUCAA to coordinate Intl Year of Astronomy 2009 - Indian Express
Content:
The city police have released the sketches of two of the suspects who had allegedly kidnapped and released Brigadier Shreechand Acchtani last Wednesday.

While briefing the media on Monday, Additional Commissioner of Police (Crime Branch) Rajendra Singh said, "according to the description given by Acchtani, the sketches of two of the kidnappers have been made. We have also obtained two pictures of them registered by the camera in an ATM centre. Although the pictures are not very clear they will help us in our investigations immensely."

Singh said, "the case is being investigated with the help of the rural police. Anyone who gives any information about these two kidnappers, will be rewarded with a cash prize of Rs 20,000."

Deputy Commissioner of Police Anil Kumbhare said, "The work appears to be that of professionals. All of them are in the age group of 20-30. According to the statement given by Acchtani, they spoke mostly in Marathi amongst themselves but spoke to him in Hindi. They also were wielding weapons, and withdrew Rs 89,000 from his account."

Singh said, "Personal rivalry was definitely not the reason for kidnap. It was done only for money, as Acchtani and his family have not had any animosity with anyone in the building or anyone else. However, we are investigating all possible angles."

Acchtani, a retired brigadier, had gone for his lecture on Wednesday morning. He was kidnapped, on his way back home near Katraj, by six to seven unidentified youths. The kidnappers had called his wife on the mobile phone and demanded Rs 20 lakh for his release. His wife, however, informed the police, even as calls from the kidnappers continued.

Initially, they asked his wife to come with the money to Satara district but later changed the venue to Hadapsar, Wakad and Jejuri. While the crime branch teams were engaged in tracing the calls, the kidnappers released Acchtani at Katraj and fled away.

The police said that Acchtani had also been assaulted by the kidnappers and is recovering.

If any information about the kidnappers is known, call the offices of the crime branch or that of ACP S. Nishandar (992319999), Additional SP (rural) Morale (9823157525).

Heading: LDA scam: UP moves SC for action against Amar - Indian Express
Content:
The Inter University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics (IUCAA) has been designated as the nodal centre for India to coordinate the year-long celebrations of the International Astronomical Union and UNESCO — the International Year of Astronomy 2009. This international event is to celebrate the first astronomical use of a telescope by Galileo, about 400 years ago.

In India, the event will focus on bringing the excitement of new astronomical discoveries to students and general public, especially those in rural or semi-urban areas.

Samir Dhurde, member of science popularisation programme IUCAA, said that despite many astronomical organisations reaching out to different parts of the country, it is a daunting task, considering the vastness of the country and the varied linguistic and socio-economic situations.

"We are in touch with all the science organisations in the country apart from science centres, museums, planetariums and observatories. We will have sky-watching events, resource materials, workshops, project lectures and demonstrations," Durde said.

Over 7,000 astronomy clubs, across the country, have lined up sky watching programmes, workshops and discussions to encourage youngsters to the subject. About 200 scientists, pursuing frontline research in astronomy and astrophysics in various institutes across the country, are expected to participate in the event.

Heading: RS nominations over, last candidates in - Indian Express
Content:
The Mayawati government has moved the Supreme Court seeking permission to take action against Samajwadi Party general secretary Amar Singh. The basis of the plea is an inquiry report by state's Principal Secretary, Urban Development, on the alleged illegal allotment of plots in Gomti Nagar, Lucknow. The report holds Singh guilty of misusing his power during the Mulayam Singh Yadav regime.

The state government had filed an application on November 8 seeking permission to take action against Singh. "It is prayed that the court permit the government to proceed in accordance with law and to take necessary action on the basis of the report," the state government had said in its application.

The Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) had allotted Singh a plot in 1994 that was meant for the Economically Weaker Sections, according to the report.

The state government's move comes in the wake of the Allahabad High Court restraining it from initiating action against Singh. However, the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court, on June 13, gave liberty to the state government to approach the apex court for proceeding against Singh.

A petition filed by advocate Vishwanath Chaturvedi seeking a high-level probe into the allotments worth Rs 2.80 crore made in Vipul Khand, Gomti Nagar, has been pending in the apex court, which on September 12, 2005 by an interim order had restrained transfer of the plots until further orders.

The UP government's application said that on November 2, 2007, the apex court had issued notices to Yadav and Singh, among others, to initiate criminal prosecutions against them as they were beneficiaries of the alleged illegal allotment of plots.

The report said two plots were illegally allotted to the politician, out of which one was meant for EWS.

"It is clear on examination of the record that in this case Amar Singh was allotted (one) plot directly from EWS category which is completely against the rules," the report said.

In another case, two plots were illegally allotted to one Aaliya Khatoon by the LDA, out of which one plot was purchased by Singh.

Heading: 4 brothers get punishment for the murder that wasn't - Indian Express
Content:
All 10 RS candidates are millionaires
The two candidates who filed their nomination papers for the RS on Monday, also turned out to be crorepatis like the six candidates of the BSP and two of the SP. Total assets of Kusum Rai are nearly Rs 4 crore, while the assets of Mohammed Adib, the joint candidate of the SP and Congress, are over Rs 1 crore.

As per the affidavit filed by Rai, her husband owns agriculture land worth Rs 24 lakh at Mohanlal Ganj in Lucknow. Total worth of the residential plots, flats and residential buildings owned by the BJP leader is close to Rs 2.6 crore. Cash, bank deposit and gold held by Rai and her husband are worth over Rs 30 lakh and the total value of fixed deposits in name of her two daughters is Rs 41 lakh. Both Rai and her husband also own one revolver each. Assets of Adib include land in Aligarh worth Rs 60 lakh, residential building in Barabanki worth Rs 40 lakh and bank deposits and gold worth Rs 4.2 lakh.

Heading: Adib candidature cements SP-Cong poll alliance - Indian Express
Content:
Three years in jail and a pending case of murder which did not happen at all. That sums up the trauma of four brothers from Bajauli village in Faizabad, who have been making rounds of court in vain to prove their innocence.

On January 16, 1999, an FIR was lodged at Patranga police station in Faizabad in which four brothers — Ram Kumar, Ram Pratap, Ram Kripal and Santosh Kumar — were accused of murdering Ram Sajivan and disposing of his body. Ten days later, police recovered an unidentified body from near Mawai police station.

The then station officer of Patranga, Ahamad Jalaal Zaidi, declared that the body was of Sajivan, and the four brothers were arrested for the murder and sent to jail.

On Monday, Chandrakala, the mother of the "deceased", admitted before additional district judge R K Shukla that her son was alive and was in Pune at present. "The station officer forcibly took my signatures on some blank papers. I had gone to the police station to lodge an FIR that my son had left home and fled to Gujarat. Ten days later, the officer showed me a body and told me that some persons of my village had murdered my son," she told the court.

However, the then station officer maintained that he had lodged the FIR on the basis of the written application of Chandrakala.

The judge ordered the Pune Police Commissioner to arrest Sajivan and present him at the next hearing on November 24.

Sajivan had returned to the village a few months after the incident. "When the villagers asked where he had been, he said he had gone to Ahmedabad in search of employment," said Vipin Tiwari, advocate of the accused brothers.

"The return of Sajivan should have ended the ordeal of the brothers but it did not," he added. " Neither Sajivan himself nor the station officer informed the court about the development as it could have landed them in trouble."

On January 17, 2002, the accused brothers moved the High Court for bail, which was granted in the first week of February 2002.

The case at the CJM court continued since then. But on September 19, it was committed for the session trial.

Heading: Kusum Rai is BJP candidate - Indian Express
Content:
The electoral alliance between the Congress and the Samajwadi Party was formalised on Monday, with both parties agreeing to support Independent candidate Mohd Adib for the Rajya Sabha polls.

Leaders from both parties accompanied Adib, who filed his papers.

The AICC general secretary, Digvijay Singh, UP Congress committee president Rita Bahuguna Joshi, senior Congress leader Salman Khursheed, Akhilesh Yadav, MP and son of SP president Mulayam Singh Yadav , senior SP leader Ambika Chowdhary and Congress legislature party leader Pramod Tiwari were present on the occasion.

The in charge of UP affairs, Digvijay Singh, said: "The selection of a common candidate for Rajya Sabha was a collective decision of the leadership of both the parties — the Congress and the Samajwadi Party."

Mincing no words in praising the Samajwadi Party, he said the Congress is thankful to the SP for the support it extended for the nuclear deal and it was always there with the Congress to thwart the evil designs of communal forces.

Smiling, he added, "we would like to contest the next Lok Sabha polls in alliance with the SP".

Senior SP leaders Ambika Chaudhary and Akhilesh Yadav were not so forthcoming on the alliance, saying only the party high command will talk on the issue. "We will let you know when it happens," Chaudhary added.

Adib, a former Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) students' union president, will make his maiden entry to Rajya Sabha. Talking to the media immediately after the nomination, Adib said he would like to be considered a candidate of both Congress and the SP.

Heading: Traffic training institutes all set to start early - Indian Express
Content:
With the filing of nominations by the two remaining candidates, nomination process for the biennial Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh concluded in Lucknow on Monday.

Eight candidates had earlier filed their nominations, as 10 RS members from Uttar Pradesh are completing their terms on November 25.

Flanked by senior leaders of the Congress and the Samajwadi Party, Mohammed Adib filed his papers as their joint candidate. Springing a surprise on political observers, Kusum Rai filed her nomination as the BJP candidate. A member of the state legislative council, Rai is the lone BJP candidate to contest the RS polls from the state.

The BJP leader denied that she was given preference to placate her mentor, Kalyan Singh, who had reportedly expressed his differences with the party leaders over various issues.

"It is wrong to say that the BJP nominated me due to the pressure exerted by Kalyan Singh. There are no differences within the party," she added.

Singh, though, was absent during filing the nomination. "He is too big a leader to be present at this moment, but his experience will be sought whenever required," said Rai. She added, "My nomination indicates the commitment of my party for the betterment of women and their reservation in legislative Houses."

BJP state president Ramapati Tripathi said: "Kusum Rai deserved the nomination, as she is a senior woman leader of the party and a former chairperson of the UP Women Commission and also the national vice-president of the party's Mahila Morcha."

Earlier, six Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) members, Veer Singh, Akhilesh Das,

Brajesh Pathak, Avtar Singh Karimpuri, Raja Ram and Brijlal Khaabari, and two SP candidates, Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav, had filed their nominations.

All 10 candidates are likely to be elected unopposed on November 14, after the last date of withdrawing the nominations is over.

Heading: Smuggled currency in the past too, admits accused - Indian Express
Content:
Now, perhaps we can expect fewer accidents in the state. The Traffic Police Department is all set to begin at the beginning and educate children about different traffic signals and road signs by setting up traffic training parks in all the districts. 

While one such park is already running successfully in Kanpur since 1989, Ballia and Azamgarh districts have recently got one each. In the remaining 68 districts, land acquisition process for developing the parks is underway.

"Our target is to set up the parks in all the 71 districts. Directives have been issued to the concerned officials through the Deputy Inspector Generals to communicate with the authorities and municipal corporations to provide the land for the purpose," said Arun Kumar Gupta, Additional Director General, UP Traffic Directorate.

In the traffic training parks, children will be exposed to the various road safety measures through boards displaying the traffic signals and rules. Lights and boards will be put up along the miniature roads, walking tracks and green area that will be developed inside the park. Free literature on traffic rules and regulations will also be provided to the visitors, said Gupta.

A dummy of flyovers, airport, banks, schools, railways stations and hospitals will be erected in the parks to create awareness among the students, directing them how to drive near these places.

"To make the training interactive, documentaries explaining all the traffic rules and road signs will be screened in open theaters and mini auditoriums that will be developed inside the parks as per the availability of space," said Gupta.

"A museum on traffic rule awareness will be set up and swings will be installed for the entertainment of the children," Gupta said.

To woo the visitors, the authorities have decided to make the entry to the parks absolutely free of cost.

The department also intends to call schoolchildren to the parks from time to time.

According to an official, road accidents generally occur due to the violation of traffic rules. Owing to this the department decided to groom the young generation so that they eventually become responsible drivers.  

The process for land identification and acquisition for the parks has already been started in Jalaun, Badaun, Gautam Buddha Nagar, Meerut, Noida, Jyotiba Rao Phule Nagar, Bareilly, Muzaffarnagar and Saharanpur districts. The Mathura Development Authority has given the assurance to provide land for the parks.

"In Lucknow, we have approached the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) for eight acres to build the park. The authorities have asked us to propose the sites where we could develop the parks," said Gupta.  

The department has already started facing problems in acquiring land for the project. "Ideally, we need six to eight acres for developing a park. But in most places we have to manage with just one to four acres," he said.

Heading: Green Park stadium pulled up for tax default - Indian Express
Content:
Unnao-based Kamlesh Kanaujia and Virendra Kanaujia arrested on Saturday for allegedly smuggling currencies told the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) officials that they had carried out such activities in the past too.

The duo was arrested for allegedly carrying Rs 1 crore of Indian currency and Saudi Riyal and Dirham worth Rs 60 lakh.

A senior official with the agency said the currency seized from the accused was not part of any hawala racket. The cash was just being smuggled to Sharjah.

The court has remanded the two in DRI custody for 14 days. The transfer to the Lucknow jail will come into effect from Tuesday.

According to sources, the arrest was made following a tip-off from the Sharjah wing of DRI and the operation was conducted by a team from the Delhi office of the agency.

While Kamlesh Kanaujia runs a laundry shop in Sharjah, Virendra Kanaujia was an employee of the shop.

The Sharjah officials came to know about the consignment being carried by the two after intercepting their phone calls. The information was passed on to the Delhi headquarters and a team of the officials laid a trap at the Amausi airport.

The officials with the agency revealed that the scanning system put by the Customs & Excise Department and the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) at the Lucknow airport were not upgraded, as the baggage of the accused containing the hefty sum had been cleared.

The DRI team trapped the accused when they were about to board the aircraft, sources said.

Commandant CISF Lucknow airport S Ambastha, meanwhile, said: "The CISF checkpoint is supposed to keep a watch on objects, which could cause harm to the aircraft and the passengers."

"We ensure that no arms and ammunition, plastics or any wildlife-related objects pass while scanning of the baggage. We do not have any such device which could scan currency, gold or any such objects meant for smuggling," Ambastha said.

Heading: Targeted repeatedly, ciy traders nervous - Indian Express
Content:
Just days before the India-England one-day cricket match to be played at the Green Park stadium, the Kanpur Jal Sansthan has served a notice to the stadium authorities to clear the pending dues worth Rs 12.75 lakh.

The water board has asked the authorities to pay Rs 1.5 lakh before the match and clear the remaining amount before November 30, failing which sewer lines to the stadium will be disconnected.

 General Manager Jal Sansthan Ratan Lal told The Indian Express, "A notice was served to the Regional Sports Officer (RSO) and Director State Sports Department on Saturday but we are yet to receive any response." He added: "Considering the importance of the Indo-England ODI on November 20, the deadline of receiving the dues has been set for November 30. After which, we will block the sewer lines of the stadium."

Lal said Green Park authorities have to pay Rs 9 lakh in form of water and sewer tax, Rs 2.5 lakh for maintenance work carried out earlier in the stadium, and Rs 1.25 lakh for the maintenance work for the forthcoming Indo-England cricket match. "The stadium authorities have not cleared the taxes for the last 10 years," he added.

RSO Bula Ganguly, however, said, "I have not received any notice in the regard, hence I cannot comment on the issue." She claimed that no official of the Jal Sansthan has contacted her for the payment of pending dues.

Heading: Campaign against GM crops gaining momentum - Indian Express
Content:
With the recent spate of crime against traders and the city police yet to crack most cases, the business fraternity say they feel threatened and insecure.

On Sunday night, surgical equipment dealer Sardar Daljeet Singh was shot dead by two motorcycle-borne youths who fled with his bag containing several thousand rupees. The police are yet to establish the motive behind the murder.

The trader fraternity, particularly jewellers, say they have been a soft target for criminals.

"In the past one year, a number of crimes have taken place where businessmen have been targeted," said Vinod Maheshwari, general secretary, Lucknow Jewellers' Association. "In most cases, the offenders committed both murder and robbery."

This is the fourth incident in less than two months in which a trader has been targeted (see box).

None of the cases have been solved. Instead, the police allegedly harassed the trader community.

On September 18, Wazirganj police detained a traders' body leader illegally and kept him in the lock-up for a night. Two cops were suspended by the Senior Superintendent of Police.

Earlier this year, the entire jeweller community had come out on roads after two persons were murdered within five days.

On January 27, jeweller Rakesh Kapoor was killed by unknown miscreants. Five days later, Sunil Sahu was murdered in Hussainganj, the postmortem report said that the bullet that hit Sahu came from a.38 bore weapon.

Denying the allegation that the police are not concerned about the trader community, IG (Lucknow zone) AK Jain said: "The two recent incidents have made the people feel that we do not care. The fact is that we have even worked out the Khunkhunji case and arrested all the accused."

RECENT CRIMES AGAINST TRADERS
* November 9: Surgical equipment dealer Sardar Daljeet Singh shot dead by motorcycle-borne youths who fled with his bag containing cash
* November 5: Half a dozen miscreants broke into the house of the owner of Khunkhunji Jewellers and beat his wife, Usha Rani Aggarwal, to death
* October: Jeweller Jitendra Singh shot dead in Thakurganj
* October 26: Over a dozen robbers decamped with medical stock worth Rs 21 lakh from a godown in Sarojini Nagar after overpowering the security guard
* September 13: In a daylight robbery, three unidentified gunmen fired at Mahalaxmi jewellery shop owners before fleeing with jewellery from their shop in Indira Nagar

Heading: ID recruitment scam: CBI yet to submit papers - Indian Express
Content:
The distinction between a vegetarian and a non-vegetarian might soon get blurred with the introduction of genetically modified crops.

Now, imagine tomatoes, which are genetically modified with the gene of a pig. This has sparked a global campaign against genetically modified (GM) foods. Uttar Pradesh, too, has been engulfed in the campaign — "I am no lab rat".

With over 9,000 school and college students from Lucknow having become a part of the campaign in the last one month, the campaign moved to the remote areas of the state through extensive signature and awareness campaigns.

Speaking about the campaign, Utkarsh Kumar Sinha, Director of Centre for Contemporary Studies and Research, which is initiating this campaign, said: "GM foods will slowly be entering our lives. BT Brinjal, which is genetically modified with an animal gene, is likely to be approved by the Centre. The other food items whose trials are being conducted include ladyfinger, cauliflower, cabbage, potato and corn."

The campaign brings to limelight the fact that human beings are not ready to be used for such tests and strongly oppose the consumption of such products. "Imagine eating a tomato with a pig's gene, a potato with a scorpion's gene, a ladyfinger with a cow's gene and so on," said Sinha.

"There have been reports of a popular international wafers brand using GM potatoes. Modifying may add to the nutrition value of the vegetable. But the interchange of the two different families of the gene — plants and animals — has resulted in the increase in allergies among human beings, especially children," added Sinha.

After schools and colleges, the campaign has reached the cinema halls too. "We have spoken to the entertainment tax commissioner. While slides on awareness against GM foods are already running in cinema halls across the city, we will be doing the same in all the halls across the state," said Dr Anupam Pandey, coordinator of the campaign.

"We will be creating awareness among the farmers and the rural populace, along with the urban youth and the intelligentsia. We are running a signature campaign for the Union Health Minister, Ambumani Ramadoss, as GM foods have strong health hazards," said R P Shahi, another coordinating partner of the campaign.

Heading: Teenager kills aunt to avenge ‘insult’, arrested - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation has again failed to submit the documents related to the refusal of prosecution sanction for UP Home Secretary Mahesh Gupta in the Information Directorate recruitment scam.

Gupta held the post of the director when the scam was detected.

The court had asked the Investigating Officer to submit the papers on Monday after Gupta's lawyer raised objection over filing of the chargesheet.

The CBI lawyer, however, submitted an application seeking more time for making the required papers available to the court.

"The court has set the date of November 29 to hear the matter and has asked the CBI to produce the documents," said CBI lawyer KP Singh.

Defense lawyer Nandit Srivastava, however, said: "I had raised strong objection over the CBI filing the chargesheet against Gupta concealing facts from the court."

The state government, he said, had sent the documents related to the prosecution sanction against Gupta to the CBI and the Centre, "scuttling the grounds sought by the investigating agency".

The Centre, too, has found the grounds insufficient and turned down the request for the prosecution against the IAS officer. But the CBI, Srivastava said, did not apprise the court about the refusal of the prosecution sanction.

Heading: Toll in Meerut blast reaches 6 - Indian Express
Content:
With the arrest of two youths and the recovery of the stolen laptop and two mobiles, the Allahabad police claim to have busted the Kusum Singh murder case on Monday.

The arrested youths were identified as 18-year-old Pinto Singh — nephew of the deceased woman Kusum — and his friend Shailendra Singh.

Kusum Singh (50), wife of Prithvi Pal Singh, a railway contractor was brutally murdered while she was alone in her house at George Town on November 7.  

After surveillance, the George Town police arrested the accused from their residence. "My aunt used to rebuke me and never liked me. A year ago, she caught me stealing something from her house. Since then she looked at me with scorn," said Pinto, who was in police custody.

On the fateful day, Pinto visited his aunt Kusum. Following an altercation, Pinto attacked his aunt.

According to the police, Pinto dragged her to the kitchen and hit her on the head with a heavy frying pan. In a fit of rage, Pinto repeatedly stabbed her with a knife. He then took out the laptop and two mobiles from the cupboard and left the spot.

After covering some distance Pinto called his friend Shailendra and went to Sarai Inayat. "I had made up my mind to take revenge of the insult," said Pinto.  

Senior Superintendent of Police Ashok Muttha Jain said that the police were also working on the abduction of Kusum's son Balram, who did not return home for the last four years.

Heading: Govt cautious on Russian submarine - Indian Express
Content:
With a 12-year-old victim, Amir, succumbing to his injuries on Sunday night, the death toll in the Saturday blast in Ashiana Colony in Ahmed Nagar has risen to six. The police and Army authorities are clueless about where the bombs came from. The Army says such heavy mortars are not used in the firing ranges here, and the Army keeps records of used and unused mortars. They suspect the mortars were perhaps found in imported scrap and found its way into the scrap dealer's shop after someone dumped it.

Asserting that investigations were on, SSP Raghubir Lal said the mortars came from the local scrap, not the imported one, and had exploded during casual handling. Police officers said a search was conducted in the basti but no more bombs were found. Earlier, six mortars found in the basti were also defused by the bomb disposal squad.

The police will conduct an identity verification drive of the Bengali basti where six persons were killed in a blast on Saturday. The state Director General of Police Vikram Singh visited the area on Monday evening where the blasts had taken place.

Heading: Culture-Shocked - Indian Express
Content:
Unlike the film industry, new soaps introduce 'fresh' faces for lead roles instead of cashing in on the established ones

With every new soap, half-a-dozen new faces are launched. If we go by the average — five new soaps a month — 2008 alone has seen over 250 new actors on television. The astounding statistics compel one to ask how does the industry absorb so many actors?

Part of the answer lies in the launch of new channels. But the main reason is the dynamics of the industry where a fresh face is preferred over an established name. The known actors then rarely return in lead roles, acceding to play supporting cast in a soap or participating in reality shows.

Often, 'big' faces go obscure once the soap's off the air or the script changes track. They age off, die, get kidnapped or undergo plastic surgery. Sumeet Sachdev, Gautam in Kyunkii Saas Bhi Bahu Thi, was once the lead but generation leaps ate into his role. He's not been part of another show. Now, with Kyunkii's doubtful future, he too may become invisible unless he reinvents himself. Instant recollection yields other such names — Preeti Amin of Jhoom Barabar Jhoom, Poorva Gokhale of Kkoi Dil Mein Hai, Vikas Manaktala and Priyanka Bassi of Left Right Left.

The word in the industry is that the new-face phenomenon is the offshoot of the tantrums the actors throw after tasting success. The producers however, deny this. "The characters on the small screen are more memorable than the actors who play them. So it's difficult to launch, say, a Rajshri Thakur as the lead in another show as people still remember her as Saloni of Saat Phere. Moreover, even though I wish to hire her, I can't, unless I have a script where her character will override Saloni's popularity," explains Sunjoy Wadhwa of Sphere Origin Productions. One can recall how Sakshi Tanwar's role as Ganga in Kahaani Hamaarey Mahabharat Ki didn't go down well with the audience because they couldn't think of her as anyone but Parvati of Kahaani Ghar Ghar Kii.

Rajan Shahi of Director's Kut feels that time commitments also contribute to the strain. "To play the lead is as much a drawback as an advantage. If an actor is shooting for me 10 hours a day, they don't have time to do much else," he remarks. "Besides, soaps are driven by scripts — new faces bring freshness to new characters." Citing an example, he points out that there are hardly any faces in the industry that could have done justice to the four young characters in the new show Miley Jab Hum Tum.

It leads to fierce competition, but these days, with the advent of reality shows and experimentation with scripts, a la Balika Vadhu, the actors have more options. Karan Panthaky, the lead in Jhoom Barabar Jhoom, points out, "Reality shows like Nach Baliye require many senior actors, which paves the way for new ones on other shows." Panthaky has not been seen after his show went off air two months ago. "I'm open to doing non-lead roles; after all, these days, villains are more important."

But Sanjeeda Sheikh disagrees that the career scope of an actor is limited after having played the lead. "My role as a vamp in Kayamath became more popular than my lead character in Kya Hoga Nimmo Ka."

Sheikh will soon be seen in a film but says she's happier doing TV. "There's so much to do. I have no complains."

Heading: TALKING POINT with  RJ Maliska - Indian Express
Content:
Young visitors from Pakistan gape to find the world famous 'Lakhnavi tehzeeb' missing

Famous for its tehzeeb, the city of nawabs has failed to live up to the expectations of Pakistani delegation visiting the city. The ten member delegation from Laurelbank School System, Lahore, comprising students and teachers are in the city to take part in the four day International Geography Olympiad 'Geofest 2008' taking place in City Montessori School (CMS), Kanpur Road from November 8-11.

"We had heard a lot about the culture and pehle aap tehzeeb of the city. While traveling in city buses yesterday, the scenario was bad. However, we haven't seen much of the city yet and will hopefully get a glimpse of the rich tradition then. Though we received a warm welcome from the school authorities, the city is like any other," said Salma Miyan, Director of the Laurelbank School System.

Even the children participants from Pakistan are a disappointed lot. "As the name suggests, we thought that questions related to 'Geofest' would be from Geography. We did extensive preparations accordingly. However, during the competition, questions related to other subjects like English, Hindi, Biology and Physics were also asked. Though we were not expecting that, we still did our best," said Sumaiya Kidwai, an eleventh standard student of the school.

Taking an inspiration from the co-curricular activities here, Miyan said, "Extra curricular activities take places in our school, but the focus is on the academic. I think we need to put more emphasis on extra curricular activities in our schools as well.

" The high confidence level of the students here is motivating for the Pakistani students as well. "The students here are extremely confident. While we get nervous before competitions, their confidence level seems to be intact. I think we need to work more on increasing our confidence level," said Kidwai.

With their trip coming to an end on Wednesday, the students are all set to shop so that they can take back chikankari and jewellery as requested by their friends and family members. "I have made many friends here and we will stay in touch through emails and letters," said Khansa Saeed, a tenth standard student of the school.

Heading: 'Bomber' Sadiq also hit American Center: Cops - Indian Express
Content:
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Monday night said that US President-elect Barack Obama had tried to speak to him but the contact could not be established because of "paucity of time" and his travel.

"No, this is not true," Singh said when asked if the newly elected US President had ignored India by not calling him.

"President Obama wanted to talk to me day before yesterday (November 8) (but) we could not establish contact because the time that was suggested was too short for me (to establish contact). Since then, I have been travelling... as soon as I go back (we will try to establish contact)," Singh told reporters on way back to New Delhi from his maiden three-day visit to the energy rich Gulf region.

Obama had phoned fifteen world leaders including Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari after being elected US President.

As Singh did not get any call from Obama, there were suggestions that the next US President was ignoring India.

Singh said Obama had written to him a "very warm" letter even before he was elected President.

"I had myself written a warm letter to him," he said.

Singh was hopeful that Indo-US ties under Obama would be further strengthened.

"I got a very warm letter from him, a detailed letter spelling out his approach to India, his approach to international affairs and therefore, I have every reason to believe that India's relations with the US under President Obama will become stronger than ever before," he said.

The Prime Minister said he had received immediate acknowledgement of the condolence message he had sent to Obama on the death of his grandmother.

"I also condoled his grandmother's death and he immediately acknowledged that letter," Singh added.

Heading: Traffic heads south as recession hits airlines - Indian Express
Content:
Police in Kolkata and Mumbai on Monday announced that Mohammed Sadiq alias Sadaqat, one of the terror suspects held for the recent string of blasts across the country, had also carried out the January 2002 attack on the American Center in Kolkata which left six policemen dead.

Rajiv Kumar, Special Additional Commissioner of the Special Task Force of Kolkata Police, said Sadiq, who hails from Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh, was arrested from the Cheetah Camp near Trombay on September 24 by Mumbai Police. Kolkata policemen went to Mumbai to question him. Mumbai policemen and the STF also interrogated Aftab Ansari, the prime accused in the American Center attack, and his accomplices in the Alipur Central Jail recently.

According to police, it was Sadiq who gunned down the policemen outside the American Center on January 22, 2002. The attack was planned by Amir Reza Khan and Aftab Ansari who was then based in Dubai. Ansari was later held and deported to India.

The police claimed that during his questioning, Sadiq confessed to firing at the policemen from an AK-47 rifle after reaching there on a two-wheeler with one of his accomplices. A day before the shooting, he had stayed at a house in Tiljala Lane and had introduced himself as Sadaqat.

Mumbai Joint Commissioner of Police Rakesh Maria said: "We have established that Sadiq was one of the two men who had opened fire on the American Centre in Kolkata in 2002. This has been verified through information gathered by us and by positive identification of the accused. Sadiq is currently in judicial custody and he will eventually be taken to Kolkata."

Police said he fled to Hazaribagh, boarding a train from Howrah within an hour of the attack. Police tracked him down to Hazaribagh but he managed to escape. However, one of his accomplices, Zaheed, was killed in an encounter with the police. Sadiq surfaced in Azamgarh and later headed for Mumbai.

Heading: Buddha seeks CRPF deployment - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Civil Aviation Ministry has projected yearly air traffic of 20 million passengers by 2010, most domestic airlines are trying to tackle the decrease in passenger load.

While suspension of the London-Kolkata flight of the British Airways was the first major blow in international segment, Air India also recently announced withdrawal of its London-Kolkata from March 2009.

Domestic flights are also feeling the pinch. Compared to October 2007, the number of Jet Airways flights operating from Kolkata has gone down by four. While one of the two Chennai-bound flights has been withdrawn, the airlines has suspended its flights to Port Blair and Ahmedabad.  One flight to Delhi also remains suspended.

Jet Airways sources said the night flights to Mumbai and Delhi are reeling under pressure, with less than 45 per cent seat occupancy.

After the merger of Kingfisher and Air Deccan, the number of flights has also gone down. "In October last year, Kingfisher had 16 flights from Kolkata. This year the number stands at 14. We are facing a decline of 10 to 15 per cent in air traffic compared to last year," said an official of Kingfisher Airways.

Low cost carrier SpiceJet has also withdrawn its flight to Hyderabad from July 2008.

"While the seat occupancy last year was near 75 per cent, this year it is less than 70 per cent," said an Air India official. According to officials of the Kolkata airport, passenger traffic in the domestic sector has decreased by 15 to 20 per cent in the last few months.

Heading: CPM, Maoists the same, Mamata tells Nandigram - Indian Express
Content:
Lalgarh going out of control

With the Maoist-affected areas of West Midnapore being cut off from the rest of Bengal following the tribal protest against police, the state government has asked for Central Reserve Police Force.

On Monday, tribals cut off two vital road links in Binpur and Lalgarh police station areas in the presence of the much-hyped state combat force.

As the news reached the Writers' Buildings, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee held an emergency meeting with Chief Secretary Amit Kiran Deb and Home Secretary Ashok Mohan Chakrabarti. Sources in chief minister's secretariat said Bhattacharjee has realised that the situation is beyond the control of the state police and asked for CRPF deployment at the earliest.

After the meeting, the home secretary said: "The chief secretary is visiting Delhi tomorrow.

We have asked for six CRPF companies to tackle the situation." Sources said the Central agency will be deployed in Lalgarh, Lalgarh, Binpur and Belpahari police station areas.

During his telephonic conversation with Home Minister Shivraj Patil on Sunday, Bhattacharjee had mentioned the situation in Lalgarh and the need for CRPF deployment.

Additional District Magistrate R A Israel was present when the roads were dug up by villagers in Dherua. "Though our combat force was deployed, we could not prevent the villagers," he said, "we will again request them to sit for talks and desist from such acts."

The area has been on the boil after the combing operations by police following the attack on chief minister's convoy on November 2.

The blast took place in Shalboni, 50 km from Lalgarh. But on the night of November 3, police raided Chotopelia, Dalilpur and Kantapahari villages in Lalgarh and tortured six women. Locals say they also picked up several innocent people, including some schoolboys.

"Until police admits their atrocities, our agitation will continue," said one of the protesting locals.

Bharat Jakat Majhi Maroa (BJMM), headed by one Chandrashekhar Mahato, is leading the agitation.

The district administration tried to control the situation by calling an all-party meeting, but the effort failed as all parties except the CPM walked out of the meeting.

"We are trying to resolve the crisis," said Rajesh Singh, a district police officer. The CPM, meanwhile, has decided to take its own initiative.

The party's district secretary Dipak Sarkar said: "The police have asked the protestors to repair the roads by Monday. If they don't, we will go there tomorrow and undertake the repair work ourselves."

District Magistrate NS Nigam held a meeting at Jhargram today. After the meet, he said: "The government has agreed on some proposals submitted by the protestors."

On Tuesday, he will meet the tribal leaders again.

Heading: Gujarat team in Bengal to woo agro-based industries - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee alleged that Maoists and CPM are hand-in-glove in the state and dared the government to ban the ultra Left outfit. Kicking off her campaign for the Nandigram by-elections at a rally there on Monday, she said her party's candidate belong to one of the 14 families who lost a loved one in the March 14, 2007, police firing.

"They are the family members of the martyrs," Banerjee said at the Gokulnagar High school, "I have asked my district leadership to find a suitable candidate". Coming down heavily on the ruling party, Banerjee said the CPM and the Maoists "are the same".

"I dare them to ban the Maoist organisations," she said. "The so-called Maoists are active in West Midnapur, Bankura and Purulia. The Trinamool has won no seat in these districts, how does the CPM always win? The CPM has entered a secret deal with such outfits and is using them."

By-elections in Nandigram are to be held in December, as legislator Muhammed Illias had to resign recently after charges of bribery.

Banerjee also announced that she has instructed the district leadership to provide help to the family members of those killed and missing.

"I have given my district leaders three months time to help these people. They should be provided houses under Indira Bikas Yojana and help through other such programmes. I will inspect the progress personally. We should not forget the martyrs," Banerjee said.

Alleging that the CPM-led state government is not allowing TMC-led East Midnapur Zilla Parishad to undertake development works, she said the dates for by-elections have not been announced. But district administration is not allowing any big development project. "The district administration is deliberately not allowing us to work for the people," she said.

Regarding Sunday's CPM rally in Nandigram, she said Trinamool is ready to combat them politically. "But if they use force anything can happen. I will urge the CPM and the state government not to play with fire and not repeat the mistakes of Nandigram and Singur again."

She donated six ambulances for Nandigram and provided a monitory grant of Rs 5 lakh each to the Dawudpur Madrasa and Benepur High School.

Heading: CBI rapped for being soft on cops accused in Rizwanur case - Indian Express
Content:
To woo investors from West Bengal, the Gujarat government in association with the Confederation of Indian Industry organised a presentation, "Vibrant Gujarat", on Monday to promote agriculture and food processing industries in the western state.

Keventers Agro Limited, Ma Sarada Cold Storage, Amit Biotech, GTS Sea Foods, Exodus Marine Products and Exports and Adhunik Corporation were some of the companies from West Bengal who attended the presentation.

Speaking regarding the potential of agriculture-based industries and possibilities of investments in the sector, representatives of the Department of Agriculture and Cooperation of Gujarat said the agriculture is still in its nascent stage and the Gujarat government is looking for private investments in the sector.

"Agriculture sector in Gujarat has transformed in the last few years. This year, it has registered a growth of 12 per cent at constant prices and is estimated to touch 15 per cent by the year end," said SC Srivastav, Managing Director, Gujarat Agro Industries Corporation.

The Gujarat team emphasised that the state provides a number of advantages to investors like integrated water management, well-developed irrigation facilities, 40 major crops and cropping systems, strong agri-research capabilities, emerging contract farming and the state government's policy for single window clearance of projects.

Principal Secretary of Gujarat's Agriculture Department PN Roy Chowdhury refused to comment on the West Bengal government's handling of the Singur issue.

"The Gujarat government can efficiently handle the tussle between industries and society, keeping in view the interests of all parties," said Roy Chowdhury.

He added, "When it comes to business, time is precious and problems should be resolved quickly."

With four agriculture universities in the state, the Gujarat team also stressed on the possibility of cooperation between the two states in research areas.

"We have seen West Bengal's growth in agriculture sector. We are constantly in touch with the state government on cooperation in the field of agriculture and food processing research," said Chowdhury.

The Vibrant Gujarat in the city precedes a two-day global investors' summit on agricultural prospects in Gujarat that will be held in Ahmedabad from November 12.

According to organisers, the presentation will also be held in Mumbai and New Delhi.

Heading: Don’t arrest Todi till Nov 17: SC tells CBI - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation is drawing flak for dropping the name of former deputy police commissioner (Headquarters) Gyanwant Singh from the list of accused in the murder of graphic designer Rizwanur Rehman. CBI sources said the newly-appointed director of the agency, Ashwani Kumar, has rapped some officers in Kolkata in this regard.

Sources said some CBI officials, probing the Rehman case, were reportedly lenient towards the accused police officers. "Singh was named in the chargesheet several times but his name did not figure in the list of the accused," said a CBI official. "If Ajay Kumar and the other two officers can be accused of abetting Rehman's suicide, then Singh should also be held responsible," he added.

CBI lawyers in Kolkata have recently sent a letter to Kumar, pointing at the anomaly. "The letter says that the CBI advocates believed that Singh should not have been left out from the list of the accused," said a source in the CBI legal cell. Sources said some CBI officers were also not happy that senior CBI prosecutor Partha Tapaswi had opposed the bail petition of the three police officers— former Deputy Commissioner (Detective Department) Ajay Kumar, Assistant Commissioner Sukanti Chakraborty, Sub-Inspector Krishnendu Das— on September 27. "Some CBI officers had called us several times and asked why we were opposing the bail petition," said the source in CBI legal cell.

Many trace this lenient attitude of the Central agency to the meeting of former Kolkata police commissioner Kolkata Prasun Kumar with the then CBI Director, Vijay Shankar, on October 10, 2007. "The two are very good friends and are from the same IPS batch of 1973-74. Prasun had reportedly requested the CBI to be soft towards the accused police officers," the source said.

Scenario changed after Ashwani Kumar took over as the new CBI Director and issued strict instructions that no one should be spared in the case. "He has pulled some CBI officers in Kolkata for not taking the three officers in custody, when the court had not granted them bail," said the CBI source.

Heading: Govt ready to change PTTI diploma into 2-yr course - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Monday asked the CBI not to arrest industrialist Ashok Todi till November 17 in connection with the Rizwanur Rehman murder case.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan and Justices P Sathasivam and J M Panchal said, "The CBI may see that he is not arrested till Monday (November 17)."

A metropolitan magistrate in Kolkata had asked Todi to appear before the court on October 27 but he failed to abide by the order, prompting the court to issue non-bailable warrants against him.

Todi's plea seeking a stay on the NBW will be taken up by the apex court on November 17.

Fearing arrest in the case, Todi had moved the apex court on November 7 seeking urgent hearing in the matter.

Senior advocate Harish Salve, appearing for Todi, had said despite the October 13 order of the apex court there was no protection to the industrialist. The SC had said in its October 13 order that trial in the case would not commence till the Calcutta High Court decides a petition filed by Todi challenging CBI's decision to chargesheet him.

In a related development, the three police officers, accused in Rizwanur Rehman murder case, appeared before the CBI court on Monday. Magistrate Madhumita Roy fixed November 20 as the date of next hearing.

The three officers — former Deputy Commissioner (Detective Department) Ajay Kumar, Assistant Commissioner Sukanti Chakraborty, Sub-Inspector Krishnendu Das — were released on an interim bail granted by the sessions court on October 1. Another accused Pappu, a friend of the Rizwanur family, was also produced in the CBI court on Monday and remanded in custody for another 10 days.

The counsel of the Rehman family, meanwhile, moved a plea before a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court that the hearing of the appeal filed by Ashok Todi begins as soon as possible. Chief Justice of the Calcutta HC S S Nijjar said the case will come up for hearing in due time.

Ashok Todi and the three police officers had filed an appeal before the Division Bench headed by the Chief Justice challenging the verdict by Justice Dipankar Dutta, who had observed that the action of the police officers in the Rehman murder case was unconstitutional.

Heading: Minister calls BESU violence unfortunate, supports code of conduct for students - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has requested the National Council of Teachers Education (NCTE) to approve the one-year old diploma of nearly 75,000 students, after which the government will accept other suggestions of the NCTE.

"We have suggested that the NCTE should approve the one-year diploma and then we are ready to make it a two-year correspondence course and augment other infrastructure facilities," said School Education Minister Partha De.

The state government has approached the open universities in the state for providing a one-year diploma to the PTTI students through correspondence.

Vice-Chancellor of Netaji Subhas Open University Monimala Das said the government has sent a proposal to the university.

"Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee has written to Human Resources Minister Arjun Singh on Monday and we hope that in consultation with the NCTE and the Centre the issue can be resolved," said De.

The minister said there is a shortage of 38,000 teachers in the state and the appointment of teachers will not be suspended.

"Since the court has declared the degrees of the PTTI students invalid, the state government cannot give them preference in the recruitment," De said.

Meanwhile, PTTI students observed protests in various parts of the state on Monday. In Kolkata, they took out a rally on College Street.

Later in the evening, they submitted a memorandum to Left Front Chairman Biman Bose seeking his help in resolving the issue.

"We will withdraw protests only if the state government starts the recruitment of the PTTI-trained students," said Pintu Parui, a PTTI student representative.

The students also gheroed the Bishnupur police station in Bankura protesting against the arrest of 11 PTTI students for allegedly attacking the school education minister's car last week.

The arrested students have been sent in judicial custody till November 17.

The students sent a deputation to the Bankura police station In-charge Sisir Roy. Along with the students, leaders of other political parties also joined the protest.

Heading: Mayor signs agreement with Chinese city - Indian Express
Content:
State Higher Education Minister Sudarshan Roy Chowdhury has described the instances of violence in Bengal Engineering and Science University (BESU) as unfortunate and said that a code of conduct should be implemented for the students.

"BESU is awaiting the status of Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology (IIEST) and such incidents at this crucial time are unfortunate," the minister said.

Last month, Roy Chowdhury had asked the Ministry of Human Resource and Development to confer the IIEST status to the university at the earliest. To expedite the process, Higher Education Secretary Satish Tewari will be visiting Delhi in November.

The minister has also spoken to former Vice-Chancellor of BESU Sparshmani Chatterjee, who is looking into the instances of violence that rocked the campus in March this year. Chatterjee is yet to submit his report on the incidents.

"Prof Chatterjee said that he is interested in a code of conduct for the students. I have welcomed his suggestions," said Roy Chowdhury. On whether the minister is satisfied with the work of present V-C NR Banerjea, he said that he has asked Banerjea to take everybody into confidence before taking any decision.

Meanwhile, accompanied by students, celebrities like Mahasweta Devi and Bibhas Chakraborty organised a protest march between Subodh Mullik Square and Metro Channel, Esplanade, against the arrest of eight BESU students on November 6 on charges of deterring a public servant from doing his duty and injuring him. The protestors criticised the state government and university authorities for their partiality, when dealing with student unions opposing the CPM-backed Students Federation of India.

The protestors said that they will file a petition in the court for the release of the students. The judicial custody of the arrested students ends on November 11.

Heading: ‘Obama’s DNA blends Black and White races’ - Indian Express
Content:
With an aim to promote investments and cooperation in the field of tourism, culture and administrative work, Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya and a delegation from Kunming, capital of Hunan province in southwestern China, signed a 'Sister City Agreement' on Monday.

The Chinese delegation was led by Kunming People's Municipal Government Mayor Zhang Zulin and deputy Mayor Wang Xiaoguang.

"Under the agreement, both the civic bodies will encourage business organisations to invest in sister cities," said Mayor Zulin.

Kunming has two major industrial development zones — Kunming High-tech Industrial Development Zone and Kunming Economic and Technology Development Zone. While the former is dedicated to industries dealing in biological medicine, new materials, electronic information, photoelectron and agriculture, the latter promotes mechanical equipment production, biological science and food industry, information industry and software industry.

"The agreement will promote tourism in both the cities. We will try to attract tourists from Hunan province to our state," said Bhattacharya.

The opposition in the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, however, seems to be unhappy with this agreement.

"Earlier we had proposed an agreement with Sanghai, but it could not be materialised. In my tenure, I had signed memorandum of understanding with cities like Yorkshire (the United Kingdom) and Odessa (Ukraine), which attracted several investments in the city and promoted tourism. But an agreement with a city that is not as big as Kolkata, is not going to aid the development of the city," said former Mayor Subrata Mukherjee.

UK business team visits city
Even as West Bengal is trying to lure foreign investors, a UK business contingent is visiting the city on Tuesday to market UK as a destination for Indian Investors. The contingent, comprising nearly 12 representatives from 10 development agencies of the UK, will also attend the NASSCOM CEO Summit on November 11 and 12. These agencies work closely with UK traders and investors to promote overseas investment. Invest Northern Ireland, Yorkshire forward, International Business Wales, Think London are some of the agencies visiting the city. "We have four major Indian investors in IT sector in Northern Ireland. This has generated employment for nearly 3,000 people in the region. We are looking to attract more Indian investors," said Barry Clark, Senior V-P, India Invest Northern Ireland.

Heading: Prisoners set up a palette, enthrall the city with painting exhibition - Indian Express
Content:
Barack Obama's victory in the US presidential election may be seen as the triumph of Blacks over the years of subjugation, South African writer, activist and Nobel Laureate Nadine Gordimer sees it a tad differently. "Obama is being celebrated as a Black but he is actually half Black and half White. The greatest triumph is that his DNA has an amalgamation of the Blacks and White races," she said.

In Kolkata to participate in the Nobel lecture tour organised by the Ministry of External Affairs, Gordimer's talk touched upon issues ranging from a writer's responsibility towards the society, terrorism stalking human kind and the common thread running through the works of Indian and South African writers.

From Nayantara Sahgal to R K Narayan, her favourite Indian author, to Shashi Throor, Raindranath Tagore and even Arvind Adiga, all found place in her discourse, with a special mention of Tagore's Chokher Bali, she had read in 2003. No wonder, she quoted Piccaso that an artist is a political being, who constantly analyses developments in the world.

Taking note of globalisation, she said the term hints at trade agreements between different nations and not something that met requirements of the common people.

While she acknowledged the Indian Independence, she also emphasised the horrors of Partition that it unleashed and that the caste system still existed in India in spite of the freedom.

Drawing upon the shared experiences of Indian and South Africa, she said the two nations shared not merely the history but also a common attempt to preserve their vernacular literature. "South Africa has 9 traditional languages besides Afrikaanas and English, which brings it close to multilingual India," said the writer.

Heading: CESC recruits Singapore firm to improve city’s power network - Indian Express
Content:
Jailbirds pick up brush and palette, splash the canvas with colours. And become the toast of Kolkata. The works of renowned artists are not the only draw with art aficionados in Kolkata. In a recent exhibition, paintings by inmates of correctional homes in the state fetched nearly Rs 1.5 lakh, as 40 paintings were sold in three weeks.

The exhibition, held at the Birla Academy of Art and Culture, saw the fruits of months-long workshops conducted at the Alipore Central Jail, with 33 inmates of various jails participating in it.

"Of 390 paintings put on display, we sold 40. This is a big achievement considering that most of the jailbirds had had no exposure to art. In fact, they had taken up the brush for the first time," said artist Chitta Dey, who had conducted the workshops.

With several high-profile convicts like Happy Singh and Sajal Barui participating in the workshops, their paintings and sculptures priced between Rs 1000 to Rs 10,000 capture the tension of connoisseurs. A Calcutta High Court lawyer Mamata Bhargava bought Mithun Kumar Haldar's painting Orchid. "I like the vibrant colours of this painting. It does not matter that a convict painted it," she said.

Inspector General (Correctional Services) B D Sharma said the prisoners will get 40 per cent from the proceeds of the sale and the rest will be donated to the prisoners' welfare fund. "Inamtes have their monetary requirements. Although the money they earn during their stay at the correctional homes is supposed to be kept in a bank account, we are giving them cash," he said.

The IG also said, "The money donated to the welfare fund will be spent on conducting various recreational activities for prisoners and for education and marriage of their children."

The prisoners are now keen to continue with art workshops and they hope to hold another exhibition soon. Buoyed by the success of the exhibition, the Birla Academy will renovate the art and craft school at the Alipore Jail for a permanent display of art works.

Heading: Animated Takes - Indian Express
Content:
Then, the adulation flustered Chitrangada Singh; now, she is eager for more

They loved her for her looks; they loved her for her histrionics. Five years ago, most of those who walked out of the cinemas, having watched the end credits roll on Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi, got starry-eyed about Chitrangada Singh. Since talented dusky heroines have to be called the new Smita Patil, that moniker also stuck. It was anybody's dream debut, except that she wasn't ready for it. "The adulation was too unsettling for me and I did not know how to react. I had to think about what I really wanted to do," says Singh, at her home in Gurgaon, having returned from a sky-diving camp in Hissar.

So she disappeared from the scene, except for an appearance in the 2005 dud Kal: Yesterday and Tomorrow, while rumours went about in B-town that her husband, the golfer Jyoti Randhawa, had stopped her from acting. Now, after a child, a few charcoal painting sessions and yoga, she is back — in Onir's Sorry Bhai, that also stars Shabana Azmi and Boman Irani. Singh calls this "a new beginning" rather than a "comeback", and you can already sense the anxiety in her voice. "I am slightly nervous. It has been some time since I acted," she says.

The break evidently did her good; for one, she realised that two films are not even a blip in Bollywood. "When I joined, I had no godfather. Now I have learnt to cope with the attention and I don't discount the fame that my first movie has brought; it has got me where I am today. But there is no pressure to perform," she says. And Onir called her just when she was eager to return before the camera. "I had changed my phone number and was out of touch with everyone in the industry. I was also hesitant to call up directors and ask for work. Somehow, someone gave my number to Onir, he asked me and I immediately agreed to do the film," she says, laughing at the serendipity of it all.

The film sees Singh playing a girl caught between the affection of two brothers played by Sanjay Suri and Sharman Joshi. "There is a twist to the love angle. It is dealt with innocently and happily, not like a clichéd love triangle," she says. Sorry Bhai also sees Singh cast alongside her childhood idol, Shabana Azmi. "I just admire her career graph. She handles and guides the scene effortlessly, which is an art in itself. On the sets, I was a sucker for her and sat for hours watching her. She even advised me against studying acting," says Singh, as she rates Arth and Masoom among Azmi's greatest films.

The comeback girl, who calls herself "a director's actor who can't act if she doesn't understand the role", is not choosy. "Any challenging role appeals to me. Commercial, art house, period — I am open to anything," she says. After her dream debut with Sudhir Mishra, she will be back on his sets in December for Aur Devdas where she plays Chandramukhi. "He appreciates my acting and I like his kind of cinema," she says. The Mishra-Singh tango doesn't end there. She also stars in his Nawab and John Company that releases in July next year.

Heading: Lockett Charm - Indian Express
Content:
A cluster of awareness films to be shown at the Kolkata Film Festival today bear testimony to the blossoming of animation industry in the city

Between catching a Tarr or a Renoir classic at the Kolkata Film Festival (KFF) this year, you might just want to spend some time with Laadli, the last woman on earth. Or maybe take a joy ride in the Janta Car, which is the symbol of true socialism in modern India.
