Heading: Peru offers bald dog of Incas to Obama family - Indian Express
Content:
Last year at this time, Kathy Johnson and her husband traveled to London and Paris, where she spent about $2,000 on a shiny, red Louis Vuitton shoulder bag and a matching charm without much thought.

This year Johnson, who runs a tech advisory firm with her husband in the San Francisco Bay area, is recycling older dresses to save money.

"I'm thinking 'Maybe I'll just sneak in last year's dress and nobody will notice,' and I'll just accessorize it a bit differently," said Johnson, who expects to attend several holiday parties this year.

"I try to make it a little more about what I need on an everyday basis, rather than spending a bunch of money on something I'll just wear once or twice," she said.

Johnson's logic is likely to be played out across the country this season as US consumers cut spending amid the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

That is terrible news to department stores, boutiques and apparel makers, who tend to get a boost when the fashion-conscious splurge on clothes for office holiday parties and New Year's festivities.

US retail chains just posted the worst October sales results in more than three decades, prompting the International Council of Shopping Centers to pare its already grim forecast for holiday season sales. It now expects November-December sales to rise 1 per cent, from a prior view of 1.7 per cent.

What is more, a recent survey by executive search firm Battalia Winston Amrop found that one-fifth of US businesses are not having 2008 holiday parties, effectively passing out pink slips to women's 'little black dresses'.

That could hurt department stores like Nordstrom Inc and Macy's Inc, already struggling with sharp monthly sales declines, as well as women's apparel stores like AnnTaylor Stores Corp, Talbots Inc and Chico's FAS Inc, which owns the White House Black Market chain in addition to its namesake stores.

"I think (consumers) are going to be very loath to buy anything," said Wendy Liebmann, chief executive of consulting firm WSL Strategic Retail, which researches shopping trends.

As for herself, Liebmann guessed that she will feel the need to be festive during this gloomy holiday season.

"But I know there's a very wonderful corner of a very wonderful closet of mine, which has absolutely fabulous stuff in it that I haven't worn for some time. So I know I will be shopping in that corner."

"But if (people) do feel they need an affordable little treat ... there are a lot of places women feel very comfortable buying used, pre-owned or excess inventory products."

According to her most recent poll, about 51 per cent of women had bought second-hand clothes, and Liebmann expects that to increase as times get tougher and more people realize that some used clothing stores sell vintage designer dresses.

TJX Cos Inc, an off-price retailer that buys excess merchandise at below wholesale prices, has outperformed in recent months as shoppers look for bargains at its TJ Maxx and Marshalls stores.

"We often talk about the resiliency of our off-price business model, and we are seeing that resiliency benefiting us in this difficult consumer environment," said TJX CEO Carol Meyrowitz in a statement last week.

LIFE GOES ON

A spokeswoman for Goodwill Industries International, which operates more than 2,000 second-hand stores across the US, said sales have increased nearly 7 per cent over the first nine months of the year. More specifically, she said store managers in New York City -- the epicenter of the Wall Street meltdown -- were noticing new faces in their shoppers' midst lately.

Another discount avenue that is growing in popularity is sample sales, where fashion companies aim to unload excess goods at deep discounts. They have traditionally been held in cities like New York or Los Angeles, but a number of companies have emerged that now do the same thing online.

Top Button is one such company, which said it is getting a boost as fashionistas become more bargain-conscious and the credit crisis forces some fashion brands out of business.

"We haven't seen a decrease in shopping," said Top Button co-founder Michael Feldman. "If anything, it's been a lot more." The company's original site TopButton.com has information about actual sample sales while a newer site, TopSecret.com, holds virtual sample sales.

A recent event featured Andrew Marc coats at 65 per cent off retail. Feldman said they sold 1,200 pieces in five hours.

"People still have to go to parties. They may change their shopping habits ... but life doesn't stop," Feldman said.

That sentiment is being shared by executives at Ann Taylor, which usually sells many special occasion items like dresses, cashmere sweaters and party tops during November and December.

"Even in these challenging times, we still believe there will be parties, although they may take on a slightly different tone," said spokeswoman Maria Sceppaguercio.

For Laurice Rahme, founder and chief executive of boutique perfume-maker Bond No. 9, there may be fewer party invitations this year, but no drop off in shopping, especially when it comes to her favorite designer, Marc Jacobs.

"It just happened that his collection is terrific this year. I just have to have one (item from it)," Rahme said.

Heading: Recession makes women recycle last year's dress - Indian Express
Content:
Peruvians are crazy about their national dog, a bald and often toothless breed popular among Incan kings, offered on Monday to send a hypoallergenic puppy to the Obama family.

US President-elect Barack Obama has promised daughters Malia, 10, and Sasha, 7, a new pet for the White House. But Malia is allergic to most breeds, he said on Friday as speculation swirled about the dog the family would choose.

Owners of the Peruvian Hairless Dog, a breed dating back 3,000 years and depicted in pre-Hispanic ceramics, say it is perfect for kids who are sensitive to dogs.

"They do not cause any type of allergy and are very friendly and sweet," said Claudia Galvez, 38, director of the Friends of the Peruvian Hairless Dog Association.

"We want to give a male puppy to Obama's daughters, so they get to experience all the joys of having a dog but without any allergies."

According to Peruvian folklore, the dogs have above-average body temperature, which compensates for their lack of hair and helps alleviate symptoms of asthma or arthritis suffered by their owners.

Galvez delivered a letter detailing her offer to the US embassy in Lima on Monday and hopes Obama will accept it.

Galvez has a 4-month-old pedigree puppy to send to the Obama family. For now, she is calling it Ears because it has two large, perky ones.

"But if we send it to the United States, its official name will be Machu Picchu," she said, referring to the ancient Incan citadel, Peru's top tourist attraction.

Heading: Cell phone shopping makes wallets redundant in Japan - Indian Express
Content:
The misuse of 'talaq' is a problem not just in Muslim society, but in the tribal society of Mizoram an equivalent of the controversial word has caused miseries to married women for centuries.

All a Mizo man has to do is just pronounce 'ka ma che' (I divorce you) to separate from his legal wife.

Though the practice goes back to as far as memory stretches, the authorities only now woke up and promulgated an ordinance to stop the inhuman summary divorce.

The Mizo Divorce Ordinance, 2008, which is likely to be signed into law after the coming state Assembly elections, will not only check harassment of wives by men, but will also make it mandatory for them to give financial support to their divorced spouses.

The ordinance, which may bring about a fundamental change in the Mizo tribal society, has been hailed by women's organizations like the Mizo Hmeichhe Insuihkhawm Pawl (MHIP) or Women's Federation which said it would emancipate Mizo women from the strict regulations of a traditional patriarchal society.

The present Mizo Customary Law is looked upon by women in Mizoram as a patriarchal legacy which prevents a Mizo woman from having any right over the family property and also over her offspring.

Almost all marriages among Mizos are 'love marriages' and arranged marriages are almost unknown to the Mizos.

If a boy and a girl fall in love, the boy's family will send 'palai' or representatives of the boy's parents to discuss about marriage to the girl's parents and the marriage would be solemnised after both the parties agreed to the proposals.

The girl after the marriage will join the boy's family and will be entitled to take back only customary 'hmeichhe thuam' or belongings like a mattress, two pillows and her own garments if she is divorced by her husband.

She will go completely empty-handed if she commits adultery and is not allowed to take out even the clothes she is wearing.

According to the ordinance, if any one of the couple wants a divorce, he or she must approach the law court and submit a petition. Summary divorce has become illegal.

The grounds for divorce as put forward by a husband or a wife must satisfy the court in order to make any divorce legal and the husband, in accordance with his income, will now be liable to give alimony to his former wife and the amount will be fixed by the court.

'Community property', unknown to the Mizo society, will also be fixed by the court as any property acquired during the marriage can now be distributed amongst the couple.

While the present Mizo Customary Law says that children belong to the father and the father can keep the baby after attainment of three years, the child's choice will now prevail.

The court can give the child to the father or the mother keeping in view the capacity to look after the child and the character of the mother or the father.

The ordinance was issued by the state Governor and is likely to be legislated when a new Assembly is formed after the November 29 state Assembly polls.

The Indian Divorce Act, 1869 was not in force in Mizoram as the Assam Frontier Regulation, 1888 says that the act is not extended to Mizo Hills.

The former President of the MHIP, Lalnipuii, has hailed the new law as the victory for women's organisations which have fought for a better deal for womenfolk.

''We are not fighting for supremacy over men, but we want equal treatment in terms of divorce and also our places in society,'' Lalnipuii said.

She said that the Mizo Customary Law is already a slight improvement for the women, but the Mizo Divorce Ordinance, 2008 emancipated the women.

However, lawyers and judicial magistrates argue that Mizo women themselves posed problems when the courts try property cases and even before the new law is in force the courts favour better deals for women.

K L Liana, a well-known judicial magistrate, says that when a widow is going to inherit her husband's property, the mother of her husband is always the first to object and invokes the Mizo Customary Law in the courts of law.

Vanlalremruata Tonson, a journalist, expresses the fear that the Divorce Ordinace may change the social fabric of the Mizos, saying, ''A woman looking forward to remarry may go for a divorce if she has a rich husband from whom she can receive a lot of property," Tonson says.

He adds that Mizo women are more independent now and may take their independence too far even at the cost of breaking the family.

Heading: Microsoft strikes Web search deal with Sun - Indian Express
Content:
Japanese office worker Satoshi Tada pays for shopping, wins free food and gets store discounts all by waving his cell phone.

"I use it pretty much every day," the 25-year-old said. "You can charge money on it right there if needed, and you don't have to run around trying to find an ATM. You can even get points because it's linked to credit cards."

The world's top firms such as Visa Inc and Nokia are still mostly testing phone use for payments, but in Japan, more than 50 million, or about half of all cell phone users, already carry phones capable of serving as wallets.

Japan has pioneered not just the technology but also the business models that will pave the way for wallet phones to become a standard payment method in the future. Some 700 million people worldwide are expected to own such phones by 2013.

"You can't deny that having such applications on a phone is convenient, and that will likely be the way that mobile phones are going worldwide," said JP Morgan Securities analyst Hironobu Sawake in Tokyo.

"People always carry cell phones on them, and they would find it useful to have a financial function there."

Success in Japan and in trials abroad have shown that the technology is ready for cell phones to replace credit cards, cash as well as serve as transportation and movie tickets and electronic keys for homes and offices.

But there are other hurdles; from breaking the psychological barrier for consumers sceptical about using phones as credit cards, to working out new business models as the lines blur between banks, financial institutions and cell phone companies.

Japan is leading the way in this regard.

KDDI, for example, is a Japanese telecom operator that has recently set up a bank along with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group. NTT DoCoMo, Japan's biggest wireless carrier, offers credit cards and lending services as part of a tie up with Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Japan's third-largest bank.

Outside Japan, telecom industry and financial players are still in the midst of working out how the wallet phone payment business would operate, who would get a cut and when.

"Traditional financial industry met telcos by going mobile. Now telecom operators want to play a part in that chain. These talks are well under way," said Gerhard Romen, Director for Strategic Alliances & Partnering at Nokia.

The world's biggest payment card company, Mastercard, said last month it was in talks over commercial launches of phone wallets with several banks, and during the next two years it expects to see substantial activity from retail-focused banks.

"Now banks say: I have no doubt in the technology. We need to solve the business model between mobile and payments industries. It's not a trivial task," said James Anderson, a Vice President at MasterCard's mobile business.

"There is a very strong consumer pull for this service," Anderson added.

COUPONS

Tada, the Tokyo office worker, rarely pulls out his leather wallet these days as his cell phone does the job instead.

"For shopping, I use it everywhere I can ... and I also use coupons such as Gourmet Navigator Touch wherever possible," Tada said, citing services at some restaurants that offer coupons and free gifts when customers wave their phones at reader terminals.

NTT DoCoMo began the so-called "wallet phone" service in 2004 and rivals KDDI Corp and Softbank Corp have followed suit. Overseas, Nokia also has such phones on the market.

Nevertheless, despite Japan's relative success with payment phones, still only one-third of wallet phone holders use their cells for purchases.

Consumers in their 20s and 30s are the main users of wallet phone services. Research shows that once they start using, they tend to use frequently and repeatedly, making it a useful tool for companies to track their customers and shopping habits.

"For young people the phone is more important than the card when they leave home," said Nokia's Romen.

McDonald's Japan and 7-Eleven convenience stores have been testing mobile discount coupons, and FeliCa Networks, a joint venture of Sony and DoCoMo, have launched a mobile platform for retailers to offer such services.

"With many cell phones around and most of them being wallet phones, we cannot ignore them as marketing tools," McDonald's Japan spokesman Kazuyuki Hagiwara said. McDonald's plans to widen its mobile discount coupon offering nationwide next year.

EXTRA CHIP

The world's top cell phone maker Nokia has started selling wallet phones, though growth is hampered by costs stemming from an extra chip needed in phones for data security. As a result, Nokia's near field communications (NFC) version of devices costs far more than regular phones.

Near field communications (NFC) enables contactless data transmission at high speed and enables many functions at once such as various electronic money services, keys and coupons.

In contrast to Nokia, Japanese makers install Sony Corp's FeliCa chips in new mobile phones by default, and prices are competitive with other cell phones.

Globally, research firm Juniper Research says there will be 700 million NFC-capable phones by 2013, from some 50 million in Japan now, offering major growth for the phone payment industry and the companies that provide the hardware and software.

Credit card network Visa is developing an application to allow in-store contactless payments by cell phone for Google Inc's Android operating system, and UK mobile operator O2 is also testing wallet phones.

Security concerns are high among potential users but DoCoMo says a remote-lock system will protect it from being used by other people in case of emergencies.

One of the remaining hurdles to attract more wallet phone users is to expand the system network.

"It would be so useful if we can use it everywhere. For now we don't know where we can use it and we have to carry both a phone and a wallet," UBS Securities analyst Makio Inui said. "If we can spend a day with just with a phone, that would be big."

Heading: End of exile as Australia pick Symonds for Twenty20 game - Indian Express
Content:
Microsoft Corp said on Monday that it reached a Web search deal with Sun Microsystems Inc, the latest partnership struck by Microsoft aimed at chipping away at the dominance of Google Inc.

As part of this agreement, users of Microsoft's Internet Explorer browser who download Sun's Java technology platform will be given the option to also download the MSN Toolbar from where users can directly access the company's search engine.

Earlier this year, Microsoft also reached an agreement with Hewlett-Packard Co, the world's largest personal computer maker, to place a toolbar on new PCs in the United States and Canada starting in January.

"This deal will expose Live Search to millions more Internet users and drive increased volume for our search advertisers," said Yusuf Mehdi, senior vice president of the Online Audience Business at Microsoft, in a statement.

Striking distribution deals are one part of Microsoft's strategy to close the gap on market leader Google. Microsoft said competition for these types of deals is intense and that the company had to outbid several rivals for the Sun deal.

Sun said the Java platform sits on more than 800 million personal computers around the world, or on 91 per cent of Internet-connected PCs worldwide. The Java Runtime Environment is downloaded tens of millions times every month, Sun said.

Google's US Web search market share reached 63 per cent in August versus a 19.6 per cent for Yahoo Inc and 8.3 per cent for Microsoft, according to comScore.

Heading: After Obama, coach Robinson has to help his team - Indian Express
Content:
Embattled all-round Andrew Symonds on Monday made a comeback to the Australian team for Friday's Emirates All Star Twenty20 match in Brisbane.

Cricket Australia's chief executive officer James Sutherland said in a statement that Symonds, dumped from the side after the 'gone-fishing' episode, has successfully completed the prescribed "welfare process" and his return was a result of much hard work on his behalf.

'Strong desire'

"I have been in regular contact with Andrew over the last month or so. He has made significant progress during his enforced lay off and we are happy that he is now available to be selected for Australia again," Sutherland said.

"I know Andrew has had a very strong desire to fight his way back into the Australian team and I am confident that desire will be reflected in his actions over the coming months," he added.

National selection panel chairman Andrew Hilditch said he was too happy to see Symonds back. "Cricket Australia advised the NSP late last week that Andrew Symonds had completed the welfare process he has been undertaking over recent times and it was with great pleasure that we were able to select him for this game," he said.

Heading: Somdev becomes India No 1 - Indian Express
Content:
With a hint of 5 o'clock shadow and small bags under his eyes, Oregon State coach Craig Robinson took the basketball court on Wednesday to start a campaign that is nearly as daunting as the one he just helped to complete. For the past 20 months, Robinson assisted his brother-in-law Barack Obama's bid for the presidency. Robinson stumped in Iowa, gave speeches in Washington State and did interviews about his childhood on Chicago's South Side with his younger sister, Michelle, who is married to Obama.

All that work culminated in one magical Tuesday for Robinson and his family as they ate dinner at the Obamas' house on election night and later exchanged congratulatory hugs onstage at Grant Park in Chicago. "I've been so busy, I haven't been able to process it yet," Robinson said less than 24 hours later as he sat on the bleachers at Gill Coliseum after practice. "It's wild. I don't know what to say."

Now that the Obamas are preparing to enter the White House and Robinson can devote all his energy to his first season at Oregon State, Robinson and the president-elect can debate about whose task is tougher.

Robinson simply inherited an Oregon State program that is coming off an 0-18 season in the Pacific-10, carrying a 21-game losing streak and looking for its first NCAA tournament appearance since 1990. He installed the Princeton-style offense that he used to lead Brown to a team-record 19 victories last season. He also brought many of the themes prevalent in the Obama campaign: change, hope and reform.

Robinson's players at Brown said he went out of his way to separate politics and basketball. He would walk a block from his office on Hope Street and duck into the Blue State Coffee shop to talk politics. (Jesse Agel, Brown's new coach, said he would send Robinson a pound of Blue State Coffee, with its "drink liberally" slogan, to congratulate him.)

Although Robinson was happy to discuss politics with anyone who asked, he would never start the conversation. But as Robinson went from coaching in the Ivy League to coaching in the Pac-10 and his brother-in-law went from representing Illinois in the Senate to being elected the nation's 44th president, those discussions are becoming harder to avoid. In a fitting twist, Oregon State's first regular-season game under Robinson is Friday at Howard University in Washington, the future home of the Obamas. Robinson joked that he wished he had been clever enough to create that matchup.

"There's going to be so much pressure on them," Robinson said of his players and the expected circuslike atmosphere surrounding the game. "But you know what? If you're going to win games on the road in the Pac-10, then you have to win these kinds of games. We might as well just do it." Now that the pressure of the election is off, Robinson's job is to bring change to Oregon State. His campaign kicks off Friday.

Heading: Force India link up with McLaren - Indian Express
Content:
It's hard to keep Somdev Devvarman out of the news. For someone who made his professional debut just a few months ago, the 23-year-old has already ensured many of his higher-ranked conquests won't be forgetting his name in a hurry. From this week, he adds another distinction to the many he owns — that of being India's top-ranked tennis player. Of course, the youngster would rather set his sights on loftier targets.

"I wasn't really thinking hard about becoming India No 1. I think I've been rather fortunate in terms of a good coach, trainer and management company — they all ensure I can keep my focus on playing good tennis, and I hope to improve some more," said Somdev, who is now ranked 201 on the ATP circuit, ahead of No 214 Prakash Amritraj.

Somdev will play his first tournament in India for over a year this December, flying down to Pune for the Asia Cup, which is the first tournament of the newly formed Asian Tour of tennis calendar.

"I'm looking forward to playing in India, it's sure to be a great experience," said Somdev, while adding another wish to play in next year's Chennai Open. "The AITA has been really supportive so far, and it'll be great if I can get a wild card for Chennai," he added.

Prakash Amritraj will be part of the Indian team as well, while the remaining players for the December 27-30 event will be decided soon.

"Somdev and Prakash have already expressed their availability for the tournament," said AITA secretary general Anil Khanna, who also added his praise for the fast-improving player.

"It's a great achievement. In just 12 tournaments, he has risen up the rankings so fast. I hope he's in the top 100 by May next year," said Khanna.

Heading: After clinching No 2 ranking, Garcia targets Major - Indian Express
Content:
Force India will use Mercedes engines next season in a long-term deal with the German carmaker and McLaren, the Formula One team announced on Monday.

The partnership marks a significant development for McLaren's engine partners and part-owners, who have since 1995 supplied only the Woking team that took Lewis Hamilton to this year's drivers' title. Sauber were the last 'customer' team to use Mercedes-badged engines, in 1994.

Force India, who last week terminated their engine contract with Fiat-owned Ferrari, said in a statement that McLaren Applied Technologies would supply them with gearbox and hydraulic systems. The team also plan to use a KERS (Kinetic Energy Recovery System) developed by Mercedes and McLaren and will have access to McLaren's network of suppliers as well as operational support. "McLaren and Mercedes-Benz are two of the most famous names in motorsport history," said Force India co-owner and principal Vijay Mallya.

Technical boost

"These new resources and developments will provide an enormous boost to our technical armoury and, as a result, we have high hopes of making good progress in 2009 and beyond."

Force India failed to score a point this year and Mallya carried out a major management restructuring last week, with team principal Colin Kolles and technical head Mike Gascoyne both leaving. "We said at the outset that we meant business and were not interested in merely making up the numbers," said Mallya. "The announcement of our new technical partnership clearly underlines that we meant what we said."

The billionaire said Force India would be in good shape by the time India hosted a grand prix for the first time. "(Formula One supremo) Bernie Ecclestone has declared plans to stage an Indian Grand Prix in 2011, in Delhi, by which time Force India Formula One team will be exactly that: a Formula One force in, and for, India."

Heading: ‘There is a time for everyone to leave... this is mine’ - Indian Express
Content:
Till very recently, visiting off-spinners were never given a second glance on an Indian tour. That changed last Friday when a certain Australian, nicknamed 'Crazy' surprised everyone by grabbing eight wickets on his Test debut in Nagpur. Incidentally, it also turned out to be the first day on tour for another offie looking to make an impact in a land where spinners rule.

Englishman Graeme Swann arrived in India with a much-hyped reputation and with not many giving him a chance against the might of the Indian batting line-up. But the Nottinghamshire off-spinner definitely seems inspired after watching Australian Jason Krejza's amazing performance on television on the first day of his team's Indian sojourn. The pop-singing, free-wheeling 29-year-old Swann — referred to as 'Chin' among his team mates — comes across as the most intriguing and fascinating character in the touring English contingent.

Swann believes that English cricket has never been too patient with off-spinners, and they have been given a very thin rope to hang on to on most occasions.

"England is not the best place to bowl off-spin as the conditions there never allow a team to play two spinners in the team," says Swann. But he diffuses any mention of him being under pressure to perform each time he takes the field. "Every time I take the field, I know it could easily be my last game, so there is no pressure on me," he says.

Swann admits that the tag of being a bowling all-rounder sits well with him, and also hopes to display his batting prowess on the tour. "I open the batting in limited overs cricket back home and go for my strokes," says Swann, who averages a decent 27 with the bat with four centuries in first-class cricket.

Swann's outgoing nature has proved to be a bane in his cricketing career, as it has often been misunderstood for arrogance and bad attitude. But the man who is the lead singer in his band insists he has always played cricket with a smile on his face.

Disappointment is nothing new for the boisterous Swann, and he hopes that he'll finally have the last laugh, after spending seven years in the wilderness before making a dramatic comeback against Sri Lanka last year. "My shift to Nottinghamshire from Northamptonshire gave me a big lift," says Swann, who has played 12 ODIs for England.

Whether Swann's band 'Dr Comfort and the Lurid Revelations' ever hits the UK Top 10 charts or not, the exuberant off-spinner will definitely be looking to find his rhythm as he prepares to contend with the Indian batting line-up.

Heading: Bumpy ride for Delhi on flat Hyderabad track - Indian Express
Content:
'Lay off Ponting...for now', 'How cricket's top dogs lost their bark', 'Australia goes into soul searching mode' were some of the headlines with which the Australian media expressed frustration at their national team's defeat in the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

The media was not only severe with words while describing Australia's current bashing at the hands of India but also looked susceptible at their team's future. "Australia will this week begin preparations for the new home season with a captain under fire, a sick vice-captain and spearhead, out of form players and opponents believing its days as cricket's No. 1 nation are all but over," said a report in the Daily Telegraph.

"Welcome to the combustible new world of Australian cricket, an era set to be marked by uncertainty, apprehension and an increasing number of draws and defeats," it added.

The Australian described India as the "bogey" team for Ricky Ponting and Co. "Ponting remains Australia's second-most successful skipper behind Steve Waugh, but clearly India are his bogey team, accounting for four of his six Test losses in his 48 at the helm," the paper wrote.

"...Questions will also be asked about a tour where several senior players failed to provide the results expected of them," it added.

The Sydney Morning Herald hinted that Ponting's performance would be scrutinised further. "It remains to be seen if Ricky Ponting returns from India with vultures circling, but he has been there before. It was not a good look and seemed to indicate that here was a man not coping well with the pressure."

The paper praised India for the win but also lashed out at their tactics under title 'A victory deserved, but its manner left a lot to be desired'.

"India were superior in almost every position, and their best players were also the youngest. India fielded a varied attack including an impressive speedster, a canny left-armer, an inviting leggie and a combative finger spinner.

"The batting was led by two dashers and the middle order retained most of its glory. The hosts were also mentally stronger. Australia were outplayed.

"If the victory was deserved, though, the manner of its final attainment left much to be desired. Certainly the cynical proceedings seen over the past few days showed Test cricket in the worst possible light," it wrote.

Another report in The Australian, however, sympathised with Ponting. "India is a difficult cricket tour. The Australians were beaten there in 2001 and that was with Warne, Gilchrist, McGrath, Langer and the like. That tour was lost because Steve Waugh enforced a follow on allowing the Indians back into the Calcutta Test. "Australia won its first series in decades there in 2004 with the side at its strongest, but only just. Everybody makes mistakes in the heat. The important thing is to learn from them ... perhaps it is best if everybody waits to hear what was going through Ponting's mind yesterday before getting too carried away."

Heading: Federer runs into starting trouble - Indian Express
Content:
The first day of the Ranji Trophy Super League encounter between Mumbai and Gujarat in Surat turned out to be a tale of two captains. While one orchestrated a brillant move in front of the stumps and put his team into a commanding position, the other was forced to rue his decision to ask the opposition to bat first earlier in the day.

Wasim Jaffer stroked an unbeaten 172 and batted right through the day, as Mumbai ended at 327/2 at stumps. He was supported well by 20-year-old Ajinkya Rahane, who scored a breathtaking 104 and shared a crucial 218-run partnership for the second wicket with his captain.

Gujarat captain Parthiv Patel was let down by his fast bowlers as they failed to impress on a damp wicket. The hosts had struck early though, as left-arm seamer Ashraf Makda trapped Sahil Kukreja in front, and Mumbai were 5-1.

At ease

But that brought Rahane to the crease, who looked completely at ease against Makda and Siddharth Trivedi. His aggression seemed to rub off on Jaffer too, as he hit two boundaries in one over of Trivedi. Rahane then hit a number of exquisite boundaries off the fast bowlers, outscoring his partner.

When Patel brought on his big weapon, Murali-clone Mohnish Parmar, Rahane made his intentions to dominate the off-spinner very clear, stepping out to him on his first ball. Meanwhile, Jaffer quietly reached his 50, and Mumbai went to lunch at 130-1.

The pair continued to dictate terms in the second session. The duo crossed the 200-run partnership mark in the next over. But, against the run of play, Rahane seemed to choose the wrong option in attempting to hit Timil Patel over the leg-side again, as he missed the ball and was stumped with the score on 223.

Jaffer then forged an unbeaten 104-run stand with another veteran, Amol Muzumdar, who finished the day on 43.

Brief scores: Mumbai 327/2 in 90 overs (W Jaffer 172 batting, A Rahane 104, A Muzumdar 43 batting; Makda 1/40, Patel 1/62).

Heading: Lt Col Purohit put on Army disciplinary watchlist - Indian Express
Content:
Roger Federer got his quest for a fifth Masters Cup title off to the worst possible start with a 4-6, 6-4, 6-3 defeat at the hands of Frenchman Gilles Simon on Monday.

The Swiss top seed, who withdrew from the Paris Masters 11 days ago with a back injury, made 50 unforced errors to fall to a second defeat in two encounters with the 23-year-old world number nine. "The better you play, the better he plays, he's quite an unusual player and he makes you work hard and runs very well," said the world number two, who also lost to Simon at the Toronto Masters in July.

"Definitely today I missed shots I normally don't miss. I think that's just lack of practice. It's the only tournament where I really have a chance after losing the first match so I'm happy it happened here."

Murray gets measure of Roddick

Third seed Andy Murray blew hot and cold on his Masters Cup debut, prevailing 6-4, 1-6, 6-1 over Andy Roddick in the other match in the Red Group, from which two players will qualify for Saturday's semi-finals.

The 21-year-old Briton rattled off three aces in his first service game on his way to wrapping up the first set, but effectively forfeited the second to his American rival with a series of unforced errors. The deciding set was equally one-sided and Murray took just 25 minutes to despatch the fifth seed, clinching victory with a leaping backhand volley.

"I'm tired," Murray said. "I felt like I played well. You know the legs don't quite have the snap in them that they did a few months ago.

I hit the ball well for most of the match, I just didn't serve well in the second set."

Good fortune

Federer lost his only previous Masters Cup group match to Chile's Fernando Gonzalez in his opening encounter last year but still managed to claim the title for the second season in a row.

The 27-year-old said he had been happy with the way his back felt although he admitted he had been cautious, particularly on his serve, as he did not know how it it would hold up.

"At least now I have three sets under my belt and hopefully I'll play better in the next match," he said.

Simon got his ticket for the season finale when world number one Rafael Nadal withdrew injured and said he had gone out with the aim of taking full advantage of his good fortune. "It was once again one of the best victories of my career," he said. "I'm really happy to be here. I just wanted to give everything on the court."

Federer's service looked creaky in the opening set but he broke for 3-2 and looked to be cruising to a comfortable victory when he grabbed an early break in the second.

By now, though, Simon was bouncing around the court with zest. He broke back immediately before levelling the match up with a typically athletic run to the net to make a backhand volley.

Federer had already come back from 0-40 down to save his serve once in the third set when Simon got the better of him to go 5-3 up and he sealed the upset with an ace on his next service game.

"I defeated him once in Toronto, so it was easier to finish the match," said Simon. "I had no complex when I served in the last game." (Reuters)

Paes-Dlouhy lose

Leander Paes and his partner Lukas Dlouhy lost their opening Gold Group match at the Shanghai Masters in straight sets to Sweden's Jonas Bjorkman and Kevin Ullyett of Zimbabwe. The Indo-Czech duo lost this match 6-3, 7-5.

In the other doubles match on Monday, Daniel Nestor and Nenad Zimonjic prevailed over Mariusz Frystenberg and Marcin Matkowski in a super tie-break, 7-6, 5-7, 10-4.

Heading: 37-yr-old, held with fake military card, under scanner - Indian Express
Content:
The Army has put Lt Col S P Purohit, the military intelligence officer arrested by the Mumbai police in connection with the Malegaon blast, under a Discipline Vigilance (DV) ban pending the completion of investigations by the Mumbai police and the Intelligence Bureau (IB).

The provision means that the officer will not be entitled to any promotions or transfers untill he is cleared of the charges by a court of law. However, the officer would continue to withdraw his regular emoluments and retain the official accommodations provided at Pachmarhi. Under the disciplinary ban, a normal proceeding on any officer coming under investigation for a serious offence, Purohit's career status will be held in freeze and results of any promotion board will also be kept secret.

The Army has also begun an internal scrutiny into the service record and postings of Lt Col Purhoit to determine if his record correlates with other unsolved incidents that may have taken place in the past and whether he misused his military connections to help the main accused in the case. "Things being checked out include whether any arms, ammunition or explosives went missing or were stolen at a unit where he was posted in the past," an officer said.

The Army is also questioning fellow officers posted with Purhoit during his tenure as a Liaison Unit (LU) officer at Nashik. Though the Army is saying that there are no other serving officers under the scanner yet, a probe has been initiated to draw a profile and map to put how the Lt Col got involved with Maj (retd) Ramesh Upadhyay and other Abhinav Bharat members accused in the blast.

Purhoit's service record is being scrutinised and his superior officers under whom he has served earlier are being informally questioned to ascertain whether he got into trouble while posted to other units before his stint at Nashik. Military intelligence officers and Liaison Unit officers who were posted in Maharashtra and were working with him on certain 'projects' are also being quizzed.

While the army does not keep a tab on officers when they proceed on leave, Purohit's leave records are also being looked into to determine whether they fit into any set pattern. Details of the leave he took in the past few years have also been shared with the Mumbai police.

Heading: Blasts suspect Sadiq also hit American Center: police - Indian Express
Content:
As the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) continues to question suspects in connection with the Malegaon blast, investigators have now turned their attention to what initially seemed like an innocuous arrest of a 37-year-old man from Uttar Pradesh in an Arms Act case by the police in Mumbai's Matunga suburb a week ago.

Matunga police suspects that Sudhakar Chaturvedi may have links with Abhinav Bharat, the Pune-based right-wing organisation to which some of those arrested in the blast case belong to, and has sought permission from a local court to conduct a narco-analysis test on him.

Chaturvedi has come under the scanner of the ATS due to his alleged admission that he had gained access to the army's Nashik Artillery Centre on several occasions using a fake military identification card.

Acting on a tip-off, Matunga Police had laid a trap outside Mumbai's Dadar (East) railway station and arrested Chaturvedi on November 4. He was allegedly found with a factory-made Indian revolver and was booked under the Arms Act. Police also recovered a fake Indian Army ID card from him at the time of the arrest.

"The ID card shows him to be a sepoy in the Army. There is even a photo of Chaturvedi in military uniform on the card. Importantly, the card gave him access to restricted areas. One such area is the artillery at Nashik which is under Army control and is restricted to civilians. Chaturvedi told us that he used this card to enter the centre on several occasions. He has not told us what the purpose of his trip to the city was, or why he was carrying a firearm," Matunga's Senior Police Inspector Sunil Deshmukh said.

"We are also probing whether Chaturvedi is linked to Abhinav Bharat. Officers from the ATS have come and questioned Chaturvedi. He has been sent to judicial custody today, and we moved court seeking permission to conduct a narco-analysis test on him to investigate these angles," Deshmukh added.

According to the police, Chaturvedi is unemployed and belongs to Mirzapur in UP. He has been living in Maharashtra for the last 12 years — in Nashik for the last four years and in Pune before that.

Heading: Assam blasts may be linked to Bodo group - Indian Express
Content:
Police in Kolkata and Mumbai on Monday announced that Mohammed Sadiq alias Sadaqat, one of the terror suspects held for the recent string of blasts across the country, had also carried out the January 2002 attack on the American Center in Kolkata which left six policemen dead.

Rajiv Kumar, Special Additional Commissioner of the Special Task Force of Kolkata Police, said Sadiq, who hails from Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh, was arrested from the Cheetah Camp near Trombay on September 24 by Mumbai Police. Kolkata policemen went to Mumbai to question him. Mumbai policemen and the STF also interrogated Aftab Ansari, the prime accused in the American Center attack, and his accomplices in the Alipur Central Jail recently.

According to police, it was Sadiq who gunned down the policemen outside the American Center on January 22, 2002. The attack was planned by Amir Reza Khan and Aftab Ansari who was then based in Dubai. Ansari was later held and deported to India.

The police claimed that during his questioning, Sadiq confessed to firing at the policemen from an AK-47 rifle after reaching there on a two-wheeler with one of his accomplices. A day before the shooting, he had stayed at a house in Tiljala Lane and had introduced himself as Sadaqat.

Mumbai Joint Commissioner of Police Rakesh Maria said: "We have established that Sadiq was one of the two men who had opened fire on the American Centre in Kolkata in 2002. This has been verified through information gathered by us and by positive identification of the accused. Sadiq is currently in judicial custody and he will eventually be taken to Kolkata."

Police said he fled to Hazaribagh, boarding a train from Howrah within an hour of the attack. Police tracked him down to Hazaribagh but he managed to escape. However, one of his accomplices, Zaheed, was killed in an encounter with the police. Sadiq surfaced in Azamgarh and later headed for Mumbai.

Police claimed that Sadiq had visited several countries, including Pakistan where he was trained in explosives. He allegedly joined the Indian Mujahideen and rose up the ranks to become a key member. Police claimed he had a role in the 7/11 blasts on Mumbai local trains and was also involved in blasts in Delhi and Ahmedabad.

Heading: Waning influence prompted Alva outburst - Indian Express
Content:
Twelve days after the serial blasts in Guwahati and three other towns in Assam, security forces seem to be convinced of the role of the National Democratic Front of Bodoland (NDFB) — currently in ceasefire with the Government.

Officials in the police and Army, apart from Chief Minister Tarun Gogoi and the Centre are agreed that the conspiracy to carry out the blasts was hatched and remote-controlled from Bangladesh with local groups like the NDFB and ULFA helping.

The Strategy Group of the Unified Command Structure, which met here on Monday, endorsed action against NDFB cadres violating ceasefire ground rules, following which security personnel positioned themselves close to four designated camps where the NDFB cadres are holed up. Sources revealed that the Strategy Group took strong note of the ceasefire ground rules violation.

"Iinstructions were issued tonight to the respective SPs in the districts to ensure that there was no further violation of these rules," sources told The Indian Express on late Monday night.

The Strategy Group meeting of the Unified Command was attended by Chief Secretary P C Sharma, and senior police and Army officers.

The SIT, however, is yet to find 'convincing' evidence that it was actually the NDFB that carried out the explosions. Sources indicated that several of the suspects picked up by the SIT had turned out to be Bodo youths who could be members or supporters of the NDFB.

Police had on Sunday arrested one Punkha Brahma from Garchuk, a locality on the outskirts of the state capital, with sources saying that all three Maruti cars that were used in the three simultaneous blasts in Guwahati were under his custody on October 29.

The NDFB, however, has denied reports that it had any involvement in the serial blasts. In a statement issued on Monday, it said there was a conspiracy to scuttle the peace process initiated with New Delhi three years ago.

Heading: BJP C’garh sops: Re 1 kg rice, free power to farmers - Indian Express
Content:
The recent "emotional outburst" of 10, Janpath loyalist Margaret Alva about sale of party tickets and double standards in selection of candidates pointed to an intense rivalry and power games at the top echelons of the Congress.

Although Alva was ostensibly targeting AICC general secretary Digvijay Singh — who headed the screening committee that denied ticket to her son Nivedit in Karnataka Assembly elections on the plea that it would encourage nepotism and who also headed the screening committee which gave tickets to a host of relatives of other leaders in Rajasthan — party insiders say her diatribe was not borne out of her frustration as a mother, as Congress spin doctors would have us believe.

For a leader who was one of the four joint secretaries of the AICC way back in 1975, who was in Parliament for 29 years and who got ministerial portfolios in both the Rajiv Gandhi and P V Narasimha Rao regimes, an outburst cannot but be "calculated", pointed out a senior Congress leader. Sources said she had the backing of a section of well-ensconced leaders who are jittery about the prospects of a 'regime change' in the party sooner or later. It is not just a coincidence that many of those involved in ticket distribution exercise also happen to be cosy with heir apparent Rahul Gandhi.

Understandably, pointed out her party colleagues, the AICC general secretary in charge of six states who has been close to the Nehru-Gandhi family since the days of Indira Gandhi, waning influence and authority in recent times have been a matter of anxiety. The denial of ticket to her son and the more recent appointment of her bete-noire R V Deshpande as Karnataka PCC chief were, of course, irksome.

But Alva has seen many ups and downs in her over four decades in politics. It was no secret that she also harboured presidential ambition. A dominating and no-nonsense individual, she has had not been on best of terms with many regional kshatraps who find her too 'intrusive'.

Sources said how she was left in despair when her colleagues succeeded in "saving" Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh despite cases piled up against him by her and a host of other leaders who shared her assessment of his performance. But the high command went over her head to deal directly with the CM and his rival Narayan Rane leaving Alva, state in-charge, to watch the drama from the sidelines, sources said.

Also in charge of Punjab, Alva is charmed by a zealous Rajinder Kaur Bhattal who has been unrelenting in her dogged pursuit to annihilate Capt. Amarinder Singh politically. Thanks to his indispensability for the party in Punjab, the high command had to appoint the the former CM as chairman of the campaign committee in the state.

Another state under her charge, Haryana also saw Alva making a forceful attempt to intervene in administrative matters. But Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda was able to stand his ground.

A senior Congress leader, however, said Alva's frequent brush-offs with regional kshatraps was wrongly attributed to her impetuosity. "She is used to keeping regional chieftains on a leash. She is not alone in this mission," he said.

The Congress sources maintained that Alva chose the timing of her outburst. While Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi were in Bhutan, she chose to spill the beans. Clubbing her grievance with that of C K Jaffar Sharief, whose grandson was also denied ticket, Alva ensured that the party leadership would be in a bind in an election year.

Despite repeated attempts to contact her, Alva was not available for comments.

Heading: Case against MP minister for threatening Returning Officer - Indian Express
Content:
The ruling BJP on Monday unveiled its plans for providing freebies and subsidies such as free salt, rice at Re 1 per kg to poor and free electricity and interest-free loans to farmers in the event the party retained power in the Assembly polls.

"At present, we are giving 35 kg of rice per month at Rs 3 per kg. If voted to power, the poorest will get it for Re 1 per kg while the poor belonging to all sections will be provided rice at Rs 2 per kg," Chief Minister Raman Singh said while releasing the party's manifesto for the polls.

The party's promise came after the Congress in its election manifesto promised to supply rice to BPL and APL families at Rs 2 per kg. Besides, the Congress also promised to provide an additional bonus of Rs 251 per quintal on paddy procured on support price from the farmers.

The ruling party went a step ahead and promised Rs 270 as bonus to farmers on procurement of paddy, besides electricity free of cost to the farmers using irrigation pumps up to five hp. It said dedicated power lines will also be laid to ensure uninterrupted power supply to farmers.

Announcing that the loan limit to farmers will be increased from Rs 3 to 5 lakh, Singh said the party will provide 50 per cent grant on purchase of agricultural implements while marginal farmers will be completely exempted from registration fees.

Unveiling its promises for youth and women, the manifesto said interest-free loans will be given to youth for higher education and students in government-run technical institutions will be exempted from tuition fees.

Heading: CJI wants future judges to clarify if kin practising in court - Indian Express
Content:
Minister of State for Tourism Tukojirao Pawar, who openly threatened Sanjana Jain, a returning officer (RO) in Dewas, and allegedly misbehaved with her, is in trouble.

A case under Section 353 and 504 of the IPC was registered against Pawar on Monday in the Kotwali police station of Dewas, a town under the erstwhile rule of his family. Simultaneously, the Election Commission has taken cognizance of complaints against him and ordered that an FIR be registered against Pawar. The EC direction to the Chief Electoral Officer to file the FIR came hours after Jain filed a police complaint against the BJP leader saying that she had been "obstructed from doing official work."

Pawar had gone to Jain's office on Saturday seeking cancellation of the nomination of Sajjan Singh Varma, a Congress candidate from Sonkutch constituency in the district. BJP candidate Fulchand Varma had accompanied the minister, who is contesting from Dewas.

The minister was arguing that 'A' and 'B' forms were missing when Varma filed his nomination on Friday. Though the deadline was over at 3 pm that day, the RO accepted both the forms on Saturday. "The form should have been rejected. I was only insisting on getting receipts of my objections. If I am being hauled up for speaking the truth so be it," he told The Indian Express, insisting that his objections were valid. He alleged that the RO had accepted a huge bribe from the Congress candidate to accept the papers, a day after the deadline.

Heading: LDA scam: UP moves court against Amar - Indian Express
Content:
Under fire from the Government, jurists as well as parliamentarians on various counts, especially the manner in which judges are chosen, the judiciary has quietly ushered in a significant change in the way it appoints lawyers to the Bench.

According to sources in the Supreme Court, henceforth, lawyers whose names are considered for elevation to the Bench — either in the state high courts or the Supreme Court — will have to state in writing if any of their kin are practising in the same court, their names and details of their relationship.

The lawyers will also have to indicate in writing if it is alright with them if they are transferred to high courts other than where they are practising.

These additions would also be part of the performa that lawyers whose names are under consideration by the collegium have to fill before their names are recommended for elevation.

Sources in the Supreme Court say the changes have been circulated to all high courts for implementation.

It is learnt that the additions were cleared by the Supreme Court on the suggestion of Chief Justice of India (CJI) K G Balakrishnan. The CJI, it is learnt, has told senior colleagues that steps like these would go a long way in ensuring that undeserving candidates don't make it to the Bench.

There has been a persistent demand for transfer of high court judges whose relatives practise in the same court in order to check corruption. While there has so far not been any recorded instance of a high court judge found favouring either his own kin or those of other judges in judicial work, sources point to the fact that when it comes to choosing lawyers for elevation to the Bench, the collegiums in many high courts have shown a marked inclination for kin of sitting and retired judges.

A few years ago, the then Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court B K Roy had debarred lawyers related to sitting judges from appearing before all those judges whose kin were practising in the same court. The order had drawn applause from legal experts and jurists.

Thereafter, in 2006, in its report, the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice, headed by Congress Rajya Sabha MP E M Sudarsana Natchiappan, while recommending a change in the system of selection of judges, had talked of a vicious circle.

The committee felt that under the present system of a collegium recommending names of lawyers for elevation to the Bench, the kith and kin of sitting and retired judges were cornering a major chunk of appointments.

Incidentally, in 2003, acting on a missive from the Union Ministry of Law and Justice, the Bar Council of India (BCI) had conducted a survey to find the total number of judges in high courts whose kin were practising in the same court. It had come out with a list of 131.

The BCI had also demanded transfer of all such judges to other high courts. However, nothing had happened thereafter.

One of the major demands from various quarters has been for judiciary to switch back to the earlier system whereby at least one-third of the total judges in every high court were outsiders — those who had not been appointed in the same court.

This system, which was first introduced when Indira Gandhi was the Prime Minister, was later junked after a resolution to this effect was passed at a Conference of Chief Justices.

Heading: Kusum Rai, Adib file RS nominations - Indian Express
Content:
The Mayawati Government has moved the Supreme Court seeking permission to take action against Samajwadi Party general secretary Amar Singh. The basis of the plea is an inquiry report by state's Principal Secretary, Urban Development, on the alleged illegal allotment of plots in Gomti Nagar, Lucknow. The report holds Singh guilty of misusing his power during the Mulayam Singh Yadav regime.

The state Government had filed an application on November 8 seeking permission to take action against Singh. "It is prayed that the court permit the Government to proceed in accordance with law and to take necessary action on the basis of the report," the state Government had said in its application.

The Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) had allotted Singh a plot in 1994 that was meant for the economically weaker section (EWS), according to the report.

The state Government's move comes in the wake of the Allahabad High Court restraining it from initiating action against Singh. However, the Lucknow Bench of the High Court, on June 13, gave liberty to the state Government to approach the apex court for proceeding against Singh.

A petition filed by advocate Vishwanath Chaturvedi seeking a high-level probe into the allotments worth Rs 2.80 crore made in Vipul Khand, Gomti Nagar, has been pending in the apex court, which on September 12, 2005 by an interim order had restrained transfer of the plots until further orders.

The UP Government's application said that on November 2, 2007, the apex court had issued notices to Yadav and Singh, among others, to initiate criminal prosecutions against them as they were beneficiaries of the alleged illegal allotment of plots.

The report said two plots were illegally allotted to the politician, out of which one was meant for EWS.

"It is clear on examination of the record that in this case Amar Singh was allotted (one) plot directly from EWS category which is completely against the rules," the report said.

In another case, two plots were illegally allotted to one Aaliya Khatoon by the LDA, out of which one plot was purchased by Singh.

Heading: Don’t arrest Todi till Nov 17, CBI told - Indian Express
Content:
With the filing of nomination papers by the BJP and the joint candidate of the Congress and the Samajwadi Party, the nomination process for the biennial elections to the Rajya Sabha concluded here on Monday. Ten sitting Rajya Sabha members from Uttar Pradesh are retiring on November 25.

The Rajya Sabha biennial polls are scheduled for November 21 in the state. The scrutiny of the papers will be held on Tuesday and the last date of withdrawal is November 14. All the 10 candidates are likely to be elected unopposed.

While Mohammed Adib, the Cong-SP candidate, filed his nomination flanked by senior leaders of both the parties, Kusum Rai, a member of the Upper House of the state legislature, filed nomination as the BJP candidate.

After filing her papers Rai said, "My nomination to the Rajya Sabha manifests the commitment of my party for the uplift of women and reservation for women in legislature." Denying the role of her mentor Kalyan Singh in her nomination, she said, "It is incorrect to believe that the BJP nominated me following the pressure exerted by Kalyan Singh."

Earlier, six Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) members, Veer Singh, former Union minister and BSP general secretary Akhilesh Das, Brajesh Pathak, Avtar Singh Karimpuri, Rajaram, Brijlal Khaabari had filed their nominations. Besides, two SP candidates, Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav, had also filed their nominations.

Adib and Rai turned out to be crorepatis like the other eight candidates. The total assets of Rai are close to Rs 4 crore, while that of Adib is a little over Rs 1 crore.

As per her affidavit, Rai's husband owns agriculture land worth Rs 24 lakh at Mohanlal Ganj in Lucknow. Total worth of the residential plots, flats and residential buildings owned by Rai is close to Rs 2.6 crore. The cash and bank deposit and

gold held by Rai and her husband is little over Rs 30 lakh and fixed deposit in the name of her two daughters is Rs 41 lakh. She has two revolvers, one in her name and the other in her husband's name.

Adib's assets include land in Aligarh worth Rs 60 lakh, residential building in Barabanki district worth Rs 40 lakh and banks deposits and gold worth Rs 4.2 lakh.

Heading: Lawyer pulled up for tarnishing judiciary’s image - Indian Express
Content:
In a relief to industrialist Ashok Todi, the Supreme Court on Monday asked the CBI not to arrest him till November 17 in connection with the Rizwanur Rehman murder case. A trial court here has issued a non-bailable warrant against him. On November 17, Todi's plea seeking a stay on the NBW will be taken up by the apex court.

A bench comprising Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan and Justices P Sathasivam and J M Panchal said, "We are not passing a formal order but the CBI may see that he is not arrested till Monday (November 17)."

Todi, fearing arrest in the case, had moved the apex court on November 7 seeking urgent hearing in the matter.

Senior advocate Harish Salve, appearing for Todi, who has been chargesheeted for alleged abetment of suicide of his son-in-law Rizwanur, had said despite the October 13 order of the apex court there was no protection to the industrialist. A Metropolitan Magistrate in Kolkata had asked the accused to appear before it on October 27 but he failed to abide by the order, prompting the court to issue the NBW.

The apex court had earlier said trial in the case would not commence till the Calcutta High Court decides a petition filed by Todi challenging CBI's decision to chargesheet him in the case. Todi, along with six others, was chargesheeted by the CBI on September 22 for alleged abetment of Rizwanur's suicide under sections 306 (abetment of suicide), 120-B (criminal conspiracy) and 506 (criminal intimidation) of the IPC. Rizwanur's body was found on railway tracks on September 21, 2007. He had married Todi's daughter Priyanka on August 18 last year.

Besides the Todi brothers and Saraogi, the chargesheet names the then deputy commissioner of Kolkata Police Ajoy Kumar, then assistant commissioner of police Sukanti Chakraborty, sub-inspector Krishnendu Das and family friend of the victim S M Mohiuddin alias Pappu.

Heading: 4 Gujarat riots accused plea for narco test - Indian Express
Content:
An advocate seeking contempt action against two judges of Allahabad High Court in connection with the death of a lawyer, who was sent to jail for making insinuations against the judges, earned the wrath of the Supreme Court on Monday. The SC severely reprimanded him for tarnishing the judiciary's image.

"It's absolutely false (what you have stated in your petition). You are tarnishing the image of judiciary. It is unfortunate and you are a member of the Bar," remarked Chief Justice of India K G Balakrishnan, heading the Bench that took the petition filed by advocate Aeltemesh Rein.

Rein has alleged that the victim, who served a month-long imprisonment for committing contempt, died after he was illegally chained, handcuffed, tortured by the jail authorities.

The High Court had held advocate S K Awasthi guilty of contempt of court for attributing motives to judges and accusing them of being biased.

The court, perusing his affidavit, was perturbed that Rein did not state that the wife of the deceased was given a job and compensation of Rs 3 lakh. It sought to know if it was the judges who caused injury to the deceased advocate. Rein said injury was inflicted by the jail inmates. While sending the matter to HC, the Bench observed, "At least a lawyer should not file such a petition."

The petition had alleged that two HC judges, B S Chauhan (now Chief Justice of Orissa High Court) and Arun Tandon, who had punished Awasthi for contempt, had themselves committed contempt by violating directions given in 1998 by the apex court that an accused can be handcuffed only in exceptional cases. The petition had alleged that Awasthi was handcuffed and produced before the Bench for hearings.

Awasthi was sentenced to one-month imprisonment by the HC on April 22 for scandalising the court. However, his sentence was kept in abeyance on the plea of a lawyers' body that the advocate will apologise for his conduct. On April 1, the advocate appeared in the court and repeated his misconduct following which the suspension of sentence was lifted.

In jail, Awasthi developed medical complications and was shifted to a hospital where he died on May 14.

Heading: MNS violence: SC seeks state Govt response - Indian Express
Content:
Four men, suspected of perpetrating the Naroda Gam riots in 2002, have sought permission for narco tests to be conducted on them and the witnesses in order to "bring out the truth".

Residents of Naroda Gam — Vasudev Patel, Bhupendra Thakur, Ashok Panchal and Pramukh Patel — made this unusual request in an application filed at the Special Investigation Team (SIT) office in Gandhinagar on Friday. They claimed that the witnesses in the rioting case had given "false statements against them because of some ulterior motives".

The four were, however, arrested two days later by the Supreme Court-appointed SIT, which is investigating the post-Godhra communal riots in Gujarat, on charges of murder, conspiracy, rioting and arson. The men were produced before a local court here on Monday.

Heading: Oppn keeps away from all-party meet on migrants - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Monday brought the Maharashtra Government under the judicial scanner for its apparent failure to put an end to unabated attacks against north Indians, especially people from Bihar and UP. But it refused to order a judicial inquiry into the killing of Bihari youth Rahul Raj in an alleged police encounter and murder of a UP resident in Mumbai train last month.

Seeking a detailed response from the Chief Secretary of Maharashtra in this regard, a Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan issued a notice to the state while perusing a PIL filed by Salek Chand Jain, a Delhi-based businessman, which has sought directions to the administration for protection of life and property of north Indians in Mumbai.

After listening to advocate Sugriva Dubey's submissions, who appeared for the petitioner, the court agreed to examine the petition that has brought to the fore the state's apparent failure to prevent attacks against non-Marathis in the wake of an alleged hate campaign unleashed by Raj Thackeray-led MNS.

Dubey contended that attacks on north Indians allegedly by the MNS had led to a chain reaction elsewhere in the country and threatened to destroy the nation's unity and integrity.

While the court agreed to seek the state Government's response, it did not touch the Ministry of Home Affairs and state of Bihar, which were also named as respondents in the petition. Even though the counsel contended that there was a constitutional crisis in the state and the Centre remained a mute spectator choosing not to exercise its power under Article 355 of the Constitution, the Bench refrained from passing any directions.

However, the Bench refused to entertain another related PIL, filed by advocate Sanjeev Kumar Singh, which besides judicial inquiry, has sought transfer of cases against Raj Thackeray. "Your prayers cannot be granted. Your plea for judicial inquiry is not possible," the court noted.

Heading: MNS moves on: first heat on migrant taxi drivers, now AC cars for Mumbai - Indian Express
Content:
An all-party meeting called by Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on Monday to discuss the issue of attacks on migrants in the state turned out to be a damp squib as opposition leaders chose to stay away.

The meeting had been called after Deshmukh's recent announcement that he would lead a delegation to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on the issue of Maharashtra's image being maligned by politicians from northern states like Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

The meeting was attended by a few politicians like deputy chief minister R R Patil, Sachin Ahir (NCP's Mumbai chief), and Ramdas Athawale (RPI leader). The meeting has now been scheduled on Wednesday as Shiv Sena and BJP leaders stayed away.

"The government should first determine the policy (of what stand to take) and then call us," Sena leader and MLA Subhash Desai said. "When several leaders of the Congress and the NCP are talking in different voices, there is no point in discussing the issue."

He pointed out that Congress MP Gurudas Kamat had publicly demanded the arrest of Sena chief Bal Thackeray. "There was absolutely no need for Kamat to make that demand," said Desai.

Heading: Protesting Lalgarh still cut off, Buddha turns to CRPF - Indian Express
Content:
After driving away taxi drivers and rickshaw pullers — mostly migrants to the metropolis — the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) is planning to start a 500-car fleet of air-conditioned taxis in Mumbai.

As MNS chief Raj Thackeray inaugurated the central office the Maharashtra Navnirman Transport Union (MSTU) in Kurla on Monday evening, party workers revealed the plan to launch taxi service.

"As per the current plans, there will be a fleet of 500 cars in the service with good drivers. We want to offer good services to the Mumbaikars," said Balkrishna Mhetre, executive president of MSTU.

Mhetre said that such services are required if Mumbai is to become an international city. "When women travel at night, they need drivers who are well behaved. There won't be much difference in the fares of ordinary taxis and the air-conditioned service," Mhetre added.

MSTU currently has 52,000 members across the state. "All the members will be given identity cards and ID numbers. In case they need any assistance in terms of accidents, loans, they can contact the central office and the local leaders will reach them. This office will remain open 24X7," said Mhetre.

He was greeted with much fanfare at his first public appearance since his release on bail from Kalyan court last month. With the gag order still in force, Raj refrained from making a speech.

"We will follow whatever Raj saheb says. Even if there are protests on the street, no one will dare to touch these vehicles. With the help of 24-hour computerised centre, we will be able to reach all our members at all times," said Haji Mastan Sheikh, chief of MSTU.

"We are planning to give insurance to all our members for accidents and damage. Details of the insurance are still being worked out as we are in talks with an insurance company," he added.

Heading: Mamata to field police firing victim kin in Nandigram - Indian Express
Content:
With the Maoist-affected areas of West Midnapore being cut off from the rest of the state following the tribals protesting against the police, the state Government has asked for Central Reserve Police Force to control the situation. On Monday, tribals cut off two vital road links in Binpur and Lalgarh police station areas in the presence of the much-hyped state combat force.

As the news reached the Writers' Buildings, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee held an emergency meeting with Chief Secretary Amit Kiran Deb and Home Secretary Ashok Mohan Chakrabarti. After the meeting, the Home Secretary said: "The chief secretary is visiting Delhi on Tuesday. We have asked for six CRPF companies to tackle the situation." Sources said the Central agency will be deployed at Lalgarh, Binpur, Belpahari police station areas.

During his telephonic conversation with Home Minister Shivraj Patil on Sunday, Bhattacharjee had mentioned the situation in Lalgarh and the need for CRPF deployment.

Additional District Magistrate R A Israel was present when the roads were dug up by villagers in Dherua. "Though our combat force was deployed, we could not prevent the villagers," he said.

The area has been on the boil after combing operations by the police, following the attack on Chief Minister's convoy on November 2. The blast took place in Shalboni, 50 km from Lalgarh. On the night of November 3, the police raided Chotopelia, Dalilpur and Kantapahari villages in Lalgarh and allegedly tortured six women. Locals allege they also picked up innocent people, including some schoolboys.

"Until the police admit their atrocities, our agitation will continue," said one of the protesting locals.

Bharat Jakat Majhi Maroa, headed by Chandrashekhar Mahato, is leading the agitation. The district administration tried to control the situation by calling an all-party meeting, but the effort failed as all parties, except the CPI(M), walked out of the meeting.

The CPI(M) has decided to take its own initiative. The party's district secretary Dipak Sarkar said, "The police have asked the protestors to repair the roads by Monday. If they don't, we will go there and undertake the repair work ourselves."

Heading: Internal democracy: Rahul plans US-style debates in Youth Cong - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee alleged that Maoists and the CPI(M) are hand-in-glove in the state and dared the Government to ban the ultra Left outfit. Kicking off her campaign for the Nandigram bypolls at a rally there on Monday, she said that her party's candidate belongs to one of the 14 families who lost members in police firing on March 14, 2007.

Coming down heavily on the ruling party, Banerjee said, "The so-called Maoists are active in West Midnapur, Bankura and Purulia. The Trinamool has won no seat in these districts, how does the CPI(M) always win in these areas? The CPI(M) has entered into a secret deal with these outfits and is using them."

Bypolls in Nandigram are to be held in December, as legislator Muhammed Illias had to resign after charges of bribery.

Banerjee said that she has instructed the district leadership to provide help to the family members of those killed and missing. "They should be provided houses under Indira Bikas Yojana. I will inspect the progress personally. We should not forget the martyrs," she said.

Alleging that the state Government is not allowing TMC-led East Midnapur Zilla Parishad to undertake development works, she said the dates for bypolls have not been announced. "The district administration is deliberately not allowing us to work for the people," she said.

Regarding Sunday's CPI(M) rally in Nandigram, she said Trinamool is ready to combat them politically. "But if they use force, anything can happen. I will urge the CPI(M) and the state Government not to repeat the mistakes they made in Nandigram and Singur."

Heading: ITBP downs gender barrier, woman commandos set to guard President - Indian Express
Content:
Taking a leaf out of the recently-concluded US presidential elections, AICC General Secretary Rahul Gandhi has decided to introduce Presidential debates in the Punjab Youth Congress president election scheduled for December. The audience will comprise 2,940 delegates chosen through elections at the block, district and state level.

"All candidates vying for the presidential post will participate in the debate. It will be like the US presidential debate or JNU elections. Everybody should know what a candidate wants to do. What is his ethic?" said Ashok Tanwar, president of the Indian Youth Congress (IYC).

The election for PYC president is part of Rahul's experiment with internal democracy in the IYC and the National Student's Union of India (NSUI). The IYC in Punjab and NSUI in Uttarakhand are the organisations Rahul Gandhi has chosen to kickstart the exercise with. In Punjab, the PYC has already enlisted three lakh members and provided them voter identity cards.

Apart from his ambitious agenda of revamping the youth and students' wing of the Congress, he has also managed to secure party tickets for at least 14 IYC leaders and several NSUI workers in the forthcoming Assembly elections in six states. They include state Youth Congress presidents of Delhi, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Mizoram and Jammu & Kashmir. "Earlier, we used to get barely one to two tickets. Even state presidents of the Youth Congress were denied tickets. But this time at least 80 to 90 per cent of those recommended by us have been given tickets," said Tanwar.

Heading: Look at its capability: Rafale makers to India - Indian Express
Content:
It will be another first for the country's first woman President. Come November 2009 and President Pratibha Patil will become the first incumbent of Rashtrapati Bhavan to be guarded by women commandos.

The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), which is in the process of recruiting 480-odd women in combat ranks, plans to deploy a good number of them to guard the President and the Rashtrapati Bhavan. Women commandos will also make a debut in the Vice-President's residence around that time. ITBP's male personnel at present man both the premises.

Once selected, early next year, these women will undergo 48 weeks of training including specialised commando training at ITBP's Commando Training School in Mussoorie before being deployed for various assignments. Not limiting them to VIP duties, ITBP also plans to deploy its Mahila Constables on the Indo-China border at Nathu La and also on escort duties with pilgrims of the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra.

"As many as 17,000 women have applied for these 450 posts and the applicants include some of the finest national level sportspersons representing the country in various disciplines. After training them for around 48 weeks, we plan to start deploying them on a host of duties including those at the Rashtrapati Bhavan, the Nathu-La Pass and the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra," ITBP Director General Vikram Srivastava said.

Heading: ‘Sukhoi 30 outshone in US aerial exercise’ - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when the United States and France have taken the lead in engaging India and other emerging economies to find a way out of the global financial mess, aviation majors of the two countries are locked in a turf battle of a different kind, vying with each other for the $10-billion India contract for 126 Medium Multi-Role Combat Aircraft (MMRCA).
