Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas and Israeli Foreign Minister Tzipi Livni briefed representatives of the quartet, which includes the US, UN, EU and Russia on Sunday at a hotel here.

Despite a lack of obvious evidence of political progress, representatives of the quartet were clearly hoping that the peace process would survive the political transition in the US and a possible change of Government in Israel, where elections are scheduled for February 10.

Abbas said that he and the Israelis would continue to meet until the Israeli elections were over and the new American administration was in office, and that joint technical committees would continue with their work.

UN secretary-general Ban Ki-moon said that while obstacles remained, the parties to the talks "shared their assessment that the present negotiations are substantial and promising" and that they have put in place a "solid negotiating structure for continued progress in the future".

Heading: Ahmadinejad defends his economic policies - Indian Express
Content:
Miriam Makeba, a South African singer whose voice stirred hopes of freedom in her own country even though her music was formally banned by the apartheid authorities she struggled against, died early on Monday after performing at a concert in Italy. She was 76.

The Associated Press quoted hospital authorities as saying she died following a heart attack after being brought to a hospital in Castel Voltumo near Naples in southern Italy. She had been singing at a concert in support of Robert Saviano, an author who has received death threats after writing about organised crime.

She was widely known as "Mama Africa" and had been a prominent exiled opponent of apartheid since the South African authorities revoked her passport in 1960 and refused to allow her to return after she traveled abroad. She was prevented from attending her mother's funeral after touring in the United States.

For 31 years, Makeba lived in exile, variously in the US, France, Guinea and Belgium. South Africa's state broadcasters banned her music after she spoke out against apartheid at the UN in 1976 — the year of the Soweto uprising that accelerated the demands of the Black majority for democratic change.

"I never understood why I couldn't come home," Makeba said upon her return at an emotional homecoming in Johannesburg in 1990 as the apartheid system began to crumble, said The Associated Press.

Music was a central part of the struggle against apartheid. The South African authorities of the era exercised strict censorship of many forms of expression, while many foreign entertainers discouraged performances in South Africa to isolate the white authorities and show their opposition to apartheid.

From exile she acted as a constant reminder of the events in her homeland as the white authorities struggled to contain or preempt unrest among the black majority.

Makeba wrote: "I kept my culture. I kept the music of my roots. Through my music I became this voice and image of Africa, and the people, without even realising."

She was married several times and her husbands included the American black activist Stokely Carmichael and the jazz trumpter Hugh Masekela, who also spent many years in exile.

In the US, she toured with Harry Belafonte in the 1960s and won a Grammy award with him in 1965. She also performed with Paul Simon on his Graceland concert in Zimbabwe in 1987.

Makeba was born in Johannesburg on March 4, 1932, the daughter of a Swazi mother and a father from the Xhosa people who live mainly in the eastern Cape region of South Africa.

According to Agence France-Presse, she was often short of money and could not afford to buy a coffin when her only daughter, Bondi, died aged 36 in 1985. She buried her alone, barring a handful of journalists from covering the funeral.

Heading: Chandigarh Carnival to showcase many a first - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Drugs 6 times costlier, treatment gets unaffordable for many - Indian Express
Content:
Fireworks, an ethnic village, participation of foreign embassies, a helicopter showering flower petals-the annual Chandigarh Carnival is set to showcase events that it never did before.

In a recent meeting, UT Home Secretary Ram Niwas instructed all his men to make the show a "never-seen-before" spectacle. "It is going to be a spectacular show with lots of novel concepts. There will be fireworks, music, food courts, lots of fun elements for children, police control room for safety and security and even a special corner for senior citizens," said Ram Niwas.

The UT Administration has requested the Air Force to offer its chopper services to shower flower petals at the inaugural event on November 22. While a formal confirmation in this regard is awaited, officials are confident on a positive response.

An ethnic village will be created at the Leisure Valley in Sector 10 that will host the two-day carnival to be inaugurated by UT Administrator General S F Rodrigues (Retd).

Unlike previous years, stalls and other related structures will be in the shape of shacks made with bamboos. N K Saathi, an artist, has been entrusted with the task of setting up the Carnival Village. The Municipal Corporation has been asked to arrange for plants and flowers to decorate the venue and also set up a temporary fountain. The decoration of the main entrance will be based on the carnival's theme — "fun and games".

The Administration has also approached the embassies of Tajikistan, Poland, Hungary and Japan to put up stalls. Officials said they had already received confirmation from the Embassy of Hungary.

France will be the partner country at the carnival and put up a special stall. A replica of the Eiffel Tower is already in place at the entry of the venue (see photo).

Another proposal pertains to a 'corporate street' put up by companies like LG, Samsung and Sony among others to generate funds.

A display of "high-quality" fireworks will be part of the concluding day extravaganza on November 23, for which the Administration is holding negotiations with experts in Mumbai and Meerut. Also, trees at the park will be illuminated, for which the engineering department has been asked to make necessary arrangements.

Another major attraction will be a CITCO Da Vehra in ethnic Punjabi style, where various kinds of traditional delicacies, particularly Makki Di Roti and Sarson Da Saag, will be served. Cooks are being called from the interiors of Punjab to prepare the famous Amritsari Kulcha Channa, Gur Da Halwa, Chati Di Lassi and Phagware Di Kadhi.

Heading: Less jobs, low pay packages, global meltdown hits UIET - Indian Express
Content:
The last six months have been tough for patients suffering from the life-threatening genetic disorder, Primary Immunodeficiency Disease (PID). With the prices of medicines witnessing a six-fold increase, treatment has become unaffordable for many.

According to doctors at the PGI, the escalation is linked to the Beijing Olympics as the entire stock of medicines is imported from China and Korea, which jacked up its export rates before the games.

"There is no indigenous production of the injection — intravenous immunuglobulin (IVIG), which is required to be administered to the children suffering from Primary Immunodeficiency disease (PID). The prices have escalated from around Rs 2,700 per 5 gram in the beginning of the year to as high as Rs 14,000. It had in fact peaked in August when the price was Rs 16,000 per 5 gram. The dealers said the supply and the price hike was affected due to the Olympic Games in China and it was only by the end of this year that the prices were expected to come down," said Prof Surjeet Singh, additional professor, Advanced Paediatric Centre, PGI on Tuesday.

He was speaking to the media. Seeing the plight of its patients, whose monthly expenditure on the treatment has increased to Rs 32,000 from around Rs 7,000, the centre made a formal appeal to the public to donate generously.

Vivek Kapoor, president of Paediatrics Medical Support Society, an NGO working for PID patients, said though they had several donors pitching in with financial support, the high prices of the medicine had made it tough for them to help all patients. "Once diagnosed, the patients have to be on medicines throughout their lives. A child weighing 30 kg requires 12 to 15 grams of IVIG every month and the dosage increases with the weight of the patient. If the drugs are not given in time, it can prove fatal."

Narrating how the past few months have become extremely strenuous, Tarachand Rana, whose 16-year-old son Himanshu suffers from PID, said: "I work as an assistant in a medical centre at Kurukshetra. The monthly expenditure of Rs 32,000 is unaffordable for me."

Similar is the plight of Arun Kambhoj, a cable operator in Kullu whose 11-year-old son Abhinav is a patient.

Heading: Their pending cases with UT, burden off Punjab and Haryana; consumers finally see justice - Indian Express
Content:
Packages dip to Rs 3.5 lakh per annum from Rs 8 lakh in '07

With the country's job market in the grip of global recession, the University Institute of Engineering and Technology (UIET), Panjab University, is feeling the heat. Not only has there been a steep fall in the number of placements, the pay packages being offered this year is also considerably low. Campus placements so far have seen Rs 3.5 lakh per annum as the highest offer, against last year's Rs 8 lakh per annum.

To add to the students' woes, those recruited this year don't know yet as to when they will join their first job. And the problems don't end with the current batch. The students hired last year, too, face an uncertain future as their joining dates have been postponed till further notice by the respective companies.

With the academic session coming to an end, the authorities are trying their best to place all the students. It is learnt that they are now inviting companies that they had never called earlier, Newgen Software being one of them.

Talking to Newsline, UIET placement officer in-charge Dr Gurdeep Singh says: "Recession has affected the placements in colleges. The previous years have seen 100 per cent placements, but things are difficult this year."

With an over 50 per cent dip in the number of students getting placed, according to officials, many students are yet to get a job. Campus placements usually get over at UIET by November. Big companies like HCL, Wipro and Accenture have given UIET a miss this year. They are also among the companies that have put off the joining of the students absorbed last year.

The select few who have been hired this year, too, may have to wait for over a year before their joining is confirmed, according to sources. Among the firms that visited the campus for placements are Aricent, which offered the year's highest package, Winshuttle and Tech Mahindra.

UIET placements are significant as they also cater to the students of chemical engineering and Master of Computer Applications.

Commenting on the poor placement scenario, UIET director Prof B S Sohi said: "We are trying our best and are looking out for the companies that can hire our students. We are not the only ones to be at the receiving end, but the entire job market is reeling under the global recession."

With few jobs in the market, students are a worried lot and they are clueless about their next step.

Aman, one of the students, said: "Most of us take admission here (UIET) because it assures placements. But the scene is different this year. We are not able to figure out the solution. The department is, however, trying its best and we are still hopeful."

Heading: Defamation case against Amarinder: Badal questioned - Indian Express
Content:
Working as a labourer in Muktsar district, Ram Brij Paswan waited for seven long years to get back the money he sent to his village in Bihar in 2001 as a money order that was never delivered. It had been a tough fight for him as his consumer case moved from the district forum to the Punjab state commission where the post office had filed an appeal against the order issued in his favour. The heavy pendency in the Punjab commission resulted in a long wait for him to get back his Rs 2,800.

Paswan is a contented man today. His case was transferred to the UT State Commission, following an order by the National Commission this year. He has got his money back, along with a compensation of Rs 1,500 from the post office concerned.

"I had lost all hope. It was good that the case was transferred to UT," said the labourer.

The UT State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has settled 2,687 cases that were transferred to it from the Punjab and Haryana commissions since last year. With a disposal rate of over 60 per cent, the UT commission has been quite successful in reducing the pendency of the two states, if the statistics are any indication.

Of the 919 cases received from Punjab, UT has disposed of 635 cases till now. It received 1,768 consumer cases from Haryana, of which 941 stand settled.

With the two state commissions burdened with heavy pendency and non-availability of benches and infrastructure, the transfer of cases proved to be a boon for the consumers fighting for their rights. The Haryana State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has a burgeoning 14,564 cases pending before it, while the number is 17,747 in the various district forums of that state.

In Punjab, the district-wise pendency adds up to 4,973 cases, while 5,101 cases are pending before the Punjab State Commission where appeals and claims above Rs 20 lakh are filed. The UT commission received cases, dating back to as early as 2001 and 2002, pertaining to problems of farmers, medical negligence, coaching institutes and those related to electricity boards of the respective states.

In one such case decided on October 31 this year, the Haryana Vidyut Parsaran Nigam was directed to pay for imposing wrong penalty in a bill dating back to 1999.

Most of the cases heard by it were from far-flung areas of Bhiwani, Rohtak, Mukstar, Sirsa, Narnaul and other districts of the two states.

"It was a good decision to transfer the pending cases to UT. The cases mostly pertained to cattle insurance and electricity complaints," said Justice K.C Gupta, president of the UT State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

"This has eased our burden to a great extent. Many consumers have got justice which could have been delayed here due to the long pendency," said Justice S N Aggarwal, president of the Punjab State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

Heading: 4 yrs after death, convict’s  plea comes up for hearing - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal was cross-examined in the ongoing civil suit on Monday in relation with a defamation case of Rs 5 crore filed by him against former CM Captain Amarinder Singh.

The defamation case was filed on August 12, 2002, in connection with an advertisement portraying Badal as having amassed illegal property worth crores.

It has been alleged that the advertisement published on January 1, 2002, under the heading — 'THE GREAT BETRAYAL' — had wrongly conveyed a message that the Punjab CM had mortgaged the state's interest in the Sutlej Yamuna Link (SYL) canal.

Badal reached the district courts at 11.30 am amid a battery of supporters and was questioned by the defence counsel for more than 90 minutes in the jampacked court of Chief Judicial Magistrate Kanchan Mahi.

Facing a volley of questions on the alleged bartering of Punjab's interest in SYL by Badal to Chautala in lieu of land in Gurgaon as a "gift" and the PPSC scam, a visibly calm Badal deposed before the court that if any amount was received from Haryana for SYL, they never claimed any amount nor ever asked for it and the records must be with the Irrigation department of Punjab.

The CM was also grilled about former Punjab Public Service Commission chairman Ravinder Pal Singh Sidhu against whom allegations were levelled that he used to bribe people in order to grant them jobs in the Punjab Civil Services during the Badal regime.

Badal, in his reply, said that when the SAD government came to power in 1997, all members of the PPSC were appointed by the previous Congress government.

He also said it is correct that the inside fight between the members and chairman of PPSC got published in newspapers and writ petitions were filed in the High Court questioning the working of former chairman Ravinder Sidhu.

He added that he was not aware whether there was populate resentment over the appointments being recommended by the Bench headed by Sidhu in 2001. He admitted that the members and the chairman of the PPSC were not working harmoniously and therefore, work started to suffer.

"The PPSC is an autonomous body and the recommendations made by it were bound to be accepted," he said.

"I came to know about the PPSC from the media briefings," said Badal and added that he does not remember whether any other MP or local leader or MLA informed him about the bungling situation in the PPSC.

He also said that he came to know about the recovery of huge amounts of money from Ravinder from the media clippings only.

The case was adjourned to January 10, when Badal will be cross-examined again.

Heading: Clean the system, it is must: HC to Bar - Indian Express
Content:
High Court's Division Bench stresses on IT-based system to speed up delivery of justice

Convicted in 1998 for the murder of a man in 1994, Mohinder Singh, a resident of Sangrur, had challenged the lower court's verdict in the Punjab and Haryana High Court. His plea, however, didn't come up for hearing during his lifetime.

When the court finally sat down to hear his application, it learnt that Mohinder had died four years ago.

Expressing deep regret over the inordinate delay, a Division Bench headed by Justice K S Garewal passed an order recommending that an IT (information technology) based system should be set up in Punjab and Haryana, so that delivery of justice is not delayed in the future.

A case on charges of murder was registered against Mohinder, a resident of Longowal village in Sangrur, on April 6, 1993, in Longowal Police Station. He was arrested on April 18, 1993, by the Punjab Police on charges of murder.

Allegations against Mohinder Singh were that he had murdered Major Singh over a property dispute. Mohinder Singh had hit Major Singh with a sharp-edged weapon on his head, following which Major Singh was rushed to Rajindra Hospital in Patiala.

From there Singh was referred to PGI, where he succumbed to his injuries. The complaint was registered on a complaint of wife of the deceased. After a trial, which continued for more than five years, Mohinder Singh was held guilty by the trial court and was awarded life imprisonment on April 15, 1998.

Mohinder remained in custody during trial and was denied bail. He filed an appeal through jail, which was admitted in the High Court on August 7, 1998. He served his life sentence and was released. Mohinder died on September 10, 2004.

"It is extremely disheartening to note that Mohinder's appeal was listed for hearing for the first time in October 2008. There is obviously a complete disconnect between fate of a convict and the hearing of his appeal. In the present case, the convict had completed his sentence, was released and unfortunately died, by the time his appeal was set down for hearing," Justice K S Garewal observed.

Laying stress on the need to have an IT-based system to avoid such incidents in the future, the Division Bench observed that there should be an IT-enabled data using modern information technology covering everyone who enters the criminal justice system. This would enable anyone access it through the Internet to see the important milestones in the journey of persons passing through the criminal justice system.

Some of the important milestones are given below. The list is not exhaustive.

* Date of arrest

* FIR number

* Date of release on bail.

* Date of conviction and sentence.

* If appeal has been filed, details thereof.

* Date on which sentence of imprisonment will be completed.

"The database would serve as a permanent record accessible to all who have to deal with the accused person in their capacity as police officers, prosecutors, judges or jail superintendents. This is a duty that the state owes to those who are arrested, prosecuted, tried, convicted and sentenced by the state," reads the order. The copy of the orders will be given to Advocate Generals of Punjab and Haryana.

Heading: Amritsar land case: Punjab to revoke land acquisition order - Indian Express
Content:
Expressing concern over the malpractices being followed by a few advocates, thus bringing a bad name to the profession, the Punjab and Haryana High Court held that the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana should ensure that such malpractices do not happen in the future.

Giving full support to the need of cleansing in the Bar Associations, a Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and Justice Jasbir Singh opined that the High Court would be very happy to see if there is a cleansing done in the system by the Bar Council.

The observations were made in wake of a petition filed by Advocate Jagmohan Singh Bhatti. The petitioner had sought quashing election of Harish Narang as the honorary secretary of the Bar Council terming it as illegal and against enunciated provision of the Advocates Act, 1961. The petitioner had also alleged that the law degree done by Narang was not recognised.

The counsel for the petitioner demanded that the High Court should initiate action against Narang. Showing no conviction in the averments, the High Court observed: "We are not directing prosecution. Let the Bar Council decide it."

The counsel for the petitioner demanded that cleansing of the system is required. Holding that malpractices should not be allowed to happen in the profession, the Chief Justice observed: "Don't allow people to commit malpractices. Clean the system. We will be very happy to see if there is a cleansing done by the Bar Council."

Taking a dig at the Bar Council for not entertaining complaints filed against advocates, the counsel for the petitioner said: "The Bar Council is no more the same as it used to be few years ago. Nobody is there to hear us in the Bar Council. Instead of hearing me they asked me how dare you come here and file a complaint."

On the other hand, the defence counsel, senior advocate R S Cheema stated that prosecution has already been recommended against Narang and that he has left the office last December. Cheema further stated that it was for the Bar Council to decide as to what action is to be taken against Narang.

The Court held that as on date there is nothing on record to prove that he has committed perjury. "There is no room for issuing any directions in this case. Any observations of the Court shall not prevent Bar Council of India (BCI) to initiate proceedings against Narang for commission of any kind of offence," the order reads.

Heading: ‘Parents should treat children as friends once they reach the threshold of adolescence’ - Indian Express
Content:
In the ongoing dispute pertaining to the Amritsar land case, the Punjab government has submitted an affidavit stating that it has decided to revoke January 13, 2006, notification wherein 32.10-acre land of Veer Colonisers in the Amritsar Improvement Trust land case was exempted from acquisition. The case is being investigated by the Vigilance Bureau.

Major General Sukhdip Singh Randhawa (retd) and others had moved the High Court against the Punjab government, praying for quashing a notification dated December 2, 2003, issued under Section 36 of the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922, along with all consequential proceedings on the grounds that basic layout plan of 188-acre development scheme framed by the Amritsar Improvement Trust had been completely altered. The petitioners had further prayed for quashing January 13, 2006, notification granting exemption to Veer Colonisers from acquiring 32.10-acre land, saying that it was wholly illegal, arbitrary and malafide.

Additional Secretary of Department of Local Bodies M P Arora filed an affidavit tracing the controversy of the issue, which even resulted in the expulsion of former chief minister Amarinder Singh from the Vidhan Sabha.

According to the affidavit dated November 10, 2008, a Vidhan Sabha committee, which was constituted by the Speaker to enquire and report the facts of the case, concluded that the decision of the government to exempt the land from acquisition was illegal. Following this, the VB had registered an FIR under Sections 20/467/468/471/120-B of the IPC at Mohali. The Division Bench ruled that the issue required consideration at length and admitted the case to the Division Bench for further hearing.

Heading: ‘Strike a balance between commercial and literary usage of words’ - Indian Express
Content:
I believe that during teenage years students should be most careful about getting into relationships.

I have often warned my students not to fall prey to insensitive people. Adolescence is one such stage in life, where children tend to slip and get into things absolutely uncalled for.

My advice to students is that they should spend time in first understanding the other individual and only then should they get into any serious kind of bonding.

Children, when in their teens, are quite vulnerable and thus easily get attracted to new things. At our school, we have special sessions for adolescents where experts try and solve their issues and guide them.

I am glad that the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has made these sessions compulsory in schools as these really help students to clear their myths.

There are many questions that arise in the minds of young adults which they wish to clarify so these sessions prove to be quite helpful. Though it is a known fact that an individual becomes mature with life's experiences, it is equally correct that a guide can help lower the number of bad experiences one has to go through.

I believe that every school must arrange for such sessions with experts.

Many a time, it has been seen that a wrong act in one's childhood has made him or her suffer for the entire life.

Therefore, if a student is careful from the beginning itself, things would definitely fall in the right place.

Also, the role of parents is very important in one's teenage years. Parents need to learn to form a relation with their children where the latter does not hesitate to walk upto them to discuss any problem.

It has been observed that parents keep snubbing their children for some reason or the other. Here parents need to understand that their child is growing up and is going through biological changes which might make him or her more prone to mood swings. Parents, being more mature, need to understand and comfort students in all ways they can. I would like to tell parents that once their child reaches the glorious period of teenage life, they should start treating children as their friends.

I conclude by saying that children especially in their adolescence have many issues and it is the duty of the schools and parents to help them pass through the stage smoothly.

Heading: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad remembered on National Education Day - Indian Express
Content:
A talk on the 'Role of Newspapers in Changing Contexts of Punjabi Language' was delivered by Sham Singh, former editor Punjabi Tribune, at the Government College of Education, Sector 20 D on Tuesday.

Singh emphasised on the importance of the written word and said that in the field of newspaper journalism, editors make the decision of using or changing a word on the spot as the matter has to be printed overnight to reach the readers the following morning.

"It is important that editors have the correct knowledge of the language and its vocabulary. Editors have to decide on the most appropriate word for conveying the exact shade of the meaning," said the former editor while highlighting the common errors found in Punjabi newspapers.

Singh added that one has to strike a balance between commercial and literary word usage.

"Due to migration and settlement of the Punjabi population across the world, different styles of language usage are in the process of evolution," concluded Singh.

Heading: Political parties target Rodrigues to woo residents - Indian Express
Content:
National Education Day was celebrated across city schools and colleges on Tuesday, to commemorate the birth anniversary of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, an eminent educationist and the first union minister of education of independent India. To mark the occasion, various competitions were organised.

Students of Aryans Business School (ABS), Aryans School of Management (ASM) and Aryans Institute of Management and Technology (AIMT) participated in the events organised on the ABS campus.

Viveka, a teacher at ABS, enlightened the students about the contributions of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad in the establishment of a national education system and the foundation of the University Grants Commission (UGC), an important institution to supervise and advance higher education in the country.

St Xavier's Senior Secondary School in Sector 44 also remembered the great educationist as they celebrated the day.

Various competitions including slogan writing and essay writing were organised for students to realise the importance of education in life.

Meanwhile, Saint Soldier International School was not left behind in observing the first National Education Day. A slogan writing competition was also organised where students of Class VI and VII participated and stated their views on various aspects of education.

Satluj Public School also organised an essay writing competition on the role of education in society to mark the occasion. Principal Krit Serai said, "The day is being celebrated to remember Maulana Abul Kalam Azad on his birthday. He was someone who contributed immensely to the cause of education in our country."

Also, a special programme was organised in Blue Bird School in Sector 16, which started with students of the school speaking on the importance of literacy and commitment to all aspects of education.

Students from Classes I to IV participated in a card making contest on the subject of 'Literacy for All'. Students from V to VII wrote slogans, while the students of Classes VIII to X participated in an essay-writing competition on the significance of celebrating National Education Day.

An essay writing competition and an elocution contest were also held in Government College in Sector 11, to mark the day. Convener of the event, Dr Suchita Malik, said the meaning of Abul Kalam's name is 'the lord of dialogue'.

The pen name 'Azad' which was adopted by him later signified his emancipation from the narrow views of religion and life. Teachers and students later held a rally on Madhya Marg, holding banners and placards. In essay writing, the first position was bagged by Anish (BA III), while the second and third position went to O Naresh (BA III) and Harmanjeet Singh (BA II) respectively. In elocution, Anish (BA III) stood first again while Ravdeep Gill (BSc II) stood second and Gurpreet Singh (BA I) came third.

The faculty members at Punjab Engineering College, meanwhile, spoke to the students about the 'Future of Education in PEC'. Director Dr Manoj Dutta, presided over the function and accentuated the need of an industry-academia interface. Dr Shiv Narayan also emphasised that students should be equipped with adequate skills to enable their participation in the emerging social, economic and cultural environment. Professor P Thareja highlighted the humanistic role of teachers and discussed the importance of innovation with respect to world-class benchmarks.

To observe the first National Education Day, Government Model Senior Secondary School in Sector 46 also organised a rally, which was flagged off by school principal Sudesh Raghav. Over 150 students participated in the rally holding placards with the message 'Education for all'.

Heading: Abolish post of Administrator: CPI - Indian Express
Content:
With elections to the Lok Sabha fast approaching, UT Administrator General (Retd) S F Rodrigues is emerging as the favourite target of almost all political parties in the city. While reasons may differ, the Administrator figures prominently in almost every election campaign.

The spat between the Administrator and Union Minister of state for Finance Pawan Kumar Bansal has been going on for quite some time now. Bansal had, earlier, written letters against the compensation being offered to farmers for acquiring land for the IT Park.

In one of the several issues, he had stated that while the farmers in Punjab were being paid around Rs 2 crore per acre for the land adjoining the city, the compensation is Rs 7.5 lakh for the farmers in Chandigarh.

The UT Administrator and the Congress also locked horns after the name of Mayor Pardeep Chhabra did not figure in the invitation card for the inauguration function of the Solid Waste Mangement Plant. The Congress boycotted the function. It was alleged that the Administrator had a major role to play in the muddle.

The city unit of the Communist Party of India (CPI) has questioned his policies. Secretary Devi Dyal Sharma said: "The policies adopted by the Administrator and the Administration are not for the common man. Land measuring 230 acres was allotted to IT Park.

More land should not be acquired for this. More than 120 acres was made available at cheap rates for the Parsvnath group for building housing society, which are beyond common man's reach."

Meanwhile, the BJP leaders are also not sitting idle. Former MP Satya Pal Jain said the spat between the Congress and the Administrator is a drama to divert attention of the residents, who are irked with the lack of development in the city.

"The Administrator is appointed by the Centre. With the Congress-led government at the Centre, the leaders there should intervene. Rather, the local MP has constantly alleged that the Administrator does not listen to him," he says.

Heading: BSNL to cough up Rs 5,000 for harassing customer - Indian Express
Content: The Communist Party of India (CPI) demanded that the process of acquiring land be stopped and compensation be given to land owners at the market price. Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, secretary of the party city unit, Devi Dyal Sharma, said the UT Administration should think about the welfare of the people. "At least 30,000 houses should be constructed for the homeless and needy persons and these should be provided at reasonable prices," he said. He added that no meeting of the Chandigarh Advisory Board has been held in the last two years. "The Administrator is trying to smother the voices of the people. We want that the post of Administrator be abolished while the post of chief commissioner be revived," he said. AITUC president H S Gambhir, Trade Union Council president Raghbir Singh Sandhu, Youth Federation president Raminderpal Singh, Trade Union leader Manjit Singh Tiwana, Hotel Workers Union president Parmanand Sharma and AITUC Vice-President Dev Raj were among the other dignitaries present.

Heading: Two constables commit suicide in separate incidents - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed the Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) to redraw the inflated telephone bills of a customer and ordered to issue fresh bills. The department has also been directed to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for causing harassment.

The complainant, Gurdip Singh Gill, had a BSNL landline connection with an incoming facility. He later came to know about Plan 111, according to which, the subscriber could call anywhere in the circle without having to pay any charges.

When he went to get the plan activated in his name, he was told to opt for another plan with an outgoing call facility, in order to activate the said plan.

He then opted for the minimum rental plan amounting to Rs 150 per month, along with Plan 111, which was then activated in February 2007. His bill for the month of March, however, amounted to Rs 501.

After approaching authorities at the office of the telecom company, he was told that Plan 111 was not available on the telephone number starting with digits 2541 and was advised to get his phone number changed, to which he agreed.

His bill for the next month, however, was inflated, after which, he moved the forum.

Heading: Fire at Sector-23 shop destroys property worth Rs 40 lakh - Indian Express
Content:
Two constables — one with the Chandigarh Police and another with the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) — committed suicide in separate incidents on Tuesday. Kuldeep Singh, a constable with the Chandigarh Police, jumped from the roof of his house in Sector 40. He was posted at the Police Lines in Sector 26.

Police said Kuldeep was disturbed since the last few days. His family members said Kuldeep returned to his house at 5 pm and went to his room. He later told them not to disturb him as he was going to the terrace.

"After a few minutes, a person from downstairs told them that Kuldeep had jumped from the roof and had sustained head injuries. He was rushed to the hospital where he breathed his last," said a police officer. No suicide note found from from his possession.

In another incident, one Kamaljeet Singh allegedly shot himself with his service gun at the ITBP training centre in Bhanu near Panchkula. ITBP officials said Kamaljeet was depressed since the last two days. They claimed to have heard a gunshot from his barrack.

"When we reached the spot, we found Kamaljeet in a pool of blood. He had fired the bullet on his neck which came out piercing his head," said an ITBP official.

He was rushed to the hospital where he was declared brought dead. Police have initiated inquest proceedings under Section 174 of the CrPC and started investigations into the matter.

Heading: Surgery with incision, music with precision — the story of a ‘strumming’ doctor - Indian Express
Content:
A major fire that broke out in a Sector-23 shop on Tuesday morning reportedly destroyed property worth Rs 40 lakh. A short-circuit is believed to have sparked the fire.

"When we reached the spot, heavy smoke had engulfed the shop. As the fire could potentially affect adjacent shops, we immediately pressed three fire tenders into service to douse the flames," said a fire officer.

Cash worth Rs 10,000, stored in the cash box, was recovered by the firemen and handed over to the owner of the shop.

M P S Chawla, chairman, Fire and Emergency Services Committee, said: "The electricity wiring was not proper and unsheathed wires with loose connections could be seen hanging."

Chawla added: "We have already lost one life due to lack of proper gear. This time, firemen used the protective suits and they found them to be useful."

Heading: New telecom players enter unexplored territories in city - Indian Express
Content:
"Music is passion and not a pass-time," says Dr Rupak K Das, who strums the guitar with as much love and commitment, as he treats his patients.

"Yes, I have the same dedication for my music and profession," says the laparoscopic surgeon and urologist who began playing the guitar since his school days at Bishop Cotton, Bangalore.

Thrown into a music competition, Mirage '83, as a replacement for a base guitarist in the school team, the band of four picked all the three prizes.

"The boys were surprised with my performance and the obvious question was — who was my mentor? And when I told the lead guitarist that I had picked up the intricacies by just watching and lending an ear to him, he was overwhelmed," says the doctor who has invested several hours in listening to Jimi Henderix.

At the Armed Forces Medical College (AFMC), Pune, recalls Dr Das, his musical journey took a step further with regular participation in college fests.

"There was stiff competition and it helped me get into the groove," says Das while adding that the six years spent in the UK saw him fit effortlessly into the music scene there.

In Chandigarh, the doctor has a group — MLC (Medico Legal Case or Mid-life Crisis).

"Forming a band here was tough, for the music scene was dry and we had a mobile population, but, finally, we five like-minded people — one lawyer, two surgeons, one BBS student and another RJ — have been together for long furthering our commitment to Classic Rock," says Das.

Asked about the effort needed to balance his profession and his passion, the doctor says, "Of course, my responsibility as a doctor comes first. But as the coordinator of our band, I ensure that music keeps flowing with discipline."

He adds: "In fact, music helps me with surgery. It is a stolen pleasure and that is what makes it so precious. Music takes me to a different world, where nothing else exists."

Das has recorded two albums, yet unreleased, and is currently working on a new album with Subhash Ghosh. "Just like surgery, where you can't step out of the line, the basics of sur and taal have to be maintained," says Das.

MLC is all set to perform this weekend at the Lawrence School, Sanawar. So, let the music play!

Heading: Global meltdown: experts offer diagnosis and remedial measures - Indian Express
Content:
Telecom players in the region are venturing into new territories to tap potential users. While the established brands are playing safe by targeting all segments of the society, relatively new players like Ping and Virgin are focusing on newer segments.

Ping, an offshoot of HFCL, has been able to gain a customer base of over 2.5 lakh people in one year, a majority of them hailing from the rural areas of Punjab.

Vijay Bainsla, senior marketing manager, HFCL, says: "The rural folks are perceived as the marginal customers, which is a major reason why the established brands tend to ignore them. Since it was an unexplored territory, we focussed on it and the results are for all to see."

Ping now has services spread across 270 towns and 2,050 villages in Punjab and Chandigarh through more than 8,000 retail outlets.

Another new entrant in this arena, Virgin, is concentrating on urban students as its core customers. "Students receive a limited amount as pocket money and spend a major part of it on mobiles. That is why, we decided to penetrate this segment and came up with pocket-friendly schemes," says a senior official of Virgin.

These companies are also offering various plans with a view to rope in certain segments. "Our aim is to provide the optimum value of money to the customers. We have tried to centre upon the granularity factor. A Ping customer is thus charged on the one paisa per second pulse. Apart from this, we are also offering value-added services like caller tunes and background music at nominal rates," says Bainsla.

Heading: ‘Doctor’ booked on charges of raping nurse - Indian Express
Content:
Global financial meltdown in the USA and its trickling effects on the Indian Economy formed the theme of the panel discussion, "Boom! Gloom! Doom! economy in crisis", organised at the British Library on Tuesday.

Former professor at UBS and Advisor, ICFAI Business School, Prof B B Tandon rubbished the claims of a 7 to 8 per cent growth rate for India and said he would be pleased if the economy even touches a growth rate of 6 per cent in the coming year.

"We are going to be affected as we are not insulated by the developments taking place in the US and Europe. But, as we have a regulatory system in place, the effect of the Global Meltdown will be less severe in India," said Prof Tandon.

Regional Director of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Dr J Sadakkadulla assured that the Indian economy is in safe hands, due to the regulatory policies of the RBI. Comparing the financial upheaval to a "tsunami", the regional director said the events taking place in the world economy are "once-in-a-lifetime events".

"The RBI was often criticised for what critics termed as 'conservative' policies. But, it is our sound regulatory policies and fundamentals that have lent security and stability to our banking system," said Sadakkadulla.

Sanjay Tandon, chairman, Competent Group, discussed what investors should do in the current financial situation and explained how the crisis might affect investor portfolios and saving plans.

Heading: Prisoner hangs self in Patiala Central Jail - Indian Express
Content:
The Mohali Police have booked a man, believed to be a doctor, on charges of rape. A 24-year-old nurse from Tewar village near Kharar complained to the police that accused Harpal Singh, a resident of Sector 66, had been "raping" her for the last four years. She said she did not approach the police earlier because the "doctor" had promised to marry her.

It was reportedly after she was "dumped" by him in September that the "victim" lodged a formal complaint with the Phase XI police in Mohali.

In her complaint, the nurse said she first met the accused in 2004 when he opened a clinic in her village and offered her the job of a nurse. After a couple of months, she added, the clinic was closed and she was shifted to other clinics in Chunni, Badali Alla Singh and other villages.

"One day at the Badali Alla Singh clinic, he offered me soft drinks laced with sedatives. I was in a semi-conscious state when he raped me," she alleged.

"He threatened me against raising my voice and also promised to marry me," she said adding that he continued to have physical relations with her on the pretext of marriage.

"After some time, he started making monetary demands. I sold the gold ornaments of my parents to give him the money," she alleged, adding that she had to later flee home to avoid facing her angry parents.

The nurse said that while Harpal had claimed he was a bachelor, she got to know two years ago that he had a wife and two children.

"He played smart and assured me, through his wife, that I will be suitably adjusted in his family," alleged the nurse.

She added that when she insisted on an "early" marriage, she was dumped and threatened with dire consequences.

"Left with no alternative, I went back to my parents and narrated the entire incident to them. When we went to his (Harpal) place in mid-September, he threatened to make public my objectionable photographs," she said.

A case under Sections 376 and 506 of the IPC was registered against Harpal on Monday, at the Phase VIII police station.

Investigating officer S-I Deepinder Singh, Station House Officer, Phase XI, Mohali police station, said the accused was evading arrest and raids were on to arrest him.

Judgment on bail of gangrape accused today

PANCHKULA: The order in the anticipatory bail hearing of Kushal Kaushal, one of the accused in the gangrape of a 17-year-old of Panchkula, was reserved for the next hearing on Wednesday. The youth was allegedly involved in transporting the 17-year-old gangrape victim from Sector 12A in Panchkula to Chandigarh on the day the crime had taken place. The counsel for Kushal Kaushal said he was being made a scapegoat in the case and should be granted bail. — ENS

Heading: Red Ribbon Express to reach Ambala on Nov 14 - Indian Express
Content:
Meet Ram, a prisoner in the Patiala Central Jail, committed suicide by hanging himself from the roof of his cell on Tuesday.

He had been convicted in a rape case and was sentenced to seven years rigorous imprisonment.

Sources say Meet was normal on Monday night. At 11:30 pm, however, he complained of feeling unwell and was taken to the jail doctor who prescribed some medicines. At 2 pm, his neighbour, hearing no activity from Meet's room, reported to the jail staff, who found him hanging from the roof.

He was rushed to Rajindra Hospital, but died on the way.

10,000 capsules of drugs recovered
The staff of the Patiala Central Jail today recovered a packet containing 10,000 capsules of drugs and intoxicants inside the jail premises. Sources say a man came near the wall of the jail on the side of Phulkian Enclave and threw the packed inside. He later ran away.

The alert staff recovered the packet. Sources say the packet was meant for distribution among the inmates. Jail superintendent Jiwan Kumar Garg said jail authorities had been strict regarding such things in the recent past and thus such an incident.

Heading: Sukhbir meets Tota’s son in jail - Indian Express
Content:
All arrangements have been made for the two-day halt of the Red Ribbon Express (RRE) at the Ambala Cantonment railway station on November 14 and 15, said deputy commissioner S P Sarao, while interacting with the media at Panchayat Bhawan on Tuesday.

He said the train will reach the station after covering a distance of 9,000 kilometres across 180 districts of the country. The train will reach Ambala from Ludhiana around 4.30 am on November 14, he said.

Sarao stated that the volunteers of Rajiv Gandhi Foundation, National AIDS Control Society and Nehru Yuva Kendra (NYK) will disseminate information about HIV/AIDS during these two days.

He said the campaign was "one of its kind in the world" and added that it was the biggest IEC project undertaken by any country against HIV/AIDS with a broad-based, multi-media, multi-sectoral and mass mobilisation approach.

The train was flagged off from New Delhi by UPA Chairperson Sonia Gandhi on December 1, 2007 on World AIDS Day for a year-long journey across all the states in the country.

The train will later halt at the stations of Chandigarh on November 16 and 17, Kurukshetra on November 18 and 19, Panipat on November 20, Jind on November 21, Rohtak on November 22 and 23, Bhiwani on November 24, Hissar on November 25 and Rewari on November 26 and 27.

The deputy commissioner further said that the RRE comprised seven coaches.

The first three coaches host a high-tech exhibition with plasma and touch screens. The fourth coach is an auditorium-on-wheels with a facility to impart training to specified groups by skilled resource persons. The fifth coach will render counselling and clinical services to tackle the problem of Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs).

The sixth coach has a group of 60 performers of NYK to disseminate knowledge about HIV/AIDS to villagers.

Sarao said RRE performers will be assisted by Nehru Kendra volunteers to perform at 48 gram panchayats in the district during the two days.

Besides, students from schools and colleges have also been mobilised to visit the exhibition and receive information about the infection.

Heading: Barjinder gets bail; HC says no direct evidence against him - Indian Express
Content:
The Patiala Central Jail had a surprise visitor today morning. Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal came calling on the son of former Akali minister Tota Singh in the jail.

Even the local Akali leaders were unaware of the visit and only the Patiala DC and SSP accompanied him.

Sukhbir's visit comes as a major relief to Barjinder Singh, who was yesterday sent to the Central Jail on a 14-day judicial remand by a special CBI court.

The SAD chief arrived at the jail at 9:30 am and met Barjinder for about 20 minutes in the Jail Superintendent's room.

Barjinder, who is a Youth Akali Dal leader, is seen is a future prospect by the party and the Akalis had put up a major show of strength outside the local courts yesterday when Baljinder was brought to the court by the CBI. Party supporters even tried to stop camerapersons from taking his photos.

However, despite the Punjab and Haryana High Court granting him regular bail today, he would have to spend another day in the jail.

Sources said his release would be sought on Wednesday. The requisite bail bonds could not be submitted today by his counsels due to paucity of time as the court delivered the verdict late in the day.

Heading: CM’s order falls on deaf ears - Indian Express
Content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court today granted bail to Moga sex scandal accused Barjinder Singh, who is, at present, in judicial custody and lodged in Patiala Central Jail. In the detailed order, the High Court has given significant findings regarding the case. "There is no direct evidence that Barjinder participated in extortion of complainants or any other persons. The court has not been taken through statements of any witness who had said or perceived petitioner participating in the crime," reads the order. Significantly, the High Court has also held that a case on charges of public servant who commits criminal misconduct under Section 13 (d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act is not made out against Barjinder. "Barjinder Singh was not holding official status when he is alleged to have committed the offence," the order says. The High Court said there is no chance of Barjinder absconding and nothing fresh has come out against him in the CBI enquiry report. The proceedings in the case are, at present, stayed by the Supreme Court.

Heading: Arms, drugs haul: Manhunt for GNDU scholar on - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal's last week's advisory to his Cabinet colleagues on attending office, at least three days a week, found no takers on the first day.

The CM had asked all ministers to make sure they are in office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. Today, when there should have been a full strength at the Civil Secretariat, only four of 17 ministers attended office. The remaining were either in their constituencies, at home or out of station. None of the five BJP ministers were present.

Finance Minister Manpreet Badal, Information and Public Relations Minister Bikram Singh Majithia, Corporation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh and Irrigation Minister Janmeja Singh Sekhon attended office.

The CM's order on November 6 was communicated by way of a formal press statement. The idea behind the directive was the convenience of the people who reach the office of ministers from far-off places. The disregard for the directive comes at a time when the state government has stepped up efforts to rein in employees who are not only latecomers, but also missing from their seats.

The Indian Express contacted offices of all ministers in the Secretariat today. Majority of them were away to their constituencies and the staff expressed ignorant about mantriji's whereabouts. The work was going on at slow pace as employees were already hoping for a half-day holiday ahead of Gurpurab on Thursday.

With majority of ministers missing and the half-day holiday wish coming true, many left much before lunch. Majority of the Chief Parliamentary Secretaries (CPS) and Parliamentary Secretaries too were nowhere to be seen.

A close confident of the CM said, "The CM is aware that ministers have work elsewhere as well. It's imperative that they spare time for this as well."

Heading: Boy makes video, slaps college girl - Indian Express
Content:
Follwing the seizure of one of the biggest hauls of drugs and arms in the recent times on Saturday, Amritsar and Ferozepur police along with the CID launched a joint operation to trace Harmit Singh, a PhD scholar of Guru Nanak Dev University who is wanted in the case.

The raids are being carried throughout the area and police teams also visited the GNDU campus. Harmit has been missing ever since his friend Gursagar Singh was nabbed by the police three days ago.

In a joint operation, the police had earlier nabbed Sukhwinder Singh, alias Sukha, sarpanch of Khane Ke Ahal village , Kuldeep Singh, alias Billa, of Mithianwala in Ferozepur and Gursagar Singh, a local, in two separate raids and seized about 25 kgs of heroin, five AK-57 rifles, 11 pistols and 890 cartridges. The accused had also planned to kill Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmit Ram Rahim Singh.

The interrogation of these persons revealed the involvement of Harmit, a resident of Kartarnagar in Chheharta locality. "We are carrying out raids to trace him. His colleagues say he is a composed and religious person," said Parveen Kumar Sinha, Amritsar CID SSP.

Source said drugs and arms came from Pakistan on October 31. Names of some Pakistani smugglers, including Ashraff Bholla from Kasur and Nayyar Khan, had also come up during interrogations.

The Rs 21.5-lakh fake currency was also seized from the accused. DGP N P S Aulakh had said these youths had close links with terrorists in Pakistan and were in touch with KCF chief Ranjit Singh Neeta, who had delivered weapons, near Hussainiwala border in Ferozepur.

A high-level team of the Border Security Force (BSF) has also visited the area along Indo-Pak border to assess chinks in security. The BSF has been saying that the smugglers had used the riverine belt to sneak into and they were making efforts to plug the gaps.

"We are hopeful of getting more information with the arrest of Harmit," said Ferozepur SSP DP Singh, adding that there was a close link between smugglers and former Punjab terrorists hiding in Pakistan. "Terrorists will use the money earned from smuggling to further their nefarious designs," said another senior police officer.

Heading: 3-year-old kidnapped - Indian Express
Content: Vishal Bajaj, a student of Doaba College, Jalandhar, allegedly video filmed a girl of his college and slapped her when she objected to it. Family members of the girl were also threatened by Vishal and his friend Manu, who is not a student of the college. The girl reported the matter to SSP Pawan Kumar Rai and a case was registered. Manu has been arrested, while Vishal, who has been rusticated, is absconding. The angry students raised questions over security on the campus. Vishal also sent an SMS to the girl, threatening to throw acid on her face.

Heading: Review black list: SAD committee - Indian Express
Content: Three-year-old girl, Swati, daughter of a marble dealer, was kidnapped from outside her house in Bhargo camp on Sunday. The kidnapper gave a call for Rs 10-lakh ransom to the girl's father from a Bihar number on Monday. The Jalandhar police are sending a team to Bihar. The ransom caller identified himself as Sikander. Sanjay, father of the girl, said he does not know any Sikander and a business rival may have kidnapped the girl. Police division six SHO said they were investigating the matter and a kidnapping case has been registered.

Heading: Disaster mgmt plan in D’shala inadequate - Indian Express
Content: The core committee of the ruling SAD, which met on Monday evening, has decided to take up the case of reviewing the black list with the Centre. The marathon meeting, which ended past 11 pm, also decided to expedite pending cases of NRIs. There are several NRIs, who have been embroiled in some civil litigation, especially property disputes, and have been declared proclaimed offenders. A senior member of the core committee said, "The black list will also be reviewed. We have demanded a consolidated list since at present there are three lists, one with the IB, others with the External Affairs Ministry and embassies."

Heading: Chopper plan grounded, govt looks for reliable firm - Indian Express
Content:
Observers of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) detected major gaps in the preparedness of the district administration to meet any calamity in case of an earthquake during a mock exercise carried out by the district administration on Tuesday. The NDMA has directed the administration to remove these gaps. They also found that there is no District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) in place.

NDMA member J.K. Sinha, who was here along with another NDMA member N. Vinod

Chandra Menon as observer, said one of the gaps was that there is no civil defence set-up in the state, which needs to be created so that information could percolate to the people and they be sensitised about disaster management.

Since Himachal falls in seismic zone IV and V, Sinha said the NDMA would write to the Chief Minister for setting up DDMAs in every district.

This would help in making the people aware about the disaster mitigation plan and how to conduct themselves during the disaster.

The NDMA member said they have asked to set up a civil defence unit in the district so that people could be trained in rescue and relief operations.

In fact, at least one unit of the civil defence should be in place in every district, he added. The observers pointed out that the administration lacks in training for the rescue and relief operations.

Another gap is the non-availability of modern equipment, including fire-fighting equipment, with the district administration to meet the challenges posed by the calamity.

He said the youth would be involved in sensitising the people and this work would be done through Nehru Yuvak Kendras, Scouts and Guides units, National Service Scheme wings and the National Cadet Corps units.

Earlier in the morning, the district administration carried out a mock drill on the premises of the Tibetan Children Village School at Naddi in upper Dharamshala and the HP Board of School Education here. The members of the NDMA said that more such mock exercises should be carried out in the district.

Heading: Govt to hear Brakel on Nov 15 - Indian Express
Content:
Firm allotted contract had no choppers in the first place

The Himachal Pradesh government's plans to hire a new helicopter and enter into a tie-up with a new company has fallen flat. The company, which was chosen to provide a seven-seater helicopter, apparently took the Prem Kumar Dhumal government for a ride, as it had no helicopter to send to Himachal.

Put into serious embarrassment, the government has finally gone back to M/s Masco Airlines, which had been providing services to the Himachal government for over the past decade. The company, instead of its earlier flying rates of Rs 1.35 lakh per hour, will now be charging Rs 1.75 lakh for each flying hour.

Initially, Himachal had a problem in finding a safe parking place for the helicopter at Annandale ground, currently in control of the Army and being used by golf enthusiasts. But, now, the challenge is to get a new helicopter from a reliable company for VVIP flights.

"The agreement with M/s Masco Airlines has been extended till April next. We have cancelled the deal offered to M/s Simm Samm, a company that had been unable to provide the helicopter despite keeping the government waiting for more than a month. We have served a one-month notice to the defaulting company and cancelled the deal," confirmed GAD

secretary Diljeet Dogra.

The helicopter is being used mainly by the Chief Minister and occasionally by Governor Prabha Rau. In winter, the helicopter is used for flights to snow-bound tribal areas and also emergencies.

The BJP government had invited fresh offers from airlines companies for hiring a new helicopter. Nearly half a dozen companies, including Masco, had submitted offers with Pawan Hans reportedly bidding for over Rs 2 lakh per hour. M/s Simm Samm's bid was lowest at Rs 1.25 per hour and it claimed to have a seven-seater helicopter. The Masco offer was to the tune of Rs 1.99 lakh per hour, which the

government rejected.

After the Simm Samm fiasco, the government last month chose to engage Masco. Being election time in five states, private airline companies are flooded with requests by political parties to provide services for their campaigns. In fact, the Lok Sabha elections next year may make Himachal's task even tougher to get a new helicopter.

Heading: Cong claims credit for ADB loan - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Cabinet has already taken a decision to cancel allotment of the 960-MW Jangi Thopan Powari project to Netherlands-based company Brakel Corporation, a high-level committee formed recently is learnt to have decided to grant a personal hearing to the company on November 15.

Chief Secretary Asha Swaroop, who heads the committee, told The Indian Express here today that the company's top officials, including its Netherlands and Indian partners, had met her last week and asked for an opportunity to submit some documents. "They also wanted a personal hearing, which the committee decided to grant as a matter of natural justice," she added.

In tomorrow's Cabinet meeting, there is no likelihood of any decision being taken on Brakel, whose fate hangs in balance for the past 10 months, after Principal Secretary (Power) Ajay Mittal slapped a notice for cancellation of the project in February 2008.

After the Cabinet's decision in June, the Power Secretary served a fresh notice for cancellation, which the company duly replied in over a 1,000 pages. This month, Mittal submitted his report to the Chief Secretary, recommending cancellation of the project allotted and even forfeiting of the nearly Rs 200 crore that the company had deposited with the government as upfront premium and interest thereof.

Dissatisfied with Power Secretary's order and alleging personal bias, the company had approached the Chief Secretary and members of the high-power committee for an opportunity to he heard.

It is understood that the company has almost realised that the government might cancel the deed and is already prepared for a legal battle. A close rival of the company, Reliance Power, in fact, has already filed a petition in the High Court to stall the government's move for fresh bidding on the project.

The project, already delayed inordinately, is likely to land in protracted litigation even as a leading hydro company already working in Kinnaur area is also eyeing the project.

Earlier on April 11, the Cabinet had dropped the earlier notice and set out five tough terms for the company to sign the implementation agreement. The company had accepted the terms to drop the international arbitration term and to meet pre-defined milestones for implementation of the project. Later, the government dug out more evidence against the company.

Heading: A la Cart! - Indian Express
Content:
Here is the designers' guide to look trendy even when the economy is not looking good

David Abraham of

Abraham and Thakore
Don't bring the drab meltdown mood to your clothes. The optimistic thing to do now is to go in for cheerful dressing, as if nothing has happened. Bring out the classy items from the wardrobe and choose colours like black, dull-gold, coffee and toffee with dull metallic glints that can give a rich and luxurious look even without accessories. Similarly, for our autumn-winter collection, we have worked with baroque influences on a muted-colour palette.

Zubair Kirmani
Go, mix and match items of clothing to get the perfect look. The ideal thing to do is buy one designer item, like a pair of trousers or a skirt, and then team it with everyday items from the wardrobe. Colours go a long way in defining your dressing sensibility. Invest in safe colours like charcoal-grey, ivory and maroon that can hold its own beyond a single season. Focus on visually rich looking accessories, like mufflers, caps, bangles, which can make you look simple, yet classy.

Anupamaa Dayal
Recession hardly means dressing down. What it does imply, instead, is to cut out whimsical shopping. Buy one item of clothing, but make sure it is of the best quality. Trans-seasonal dressing is going to be big in a way, since the ideal way to deal with the situation is to buy clothing which is not seasonal. Buy a dress which you can also wear in summer, but team it up with a polo neck sweater, leggings or skinny jeans, and accessories like a dressy shawl or stole. This way you'll have a compact wardrobe, but you'll still be dressed for the season. I am not particularly fond of classic styles of dressing, unless it's pepped up with imaginative accents. For my autumn-winter collection, I have been careful to keep the silhouettes slim because you cannot go in for a layered look if any one item is bulky.

Varun Bahl
Even though recession may not affect trousseau expenses, you can exercise moderation in your everyday wardrobe. Go for basic clothing, which you can team up with a lot of other accents. Bring back black. Invest in a lot of blacks, since it is one colour that can be worn in many different ways, for both casual and formal occasions. You can go in for bright accessories — bright belts, colourful bags and shoes. These will lend warmth to the entire look.

Heading: Wake-up call - Indian Express
Content:
The city will soon see a unique concept, a Health Cart, where good health comes to you. Savour the benefits of this health café at Sukhna first

Step on to this cart of health and savour a journey that's delectable and nutritious. It's a unique concept and the first for the city, where an exotic range of health foods will be at hand on a portable cart. The brains behind the healthy idea, Aditi Mehrotra and Pooja Chopra feel there are many natural and healthier choices that people can turn to and opening a Health Café in the city is a small, yet firm step in this direction.

"We approached CITCO with the project and have received tremendous support and encouragement and the good beginning will be at Sukhna Lake very soon. The cart and facility will soon be extended to various parts of the city,'' the young ladies are all set for a big launch.

The idea, explains Aditi, a nutritionist, is based on sound scientific principles of providing food products that are nutritious, safe and suited to body type and their USP is, Where Good Health Comes to You! "This will cover the path between consumers and us in order to provide them with health benefits that are imperative for them. A health cart positioned at prime locations frequented by morning walkers and also by floating tourists will cater to their need for a sip and bite halt, but introduce them to the world of healthy goodness,'' quip the two.

The Health Café will offer therapeutic, creative, preventive food and Aditi and Pooja hope that it will encourage fitness and make people look at food from a new perspective, "we plan to educate the public by giving dietary advice and counselling.'' In addition to the food menu being exotic and nutrient dense, menus will change to take advantage of seasonal availability. All low-calorie items, various types of teas, including herbal and ayurvedic ones, tizanes, which are healthy infusions, juices of a combination of vegetables and fruits, fruit mashes, which don't not excluding fibre, herb-enriched salads, high-value dressings and drizzles, high-fibre bagels and foot longs...it's a tempting spread, "the price range is between Rs 5 and 55 and it's health and not profit that we're aiming at,'' it's ho for health!

Heading: Farewell strokes - Indian Express
Content:
There is a difference between being awake and awakening

When the waves crackled with 'ab dilli door nahin', we shuddered at the mere thought and picture of it. All it took was this one nightmare of a line to trigger reaction to this impending doom. Clouds of smog, treeless roads, blocks of concrete, snarling traffic jams...no, Chandigarh is not and will never be like Delhi, we vowed as we listened to the infomercial on Big FM 92.7 with all earnestness. And nodded our heads, just like we did the same night when Tata Tea flashed its Jaago Re campaign. What better way to spice up the grand Indian tea-time which happens every five minutes, can you imagine the recall value to the campaign on that! While advertisement are utilizing the much- wasted telly with their truth and dare infomercials, the government, in our case, the UT Administration has buckled up and taken to the new media to create awareness and turn the common man into a vigilante, or what newsmakers term as citizen journalist.

Talking about their anti-corruption campaign, DSP Pramod Kumar of Vigilance Department, Chandigarh says the idea is primarily to educate people. "That's why an SMS with our number on it...see people usually don't know where to report corrupt activities," he adds, urging the janta to come forward and grab their right. A good start is a job half done, and DSP Traffic, Jasbir Singh Cheema, is satisfied with their traffic awareness, and creating awareness post bomb blasts. "Over the last few months of this activity, we've got a good response, especially from the youth."

Call it a collective act of national consciousness or social awakening, but in these times of terror, information is the best weapon. "It's a way of offering a helping hand to a section of society which is facing these problems," feels Siddharth Bhardwaj, Regional Director, North, Big FM 92.7, as he throws light on their campaigns which fall

under the Corporate Social

Responsibility.

Meanwhile, social activist Gaurav Gaur, who teaches in the department of social work, PU and Yuvsatta's Pramod hail this as a good step. "At least, they've started taking it seriously and they are tracking young people through new technology," says Gaurav, who feels that an SMS is personal and there is a voice of concern in it. "The information, like website and contact numbers makes a huge difference, it's a helpful tool for our students and workers," they add.

Heading: Among dunes & delights - Indian Express
Content:
As they move on, students of MFA, Government College of Art, leave behind their impressions

A look ahead and one to the times that have passed...a hope for the future and gratitude for what has been...STAMP 2008 is one such tribute by MFA students of Government College of Arts- Sector 10, Chandigarh. Nineteen students share their visions to form a body with numerous faces. Some choose the traditional modes while others explore what technology offers them.

Each student submitted three to four of their works, so on display is creativity in varied forms — hoardings, advertisements, photographs, posters, sculptures et al. Anurag and Ashvinder spread a shade of pink to a milk advertisement and one for a party organizer, Ratika gives a creative green touch to a guava for Juicy Treat. Aishwarya gets candid with her secrets, revealed in mix media. For some, the unknown becomes a calling, sans a defined shape or a message. Anuradha, Bijaya and Pawan look for meaning among such shapes on their canvas. Charu takes an angelic flight through Serigraphy and Manjeet brings alive a clay model of a woman, while Joginder constructs an innovative dining table in wood.

On at Art Gallery of Govt College of Art, Chandigarh till November 14.

Heading: Chandigarh team returns after creating history in Goa - Indian Express
Content:
Dancing damsel

Pracheen Kala Kendra organised its 135th Baithak Programme featuring Bharatnatyam recital by Anuradha Venkataraman at the Bhaskar Rao Indoor Auditorium. Anuradha's dance performance was marked with striking stage presence, chiselled dance line, expressive abhinaya and clarity of rhythm. A unique quality of her dance is that it rediscovers, grasps and reveals the unknown. Anuradha's rendering of the celestial form of Bharatanatyam has often been described as a poetic voyage, a result of a unique temperament and the dancer evokes passion through her simplicity, commitment and endurance.

Heading: Stephen's, GNPS to meet in final - Indian Express
Content:
With their ever improving performance, Chandigarh Football Academy players showed that if it is skill that is required to win matches then they have got plenty of it.
