With ten CFA players out of the eleven playing in the team- the remaining lone player from St Stephen's Football Academy, the Chandigarh team dished out hopes of some of the title contenders in the form of Manipur and Punjab en route to the path to the final where they surprised hosts Goa by 3-1 to win the Under-17 boys' title in the 54th National School Games on November 7 at Nehru stadium, Fatorda, Goa.

What is worth mentioning is the fact that two of the CFA players- Shenaz and Abraham Lalrinngheta walked away with best midfielder and best defender of the tournament out of the players from 17 states participating in the event. "I never thought that they would choose me as the best defender. I just tried to put in my best and I was pretty surprised when they announced my name," says the 16-year-old Abraham.

Meanwhile, Shenaz who donned the additional role of the team's skipper simply puts it as the result of his hardwork. "Since the entire onus falls on the midfielder like supplying balls and orchestrating the flow of the game, it was my duty to put the ball in the right areas so that our strikers could score. I am glad it worked. Besides we were eager to do well in the tournament to make up for the loss in final to West Bengal last year at Andaman in the Under-14 category," shares the midfielder who scored a brace in the final, including a stunning free-kick that curled and sailed into the net, thus dodging the Goa goalkeeper.

With the Administrator's Cup already in their kitty and a fine performance in the Subroto Cup afterwards, the path to the final in Goa was not as easy as it seemed on the paper. "Playing the Manipur team in the league match was very tough and we were beaten by them. The semi-final match against Punjab was also tough as we won the match only through penalty shoot-out. The final was special because we were playing against a strong Goa team and their striker Chikowdi Chukuwama was on fire. However, all the team members played to their potential and we won the match comprehensively. It is a special feeling being part of the winning team," shoots Abraham who hails from Mizoram.

Shenaz on the other hand cherish the adulation that the Chandigarh team got from the coaches of all the teams. "Coaches from every state came and asked where we were from and they were surprised to find out that we were from Chandigarh. Perhaps they thought that Chandigarh was a weak team. But the finest moment was with the Goa coach who praised our game a lot. It was really good to hear encouraging words from all the coaches," says an exulted Shenaz who has modeled his style on the former French mid-field maestro Zinedine Zidane.

While the coaches at CFA left no stones unturned to turn them into the players that they are now, they want the team to come up with many more such performances. "I knew from the very beginning that we will win the title. The win against Punjab made me happier than the win in the final because Punjab has so much football academies and they have plenty of talent at their disposal but we still managed to beat them. This shows that Chandigarh is by no means a laggard when it comes to football. The Punjab team has not been able to beat us in any competitions this year," shares coach Harjinder while pointing out that the selection trials were more strict this time than before.

Heading: Gagan takes early lead with two under par on Day One - Indian Express
Content:
St Stephen's School, Sector 45 and Guru Nanak Public School, Sector 36 set up a title clash as they meet in the final of the 5th Moly Carver Memorial Cup Cricket Tournament for high schools being jointly organised by St Stephen's School and Dronacharya Desh Prem Azad Cricket Academy here today.

A third wicket partnership between Sachit Nayyar (74, 48 balls, 13x4s) and all-rounder Abhilash Sharma (50), helped St Stephen's-45 outplay St Kabir School, Sector 26 by 147 runs in the semi-final played at the St Stephen's School, Togan.

Stephen's School batted first and piled up 216 for 8 in allotted 30 overs. Sachit Nayyar and Abhilash batted well and bolstered their innings. Jaspreet (20) and Udit Hari Mehta (14) also made valuable runs.

For St Kabir School, Divjot Singh (3 for 34), Joy Mandotra (2 for 43) and Kanav Devgun (2 for 34) were among the wickets.

In reply St Kabir School were bundled out for 69 in 17.3 overs. Only Taran Sondhi could reach the double figure mark by scoring 28 runs. Off spinner Abhilash Sharma spun a web around the St Kabir's batsmen as he took six wickets for 15 runs in a most economical bowling spell. Medium pacer Jagpreet Singh bagged 2 for 17.

A 161-run opening wicket partnership between Jaskaran Singh (71) and Manan Vohra (87) enabled Guru Nanak Public School-36 oust St Anne's School by 119 runs in the second semi-final played at St Stephen's School in Sector 45.

Propped up by a century opening wicket stand, GNP School scored a massive total of 295. Gaurav contributed 41. Anirudh was the most successful bowler for St Anne's.

In reply, St Anne's School were bowled out for 176. Vishesh (20), Pukhraj Singh (38), Shivadeep (39), Shitij (20) and Shivam Ravi (20) were their main scorers.

GNPS medium pacer Vivek got five wickets for 24 runs and Karan Goel got 2 for 28.

Brief scores:

St Stephen's School-45: 216 for 8 in 30 overs (Sachit Nayyar 74, Abhilash Sharma 50, Jagpreet 20, Udit Hari Mehta 14, Divjot Singh 3 for 34, Joy Mandotra 2 for 43, Kanav Devgun 2 for 34). St Kabir School, Sector 26: 69 in 17.3 overs (Taran Sondhi 28, Abhilash Sharma 6 for 15, Jagpreet Singh 2 for 17); Guru Nanak Public School, Sector 36: 295 all out (Jaskaran Singh 71, Manan Vohra 87, Shubham Mahajan 19, Gaurav 41, Karan Goel 10, Harshit 2 for 46, Anirudh 3 for 51, Kshitij 1 for 65, Shivdeep 1 for 43). St Anne's School, Sector-32: 176 all out (Vishesh 20, Pukhraj 38, Shivadeep 39, Kshitij 20, Shivam Ravi 20, Sukhpreet 10, Vivek 5 for 24, Karan Goel 2 for 28, Shashank 1 for 55).

Heading: SGGS College emerge as winners - Indian Express
Content:
The Union Minister of State for Home, Dr Shakeel Ahmad has said that the country was well prepared to check any sort of terrorism. While refusing to get into any controversy about any acts of terrorism including that of Malegaon, Ahmad said the government was handling all the issues on the same plane.

In an informal conversation with a select group of reporters at the residence of senior party leader, Pawan Dewan here last evening, the Minister pointed out, the law was taking its own course and no leniency was being shown anywhere. He however criticised the attempts of certain communal forces, who were trying to glorify some terrorists. He warned such things would only encourage terrorism of different sort.

Ahmad, who is also the spokesman of the AICC said, the Congress was all set sweep the elections in different states scheduled in the months of November and December. He said, the people had been appreciative of the performance of the Manmohan Singh government. He said the party was quite optimistic about improving upon its previous tally in Parliament and was all set to form the government.

Manish Tewari, who accompanied Ahmad, said in Punjab also, the Congress was set to break all the previous records as the people were quite fed up with the SAD-BJP government. He said the Congress would win all the 13 seats in Punjab this year.

Later Ahmad was felicitated by senior party leaders, including Pawan Dewan, Milkiat Singh Birmi, Krishen Kumar Bawa, Yogesh Dewan, freedom fighter Rajinderpal Syal and youth Congress leader Akshay Bhanot.

Heading: Kin of HCS officer’s wife doubt suicide theory - Indian Express
Content:
Finally waking up to the case of two college-going girls, belonging to the Scheduled Caste, having been burnt to death in Kaluwas village in a case of alleged honour killing, the police have registered an FIR against the entire village. The FIR was registered on a complaint lodged by Rajinder Shivran, a resident of the village.

The village, incidentally, is the native village of Olympic bronze-medallist pugilist Vijender Singh. Forensic experts have visited the village and inspected the spot of the crime and also the village cremation ground, sources said.

A senior police official said that a case under Sections 302, 201 and 34 of the IPC has been registered at the Sadar police station and four members from the families of the deceased have been detained for questioning. However, the fathers of the girls, Shriniwas and Vedpal, are absconding, he said.

As per the information received, on the night of October 28, the two girls, who belong to the Dhanak community, were attacked with sharp-edged weapons and stones. Later, they were burnt to death by the attackers after pouring kerosene on them, sources added. The villagers, however, ruled out any foul play and said the girls had died of acute stomach pain.

Superintendent of Police Sanjay Kumar said the FIR has been registered but no one has come forward to record a statement. A special team has been called in to investigate the matter. "It appears to be a case of honour killing and such cases invariably become weak in the absence of witnesses," he said.

Heading: Banta Ram joins Cong - Indian Express
Content:
IG, State Crime Record Bureau, who is Anju's uncle, claims she could not have shot her kids or committed suicide. Also wants her husband to join the investigation

The Panipat Police have so far not made much headway in investigating the death of the wife of Virender Sehrawat, General Manager, Haryana Roadways, Karnal, and their two children. The three had been found dead at their

Panipat residence on

November 9.

The Panipat Police had initially indicated that it was a case of suicide. The two children, Meghna (11) and Paras (7), had been shot in the head. There was a bullet wound in the head of Anju as well. A suicide note supposedly written by Anju had been pasted on the wall of the bedroom. The police had assumed that Anju might have shot dead the two children before shooting herself.

But Laik Ram Dabas, IG, State Crime Record Bureau (SCRB), Karnal, has come out strongly against the suicide theory of Anju, his niece, and the two minor children. "I just can't believe a simple and good-natured person like Anju could have shot dead the two children and herself. I knew her from her childhood and she was a loving and caring person. She was the daughter of my older sister, Khazani Devi. Our relatives have written to the Panipat Police to hasten the investigation to find out the truth,'' said Dabas, while talking to The Indian Express.

Expressing serious doubt about the suicide theory, Dabas said, "How is it possible that no one heard the sound of three bullets from a revolver when they were fired in the dead of the night? There was a cook and a guard at the home, beside Virender Sehrawat himself, when the incident supposedly happened,'' said Dabas.

Asked about the role of the woman in the whole episode who had alleged molestation, Dabas said that, too, needed investigation. "There is a need for a proper and quick investigation in the case to find out the truth. Virender Sehrawat also must join the investigation immediately,'' he said.

The suicide note written by Anju, however, had said that the cause of their death would be due to disturbance caused in their family by a woman in Gannaur, Sonepat, who had allegedly lodged a molestation charge against Virender Sehrawat. Blaming the Sonepat woman for all the trouble, the note had said that she should be hanged for making their life hell.

The police have sent the suicide note to handwriting experts in Karnal to check if the handwriting tallies with that of Anju. Samples of food collected from the house of Virender Sehrawat have also been sent to the forensic lab, Karnal, for testing. But the police is yet to record the statement of the most important person in the whole episode, Virender Sehrawat, who is reportedly still in a state of shock, as per the police.

Heading: German tourist was raped too, says CFSL report - Indian Express
Content: Former Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) MLA and Dalit leader Banta Ram on Tuesday joined the Congress in the presence of Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda at a special function held at the Haryana Congress Bhawan here. HPCC president Phool Chand Mullana, Rajya Sabha MP Dr Ram Prakash, HARC chairman Karan Singh Dalal and Indri MLA Bhim Sen Mehta were also present, besides a large number of supporters of Banta Ram. Incidentally, he had quit the INLD when he had been refused ticket by the party in the last assembly elections. He had a short stint in the Haryana Janhit Congress as well, but had quit that party too.

Heading: Sahoo beatsThyssen, Lakhani enters round two - Indian Express
Content:
New section to be added in case against 6 youths arrested on charges of molestation and abduction

Charges of rape will be added to the case registered against all six accused who were arrested for allegedly molesting and abducting a German national in September this year. A decision follows a report submitted by the Central Forensic Sciences Laboratory (CFSL), confirming that the woman was raped.

Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Madhur Verma said: "We will file a supplementary chargesheet in the case, incorporating the charges of rape against all the accused. There are a few points mentioned in the CFSL report, based on which all the accused have to be charged with rape, as they have a joint liability in the crime."

According to the CFSL report, the vaginal swabs of the 20-year-old German national matches the DNA of 24-year-old Pankaj Punia, the main accused.

The report also confirmed that the nail samples of Manveer Singh Jolly and Harpreet Singh Dalli and hair samples of Sompal and Sukhwinder Singh Sukhi, too, matched the samples taken from the victim's body and clothes. The cigarette butts recovered from the farmhouse in Samalkha near Ambala, where the victim was illegally confined, have matched Jolly's DNA. The skirt the victim was wearing when she was raped, too, had stains of Pankaj's semen, the report said.

In her complaint, the German tourist who had come to Chandigarh along with a friend to attend the latter's wedding had alleged that six youths abducted her from outside Hotel Taj. She had gone to the hotel with her friend and her husband for a cup of coffee.

The CFSL had taken 48 samples of the accused to probe their involvement in the case. The bite marks, nails and other injuries confirmed the involvement of all accused in the case. Pankaj was arrested first after he dropped the woman in his Maruti car on September 28. The girl had noted down the registration number of the car, which helped the police track down all the accused.

Heading: Ansari’s century puts Maharashtra in strong position - Indian Express
Content:
Little-known Shalini Sahoo of India made it through the qualifying rounds upset seventh-seeded Nicole Thyssen of the Netherlands, while another Indian Isha Lakhani scored an easy win to move into the second round on a day when two other seeds were shown the door at the $25,000 NECC- ITF women's tennis championships sponsored by the National Egg Coordination committee (NECCC) being organised by the Deccan Gymkhana and being played on their courts here.

In the first round matches played on Tuesday, Sahoo upset the seventh seed and 236-ranked Nicole Thyssen 7-5,2-6,6-2 in a 2 hour and 15 minutes long battle. Left-handed Isha Lakhani became the third Indian player to enter the second round as she accounted for Julia Glushko of Israel 6-3,6-1. Ankita Bhambri had moved to the second round earlier.

In the biggest upset of the day, Serbian qualifier Bojana Jovanosvski knocked out third seeded and 201-ranked Agnes Szatmari of Romania 6-3,6-4, while in another upset 270th ranked I-Hsuan Hwang of Taipei scored a 6-2,7-5 upset win over fifth seeded Liana Gabriela Ungur of Romania to make it to the second round. In the first set, which lasted for 50 minutes, Shalini broke Thyssen in the 12th game to win the set. In the second set Sahoo was broken in the first fifth and seventh games by Thyssen who won the second set easily. In the third set, Sahoo again found her bearings and raced to a 5-0 lead. Thyssen, who struggled with a shoulder injury couldn't keep up with the pace and surrendered the set and match 6-2 to let Sahoo record her biggest victory so far.

Another Indian wildcard entrant fresh from her double crown triumph at the Grade three junior event in Malaysia and member of the MSLTA Vision 2010 programme, Rashmi Teltumbde went down playing a close second set against fourth Seeded Ksenia Palkina of Kyrgyzstan. Palkina won 6-3, 7-5 to move into the second round.

In the second round, Ankita will take on top-seeded Melanie South, while Sahoo will take on Uzbekistan junior and wild card Alexandra Kolesnichenko. Isha Lakhani will take on eighth-seeded Jing jing Lu of China.
