Heading: Sweet poison - Indian Express
Content:
Pune will host the Asia Cup Men's Team tennis Championships from December27–30 at the Shiv Chhatrapati Sports City, Balewadi.

Anil Khanna, president of the Asian Tennis Federation and secretary general of All India Tennis Association said, "India was chosen to host this year's event over Chinese Taipei, and Thailand. We are extremely happy with the facilities offered at the Balewadi tennis complex and hence chose Pune to host the event."

The total prize money of $1,00,000 will be offered at the event, which will see top eight Asian teams Japan, Korea, China, Chinese Taipei, Thailand, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and hosts India vie for the crown. The winners will get $30,000 while the runners-up will get $15,000. The matches will be played on a round-robin basis with teams divided into two groups of four each, and the top two teams getting into the finals.

This will be the third edition of the Asia Cup, which was earlier held at Tashkent and Bangkok. The women's team championships will be played at Indore from December31, Khanna said.

He said that country's newly crowned No.1 player Somdev Dev Barman would lead the Indian challenge; the other two members of the team will be announced in the next week. Khanna also said that the AITA believed that the country needed a competitive tournament structure and around 40-50 weeks of international tournaments were being planned in 2009.Out of these Pune will witness 8-10 tennis events every year. He added that the AITA (All India Tennis Association) and the MSLTA (Maharashtra State Lawn Tennis Association) team visited the Balewadi complex and the AITA has decided to also select Pune as a centre to train the team of 40 selected players under the scheme for Commonwealth Games 2010 and Asian Games 2012.

International coaches and trainerers will soon be appointed to work with these players and they will be staying in the city. Khanna also announced that three coaches from Pune — Nandan Bal, Nitin Kirtane and country's first level three women's coach Radhika Tulpule Kanetkar — have been selected in the coaches panel for the programme. Former Indian captain and Davis Cupper Jaideep Mukherjee will lead the panel.

Heading: Smile wide - Indian Express
Content:
Experts express concern over lifestyles which put people at a high risk of diabetes

* Every 10 seconds, a new diabetic patient is diagnosed in the world.
* Nearly 19,000 every day die due to diabetes and its complications.
* A diabetes related amputation every 30 seconds.

Diabetes is increasing all over the world both in developed as well as developing countries. With November 14 observed as World Diabetes Day, a host of special awareness programmes has been organised in the city that includes rallies and exhibitions about the disease. An India Diabetes Week will also coincide with the World Diabetes Day.

Says Dr Abhay Mutha, president, Diabetes Care and Research Foundation, "The total population of diabetic patients in the world in 2003 was approximately 150-180 million out of which 35-40 million were in India itself and this number is going to almost double in next 15 years, say, 300 million in 2020."

According to the prediction of WDF (World Diabetes Federation) the developing world will have the major impact of diabetes and will harbour almost 220 million patients and developed world will have approximately 75-80 million patients in 2020.

Mutha cited a recent study in five metropolitan cities of the country, which stated that Pune has at least three-four lakh diabetic patients. "Almost 15 per cent of the people in the age group 30 onwards have diabetes," says Mutha pointing out that perhaps this was the reason why Pune has a higher incidence of heart diseases as compared to other cities.

"While the hereditary factors play an important role, change in lifestyle is also one of the leading causes of diabetes. Increasing obesity is a serious problem all over the world and in the country too," says Mutha. There is a serious health challenge of childhood obesity.

It is more dangerous to have a central obesity than a generalised obesity. Central obesity is associated with higher chances of diabetes, increased lipids, heart attacks, hypertension and others. Also, reduced physical activity and wrong food habits lead to problems of increased cholesterol and hypertension.

"Here there is a need for early detection of diabetes with a regular screening of the population at high risk. People at high risk of developing diabetes (Age > 40, obesity, abnormal lipids and strong family history) need special attention and should undergo regular screening for diabetes," says Mutha.

Regular exercise, a strict change in dietary habits (low calorie, low fat, high fibre diet), decrease in stress in routine life, proper sleep, music, games, yoga and other activities are important ways of preventing diabetes in high risk population.

In fact a countrywide diabetes education programme for patients is underway from November 10 – 14 by the Abbott Diabetes Care where the medical fraternity including doctors, hospitals and chemists across cities in the country are involved in creating awareness about diabetes.

Other organisations will also conduct camps in the city on the occasion. The National Acupuncture organisation will conduct a special acupuncture camp for diabetic patients that will be held from November 15 - 17 at Hotel Suyash.

Heading: The pursuit of happiness - Indian Express
Content:
With dental implants, modern medical science gives you another reason to smile

With increasing life expectancy in India, old age no longer means being tucked into bed all day with failing eye sight, hearing and false teeth set out on the nightstand. The twilight years have now become the time to have all the fun, you missed out on during those office years. And the advancement of science and technology has certainly made this possible now.

One of the most conspicuous affects of old age is losing ones teeth. Fortunately, it is no longer an affect that needs to make you hide under the covers. Dental science has made huge leaps in implant and aesthetic dental solutions.

Dattatray Barve, 70, from Pune, who lost all his teeth due to periodontal disease thirty years back, opted for removable dentures as there was no other alternative available during those years. He has used six different dentures during these years giving him multiple problems like slipping of dentures causing embarrassment, restrictions to eat comfortably, feel and look older. Recently he underwent the dental implant surgery for all his missing teeth with prosthesis placed on eleven implants. Dr Nitin Barve, general dentist, who has performed this surgery on his father, for the first time in Pune says, "This new set of fixed implants will be the third set of teeth in human life following primary and permanent dentition. Being a general dentist, I will emphasis on a point that a Nobel Biocare protocol for guided keyhole surgery is really comfortable for patients and assured for their further journey of life."

Modern medical science has made it possible to have permanent dental solutions that don't embarrass you. When all teeth are missing, or in such condition that they need to be replaced, a fixed bridge anchored to dental implants provides the best permanent solution. In any case, old-fashioned dentures have only two advantages – low price and easy installation – and many disadvantages, including discomfort in eating, poor aesthetics, affected speech, and sore gums from denture movement. But full dental implants let you carry on with life without hitch in your stride. Not only does it let you eat and function like having natural teeth, it also preserves your facial appearance and prevents bone loss. Your new teeth should be hard to tell from natural – both for you and others.

So, chuck those boring old dentures. Get new teeth if that's what you need and, of course, keep smiling.

Heading: Rock and roll - Indian Express
Content:
Urban Ashram, a concept by city-based Sheetal Sanghvi, is the place to explore happiness of life through art, yoga, music and films

Don't ask what the world needs. Ask what makes you come alive, and go do it. Because what the world needs is people who have come alive.
- Howard Thurman

No wonder this quote motivates Sheetal Sanghvi as he attempts to bring alive minds and spirits — facilitating people revive the happiness within. His singular model, The Urban Ashram, a place meant to explore happiness and life through art, dance, yoga, music, movies, discourses from therapists across the country and much more sets a paradigm that aptly brings out the inner beauty and leads to spiritual revival.

Sanghvi has a precise account that changed the 29-year-old while he was pursuing MS in Financial Markets at the Illinois University. "While I was in America nurturing dreams of a successful career, I met many people who were professionally highly successful but did not seem genuinely contented. I also began to travel a lot across America visiting Mahhattan's yoga studios, California's Zen therapy centers and so on. That was when I discontinued my course and returned to India to further tour the country for beautiful places and amazingly intellectual people for the next two years. However, somewhere in between I also went back to complete my course," adds Sanghvi who has traveled to places such as Rishikesh, interacted with artists in Pondicherry, spent time at Prithvi Theatre and is overwhelmed by Manav Seva Sadhna's matchless service.

All this followed the conversion of his 40-year-old ancestral home in the city to The Urban Ashram. Elaborating on the concept of the ashram, Sanghvi says, "This is a place primarily for the city people who remain preoccupied in their jobs oblivious of the fact that the things they sideline in the process are more important. Here you can take the time and freedom to recognise and realise what really inspires you to remain happy. The activities here inspire you to look within, explore and practice the talent that lies ignored and is in fact your true expression."

Spread over 5000 sq ft, this 'lounge for the soul' as Sanghvi calls it, has space for various activities including art displays, talk rooms and an Irani café. "Along with practicing yoga, meditation and silence, we have expert speakers, dancers, artists, poets attending as well as sharing their views. Then there is dance, pranik healing, reiki, therapy theatre or simple casual conversations. We follow a schedule, for instance, there are inspirational films like The Secret and The Pursuit Of Happiness screened every Saturday," adds Sanghvi.

He calls this his 'social work' that leads people to view life as a creative journey and says, "It would be nice if these people further open similar centres in the wake of their own insight. Its all about living your dreams."

Heading: On High Notes - Indian Express
Content:
City girl Manasi Naik was recently declared the winner of television show Halla Bol

Manasi Naik is on cloud nine. And she very well has a reason to celebrate too! In a hard-fought competition at the finals of a popular TV show Halla Bol, a celebrity dance contest; city-based Naik was declared the winner.

Speaking about her experiences, she says, "The journey has been mind-blowing. I was determined to give it my best shot. It came as a pleasent surprise when I was declared winner among the 20 other participants."

Naik who has also worked in a Marathi film Jabardast directed by Mahesh Kothare, gives the credit of her success at the show to choreographer Umesh Jadhav who had approached her during her shooting and described the basic plot of the show. "I liked the idea and felt it was the right platform to showcase my talent, as it could not get any bigger than this in the Marathi industry. I took every stage of the competition as an opportunity to go one more step forward." She further adds, "My biggest competition was with myself. Each time I kept on challenging myself to perform better than my own previous performances."

Naik says, "Participating in any event is good. If you have a positive mindset, confidence in yourself, talent and potential, you will automatically sparkle on the big stage. But other than the technical aspects related to a talent show, what is more important are the health aspects of the participants. I observed that more than 75 per cent of the participants fall ill at one point or another during the show because of their eating habits. It is very important for a performer to be fit."

So what's next? "I have been offered a lead role in a new Marathi serial. I won't be able to disclose the name of the serial however. Bollywood is in the pipeline as well, but for the moment, my formula is — one thing at a time," she concludes.

Heading: A plan made, a plan dashed - Indian Express
Content:
Helen Bruner believes that you can master the violin through discipline

A strict follower of the Suzuki method of teaching, this violin Maestro manages to turn every performance whether good or bad into a positive experience that has even the most nervous learner smiling widely by the end of the session. Having graduated from Dr Suzuki's Talent Education School, Japan, this immensely talented violin teacher who has held workshops all over the world, she was here to train 60 young students in the age group of three to 15 years at a music conference organised by the Suzuki School of Violin. It was here that she displayed her perfectionist style of teaching.

"I was introduced to the Indian style of playing violin by Rama Chobe, which was really interesting. This is my second visit to India and the variety of colors, languages and people and their life really inspires me to come back again. I am really not able to comprehend that India has so many languages and every Indian from his childhood is familiar with more than two languages, and its this grasping power which is really unique. In the west we are hardly able to master any other foreign," she adds.

After teaching thousands of children over the years she feels that the technique has nothing to do with being musical or with being intelligent, instead, it is a well-developed physical movement. Talking about her students in the group playing violin, Brunner adds, " They are kids of 3 to 15 years age group but they all are very talented. I am grooming their potential and have a very strong rapport with children. I teach them to play violin as a language. It's a question of directing the playful and bubbling energy of children."

Brunner who introduced the Suzuki method of teaching, through her school in Britain ended her session for the day with an insightful technique as she added, "Visualize your body as a tree, where the part down the waist are the roots looking for water and the part above the waist are leaves looking for sunlight. This is just what playing the violin in a standing position is all about."

Heading: Sassoon Hospital gets Rs 70 cr for new building - Indian Express
Content:
...University to scrap Rs 40-cr contract for campus makeover

The University of Pune's ambitious campus makeover plan (UoP) has received a major set back, with authorities deciding to withdraw a Rs 40-crore contract from Engineers India Limited (EIL), a public sector company entrusted with the construction of 17 new buildings. The company is accused of failing to meet deadlines and giving wrong estimates for the project.

Narendra Jadhav, vice-chancellor of UoP, had previously said that EIL had a good track record and extensive experience in the construction business. Presiding over UoP's senate meeting on Tuesday, he, however, did a complete volte face and said that the company's performance was disappointing, that it was not meeting targets on time and that the progress of the project was poor.

"The company had assured us thet they will give a detailed plan and estimate by June 2008. But it delayed the work and gave the plan on November 4. The UoP had estimated that the work would cost Rs 40 crore, but the company's estimate is Rs 85 crore," said Jadhav. "Moreover, the plan is very poor and there are many mistakes in the estimate," he said.

Jadhav said the UoP was thinking of cancelling EIL's two-year contract. "The University will try to do this work on its own as the EIL is not doing satisfactory work," he said. Jadhav also pointed out that the EIL had been initially dissatisfied with UoP's estimate of Rs 40 crore. "The EIL had said that it did not take contracts that were below Rs 50 crore. Somehow, we managed to convince them. The UoP had no choice either as it was binding on it to give the contract to a public sector company."

The university had made a Rs 128 crore allocation in this year's budget for the makeover plan, which includes construction of new buildings as well as renovation or extension of the existing structures and landscaping. The revised budget, however, has suggested a Rs19-crore reduction of the construction cost of new buildings. Extension and landscaping will also be delayed, as the UoP was apparently unaware that the development plan had to be presented before the Pune Municipal Corporation prior to starting work.

Jadhav said that in the last 60 years, the UoP had never gone to the PMC for approval of any development plan. "But to develop this land, we need the PMC's permission. We have now made a concrete development plan and will submit it to the PMC this week," he said. While answering a query on the triple connectivity project raised by senate member Balasaheb Agarkar, Jadhav said that ten locations in the university campus would be connected on an experimental basis by December 2008. The new deadline is June 2009. "We will connect 135 colleges in a phased manner by June 2009," said Jadhav.

Delay after delay
June 2008: Deadline for the detailed plan for construction of new building
November 2008: Actual submission
November 2007: Triple Connectivity Project to be made workable
December 2008: Extended deadline
January 1, 2009: Initial deadline for V-C to shift office in main building
February 10, 2009: New deadline

Heading: As goods trade sinks, so does transport business - Indian Express
Content:
A whopping Rs 70 crore has been set aside for the construction of a new building at the state-run Sassoon General Hospital.

The building will accommodate departments such as ENT and pathology. The administrative section will also be relocated here. State Medical Education Secretary Bhushan Gagrani, who was in the city on Tuesday, told The Indian Express that the problem of staff crunch at the affiliated B J Medical College had also been addressed.

His visit assumes significance a week ahead of a scheduled visit by a Medical Council of India (MCI) team from Delhi; that team is likely to inspect various departments of the college.

Gagrani met the acting dean of B J Medical College and other officials to discuss details about the proposed new building. Speaking about the Infosys-sponsored building, he said it houses departments of urology, the Anti-Retroviral Therapy (ART) centre and nephrology. Plans are afoot to install a new Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) machine and upgrade the radiology department, he said. Further, Rs 10 crore has been earmarked for state-of-the-art equipment at the Cathlab.

To deal with staff shortage, public health department doctors will be brought to the college on deputation. Sources at the department of public health said the college had requested for 30 such officials to deal with staff shortage.

Posts of at least 70 teaching and other staff had been lying vacant at the college.

With an MCI inspection imminent this week, all efforts are being made by the college authorities to fill the posts. Acting Dean of the college N Borade said public health department officials will join on deputation and others on contract.

Computerisation plans
Sassoon General Hospital will soon be computerised. Old case papers will be a thing of the past as each patient will have a computerised registration number that will make it easy for the administrative section and doctors to get access to the medical history. Dr N Borade, Acting Dean of B J Medical College who is actively working on the project, said it will take four months to make the hospital fully computerised. J J Hospital was the first in the state to be fully computerised.

Heading: Rs 76-cr bank loan for civic projects - Indian Express
Content:
Deeply affected by the reduced demand in the industrial belt around Pune, the ancillary trade involving transportation of goods is now reporting a downturn of its own. In the past few months, fleet operators have been getting fewer enquiries for hired trucks, trailers or tempos, causing their incomes to shrink by almost half, according to some operators.

"The demand for hired trucks for transporting goods has gone down by at least 40 per cent in the past few months," said president of the Maharashtra State Goods and Passener Transport Mahasangh, Baba Shinde.

Earlier, trucks to Pune from other states would get return trips within a day or two. Not anymore. "Lately, some of them are waiting for 10 days to get a return trip," Shinde said.

Operators are saying the reason for fewer trips is that companies in Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad are getting fewer orders and hence are getting fewer raw materials into the city as dictated by rising costs and lowered demand. Rajendra Roadlines owns 20 trucks and has over 15,000 trucks from other states attached to it. "Even two months ago, 70 per cent of the loading and unloading for us would happen in the industrial areas, now it is down to 20 per cent," said Raju Khedekar, who owns the fleet. "Income has reduced by nearly 70 per cent," he said.

Nitin Ramchandra Raskar of Raskar Transportation Company owns a fleet of 10 trucks. "Enquiries are down. A few months ago, some companies would make 14-15 trips, now getting seven to eight trips is proving to be difficult," said Raskar. He added that compared to this time last year, business was down by 40-50 per cent.

Even with the trips that he gets, sometimes margins are lower. A distance of around 250 km costs the operators around Rs 6,000, inclusive all road expenses, leaving behind a profit of around Rs 800- Rs 1,000. "If I know that there is an assured trip from Kolhapur to Pune, then I don't mind going to Kolhapur for a company at a lower price," said Raskar.

The situation at the grains and the vegetable-fruit market yard is similar as well. Fleet operators say that there has been a decrease in the numbers of the trucks bringing supplies of grains and vegetables coming into Gultekdi market. "Earlier around 1,200-1,500 trucks would come everyday to Gultekdi. It has reduced to less than 1,000 trucks coming in daily," Raskar said. Although essential supplies are coming in, trade has reduced and fewer trucks have been coming from Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, he added.

"Production is steady, but demand is less now," explained Shivlal Bhosale, president of APMC traders' association. "Now, because of the widely fluctuating grain market, traders are hesitating in making big purchases," he said. A few months ago, the situation was different when the unseasonal rains had wrecked crops, because of which the quantity of vegetables coming into the market was less.

Heading: If voters don’t come to apply, forms will go to them - Indian Express
Content:
Feeling the pinch due to lack of sufficient funds, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) will take a loan of Rs 76 crore from the Bank of Maharashtra at 10 per cent interest.

The amount will be used in the current financial year to complete vital projects such as sewage treatment and roads and water supply. The biggest chunk, Rs 58 crore, will used for sewage treatment projects.

The civic administration has cited a drop in prices of cement and steel as a reason for putting up this proposal immediately.

A few years ago, the PMC had approved Rs 200 crore loan from BoM, of which the civic body had earlier taken a loan of Rs 100 crore. It has now sought to procure the loan from the remaining balance. The civic standing committee gave its approval on Tuesday.

The Congress meekly expressed its protest for the haste in which the commissioner put up the proposal. But the BJP is in full support of this move, saying it would facilitate completion of projects at a faster pace.

Speaking to journalists later, Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi said: "In our reassessment, we have found that many projects could be completed this year if funds are made available." He said work at the Naidu Hospital, going on for 10 years, could be completed immediately if Rs 1 crore was made available.

Pardeshi said, "If we wish to complete the ongoing development works of Mundhwa Road, North Main Road, Bavdhan, Sinhagad Road, Paud Road and also of Holkar and Cantonment water works by March-end, we have to go for this loan." He said the civic body could repay the loan by April.

Supporting this move, BJP leader Vikas Mathkari said, "Since last year, the PMC has adopted a policy of completing work in the same year, rather than stretching it for years."

NCP leader Anil Bhosale said, "The loan is intended for immediate completion of work, which is important as PMC's revenue, including octroi, is on the decline."

Hike in honorarium
The civic standing committee on Tuesday approved the proposal of bringing the amount of honorarium, which the PMC corporators get, on par with the corporators in Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC).The maximum amount of honorarium that PMC corporators get is Rs 4,400. Of this, the basic honorarium is Rs 4,000. BMC corporators get Rs 10,000 honorarium.

Heading: Now, a helpline for the gay fraternity - Indian Express
Content:
Ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, district poll authorities have undertaken a special drive to encourage fresh voters.

If voters are turned off by the procedures involved in getting an identity card, the authorities will make it easier for them. They need no longer go out of their way to get an application form. The district election office will distribute forms in every household; voters need only fill them up and submit these with their documents at the nearest polling booth.

The election office will also carry out fresh registration of voters. "Only 56 per cent of the total 57 lakh voters in the district have photo identity cards, with poor response from urban voters as compared to those from the rural area," a district election official said.

The Election Commission will appoint officers at booth level for preparing rolls. The officers would visit cooperative institutions, housing societies and ward offices to read the electoral rolls. The special drive will begin on November 16 and run till November 23.

Provisional rolls will be published soon; objections and suggestions will be accepted till November 24. The final rolls will be out on January 10.

Heading: Farmers make the most of krishi dindi - Indian Express
Content:
Budhwar Peth, the address of female sex workers for years, has always hogged the limelight of organisations working overtime to prevent AIDS. Now for the past seven months, they are making a concerted effort to reach out to members of the gay fraternity.

Having started a helpline, they have already counselled at least 700 Men who have Sex with Men (MSM).

Bindumadhav Khire, head of Sampathik Trust working in this direction, said: "At present, we are implementing a targeted intervention project for the MSM. Called Humsafar-Mukta, the project is funded by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation via Pathfinder International.

Khire pointed out that unlike commercial sex workers who have been traditionally located at one place for years, members of the alternate sexuality prefer to meet in crowded areas such as the railway station or bus stands. "It is very difficult to identify trans-sexuals and gays and provide service to them," said Khire.

The one-year Humsafar-Mukta project, with a grant of Rs 18-lakh, has the challenging task of reaching out to these people and giving them information about safe sex.

So far, eight locations in Pune and six at Pimpri Chinchwad have been identified, where workers of the project meet the group at night. "We have reached out to more than 700 people," said Khire.

Speaking about the trying task, he said: "We have to identify doctors who are sensitive to the problem of these men. Most are referred to National AIDS Research Institute (NARI)'s centre at Gadikhana."

Pune AIDS Control Society gives out condoms free of charge. On an average, 30,000 condoms last three months.

To help out the men in need, a helpline has been started on sex education. It is functional on Mondays from 7 am to 8 pm at phone number 9890744677.

Heading: PMC dreams of a bicycle city - Indian Express
Content:
Farmers from 28 villages from Pune district are learning new tricks in farming at the krishi dindi — an educative exhibition for the farmers. With exhibitions, alternate technologies and farming methods, the one-month programme will cover all the villages in the district.

The department of agriculture have proposed a target of 64.79 lakh tonnes of food grains — 11 per cent higher than the previous year — during the rabi season for the state. This initiative is lined up as an aggressive and integrated extension approach to create awareness among the farmers.

Deputy director of agriculture (extension) Uday Deshmukh said that all the districts in the state have started the programme except Akola and Washim who are following the model code of conduct because of zilla parishad election. All the districts have conceptualised and planned their floats involving all branches of agriculture department with active participation of field level officers.

"Revenue circle villages and major markets will be covered by the krishi dindi,'' he said.

A float and mobile agriculture exhibition, audio, video shows, power point presentations, workshops, interactions with progressive farmers will be part of the dindi.

One of the farmers, Baban Yadav, from Khed said that method demonstrations like seed treatments and soil health testing have been very useful. Yadav plans to implement the technique in his farm.

Tai Waghmode, a villager from Kanersar said that the float was very informative. She could also get some queries answered after the power point and audio video shows in the village.

The mobile agriculture exhibition is being organised at each village with independent compartments for package of important crops, crops production technologies as well as passing on information about government initiatives.

The commissionerate office from Pune has also prepared a CD which includes presentation of package practices, technologies, government initiatives and success stories.

Heading: To familiarise with women leadership, SDC head visits Gawdewadi - Indian Express
Content:
Ties up with the Netherlands-based NGO to promote use of cycles

The Netherlands-based Interface for Cycling Expertise (I-ce), an international NGO for low-cost mobility and integrated cycling planning, on Tuesday said that there is a great potential for cycle to be major mode of commuting in the city, but the infrastructure is poor.

The Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) has signed an agreement with I-ce to bring back bicycles with a bang through a Bicycle Partnership programme. As per the programme, valid till 2010, the NGO will assist the civic body to design as well as promote use of cycle through training and awareness programme. The PMC has planned 300 km cycle track.

The experts, who studied the already-constructed cycle tracks by the PMC, have pointed out serious loopholes in the infrastructure and given suggestions.

"More roads is no solution for traffic chaos as it promotes use of motorised transport. Instead, there should be more use of non-motorised transport," expert Joren Buis said in his presentation.

"The city has great potential for bicycle use. The city is flat and has a better climate than that in the Netherlands.

Buis said that cycling is healthy as the riders inhale less polluted air than those who opt for motorised transport. Cycling increases concentration and helps in better stress management.

More cycles on the road will reduce congestion on the roads and reduce pollution, he said.

Ranjit Gadgil, director of NGO Janwani, and working with Parisar for promotion of bicycle in the city, said that they have started the cycle promotion campaign and will target school children initially.

"A kit will be distributed to students. We need public support for outreach and awareness campaign in schools," he said.

In a later stage, the campaign will include workers, auto vehicle users and elected representatives, Gadgil said.

The pilot promotional campaign in two schools -- Aksharnandan and Abhinav -- had received a good response with students raising doubts on safety measures, he said.

The PMC is also planning a 'hire and ride bicycle' programme similar to the system in Paris. PMC efforts have received a boost with the Global Environment Facility of the UN approving the proposal for developing cycle tracks on BRTS routes.

Heading: Bomb hoax at St John’s school - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to familiarise with women leadership and the ongoing developments in the village, Editha Vokral, head of regional corporation, Swedish Development Corporation (SDC) visited Gawdewadi village near Pune on Tuesday.

The village has undertaken several projects in water conservation, agriculture, reverse migration etc and had received the Indira Priyadarshani Award for planting seven lakh trees. Vokral interacted with the women in the village and the women sarpanch from the adjoining villages to understand their problems and progress due to them.

The programme organised by Mahila Rajsatta Andolan had open discussions on the integrated development of Gawdewadi. Speaking on the projects Vokral said, "I am visiting the village because I am keen on seeing the women leadership in this country. Women like you are an inspiration for a country like Switzerland also."

Sarpanch of Gawdewadi Meena Gawde presented a review of the activities including rural afforestration and youth and women empowerment. "This village has a women sarpanch for over six years and collectively we have been successful in taking steps towards social development such as liquor ban and family planning. Many youths from the village have gone abroad and the number of girl students is higher, when compared to other villages. However, Vanarai foundation has a major contribution for changing the facet and mindset of this village," added Gawde.

Bhim Raskar, programme director of Resource and Support for Development and Preetha Lal, member of Swedish Devlopment Corporation, Delhi also interacted with the villagers. Manisha Gawde spoke on her projects as a Sarpanch till 2006.

"The village has been in the forefront in terms of self reliance and development and the leadership of women for the past seven to eight years shows our contribution and potential. Women leaders across the country motivate us to stand up and to raise our voice and the president's visit last month has taken Gawdewadi on the world map with people from different fields wanting to visit this place," added Gawde.

Several women were felicitated for their participation in the governance.

Vokral also presented the constitution of India to the sarpanch. Speaking on her organisation she added that the SDC is active in 16 countries and that in India, it is working along with Hunger Project and other organisations towards rural development.

Heading: Single point supply for housing societies suggested - Indian Express
Content:
A bomb hoax was reported at St John's school, situated at Sachpir Street in camp area on Tuesday at 10.15 am. After conducting a search in the school premises, the bomb detection and disposal squad said that it was a hoax call.

Speaking on the issue J.S Thorat, head mistress of St John school said, " On Tuesday, at 10.15 am, we received a call informing us that a bomb has been placed in the school and all the students should be vacated from the premises. I immediately called up the police who reached the school within ten minutes and checked the premises for one hour before declaring that the place was safe."

Thorat added that the students had assembled for their daily prayers from 10.15 am to 10.25 am.

"I didn't inform the teachers and the students about the bomb hoax to avoid unnecessary panic. Instead, I requested the teachers to continue the assembly for one hour, till the BDDS team finished checking the school premises," said Thorat.

Heading: Govt depts join hands for village welfare - Indian Express
Content:
The Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC), has suggested an amendment to the electricity supply code. They have proposed that housing societies should have a single point supply. They have also invited suggestions and objections. City-based organisations like Sajag Nagrik Manch, Prayas, Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat etc have opposed this as societies find it hard to collect maintenance at times and to thrust responsibility on them to provide individual meters was farfetched.

The groups have filed their objections and demanded a public hearing.They have objected to point number 4 of the proposed amendment. Says Vivek Velankar, president of the Sajag Grahak Manch, one of the major revisions proposed in the supply code amendment is allowing single point supply to the group housing societies. On one side, it looks good from utility side to pass on its responsibilities to such mini franchisee. But considering the housing society history where some times even collecting maintenance charge also becomes hard, commission should ensure that this provision should not be misused to harass consumers, Velankar pointed out. He said the proposed amendment may prove to be futile exercise as the registered society with ownership of premises can only apply for single point connection. But before that the individual connections are already in place, they pointed out.

Heading: Four girls rescued, pimp arrested - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time, the government machinery in the district — the revenue department, the Zilla Parishad and the rural police department — will join hands to work towards a nirmal gram and a dispute-free village under the Mahatma Gandhi Tanta Mukti Abhiyan.

While announcing this, district collector Chandrakant Dalvi and Zilla Parishad CEO Shyam Vardhani said that nearly 700 officers from the three departments will work together to implement these programmes. Vardhani said that 370 Zilla Parishad officers, 125 revenue department officers and around 200 police officers will work towards these programmes. "For example, if a person is caught defecating in the open, he can be fined and even arrested under the Bombay Police Act. Both the ZP officers and the police can work together towards this,'' said Vardhani.

He said, "Pune district will be among the first to have all the government machinery mobilised to work towards implementing the programmes. Earlier, each of the programmes — the Nirmal Gram Abhiyan, Sant Gadgebaba Gram Swachata and the Mahatma Gandhi Tanta Mukta Abhiyan — were implemented by independent departments. The Tanta Mukta Abhiyan was implemented by the gram panchayat and now the police department and the revenue department will intervene according to the case,'' said Vardhani.

Heading: PCB announces ‘public outreach programme’ - Indian Express
Content:
The city police have rescued four girls suspected to be involved in flesh trade and an alleged pimp at 11am on Tuesday at Rahtni in Pimpri Chinchwad.

"On Tuesday morning, we got the information that one Rehmat Mulla is smuggling girls from outside the state to push them into prostitution. And, that he would pass by Rahtni with the girls," said Assistant Commsioner of Police, Vinod Satav.

"A police team laid a trap in Rahtni and nabbed a man along with the four girls. During investigations, the man identified himself as Rehmat Mulla Abdul Sattar Mulla (52), a resident of Kalyan, in Thane district," he said.

Mulla said that he had brought the girls from Mumbai and was going to involve them in sex trade in the city. Half their earning will go to him as his share. Satav said that a case has been registered against Rehmat Mulla Abdul Sattar Mulla while the rescued girls are being interrogated.

Heading: Babasaheb Bhosale’s statue unveiled - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune Cantonment Board (PCB) on Monday announced a public outreach programme with the objective of sorting out the problems faced by cantonment residents.

According to board cantonment executive officer S K Sardana, the programme will strive to reach out to all the residents of the cantonment zone — across the eight wards — and address their grievances.

Under the initiative, which is slated to begin on Wednesday, Sardana and the heads of the various departments, along with the elected member from the respective wards, will organise open darbars where the residents can put forth their issues. A majority of the complaints are related to sanitation and hygiene, he said.

"Of late, cantonment residents have been requesting an opportunity to directly interact with the board administration and elected members. Such jan adalats had been held by the board earlier and had received a positive response. We aim to reach out to the common man and get a first-hand account of the issues faced by them," Sardana said.

Meanwhile, development work in the cantonment area are on in full swing, Sardana said. "The integrated sewerage management project, with an investment of Rs 16 crore, is progressing smoothly and will be completed soon," he said.

Heading: Muslim panel defers plan to float political party - Indian Express
Content:
Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar unveiled the statue of barrister Babasaheb Bhosale next to Hotel Kalasagar. The function was organised by the Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation and the Barrister Babasaheb Bhosale Charitable Trust recently. Pawar said, "Bhosale was a humble man who stayed away from petty politics."

CM Vilasrao Deshmukh said, "Bhosale was the one who first gave me the chance to be a state minister in his cabinet. He faced many political storms during his career but sailed through. I have been a minister under various CMs from Babasaheb Bhosale to Sharad Pawar and I feel like writing a book on my experiences working with them.

Heading: Malegaon: Adityanath dares Cong, ATS - Indian Express
Content:
Jamaat-e-Islami, a Muslim religious organisation, advocating theocracy and making India an Islamic state, has deferred its plans to float a political party.

Maulana Syed Jalaluddin Ansar Umri, Ameer-e-Jamaat (national president), while speaking to mediapersons on Tuesday, said: "The committee constituted to explore the possibilities of floating the party has submitted its report. But it looks like it will be difficult to start a party of Muslims before the next Lok Sabha elections."

He was in Lucknow in connection with the nationwide caravans taken out by Jamaat-e-Islami against terrorism and communalism.

At present, the Jamaat-e-Islami was striving to bring all secular parties on a common platform to place the demands and grievances of the Muslims before them, he said. "For the larger interests of Muslims, the Jamaat-e-Islami has settled its differences with the Jamat-ul-Ulema Hind. We have even attended the anti-terror conference organised by it in Hyderabad recently," said Maulana Umri.

On the present political scenario, he said Muslims across the country have no expectations from political parties. "It's a dangerous trend that after every blast, the police and the investigating agencies blame Muslims and their organisations. All parties look on as mute spectators," he added.

Muslims have been branded terrorists in this country. The whole community and a particular religion can not be held responsible for the acts of terror, the Maulana said.

"Within minutes of the blasts, the police come out with a standard statement blaming the foreign hand and organisations with Muslim names. They arrest youths and unleash terror in Muslim localities," he said.

The organisation also submitted a memorandum of 14 demands to the state governor. Among others, it demanded that the investigating agencies must not blame any organisation or community for the acts of terror without any tangible evidences, no arrest should be made without proper warrants and those in police custody should not be tortured to extract confessions.

Heading: HC asks CBI to probe police firing on Etawah students - Indian Express
Content:
Names of three senior state leaders did the rounds in Uttar Pradesh a day after a Nashik court allowed the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) to question a "very very high profile" person from UP in connection with the September 29 Malegaon blast probe.

The ATS is expected to travel to UP to pursue what they say is a key lead but UP Addl DG (Law & Order) Brij Lal said "we are yet to receive any specific information from the ATS if they are on the lookout for a religious leader or any politician".

In Gorakhpur, BJP MP Yogi Adityanath accused the Congress of "framing members of Hindu organisations in false cases" and warned Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil not to try and initiate any action against religious leaders in his Parliamentary constituency in connection with the Malegaon case. He claimed the ATS had no evidence against activists of Hindu organisations arrested for their alleged roles in the blast.

DIG Rajiv Krishna of the UP ATS said: "We are unaware of any permission sought by our Mumbai counterparts from court regarding the questioning of a UP leader. We are in constant touch with officials there and are also providing information they have been seeking. But they (Maharashtra ATS) have not yet told us if any leader has to be interrogated."

Intelligence sources said it was likely that the ATS would turn up in UP only after collecting sufficient evidence to go ahead with questioning of any leader on their radar. The ATS had asked their UP counterparts to provide call details of some with close links to Hindu outfits, the sources said.

Meanwhile, Army chief General Deepak Kapoor has described the alleged involvement of Lt Col Srikant Purohit in the Malegaon blasts as an "aberration".

Speaking to NDTV in Uri in J&K, Gen Kapoor said appropriate disciplinary action will be taken against Purohit if he is found guilty. He promised to take corrective measures to ensure there is no such recurrence in the force.

"Once everything gets proved, as far as the officer is concerned, appropriate disciplinary action will be taken as per the law of the Army," he said. "It (Purohit's involvement) is yet to be proved but it may be an aberration".

Heading: NREGS audit exposes corrupt practices - Indian Express
Content:
The Allahabad High Court has directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to investigate the police firing on students at the Chaudhary Charan Singh PG College in Saifai on January 9.

A student, Mukesh Yadav, was killed and two others sustained serious injuries when the students and Samajwadi Party (SP) supporters resorted to violence during a protest at the college.

They were protesting against the manhandling of SP leaders Shivpal Singh Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav by the police.

A Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court, comprising Justices Imtiaz Murtaza and R M Chauhan, has directed the CBI to submit its report within three months. It will hear the case in the first week of December.

In its order, the judges directed the police officers named in the FIR be transferred immediately from Etawah.

The order was passed after the court heard a writ petition filed by Ram Gopal, an employee of the college, who had moved the court seeking inquiry by an independent agency.

The petitioner had alleged that though the firing had taken place on June 9, the police had registered an FIR only when an order was passed by the magistrate after a few days.

The police in its final report had also tried to protect high-level police officers, he added.

The FIR was lodged against Etawah SSP Siyaram Saran Aditya, ASP Ram Pal Gautam and others.

The court in its order observed: "We are of the view that in order to ensure justice, it is necessary to entrust the matter for investigation to the agency other than the local police which did not appear to have conducted the investigation fairly and properly. In the circumstances, the investigation was ordered to be entrusted to the CBI."

Heading: Bank brings light to rural homes, receives national award - Indian Express
Content:
Barely three days after UP Chief Secretary Atul Kumar Gupta claimed a Central team had denied charges of corruption in the National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS) in the state, a day-long district audit of the programme in Lucknow refuted the claim.

In Mohanlalganj tehsil of the state capital, of 287 job cards made so far under the scheme, only 20 people have been given work in this financial year. Lucknow Chief Development Officer Sanghmitra Shankar noted several anomalies when she visited the Garha, Aslam Nagar and Abbas villages of the tehsil on Tuesday for the district NREGS social audit.

"These villages have a population of over 1,000 in all, but only 287 job cards have been made so far. Another 100 forms are pending with the block development officers for the last two months. The actual number of people who wanted to get the job cards is, however, much higher," Shankar told The Indian Express after the audit.

Interestingly, Shankar also found that although there were a number of works underway like construction of link roads in the three villages, only 20 people were employed in the projects under the NREGS, while others were working on contract.

"We had approved the list of a large number of developmental projects for Mohanlalganj amounting to Rs 27 lakh under the NREGS for this fiscal year. But, only Rs 46,000 has been used so far. The number of people given work under the scheme was shockingly low," she said.

The Gram Rozgar Sewak, who is responsible for ensuring and monitoring work under the scheme, the gram pradhans and the block development officers were warned of strict action.

"We will conduct such audits regularly and people can also come straight to our offices with their complaints and grievances," said Shankar.

Heading: Religious groups stake claims on Ganga - Indian Express
Content:
Over 3,500 families in villages now continue their daily chores after dusk. Jyoti Scheme, a programme to bring solar power to households, launched by the Prathama Bank has brought light and hope to their homes.

The Moradabad-based bank bagged the national award (North Zone) for promoting and financing solar lighting systems and installing over 150 solar panels in Lalatikar and Karnapur villages of the district.

Two managers of the bank — A K Verma and Rajendra Singh — received the newly-instituted award.

The award was set up by the Solar Finance Capacity Building Alliance, comprising the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), Delhi-based Winrock International India, Syndicate Bank, Centre for Technology Development and the Bharatiya Vikas Trust.

The award aimed to recognise bank managers, who promote solar energy to their customers.

The alliance has trained over 7,000 bank officials on financing solar systems, besides imparting technical training to 600 youths for installing and maintaining the systems at villages in 15 states.

The Prathama Bank offers loans to villagers for buying a solar lighting system worth Rs 14,000.

The loan amounting to Rs 13,000, runs for seven years and is offered at an interest rate of 9 per cent.

"We have always focused on non-mainstream locations like villages, which require innovative microcredit solutions. Over 90 per cent of our 19 lakh customers are villagers," said G C Mishra, Chairman, Prathama Bank.

The bank expects the number of solar energy-powered homes to touch 8,000 by March, 2009.

Prem Vrat, Vice-Chancellor of the UP Technical University, said economical and effective solutions should be provided to Indian consumers to increase awareness about solar energy.

"One sixth of the world's population lives in India. Renewable energy must be given a high priority for their energy requirements," he said.

Stressing on the need for a holistic approach, he said, "Solar appliances for homes can help a household become energy-independent."

Noting that solar panels are yet to catch up with consumers, Amit Kumar, deputy general manager at Tata BP Solar, said: " Corporate sector must invest in manufacturing solar equipment."

Heading: State to host Children Parliament on Nov 20 - Indian Express
Content:
A week since Ganga was accorded the national heritage status, a tug of war has erupted between religious leaders over who should take the credit for for it.

Yoga guru Baba Ram Dev has been accused of highjacking the river agenda. "Ram Dev does not have time for the river. He wanted a pollution free Ganga only in UP, whereas we do not want any pollution in the river from Gangotri to Ganga Sagar," said Dwarkapeethadhishwar Jagadguru Sankaracharya Swami Swaroopanand Saraswati, who also heads the Ganga Seva Abhiyan (GSA).

On November 5, Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) president Ashok Singhal had claimed that credit for the national heritage status for the Ganga should go to Ram Dev, who had sat on a dharna demanding the status for the river.

The Sankaracharya, however, sought to refute Singhal's claim and said getting the status for the river was a goal of the GSA. He said: "Several scientists and experts accompanied me in a meeting with the Prime Minister on October 16, wherein we asked him to preserve the sanctity of the river." He added, "Subsequently, the Prime Minister announced the the status of national heritage for Ganga on November 4."

Notably, while the VHP is a right wing organisation, the Sankaracharya is reportedly close to the top leadership of the Congress.

The Sankaracharya also announced that ten members of GSA will soon take out a bicycle rally from Varanasi to Rameshwaram. After that, another rally will begin from Lucknow on December 6, reaching Delhi on March 15 to spread awareness about the river.

He also announced that the GSA will offer a 2,250-km long chunri to the river on the occasion of Ganga Dussera next year.

The chunri will be made by joining 5 lakh saris, which the GSA members will collect from devotees across the country.

Heading: Coach factory: ‘Begin work but with conditions’ - Indian Express
Content:
On the lines of Bihar, Uttar Pradesh is all set to host a 'Children Parliament' this year. The first such parliament will take place in the state capital on November 20, which will also mark the Universal Child Rights Day.

Social organisations and volunteers working for child welfare across the state have been invited by the UNICEF. Nearly 200 children, including poor children, child prostitutes and rescued child labourers, will participate in the Children Parliament.

The programme aims to raise issues related to child protection and development in the state.

"From now on, the event will be organised on November 20 every year. In the years to come, we will make it more organised and democratic. In this year, we have decided that while there will be around 200 participants, 60 children will actually initiate discussion over various issues," said Augustine Veliath, Communication Head at UNICEF, Lucknow. He said: "These 60 children will be divided into 10 groups on different issues and each group will nominate a person, who will move the motion on that particular issue."

The organisers are in touch with senior officials of the state government to invite Speaker of the state Assembly for the occasion. "There has been no assurance as of now. Even if he is unable to make it to the parliament, we will try that representatives of the Children Parliament can call upon him and tell him what all has been discussed in their parliament. Later, we plan to place these issues in front of a state legislative committee," Veliath said.

Informing about the need to have such parliament in the state, Shachi Singh, who has been working for the rights of the poor children, said: "Child protection issues remain neglected in the state. There is no child protection policy, no child right commission or an action plan for the children in the state."

She added, "We believe that this parliament will force the government to take issues of children." The participating children will arrive at the venue on November 18. They will be trained on various issues for two days.

Heading: Woman shot at over property dispute - Indian Express
Content:
The Railway Ministry moved a plea before the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court on Tuesday that the court allows the ministry to begin construction on the rail coach factory site in Rae Bareli. In its interim order earlier, the court had ordered a status quo over the land.

The court admitted the plea with a condition that the construction can begin only after the ministry completes all the formalities for executing the lease deed of the land as per the directives of the state government.

The court asked the Railways to complete the formalities within next two weeks.

Dr Ashok Nigam, the Additional Solicitor General and the counsel of the Railways, said, "We have informed the court that the Centre had paid the entire price for the land on market rate, when lease of the land was granted. Since the money is still with the state government, no further amount is to be paid now." The court has fixed the next hearing on November 26.

Heading: Man ‘kills’ daughter, wife in Kanpur - Indian Express
Content:
The brother-in-law of a woman was arrested after she was shot dead over an alleged property dispute in Pakbada area of Moradabad on Tuesday.

Additional Superintendent of Police (City), S C Baghel said, "The incident was reported around 5.30 am. An unidentified person knocked at the door of Bhagmati (35). When she opened it, the assailant shot at her." He added, her husband Harikesh was away and she was alone in the house with her six-year-old son.

Baghel said they have detained Harikesh's brother Gauri Shanker, as the deceased recently had a tiff with him over some property. The family had sold a piece of land a few days ago, after which Harikesh, Gauri Shanker and their mother had a dispute over sharing the sale amount of Rs 4.5 lakh.

Bhagmati had objected when the the mother had decided to give her share to Gauri Shanker.

In another case, a resident of Saipura village lodged an FIR Tuesday morning at the Tanda police station alleging gangrape by one Mohammad Saeed, his nephew Khalil and an unidentified youth. The accused barged into her house when she was alone last night and raped her, she alleged.

Rampur ASP Dayaram Saroj said primary investigations revealed that all the accused were in Almora on Monday night. The woman had a dispute with Saeed, which was pending for a year.

Saeed and his son had sold a house in Kashipur, Uttarakhand to her husband last year but they were yet to give her the possession of the house, said the ASP.

This had led to altercations between the two groups several times earlier and Khalil was also sent to jail in one such dispute, added Saroj.

Heading: Atiq’s cousin surrenders, remanded to judicial custody - Indian Express
Content:
Accused term the deaths as suicides

A man, who allegedly poisoned his wife Alpana (28) and seven-year-old daughter Gauri late on Monday night, was arrested on Tuesday.

Following a complaint made by Alpana's brother Hari Om Sharma, a case of murder was registered against the accused, Shyam Kishore Sharma, with the Naubasta police station on Tuesday.

On Monday morning, the bodies of Alpana and Gauri were recovered from their Hanumant Vihar residence. Though at first Sharma termed the deaths as suicides, he failed to reply convincingly why his wife and daughter had committed suicide.

Govind Nagar Circle Officer Surendra Nath Tiwari said: "Prima facie it appears that the two were poisoned as the bodies had turned dark blue. We have sent their bodies for postmortem."

Hari Om, a resident of Jalaun, told mediapersons: "Alpana had married Sharma around 10 years ago. On several occasions, he had demanded dowry from my family." Whenever the family failed to meet the demand, Sharma used to beat up Alpana, he alleged. "In the wake of repeated dowry demands, we had registered a case against Sharma in Jalaun district court a few months ago," he said. Three months ago, Sharma had apologised to Alpana's family and the case against him was withdrawn.

According to Hari Om, heated arguments took place between Alpana and Sharma over the dowry issue in the last few weeks.

"I was shocked when Sharma called me up on Tuesday and said Alpana and Gauri had committed suicide," said Hari Om.

Sharma, however, had a different take. An employee in a paint factory of Dassukunwa area, he said: "After dinner on Monday night, I went to my brother's place in the Gangapur area." When he came back on Tuesday morning, he found both Alpana and Gauri dead, he claimed.

Superintendent of Police (Kanpur West), Dayanand Mishra, said Alpana was Sharma's second wife. "His first wife Uma had died over 10 years ago. We are interrogating his neighbours and relatives for more information," he said.

Heading: Six gangmen run over by Sarnath Express - Indian Express
Content:
Jailed MP Atiq Ahmad's cousin Hamza Usman surrendered in the gangsters court on Tuesday in connection with two cases pending against him. He was booked under the Gangsters Act for initiating violence in the Kareli area and for intimidating people in the Shivkuti area.

Usman, who was declared an absconder a few months ago, was carrying a cash reward of Rs 20,000. A proposal to increase the reward up to 50,000 was pending with the office of Director General of Police Vikram Singh.

The district police have registered 16 cases of henious crimes including murder, extortion and intimidation against him.

On Tuesday, Usman surrendered in the court of special judge (Gangsters Act) M P Yadav. He was remanded to judicial custody.

The jail authorities have been instructed to provide him special security cover, when he will be taken to the court for hearing.

According to sources, the district police had information that Usman and Atiq Ahmed's younger brother Khalid Azim alias Ashraf were in the city and wanted to surrender in the court.

Senior Superintendent of Police A M Jain, however, claimed the police did not have any information regarding Usman's whereabouts. "The police will seek the court's permission for Usman's police remand," he added. A source in the police department claimed Ashraf will surrender in the court within a week.

Heading: Cross-Border Muse - Indian Express
Content:
Designer Aki Narula on dressing up the hunks in Tarun Mansukhani's Dostana

Life is supposedly one long party when you're based in Miami. Aki Narula, however, discovered that life on pristine beaches can also mean a lot of hard work. The designer, who has dressed up actors John Abraham, Abhishek Bachchan, Bobby Deol and a handful of others (only Priyanka Chopra's costumes have been done by Manish Malhotra) for Tarun Mansukhani's film Dostana that releases this Friday, got his brief for the film approved in half an hour, when he met the director and producer Karan Johar in Mumbai last November. But when he landed in Miami for a recce in early January, he knew he was in for a mad ride. "There's a very Cuban, Mexican feel to Miami, particularly with its cosmopolitan crowd, its white sands and clear blue skies. Since the characters in the film are based there, imbibing the local culture was important. Translating that mood to clothes was quite a task," he says.

In the movie, Abraham plays a fashion photographer and Bachchan a male nurse, while Bobby Deol is an urban sophisticate. So while Deol goes around in more formal clothing— slim Louis Vuitton suits and Dolce Gabbana jackets, the other two have a more casual style. "Choosing clothes for John was easy. He's in shorts for most of the movie and all you ladies are in for a treat with his toned body on display," smiles Aki. "I gave him a lot of tees with social messages on them. I made Abhishek wear all sorts of bright colours, from oranges to greens to reds and pinks with low-waisted jeans and cargo pants," says Narula, who has been styling for Bachchan junior since his Bunty Aur Babli days. In fact, Narula experimented a fair bit with Bachchan's outfit, apart from making him wear colour. "Even though this movie is aimed for an urban crowd, I always believe that a trend should be able to cut across masses, like the shirt kurtis in Bunty Aur Babli that became such a rage after the movie. Most of the shirts that Abhishek wears in Dostana have collars that are 30 inches long, and reach his knees. A friend of mine was telling me he has already seen replicas on Carter Road!" says Narula. Shooting was a whole lot of fun too. "John would be ready in a jiffy while the other two took their time getting dressed for the shot. So John would laugh his head off all the while and irritate them," he grins. Post Dostana, Narula's appointment diary is choc-a-bloc with assignments. Up next is Aditya Chopra's Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi, and Renzil D' silva's debut film with Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor and Viveik Oberoi. He is also doing the costumes for Kareena Kapoor for her next project, Kambaqt Ishq. For now though, look out for the dandies.
