Heading: A big bite - Indian Express
Content:
Children's Day lineup or gifting season, retailer shelves are dressed with cool gadgets for young fingers

Dealing with a precocious child could need a special kind of fortitude for many. But a simple solution would be to hand over your TV remote to them or simply let them run their hands over your laptop. This generation, after all, is not about stuffed toys and building blocks but X-boxes and hi-tech gadgets that have caught the imagination of tiny tots. Toy manufacturers seem to have caught on to this trend quickly as the plethora of gadgets in the market testify.

"Convergence is the way forward. Children must be exposed to gadgets very early in life. If they are technologically comfortable at an early age, then handling difficult devices or gadgets in future becomes easy," says Atindriya Bose, country manager, Sony Computer Entertainment who launched Playstation3000 series last week, a device that has special games for children based on spellings and music. For those who want to burn a smaller hole in their pocket can opt for an Xbox 360 console instead. There is a fascination and admiration for technology from a very young age, making hi-tech gadgets the gift of choice for most children. "But one must make sure that these gadgets have educational value in them too," says Bose.

From creating greeting cards to flying airplanes, the Digital Arts and Crafts Studio created by Fisher Price especially for pre-schoolers makes sure your kids have fun while helping them learn. "The range has been designed to get children to learn, using their creativity to the fullest and ensure the overall development of little ones, while they are getting entertained," says Rahul Bhowmik, marketing head, Mattel Toys, India.

Value for Money
* Playstation 3000 series - Rs 39,000/-
* Digital Arts and Crafts Studio - Rs 2,999/-
* Computer Cool School - Rs 2,999/-
* All-in-one Learning Desk- Rs 3,999/-
* Disney Mix Stick MP3 - Rs 1,800/-
* Funky Beats Keyboard - Rs 2,870/-

Heading: Neighbour held, cops point to ‘love angle’ - Indian Express
Content:
It turns out there's nothing a Mac can't do. Rolling Stone magazine joined hands with Reliance Digital's iStore on Monday to host a workshop on using Apple software to create music. Loy Mendonsa—of the Shankar, Ehsaan and Loy trio—known for spinning magic on the synthesiser, demonstrated the uses of Apple's 'Garage Band' to an audience comprising of the likes of Luke Kenny, Ehsaan Noorani, Gary Lawyer, Uday Benegal, Punjabi rapper Hard Kaur and several young, amateur musicians who interacted with Loy and his son Shane. Editor Radhakrishnan Nair looked evidently pleased with the whole event.

Showstopper The demonstration is part of a series organised by 'Amplify Your Music', Rolling Stone's initiative to encourage interactions between professional and amateur musicians.

Heading: Flying high: City girl bags gold in national event - Indian Express
Content:
Sneh Lata murder: Police say Lucky liked her elder sister who married someone else

The police said that a youth from the neighbourhood has allegedly murdered 13-year-old Sneh Lata in the Postal and Telegraph (P & T) Colony near Tagore Nagar on Sunday afternoon. The police added that the lovelorn youth, Lucky Rajput, was romantically interested in the deceased's elder sister. The police claim that the Lucky also wanted to kill Sneh Lata's elder sister.

Lucky was arrested today from the Rajpura chowk near the DMC hospital.

The police said that in his preliminary interrogation, Lucky had confessed that he used to love Sneh Lata's elder sister but she was unaware about his feelings. As Sneh Lata's elder sister got married elsewhere, Lucky felt dejected and out of frustation murdered Sneh Lata, the police said.

The police said that Lucky had also confessed that he had plans to kill Sneh Lata's elder sister as well.

Ever since Sneh Lata's murder, the police were suspecting the involvement of an acquaintance in the crime as there were no signs of forced entry into the house. Sneh Lata was found dead on Sunday afternoon when she was alone in her house.

Heading: ‘Spooky’ affair: akhand path on Nov 13 to ward off phantom of the PAU hostel - Indian Express
Content:
A girl has brought laurels to the city. Meet Jaspreet Kaur, who has become the first woman NCC (flying wing) cadet from the Directorate of Punjab, Haryana, Himachal-Pardesh and Chandigarh to win a gold medal in flying. A final-year student of B Sc at S C D Government College for Boys, she was awarded the gold medal in the 'microlight flying' category during the 'All India Vayu Sainik Camp' held at Bangalore recently.

Sahnewal Airfield Chief Gliding Instructor Captain Charanjeet Singh said, "Her win has elevated our directorate to the fourth position out of 17 directorates in the country. She also scored 100 per cent marks in the written examination. More than 60 cadets across the country participated in the event."

Sharing her success Jaspreet said, "Wing Commander Pardeep Bishnoi, the Commanding Officer of 4 Punjab Air Squadron NCC in Ludhiana, not only guided me but also motivated me to attend the camp. I thank God for rewarding me for my hard work. I have 12 hours of flying experience in a two-seater aircraft."

Wing Commander Bishnoi said, "Having won the gold medal, she will get a chance to fly in the fly past ceremony on the Republic Day in New Delhi." Sky is not the limit for this achiever as she will soon start solo flying with her instructor Wg Cdr Bishnoi. She said, "I will achieve it within the next two months."

Ask her what made her join this field, she beams and says, "I saw a letter on the college notice board about NCC air wing. I decided not to leave this opportunity as earlier I had brought forms of the National Defence Academy after passing my Class XII, but my parents did not allow me to take the exam.

A voracious reader and a couch potato, Jaspreet's father Gurcharan Singh serves in a sugar mill and mother Joginder Kaur is a homemaker. Her only elder brother is settled in England. A product of R S Model School, she aims to join the defence services, "I want to join defence services through the Short Service Commission. After my graduation I will prepare for SSC exam the next year."

Heading: Dr Sofat sent to police custody till Nov 14 - Indian Express
Content:
Though Punjab Agricultural University is known for using scientific practices, it is the ghost tales that are giving sleepless nights to students. While phantom sagas are common for any hostel, the university is grappling with one such issue which has become both a matter of concern and mirth on the campus.

These days the students of hostel number seven and the employees of the university serving in the hostel are busy getting rid of the ghost. They claim they have a reason to believe in such a tale as a couple of years ago a student committed suicide in the hostel by hanging himself from the ceiling fan.

To ensure a peaceful co-existence with the spooky resident, the hostellers have organised an akhand path from November 13 to November 15. While students claim that the path is being organised to observe the birthday anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev that falls on November 13, insiders say the trouble has been taken to ward off the spirit.

Hosteller Kamalbir Singh said, "The hostel guard on the night duty has refused to man the hostel in the night. The guard claims to have seen a young boy in a white kurta pyjama and a green turban roaming about on the campus at night."

Notable here is that hostel residents claim to have seen the ghost of Gobind Singh Bhatti, a postgraduate student who committed suicide around three years ago. Though the batchmates of Bhatti have finished their degrees and left the campus, the room in which he had committed suicidestill remains unoccupied.

Mitterman Singh, another postgraduate student, said, "The entire Bhatti story came out when new students in the hostel reopened the room to hold Ganesh Puja."

While hostellers are scared of the 'ghost', Bhatti's friends are not taking this issue very kindly. Charanjit Singh, one of his friends, said, "Bhatti was such a nice guy and had never troubled any one even in his lifetime. We still can not understand why he committed suicide. Even if ghosts exist, Bhatti's ghost can never trouble anyone."

Heading: Shaukat Ali: Singing parallel to pop singers gives me jitters - Indian Express
Content:
DR Sumit Sofat, who was arrested yesterday in a land forgery case by the Economic Offences Wing (EOW) of the Ludhiana police, was today sent in the police custody by a local court till November 14.

The police produced Dr Sofat in the court of Judicial Magistrate Jagdeep Sood and sought his police remand saying that they had to further question him in the case. Accepting the plea of the police, the court sent Dr Sofat in police remand for three days.

The EOW wing in-charge Inspector Jaswinder Singh Mangat told Newsline, "We have to question Dr Sofat to know who others were involved with him in the conspiracy that he had hatched to frame complainant Ramesh Kumar Pashan in the alleged kidnapping and murder of his (Dr Sofat's) servant's murder. We also want to know that who had helped him in preparing the fake documents."

A leading city doctor, Dr Sumit Sofat was arrested on Monday evening after his anticipatory bail plea was turned down by the court.

The case was registered against Dr Sofat on October 17 this year. In 2000, Dr Sofat had purchased a 1,200-square yard plot on the Ferozepur Road from Pashan for Rs 70 lakh. But Dr Sofat did not get the land registered in his name saying that he was under the scanner of the Income Tax Department. The seller then cancelled Dr Sofat's power of attorney. In 2004, a settlement was brokered between the parties under which Dr Sofat sold the plot back to Pashan. But when Dr Sofat came to know that Pashan had sold it further for a hefty amount, he got the plot registered in his name using a fake power of attorney, sources said.

Heading: Customers’ meet kicks off at IOB - Indian Express
Content:
Kiyon dur  duo rehende o mere kohlon, mainu dass deo hoea ki kassor mere kohlon or the kaddin taan has bol venaa jind saadi rol ve — the voice that made these and many other immemorial songs finds himself a misfit in the age of pop.

Legendary singer Shaukat Ali Khan who hails from Punjab in Pakistan gets the jitters when he has to perform on stage. "My heart begins to beat very fast and at times I feel as if this is not the place for me. But then the love of my fans and with the grace of God and my mother, it is very heartening to see that there is still an audience for classical, pure folk and songs that pass through generations to become a part of our lives."

A fan of the legendary Mohammad Rafi, Surinder Shinda, Harbhajan Maan and an ardent admirer of another living legend Kuldeep Manak, Shuakat is in town to give another scintillating performance. The singer is currently touring the state and performed at the Kapurthala heritage festival along with his younger son Mohasan Abbas.

"People may listen to 'Gadde te chardi' type of songs but even today they want to listen to Heer, Challa and other timeless songs. Though I have sung every genre of music including Sufi, folk, filmi, over the years I have learnt that both Punjabs share a strong bond with sur, pain, Partition and this pain gives birth to songs that when sung bring tears to the eyes of a listener," adds the singer.

A living legend with no starry tantrums, he has only one advice for budding singers, "Good singing in its purest form is something that we need to incorporate in the present times. Music brings peace and helps heal broken hearts." He adds, "People should not stop reading. Read books and learn more about what is happening around the world. Even today such beautiful poetry is being written," sums up the singer.

Heading: Capt given more time for inspection of case file - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Overseas Bank (IOB) is observing `Customer fortnight' throughout the country from November 10 to 22. In this connection, the Ludhiana region held a customer-meet at Dhoda restaurant, Civil Lines, in which customers from different segments and fields participated to share their views about the services being rendered by the city branches of IOB.

A large number of customers participated in the meeting. Chief regional manager, V. K. Gupta presided over the meeting. He highlighted various features of bank's products and E-see banking and requested the customers to make best use of these friendly customized products.

Heading: Nursing college principal felicitated - Indian Express
Content:
District and Session judge G.K. Rai today accepted the applications filed by former Punjab Chief Minister Capt Amarinder Singh and other co-accused seeking more time for the inspection of case file before hearing the arguments on framing of charges in the alleged multi-crore City Centre scam.

After hearing the arguments of both sides, Justice G K Rai allowed the applications and directed the defence counsel of former Punjab Chief Minister, Capt Amarinder Singh and other co-accused to complete the inspection of the documents along with the challan till December 13. The judge has also changed the date of hearing, which is November 15, and fixed December 13 as next date of the hearing.

On September 27, the previous date of hearing, Justice G.K. Rai had directed the defence counsels of former Punjab Chief Minister, Capt Amarinder Singh and other co-accused to complete inspection of the documents along with the challan till September 8 and also fixed November 15 for consideration for framing the charge against Capt Amarinder Singh and the other accused, but the defence counsels had failed to complete the inspection of the documents and filed an application before the judge.

Justifying his demand for more time, Capt Amarinder Singh's counsel, Trilok Singh Sood submitted before the judge that the inspection work could not be completed due to the voluminous record produced by the bureau. It was the right of an accused to inspect the file and get all documents produced by the prosecution on record.

On the other hand, District Attorney, Mitter Sen Goyal strongly opposed the application filed by Capt Amarinder Singh and other co-accused and stated that the defence was only attempting to delay the proceedings in the case.

Heading: Freshers accorded welcome at RIMT - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Jasbir Kaur, Principal, College of Nursing, DMCH, has been awarded the Centenary Award for her commitment and passionate dedication toward growth of nursing in India and her efforts in promoting nursing education and research.

Former President of India, Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam at function held at Sri Shanmukhananda auditorium, Sion, Mumbia, on occasion of Centenary Conference of Trained Nurses' Association of India felicitated this award to Dr Jasibir Kaur on November 4.

Dr Kaur, a recipient of Mother Teresa award by Omini College, Canada, has signed a partnership with University of British Columbia, B.C., Vancouver, Canada to foster the development of international standards of nursing in Punjab.

She has held various positions at the state-level Trained Nurses Association of India (TNAI). At present, she is vice-president of TNAI, Punjab state, and vice-president of North Zone Indian Society of Psychiatric Nurses. Her active participation in TNAI national conferences brought her gold and silver medals and plaques.

Heading: District-level science exhibition gets underway - Indian Express
Content:
A grand welcome party was jointly organised at RIMT-IMCT campus by all the senior classes of RIMT-Institute of Management & Computer Technology and Gobindgarh Institute of Management and Technology, Mandi Gobindgarh.

In this programme, a large number of BBA, BCA, MBA, MCA, M.Sc, and PGDCA students took part. Noted industrialist and philanthropist Hukam Chand Bansal, the chairman of RIMT group of educational institutes, who was the chief guest on the occasion inaugurated the function by lightening the lamp.

Neena Bansal, the co-chairperson of the trust, was the guest of honour. Bansal, while welcoming the freshers, wished them a great future as professionals in this burgeoning economy. The chief director, Dr B.S. Bhatia, the director general of institute, assured the students his full support.

Rahul Sharma, a senior student of MBA, welcomed the freshers on the behalf of all the seniors. Attired in best of their dresses, the students also presented a lively cultural programme on the occasion. The various foot-tapping group dances were presented by Gurvinder and Group, Sandeep and

Group and Hitesh and Group. Whereas Ishan (BBA), Sandeep and Sunaxi presented melodious solo songs.

Meenal of MCA and Salil Soshi of PGDCA were selected Ms Fresher and Mr Fresher, respectively while the titles of Ms Gorgeous and Mr Handsome went to Neha (MBA) and Manish Sahi (MBA), respectively.

Prominent among those present on the occasion were the director of the RIMT-IMCT, Dr S.P. Singh, the director of RIMT-SMS, Dr Surinder Singh, principal of RIMT Institute, Prof S.N. Panda, Media Advisor Prof Gurvinder Bakshi, Prof N.K. Maheshwary and Prof Ranjeev Chopra. The programme ended with the rendering of the national anthem.

Heading: Become job-creators, PAU V-C tells students - Indian Express
Content:
The three-day long district level science exhibition on the theme "Science and technology for global sustainability" kicked off at BCM Arya Model Senior Secondary School, Shastri Nagar, here on Tuesday.

Students and budding scientists of various schools put on display a rich collection of chart models (working and non-working) as well as posters on various sub-themes.

A wide array of activities viz poster and chart making, science quiz, science drama, teaching aid competition and extempore was organised with a view to provide opportunity to all participating students and teachers to get acquainted with different kind of equipment, devices and techniques of science and to explore and motivate scientific and technological talent among the students.

Pradeep Kapoor, District Science Supervisor, Ludhiana, inaugurated the exhibition.

Students were at ease to explain the application of scientific principles. A number of models viz. terofilter, sale housing structures, flood prevention measures, vertical farming, rain drain and water harvesting, circular stadium with magical stairs and laser leveller attracted maximum eyeballs. Students, mindful of the fact that the best exhibit will find its way to the state-level science exhibition to be held shortly, vied with each other in displaying their talent.

Heading: Vet varsity holds essay contest - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Agricultural University celebrated the National Education Day, to mark the birthday of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, by holding a series of activities on the campus on Tuesday.

Different colleges and departments displayed slogans on the importance of education. A list of 10 approved slogans was circulated among different quarters. The slogans were put up in the library, VC's committee room, Centre for Communication and International Linkages, departments of Forestry and Natural Resources, Department of Plant Pathology, Students' Home, etc.

Three lectures were organized at different places in the university.

Dr Parm Randhawa, from USA delivered a talk on "Agriculture and private practices" in the committee room of the Vice-Chancellor. "Enormous opportunities exist provided there is a will and vision to excel," said Dr Randhawa while elaborating on the theme of his talk. He traced his success story from a garage to modern laboratory for pathogen detection, seed health testing, genetic testing disease diagnostic service commercially.

Dr Randhawa said that seed testing and field inspection (pre-harvest and harvest inspection) held immense opportunities for hard working and visionary plant pathologists. He suggested to students to commercially exploit their talent by constituting inter-disciplinary custom groups.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Manjit Singh Kang, Vice-Chancellor, PAU said that the students should aspire to be job creators rather than being the job seekers. He said that with a vision and expertise one could do wonders in one's profession saying that he himself had visited the excellent laboratory developed by Dr Param Randhawa.

Dr. Serge Savary, Plant Pathologist from International Rice Research Institute, gave a talk on 'Effect of climate change on plant diseases' to the faculty and students from different departments. Dr Savary said that ground temperature at soil level was increasing while snow cover was decreasing with every passing year. He said that drought was seizing more areas under increased temperature, adding that agriculture depended on water in South-East Asia where rainfall reception was scarce.

Rice is a good case for studying the impact of climate change on crop disease scenario, said Dr Savary. He said that Plant Pathology has a role to play in adaptation and mitigation, anticipation and containment of pathogens for which good techniques and tools were needed to be developed.

On this occasion, Dr Mann said that under the changing scenario of climatic factors a pro-active approach was needed and highlighted the importance of network approach for distilling simulation models based on the data available. Crop improvement programme with respect to tolerance for leaf spots, non-specific pathogens would be required in view of their increasing trend, said she.

Dr Jagtar Singh Dhiman, Additional Director of Communication, while proposing a vote of thanks to the speaker said that global warming was a world-wide issue, for which a concerted sustainable plant protection approach through information and communication technology would help.

In yet another lecture held at the College of Basic Sciences, eminent geneticist from Vienna, Austria, Dr B.S. Ahluwalia dwelled on 'Invasion of genes: our genetic heritage'. He gave a perspective as to how mixing of genes had occurred since the beginning of civilization. 'Civilizations die, but genes do not', he said. Dr Ahluwalia said that every invasion that took place brought with it the mixing of genes. The faculty members of the college and students participated in the deliberations and interacted with the speaker.

Heading: God save Queen - Indian Express
Content:
Children's Day lineup or gifting season, retailer shelves are dressed with cool gadgets for young fingers

Dealing with a precocious child could need a special kind of fortitude for many. But a simple solution would be to hand over your TV remote to them or simply let them run their hands over your laptop. This generation, after all, is not about stuffed toys and building blocks but X-boxes and hi-tech gadgets that have caught the imagination of tiny tots. Toy manufacturers seem to have caught on to this trend quickly as the plethora of gadgets in the market testify.

"Convergence is the way forward. Children must be exposed to gadgets very early in life. If they are technologically comfortable at an early age, then handling difficult devices or gadgets in future becomes easy," says Atindriya Bose, country manager, Sony Computer Entertainment who launched Playstation3000 series last week, a device that has special games for children based on spellings and music. For those who want to burn a smaller hole in their pocket can opt for an Xbox 360 console instead.

There is a fascination and admiration for technology from a very young age, making hi-tech gadgets the gift of choice for most children. "But one must make sure that these gadgets have educational value in them too," says Bose.

From creating greeting cards to flying airplanes, the Digital Arts and Crafts Studio created by Fisher Price especially for pre-schoolers makes sure your kids have fun while helping them learn. "The range has been designed to get children to learn, using their creativity to the fullest and ensure the overall development of little ones, while they are getting entertained," says Rahul Bhowmik, marketing head, Mattel Toys, India. Priced between Rs 2,000-3,000, the collection is also inclusive of Computer Cool School with CD-ROM software, keyboard, writing tablet and stylus for left or right-handed children and All-in-one Learning Desk where your child will learn school-ready skills like letters, numbers, counting, phonics, vocabulary and writing. "The desk has spaces to put regular paper, markers and crayons which help the child tidy up the room," says Bhowmik.

While gadgets these days are mainly designed to encourage educational activities, Disney proves that you're never too young to have an MP3 player with the introduction of the Disney Mix Stick digital audio player. And not just this, for kids who have a penchant for music, ELC Toys introduces the Funky Beats Keyboard with pre-recorded demo songs, rhythm and drum sounds and a microphone. "You can even record your performances and dance to your own music when you play it back," says Prema Saldanha, mother of a four-year-old.

If your tiny tot is not into action toys or computers, there are lots of other gadgets like skincare devices, body massagers, flip-top mobile phones, fancy stationary and even a battery operated eyelash curler that range from Rs 30-300. Available at Heera Panna at Mahalaxmi and Alpha at Andheri, these are among the new entrants. "While the need for gadgets cannot be undermined, one must be sure about what goes into the hands of their children," cautions Bhowmik.

Value for Money

* Digital Arts and Crafts Studio - Rs 2,999/-
* Computer Cool School - Rs 2,999/-
* All-in-one Learning Desk- Rs 3,999/-
* Disney Mix Stick MP3 - Rs 1,800/-
* Funky Beats Keyboard - Rs 2,870/-

Heading: Real estate giant to sell off 4.5mn sq ft - Indian Express
Content:
Queen's biggest and most flamboyant USP, apro Parsi boy, Freddie Mercury is legend. The tights-wearing singer was known not just for his on-stage theatrics, but also for his ability to write sure-fire hits and his distinctive tenor voice and formidable powers of projection. His death at the age of 45, from HIV-related complications, and his band's subsequent inability to produce anything of note only served to underscore what everyone was already convinced of—Queen without Freddie was rudderless.

Enter Paul Rodgers, he of Free and Bad Company fame and a legend in his own right. The vocalist, in what is surely an act of bravery, has stepped into Mercury's rather large shoes to collaborate with Queen survivors, Brian May and Roger Taylor, to produce The Cosmos Rocks. This is Queen's first studio album in 13 years and expectations from the band as well as Rodgers are high.

Let's get one point out of the way, first. Rodgers is not a Mercury replacement. This is proved by the fact that he's actively collaborated with May and Taylor in the studio, lending not just his voice, but also his song-writing abilities and his skills at the bass. But one still wonders what Mercury would've done with the songs? All the tracks on the album hark back to classic rock and have a very 'live record' feel to them. But they lack the accessibility and cheerful campiness of Queen anthems, like Radio Ga Ga and I Want to Break Free. Part of it has to do with the vocals. Rodgers has a more gravely voice than Mercury, which lends itself splendidly to rock, but the pop vibes that made Queen a legend could've been achieved only by Mercury. The latter's vocal somersaults and incorporation of wide choral effects paved the way for pop-rock with hits like the baroque classic Bohemian Rhapsody.

As it happens, it's the more 'rock' songs that work really well, notably Cosmos Rockin' and Time to Shine. C-lebrity, the first single to be released from this collection, pokes fun at tabloid culture and this is where Rodgers sounds in his element. Some Things that Glitter sounds good, but one feels that more could've been made of it if only some of Mercury's drama had been incorporated here. The real duds of the album are Call Me, which sounds a lot like Crazy Little Thing Called Love, without the pop appeal of the latter, and We Believe, which sounds like a fluffier and emptier version of We Are the Champions.

This is not an album for classic Queen fans. The lack of vocal theatrics and few grandiloquent flourishes in the musical arrangement are enough to cause heartbreak. This isn't Queen. It's Queen + Paul Rodgers.

The Cosmos Rocks
Rs 350

Heading: Approvers from IM willing and welcome but not vital, say police - Indian Express
Content:
Realty bites: Sale of plots in Kurla, Andheri, Malabar reflects market crunch, say analysts

In a sign of the times, the country's third largest real estate player, Housing Development and Infrastructure Limited (HDIL), has offered to sell off three of its plots totalling about 4.5 million square feet.

Analysts say the rare move shows the extent of liquidity crunch in the realty market where no developer normally takes the extreme step of off-loading valuable land stock.

The plots along with their potential Floor Space Index amounts to 1.5 million sq ft saleable land at Andheri, 2.5 million sq ft at Kurla and 63,000 sq ft at Carmichael Road in the upmarket Malabar hill area. At present, the Carmichael Road plot houses a bungalow.

The Kurla plot is a portion of the 53 acre land acquired by HDIL to rehabilitate 20,000 of the 85,000 slum-dwellers' families, in Phase I of the massive Mumbai Airport Slum Rehabilitation project.

Earlier this year, HDIL had raised money through debts to purchase the Premier Automobiles Kurla land from an IFLS affiliate at Rs 1,900 crore.

The current debt of the listed real estate company, which is also one of the largest landowners in Mumbai, stands at over Rs 3,000 crore.

Sarang Wadhwan, HDIL managing director, brushed aside any co-relation between the debt and the proposed land sale. "It's just a business move where we are planning to offload some land as a means of revenue. We are trying to raise money for the airport land rehabilitation. At present, work is on as per schedule at 125 of the 190 buildings," he said.

Wadhwan refused to comment on how much money he expected to raise from the land sales. On whether the land would have any takers in the present market, he said, "The market is seeing a correction and there will definitely be no problem in getting buyers."

Realty analysts state that HDIL's move is just the tip of the iceberg in the real estate industry which has been aggressively acquiring land over the past few years. According to Akshaye Kumar, CEO of Parklane Property Consultants, over the last few months, a significant number of developers have put up a few sites on their portfolio for sale. "Historically, developers never sell land. Even when the previous real estate crash happened, there was only an odd developer who put up his land for sale. But this time, considering the asset-rich cash-strapped scenario, such a step might be unusual but not surprising," said Kumar.

Amol Shimpi, national director for land sales at Colliers International, added, "Developers would not have done this during normal times. But with the tight cash flow, developers have more stock than they can build. A few have recently approached us to put up their land for sale; several others are expected to follow suit."

Heading: Killer strikes as family sleeps - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Police crime branch says it has enough evidence to ensure the conviction of the Indian Mujahideen (IM) suspects it has arrested, though it does concede that an approver would give it a stronger case.

Pune software engineer Mansoor Peerbhoy, accused of drafting and sending terror emails ahead of terror strikes in various parts of the country, has filed an application to the special Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) court stating his desire to turn approver. The crime branch has been directed to file a reply to the application.

JCP (Crime) Rakesh Maria today said Peerbhoy's application was being considered; he added that others among the arrested too had expressed a willingness to become approvers.

"In criminal conspiracy cases, it helps to have an approver who can corroborate certain facts such as meetings and plans. However, we have enough evidence against the arrested accused to secure convictions against them. We have seized five laptop computers which have files, email drafts and photographs stored on them. The mirror image of the hard disks of these computers have already been analysed by forensic experts. Besides this, 12 of the arrested accused have given confessions before an officer of DCP rank; these confessions have been ratified in court," said Maria.

"We are considering Peerbhoy's request, and will take a decision soon. The court order directing the crime branch to file a reply has not yet been served on us. We have also received offers from other arrested accused expressing their eagerness to turn approvers in the case. These requests are also being considered, and we will take a decision shortly."

Heading: See them soon on national park safari - Indian Express
Content:
A family of four was found dead, murdered in their sleep, in their home at Nallasopara on Tuesday morning.

The family ran a laundry business and the bodies were found by a teenager who had gone to their shop to get some clothes ironed. The family's home is right behind their shop. When the teenager found the shop shut, she went to the back of the shop and peeked into the house through the window and saw the bodies.

The throat of Phoolwati Kanaujia (40) had been slit, while the bodies of her husband Kallu Kanaujia (45) and daughters Nisha (9) and Soni (8) bore wounds around their eyes and heads. The weapons have not been recovered from the site and the police have not been able to figure out the motive either.

The Kanaujia couple is survived by two other children, said the Nallasopara police who have registered a case of murder.

"Daughter Rita (20) is already married and stays with her in-laws at Moregaon in Nallasopara. Son Jitendra (17) runs a shop at Tardeo with the father; Phoolwati ran the laundry business at Nallasopara," said ASP (Thane Rural) Shashikant Mahavarkar.

The shop and the house where they were found dead is at Sai Sahara building at Nagindas Pada in Nallasopara.

"We are questioning Jitendra and Rita and also a person who had given a loan of Rs 1 lakh to Kallu," said Mahavarkar. "A police team has been sent to Tardeo and a case of murder under Section 302 of the IPC have been registered against persons unknown. The murder could have been taken place between midnight and 4 am. There was no forced entry into the house as the door used to be ajar most of the time," Mahavarkar added.

Heading: Railway cops flounder as thieves drug and rob passengers at will - Indian Express
Content:
Two newly born royal Bengal tigers, currently being raised with utmost care in the Sanjay Gandhi National Park (SGNP), will soon become the star attraction of the park's tiger safari rides. One-and-half months from now, the park officials plan to let out the cubs in the secondary cage along with their mother, 9-year-old Basanti, for the viewing pleasure of visitors.

Bengal tigers are highly endangered animals, with an estimated population of between 1,300 and 1,500 in wild in India. However, conservationists say, captive births are inconsequential as it is almost impossible to rehabilitate the big cats.

The two fluffy, new flaming orange cubs — a male and a female — were born on October 7, to Basanti and Palash (both 9). The cubs have not been weighed, named or handled by humans yet, and currently occupy a makeshift den created in one of the tiger cages. They spend most of their time feeding and huddling with their mother, the tiger safari handlers said.

According to SGNP wildlife vet, Dr Vinaya Jangale, infection and deaths are very high among tiger cubs, whether in wild or in captivity. "However, the first month after its birth is usually the most tenuous, and now there is a high chance that both the cubs will survive," she said.

Among the first threats to the cubs, she stated, was climactic changes. "Their resistance to the weather is very weak. For an entire month, we monitored their den by providing a heater at night and cooler in the day. Since their eyes were closed for the first few days, we had to ensure that light doesn't filter into their cages. A slight glare can affect their vision," she explained.

Instructions were also given to handlers to not touch the cubs, for the fear of being rejected by their mother. "The olfactory senses or tigers are very sharp. The mother may refuse to feed or attend to the babies if she gets a human scent from them," she explained.

As the cubs' sole diet is their mother's milk, handlers are now supplementing Basanti's meals with vitamins, Jangale said. "She gets two live chickens to eat every day aside from her regular beef diet. Also we supplement her intake with extra doses of calcium and vitamins added to her water."

In the wild, cubs remain attached to their mother for nearly two-and-a-half months so that they can fully cultivate their skills to prey, but according to Jangale, captive tigers could be separated in just one-and-a-half months. When the two SGNP cubs complete three months, they will be administered their first vaccine shots she added.

With the birth of the two new cubs the park has a total of 10 tigers, and just two lions. Now, officials have plans to exchange two other tigers for a pair of Asiatic lions from Gir. "Provided that cubs survive their early days, we will try to exchange an older tiger couple for lions. We are in correspondence with Gir as well as some other zoos for it," Jangale said.

However, Kishore Rithe, a wildlife conservationist working at the Melghat Tiger Reserve, dismissed the news of the tiger births in SGNP stating that birth of the big cats in captivity doesn't help in reversing the dwindling tiger population of the country.

"While certain animals like the vultures can be bred in captivity and then re-introduced to the wild, tigers can't be rehabilitated. As far as conservation of the species is concerned, captive tigers have no future. In fact, when we count the tiger population in India, we don't even include captive tigers in it."

Heading: Fire erupts at Andheri timber mart in Amboli - Indian Express
Content:
Some 20 such crimes registered between January & September this year, only three of these detected

On October 10, the Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST) railway cops found 29-year-old Kul Mani Sahu in an unconscious state in the Devgiri Express. A primary teacher with a government school in Orissa, Sahu was drugged by an unidentified man in the train after befriending him when he was on way to Mumbai. Rs 2,200 cash and a Nokia mobile phone were stolen from him.

In September, the CST railway cops found five people in an unconscious state. Police said the five men from Thane and Kalyan were travelling in the Punjab Mail where they befriended two fellow passengers, who gave them something to eat after which they fell unconscious.

According to figures obtained from the Mumbai railway police, some 20 crimes pertaining to passengers being drugged in long distance trains were registered between January and September this year by railway police stations in the commissonerate. Cash amounting to Rs 3.8 lakh was stolen, but only three crimes were detected by the police. Of the 20 cases registered, only nine cases were registered at the Kalyan railway police station.

Last year's figures show that 43 cases were registered at Kalyan railway police station again recording 20 such cases but with only four detections.

"In most of the cases, the crime takes places in jurisdiction of other police stations and many a time in other states. By the time the victim regains consciousness, they are at the station where the train terminates. In such cases, the passengers too have little details to give as they are under the influence of drugs," said Vasant Koregoankar, DCP (Central Railway).

"We investigate the cases when we find that the crime has occurred in our jurisdiction," says Mumbai Railway police commissioner Ashok Kumar Sharma.

The drug that is administered on the passengers is very harmful. Chief Security Commissioner of the Central Railway B S Sidhu said: "The culprits administer dhatura on the victims which usually grows along the rail tracks. Seeds of these plants are poisonous and crushed to prepare a powder. Its effect lasts 2-3 days depending on the dose." They usually prefer cream biscuits and mix the powder in the cream which is placed between two biscuits. The packet is then sealed. Sometimes, they inject it in oranges and Frooti packets. They even mix it up in tea.

"They are very good at mind game and generally to a recce before zeroing in on the victim. They befriend the victim which takes 2-3 hours," said Sidhu. Cops said majority of the cases occur during Diwali as migrants return to their native places and definitely have some cash or valuables with them.

Heading: Aviation slump hits domestic flyers but foreign carriers expand base in India - Indian Express
Content:
Days after a fire gutted Oshiwara timber market, another incident of fire took place at the Andheri timber mart in Amboli on late Monday night. The fire flames were so large that it threatened to engulf the nearby railway line and the overhead wires on the Western Railway. Train services were put on hold till the fire could be brought under control.

The fire erupted on the timber market located on SV road at 11.45 pm. All the 16 shops in the market were gutted and the fire department could save only few bamboos and wood. Deputy chief fire officer, P D Karguppikar said that the fire was major and posed a big problem for firemen as all the materials at the spot were combustible.

"There was a lot of wood across the market and the flames kept getting stronger," he said. "At a point it was too close to the railway line and even threatened to go near the over-head lines of the WR. However, the fire was controlled before that," he added.

WR officials said that while there was no damage to the over head wires, an empty local train which was standing near by suffered a minor damage.

"There were two empty local trains standing near the spot and the exterior paint of one local melted due to the heat, however it was just a minor incident. The trains were immediately moved," said WR, PRO, Shyam Sunder Gupta.

He also said that the trains, running towards Borivli and Virar were diverted due to the fire and were late by a few minutes.

Around 12 fire engines, eight tankers and an ambulance were used to douse the fire. Two fire men were also injured in the operation. Their condition is stable now.

Heading: Kalyan court extends relief to Raj till Dec 5 - Indian Express
Content:
After dizzying northward growth — which the country's aviation sector witnessed before the rise in aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices— in terms of capacity addition and flight frequencies between major Indian destinations, the country's domestic carriers have trimmed down the frequency of flights for now and are waiting for the dust to settle down. However, on the other hand, international traffic to and from India's busiest airport is on the rise and this can be gauged by rising number of frequencies of international flights and their slot allocations. According to the figures obtained from Mumbai International Airport limited (MIAL), the private operator that runs city's Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport (CSIA), while number of domestic slots at the airport has remained at 502 this winter schedule, slots for international airlines have seen a rise from 198 slots in the previous summer schedule to 214 slots in the winter schedule.

An airport slot, according to International Airport Transport Association's (IATA) Worldwide Scheduling Guidelines (WSG), is the scheduled time of arrival or departure available for an aircraft movement on a specific date at a coordinated airport. As per IATA's WSG guidelines, the Mumbai's CSIA is a level 3 airport in terms of slot allocations. In CSIA, the demand for slots by airlines exceeds the availability and thereby slots are decided by an independent coordinator, a role played by the Ministry of Civil Aviation (MCA) through its implementing body, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA).

With domestic carriers cutting down the number of operational flights owing to domestic slump, international carriers are increasingly trying to push their presence in domestic skies and therefore the increase. But to most of them, the demand was always there with the increase in frequency only catering to latent demand.

"For international carriers, the effect of the slump has been a little soft as our business does not depend on point to point operations like the domestic carriers. Instead, we operate on various models like the hub & spoke system where there are several origins and destinations with balanced flow of traffic from both ends," said a senior international airline executive. Carriers like Qatar and Emirates have already increased their presence in the country by adding more flights. While Emirates added 18 additional flights per week in July this year to various destinations taking its India operations to 132 flights per week, Qatar Airways started daily operations to the United States from nine Indian cities.

"According to the Airports Authority of India (AAI), 24.62 million people flew on international routes to and from India between April 2007 and January 2008. We believe the long-term prospects of the Indian economy are very strong and this will drive demand for air travel," said Orhan Abbas, Vice President (Indian & Nepal), Emirates.

"There has been a considerable drop in domestic capacity and therefore there is no requirement for additional slots, considering negative growth in passenger figures since June this year," said Philip Cash, Airport Director at CSIA. Incidentally, domestic passenger movements fell down by 22 per cent in September this year as compared to that in last year in the same period. Even though international passenger movements fell to 5.6 per cent from 16 per cent this September, the fequency of international flights has shown an 8 per cent rise this year compared to that in 2007. "However, the international sector has still got some growth and carriers plan for expansion in the Indian market," said Cash.

"Basically, it's an increase in frequency and not carriers," said an MIAL spokesperson.

Heading: Six arrested for murder of Reliance union leader - Indian Express
Content:
Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray's interim relief in connection with attack by MNS activists on railway examinees was extended till December 5 by the Kalyan sessions court on Tuesday after the prosecution sought time to file the reply. A case was registered against him with the Kalyan Government Railway Police (GRP) for inciting violence against north Indians.

Additional Session's Judge K K Tantrapale extended the interim bail given to Raj as Public Prosecutor Ajay Misar sought more time from the court to study the case. Misar had replaced Rohini Salian who was busy seeking a Bombay High Court stay on the interim bail granted to Thackeray by the Kalyan court.

On October 22, 2008, three days after the attack on railway examinees at Manpada and Kalyan, the Kalyan sessions court refused police custody of Raj Thackeray. In Manpada, where he had been shown as arrested, the court had granted bail. In the Kalyan GRP case, inwhich police were seeking transfer of his custody the court had granted interim bail.

Since this is an interim bail and he is yet to be arrested by the Kalyan GRP, Raj Thackeray has also filed an application for anticipatory bail, the decision of which is pending before the court.

On Tuesday, Raj Thackeray was represented by a battery of lawyers led by senior advocate Srinivas Modak in the court.

Heading: Meanwhile, corporators slam poor implementation of fire safety norms in city - Indian Express
Content:
Rivalry for post of building society office-bearer was the motive: police

Six men were arrested on Monday night from different parts of the city for stabbing Reliance Energy employee Shantaram Kanade on the threshold of the office of his residential society in Thakur Village Kandivili (East). According to the police, the accused have confessed to their crime and say the motive behind the murder was the rivalry over the post of building society office bearer.

On Sunday, 10-12 unidentified men barged into Kanade's office, who was the secretary of the society, and stabbed him 25 times. He was rushed to Bhagwati Hospital where he was declared dead on admission.

The police are now on the lookout for a man identified as Vijay Salvi alias Tambad (40) who had allegedly ordered the killing.

DCP Ajit Patil, (Zone 12) said, "Salvi, who owns a marble business, had several disputes with Kanade in the past over the secretary post. These two would often get into fights and approach the Samta Nagar police station to file complaints on a regular basis."

After the incident, the police released sketches according to eyewitness accounts and arrested six assailants. Salvi, say the police, could not be arrested as he had left for London for some business purpose and has not come back yet.

"The accused have criminal charges against them at various police stations in Mumbai as well as in Thane. They told us during interrogation that they had been working as bodyguards for Salvi. Even Salvi has cases of murder, rioting and criminal intimidation against him in Mulund and Samta Nagar police stations. We also recovered some weapons from the six arrested and are conducting enquiries to trace others who were involved in the murder," said Patil.

The arrested men have been identified as Dashrath Shinde (39), Babu Nimbalkar (24), Kapil Ahir (28), Gorakh Shinde (38), Rajesh Tandel (33) and Sarfaraz Sheikh (29).

The six have been remanded to police custody till November 19 for further interrogations.

Kanade had been staying alone in his flat at Evershine Millenium after his wife passed away two years back. His 11-year-old son studies in Panchgani. Kanade, a former engineer with Reliance Energy was sacked from Reliance Energy 9 years back after an argument with the manager and was actively involved in labour union issues at Reliance.

Heading: Two killed, 2 injured in robbery attempt - Indian Express
Content:
With an average of 25 fire accidents in the city every month, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has said that the city is facing a shortage of fire stations. Currently, there are only 33 fire stations in Mumbai, including six fire stations which are under construction. According to the sources, in the city, the area of which is over 400 sq km, there should be at least 144 fire stations as per international standards.

Replying to a notice of motion on Tuesday in the general body meeting at the civic headquarters, Additional Municipal Commissioner R A Rajeev said as per the existing norms in the city, there should be a fire station in every 10 kilometre area. "Accordingly, there should be 44 fire stations in the city. But we have only 33 fire stations in the city," he said. The international standards state that there should be a fire station in every two kilometre area.

The issue of fire safety has been raised by several corporators. According to them, fire safety norms are flouted in most of highrises, industrial estates and shopping malls in the city. "Mumbaikars living in high rises are in grave danger. In the past few months, the city has seen several fire accidents. Most of the new constructions do not have enough firefighting equipment. Even municipal fire hydrants are missing in many wards," said Mohsin Haider, Samajwadi corporator, who raised the objection.

"Incidents like the Infinity mall fire accident prove that even shopping malls are not keen on implementing all the norms," said Yogesh Sagar, BJP corporator. Corporators also claimed that several highrises are also flouting open space rules. "Several buildings in Bandra are using their underground parking area for purposes like basement restaurants and eateries. They're flouting DC rules which were passed in 1998. Around 50 per cent of malls in the city do not even have proper Occupational Certificate (OC)," alleged Congress corporator, Sheetal Mhatre. They have also demanded a strict action on the defaulters.

Rajeev said that the Occupation Certificate was given only after verifying that all fire safety norms were followed. He also said that the Fire Act which was passed in 2007 was not implemented as the report on the conditions and guidelines was still being prepared.

Heading: Exchange programme students set to get varsity marks - Indian Express
Content:
Two employees of a laundry shop at Oshiwara were killed and another two seriously injured in robbery attempt on Monday night.

According to the Oshiwara police, the bodies of the two men were discovered by the owner of the laundry shop, Suresh Chandwani, when he went to open the shop on Tuesday morning at 9. He found the shutter slightly opened and on entering the shop spotted four of his employees in a pool of blood. They were rushed to Cooper Hospital, but two of them were declared dead on arrival. The victims have been identified as Sandeep Nirmal (20) and his uncle Prakash (35). The injured — Sandeep's father Ramvilas and another employee, Pankaj (24)— suffered serious injuries and are being treated at the hospital. The fifth employee of the shop, Shiva, has been missing since Monday morning and police are on the lookout for him. The manager of the laundry, Jagdish Kanojia, has also been questioned in the case.

Acting Senior Police Inspector Dattatray Sankhe from the Oshiwara police station said, "All four had sustained injuries on heads and faces. From the nature of the injuries, it seems they were attacked by a hammer and some other sharp object. We have recovered a hammer from the spot. There were no signs of any struggle. We found that Rs 18,000 cash was missing from the shop."

All the four employees hail from Rae Bareilli and had been working for Chandwani for the last seven years. Chandwani was unavailable for comment.

Heading: Mulund resident held for dowry harassment - Indian Express
Content:
The University of Mumbai is mulling to give marks to students who undertake exchange programmes through their colleges. Until now, recognition of these exchange programmes for select students from different colleges would only be in the form of participatory certificates. These kind of programmes, however, could soon be considered as part of internal marks for assessment, informed pro vice-chancellor of the university Dr A D Sawant.

The idea was thought about during the US visit of a delegation of around 13 principals and secretary, Higher and Technical education department, J S Saharia to nine universities in the US, led by the vice-chancellor and the Sheriff of Mumbai that concluded last week.

Among other universities that have such tie-up programmes with city colleges, the New York University Stern School of Business, which was visited by the delegation, has exchange programmes with St Xavier's college, Fort and HR College, Churchgate.  

"It was at this school that we thought of formulating a credit system for such exchange visits. Students go to these universities and spend two-three weeks working on projects. These could easily be considered as part of their curriculum assessment. They should be able to get this benefit," Dr Sawant said. This idea will soon be put forward before the management council, he added.

Besides this, the delegation also met Fulbright officials and discussed with them the possibility of introducing short term Fulbright programmes for working professionals and academicians. Dr Sawant elaborated, "The Fulbright officials said they will try to design short modules that could be specifically used for Indian professionals. These could enable vice-chancellors, professors, business executives to undertake shorter visits and resume their work."

Currently, these programmes extend to not less than six months.

In all the visits to the universities, the delegation noted that there was a lot of emphasis on extracurricular activities besides academics. "In Columbia University, there is a dedicated team of 40-50 staff members who only handle 250 societies that look after extra curricular activities like sports, music, counselling, art, theatre etc. Colleges here have a lot to learn from institutions there," said Sawant.

Heading: New rail services between Dahanu and Panvel - Indian Express
Content:
A 26-year-old Mulund resident, who had married an 18-year-old aspiring actress in October after having met her through his online 'entertainment' company, was recently arrested by the Mulund police after his wife registered a complaint that he had harassed her for dowry.

The accused Abhishek Sanghvi had married another such aspirant earlier and divorced her.

Sanghvi, a resident of Ashok Nagar in Mulund, had started an online entertainment company , which invited portfolios of prospective actors, promising to land them meaty acting assignments. Srirang Bhosale, sub-inspector of Mulund police station, who is investigating the case said, "He claims to own a company named Lemon Craft Entertainment and Films, which operates through a website and does not have any registered office. Through the company, Sanghvi met the girl, the daughter of a wealthy Ghatkopar-based builder, who had responded to his advertisements and approached him with her portfolio." Adding, " Sanghvi met the girl often under the pretext of introducing her to producers and directors and he claims that love blossomed between them during those meetings."

Though the couple's relationship started in August, Sanghvi could not marry her until October when she turned 18.

On October 14, around a week after her birthday, the couple had a registered marriage in Bandra court and Sanghvi brought her home to his family in Mulund.

"The couple had initially hidden their marriage from the girl's parents fearing a reprisal but eventually notified them and even submitted a copy of their marriage certificate at the police station,"Bhonsale said.

"A few days into the marriage, however, Sanghvi and his family began pressurising the girl to ask her folks for Rs 2 lakh, if they wanted to meet her. The girl somehow managed to convey her helplessness to her family, following which her grandfather arrived at Sanghvi's house and took her away with him," he added.

Fifteen days after her marriage, the girl's family filed a complaint of dowry harassment against Sanghvi and his mother, on the basis of which the police arrested them on November 3.

"In her statement, the girl revealed that Sanghvi had told her about his first marriage to a girl hailing from Nallasopara. He had reportedly started the company around a year back and had married the girl who had also been an aspirant. He had, however, divorced her soon after," said Bhosale.

The girl's family could not be contacted as police said they were concerned about their daughter's future, and wished to remain anonymous. The girl is presently preparing for her class 12 exams.

Heading: GUILTY: CPM’s Suhrid Dutta, ally Debu Malik for killing Tapasi - Indian Express
Content:
Railway is set to start new services connecting Panvel and Dahanu stations by the end of the month. The line would prove to be a boon for those who commute between these two stations, as they lie at two extreme ends of the Central (Harbour) and Western lines respectively.

Railway is planning to start five new services on the route on a daily basis. "The time table is being worked out and services should later this month," said Shyam Sunder Gupta, chief spokesperson for the Western Railway (WR).

"We plan to run MEMU rakes (Mainline Electric Multiple Units), a shuttle service, on this route," Gupta added.

Currently, MEMU rakes' services are used on the Diva-Panvel-Roha route and Vasai-Diva route. However, on this route, the services terminate at Vasai station. With the commencement of this new service, commuters can directly take a train from Panvel to Dahanu.

The new service would give boost to the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) beyond Virar. Plans are in the store to extend the MMR region till Dahanu.

The Western Railway (WR) also has plans to take the EMU services to Dahanu which otherwise extend till Virar. The shuttle service is already widely used by the local villagers between Panvel-Diva-Vasai as it not connects the Central line to the Western line. It also proves to be a boon for Bhiwandi.

The Diva-Panvel-Roha line is useful for villagers between Roha and Panvel as the area after it is an industrial belt.

Interestingly, by the month end, the CR would also be starting its Turbhe-Nerul section. The commuters would be able to take a direct train from Thane to Nerul.

Heading: Buddha, Gandhi at loggerheads over transfer order to press secretary - Indian Express
Content:
Party unmoved: We shall go to higher court, won't expel Dutta

Barely a whisper away from the general elections, West Bengal's ruling CPM was dealt a body blow on Tuesday when a district court pronounced prominent party worker Suhrid Dutta and his accomplice Debu Malik guilty of murdering Tapasi Malik — the 18-year-old Trinamool Congress sympathiser, whose badly-burnt body was found inside the Nano project site on December 18, 2006.

Additional District and Sessions Judge of the Chandernagore fast-track court, Amar Kanti Acharya, will decide on the punishment on Wednesday.

The ruling party, however, is putting up a brave face and has decided it will continue to support Suhrid Dutta — its "old comrade" and former CPM zonal secretary in Singur, Hooghly. The state leadership announced it would challenge the court's verdict in the higher ranks of the judiciary. There was also no talk of expulsion.

Tapasi Malik's murder was a watershed in the Opposition's protest against the 'forceful' acquisition of farmland for the now-abandoned Nano project. Following a flurry of remonstrations that culminated in a long sit-in demonstration by Trinamool leader Mamata Banerjee, the state government handed over the probe to the Central Bureau of Investigation. It was also found that Tapasi — a member of the Save Farmland Committee — had been raped and murdered before her body was set on fire.

On Tuesday, Tapasi's father Manoranjan Malik said: "We were confident of justice. I am happy my daughter's murderers were finally found guilty. Now I want them to be hanged."

Earlier in the day, the two accused Dutta and Debu Malik were brought to the court amid tight security. The magistrate declared the two guilty under Sections 120(B), 302, 201 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) which relate to murder, criminal conspiracy and tampering with evidence. He declared the verdict before a packed courtroom at 1.30 pm.

Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee welcomed the judgment. "We are happy with the CBI probe. The chief minister should take responsibility of his partyman's deeds and resign," she said.

But the CPM was unflappable. The party's district secretariat member from Hooghly Balai Sanpui said:

"There is no question of expelling Dutta. The legal battle is not over yet."

Dutta's advocate Arindam Bhattacharjee said: "We will move a higher court after the quantum of punishment is defined. Today's judgment was a miscarriage of justice." Malik's advocate Kishor Mondal said he would also challenge the lower court's judgment.

CBI's advocate Partha Tapaswi said: "The minimum and maximum punishments for one found guilty for murder and criminal conspiracy are life and the death penalty respectively."

Dutta's elder brother, Saroj Dutta, who is secretary of the CPM's local committee in Bora, Singur, said: "We will unite the masses to defeat the conspiracy against my brother and the party."

The Chandernagore court had a rough time during the day with both the CPM and the Trinamool outbidding each other on a show of strength. There were hundreds of party workers waiting outside to hear the verdict. Trinamool men also tried to break down the heavy police cordon around the accused when they were on their way to court from the Chandernagore sub-divisional correctional home.

Several senior CPM district committee members, including MPs Rupchand Paul and Santashree Chatterjee, were also present in court.

Heading: ‘Sadik brought youths from Azamgarh to execute terror plans’ - Indian Express
Content:
Governor Gopal Krishna Gandhi, who has often criticised various policies of the CPM-led state government, has now locked horns with the state government over the transfer of his press secretary, Dhruba Basu.

Basu, an officer of the Information & Culture Department (I&C) under Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, received the transfer order on November 8.

The standard practice has been that the government usually consults the Governor before the transfer of any Raj Bhavan top officers. But this time, the practice was not followed, which annoyed the Governor. He immediately crossed swords with the I&C Department, demanding that the officer be retained in his job.

Basu, supposed to be replaced by chief of news bureau Apurba Chatterjee, had joined his present duty in May 2000. He become an anathema to the CPI(M) as he was perceived to have given the maximum media mileage to the Governor. Basu, also the Bengali language teacher of the Governor, was allotted a flat at the Raj Bhavan quarters about a year ago.

On Tuesday, principal secretary to the Governor Rajendra Kumar, on behalf of the Governor, wrote to the I&C Department that the press secretary be retained in his post.

Basu, who will retire in March 2012, also wrote a letter to principal secretary to the I&C Department, Dilip Chakraborty, requesting him to allow him to stay in his office at Raj Bhavan.

Chakraborty, however, said the transfer of Basu, who faces allegations of misbehaviour towards his colleagues, was a routine affair. "His is a transferable job and he cannot object if he is moved out after working more than eight years at the same post. I don't know why he wants to stick to that post. But, well, if the Governor takes up the matter with us, we will have to do something because he is the head of this state," Chakraborty told The Indian Express.

However, according to sources, there are officers in the Chief Minister's secretariat as well as the Raj Bhavan who have been in their posts for more than 10 years.

Heading: Mamata announces ‘Tapasi Malik Divas’ - Indian Express
Content:
2002 attack on American Center: Kolkata police interrogate accused

All the youths involved in the Batla House shootout in Jamia Nagar, New Delhi, were recruited by alleged Indian Mujahideen (IM) founder Sadik Sheikh, now in the custody of the Gujarat Police. Senior Special Task Force (STF) officers of the Kolkata Police, who interrogated Sheikh in Ahmedabad earlier this week, said he had brought the youths and many other IM operatives from his native Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh.

The STF team had interrogated Sheikh in connection with the attack on the American Center in Kolkata in January, 2002. The interrogation revealed Sheikh was the one who had opened fire from an AK-47 assault rifle. Six policemen were killed in the attack. Since then, Sheikh had eluded investigators till he was arrested in Mumbai on September 24 in connection with the blasts in Delhi, as well as in several other parts of the country, including Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Uttar Pradesh.

Special Additional Commissioner of Police and STF Chief Rajiv Kumar told The Indian Express after returning from Ahmedabad that Sheikh's co-accused in the American Center attack, including gangster Aftab Ansari, had refused to identify Sheikh from the photographs taken after his arrest.

"Following his arrest, we sent a team to Hazaribagh in Jharkhand, where he had set up base. He had purchased a house there, and had stayed there after the Kolkata attack for over six months. His photograph was recognised by shopkeepers near his safe house," he said.

When investigators tracked the attack trail to Hazaribagh in 2002, Sheikh escaped arrest as he was away on a trip to Patna. On the way back, he came to know about the raid and escaped to his native place Azamgarh. He then left the country for Dubai, among other locations, where he continued to recruit people for training in terror-related activities.

"Our impression after interrogating him was that he is not doing this for money alone. After returning to the country, Sheikh frequently visited Hazaribagh, Azamgarh and several other places in India to recruit operatives and set up bases. But most of his recruitment work was done in Azamgarh," STF sources said.

"We believe he is the mastermind behind all the blasts for the past eight years or so. He has, however, mentioned that he took orders from Riyaz Bhatkal and Iqbal Bhatkal, both of whom are absconding," they said.

They added Sheikh's source of funding is still under investigation and it is possible that he met with members of the LeT as well. "It's too early to say if he was being funded by any foreign country," sources said.

Heading: Seige enters fifth day, Lalgarh remains cut off - Indian Express
Content:
The verdict of the Tapasi Malik murder case has provided a new impetus to the Singur agitation of the Trinamool Congress. An elated Mamata Banerjee announced November 15 will be observed as 'Tapasi Malik Divas'.

"Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's administration failed to arrest the accused in the murder case. He has lost credibility, therefore, he should resign immediately," Banerjee said.

"We will hold a rally in Singur on November 15. The Trinamool will also organise a bigger rally in Singur on December 2," the Trinamool leader said.

"The verdict should open the eyes of the government. Now, they should return 400 acres of land to the unwilling farmers," she said.

She claimed the CPM is spreading terror in the state before the parliamentary elections. "The policemen are supporting the CPM cadres. Minorities of various districts who support the Trinamool are being threatened," she alleged.

"If the Centre can intervene in Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra, I do not understand why it cannot do anything about the situation in Bengal," she said.

Heading: Officials smell a rat as KMC sits on stocks of larvicides but orders more - Indian Express
Content:
Meetings fail to reach consensus, prices of essential commodities go up

Lalgarh remained cut off from the rest of West Bengal for the fifth consecutive day on Tuesday, as all-party meetings called by the district administration to resolve the crisis failed to reach a consensus. The state government has alleged that outsiders are instigating the locals of the area.

"The type of slogans being raised in Lalgarh show the presence of outsiders who are instigating violence," said Home Secretary Ashok Mohan Chakrabarti.

"The trouble at Lalgarh is also hampering the investigations in the Salboni blast, as the officers involved in the probe are now busy with controlling the law and order situation in Lalgarh. Moreover, the snapping of roads has affected the supply of kerosene oil, which is widely used in the area that has no electricity," he added.

Political parties and the administration have failed to arrive at an agreement to allow repair of roads dug upin the Lalgarh area of West Midnapore. Two separate meetings were called by the administration on Tuesday.

The first meeting — called by the block development officer (BDO) of Lalgarh — was held at his office and was attended by gram panchayat pradhans and panchayat samity members of the area. Another meeting was called by District Magistrate Narayan Swarup Nigam in Jhargram with all the political parties. Both the meetings failed to serve the purpose.

"We do not intend to use force to repair the roads that have been dug up. We want to resolve the issue through dialogue," said Nigam.

Another meeting has been called on Wednesday.

In both the meetings, the Opposition demanded an end to the atrocities by the police and that the police should release all those arrested or detained for their alleged involvement in the Salboni blast. The Opposition also sought a public apology from the police.

District police sources, however, said since the case was linked with the attack on the chief minister's convoy, it would not be possible for them to allow release of those arrested.

"This will give a signal that the administration is compromising even in such a sensitive case," said a senior police officer of the district police.

Panic was evident among the residents of Lalgarh, with most of the roads remaining deserted on Tuesday. The three police station areas of Lalgarh, Binpur and Belpahari remained cut off, which has resulted in the rise in prices of essential commodities — with potato and candle being the worst hit. A source in the Lalgarh BDO office, however, claimed there was no shortage of dry food. The administration is arranging for supply of kerosene in the area.

Lalgarh comprises 10 gram panchayats. Of these seven are run by the Jharkhand Party and three by the CPM. The panchayat and samity members have been requested by the state administration to go back to the villages and try to convince the villagers to allow repair of roads.

Heading: More malaria cases reported at NRS Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
The Kolkata Municipal Corporation's decision to order larvicides and mosquitocides has left many puzzled. According to officials, the Vector Control Department (VCD) has sufficient amount of the chemicals.

An official said the department, at present, has a stock of 500 litres of Vectobac AS, a liquid formation of larvicide, 50 kg of Biosite WP and 500 kg of Cyfluthine, which is used to kill adult mosquitoes.

A senior civic doctor said: "We have enough stock for this season and don't require more. In fact, we cannot store these chemicals for the next season as by then these will expire and hence be wasted."

He added: "The suppliers have reportedly been asked to supply more chemicals, which is not needed as the breeding season is about to get over." The doctor claimed that there is a secret nexus between some officials of the health department and suppliers of the chemicals.

A department official confirmed that there are enough stocks of chemicals but the Chief Medical Health Officer (CMHO) and the VCD has ordered for more.

According to an official, the KMC will procure 2,500 litres of Vectobac AS and 2,000 kg of Biosite WP. Vectobac and Biosite cost nearly Rs 1,300 to Rs 1,500 per kg and per litres, respectively. Sources said the civic body has a stock of Vectobac worth Rs 6,50,000 and Biosite worth 75,000. Even then, the KMC is procuring Vectobac worth Rs 32 lakh and Biosite worth 30 lakh.

Salil Sen, a supplier from Mumbai-based Swan Distributors, said: "We supplied 500 kg of Vectobac a few days ago and have now received more orders. We have a tie-up with a KMC official but cannot disclose the name."

Several companies, including Biotech International, BASF Distributors and Bayer India Pvt Limited, are assigned to supply the chemicals.

CMHO Deb Dwaipayan Chattopadhyay, however, denied the allegations and said: "We do not have chemicals in excess. We have procured whatever was required by the VCD and asked by the Vector Control Officer, Debashis Biswas."

Chattopadhyay added, "There is no question of wastage of chemicals, as we undertake vector-control operations throughout the year."

Incidentally, most of the councillors often complain that they receive only bleaching powder, which can be used as a disinfectant during an enteric outbreak, but cannot curb vector-borne diseases.

Leader of the Opposition Javed Ahmed Khan said: "I have never seen KMC field workers sprinkling larvicide or spraying mosquitocide in my ward. Instead, they often conduct fogging, which is ineffective and is also banned by the World Health Organisation."

He added: "Sometimes they sprinkle bleaching powder that should be used during an enteric outbreak and not now."

Mamata's mother in hospital
Kolkata: Gayatri Devi, mother of Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee, was admitted in a private hospital with a high fever on Tuesday. Although no blood test has been done yet, doctors suspect she is suffering from a vector-borne disease.

Heading: HC lawyers threaten protest if posts of judges remain vacant - Indian Express
Content:
With the city reeling under malaria-dengue-Japanese Encephalitis attacks, it seems the hospitals are becoming breeding ground for mosquitoes.

Three more staff members and students of the NRS Medical College and Hospital were admitted to the hospital on Tuesday after being diagnosed with the vector-borne diseases.

While staff nurse Nomita Maiti was diagnosed with plasmodium vivax, students Geeta Dutta and Lolita were diagnosed with plasmodium falcifarum and dengue, respectively.

A staff nurse, Kaveri Bhowmik, had recently died after suffering from an unknown fever.

"It is not a surprise that those who treat the patients are now being affected with vector-borne diseases. Unhygienic conditions in hospitals provide a breeding ground for mosquitoes," said Rituparna Mahapatra, Calcutta District secretary member of Medical Service Centre.

Maiti has been admitted to the emergency medicine ward. The hospital authorities have always neglected the regular notices sent by the KMC to clean up its premises, she said.

"Filth, stagnant water and unclean drains are a common site at the hospital premises. In spite of the recent outbreak of diseases, the authorities have not carried out any fogging on the campus," added Maiti.

The recent cases have again highlighted the plight of the state-run hospitals, as staff and students of four of the biggest hospitals in the city — NRS, SSKM, RG Kar and Lady Dufferin Hospital — have repeatedly fallen prey to the diseases.

Lady Dufferin was one of the first hospitals, where nearly 25 trainee nurses were diagnosed with dengue in October.

Three hostellers of the RG Kar Medical College and Hospital were recently diagnosed with plasmodium falcifarum. Sams Musafir, a fourth year student, said: "A couple of deaths have already been reported in the locality, but the drains are still open and garbage piles are yet to be removed. The authorities have not taken notice of the situation."

Heading: Students gherao Gorkha League office - Indian Express
Content:
Demanding appointments of judges in the High Court, the Bar Association of the Calcutta High Court has threatened to begin a protest if the posts are not filled within two weeks.

At a press conference on Tuesday, Bidyut Kiran Mukherjee, president of the bar association, said: "Work in the High Court has been hit due to the vacant posts of judges, as a result justice gets delayed in several cases."

Mukherjee said that he has been requesting Chief Justice S S Nijjar to resolve the issue in the interest of litigants and advocates, but the court has not taken any initiative to fill up the posts. He added, "The bar association will begin a movement after two weeks if the issue was not resolved during this period."
