Against 58 posts of judges in the High Court, 19 are lying vacant for a long time.

According to Mukherjee, it is a normal practice to pay bribes to get a copy of an order passed by the court.

He added that orders passed by the court are not executed in time, as their copies are not available within 48 hours.

"If the court grants a bail to an accused today, its copy will be available only after two or three weeks. The accused will have to remain in jail for that period owing to the delay on the part of the High Court administration. The Chief Justice has taken a few steps in the last few months to streamline the system, but it needs to be properly administered," Mukherjee said.

Heading: Staff against minister’s plan to shift office - Indian Express
Content:
Stepping up agitation against the All India Gorkha League (AIGL) president Madan Tamang, school students gheraoed the AIGL office in Darjeeling on Tuesday.

While no untoward incident was reported, senior district administration officials said the functioning of three schools was affected. The protesting students gheraoed the office under the banner of the Gorkha Janmukti Vidyarthi Parishad (GJVM).

Darjeeling Deputy Magistrate Surendra Gupta said the administration was keeping a close watch on the situation. "Since there is no prohibition against public gatherings, the gherao cannot be termed illegal. Due to the absence of students from three schools, their functioning was affected, but no school was shut down."

He added, "None of the schools have lodged any complaints. The schools were approached by the Gorkha Janmukti Morcha's student wing. Unless someone lodges a complaint, there is little we can do."

While Tamang has not lodged any official complaint with the police yet, the district administration has received a phone call from the AIGL office on Monday in connection with the gherao.

Since November 8, the district police have deployed over 100 police personnel at the AIGL office and Tamang's residence. The police force at both locations are led by a deputy superintendent.

Tamang, meanwhile, seemed unperturbed by the agitation against him. "There was no problem as such. We are ready for any eventuality. I have been used to this kind of agitation for the last two decades."

"My boys are ready to face the GJM. There is no question of bowing down to its diktat. Who are they to set deadlines and ask me questions? I have the freedom of expression in a democracy and their agitation is an attack on democracy," the Gorkha League chief added.

The GJVM, meanwhile, has declared that it was planning an indefinite movement to prevent Tamang from participating in politics. "We will not allow the AIGL office to open. Every time there is an attempt to do so, we will gherao the office. We will gherao the office on Wednesday as well," GJVM leader Kismat Chettri said.

He added, "Today, nearly 500 school students participated in the agitation. The students were from the Nepali Girls' High School, Turnbull School and Municipal Boys' School. All schools will take turns to participate in the agitation. We don't feel the schools are being disturbed in any way. Students will resume classes soon."

Heading: Builder locks elderly woman in her house - Indian Express
Content:
Commerce and Industries Minister Nirupam Sen, who recently suffered severe setbacks on account of the Nano project pullout and uncertainty over land acquisition at Geonkhali in East Midnapore for a shipyard, is now facing a rebellion in his own backyard.

The employees of his department, who were asked to vacate the office at Writers' Buildings and move to a new office at Camac Street, have refused to comply.

As the department includes employees of the Coordination Committee of the state government, all work has come to a standstill. It's only the minister and a few of his secretaries who have reported for duty at the new office.

The employees cite various reasons for refusing to shift to the new office. "It is located in a posh area where buses do not ply and you have to walk for at least 15 minutes to reach office. The food available there is very costly and you know the kind of salary state government employees get," said Anindya Basu, an employee.

He also questioned the logic behind shifting the office. "This department works in tandem with departments like the chief minister's secretariat and Land Reforms Department. If we shift there, the cost of communication between departments is going to increase. There are four directorates running from rented houses and the government pays nearly Rs 1 lakh in rent. Why is the government not shifting those offices there?" he said.

Heading: Travel agents take to Gandhigiri, present bouquet to Kingfisher manager - Indian Express
Content:
A builder locked up an elderly woman in her house for more than 10 hours on Monday for violating a sale agreement between them.

Christine Joseph (52), who owns a property on South Purbachal Hospital Road, had signed an agreement to sell it to a local promoter, Shankar Das, nearly three months ago.

"She is a widow and her son lives in Bangalore," said Joseph's neighbour Swapan Poddar. The police said the elderly woman wanted to settle down in Bangalore and the builder offered her Rs 14 lakh for the property. Das had also paid an advance of Rs 3 lakh to Joseph after signing the agreement. Last month, she was contacted by another builder, who promised her to pay Rs 19 lakh for the property. Joseph signed another agreement with the second promoter and after taking an advance of Rs 1 lakh from him she left her house.

When Joseph returned on Monday to collect her belongings, Das and his associate locked her door from outside and filed a complaint against her at the Kasba police station.

Finally, the police intervened around midnight and broke the lock. "On Tuesday morning, we received a complaint from her son David Joseph and arrested Das," said Shankar Biswas, Officer In-charge of the Kasba police station. Later, the agreement with the second promoter was cancelled.

Heading: Fresh trial to start in Bankshal court - Indian Express
Content:
City-based travel agents once again resorted to 'Gandhigiri' and presented a bouquet to Kingfisher Airways Manager (Eastern India) Kiran Naidu on Tuesday, to protest against the airlines decision on 'zero commission' regime.

As many as 35 representatives from various travel agencies had gathered at the Kingfisher office on Bankshal Street to meet Naidu, but were peeved when she did not agree to come out and instead asked them to come to her cabin.

"At the Travel Agents Federation of India (TAFI) convention held earlier this year, Vijay Mallya had said that Kingfisher Airlines would never target travel agents for cost-cutting. But he seems to have forgotten his promise," said Anil Punjabi, TAFI chairman, Eastern Chapter.

After deciding to implement 'zero commission' from November 1, travel agents and airlines had discussed the possibility of introducing a transaction fee on the ticket price.

"Four airlines — Jet Airways, Air India, Kingfisher and Singapore Airlines — have added transaction fee as a ticket component which will be given to us," said Anil Punjabi.

While Air India has already started charging the fee at its counters and website, Kingfisher, Singapore Airlines and Jet Airways have not introduced the new system on their websites yet, Punjabi added.

The TAFI has already boycotted three airlines — Air France, Northwest Airlines and KLM.

According to the treasurer of TAFI (Eastern Chapter), Sheik Afnan, who also owns a travel agency, 95 per cent of their income comes from selling airline tickets.

"When the business is good, we sell about 80 to 100 tickets per day. At least 200 agents and 53,000 sub-agents will be affected by this decision of the airlines," said Afnan.

"If the commission is not reinstated, most travel agencies will either halve their staff or close down their businesses. About 4,00,000 people are likely to lose their jobs across the country," said a travel agent.

"Going ahead with Gandhigiri, we may organise sit-in protests or keep our offices closed for three days," said a travel agent. Earlier, TAFI had sent samosas and specially-designed T-shirts to airline offices to register their protest against the decision.

TAFI Eastern Chapter will appeal against the decision of the airlines to stop the commission of travel agents in the Calcutta High Court on Wednesday.

TAFI and Travel Agents Association of India has claimed that they sell over 85 per cent of all airline tickets in the country.

Heading: Welcome home: Sourav now looks forward to meeting Maradona - Indian Express
Content:
Though Sadik Sheikh, the prime accused in the American Center attack case of 2002, is now in custody of the Gujarat Police, the Kolkata Police are keen on beginning trial procedures against him.

In this regard, a fresh trial will begin in the lower court. "A fresh case will be started in Bankshal court. Then it will be transferred to Bichar Bhavan," said Naba Kumar Ghosh, public prosecutor in the American Center attack case.

According to the police, Sadik is also an accused in the abduction of shoe baron Partha Pratim Roy Burman. "The trial for the case is on. If Sadik can be brought to Kolkata, he can be tried for the abduction case too. We are trying to bring him to Kolkata," said Jawed Shamim, Deputy Commissioner of the Detective Department.

The Mumbai police had arrested Sadik on September 24 for his alleged role in the recent serial blasts in New Delhi, Ahmedabad and Bangalore. The Gujarat Police had secured his custody early this month to interrogate him in connection with the July 26 serial blasts in Ahmedabad and planting of bombs in Surat.

The Kolkata police, however, only recently came to know that Sadik was involved in the attack on the American Center on January 22, 2002. Seven accused, including Sadik, have already been sentenced to death by a special court in connection to the attack. Sadik was shown as absconding in the chargesheet filed in the court.

Aftab Ansari, an accused in the case and five others have appealed to the High Court against the death penalty.

In all, 17 people were accused of being involved in the attack on the American Center. Among them, 13 were chargesheeted on April 26, 2002. The final verdict was passed on March 26, 2005. Accused like Amir Reza Khan, Zuber Ahmed and Nasir Ahmed are still absconding.

Heading: Kanitkar steals show after Dinda makes early inroads - Indian Express
Content:
Chaotic scenes, lathi-charge, Dalmiya's absence overshadow Ganguly's arrival in Kolkata

As Sourav Ganguly returned to his hometown this evening from Nagpur, the Prince of Kolkata's die-hard fans may be shedding a tear or two over their hero's exit from international cricket. But the man in the centre of it all himself reckons that there's much to look forward in the coming days for him — the much-awaited visit of Diego Maradona.

Amidst the emotional welcome at the airport in the evening and the extended press interaction later at his Behala residence, Ganguly pointed out during a candid chat with a TV channel that he just can't wait to see the legendary Argentine footballer.

Maradona is expected to drop in at Kolkata on a two-day whistle-stop trip, and Ganguly — himself a keen football-lover — is looking forward to catching up with the 1986 World Cup winning captain.

"Just to watch him (Maradona) is like a dream come true," Ganguly gushed during a chat with a TV channel in Nagpur shortly before setting off for Kolkata earlier in the day. "I am very excited about Maradona's Kolkata trip," he said, when asked whether he, too, is eagerly waiting for Maradona to turn up in his hometown.

In fact, it was much later in the day that Ganguly even made a passing mention to world football's two biggest names — Pele and Maradona — while he was explaining to mediapersons that every sportsperson, no matter how successful he or she's been, has to call it quits someday or the other. "Everyone has to go someday. Even Pele, Maradona had to go someday, it's part of the game," pointed out Ganguly. The former India captain, known for his passion for football in the Kolkata Maidan, is expected to turn up for the city's football club Chirag United SC this winter in the national league.

Meanwhile, Ganguly's return to the city was marked by chaotic scenes at the airport, with the Kolkata Police even resorting to mild lathi-charge at excited crowd to take stock of the situation. A battery of officials from the Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB) gave the player a warm welcome, presenting him with a gorgeous basket of 113 roses — a symbolic tribute to his 113-Test career — but surprisingly, CAB chief Jagmohan Dalmiya was conspicuously absent from the welcoming ceremony.

The welcome had to be wrapped up briskly, though, after hundreds of fans thronging outside the airport made a dash for their hero when he stepped out with his family to take the car back home. Policemen were forced to resort to lathi-charge, even as Ganguly's fans went wild chanting his name and following his vehicle on its way out of the airport.

The chaos was no less at Ganguly's Behala residence as well, where hundreds of supporters flooded the locality and the yet again, the police had to struggle hard to keep fans and shutterbugs under control.

Later, an unusually calm Ganguly held an extended press conference at his residence, recounting his best days at the highest level. "My debut Test match, my first match as captain of India, and the last day of the Nagpur match," he rattled off, when asked to pick out the three most memorable moments in his illustrious international career.

Ganguly also rued missing out on playing in front of his home ground in the last lap of his international career. "I would have loved to play at the Eden Gardens as my last match. That would have been really special," Ganguly admitted.

Heading: Stunned by ‘Nano note’ leak, govt probes to plug the hole - Indian Express
Content:
Hrishikesh Kanitkar (76 batting) used all his experience to ensure Madhya Pradesh don't throw away the advantage on the second day of the Plate Group Ranji Trophy match against Bengal in Gwalior today. Replying to Bengal's first innings score of 210, the hosts finished the day on 178 for 5, just 33 short of taking a first innings lead.

Resuming on overnight 4 for no loss, MP lost their first 3 wickets in very quick succession and were reeling at 5 for 3 after 7 overs. Bengal medium pacer Ashok Dinda (3/49) spat venom with the new ball and got rid of both the openers, Naman Ojha (1) and H Sagar (0). Ranadeb Bose (1/38) trapped Sunil Dholpure (0) in front of the wicket and Bengal had their tails up. With just 210 on the board, the visitors needed to strike early and the new-ball bowlers responded brilliantly.

Kanitkar, however, was concentration personified. He had a 46-run stand with D Bundela (15) for the fourth wicket that somewhat steadied the ship. The latter's 120-minute stay came to an end when he misjudged a run. Dinda then removed JS Saxena (9) to put Bengal once again on top. But the visitors surrendered the initiative as the medium pacer lacked support.

Kanitkar and BR Tomar (51 batting) have already put on 115 runs in an unfinished sixth wicket stand and more importantly, they have managed to take a psychological upper hand over their opponent.

A couple of early wickets on the third day will once again shift the balance though. The main thing will be to see the back of Kanitkar.

Heading: Aviation industry no more a hot career - Indian Express
Content:
Concerned about the reported leak of the 'Cabinet note' purportedly containing details of the incentives being offered to Tata Motors for its Nano car project in Gujarat, the state government has intensified its efforts to trace the source of the leak through an internal probe.

"As soon as we learnt on Monday evening that a 'Cabinet note' was being circulated among media persons, we directed the Industries Department to inquire into the matter. We have intensified the internal probe," said a senior official in the CMO.

The official told Newsline on Tuesday that he would not comment on the 'note' and the sops being offered to Tata Motors for the Nano project. But the possibility of a corporate rivalry behind the leak could not be ruled out, he said.

When contacted, a Tata Motors spokesman said that as a policy the company does not comment on such matters.

"The government doesn't want to hide anything (on incentives offered to the Tatas). It has already announced the rate at which the land has been allotted to Tata Motors for its small car project. Likewise, it will announce other sops to be given to the auto company," the official said.

As part of its efforts to trace the source of the leak, the CMO as well as senior officials in the state Industries Department today obtained a copy of the 'note' from media persons. "This will help us identify the source of the leak," said a senior official.

Chief Secretary D Rajagopalan said: "I don't want to make any comment on this issue. You better contact senior officials of the Industries Department to know more about this."

Deputy Secretary (Industries) Shobhana Desai also declined to comment on the matter.

Gujarat Minister of State for Industries Saurabh Patel told Newsline over the phone from Hyderabad this evening that he would offer his comment on the leaked 'Cabinet note' only after he goes through its contents. The minister has directed his office staff to obtain a copy of the 'note' before he returns to Gandhinagar from Hyderabad late on Tuesday.

Why is the deal under wraps?

The Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed between the Gujarat government and Tata Motors for the Nano project cannot be disclosed because the Tatas have said the disclosure would affect their competitiveness, the Gujarat Government said last Saturday, in reply to a query raised by a journalist of a Gujarati daily under the Right to Information (RTI) Act.

The information officer from the state Industries and Mining Department replied a month thereafter: "The query was sent to the company (Tata Motors Ltd) as it pertained to a third party as per the RTI Act Section 11. The company has requested that no information pertaining to the Nano project be given out as it can affect its competitiveness." The RTI application had sought details of the MoU, the copy of the MoU draft, the industrial status given to Tata Motors for the Nano project, the incentives and waivers, the details of the projects in Gujarat and their investment, the infrastructure facilities to be given to Tatas, the special incentives as compared to other industries, the land rates and incentives offered in Sanand where the Nano project is being relocated, and the actual benefits to Gujarat.

Heading: In Amreli, child labourer toils at district collector’s office compound - Indian Express
Content:
Reduction in number of flights, layoffs have made aspirants look to other fields

With the growth in the number of passengers travelling by air and new players entering the sector, the expectations from the aviation industry reached great heights. But that was 2006-2007. The youth were very keen to make their career in the field, but suddenly the sector seems to have lost its appeal.

Reductions in flights and layoffs by major airlines have forced the aspirants to look at other careers. The airhostess training institutes have begun helping the aspirants to take up careers in hospitality, telecom and BPO sectors.

"Demand for trained professionals in aviation industry is a bit sluggish and hence the conversion of inquiries has reduced," said Shivaji Khasnobis, the centre head, Maple Institute of Air Hostess Training (MIAT). Earlier, MIAT used to get two campus interviews every week from airlines; now it is one in a month.

Previously, most students got placements the moment they registered with training institutes. But recruitment has been very disappointing because of global recession and increased operating costs.

"The last campus recruitment took place in July-August," said Sameer Saxena, centre head, Air Hostess Academy (AHA), Ahmedabad.

He added: "The hospitality industry is booming in Gujarat and hence we are diverting inquiries to hospitality, BPO and telecom sectors. After the layoffs triggered by Jet Airways and Jetlite, parents don't want their children to make their careers in this sector."

The international airlines, however, are still in the recruitment mode. According to Frankfinn Air Hostess Training Institute, the recruitment by domestic airlines has reduced, but international airlines are still hunting for trained people.

"Emirates and Singapore Airlines came for the campus placements just two days ago and will continue to do so. Some others are also in the process of recruiting the ground staff," said Rachna Daruwala, center head, Frankfinn, Ahmedabad.

However, layoffs in the industry have discouraged the youth from joining the sector, she said.

"We are making up for losses in the aviation sector by diverting students to hospitality, retail and BPO sectors," said Daruwala.

Heading: The Tata files Gujarat vs Bengal - Indian Express
Content:
The boy states in the video that he serves tea. He is, however, too young to know his age or his date of birth

Under the provisions of the Child Labour Prevention Act, the district collector has been given the specific duty of checking the menace of child labour in his/her district. But in Amreli district, the menace seems to be prevailing right under the nose of the collector.

The Ahmedabad-based organisation, Dalit Hak Rakshak Manch (DHARM), which is working for the protection of the rights of the downtrodden, has caught on camera, two children, working at a tea-stall on the campus of the Amreli District Collector, during a visit to the office on November 6.

Rajesh Solanki, the secretary of the organisation, has now sent a note via-phonogram to the Amreli district collector to take note of the issue and requested him 'to eradicate child labour from the district and particularly from his office.'

Solanki has made a DVD, a copy of which is available with Newsline, containing the video-graphed interview of one child labourer working at a tea-stall inside the Amreli district collector's campus. The boy named Prakash states in the video that he serves tea. The boy, however, is too young to know his age or his date of birth.

Amreli District Collector D G Jhalavadiya said: "I am in the field today. So, I do not know anything in this regard. But, I will definitely check it up with my office." When asked if he has ever seen any child labourer inside the compound or around it, he said, "I've never seen any such thing."

According to Deputy Labour Commissioner K O Shah, the collector is the chair person of every district's Child Labour Rehabilitation and Welfare Committee and is responsible to make sure that the child labour prevention provisions are being followed in his/her district.

Solanki told Newsline: "The incident shows the kind of insensitivity prevailing among the government machinery over the issue of child labour. If the district collector is not able to check child labour inside his office compound, we can understand how well the job could have been done in the district."

Heading: Cong accuses Modi of receiving kickbacks in Nano deal - Indian Express
Content:
The note leaked to the media claims to record the discussion Chief Minister Narendra Modi had with his ministers before the Memorandum of Understanding was inked with the Tatas. It purportedly lists the demands the company made on Modi. Were those too different from what West Bengal had agreed to?

* Bengal had declined to sell the Singur land to Tatas for the project, only leased it for 90 years at graded lease rates. Modi sold the Sanand land to the automaker, payable in eight annual instalments. The 'note' also mentions that the Tatas might be exempted from paying stamp duty, registration charges and land transfer charges.

* Bengal had offered to sell power for the Nano plant at Rs 3 per KWH. Apparently, the Tatas asked Gujarat to facilitate 220 KVA of supply and also to exempt it from paying electricity duty.

* The 'note' also suggests the Tatas wanted exemption from state labour policy clauses that insist on 85 per cent local employment, including a 60 per cent quota in managerial and supervisory jobs.

* The Gujarat government had not "clarified" to the Tatas its rule that 50 per cent of the amount granted as state sops should be invested in the state itself, and that two per cent of it should be contributed to the rural welfare programme — Gokul Gram Yojana.

* The Tatas had allegedly pushed for another 100 acres of land near Ahmedabad to set up a township; a pipeline at the state's cost to supply natural gas to the Nano project site; provision for 14,000 cubic metres of water per day at the site; and permission to draw groundwater for immediate needs.

* The 'sops' the Tatas were being provided were to be considered as 'special exception', which other similar industries would not be eligible for.

Heading: ‘Condition of safai karmacharis in Gujarat possibly worst - Indian Express
Content:
BJP denies allegations, asks Congress to apologise

State Congress leaders on Tuesday accused Chief Minister Narendra Modi of receiving "kickbacks" and "commission" while allowing Tata Motors to shift its Nano car project to the state from West Bengal. They also demanded a white paper from him on the incentives given to the Tatas.

The Congress leaders made the demand after some quarters in the state administration leaked out portions of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) pertaining to sops offered to Tata Motors for shifting the Nano project from Singur to Sanand.

The Congress leaders said the fact that the government was keeping matter under wraps, suggested at some foul play. "If the government is really honest, it must make the MoU public," they said.

State party spokespersons Arjun Modhwadia said that when the party filed an RTI application to demand a copy of the MoU, it was turned down on the ground that it was a "business secret" and could not be made public.

Modhwadia said that it was not "incentive" but a total "sell out" by the state government with the Chief Minister playing the role of a "broker." He asked Modi to tell how money had changed hands in the Nano deal.

He said the party was not against the Tatas or the Nano car project. State party chief Siddharth Patel said, offering an incentive of Rs 31,000 crore from the public exchequer was not justified for a project worth Rs 2,200 crore.

Modhwadia said that if all the incentives given to the Tatas were included, it came to Rs 60,000 per car.

Quoting the leaked documents, he said the Tatas would roll out as many as 50 lakh cars in 20 years and the people of Gujarat will have to contribute at least Rs 60,000 per car from their pocket to meet the incentives given to the company.

He said there were 80,000 sick industries in Gujarat and if the state government really wanted to give incentives for industrial growth, then it should provide sops to rehabilitate these industries and provide employment to those who had lost their jobs.

He said the diamond industry in the state was suffering badly due to recession but the government had not come forward to rescue them.

Asked if the leaked documents were genuine, Patel said, "the state government has not denied the validity of the documents so far."

On being asked if the party will launch an agitation against the "sell out" and the "kickbacks" received by the BJP in the deal, Modhwadia said, "we will work in consultation with our party leaders."

In a statement, state Industry Minister Saurabh Patel denied the allegations of kickbacks.

He demanded a public apology from the Congress leaders for levelling false allegations against the Chief Minister and the state government. He said the Congress reactions amounted to obstruction on the path of industrial growth of the state.

Heading: Global recession hits Saurashtra’s ginning industry - Indian Express
Content:
Here is the designers' guide to look trendy even when the economy is not looking good

David Abraham of Abraham and Thakore:
Don't bring the drab meltdown mood to your clothes. The optimistic thing to do now is to go in for cheerful dressing, as if nothing has happened. Bring out the classy items from the wardrobe and choose colours like black, dull-gold, coffee and toffee with dull metallic glints that can give a rich and luxurious look even without accessories. Similarly, for our autumn-winter collection, we have worked with baroque influences on a muted-colour palette.

Zubair Kirmani:
Go, mix and match items of clothing to get the perfect look. The ideal thing to do is buy one designer item, like a pair of trousers or a skirt, and then team it with everyday items from the wardrobe. Colours go a long way in defining your dressing sensibility. Invest in safe colours like charcoal-grey, ivory and maroon that can hold its own beyond a single season. Focus on visually rich looking accessories, like mufflers, caps, bangles, which can make you look simple, yet classy.

Anupamaa Dayal:
Recession hardly means dressing down. What it does imply, instead, is to cut out whimsical shopping. Buy one item of clothing, but make sure it is of the best quality. Trans-seasonal dressing is going to be big in a way, since the ideal way to deal with the situation is to buy clothing which is not seasonal. Buy a dress which you can also wear in summer, but team it up with a polo neck sweater, leggings or skinny jeans, and accessories like a dressy shawl or stole. This way you'll have a compact wardrobe, but you'll still be dressed for the season. I am not particularly fond of classic styles of dressing, unless it's pepped up with imaginative accents. For my autumn-winter collection, I have been careful to keep the silhouettes slim because you cannot go in for a layered look if any one item is bulky.

Varun Bahl:
Even though recession might not affect trousseau expenses, you can exercise moderation in your everyday wardrobe. Go for basic clothing, which you can team up with a lot of other accents. Bring back black. Invest in a lot of blacks, since it is one colour that can be worn in many different ways, for both casual and formal occasions. You can go in for bright accessories — bright belts, colourful bags and shoes. These will lend warmth to the entire look.

Heading: Delhi HC questions Gujarat over plea of five blasts accused - Indian Express
Content:
Ginners' association resolves to shutdown more than 570 units twice a week

Global recessionary trends have adversely affected the ginning industry of Saurashtra.

In a recent working committee meeting, the members of the Saurashtra Ginners Association (SGA) resolved to shutdown more than 570 ginning units twice a week and work only in one shift in the remaining five operational days.

The decision was taken in a working committee meeting of SGA held at Gondal on November 10. SGA president, Bharat Vala, told Newsline that the overall demand by the spinning units of southern India has gone down drastically in the last few months due to the prevailing meltdown situation. This has severely affected Saurashtra's ginning industry.

More than 200 gin owners from Saurashtra participated in the meeting and discussed various options to deal with the present problem.

Vala said: "At present, the ginning industry is facing a lot of trouble as buyers are demanding one bale i.e. 170 kg at Rs 22, 100 and our cost of production for one bale is Rs 24, 500. How can we possibly sell with such a huge margin. Even if we sell our product, there is no surety that the buyer will pay us on time due to the global financial crisis. Out of the 570 ginning mills in Saurashtra, only 60 to 70 have been able to start business after Diwali."

He added: "Normally, every ginning unit in Saurashtra produces 300 to 1, 000 bales per day by running their unit round the clock in three shifts. But due to the financial crisis, the production has fallen to 100 to 200 bales per day. Thus, we have resolved to shutdown the units twice a week and to work in just one shift in the remaining five days."

He further revealed the poor situation of the export market, saying that the exports have become nil as none of the units in Saurashtra are able to do international business these days. "We sought the support of the government, but no concrete steps have been taken so far," he said.

Heading: HC dismisses Haaris Ansari’s bail plea - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday sought a response from the Gujarat government on a petition filed by suspected terrorists, allegedly involved in serial blasts, challenging a magistrate's order to grant their custody to the police from that state for investigations into terror attacks in Ahmedabad.

Justice Kailash Gambhir asked the state police to file a reply by December 11. In their petition, accused Mohammed Shakeel and others alleged that the Delhi Police had earlier been obtaining their remand illegally and last month they were handed over to the Gujarat Police. The suspected terrorists alleged that neither the Delhi Police nor the Gujarat Police have informed them about the basis on which their transit remand was taken on October 27. Their counsel submitted before the court that the city police here have filed five different cases against them and illegally obtained 15 days' separate remand for interrogation in each of the FIR, which is against the fundamental rights of a person.

All the suspects, Mohammed Saif, Zeeshan Ahmad, Mohammed Shakeel, Zia-ur-Rehman and Saquib Nissar, were handed over to the Gujarat Police after they moved an application before a Metropolitan Magistrate seeking their transit remand for taking them to Ahmedabad for probing their role in July 26 blasts which claimed 56 lives.

The Magistrate while granting the remand had rejected their plea opposing the remand and seeking details on materials against them.

At least 27 persons have already been arrested by the Gujarat Police in connection with such cases there and names of these suspects have surfaced during the probe.

Heading: Hard times for auto ancillary units in Gujarat - Indian Express
Content: The Gujarat High Court on Tuesday dismissed the bail plea of Haaris Ansari, accused of conspiring bomb blasts at different places in the city between August 2002 and February 2006, along with two other persons. However, judge M D Shah directed the trial court to conduct the trial on a day-to-day basis and complete it within three months. Haaris has already been acquitted in the Nehrunagar blast case of November 2003 due to lack of evidence.

Heading: Girnar Parikrama registers record number of devotees - Indian Express
Content:
Global meltdown leads auto giants to cut down production; manufacturers of auto parts hit

The ancillary auto industry in Gujarat, which was buoyed by the entry of the Tata Motors' Nano car project in the state, is now looking to a grim picture. The industry, which was looking forward to growth and expansion, is now fighting slowdown due to the recent global meltdown.

Due to the global decline in demand for automobiles, giants like Tata Motors and others, are closing shop for six days from November 21. The result, from auto parts manufacturing units in Saurashtra to chemical units in south Gujarat, all are staring at a complete U turn on their growth chart. Over 100 ancillary units in the state, which supply auto parts to Tata Motors, Mitsubishi and Mahindra & Mahindra, have shortened their working time from 6 to 5 days a week, following a nearly 50 per cent dip in business due to the market crash.

Rupesh Shah, President of the Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industries said: "The situation is grave, but then what we are seeing now is just the tip of the iceberg. Ashok Leyland closed down for 15 days; Tata Motors are closing for 6 days, while Patan Ganga has closed down indefinitely. General Motors and Ford are planning a slowdown. This is a clear indication of the effect that will trickle down to the automobile industry and the ancillary units in the state."

He added: "As the sale of automobiles in the US market has decreased to the tune of 30 to 50 per cent; the exports to these countries has collapsed while the domestic market is crashing. The effect will be much more severe in the coming months."

Besides, more than 50 per cent of the total 250 chemical units, which mainly supply dye to the automobile industry – and have a turnover of Rs 800 crore, including exports worth Rs 500 crore – are yet to restart operations after closing for Diwali vacations, affecting more than 2 lakh workers across the state.

Babu Patel, President of the Nandesari Industries Association said: "The automobile-related industries are badly hit. Exports by our chemical industry to around 5,000 clients including the US and European countries have taken a severe dip. While clients are negotiating to buy at the current rate, neglecting the pre-listed price, the manufacturers are trying to liquidate the material at a loss, fearing a further dip in prices."

Kishor Kadvani of Kadvani Forge Limited that manufactures auto parts for Tata Motors, Mitsubishi, Ford and others, said: "The picture has changed within a short period. When a domestic development had generated much of the hope, global factors have crashed all dreams.

Heading: DGCEI unearths duty evasion in tile frit manufacturing units - Indian Express
Content:
More than one million devotees have already participated in Girnar's annual Parikrama during the last five days, the highest figure in the history of the event.

According to forest officials, while 10 lakh people have already completed the 36-km-long Parikrama, a huge number of devotees are still visiting the place from across the state.

M R Vyas, Junagadh ST depot manager, said, "We are running more than hundred extra services to different destinations across Saurashtra region."

According to Vyas, state transport buses are ferrying over one lakh passengers every day from the Junagadh depot.

Railway officials said, on an average, 20,000 people have used the Railways as the means of transport in the last five days alone.

In order to ensure a comfortable journey to the people, railway officials, along with a local NGO, have started 'Annashetra' (free food facility) for passengers. Around 70 'Annashetras' have been opened along the Parikrama route.

Heading: Electoral roll revision targets Modi’s constituency - Indian Express
Content:
The Directorate General of Central Excise Intelligence (DGCEI) has unearthed excise duty evasion of over Rs 25 crore in thirteen ceramic glaze frit manufacturing units in the state, agency sources said on Tuesday.

The 13 manufacturers are under the scanner of the agency for indulging in undervaluation of products by around 50 per cent, sources in DGCEI said. "The units mis-declared the sale price to evade central excise duty of 16 per cent, and have deposited Rs 5 crore so far," sources added.

There are 12-15 gas fired plants of ceramic glazed frit manufacturers strategically located on the outskirts of Vadodara and Mehasana cities where the availability of gas is easy. The manufacturers are working for the Morbi based tiles industry. The units have been engaged in giving glossy finish to tiles by fusing fine glass powder coating on the raw tiles, after baking them in furnace.

Morbi based tile manufacturing units account for 70 per cent of the country's total tile production, a senior excise official said.

Heading: Online voter I-cards to be issued in 2 phases - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 10,502 voters removed from Maninagar, against total deletion of 44,911 votes from all 21 assembly constituencies in the district

Chief Minister Narendra Modi's Assembly constituency, Maninagar, has witnessed the maximum deletion in electoral rolls during the ongoing exercise for the electoral roll revision.

Officially, the main reason given for the move is the demographic changes that have taken place in the constituency, forming part of the eastern segment of the commercial capital of the state.

According to officials, it is the shifting nature of the population in some constituency pockets that has resulted in deletion of as many as 10,502 voters from Maninagar against the total deletion of 44,911 votes from all the 21 assembly constituencies in the district.

The next highest deletion has been recorded in Danilimda, a new constituency formed after the bifurcation of Sarkhej. The total number of deleted voters from Danilimda is 9,410. Next comes Dhandhuka (4,527 voters), Viramgam (3,065 voters) and Sanand (2,807 voters). All are BJP-dominated areas.

The recent deletions include the names of 275 Bangladeshis, who found a place in the electoral list due to some negligence by the electoral staff. Senior electoral officials said they deleted all the Bangladeshi names as soon as the report reached them.

According to election officials, it was not immediately possible for the electoral staff to identify bogus voters, as the Bangladeshis lived among the migrants from West Bengal and shared many similarities with them.

Meanwhile, a special drive will be taken up on November 11 and 16 in order to correct the names in the electoral rolls. Electoral staff and representatives of political parties will be present at every poll booth in all the constituencies. The election department has already put up hoardings all over the district to inform the public about the exercise.

District Collector Hareet Shukla said the total number of voters enrolled so far is a little over 45.11 lakh, including 23.43 lakh males and 21.70 lakh females.

Heading: IIM-A adjudged country’s number one B-school - Indian Express
Content: District Collector Hareet Shukla has said that arrangements to issue online voter I-cards have been made for those who have not received the same. They will, however, have to furnish any one of the 14 documents approved by the Election Commission of India as their residential proof for getting online voter I-cards. The process will be conducted in two phases. While constituencies like Nikol, Dariyapur, Danilimda, Asarwa, Bapunagar, Vatva, Dascroi and Jamalpur will be covered in the first phase from November 17 to November 23, the remaining constituencies of Vejalpur, Naroda, Thakkarbapa Nagar, Maninagar, Naranpura, Ghatlodia, Ellisbridge, Amraiwadi and Sabarmati will be covered in the second phase from November 24 to 30.  A helpline for voters has also been started at the District Collectorate. The helpline number is 27552975.

Heading: Suspecting infidelity, man strangles wife - Indian Express
Content:
In what is being considered as India's most comprehensive B-school ranking, the Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad (IIM-A) has been adjudged the country's number one business school, followed by IIM-Bangalore and IIM-Lucknow at number two and three respectively.

The Delhi-NCR-based Management Development Institute (MDI) and the Jamshedpur-based Xavier's Labour Relations Institute (XLRI) come in at number four and five, edging out a few IIMs to complete the prestigious top 5 slots. IIM-Calcutta is ranked at number 6.

The rankings have been made by business news channel CNBC-TV18 with management portal MBAUniverse.com and research agency TNS.

The report says: "In a first of its kind research and analysis, the 'A of B Ranking' survey looks at three different viewpoints to present the complete 360 degree picture on which are India's leading B-schools."

For the analysis, data was first collected directly from the IIMs and other business schools. The opinion of over 5,000 stakeholders, including recruiters and people from the management community was then taken, which was finally analysed by TNS.

But the surprise in the quantitative rankings comes from the New-Delhi based International Management Institute (IMI), which is ranked at number 8.

The other B-schools in the top-ten list are: Bhavan's S P Jain Institute of Management & Research, Mumbai; Shailesh J Mehta School of Management, IIT Bombay; and Jamnalal Bajaj Institute of Management Studies, Mumbai.

The detailed finding of this survey will be available in the form of a special 200-page guidebook.

According to CNBC TV 18, the rankings guidebook will be on the stands by November 12. Apart from the rankings data, the guide book will carry advice to MBA aspirants on how to choose the right B-school, the student-life at B-schools, as well as tips on doing well in management entrance exams.

Heading: Jamalpur flyover construction hits roadblock as work started without a bhoomi poojan - Indian Express
Content:
Suspecting his wife of infidelity, a 39-year-old businessman from Chandkheda killed her by strangling her with a dupatta. The Adalaj police have registered a case of murder and further investigations are on.

The deceased has been identified as Asha Anand (37), a resident of Shailganga Society in Chandkheda. His husband Sunil is a dealer of a battery company in Adalaj. The couple has two children; a 12-year-old son and a seven-year-old daughter.

According to the police, the incident occurred on Monday night when Asha's daughter came home from a personal tuition and found her mother lying dead on the bed.

Soon, neighbours rushed to the spot and called up the 108 emergency service.

Adalaj Inspector M J Solanki said: "Initially, the accused told us that somebody seem to have killed his wife while trying to rob valuables from the house. On inspecting the scene of the crime, we suspected his version. During intensive interrogation, Sunil broke down and revealed that he had killed Asha as he suspected her of infidelity."

According to Solanki, Sunil first added sleeping pills to a paan he offered to his wife. As she fainted, he strangled her with a dupatta.

Asha's brother Raju Uppal lodged the complaint with the police.

Heading: Professors in six medical colleges to be promoted - Indian Express
Content:
The city will be in for yet longer traffic snarls with the start of the work on the Jamalpur flyover from Gita Mandir to Paldi, across the road connecting Jamalpur Gate to Behrampura police chowky. In fact, work was started a few days ago and has now been stalled at the behest of the political wing for reasons other than technical.

About the recent spat over the unannounced start of work on the Jamalpur flyover project a few days ago, he said the bhoomi poojan was yet to be performed.

"What was started was not actual start of the work but digging of bores for taking soil samples, on which the pillar design and depth would be decided," he said, adding, that sampling was not a khaat muhurt (beginning), which was yet to be performed.

Manubhai Kathrotia, the chairman of roads and buildings committee, said it was discussed at the Monday meeting of the committee that the work was started unannounced and that the officials had also admitted to this. On Monday, Kathrotia ordered stopping of work till the khaat muhurt, which will now be done after sometime.

Even while the Ambedkar Bridge connecting Pirana to Vasna is yet to be restored to normal traffic due to the continuing work of laying of storm water drains on the approach road, the traffic will now be stopped on the Sardar Bridge connecting Jamalpur and Paldi. The road caters not only to the AMTS, but also to the GSRTC bus service to Saurashtra and north Gujarat. As a result, the Agriculture Produce Market Committee and the AMTS head office will also be affected. All these office will have to be shifted elsewhere till the flyover work goes on for about two years.

Municipal Commissioner I P Gautam said that talks were on with the city traffic police for the smooth diversion of traffic necessitated by the flyover project. The APMC is likely to be shifted to Guptanagar, the venue of the Chimanbhai Patel market.

Gautam expressed hope that the Ambedkar Bridge will be ready for use by December 1, enabling the AMC to shift the traffic on Sardar Bridge to Ambedkar Bridge, thereby enabling it to divert the GSRTC traffic to Saurashtra via Nehrunagar and the S G Highway.

Heading: Shukarvaari Bazaar issue: District Collector to question cops - Indian Express
Content:
With the six medical colleges struggling to match up the student – teachers' ratio for sometime now, the Health Department has decided to promote a number of associate and assistant professors in a bid to avoid a staff crunch in the face of an increase in the number of seats. The move is also being looked upon as a way to contain attrition.

The number of professors to be promoted in each of departments in the college, will, however, depend on the requirement of teachers in the respective departments.

Director of Medical Education Dr Vitlani confirmed that the step is being taken as a precautionary measure to provide for an adequate number of teachers for the increasing number of seats in the Post Graduate (PG) courses.

"The teachers at the level of associate professors and above will be eligible for promotions to teach PG courses in all subjects. The promotion is applicable to all colleges," he said.

The decision also means an increment in the salaries of the promoted professors.

The hikes will, however, be as per the Medical Council of India (MCI) norms.

Heading: One held for illegally acquiring land - Indian Express
Content:
Following continuous representations from the affected vendors of the Shukarvaari Bazaar and no solution given by the city police, Vadodara district administration is now planning to ask the city police about the reasons for not resolving the issue.

Officials at the district collectorate said that as per the formal procedure they had forwarded the copy of the memorandum to the city police. However, if frequent representations are made on the same issue, the district administration has to seek proper clarification from the police department, they added.

"Under normal circumstances we just forward the representation to the respective departments, which are entitled to take action to resolve the issue. In case of the Shukarvaari issue, we have already forwarded the letter to the police. But the affected persons have approached us again and now we may seek a detailed explanation from the city police about why the issue has not been resolved," said Vadodara District Collector Vijay Nehra.

The agitating vendors of Shukarvaari Bazaar once again approached the district collector on Tuesday and demanded proper action in the ongoing issue.

Interestingly, the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) has already affirmed that it has nothing to do with the issue and it has to be purely dealt by the police department.

Heading: CCTV cameras not monitored properly at SSG Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
The Panchmahals police arrested one person on Tuesday evening for allegedly occupying 25 acres of land illegally.

The police arrested Devesh Patel after receiving a complaint from a tribal woman from Bakkhar village near Godhra.

According to Deputy Superintendent of Police R V Patel, the complainant, Kankuben Naik, on Monday accused Circle Inspector, Ghanshyam Parmar from Zafranbad, for allegedly conniving with the accused, who had made fake documents and got it approved by Parmar.

The Panchmahals police arrested Patel from his residence at Shraddheya Society in Zafranbad. The police said that Patel is a former BJP taluka member, who along with Nanabhai Pathar, Waliben Naik, Arvind Naik, Khumman Naik, Ramesh Naik and Champaben Naik, had acquired the land illegally.

"The 25-acre land belongs to the two Naik brothers from the city. However, with the assistance of the circle inspector, they managed to fabricate the land documents," said R V Patel.

Devesh Patel has been sent to judicial remand, he added.

Heading: MSU students create sculptures at Gandhinagar IT park - Indian Express
Content:
Out of the 50 CCTV cameras installed last year, half lie non-functional, while those in working condition are not monitored

A year has passed since 50 CCTV cameras were installed at the various wards in the Sir Sayajirao General (SSG) Hospital. But the picture is quite disappointing today. While half of the cameras lie non-functional, those in working condition lack proper monitoring.

The cameras were installed by the 'Rogi Kalyan Samiti' last year, at a cost of Rs 15 lakh. Interestingly, the cameras were installed not just to monitor the functioning of the staff and the security concerns of the hospital, but also to curb the increasing number of thefts on the hospital premises.

"There have been instances wherein newborns have been stolen or parents have abandoned their babies at the premises. The cameras can help us to trace the guilty," said an official on condition of anonymity.

According to the official, 30 cameras in the hospital are fully functional, while the remaining are temporarily out of service. "Some of the wards are undergoing renovation work due to which the wiring of around 20 cameras have been damaged. It will be repaired once the work is complete," said M H Gadhavi, executive officer of SSG Hospital.

The fact, however, remains that even the 30 CCTVs that are in a working condition are not monitored properly. "Ask the officials for the past records and they won't have it. Such a huge hospital with thousands of patients coming in every day is one of the most susceptible places for mishaps and other incidences. But proper monitoring is completely absent here," said a doctor on condition of anonymity.

He added: "Even when things are recorded, it is of no use, as the images captured on the screen are blurred and dark."

Heading: Workshop on sculpture to begin at MS University from November 17 - Indian Express
Content:
The project demands not only sculpting skill but also technical expertise, say faculty lecturers

While the IT Park being developed by the Raheja Group of architectures at Gandhinagar is believed to have drawn an investment of Rs 3,000 million, eight students of the Fine Arts institute of Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU) have been selected to add beauty to this upcoming knowledge corridor.

In what is being seen as a good learning opportunity, the students of the Sculpture Department of the Fine Arts College are assigned a project to make eight sculptures, as high as 23 feet tall.

The students were selected by Raheja Group's chief architect L Bihari this May to cast the sculptures. The installation cost of each sculpture is likely to be around Rs 1 lakh. Some of these sculptures have already been installed in the IT park.

The themes used by the students for sculptures depict a combination of logical and abstract forms of arts. Prof Deepak Kannal, Dean, Faculty of Fine Arts, told Newsline: "It is a good exercise for students to build structures as big as 23 feet."

He said erecting such huge pieces demands not only sculpting skills, but also technical expertise. The experience will build the students' confidence, he said.

Nitayanada Ojha, one of the students selected for the project, said: "I have installed an abstract form having a concept of mirror images. I have used iron sheets in my sculpture."

While one side of Ojha's model shows modern buildings, the other side depicts the environment on the riverbank. The form is modern: overlapping with semicircles, triangles and squares. However, the logic of the material used reflects the environment where the piece stands.

Another student, Nikhilesh Kanzariya, is casting models of hands and faces. He said: "The involvement of kite flying enthusiasts in the process is so deep that they feel themselves attached to the string. My model makes an attempt to display this sentiment."

Kanzariya has used metal pipes to show the string and fibres to cast models of faces showing different expressions.

Aqueel Ahmed, a lecturer of the sculpture department, said: "It is a rare chance for the students, and the faculty is also helping them to cast their thoughts in their creations."

The project will be over in a few months' time, said FFA lecturers.

Heading: Out of their Village - Indian Express
Content:
The Sculpture Department of the Faculty of Fine Arts (FFA), MSU, will organise a workshop on bronze casting from November 17 to 30, wherein art students and artists from all over the country are expected to participate. The aim of the workshop is to bring the artists under one roof and share their experiences in the field of sculpture.

Prof Deepak Kannal, Dean of FFA said: "It is for the first time that such a national-level workshop is being organised in the department. Funds amounting to Rs 8 lakh have been given by the UGC for the event."

He added that the FFA will invite students and artists from Shantiniketan, Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Fine arts students from Kolkata, Lucknow, Delhi College of Arts, Hyderabad as well as from the J J School of Arts.

Around six students and a teacher from each university will be able to participate here. The universities have also shown their readiness to bring more students with them as observers of the workshop, he said.

Prof Kannal said the foundry at the department is one of the best in India. He said the Delhi College of Arts is also setting up a foundry, wherein facilities will be made available to the students to learn how to cast models. He said: "A number of artists have also volunteered to attend the workshop on their own expenses and will make students conversant in recent sculpting techniques."

Heading: Problem Solved - Indian Express
Content:
Within a dark maze, a crinkled, old face with eyes looking upwards lights the way. As you move forward, the large-format images change from the old to the young — wrinkled, convoluted smiles give way to stubborn chins, soft eyes and frank expressions. Harsh climate and unyielding landscape too surface in the photographs, adding a morbid sobriety to people's expressions. Delhi-based photographer Samar Singh Jodha's exhibition "Phaneng", with its dozen 6 ft x 5 ft portraits, at Religare's arts.i gallery, is a journey into the village Phaneng in the Tinsukia district of Assam, and its Tai Phake people. With just about 150 families, Tai Phake is a dwindling tribe.

"There is a political theme at play. The exercise of moving through darkness is to let the viewer experience the lives of the tribal people without electricity or water," says Jodha, 39, who is bringing them into the mainstream — at least through his photographs.

Surprisingly, Jodha began as a fashion and automobile photographer, but on the way he documented the lives of Bhopal survivors and began to balance commercial photography with severe social documentation. He chanced upon Phaneng in November 2004 while driving through the Stilwell road built during World War II, connecting northeast India to southwest China. He spent time at the village, teaching kids and helping build a monastery. Perhaps that explains the relative ease with which his camera seems to have moved through the place, resulting in piquant visuals.

While the guests admired the images in the gallery, outside the chefs doled out traditional Tai Phake food. "The concept is great and the presentation is good," said the photographer Amit Pasricha. Meanwhile, designer Ritu Kumar said, "I have known Jodha since the mid-1980s when we worked on fashion shows. Later, we worked on a book Costumes and Textiles of Royal India."

The works on canvas, available in editions of four, begin at Rs 2.85 lakh, while a set of 16 x 20 inch prints is pegged at Rs 2.5 lakh.

The exhibition is on till December 8. Contact 43727003

Heading: Project Paris - Indian Express
Content:
It is the unofficial exorcist of maths phobia. Now, Kumon, the Japanese way of learning maths, finds many disciples in the Capital

Sanidhya Sharma has a secret that every child in his class would like to dig out — how did he suddenly start scoring high marks in maths? "It is because of Kumon, but don't tell anybody," grins the Class IV student of DPS, East of Kailash. It's a secret that around three lakh students in 45 countries share.

In 1954 in Osaka, another eight-year-old boy had trouble with arithmetic and came home with a terrible report card. As in any other home, the mother put her foot down and said this just couldn't go on; and the father, a teacher, finally set about making a system for his kid to learn maths. The father was Toru Kumon and his mode of teaching soon became a movement and the unofficial exorcist of math phobia.

After doing its equivalent of bell, books and candle in classrooms across the world, Kumon came to Delhi three years ago. It barely managed 100 students then; now it has about 1,000 students poring over worksheets everyday.

At its very basic, it breaks maths and languages into fundamentals, which are then drilled into students, through repetitive practice. "For a young child tackling additions, the first step is to add one. He has to finish several pages of worksheets in which he adds one to numbers. It is only when the lesson is ingrained in his head that he moves on to adding two," says Shaista Shaw, field support and planning manager of Kumon. For English, the thrust is on developing reading skills and comprehension by breaking lessons down to components like simple sentences and grammar.

While critics have pointed out that Kumon's drilling method stops kids from thinking on their feet and robs math of its many joys, Kumon happily swears by homework — and most children don't complain. They attend classes just twice a week but take home enough worksheets to practise every day. "The Kumon system revolves around the habit of everyday practice. It is 20 per cent concept and 80 per cent repetition. After a concept like addition, multiplication, verb or adjective is explained, a student has to fill as many as 10 pages of worksheet using that one concept," explains Shaw. Sanchi Gupta, a Class VII student of DPS, RK Puram, who is enrolled for English and never misses her daily ritual with the Kumon worksheets, says, "I've been here for six months, but I feel more confident about my language and diction."

The system of repetition and constant practice gets a thumbs-up even from teachers like Alpana Ahuja of Amity International School. "While schools teach formula and calculation methods, Kumon breaks it down into components and makes sure that each component is practised repeatedly until there's no room for error."

There is no blackboard, special learning aid or, after the first few lessons, a teacher. Students tackle worksheets by themselves and at their own pace, and can move on to higher grades in a few months. Yajur Ahuja, a Class V student at Mother's International, for instance, will soon begin Class VII level mathematics. "So, while his classmates in school are working on decimals, he will be handling linear equations and unitary method here. This means his school maths becomes very easy," says an instructor.

At its eight centres across the NCR, Kumon has four-year-olds as well as university students, doing simple calculation or differential calculus. On the anvil are centres in Chennai and Pune. The fee is Rs 1,461 per subject per month, plus an enrolment fee of Rs 674.

Contact www.kumon.co.in

Heading: Waxing Lyrical - Indian Express
Content:
As the Tranoi Fair celebrates India in its autumn-winter edition, designer Abhishek Dutta gets a surprise invite

While he was prepping the models and giving last-minute tucks for his comeback show at the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week last month, designer Abhishek Dutta (inset) had little inkling that someone in the audience already had big plans for him. "I saw Michael Hadida, the owner of the prestigious Tranoi Fair, in the front row and was happy, particularly because he had earlier come to my stall and browsed through the clothes. But I was so busy ensuring everything went off without a hitch that I didn't think anything beyond that," says Dutta.

It was his return to the Delhi fashion week, after four consecutive showings at the Lakme Fashion Week in Mumbai. Now, Dutta can book another ticket — to Paris and its prestigious Tranoi Fair.

Dutta's collection — a series of quirky outfits that included zippered cargos, khadi jackets, shorts and capris and dresses with appliqués, all in linen and cotton — subtly played up the Indian theme on overtly western silhouettes, and won him accolades from fashionistas. Much later, the designer from Kolkata came to know that Hadida had included him and newbie designer duo Nidhi and Pankaj for the autumn-winter edition of the fair, scheduled to take off in Paris between March 2 and 5 next year.

Incidentally, Tranoi is celebrating India as its theme at this year's fair, with an India Pavilion showcasing the works of over 15 of India's top designers. "I first heard the news from the media, but it was only when there was a correspondence from Hadida's office that I was convinced that I was actually going," laughs 29-year-old Dutta, who launched his pret label, Adnormal, in 2004, and now supplies to over 20 stores across the country, including Kimaya and Azara.

While the designer is busy working on the orders that he has received after the fashion week, his blueprint for Tranoi is also ready. "I am not much into bling since it's only suited to the Indian context. I am working towards developing new fabrics and reviving old weaving techniques, so that my Indian sensibilities come across even on a western silhouette," says Dutta, who counts actors Vidya Balan, Salman Khan, Abhishek Bachchan, and Raima and Riya Sen among his clients.

Heading: Services staring at big defeat - Indian Express
Content:
Prasoon Joshi talks about his songs in Ghajini and how interfering Aamir Khan is

In B-town, everyone is on song, even if it is a shaven, tattooed Aamir Khan who can't remember his phone number. Little wonder, Prasoon Joshi found himself penning poetry for all the brawn and brawl on display in Ghajini. "It is a pacy thriller with a lot of action and high energy, but the songs are extremely important to the narrative," says Joshi who has written five songs, all composed by AR Rahman, for the Khan starrer.

The film is a remake of a Tamil movie that was released three years ago, with songs written by N. Muthukumar, but Joshi says the Hindi soundtrack is completely original. "I did not even listen to the southern version as I did not want to be influenced in anyway," says Joshi, who, however, watched bits of the film to "gather a feel of it".

A little-known fact about ad man Joshi is that he is a trained classical musician who likes to compose and sing as well, but he has given them a miss in Ghajini. "I think it is very important for a lyricist to have a sense of music since it's then that the song shapes up wholly," says Joshi. He has composed and sung jingles for Alpenliebe and Happy Dent, among others. "But it's not something I'd do for films," he says.

Bollywood has heard enough complaints of Aamir Khan's interference, but Joshi thinks otherwise. "He is a very intelligent man and when he has a suggestion, it's often valid. When it is not, we argue a lot and whoever has a more powerful logic wins. So I'd say there's close understanding and mutual respect that allow us to bounce ideas off each other," he says.

If Joshi's poetry is not enough, then maybe you can watch the songs for another reason — one of them has Khan sporting six different hairstyles. Guess it's all relevant to the narrative.

Heading: At 36, Yere still yearns for improvement - Indian Express
Content:
Hosts collapse for a paltry 77; Faiz Fazal slams century to put Vidarbha in command

As the fog overstayed its welcome, the sun shone rather late on Tuesday. Given the previous day's gloom, however, no one complained. The wetness had vanished, the swing appeared negotiable, and the stage was perfect for the Services batsmen to overhaul Vidarbha's modest first innings total of 151.

It was easier said than done. The hosts were off to the worst possible start — the first and the second ball of the day from Sandeep Singh disturbing Devendra Israni's timber and finding AK Mohanty's edge, respectively. The remaining batsmen didn't offer any resistance either and Services folded up for 77 lasting just 31.4 overs with Sandeep settling for a five-for (5/27).

The man who really wanted to make amends for his first-innings low was Faiz Fazal. When the Vidharba opener brought up his century with his eleventh boundary, apart from the scenic sunset into the airport, there were at least two things that were worth noticing simply for cricketing reasons.

One, how he picked the worst ball of the over (last ball of the over from AK Mohanty) to glide it past the third-man fence after defending the first five and two, the way he reacted — just a second's response with a raised bat towards the dressing room without making too much of a fuss (he didn't even take out his helmet).

Punishing bad balls was evident in the way Fazal's legs moved against spinners — mostly backfoot shots and, with time, he started getting atop the pace of Pankaj and Rakesh Kumar, with the slightest nudges racing to the fence. His keeping the helmet right on his head after a sapping 314 minutes in the middle was symbolic of the way he carried his bat through the day to 119 not out with Vidarbha leading by 252 runs with eight wickets remaining.

Fazal saw through a dicey morning spell from both Kumars, and then after Pankaj's reverse swing found Amit Despande and Alind Naidu in front of stumps, reined in the temptation of going for the big shots after his century.

"Tomorrow's first hour will be crucial for us as there's a lot of time (two days) remaining in the match. After that we can go for the big shots," said Fazal, downplaying his century to a couple of 50-plus scores on grassy tracks during the last season.

As Fazal played the waiting game, Services too will have to do the same on Wednesday.

"We really don't have any choice left other than waiting for them to declare. The track has become batting-friendly and now we are only hoping our batsmen to come good in the second innings," said JP Pandey, Services coach.

Brief scores: Vidarbha 151 and 178 for 2 in 74 overs (Faiz Fazal batting 119; Pankaj Kumar 2/59) lead Services 77 (Sandeep Singh 5/27) by 252 runs

Heading: Shifting village could put Games in ‘jeopardy’ - Indian Express
Content:
At an age when most players begin planning their retirements, Yere Goud, the 36-year-old Ranji veteran for Railways, is busy working on his new batting grip to negotiate reverse swing. Goud is using a custom-made inner, which has a half cut ball stiched inside, while batting in the nets.

"I have been using it for some time now. Basically this year, I want to use my top hand more while manoeuvring the incoming ball, and that's why I am using it during nets," Goud says, adding, "I'll never use them during a match."

"Middle-order batsmen like me are more prone to reverse swing. The ball starts to reverse around the 30-35th over and bowlers aim at your pads or the stumps. I am doing all this to counter them," says Goud, who made his first-class debut way back in the 1994-95 season. Hungry for runs and striving for constant improvement, he has also shortened his back lift. "Nowadays I play with a low back lift," he adds.

Good start
In his first match back with the Railways last week in Bangalore, Goud made an unbeaten 122, helping the team take three points based on first innings lead over Karnataka — the side he had played for last year. "I had some personal problems and so Railways gave me a 2 year-old NOC to play there. This year after coming back in the Elite Division, they called me," he says when quizzed about his shifting base from Bangalore.

His Bangalore innings may have been very good for the side, but it made his pocket lighter by Rs 500 for breaking team discipline. "I played with a blue helmet on. The team got a new green coloured helmet on the second day of the match and I wasn't too comfortable with it. I continued playing with my older one and hence the fine," he says with a smile.

"We have a discipline rule within the team, whoever is found breaking it has to pay the fine. We use the money for our juice and tea," he adds. Even team captain Sanjay Bangar was 'fined' the same amount for turning up in the wrong training colours.

Heading: Rahul overwhelms, overwhelmed by, St Stephen’s College - Indian Express
Content:
Shifting the Commonwealth Games village from its present location at this juncture could "seriously jeopardise" Delhi's chances of hosting the mega event in 2010, Commonwealth Games Federation (CGF) Coordination Commission chairman Austin Sealy said on Tuesday.

Sealy was reacting to the setting up of a four-member committee by Delhi High Court to study the ecological harm the Games village, which is being constructed on the Yamuna river-bed, could possibly have.

"The federation is aware that an issue affecting the village is presently before the courts in India and therefore considers it inappropriate to comment on the matter other than to note that any change, at this late stage, to the Games village arrangements would seriously jeopardise India's hosting of the Games," said Sealy at the end of two-day meeting of the commission.

The Games village, however, was not the only issue Sealy touched upon; he was also surprised to find that the work for the cycling velodrome had not started yet. "That is a real concern. If the work is not started immediately, it will be difficult to complete things before the Games," he cautioned.

He suggested that a temporary velodrome could be a solution, but added that arrangements like changing rooms, press centre and certain other features needed to be permanent. Sealy then sought and assurance from organising committee chairman Suresh Kalmadi on the issue who, in turn, said things would be taken care of. "I have been told that tenders have already been floated and things will start moving by December 2008," Kalmadi said.

That apart, the Coordination Commission chairman felt things were "moving in the right direction" and they were "happy with the progress so far". Sealy also said his colleagues had visited the Games village and were impressed. "I will make a visit tomorrow to see if I can endorse their views," he added.

Heading: Blast suspect to High Court: Gujarat cops are after me - Indian Express
Content:
Lok Sabha MP Rahul Gandhi was back at his alma mater — St Stephen's College — but, again, found little occasion to ask questions. Instead, he found himself answering several.

"The political system in India is very closed — there is no internal democracy in the political parties. Opening up the political system can give us potential," he told students during an interaction on Tuesday. His statement was in reply to a question regarding AICC general secretary Margaret Alva's resignation from the party after alleging foul play in distribution of election tickets.

The interaction was organised by the College Students' Union Society and the Alumni Association.

There was, however, hardly any reference to Rahul's recent statement — that students, during his time at the college, were not encouraged to ask questions. But steering clear of any controversy, the Amethi MP today praised the college and the teachers who had taught him during his brief stint. "I don't think it is a crime to ask questions," he said. "Asking questions lies at the heart of progress."

Calling those gathered the "most intelligent students in the country", Rahul said asking the right questions lead to change.

But the discussion that began with questions about India's education system was, a student said, "a study on how to avoid a straight answer".

"Our education system is highly controlled and its growth is being restricted due to vested interests and other factors. It is up to us to open it up," the MP said. He also called for teachers and students to be given autonomy in running educational institutions and curriculum: "A politician sitting in Parliament should not have the power to place people in charge of educational institutions."

While students seemed impressed by the ease with which Rahul interacted, most complained that he did not in effect answer any question straight. "He didn't really say anything," a "disappointed" third-year student said. "He just cross-questioned people and made funny statements in rhetorical ways."

But another student, clearly overwhelmed, said: "He greeted us and shook hands with us instead of being aloof."

Still another, who lined up to shake Rahul's hand as the Congress leader walked back to his car, said, "He was sparring easily with the students. He could have been all formal but he wasn't."

Heading: Now more in basket: From X to Z+, cops guard 457 - Indian Express
Content:
High Court seeks reply from police

The Delhi High Court on Tuesday sought a response from Gujarat Police by December 11 on allegations by Mohammed Shakeel, one of the five accused in the September 13 serial blasts.

Shakeel, who has spent 39 days in custody since his arrest on September 21, today submitted an application in court saying he fears "bodily harm" from the Gujarat Police force. "Hum tumhari haddi pasli ek kardengey," Shakeel states in his 14-page application before Justice Kailash Gambhir, describing a threat from "a member of Gujarat Police (team)".

"The accused put on record that he had been threatened by a member of the team from Gujarat Police when he was taken to Gujarat," the application filed by advocates Jawahar Raja and Mayur Suresh for Shakeel says.

In the application, Shakeel claims he has "no previous criminal record".

The application also criticises Delhi Metropolitan Magistrate Vinay Singhal's October 27 decision allowing Gujarat Police to take him and four others — Mohammed Saif, Zeeshan Ahmad, Zia-ur-Rehman and Saquib Nissar — to Gujarat on a transit remand. "That he was threatened with bodily harm by a member of the same police team which sought his remand was reason enough to refuse application for the remand (by Gujarat Police)," Shakeel's counsel submitted.

"The magistrate did not appreciate that the accused has already been extensively interrogated by Gujarat Police while he was in custody of Delhi Police's Special Cell," the counsel said. The counsel pointed out the magistrate's "error" in not appreciating how the accused persons were "coerced to sign several blank papers and write out elaborate stories that he dictated".

The counsel pleaded that the court should declare illegal the "custody of the petitioner (Shakeel) with either Gujarat Police or Delhi Police Special Cell from October 27". The counsel said the "maximum period of detention for any number of offences, howsoever serious, can only be 15 days so long as the offences are not part of entirely different transactions."

This defence submission is in conflict with the police version that FIRs registered against the accused in connection with the September 13 blasts were to be distinguished as separate cases involving separate probes. The Gujarat Police required the five accused for investigations into the blast in Ahmedabad on July 26, which claimed 56 lives. The transit remand was given for the case registered with the Maninagar Police station there.
