All five are booked under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Explosive Substances Act and Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in Delhi.

On November 1, the Delhi Police had apprised Justice Gambhir of the alleged recovery of "incriminating material" from the arrested suspects. The police listed their find as two laptops, a pen drive, video cassettes, 42 CDs used by alleged mastermind Mohammed Atif Ameen, Zeeshan and Shakeel.

Heading: Smog parts, airlines assure: ready to take on fog season - Indian Express
Content:
The Ministry of Home Affairs increased the workload for the Delhi Police recently by recommending heightened security for four prominent politicians, under the Z+, Z and Y categories.

The ministry has accorded Union Steel Minister Ram Vilas Paswan Z + security. Two others — Bharatiya Janata Party's MP from Balrampur (Uttar Pradesh) Brij Bhushan Sharan and Union Minister of State for External Affairs E Ahmed — have been granted the Z cover. Bahujan Samaj Party MP from Unnao, Uttar Pradesh, Brijesh Pathak has been upgraded to the Y category.

With the recent additions, the total number of VIPs the city police guards has jumped to 457. A senior officer said: "There are five levels of security — Z+, Z, Y+, Y AND X. The strength depends on the varied degrees of threat perception."

A spokesperson of MP Brij Bhushan Sharan was asked what danger the politician faced. He said: "He was shot once before. However, security agencies assess the threat and decide on the strength of the cover. The MP had Y category for 10 years and has recently been upgraded to Z." Police officers said the request for increased security keeps pouring in but the ministry has the last word on who will get what.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (Security) Ajay Kumar explained how the security strength is determined for a person. "A Joint Security Resume of that person is created with inputs from the Intelligence Bureau, the police's Special Cell and the local police. This is then forwarded to the ministry which decides on the category of security." He added that the Z+ wing has 52 personnel who shuffle according to the itinerary of the VIP.

Police sources said that names for the Z+ cover have gone up to 30 this year, which include two diplomats. There are 68 people who get the Z category, among them four diplomats. A total of 243 VIPs are cocooned in the Y category, while the number for the X grade is 81.

The Z+ cover is the mightiest — six personal security officers (PSOs), two head constables, twelve constables, one escort and one pilot vehicle. The Z has three PSOs, two head constables, eight constables and an escort vehicle. Sources added the Y category consists of two PSOs, one head constable and four constables while the X category has just two PSOs.

Heading: Poll process ‘discouraging’, Delhi spells out why it doesn’t vote - Indian Express
Content:
Airlines today maintained that winter for those flying in and out of the Capital would pass comfortably despite the fog, and impending flight delays the weather has had in recent years.

Fliers had it easy on Tuesday after a three-day spell of heavy smog over the Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport. The visibility at the airport today improved to 2,000 metres, after it had gone as low as 500 metres in the past three days.

While the Meteorological Department predicts a thick blanket of fog over Delhi from December 10 to February 15, domestic airlines are expected to suffer more during this period as most of them are yet to ensure that their pilots get training to use the Category-III (CAT III) compliant runways.

But airlines officials said they are well equipped to deal with the fog season with a sizeable pool of pilots trained in CAT III of the Instrument Landing System (ILS). "Most of our pilots are trained in CAT III-B. There's no need to reschedule flights during peak hours," an Air India spokesperson said.

Incidentally, at least 80 flights were delayed on Saturday when the airport's new ILS-compliant runway reported a technical snag and remained non-operational for about an hour in the morning.

Airlines did not divulge how many CAT-III trained pilots they have but assured that the figures would be made public soon. A Kingfisher Airlines spokesperson said: "We have the largest pool of CAT III-A and CAT III-B-trained pilots. If the infrastructure is supportive, there will be no problem."

Winds could mean havoc
The Met Department, meanwhile, said though visibility improved today, it may reduce again once the winds pick up as the winter sets in. "The smoke and dust seemed settled after 10 am today, while there has been no change in the winds," aid R K Jenamani, director of IGI Met Department, said. "There will be a few spells of CAT-III dense fog on certain days from December 10 to February 15."

WHAT IS CAT?
CAT I: A precision instrument approach and landing with a decision height not lower than 200 feet

CAT II: Landing with a decision height lower than 200 feet but not lower than 100 feet

CAT III-A: Allows landing with a decision height lower than 100 feet or no decision height, but runway visual range not less than 700 feet

CAT III-B: Allows landing with decision height lower than 50 feet or no decision height, and runway visual range less than 700 feet but above 150 feet

CAT III-C: Allows landing with no decision height and no runway visual range limitations. Capable of using an aircraft's autopilot to land, and also provide guidance along runway surface 0DGCA has said airlines ready to use this advanced system would be given priority for take offs

Heading: ‘BSP not a Dalit party’ - Indian Express
Content:
Ever thought why so many Delhiites do not think twice before voting in reality shows but only around 53 or so per cent of the population makes it to the polling booths in an election?

The National University of Singapore has an interesting answer: the increasing cost of participation affects voters' motivation to exercise their franchise.

According to a study conducted by the university, people are motivated to vote for their favourite reality TV show contestant since it is just an SMS away. But the tiresome procedure of electioneering — right from registering one's name to the chaos in and outside polling booths on D-day — discourages people from lining up outside polling booths.

Uttam Prakash, a former NUS student conducted the research — titled 'Low participation rates in Indian elections: Search ways to reduce participation costs' — in 2006 as part of his university curriculum. Reason: "I was alarmed at the decreasing percentage of voters in India."

Prakash took up Delhi as the sample state and handed out questionnaires to some 500 people for the research.

He says, "The costs involved in turning an electorate into a voter are essentially the costs of getting registered as an electorate, going to the poll, casting one's vote, returning back, and the costs involved in gathering information for making a choice.

"People are not stationary. They keep moving from one place to another — for job or marriage or other reasons. Getting oneself registered again and again is a cumbersome process, and a big deterrent for voting."

Prakash says the cost (or time spent in) of getting information about contestants acts as the biggest repellent in India. "The media does not properly disseminate performance of politicians, or what they stand for. This makes all politicians look identical," he says.

In the end, he says, it leaves voters confused.

In his research project, Prakash also points out ways in which the problems can be tackled: "Adding new services, expanding existing services, organising outreach to potential beneficiaries not using the service effectively, customising some existing services to a particular sub-population, and linking available existing service systems to take advantage of potential synergies can be used to reduce the cost."

By way of example, Prakash says, "A college student has to submit documents at the time of getting an identity card from the college. The same details can be shared by the college and the electoral office to make a voter's I-card too."

Heading: Denied tickets by Cong, BJP, Jats to go it alone - Indian Express
Content:
"In the Delhi election, where Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) has fielded its candidates, we've asked voters of Muslim community to vote for SAD candidates." — Maulana Habib-ur-Rehman Sa-ani, the Shahi Imam of Punjab

Party general secretary Tanwar spells out social engineering formula

After winning Uttar Pradesh with the backing of more upper caste candidates than ever in its history, the Bahujan Samaj Party is repeating the social engineering formula in Delhi. For the Assembly elections, the party has fielded barely 10 or 12 Dalit candidates.

Going ag ainst the party's image built over the years, some BSP candidates might even feature in the list of wealthiest contestants for the Assembly polls. And leading the race from the front is Kanwar Singh Tanwar, the party's general secretary for Delhi and reportedly the richest MLA-aspirant.

Spelling out the party's new mantra, Tanwar told Newsline: "BSP is not a Dalit party any more. It now represents a vast backward population of the country. But the wealthy candidates are all social workers first."

Tanwar declared assets worth Rs 150 crore, while filing his nomination on Monday with the returning officer (Mehrauli). His assets include three luxury cars, two apartments, a farmhouse and agricultural and non-agricultural land worth nearly Rs 141 crore.

There are at least six more candidates expected to show assets worth more than

Rs 100 crore.

Some of the names include Brahm Singh Bidhuri, president of the party's state unit, who owns dairies and property worth crores in the Okhla constituency, from where he is contesting the polls.

Others are Ram Singh Netaji, the long-time Congress loyalist, who had won the elections from Badarpur seat against the Congress' present candidate Ram Vir Singh Bidhuri in 1998. Bidhuri had then been a part of the Nationalist Congress Party and had joined the Congress in September.

While Netaji could not be contacted despite repeated attempts, sources say his assets are worth crores.

"He is a rich man and has the means to invest in social work," Kanwar Singh Tanwar said. Tanwar himself runs a trust called the Narayani Devi Trust which has a mobile clinic in his constituency which treats close to 700 people a day.

Tanwar said, "We do not claim to be poor, but we are a minority among our community, which is predominantly poor." Both Kanwar Singh and Netaji are from the Gurjjar community.

The Bahujan Samaj Party, under instructions from the party higher-ups in Lucknow, did not make public the list of the approved 62 candidates from Delhi till the last moment.

"We have been instructed to keep our options open," a senior leader from the party's Delhi unit said.

Sources in the party say there are hardly 6-7 seats that have been given to Dalit candidates and the same number to the candidates from the Valmiki community (sweepers).

Besides that, the party has chosen to give tickets to nine Brahmin candidates, nine Gurjjar candidates, and at least seven candidates from the Punjabi community.

"The sole aim is to win with the help of ground work," Tanwar said. Lokesh Dikshit, an upper caste candidate who will be contesting from Rohtas Nagar, is one such candidate. He owns a dairy business in Baghpat district of UP and had spread it to Delhi only a few years back.

Speaking to Newsline, Dikshit said, "We want an opportunity to contest the polls, not just as party loyalists, which the BJP and Congress lay too much emphasis on; we have been

instructed to work on

the ground and have been doing so."

Heading: Not Jolly Good: Sheila opponent sore over officer’s appointment - Indian Express
Content:
Having been cold-shouldered by both the Congress and the BJP, members of the Jat community will now have their own candidate in Najafgarh, Kirari and Mehrauli Assembly constituencies. The village panchayats in these villages feel both parties have ignored the interests of Jat voters.

In Najafgarh, the BJP has given its ticket to Rajesh Sharma, a Brahmin, while the Congress to Kamal Singh Yadav. "Najafgarh has more than 40 per cent Jat voters, but neither the BJP nor the Congress gave its tickets to a Jat," said Choudhary Khajan Singh, a Jat leader from Najafgarh said.

Around 20 villages of the Najafgarh constituency were demanding a ticket for Baljeet Singh Dagar from the BJP. Dagar is an active Jat leader of the area. "They have given the ticket to an outsider. We will not support the BJP in this election," added Khajan Singh.

The Congress councillor from Mehrauli, Satbir Sharma, has also been denied a ticket.

"The chief minister did not want me to get the ticket, but I will win the elections," says Satbir. Satbir, an ex-mayor of Delhi, has quit the party and is now contesting the election as an independent candidate. He has the support of six village panchayats.

"Even members of the Block Congress, Mahila Congress, Youth Congress and the NSUI were present in the panchayat meeting on Sunday and have offered me support," said Satbir.

"It is unfortunate that Satbir was not given a ticket. He has been living in the area and has worked for the people. But the village panchayats will support him. We will ensure he wins the elections against Yoganand Shastri of the Congress," said Azad Singh, of Katwaria Sarai.

It is the same story in Kirari Assembly constituency. Both the Congress and the BJP here gave tickets to people who are not from the area. Anil Jha, former DUSU president, is the BJP candidate.

Panchayat candidate Pushp Raj, a BJP worker who was denied a ticket even during the councillor election last year, said, "Nobody in the villages will vote either for the Congress or the BJP as they have completely ignored the interests of the locals."

Heading: No violation of model code, says Malhotra - Indian Express
Content:
Bharatiya Janata Party MLA Vijay Jolly filed a complaint to the Chief Electoral Officer against Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit for violating the model code of conduct by appointing Justice M M Sarin as Lokayukta on November 6 after the elections were announced.

According to the complaint filed by Jolly, Sarin's appointment is in violation of provision 6 (d) of part VII of the model code of conduct of the Election Commission. "As per the Model Code of Conduct, from the time elections are announced by the Commission, ministers and other authorities should not make any ad-hoc appointments in government or public undertakings which will have the effect of influencing voters in favour of the party in power," Jolly wrote in his complaint.

Lokayukta is a standalone body which has been constituted to eradicate corruption. The Lokayukta Act takes within its ambit ministers including the chief minister, Members of the Legislative Assembly, Municipal Councillors, and the Chairman, Vice Chairman, Managing Director and Members of Boards which are subject to the control of the Government. The Lokayukta can inquire into complaints against these public functionaries.

Justice Sarin is the third Lokyukta of the Capital. The seat of the Lokayukta has been vacant since March this year when Justice Mohammad Shamim retired. "This is a malafide act of the Congress government to strategise the appointment of the Lokayukta after a delay of nearly seven months, just before the Delhi Polls. It is a deliberate and calculated move with the intent to influence Delhi voters in favour of the party in power," Jolly wrote in his complaint.

Heading: VOTERS SPEAK: Abhimanyu Prasad (26) - Indian Express
Content:
In a reply to the Election Commission, BJP's chief ministerial candidate Vijay Kumar Malhotra denied he had violated the model code of conduct while filing his nomination on Saturday. Malhotra had been served a notice by the EC on overcrowding the returning officer's room and bringing with him a huge crowd of supporters. "I went to file my nomination accompanied only by my wife and Harsh Vardhan," said Malhotra.

A crowd of persons had collected outside the office long before I reached there. I did not bring anyone along, neither the police nor the officials made a request to them to disperse," he wrote in his reply.

At the time of Malhotra's filing the nomination papers, senior BJP leader Arun Jaitley, Om Prakash Chautala, Prakash Singh Badal, Sukhbir Singh Badal, Vijay Goel, Harshvardhan, Subash Arya and Arti Mehra were present in the room of the returning officer. According to the EC rules, not more than five people are allowed.

Heading: Uphaar victims seek Kant prosecution - Indian Express
Content:
Jolly shuns publicity
Scared after the Election Commission's notice to the Bharatiya Janata Party chief ministerial candidate V K Malhotra on overcrowding the returning officer's room, MLA Vijay Jolly, went in one car, which he stopped a long distance from the office and walked till the room waving to television cameras.

In a political stunt of sorts, he managed to rope in BJP leader L K Advani's son, Jayant Advani, to be one of the persons proposing his nomination. Whether such muscle flexing is going to help Jolly remains to be seen.

Heading: ‘Unclean’ DDU gets even doctors now - Indian Express
Content:
Families of the victims of Uphaar cinema fire tragedy on Tuesday pleaded before the Delhi High Court for the prosecution of former DCP Amod Kant for allegedly allowing the theatre managers to install additional seats, blocking an exit gate in the balcony. Kant is contesting elections on a Congress ticket from Sangam Vihar Assembly constituency.

Concluding the argument on behalf of the Associations of Victims of Uphaar Tragedy (AVUT), senior counsel KTS Tulsi submitted that "the then DCP Kant, deliberately and knowingly turned a blind eye to the safety regulations to favour the accused-owners of the cinema."

Heading: Three convicted for murder of Congress Seva Dal leader - Indian Express
Content:
* At least 5 docs down with urinary infections * 3 to 4 patients per bed * 73 share three toilets without water

In a dingy ward on the fifth floor of Delhi Government's Deen Dayal Upadhyay (DDU) Hospital, Firoza Bakht gave birth to a son on Saturday. After a painful caesarean section, she now shares her bed with three others — another new mother and two newborns.

Seventy-three patients in the paediatric ward share three toilets, which have no water.

The doctors at the hospital are no better off. At least five doctors in the Obstetrics and Gynaecology department at the hospital are under treatment for Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs). Hospital Acquired Infections (HAI), especially UTIs, are a part of the package deal that come with treatment at the DDU Hospital.

As a last resort, women doctors in the hospital's Obstetrics and Gynaecology department are running a signature campaign to get hospital authorities to sit up and take notice. "We have repeatedly told our seniors to make basic facilities like water and toilets available. Since consultants have personal toilets in their rooms, they do not care about the facilities available to patients and doctors," said a senior doctor in the Paediatrics department.

Said Firoza, "The ward is filthy and toilets are filling up. No one cleans them and there is no water- to clean or to drink. Due to the unhygienic conditions and bed-sharing, pus develops in the sutures. Like most patients in this ward, my sutures too had to be re-done,".

"Since the toilets meant for patients are in such terrible shape, patients use the ones meant for doctors. They are bound to catch infections and so are we. With three to four patients per bed, there is severe risk of cross-infection, which leads to pus formation in the sutures. Close to 70 per cent of the patients' dressing is re-done every two days," said a nurse on condition of anonymity.

Hospital Medical Superintendent Dr Aveendra Prasad, however, blamed the Public Works Department for the hospital's lack of cleanliness. "Infections happen at times when you are working in such an environment. But I have no information about doctors getting infected. It is the PWD's job to maintain cleanliness of the toilets and we are also clearly short of toilets. We have proposed a renovation at the hospital, but that will take a few years," added Dr Prasad.

"We, however, cannot turn away patients because of insufficient number of toilets. They are sharing beds and this obviously leads to cross-infections. But infections can be cured. It is better than turning patients away and causing deaths," he added.

According to hospital authorities, the staff sanction for DDU Hospital is one patient per nurse, while in reality one nurse cares for seven to 10 patients. "We are the biggest hospital in the area. These problems are bound to occur when the patient load in huge," added Dr Prasad.

Heading: Accused get bail in Rs 3 crore bank fraud case - Indian Express
Content:
A city court on Tuesday convicted three persons for murdering businessman and local Congress Seva Dal leader Surender Gupta. Gupta was stabbed and shot dead at the South Extension market in May 2003.

Additional Sessions Judge S K Sarvaria convicted main accused Sushil (25) Suresh (23) and Dalip (31), based primarily on the eyewitness account of Subodh Kumar, who used to work for Gupta. Meanwhile, another accused Lekhraj, a listed criminal in the area, was acquitted by the court.

The court has fixed November 19 as the day for sentencing the accused.

Investigations had revealed that Gupta, who owned a restaurant in the South Extension market, was killed because he owed Rs 2.5 lakh to Sushil and Rs 50,000 to Suresh, the police said.

The accused were arrested from Greater Noida and a country-made weapon had been seized from their possession. The police arrested them after they received information that these persons had been missing from their respective residences.

On the day of the murder, Gupta was headed for his restaurant when he was attacked by the accused near his residence in H-Block of South Extension Part I. They stabbed him on the face and then shot him. Gupta was rushed to the AIIMS, where he succumbed to injuries.
